suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm package installations containing preinstall/postinstall scripts that execute obfuscated JavaScript, call eval(), or use ROT-based string decoding. Monitor for unusually large index.js files in preinstall hooks. Correlate against known-good baseline.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from CI/CD Environment and Local Filesystem
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Harvests secrets and credentials from the local environment and CI context: environment variables, ~/.npmrc tokens, SSH keys, GitHub tokens, and CI/CD secrets.' No detection use case covers this critical exfiltration objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js or npm processes attempting to read ~/.npmrc, ~/.ssh/, GitHub credential files, or environment variables containing secrets. Alert on credential material being transmitted from npm install contexts to external hosts.

suggestion.title: Cloud Identity and Access Enumeration (GCP/Azure)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'Enumerates cloud identities. The notable change in this variant is a pair of new collectors for GCP and Azure that enumerate every identity the infected host can assume, not just static secrets.' This post-exploitation discovery phase was not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk cloud identity enumeration (list service accounts, roles, bindings) from newly-provisioned CI/CD runners or developer machines immediately following npm package installation. Alert on `gcloud` or `az` CLI commands querying IAM resources from post-npm-install processes.

suggestion.title: npm Package Republication as Worm Propagation
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'It queries the registry for other packages the compromised identity can publish and republishes them, carrying the same payload, which is what turns a single compromised maintainer into a worm.' This self-propagation mechanism was not modeled as a detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect republication of npm packages by accounts with no prior publish history, or republication to unusual version schemes. Alert when republished package versions contain preinstall scripts or obfuscated code not present in prior releases. Monitor for rapid-fire republication of multiple packages by single identity.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions OIDC Token Request with npm Publishing Scope
suggestion.rationale: Root cause details: 'Those commits added a minimal GitHub Actions workflow that... Requested a GitHub OIDC identity token via id-token: write.' This was the injection vector and must be detected as early-stage compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new GitHub Actions workflows requesting id-token: write permissions in repositories with npm publishing credentials. Flag workflows triggered on every push that request OIDC tokens, especially in namespaces without prior CI/CD activity. Cross-check against organization baseline.

suggestion.title: npm Publish Activity from Compromised GitHub Account
suggestion.rationale: Article shows the payload was published 'in two waves on June 1' via compromised account. Alert on atypical npm publishing patterns linked to account compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm publish operations using OIDC tokens from GitHub Actions workflows, especially those added recently or triggered by unusual accounts. Alert on publishes that occur outside normal deployment windows or from previously-dormant accounts.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names codexui-android as the attack vector—'Stolen in codexui-android npm Supply Chain Attack.' Pipeline missed the core IOC: the package name itself and unusual installation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm install commands targeting codexui-android or structurally similar obfuscated package names (visual typosquatting). Monitor for installation of packages with zero historical downloads, mismatched maintainer profiles, or rapidly uploaded versions.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting Post npm Install
suggestion.rationale: Article states OpenAI tokens were stolen—attack requires code execution during/after installation to access and exfiltrate credentials. Pipeline found no execution or credential-access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js child processes spawning within seconds of npm install, particularly those reading environment variables, ~/.aws, ~/.npmrc, or making unauthenticated HTTPS requests with Bearer token headers.

suggestion.title: OpenAI API Token Exfiltration via Package
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies tokens stolen—core attack objective. Pipeline should surface network indicators, C2 domains, or token transmission patterns if present in article body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound HTTPS/HTTP from npm-related processes containing OpenAI key patterns (sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}). Correlate with DNS queries to newly registered domains or non-CDN hosts from development/CI environments.

suggestion.title: Postinstall Hook Execution Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks via npm typically execute via postinstall or preinstall scripts in package.json. Article describes code execution on install—pipeline found no execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm postinstall/preinstall script execution for: shell spawning, network calls, credential reads, script obfuscation, or downloads from external URLs. Flag any postinstall that does not match package declared dependencies.

suggestion.title: npm Registry Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Compromised or newly-published malicious package should trigger anomaly alerts. Pipeline missed package metadata (version, timestamp, maintainer, file count) as IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm registry requests for packages with: creation date <7 days old, single version published, zero prior downloads, maintainer mismatch with historical owner, or installation from non-official npm registry.

suggestion.title: XenoRAT Hash Detection with C2 Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Nine SHA256 hashes provided but UC_RMM_TOOLS uses process names instead. Hashes must be primary detection vector. Article states XenoRAT communicates to listed IPs—pair hash detection with outbound network connection to strengthen signal and reduce false positives.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation matching provided SHA256 hashes. Correlate with outbound TCP/UDP connections from same process to C2 IPs (185.235.137.106, 103.132.98.224, 103.132.98.226) within 60 seconds. This dual correlation dramatically reduces false positives versus hash-only matching.

suggestion.title: XenoRAT Persistence via Registry and Scheduled Tasks
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes XenoRAT as 'persistent remote access tool' but no persistence-phase detection is generated. Persistent RATs require auto-start mechanisms (registry Run keys, scheduled tasks, Windows services) to survive reboot.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for registry modifications under HKLM/HKCU Run keys and scheduled task creation originating from or linked to XenoRAT hash IOCs. Track suspicious service installations with randomized names created during incident window. Correlate task execution with C2 connections.

suggestion.title: Spear-Phishing Delivery to Finance Ministry Officials
suggestion.rationale: Article states SideCopy 'launched a focused cyberattack against Afghanistan's Ministry of Finance' targeting 'provincial finance officials across all 34 Afghan Mustoufiats.' No delivery-phase detection for email or document exploit suggested despite clear spear-phishing attack pattern to job-title-specific targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for emails to afghanistan.gov.af or finance ministry personnel with attachments matching provided SHA256 hashes or containing macro-enabled Office documents. Look for email subject matter referencing Afghan fiscal administration, tax collection, or audit—themes likely used in spear-phishing to finance officials.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Command Execution from XenoRAT Process
suggestion.rationale: RAT malware by definition enables hands-on-keyboard command execution. Article describes XenoRAT as tool for 'remote access,' implying cmd.exe or PowerShell spawning, but no execution-phase detection hunting for suspicious child processes is generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag spawning of cmd.exe or powershell.exe (with elevated or system privileges) as direct or indirect children of processes matching XenoRAT SHA256 hashes. Monitor command-line arguments for credential dumping (lsass, SAM), lateral movement (net.exe, psexec), or file exfiltration utilities.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Access to abimj.edu.af Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'abimj.edu.af' as a domain IOC, suggesting possible watering hole compromise or phishing infrastructure. No detection for HTTP requests to this domain or DNS resolution by finance ministry users is recommended, despite clear delivery/reconnaissance vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries and HTTP requests to abimj.edu.af originating from Afghanistan government networks or finance ministry IP space. Correlate with XenoRAT process creation events occurring within 5–30 minutes post-access. Flag unusual user agents or rapid multi-host scanning patterns suggesting automated reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: SideCopy Campaign Attribution Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article attribution to 'Pakistan-linked' SideCopy threat group provides actor context for prioritization and attribution hunting, but no indicator tying subsequent detections back to SideCopy is suggested. Missing linkage between IOCs and actor profile limits operational usefulness.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Tag all detections (C2 connections, process hashes, persistence artifacts) with SideCopy campaign context. Create composite alert rule grouping network IOCs + hash IOCs + persistence indicators + delivery artifacts under 'Operation XENOFISCAL' label to surface coordinated campaigns versus isolated incidents.

suggestion.title: Spearphishing Campaign: Fake Verification Page Initial Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'fake verification pages that trick them into running a malicious script' — this is the campaign's delivery mechanism, not covered by phishing-click UC which assumes legitimate URLs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Emails with URLs matching fake-CAPTCHA or verification-mimic patterns (verification, check, confirm, reCAPTCHA lookalike subdomains) sent to multiple users. Correlate email delivery to URL click, then to process execution on recipient device within 60 seconds.

suggestion.title: ClickFix: Clipboard Injection to PowerShell Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically identifies 'clipboard-injected PowerShell' as exploitation technique. Existing UC detects only parent-child process; must correlate clipboard read/write to immediate obfuscated script execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Clipboard read operations (WM_GETCLIPBOARDDATA, Get-Clipboard) followed within 2 seconds by PowerShell/mshta process execution with encoded payloads (FromBase64, IEX, DownloadString, MemoryStream) from explorer.exe or RuntimeBroker parent.

suggestion.title: RAT Malware Installation: File Hash Signatures
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 4 SHA256 hashes of RAT samples. Pipeline should emit hash-based detections for file execution/creation, not IOC-only templates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: File execution, registry modification, or process injection matching SHA256 hashes {1514b1268e9dc6d2f37137aa38c756cb4bf8186ac9235d6863b78e7f8bbbe976, 469bac8e10f50263e8ff0806e6ba126bb4cc660799129a8653eab3f8ec7201e5, 9c7eda2c4d3aaa8746495741bef57a07de180f0409409faf0f91658e88ba33f5, 7ba5481c873bb3081442561f749f590badd72ef249fddfe993e30b28dc0c2112} triggers immediate isolation alert.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated PowerShell Download-and-Execute Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RAT delivery via 'obfuscated' PowerShell. Existing UC too generic (iex/FromBase64); needs specificity for DownloadString → IEX pattern and correlation to attacker IPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: PowerShell process with command-line matching regex for (DownloadString|Net.ServicePointManager) AND (IEX|Invoke-Expression), where InitiatingProcessFileName is explorer.exe or RuntimeBroker.exe, with outbound connection to one of the 6 IOC IPs/domains within 10 seconds.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing: Outbound Connections to SmartApeSG Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 4 IPs and 2 domains. Pipeline should auto-generate network IOC hunts (outbound connections) for all provided infrastructure, not defer to templates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Non-server endpoints establishing outbound connections to {178.156.165.82, 178.156.173.194, 89.110.110.119, 185.163.47.217, hiddenplanetlab.top, silverharvestnetwork.com}. Escalate if connection preceded by PowerShell/cmd/mshta execution or file hash matches RAT samples within 30 minutes.

suggestion.title: Domain Masquerading: Lookalike Verification/CAPTCHA Domains
suggestion.rationale: Attack uses 'fake verification pages' to masquerade as legitimate. No hunt for domain string-similarity to Google reCAPTCHA, Cloudflare Challenge, or login verification endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: URLs clicked containing high edit-distance/Levenshtein-similarity strings to recaptcha.net, challenges.cloudflare.com, or common SSO verifiers. Flag if domain registrant info is masked, domain age <90 days, or hosting IP matches one of the 4 attacker IPs.

suggestion.title: Accessibility Service Abuse for Device Control
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malware 'Abuses Accessibility Service to control devices'—this is the signature technique and primary attack vector. No UC generated despite being the core mechanic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Android apps requesting accessibility service permissions followed by suspicious input injection, touch event simulation, or app overlay creation. Flag unexpected accessibility grants to non-system apps, especially those installed from external sources.

suggestion.title: Banking/Crypto Credential Harvesting via UI Overlay
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware targets 'banking credentials, financial data, and cryptocurrency accounts'—core impact. Trojan uses overlays to intercept credentials. No harvesting/exfiltration UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual data exfiltration from banking apps or keylogging-like input capture patterns. Alert on accessibility service + network traffic from financial apps to unexpected domains. Track credential API calls from non-banking apps.

suggestion.title: Malicious Link Click Leading to Trojan Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malware 'spreads through malicious links disguised as downloads from trusted, well-known applications'—initial access vector entirely missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate browser/messaging clicks on phishing links with subsequent sideloaded APK installations or app store downloads of trojanized apps. Flag installs from Chrome Downloads or messaging apps followed by permission escalations.

suggestion.title: Network Traffic to Malicious C2 Domain (bitlrewards-app.com)
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'bitlrewards-app.com' as IOC; standard C2 detection template applies but pipeline failed to generate it. High-confidence network hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any DNS resolution or network connections to 'bitlrewards-app.com' or its IP '199.217.99.122'. Baseline Android apps should not contact reward-themed domains. Correlate with banking app activity on same device.

suggestion.title: File Hash Detection: OverlayPhantom Trojan Variants
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 3 SHA256 hashes (9ef37376bfaa..., f8b614a2918..., 8ddc1f2a75f...). Standard hash-based detection template applies but pipeline generated nothing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match file hashes against known OverlayPhantom samples. Alert on download, execution, or installation of any file matching these SHA256s. Check sandbox submissions and app store scans for obfuscated variants.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Permission Escalation via Obfuscated APK
suggestion.rationale: Article notes T1027 (Obfuscation) and trojan persists via accessibility permissions. Detection gap: no UC for the obfuscation + permissions correlation during installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag APK installations where the binary shows code obfuscation patterns (reversed DEX, string encryption, reflection abuse) *and* requests dangerous permissions (accessibility, admin, overlay). High confidence: obfuscated + accessibility grant in single install.

suggestion.title: Dragon Weave APT Initial Access Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article headline states 'China-Aligned Groups Ramp Up Attacks: Dragon Weave Hits Czech Republic & Taiwan' but pipeline extracted zero IOCs or attack surface. Initial access vectors (phishing, watering hole, supply chain) should be detected before compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Dragon Weave typically establishes access via spear-phishing or watering holes targeting government entities. Monitor for uncommon attachment types or sender-domain mismatch to government email recipients in CZ/TW regions; correlate with known Dragon Weave C2 infrastructure if available.

suggestion.title: Dragon Weave Persistence and C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: APT 'attacks' imply persistence post-compromise and command channel establishment. Article targeting high-value government networks suggests sustained access requirement, but no C2 infrastructure or persistence mechanisms were identified.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Dragon Weave C2 often uses HTTPS or DNS tunneling to evade detection. Flag TLS certificates issued to suspicious registrars, DNS queries to newly registered domains, and anomalous outbound HTTPS traffic from government networks during off-hours.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting Preceding Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Government infrastructure breaches typically require post-access credential theft to move laterally. No detection hypotheses provided for credential access phase despite attack targeting two sovereign governments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal AuthenticationPackage values (Negotiate instead of Kerberos), failed logon clusters followed by success, and suspicious LSASS access patterns post-initial compromise. Dragon Weave uses common credential harvesters (Mimikatz variants).

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Across Government Network Segments
suggestion.rationale: Czech and Taiwan government targets (stated in title) have air-gapped or segmented networks. No mention of lateral movement detection, yet this is critical for multi-stage breach assessment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Dragon Weave uses SMB and RDP for lateral movement. Detect multiple failed RDP logons from single source followed by success; unusual inter-VLan traffic; and PsExec-like execution patterns (parent process cmd.exe spawning services).

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Government Secrets via Dragon Weave
suggestion.rationale: Article title indicates attacks on Czech Republic and Taiwan governments—nation-state targets imply espionage and data exfiltration. No detection use cases for egress of classified or sensitive documents.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk data movement to cloud storage (OneDrive, Dropbox, Mega) or FTP exfil. Flag unusual RAR/7z archive creation in user directories followed by outbound network transfer. Dragon Weave often stages data via cloud services or foreign FTP servers.

suggestion.title: CVE-2024-21182 Scanner Match — Oracle WebLogic
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2024-21182 — match against your vulnerability scanner'. Pipeline generated zero UCs despite direct recommendation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt asset inventory and vulnerability scanner outputs for CVE-2024-21182 matches against Oracle WebLogic Server instances. Flag any "vulnerable" or "missing patch" results immediately; federal patch due-date is 2026-06-04.

suggestion.title: Inbound T3/IIOP Traffic to WebLogic Servers
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation occurs 'via T3, IIOP' protocols — network indicators should anchor first-line detection. Pipeline missed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound connections to WebLogic default ports (7001, 7002, 7003) sourced from external/untrusted networks. Correlate with failed authentication or privilege-escalation attempts post-connection.

suggestion.title: WebLogic Server Error Logs — Exploitation Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions Oracle WebLogic Server as target; error logs during active exploitation attempts should show malformed requests, deserialization errors, or access violations on T3/IIOP listeners.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WebLogic Server logs (e.g., `domain.log`) for connection attempts on T3/IIOP ports from suspicious sources, followed by errors related to deserialization, reflection, or classloading. Unspecified vulnerabilities often manifest as exception dumps.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Data Access — WebLogic File/Database Reads
suggestion.rationale: Article states successful attacks result in 'complete access to all Oracle WebLogic Server accessible data'. Detection must span impact phase beyond initial exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful T3/IIOP exploitation, hunt for abnormal file reads (config files, keystores, datasource files) or database queries executed under WebLogic process context. Baseline normal data access patterns for this application and flag significant deviations.

suggestion.title: Network Service Discovery — WebLogic Port Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Pre-exploitation reconnaissance often includes port scanning for T3/IIOP listeners. Article does not explicitly describe this step but it's a necessary precursor to targeted exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple failed connection attempts or port scans targeting WebLogic ports (7001, 7002) from a single source within a short time window, especially if followed by successful exploitation attempts on the same or related systems.

suggestion.title: Tainted container image deployment from poisoned registry
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The tainted images distributed a stealer that was loaded during the KICS scanning process' — supply chain attack via Docker Hub repository compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of processes from container images pulled from unusual or recently-added Docker Hub accounts, especially those deploying known stealer families. Correlate image pull time with subsequent suspicious process execution (child processes indicating stealer behavior).

suggestion.title: Kubernetes secret enumeration and exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'steal Kubernetes secrets' as attack objective after container compromise — credential access from orchestration layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Kubernetes API audit logs for sudden spikes in `list secrets` or `get secret` operations from a single pod/service account. Cross-reference with network exfiltration patterns (outbound connections from container to external IPs immediately after secret access).

suggestion.title: Container escape via dangerous capability assignment
suggestion.rationale: Article's attack vector section references 'CAP_SYS_ADMIN CAP_SYS_MODULE CAP_SYS_PTRACE CAP_NET_ADMIN' as escape mechanisms — privilege escalation enabling host compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on pods or containers instantiated with CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE, or CAP_SYS_PTRACE capabilities, especially combined with writable /proc mounts or /sys access. Correlate with child process creation of kernel-module loading tools (insmod, modprobe) or ptrace syscalls from container namespace.

suggestion.title: Stealer malware execution from container scanning process
suggestion.rationale: Article states stealer 'was loaded during the KICS scanning process' — malware execution within development/build pipelines disguised as legitimate scanning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect KICS or other container scanning tools spawning unexpected child processes, writing to temp/cache directories, or establishing network connections. Baseline legitimate KICS execution and alert on deviations. Monitor for stealer signatures (registry access, browser cookie enumeration, SSH key theft) in child processes.

suggestion.title: Orchestration API abuse for lateral movement or persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'Exploitation of orchestration APIs' and 'Exploiting... insecure use of containerization and orchestration APIs' as primary attack vectors — requires detection at API call layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Kubernetes API for unusual authentication patterns (service account tokens from unexpected source IPs), rapid API enumeration (list pods/services/secrets), or privilege-escalation attempts (create RoleBinding/ClusterRoleBinding from non-admin accounts). Detect API calls creating new containers or modifying network policies.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability exploitation in container runtime (containerd, Docker)
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Exploiting vulnerabilities in the host system and container runtime components' as primary vector — CVE-driven escape attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline runtime versions and CVE exposure in use. Alert on container processes executing syscall patterns or CLI invocations known to trigger container runtime CVEs (e.g., namespace manipulation, cgroup escape attempts). Correlate with privilege elevation or host filesystem access from container.

suggestion.title: PHP Object Injection via Unauthenticated Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'unauthenticated PHP object injection flaw' and 'no login required'—this is the root exploit vector and warrants direct detection for serialized PHP payloads in request bodies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST/PUT requests to Mirasvit Cache Warmer endpoints (e.g., /app/cache, /rest/V1/cache*) for serialized PHP objects (signature: 'O:' followed by class names). Unauthenticated requests with Content-Length > 1KB and suspicious class names (Zend, Symfony, Laravel gadget chains) should trigger high-confidence alerts.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Code Execution from Magento Web Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'enables remote code execution'—RCE via cached PHP would manifest as php-cgi or php-fpm spawning unexpected child processes (shells, curl, wget) without legitimate request context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect web server processes (apache2, php-fpm, nginx) spawning cmd.exe, /bin/bash, or network utilities (curl, wget, nc) with parent command chains lacking normal application context. Baseline legitimate Magento plugins; alert on anomalous child processes post-exploitation of cache warmer.

suggestion.title: Mirasvit Cache Warmer Malicious Serialized Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation relies on PHP object injection—monitor for specific gadget chain prefixes in cache or request payloads targeting known vulnerable libraries bundled with Magento (Zend, Symfony).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests containing serialized PHP class instantiations (e.g., 'O:10:"ClassName"') directed to cache warmer endpoints. Cross-reference deserialization with known RCE gadget chains; prioritize requests with base64-encoded or URL-encoded payloads containing 'eval', 'system', 'exec' method names.

suggestion.title: Suspicious WordPress Admin Account Creation
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Actively Exploited to Create Admin Accounts'—pipeline generated zero UCs. Admin elevation is the stated impact and must be detected. Article body truncated, but title is unambiguous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress user creation/modification events for new accounts assigned admin role, especially outside business hours or via API. Correlate with WP Maps Pro requests. Flag accounts created with default or randomized credentials by non-admin principals.

suggestion.title: Exploit of WP Maps Pro Plugin Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references active exploitation of a flaw in WP Maps Pro. No exploitation detection pattern was generated. Plugin name + vulnerability interaction is the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor requests to WP Maps Pro plugin endpoints for anomalous parameters, POST requests to unauthenticated admin functions, or requests using known exploitation payloads (pending CVE publication). Baseline legitimate plugin traffic and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: New Admin Account Usage Immediately Post-Creation
suggestion.rationale: Admin accounts created via exploitation must be used for persistence/lateral movement. Pipeline missed post-exploitation detection entirely despite 'actively exploited' claim in title.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on WordPress sessions from newly created admin accounts within 1 hour of account creation. Flag access to plugin management, configuration, or file editor. Correlate with source IP to detect attacker login post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: High-Volume Failed Authentication Against Password Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'brute-force attacks that attempted logins from distant locations and unknown devices'—core attack vector (T1110) not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on >15 failed authentication attempts against Dashlane or similar cloud password managers in <10 minutes from single source IP. Escalate if followed by successful login from same IP within 24h, indicating credential compromise post-brute-force.

suggestion.title: Impossible-Travel Login Pattern: Distant-Location Authentication Spike
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes attackers used 'distant locations'—geographic anomaly detection is foundational for this attack class.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect failed login attempts originating from geographically distant IP ranges (e.g., opposite hemispheres) within hours for single user account. Correlate with failed authentication velocity to distinguish brute-force from legitimate VPN-hop scenarios.

suggestion.title: Bulk Device Registration Verification Email Volume Spike
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'emails contained verification codes for legitimate account owners to register new devices'—spike in unsolicited device-registration emails is leading indicator of account takeover attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unusual volume of device-registration verification emails (>50 in 1 hour across platform). Correlate send timestamps with failed login spike and source IP geography to confirm brute-force attack chain.

suggestion.title: Account Suspension/Lockout Triggered by Automated Anti-Brute-Force Controls
suggestion.rationale: Article: account suspension 'as part of Dashlane's built-in security controls'—lockout events are defensive indicators of active attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when account lockout/suspension occurs following rapid-fire failed authentication (e.g., 20+ failures in 5min window). Track unsuspension requests to detect secondary abuse of account-recovery flow.

suggestion.title: Successful New-Device Login Following Failed Authentication Storm
suggestion.rationale: Attackers targeted 'unknown devices'—successful login from unregistered device after brute-force barrage indicates attacker gained valid credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful login from previously-unseen device within 24h of failed login spike for same user. Flag if device-registration email preceded login by <2h, suggesting attacker received and acted on verification code.

suggestion.title: Cross-Account Brute-Force Campaign: Credential-Spray Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'multiple Dashlane users' targeted—platform-wide attack indicates credential stuffing or password-spray campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect single source IP attempting authentication against 25+ distinct user accounts within 30 minutes. High-confidence indicator of credential-stuffing or password-spray; cross-correlate failed vs. successful login ratio by target account.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: User enumeration via member listing before privilege escalation
suggestion.rationale: Attacker must discover valid user_id values to exploit the vulnerability. Article states the flaw 'forwards the request body's user_id...straight into MemberService.add(workspace_id, user_id, role)' with no validation. No detection for reconnaissance phase (member enumeration). Should detect GET /workspaces/{id}/members followed by POST with suspicious additions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GET requests to workspace member-listing endpoints (e.g., /workspaces/*/members) followed within 10 minutes by POST /workspaces/*/members from the same user with role=owner. Baseline on normal admin member-addition patterns and flag additions to users not previously in workspace.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: Multiple failed or rejected member-addition attempts
suggestion.rationale: Attacker may spray invalid user_ids against the endpoint before guessing or enumerating valid ones. No detection for brute-force or spray attempts. Article shows endpoint 'forwards the request body...straight' with no input validation on user_id.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for 5+ POST requests to /workspaces/*/members from same source with distinct user_id values in request bodies, especially those returning 4xx errors (user not found, invalid id), followed by a 201 success. Correlate on source IP and time window.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: Newly-added owner performing sensitive workspace operations
suggestion.rationale: After privilege escalation succeeds, attacker uses new owner account for lateral movement (policy changes, member removal, data export). Article describes privilege escalation but provides no detection for actions-on-objectives phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify users added via POST /workspaces/*/members with role=owner, then correlate to subsequent sensitive API calls (DELETE /workspaces/*/members, PUT /workspaces/*/settings, data-download operations) within 2 hours. Flag if newly-added user had zero or <5 prior actions in the workspace.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: Owner grants to recently-created or federated accounts
suggestion.rationale: Attacker likely grants privilege to new or attacker-controlled identities. No detection for suspicious identity grant targets. Article mentions 'arbitrary user' can be added—should profile target accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful POST /workspaces/*/members with role=owner against identity creation events. Flag if target user_id was created within 7 days, has never logged into the workspace, or is associated with external/guest tenants.

suggestion.title: Fake Browser Update Prompts from Untrusted Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article states threat actors 'entice victims with fraudulent software update prompts, usually impersonating browser updates' targeting Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari, Opera, Brave, Yandex, Vivaldi, Samsung Internet, and UC Browser.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect browser update prompts originating from domains outside official vendor CDNs. Alert on downloads triggered by fake update pages. Block or warn on unexpected redirects to known malware distribution infrastructure from legitimate-looking browser-based content.

suggestion.title: PowerShell Command Execution Following Social Engineering Interaction
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'ClickFix attacks involve PowerShell commands' and describes the tactic as 'deceiving victims into copying and executing malicious commands on their systems.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PowerShell execution with base64-encoded or suspicious inline arguments immediately after user browser activity. Alert on commands matching patterns typical of malware installers or commodity dropper scripts. Correlate with parent processes running browsers or chat applications.

suggestion.title: JavaScript Code Injection Matching zTDS Pattern (t.js?site=<id>)
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'JavaScript injection following the t.js?site=<id> pattern' as a technical fingerprint, with researchers discovering '80+ malicious injection domains' using this pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests matching the pattern `t.js?site=` followed by a parameter. Monitor for injected JavaScript on legitimate websites that renders fake technical support content or redirects to attacker infrastructure. Correlate with known malicious injection domain list maintained by researchers.

suggestion.title: Suspicious ZIP Archive Downloads with Browser-Update-Themed Executables
suggestion.rationale: Article describes a payload where 'fake Firefox update that downloaded a ZIP archive containing multiple DLLs and a malicious executable named Browser Update.exe,' indicating a consistent delivery pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ZIP downloads from non-vendor domains, especially those containing .exe or .dll files with browser update–related names. Monitor for automated extraction and execution of files from such archives. Flag parent processes (browser) that spawn child processes related to archive extraction.

suggestion.title: macOS Clipboard Hijacking via Verification-Themed Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'obfuscated JavaScript payload specifically designed to target macOS desktop systems, delivered via verification-themed ClickFix attacks that hijack the clipboard.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On macOS, monitor for JavaScript execution accessing clipboard functions via pbpaste, pbcopy, or Accessibility framework. Alert on verification-themed prompts attempting clipboard manipulation. Flag spawned Terminal or shell processes immediately following clipboard access attempts.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Redirects from Compromised High-Reputation Websites to TDS Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article states DriveSurge 'hijacks thousands of legitimate, high-reputation websites and silently redirects visitors to malware' through zTDS, representing initial access via drive-by compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP 3xx redirects from known-good domains to unfamiliar or newly registered domains. Alert on silent redirects (not user-initiated clicks) from legitimate websites. Baseline the redirect destinations and flag anomalies pointing to known TDS infrastructure or malware CDNs.

suggestion.title: WebSphere HTTP Exploitation Attempt — Crafted Request Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attack vector is 'specially crafted HTTP requests' to public-facing WebSphere, but no behavioral UC for detecting payload anomalies in requests to WebSphere endpoints. Needed in initial_access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/PUT requests to WebSphere admin console, deployment manager, or common plugin endpoints for malformed headers, oversized payloads, or known exploitation signatures. Baseline normal request patterns and alert on deviations correlated with CVE-2026-8633/8620 asset inventory.

suggestion.title: WebSphere Process Execution from Plugin Component
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'arbitrary code execution' via the optional Web Server Plug-ins component, but no UC for detecting unexpected process spawning or shell invocation from WebSphere worker processes. This is the impact phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned by WebSphere Java processes (wsadmin, websphere.jar) with suspiciously low parent legitimacy scores, or cmd.exe/powershell/bash invocations from unexpected parents. Look for lateral patterns post-initial WebSphere compromise.

suggestion.title: WebSphere Plugin Configuration Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is in the 'optional Web Server Plug-ins component' — asset exposure detection alone misses active post-exploitation foothold consolidation. No UC for monitoring plugin config changes, restart loops, or credential staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized modifications to WebSphere plugin configuration files (plugin-cfg.xml, properties), plugin installation paths, or environment variable poisoning that would ensure payload re-execution across restarts.

suggestion.title: AppDomainManager Registry Configuration Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: Article title and body center on 'AppDomainManager Hijacking' as primary technique. Pipeline missed T1547.014 entirely. Should detect when attackers write arbitrary DLL paths to AppDomainManager registry keys to intercept .NET CLR initialization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Classes\.NET Framework\Assembly\AppDomainManager (or assembly caches) with non-Microsoft signed DLL paths, user-writable locations (AppData, Temp), or network-mounted shares. Correlate with subsequent .NET process execution.

suggestion.title: Anomalous .NET Framework Process DLL Load Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article describes sophisticated .NET hijacking to evade EDR. Should detect when .NET runtime processes (regsvcs.exe, vbc.exe, csc.exe, aspnet_compiler.exe) load DLLs from suspicious contexts via AppDomainManager injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DLL loads from .NET-related processes when the DLL originates from: unsigned paths, user AppData/Temp, UNC paths, or has entropy signatures matching obfuscated/packed code. Priority: DLLs loaded after AppDomainManager registry writes.

suggestion.title: C2 Domain Callback via Known IOC Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article title identifies 'Application Layer Protocol' (T1071) and lists 6 C2 domains explicitly (buisness-centeral-transportation.com, premierhealthadvisory.com, ramiltonsfinance.com, business-startup.org, docspace-y4cumb.onlyoffice.com, docspace-twpf0e.onlyoffice.com). Pipeline generated zero use cases despite article recommending network IOC hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound TCP/443 or TCP/80 from .NET-related processes or child processes thereof to the 6 listed domains. Low false-positive risk; these are not legitimate business-critical SaaS endpoints. OnlyOffice subdomains require additional context (check org's legitimate OnlyOffice usage).

suggestion.title: Execution of Known Malicious File Hashes
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 12 SHA256 hashes marked 'high-fidelity only' (44f4f7ac..., 332ba2f0..., etc.). Pipeline extracted zero IOCs. Article recommends file hash hunt as 'High' confidence install-phase detection; pipeline produced empty use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hash-based alerting on exact SHA256 match for any of the 12 provided values. Alert on file creation followed by execution, or immediate execution from suspicious paths (Temp, AppData, or file share). Criticality: High.

suggestion.title: EDR Evasion via AMSI Bypass in AppDomainManager Context
suggestion.rationale: Article title emphasizes 'evade EDR Detection'; AppDomainManager hijacking commonly used to patch AMSI.dll before executing malicious code. Pipeline missed T1562.001 and T1562.008 entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor .NET runtime processes for DLL unload/reload cycles on amsi.dll or System.Management.Automation modules. Alert if AppDomainManager DLL load precedes PowerShell/WMI process creation. Flag memset/VirtualProtect calls on AMSI function addresses.

suggestion.title: Suspicious OnlyOffice Infrastructure Abuse for C2
suggestion.rationale: Article lists docspace-y4cumb.onlyoffice.com and docspace-twpf0e.onlyoffice.com as IOCs with entropy-laden subdomains (y4cumb, twpf0e). Suggests either compromised legitimate OnlyOffice instance or DNS abuse of trusted SaaS provider.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS queries to onlyoffice.com subdomains not matching organization's approved OnlyOffice tenant. Flag docspace subdomains with unusual entropy/randomness. Cross-check against legitimate OnlyOffice admin APIs to detect infrastructure abuse vs. account takeover.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation – Supply Chain Compromise Indicator
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'npm Packages' compromise; no detection rule for unexpected package versions, malicious updates, or installations from untrusted repositories despite this being the initial attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/update operations for packages matching known supply-chain compromise signatures (unexpected version jumps, unusual dependencies, installation of packages with names similar to legitimate Red Hat dependencies). Alert on installations from non-standard registries or mirrors outside the organization's allowed package sources.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration via Worm-like Process Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Credential-Stealing Worm' but no detection rule exists for process injection, credential access patterns, or memory scanning behavior typical of worms that harvest credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned/suspicious processes spawning from npm or Node.js binaries, reading credential stores (browser password databases, SSH keys, API tokens), or establishing outbound connections to exfiltrate data. Flag parent-child relationships where Node.js/npm launch processes with names matching common worm behaviors (credential harvesters, DNS tunneling, memory scrapers).

suggestion.title: Persistence via npm Package Hooks and Post-Install Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain npm attacks typically abuse post-install scripts (package.json) to establish persistence; no rule covers suspicious npm script execution or registry modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm post-install, preinstall, and prepare scripts for execution of obfuscated code, base64-encoded commands, or shell invocations. Alert on modifications to .npmrc, package-lock.json, or node_modules/ that don't match legitimate dependency resolution. Trigger if npm scripts spawn non-Node.js processes (bash, PowerShell, curl).

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Detection – Worm Propagation Across npm Monorepos
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates 'worm' behavior suggesting lateral spread; no detection for unusual file writes across monorepo structures, shared node_modules directories, or propagation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid writes to multiple node_modules directories, unexpected file copies across project boundaries, or process spawning that suggests worm-like self-replication. Flag when npm processes create/modify files in sibling projects, shared development directories, or container layer directories.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication via npm Package Registry or DNS
suggestion.rationale: Credential-stealing malware typically requires exfiltration channel; no rule for C2 communication patterns typical of worms (DNS tunneling, registry polling, HTTPS to attacker infrastructure).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTPS/HTTP from Node.js processes to non-standard ports or attacker-controlled domains. Alert on unusual DNS queries from npm/Node processes (especially queries for short-lived or newly registered domains). Flag if worm attempts to callback to npm registry mirrors or attacker-hosted registries.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Account Activity – Compromised Maintainer Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks often compromise maintainer accounts; no detection rule for suspicious npm publish events, API token exfiltration, or account takeover patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry publish events for new versions from known Red Hat maintainers published at unusual times, from new IP addresses, or with suspicious dependency changes. Alert if API tokens are exfiltrated (token reads followed by out-of-band API calls). Correlate npm publishes with credential theft alerts on the same system.

suggestion.title: NPM Preinstall Script Execution with Obfuscated Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'npm runs preinstall scripts automatically during npm install, before any of your own code executes' and 'unusually large, heavily obfuscated JavaScript file... relied on eval() and ROT-based string decoding'. Direct execution path with obfuscation markers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for preinstall script execution via npm package installation. Alert on index.js with high entropy or ROT decoding patterns, eval() calls with large string arguments, or preinstall scripts that differ significantly from benign package baselines. Cross-reference with known-malicious package namespaces.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from npm/Git/Cloud Contexts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Harvests secrets and credentials from the local environment and CI context: environment variables, ~/.npmrc tokens, SSH keys, GitHub tokens, and CI/CD secrets. Enumerates cloud identities.' Explicit credential access from multiple sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious file reads of ~/.npmrc, ~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.config/gcloud during npm package execution. Monitor for unexpected environment variable enumeration (GCP_PROJECT, AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID, AWS_ROLE_ARN) and cloud identity API calls (gcloud auth list, az account list, aws sts get-caller-identity) originating from package installation or CI runner contexts.

suggestion.title: NPM Package Self-Propagation via Registry Republishing
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Self-propagates. It queries the registry for other packages the compromised identity can publish and republishes them, carrying the same payload, which is what turns a single compromised maintainer into a worm.' Worm behavior with registry enumeration and republishing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry queries (npm view <package>) executed from install-time contexts, followed by npm publish commands with modified package manifests carrying new preinstall hooks. Alert on republishing of multiple packages by a single identity within minutes, especially if preceded by package installation from the affected namespace.

suggestion.title: GCP/Azure Service Account Enumeration from Unexpected Contexts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The notable change in this variant is a pair of new collectors for GCP and Azure that enumerate every identity the infected host can assume, not just static secrets.' Cloud-specific enumeration indicating advanced pivot capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of 'gcloud auth list', 'gcloud config list', 'az account list', or 'az account get-access-token' from non-standard processes (npm, node, package installers). Monitor for enumerate-service-account patterns and impersonation attempts (gcloud config set account, az account set) in post-installation contexts.

suggestion.title: GitHub OIDC Token Abuse in Actions Workflow
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Those commits added a minimal GitHub Actions workflow that: Triggered on push to any branch. Requested a GitHub OIDC identity token via id-token: write.' Explicit use of GitHub API token permissions for malicious publishing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for GitHub Actions workflows with 'id-token: write' permissions that execute npm publish or deploy operations, especially in repositories not typically maintained by the author. Alert on OIDC token requests followed by package republishing within the same workflow run. Flag workflows triggered on push to arbitrary branches with minimal review gates.

suggestion.title: Malicious Repository Creation with Miasma Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Newly created attacker repositories carry the description Miasma: The Spreading Blight, which is a useful hunting signal.' Explicit IOC for repository discovery and correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt GitHub for newly created repositories with descriptions matching 'Miasma: The Spreading Blight' or similar mythological/blight-themed language. Correlate with RedHatInsights organization activity, account creation timing, and commits pushing malicious orphan branches. Monitor for rapid repository creation by single account followed by GitHub Actions workflow additions.

suggestion.title: Installation of Packages from Compromised @redhat-cloud-services Scope
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'over 30 official packages under the @redhat-cloud-services npm scope.' Direct initial-access indicator; packages installed from this scope during attack window should be quarantined.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm/yarn install operations targeting @redhat-cloud-services scope packages. Correlate package installation timestamps with CVE disclosure date (2026-06-01). Flag mismatched checksums or unexpected file additions in node_modules/@redhat-cloud-services relative to public registries.

suggestion.title: Node.js Process Harvesting Credentials from npm Configuration and Secrets
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'credential-stealing malware' and 'credential-stealing worm.' No detection for credential-access phase despite explicit payload description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor node.exe or npm-spawned child processes accessing ~/.npmrc, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh, KUBECONFIG, GIT credentials, or environment variables containing SECRET/PASSWORD/API_KEY/TOKEN. Flag file reads followed by child process spawning or outbound connections.

suggestion.title: Post-Install and Pre-Build Scripts with Suspicious Command Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article: malware deployed via npm packages. Post-install and prepare scripts are standard npm payload delivery mechanism for supply-chain attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm lifecycle script execution (postinstall, prepare, preinstall, postinstall). Flag scripts that Base64-decode content, spawn cmd.exe/powershell.exe without user interaction, make unauthenticated network requests, or write to system startup folders.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Harvested SSH or Repository Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'worm' designation implies propagation beyond initial infection. Credential harvesting enables SSH/git-based lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node.exe or child processes initiating SSH connections to internal/external hosts using harvested credentials. Monitor for git operations cloning internal repositories or npm publishing to private registries using stolen auth tokens.

suggestion.title: Command and Control from npm-Spawned Processes
suggestion.rationale: Credential-stealing worm requires exfiltration and potential operator control. No C2 detection despite obvious malware callback requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTPS/HTTP POST requests from node.exe or npm-spawned children to non-whitelist domains with Base64/binary encoded payloads. Monitor for beaconing patterns (periodic requests to same host) or DNS queries to suspicious domains from npm post-install context.

suggestion.title: npm Package Installation of Suspicious or Malicious Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'codexui-android npm Supply Chain Attack' — the attack vector is installation of a backdoored npm package. No detection use case was generated for monitoring package installation, package version anomalies, or unexpected dependencies in package-lock.json.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install commands and package-lock.json/yarn.lock file modifications for unexpected new packages, especially those with low download history, recently-created publishers, or names similar to legitimate packages. Flag installations of 'codexui-android' or variants as critical.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of OpenAI API Credentials and Authentication Tokens
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'OpenAI Codex Authentication Tokens Stolen' — the attack impact is theft and exfiltration of cloud credentials. No detection use case addresses monitoring for API token access, credential enumeration, or suspicious API calls using stolen credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized access to OpenAI API endpoints, suspicious Bearer tokens in HTTP headers sent to external domains, or bulk export of environment variables containing 'OPENAI_*' or 'API_KEY' patterns from processes spawned by node_modules.

suggestion.title: Malicious Code Execution from npm Package Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain compromise typically triggers code execution during package installation or module import. Article title does not detail execution method, but npm attacks commonly run install scripts. No detection was generated for postinstall hooks, script execution, or code running from node_modules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation with parent=node or npm, especially executing scripts from node_modules/.bin, calling curl/wget to exfiltrate data, or accessing /proc/self/environ or local credential stores. Flag npm postinstall/preinstall scripts that spawn shell commands.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Network Exfiltration from Build/Development Environment
suggestion.rationale: Compromised npm packages installed in development/CI environments must exfiltrate stolen credentials. Title confirms tokens stolen but article does not detail attacker infrastructure. Detection should cover outbound HTTPS/DNS from build servers to unknown/newly-registered domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from npm/node processes to non-whitelist domains, especially connections made during package installation. Alert on DNS queries for newly-registered domains or domains with low reputation scores from build environments.

suggestion.title: Discovery of Hardcoded Secrets in Source Code via Malicious Package
suggestion.rationale: Typical npm supply-chain attacks scan installed packages or the consuming application's environment for hardcoded API keys, tokens, or credentials in source and environment variables. Article confirms tokens were stolen but method is not detailed in available text.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious file access patterns by node processes to .env, .env.local, config files, and environment variable enumeration (getenv calls). Flag reads of credential-related files followed by unusual network activity.

suggestion.title: Meta AI Chatbot 2FA Bypass Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'bypass two-factor authentication entirely... by simply asking the bot to hand over access'—core T1111/T1621 scenario absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences where Instagram/Meta support chatbot interactions are followed by 2FA disable/reset requests. Monitor for bot session tokens used to bypass MFA verification flows. Alert on password reset completion without successful MFA re-verification.

suggestion.title: Instagram Account Takeover via Support Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'stolen usernames listed for resale' and takeover of 'high-value OG handles'—impact-phase credential compromise not mapped by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid ownership/credential changes on Instagram accounts following password-reset or 2FA-bypass attempts initiated through support chatbot. Monitor for successful sign-ins from new geolocations/devices shortly after account control transfers.

suggestion.title: Legitimate Tool Abuse for Account Credential Reset
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'critical logic flaw in Meta's AI-powered Instagram support chatbot' weaponized to reset credentials—T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application) or T1195-adjacent pattern not surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Instagram/Meta support chatbot interactions for anomalous intent patterns: requests for password reset, 2FA disable, or account recovery targeting high-value accounts (verified, OG handles, dormant accounts). Alert on unusual multi-account reset requests from same bot session.

suggestion.title: Bulk High-Value Account Credential Changes
suggestion.rationale: Article notes compromise of 'high-value OG Instagram handles, dormant institutional accounts, and verified profiles'—suggests coordinated impact-phase activity not reflected in kill-chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect clusters of account ownership transfers or credential resets affecting accounts with specific characteristics (OG naming patterns, verified badge, institutional markers) within short time window. Baseline expected rate of such changes and alert on >2-3 sigma elevation.

suggestion.title: Support Chatbot Session to Account Access Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain is explicit: chatbot interaction → password reset → account hijack. Pipeline missed the temporal sequence connecting support interface to unauthorized access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Instagram support chatbot session logs with subsequent account access attempts. Flag instances where account access from new location/device occurs within hours of successful password-reset request issued by support bot, with no intermediate 2FA challenge.

suggestion.title: OG Handle Account Compromise Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Attackers specifically targeted 'OG Instagram handles' listed for resale—a high-value targeted campaign pattern. Pipeline lacked detection for account targeting based on metadata.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify attempts to enumerate or access high-value accounts (OG handles with <5 character usernames, verified badges, high follower counts, dormant high-traffic accounts). Alert on successive password reset/2FA disable requests targeting accounts matching these criteria.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Accessibility Service Binding by Non-System Apps
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malware 'abuses Accessibility Service to control devices.' This is the core privilege escalation and persistence mechanism. Pipeline omitted any hunt for this signature Android attack pattern despite being the headline attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for non-system packages requesting or enabling BIND_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE permission. Alert on accessibility service callbacks from apps installed outside Play Store in preceding 48 hours. Correlate with suspicious app package names and network C2 beaconing to bitlrewards-app.com or 199.217.99.122.

suggestion.title: Overlay Window Injection Targeting Banking Apps
suggestion.rationale: Banking trojans capture credentials via overlay windows. Article describes credential and financial data targeting but pipeline generated zero overlay-specific detections despite this being the attack's actual theft mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect apps drawing TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY windows that are not Play Store verified, not allowlisted, and correlate with timing of known banking app foreground state. Alert if overlay appears/disappears synchronously with credential entry patterns or banking app focus events.

suggestion.title: Non-Banking App Querying Banking App Packages
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware targets specific 'banking credentials, financial data, and cryptocurrency accounts.' Pipeline missed detection for app-to-app enumeration and espionage of high-value financial app packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for apps without banking permission contexts (package names outside financial/payments categories) querying PackageManager for banking app package existence, attempting intent resolution to banking apps, or reading accessibility cache after banking app foreground event.

suggestion.title: Installation of APK from Malicious Link Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'spreads through malicious links disguised as downloads from trusted, well-known applications.' Pipeline mapped zero initial-access detections for the infection vector itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate DNS queries or HTTP requests to bitlrewards-app.com and 199.217.99.122 with subsequent .apk file creation and installation events on same device within 5 minutes. Alert on .apk files downloaded via these C2 domains and installed via non-Play-Store mechanisms.

suggestion.title: Credential Logging Correlated with Banking App Focus
suggestion.rationale: Trojans must actively log credentials during banking sessions. Article implies real-time credential capture but pipeline generated no collection-phase detection for keystroke or accessibility-tree logging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag apps with accessibility service enabled that read from accessibility event cache, instantiate InputMethodManager, or read from process memory within 500ms of banking app coming to foreground. Correlate with outbound network activity to C2 domain/IP within 10 seconds of credential entry windows.

suggestion.title: Reflection-Based Code Injection and Dex Loading
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1027 (Obfuscated Files) implying runtime evasion. Pipeline generated no detection for reflection, dex injection, or memory-resident code tampering—hallmarks of sophisticated Android trojans.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for reflection-based method invocation (java.lang.reflect.*) from non-dev apps, in-memory dex class loading (DexClassLoader, InMemoryDexClassLoader) post-installation, or process memory modifications. Alert on unsigned APKs with base64-encoded or zlib-compressed payloads in dex bytecode.

suggestion.title: Dragon Weave C2 Beaconing & Network Callbacks
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly establishes active attacks; APT campaigns require command & control. Pipeline missed entirely. Article phrase: 'China-Aligned Groups Ramp Up Attacks'—implies ongoing operations with infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries and network connections to known Dragon Weave C2 nodes. Alert on repetitive beacon traffic from Czech or Taiwan networks at non-standard intervals; cross-check against threat feeds for actor infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Phishing / Initial Access from Dragon Weave
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies nation-state targeting of Czech Republic & Taiwan—initial compromise prerequisite. No phishing/malware delivery UC generated. Standard for APT actor operational pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails with Dragon Weave-linked sender patterns, malicious attachments, or embedded links to known malicious domains. Prioritize government entity recipients in Czech Republic and Taiwan.

suggestion.title: Data Staging and Exfiltration to Attacker Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Nation-state intelligence-gathering campaign (implied by 'attacks' on Czech Republic & Taiwan); exfiltration phase absent from pipeline output. Article phrase: 'China-Aligned Groups Ramp Up Attacks'—targets are intelligence-valuable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk data transfers to non-whitelisted IP space, particularly ASNs linked to China-aligned infrastructure. Alert on archive creation and encryption followed by network egress on non-standard ports.

suggestion.title: Living-off-the-Land Execution by Dragon Weave
suggestion.rationale: APT groups targeting government networks typically employ LOLBins to evade detection; no execution or defense-evasion UC produced. Missing from pipeline entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal PowerShell or cmd.exe execution from non-admin users in government environments. Alert on suspicious .NET reflection, DLL side-loading, or rundll32 calls tied to attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: CVE-2024-21182 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CVE-2024-21182 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt'; this is the primary detection vector for the KEV.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2024-21182 detections on Oracle WebLogic Server. Prioritize by asset criticality and network exposure. Federal patch due 2026-06-04 provides compliance deadline.

suggestion.title: T3/IIOP Protocol Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated attacker with network access via T3, IIOP'—exploit payloads transit these specific protocols; network signatures are viable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor T3 (ports 7001/7002) and IIOP (port 3700) inbound traffic to WebLogic instances. Establish baseline of legitimate traffic and alert on exploit signatures or anomalous patterns.

suggestion.title: WebLogic Server Network Exposure Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'patch lag is the silent killer' and recommends asset-exposure hunting; any internet-facing WebLogic Server is immediately exploitable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Oracle WebLogic Server instances reachable from the network perimeter (external port scans on 7001/7002/3700). Cross-reference with patch-compliance status to identify unpatched systems.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Data Exfiltration from WebLogic
suggestion.rationale: Article states successful exploitation 'can result in unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle WebLogic Server accessible data'—monitor for the impact phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WebLogic application logs for atypical bulk data queries, unusual user account access, and large data transfers. Correlate with network exfiltration signatures to detect data moving out of the application tier.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Deadline Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-04' (2 days from publication); narrow window; track deployment status operationally.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Automated scan: flag all WebLogic Server instances without CVE-2024-21182 patches applied by 2026-06-04. Report non-compliance to management and audit teams. Escalate unpatched critical systems.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes Secrets Accessed from Pod
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'poisoning a Docker Hub repository to later steal Kubernetes secrets and other sensitive data.' Pipeline missed detection of unauthorized secret extraction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Kubernetes API calls to list/get secrets from compromised pod service account. Correlate with unexpected outbound connections from pod namespace. Baseline service-account token usage per workload and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Container Escape via CAP_SYS_ADMIN Capability Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists 'CAP_SYS_ADMIN' as a vector in container-escape section. Pipeline ignored containerization-misconfig attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect containers launched with CAP_SYS_ADMIN or other privileged capabilities (CAP_SYS_MODULE, CAP_SYS_PTRACE, CAP_NET_ADMIN). Correlate with process execution involving kernel module loading, process injection, or namespace manipulation from container PID.

suggestion.title: Malicious Stealer Execution During Container Build/Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'stealer that was loaded during the KICS scanning process.' Pipeline missed detection of supply-chain payload execution within trusted build tools.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned by known scanning tools (KICS, container registries) or build stages. Flag exfiltration-pattern outbound connections (DNS queries, HTTP POSTs to external IPs) from container runtime.

suggestion.title: Docker Hub Repository Poisoning via Image Manifest Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'poisoning a Docker Hub repository to later steal Kubernetes secrets.' Pipeline ignored supply-chain detection for registry manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect image pushes from unusual accounts/IPs to shared registries. Alert on container-image hash mismatches vs. signed digest. Flag pulls of images with known backdoor signatures or behavioral anomalies from static analysis.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes Orchestration API Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'Exploitation of orchestration APIs' as primary vector but provides no coverage. Pipeline missed API-abuse detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual kubectl/Kubernetes API calls (create deployment, patch RBAC, exec into pod, get secrets) from service account tokens or user accounts. Correlate with changes to pod security policies or network policies.

suggestion.title: CAP_SYS_PTRACE Process Injection from Container
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'CAP_SYS_PTRACE' in container-escape section. Pipeline missed specific capability-based lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect containers with CAP_SYS_PTRACE capability spawning process-tracing syscalls (ptrace, process_vm_readv) targeting host PID namespace. Flag context switches to host namespace from container context.

suggestion.title: Asset exposure — Magento systems running vulnerable Mirasvit Cache Warmer
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'widely used' plugin affecting 'thousands of Magento' installations. Pipeline's own recommendations section explicitly names 'Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)' with template reference, yet zero use cases instantiated. This is the foundational recon-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Magento installations running Mirasvit Cache Warmer versions prior to security patch. Detection via vulnerability scanning data, plugin manifest inspection, file-system presence checks for vulnerable plugin directories, or version string analysis.

suggestion.title: PHP object injection exploitation attempt against cache warmer
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies the attack vector as 'unauthenticated PHP object injection flaw'. This is the direct exploitation mechanism and should generate detection for HTTP requests containing serialized PHP payloads targeting the plugin.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Mirasvit Cache Warmer endpoints for PHP serialization patterns (objects prefixed with O:, arrays with a:, or base64-encoded serialized data). Flag unauthenticated requests containing such patterns as exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated RCE abuse via cache plugin endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'no login, configuration changes, or admin access required' for exploitation. This access control bypass is the critical attack element and must be detected when code execution occurs without credential validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on requests to cache plugin endpoints (typical paths /mirasvit/*, /cache/*, /magento/cache/*) with code injection characteristics originating from unauthenticated sessions. Correlate repeated attempts from single IP as mass exploitation scanning.

suggestion.title: WordPress Admin Account Creation via Plugin Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'Actively Exploited to Create Admin Accounts.' This is the primary attack outcome; requires real-time detection of admin user creation outside normal administrative workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress user creation/modification events for new administrator-role accounts. Correlate timing and source with WP Maps Pro plugin requests in web logs. Alert on admin capability grants from non-administrative or unauthenticated origins.

suggestion.title: WP Maps Pro Vulnerability Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Critical WP Maps Pro Flaw.' Pipeline must detect exploitation attempts at initial access phase before persistence is established.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP requests to WP Maps Pro plugin endpoints (/wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/) with payloads indicative of code injection, parameter tampering, or unauthenticated function calls. Flag requests with suspicious query parameters or POST bodies.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable WP Maps Pro Version Inventory and Alerting
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies specific vulnerability in WP Maps Pro. Continuous inventory of plugin versions and detection of unpatched installations is foundational.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Periodically scan WordPress instances for WP Maps Pro plugin presence and version. Alert on vulnerable versions (specific version threshold to be determined from CVE). Track plugin update/activation events.

suggestion.title: Suspicious User Role or Capability Modification
suggestion.rationale: Adjacent to admin creation, attackers may escalate existing user privileges. Article emphasizes admin account persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on WordPress role changes, capability additions, or user metadata modifications (set_user_role, add_user_cap hooks). Correlate with plugin vulnerability exploitation timeframe and non-standard admin sources.

suggestion.title: High-Volume Failed Logins: Brute-Force Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'brute-force attacks that attempted logins from distant locations' and 'trying multiple passwords in succession until the correct one is found.' This is explicit T1110.001.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a single cloud account experiences 10+ failed login attempts within 15 minutes, or 25+ failures within 1 hour, especially from distinct source IPs. Dashlane should emit failed authentication events; correlate with upstream IdP logs (if any) to catch the full attack window before account lockout fires.

suggestion.title: Geographic Anomaly: Auth Attempts from Rare/Distant Countries
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'brute-force attacks...from distant locations and unknown devices' and 'received notices of suspicious access requests from foreign countries.' Establishes geographic outlier as primary signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain per-user baseline of known login countries (from device registration history or previous successful logins). Alert on login attempts from countries/regions absent from baseline, especially within 24 hours of account creation. Combine with IP geolocation enrichment and flag attempts from countries with high brute-force activity.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Device Registration Following Auth Failure Spike
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'emails contained verification codes for legitimate account owners to register new devices' and 'suspicious access requests' triggered verification flows. Device add events correlate with failed auth.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed-login events with new device/session registration or MFA enrollment on the same account.
