suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration from Finance Ministry Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates breach of government finance entity; no exfiltration-phase detection or IOC extraction for data staging, compression, or C2 upload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for compression or archiving utilities (WinRAR, 7zip) spawned by suspicious processes. Alert on large file transfers to external IPs or known Xeno RAT C2 nodes, or unusual HTTP POST traffic with large payloads.

suggestion.title: Malicious Maven Dependency jqwik-engine 1.10.0 Resolution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies compromised artifact: 'Package: net.jqwik:jqwik-engine Affected version: 1.10.0' as the attack vector. Pipeline extracted zero package-level IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Maven Central or internal repository resolution of net.jqwik:jqwik-engine at exactly version 1.10.0. Check build tool logs (mvn, gradle, Bazel) for this specific coordinate. Correlate with projects updating dependencies in late May 2026.

suggestion.title: ANSI Escape Obfuscation in Build/Test Output Streams
suggestion.rationale: Article describes evasion: 'prints ESC [2K followed by a carriage return, twice... [2K means erase the entire current line.' The ANSI escape byte sequence 0x1B[2K is the obfuscation IOC. Pipeline missed defense-evasion pattern entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search raw (non-rendered) build and test logs for the hex pattern 0x1B5B324B followed by 0x0D (ESC[2K + CR). Flag test summaries containing ANSI control bytes that would be invisible on an interactive terminal but persist in stored logs.

suggestion.title: Prompt Injection Payload in Dependency Test Output
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies payload: 'The payload told agents to disregard previous instructions and delete all jqwik tests and code' and instructs: 'Grep your CI and IDE logs for the phrase about disregarding instructions and deleting jqwik tests and code.' Exact text IOC for detection in logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search test and build output for phrases matching 'disregard previous instructions' or 'delete.*jqwik' in suspicious context. Correlate presence of these strings in Maven/Gradle output with recent jqwik dependency changes. Alert if such text appears in logs fed to agentic tools.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Agent-Targeting Method in Dependency Code
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies attack vector by method signature: 'The malicious instruction lived in a new method called printMessageForCodingAgents() inside the net.jqwik.engine.execution.JqwikExecutor class. The method name tells you the intent on its own.' Pipeline missed code-level IOC extraction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: During SCA scanning, flag dependencies containing methods with names explicitly targeting agents (printMessageForCodingAgents, instructAgent, agentPayload, etc.) combined with print/output operations. Decompile resolved JARs and audit method names for agent-specific logic.

suggestion.title: Rapid Dependency Version Increment Following Malicious Release
suggestion.rationale: Article documents remediation: 'May 25, 2026: Version 1.10.0 lands on Maven Central... Shortly after: Version 1.10.1 ships. The directive gets softened.' Malicious version → patch version transition is a detectable supply-chain signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor jqwik version usage patterns for transitions from 1.10.0 to 1.10.1 within 2 days of May 25, 2026. Detect rapid version pins or overrides of 1.10.0 in lock files. Alert on projects explicitly downgrading from 1.10.0 with commits citing 'malware' or 'injection'.

suggestion.title: AI Agent Detection and Refusal of Tool Output Prompt Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article documents defensive detection: 'Claude Code flagged the instruction on the first mvn test run, refused to act on it, and traced it back to its source in the JAR.' Agent-level refusal is a positive detection signal worth monitoring as evidence of attempted compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor agentic coding tool logs for refusal/alert events triggered during dependency testing or tool output parsing. Alert on agents that detect and reject prompt-injection-like directives in test output. Correlate such refusals with jqwik or similar library execution in the same session.

suggestion.title: npm preinstall hook execution from package.json
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'fire via a preinstall hook on every npm install.' No detection exists for preinstall script invocation itself—the primary attack vector. Need to detect when node/npm executes embedded preinstall scripts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for node/npm child processes executing scripts from node_modules/.bin, .hooks/, or generated by npm lifecycle hooks. Look for process parents of node pointing to package.json preinstall script invocation during npm install. Correlate with package installation timing.

suggestion.title: Credential provider access from npm/node context
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'credential harvester that targets GitHub Actions secrets, AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, HashiCorp Vault, npm tokens, and CircleCI.' No detection covers the actual credential harvesting behavior. Need hunts for file access to .env, config files, kubeconfig, AWS credentials, etc.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm/node processes accessing credential stores: ~/.aws, ~/.kube, ~/.vault, ~/.docker, .env files, GitHub Actions runner env vars, Azure metadata endpoints, GCP metadata service. Elevated access to /var/run/secrets (K8s mounts) or environment variable reads for CI tokens.

suggestion.title: Data exfiltration from npm/node to external C2
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'multi-stage credential harvester' implies credential exfiltration after collection. Pipeline detects installation and execution but not the command-and-control phase where stolen credentials are sent to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate node/npm processes that accessed credential files with subsequent network egress to non-standard ports or suspicious domains. Monitor for DNS queries from npm install phase contexts. Detect HTTPS POST/PUT to uncommon destinations carrying base64/encoded credential payloads.

suggestion.title: Suspicious package.json manifest with preinstall script
suggestion.rationale: Article: malicious 'preinstall hook on every npm install.' Artifact-level detection for package.json containing preinstall scripts that invoke obfuscated or network-calling code should precede execution detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse package.json from @redhat-cloud-services scope downloaded during npm install. Flag if preinstall script contains: shell metacharacters (|, >, $), network calls (curl, wget, curl), base64/encoding functions, or file write operations to /tmp. Compare against known-good baseline.

suggestion.title: Multi-cloud metadata API queries from build/CI contexts
suggestion.rationale: Article: targets 'AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes' credentials. Instance metadata API requests from npm/node in CI environment (GitHub Actions runners, build agents) are high-signal indicators of credential harvesting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to 169.254.169.254 (AWS), metadata.google.internal (GCP), or Azure Instance Metadata Service from npm/node processes. Correlate with CI/CD runner environment. Flag if multiple cloud provider metadata endpoints are queried within single npm install session.

suggestion.title: npm token exfiltration via process environment or .npmrc access
suggestion.rationale: Article: harvester targets 'npm tokens.' No specific detection for npm authentication token theft from .npmrc, environment variables, or npm auth cache.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm/node processes reading ~/.npmrc, .npm folder, or accessing npm_token* environment variables. Flag if followed by process spawning curl/wget or opening network sockets. Detect environment variable exfiltration via process command line inspection.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Installation with Post-Install Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly discusses 'payload' and supply chain attacks via npm packages. Post-install scripts are standard npm attack vector for initial code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm process spawning unexpected child processes (especially curl, powershell, bash) immediately after package install. Alert on npm registry requests to typosquat or homograph domains. Baseline legitimate post-install activity and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via npm Environment Variable Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Keywords cite 'credential harvesting' as attack vector. npm build/install context has access to CI/CD secrets (GitHub tokens, AWS keys, NPM_TOKEN) via environment variables.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm/node processes reading sensitive env vars (GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_KEY, NPM_TOKEN) and transmitting to external IPs. Monitor for unusual HTTP(S) exfiltration patterns from CI environments during build/test phases.

suggestion.title: Wormable npm Malware Self-Propagation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly mentions 'wormable malware' and keywords include 'worm propagation.' This indicates automated lateral spread via package dependencies or automated publishing to npm registry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid, automated npm package publishing from compromised dev machines. Alert on npm processes initiating lateral connections to other dev machines or CI runners. Detect recursive dependency injection patterns suggesting worm-like propagation.

suggestion.title: CI/CD Pipeline Persistence via npm Dependency Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses 'multi-stage attacks' and supply chain persistence. npm attacks commonly establish persistence in CI/CD by hijacking dependency resolution or inject malicious transitive dependencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected changes to package.json/package-lock.json targeting lower-risk packages (dev dependencies, utilities). Monitor CI/CD agents for execution of code from unexpected package versions. Baseline npm dependency trees and flag new transitive dependencies.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Payload Detection in npm Package Source Code
suggestion.rationale: Keywords include 'obfuscation' and 'payload.' Malicious npm packages typically use code obfuscation, encoding, or dynamic evaluation to evade static analysis and SBOM tools.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan npm package source for high-entropy base64 blobs, eval()/Function() calls, atob() patterns, and minified/uglified code in non-dist directories. Flag packages with disparity between declared functionality and actual bytecode behavior.

suggestion.title: GitHub Account Takeover and Malicious Package Release
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights GitHub as attack surface. Compromised maintainer accounts are primary npm attack vector; keywords explicitly mention GitHub.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for GitHub account logins from anomalous geographies/IPs for npm maintainers. Alert on npm package version bumps immediately following suspicious GitHub login. Cross-reference GitHub Actions suspicious secret access with npm publish events.

suggestion.title: Device Code Phishing OAuth Flow Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly notes device code phishing has 'surged from a research curiosity to an industrialized PhaaS offering, with more than 18 kits being actively tracked in the wild' and describes it as bypassing MFA and passkeys entirely. No detection UC created despite this being an active, quantified threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for device code authentication flows completing without user interaction on the registered device, device codes exchanged by non-official Microsoft endpoints, or device code tokens minted from suspicious geolocations. Alert on successful MFA/passkey bypasses through device flow authentication.

suggestion.title: AitM and Device Code Kit Platform Convergence
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'As AitM and device code kits converge into single platforms, we're seeing signs of heavy AI use' indicating joint proxy infrastructure + OAuth theft. Observable through session interception patterns and token exfiltration, but no UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect browsers or processes establishing multiple HTTPS connections to hosting provider infrastructure with same SNI in minutes, or session tokens replayed from non-standard geolocations within minutes of initial login event, indicating active session theft.

suggestion.title: LLMShare Malvertising Link Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article describes new attack vector: 'attackers host malicious links via legitimate AI chat sharing functionality' and 'LLMshare campaign used legitimate chatgpt.com sharing links, creating a convincing ad that is impossible to spot from just looking at the URL.' No detection UC despite named, active campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on clicks from search engine result ads pointing to legitimate chatgpt.com/share/*, claude.ai/share/*, or similar AI platform share URLs where final redirect lands on phishing infrastructure. Flag ads with homoglyph or typosquat domains.

suggestion.title: Rapid Phishing Domain Rotation Clustering
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes pattern: 'According to Spamhaus, 89% of phishing domains are active for fewer than two days' making blocklist defenses ineffective. Pattern-based detection missing despite being quantified and systemic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cluster domains registering within 24-hour windows with identical homoglyph/typosquat patterns, identical hosting ASN, or identical phishing page HTML fingerprints. Alert on infrastructure reusing the same IP/ASN across 5+ phishing domains in <48 hours.

suggestion.title: Unapproved AI OAuth Integration from Shadow Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies shadow AI adoption risk: '67% using non-corporate accounts... AI agents are requesting OAuth permissions' and average org has '17 AI-connected OAuth integrations — most of them unapproved.' Zero detection UCs despite being quantified and data-exfiltration-enabling.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on OAuth consent grants from personal Microsoft/Google accounts to ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, or other consumer AI applications. Flag consent events with broad scopes (mail.read, files.read, calendars.read, user.read.all) to non-corporate OAuth apps.

suggestion.title: AI Browser Extension Sensitive Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'AI browser extensions collect browsing context from internal applications, creating a data exfiltration path that operates outside traditional DLP' with '17 AI browser extensions...most of them unapproved.' Observable exfiltration pattern completely missed by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor browser extension network traffic for exfiltration of clipboard contents, authentication tokens, or internal application DOM/page source to external cloud AI service IPs. Flag extensions accessing *.internal, *.corp, or intranet domains with subsequent HTTPS egress to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or Microsoft cloud IPs.

suggestion.title: Malware Parsing Steam Profile Comments for Commands
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'hiding command instructions inside Steam Community profile comments.' Pipeline missed detection for steganographic command channel. This is T1001.003 (Steganography) + T1140 (Deobfuscation).

Monitor for regex operations, base64 decoding, or string extraction post-HTTP response. Flag unusual comment-section access patterns.

suggestion.title: Network Connections to Malware C2 Domain (hello-mywordl.info)

suggestion.title: Suspicious Access to Attacker-Controlled Steam Profiles

suggestion.title: WordPress Process Executing Unexpected Outbound Network Connections
suggestion.rationale: Malware running in WordPress context (httpd/nginx) making connections to external C2. Pipeline should detect anomalous egress from web server processes.

suggestion.title: WordPress Site Compromise / Malware Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'targeting WordPress websites' and malware infection but pipeline extracted no initial-access or execution-phase detections.

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound traffic from Czech and Taiwan networks for beaconing patterns, DNS exfiltration, HTTP/HTTPS callbacks to known malicious infrastructure, or anomalous connection intervals consistent with automated C2.

suggestion.title: Dragon Weave Initial Access & Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article headline describes active 'attacks' against Czech and Taiwan but zero initial-access or exploitation indicators were extracted. This is the foundational phase of any intrusion chain.

suggestion.title: Dragon Weave Post-Compromise Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Multi-country, multi-target attacks imply sustained persistence and internal network movement. Zero lateral-movement or persistence detections provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for RDP/SMB abuse, unusual service account activity, Kerberos ticket anomalies, inter-host scanning, and lateral tool deployment consistent with post-breach movement across Czech and Taiwan networks.

suggestion.title: Exposed WebLogic Server Detection via T3 Protocol
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers compromise WebLogic 'via T3, IIOP'—these are the primary network-facing attack vectors for unauthenticated exploitation. Default ports 7001 (T3) and 7002 (IIOP) are key IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound T3 protocol traffic (default port 7001) or IIOP traffic (port 7002) to internal WebLogic instances from untrusted external sources. Flag repeated probes or successful connections that precede exploitation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2024-21182 Vulnerability Scan Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CVE-2024-21182 as the specific vulnerability in CISA KEV with federal patch due-date 2026-06-04. Organizations must alert on scanner detections of this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner results reporting CVE-2024-21182 on WebLogic Server instances. Cross-reference patch dates against the federal remediation deadline; unpatched instances post-deadline represent critical exposure.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated WebLogic Exploitation Attempt

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for WebLogic logs showing inbound T3/IIOP connections immediately followed by error logs or unexpected command execution, without any preceding authentication or session-creation events.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Critical Data Access Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states successful exploitation enables 'complete access to all Oracle WebLogic Server accessible data'—hunt for anomalous data reads and exfiltration patterns post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify anomalous database queries or reads via compromised WebLogic accounts accessing sensitive tables, combined with egress of unusual data volumes to external IPs or cloud storage.

suggestion.title: WebLogic Java Process Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Impact statement ('complete access') implies remote code execution capability. Monitor for child processes spawned by WebLogic java.exe with unexpected privileges or shell invocation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag child processes spawned by java.exe (WebLogic process) including cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or network utilities (curl, certutil, wget). Correlate with unusual WebLogic error logs or deployments.

suggestion.title: WebLogic JSP/WAR Deployment Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: RCE exploitation of WebLogic often culminates in malicious WAR/JSP deployment. Hunt for unexpected application deployments or file writes to WebLogic directories during or after exploitation window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WebLogic deployment directories for unexpected WAR/EAR/JSP uploads or modifications during or immediately after detected exploitation attempts. Cross-reference with absence of legitimate deployment requests.

suggestion.title: Poisoned Container Image Distribution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'poisoning a Docker Hub repository to later steal Kubernetes secrets and other sensitive data' with 'stealer loaded during the KICS scanning process'—explicit supply chain attack. No detection rules generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor container registry push events for images with unexpected modifications, manifest digest changes, or pushes from anomalous accounts. Correlate image pull events with known-malicious scanning tool execution (KICS). Alert on images where content scanners detect embedded credential stealers or reconnaissance code in layers.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes Secrets Theft via Container Process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack chain 'steal Kubernetes secrets and other sensitive data' following container compromise. No detection for secret enumeration or exfiltration from containers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on container processes reading /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ (especially token), followed by outbound network connections. Monitor for env-var enumeration or grep-like operations against mounted secrets. Track suspicious service account token usage in Kubernetes API audit logs (bulk secret list, cross-namespace access).

suggestion.title: Privileged Capability Abuse for Container Escape
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE, CAP_SYS_PTRACE, CAP_NET_ADMIN under 'Container escape' section. No detections for malicious capability usage patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when containers with privileged capabilities execute dangerous syscalls: CAP_SYS_ADMIN + bpf/ptrace/mount/kexec, CAP_SYS_MODULE + insmod/rmmod, CAP_NET_ADMIN + network namespace manipulation. Flag any capability inheritance mismatches between workload policy and runtime execution.

suggestion.title: Orchestration API Abuse from Compromised Workload
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'exploitation of orchestration APIs' and scenarios where container compromise leads to API credential theft. No detection for abnormal API usage patterns post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Kubernetes API audit logs for service account tokens making bulk list/get requests across secrets, configmaps, or role bindings. Alert on API calls from service accounts originating from pod IPs not matching expected deployments. Flag authentication failures followed by privilege escalation attempts.

suggestion.title: Container Runtime Supply Chain Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'exploiting host system vulnerabilities and container runtime components' as attack path. No detection for runtime binary tampering or malicious hook installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /var/lib/docker, /var/lib/containerd, and runtime socket directories for unexpected binary modifications or injected shared objects. Alert on container runtime daemons executing unusual child processes or accessing unexpected device files. Track docker.sock abuse from containers (direct image pull/push, network policy changes).

suggestion.title: WordPress Admin Account Creation via Plugin Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'actively exploited to create admin accounts' — a core persistence and privilege escalation indicator. Pipeline produced zero use cases for this attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress user creation events (wp_users table INSERT records, wp_create_user() function calls) for new admin-role accounts created outside normal administrative windows. Correlate with HTTP requests to known WP Maps Pro plugin endpoints (wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/). Alert on successful user creation immediately following failed authentication attempts or unusual HTTP patterns.

suggestion.title: WP Maps Pro Plugin Endpoint Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Critical vulnerability in specific plugin. Title references active exploitation but no IOC or endpoint-level detection suggested. Article should contain specific vulnerable endpoint paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block/alert on HTTP requests matching WP Maps Pro plugin paths (wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/ and subdirectories) with POST requests containing user/admin creation payloads. Detect parameter fuzzing or unusual query strings targeting known vulnerable endpoints.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via User Role Modification
suggestion.rationale: Admin account creation IS privilege escalation. The article title describes the end goal of the exploit, yet kill chain contains no privilege_escalation phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor wp_usermeta table for role changes from subscriber/contributor to administrator (wp_capabilities field updates). Alert on any role escalation for accounts created within the last 24 hours. Cross-reference with plugin error logs for exploitation signatures.

suggestion.title: WordPress Plugin Vulnerability HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is exploited via HTTP—likely GET/POST requests to the plugin. No detection hypothesis provided for identifying malicious request patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP 200/302 responses following requests to wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/ containing exploitation payloads or user creation parameters. Baseline normal plugin traffic and detect anomalous request patterns (unusual User-Agent, source country misalignment, off-hours requests).

suggestion.title: Failed-to-Successful Login Sequence Before Admin Creation
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation likely involves reconnaissance and authentication attempts before successful compromise. Pipeline should detect pre-exploitation footprinting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed WordPress login attempts from a single source with a subsequent successful admin account creation event within 15 minutes. Flag accounts created by users with < 5 prior successful logins or from geographies not in the organization's baseline.

suggestion.title: Suspicious WordPress Database Modifications
suggestion.rationale: Admin account creation modifies wp_users and wp_usermeta tables. Direct database access or ORM exploitation should trigger detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress database for INSERT operations on wp_users or wp_usermeta tables originating from non-admin database users or from application layer (wp-config.php queries). Alert on rapid multi-row modifications to wp_capabilities, wp_user_roles, or user meta fields.

suggestion.title: Failed Authentication Rate Spike — Brute Force Attack
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'brute-force attacks that attempted logins from distant locations and unknown devices'—core T1110 behavior: multiple failed password attempts in rapid succession against target accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on accounts receiving >N failed login attempts within time window T. Enumerate distinct source IPs; baseline per account and flag statistical anomalies. Variant: failed attempts clustered by time but dispersed by geography.

suggestion.title: Account Lockout Correlated With Failed Authentication Spike
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'resulting in the suspension of those accounts as part of Dashlane's built-in security controls.' Lockout events must correlate with preceding failed auth attempts to establish brute-force cause.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate account lockout events backwards to failed authentication logs within preceding 10-minute window. Surface lockouts preceded by >10 failed attempts; score by geographic scatter of source IPs.

suggestion.title: Device Registration Attempt From Unrecognized Location After Failed Auth
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'emails contained verification codes for legitimate account owners to register new devices' following brute-force attempts—indicates attacker persistence attempt or account compromise assessment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new device registration events where source location differs from user baseline and registration occurs <1 hour after account lockout or failed auth spike. Flag registrations from countries not in user's historical location set.

suggestion.title: Verification Code Email Generation Spike Per Account
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Multiple Dashlane users...received notices of suspicious access requests from foreign countries'—each brute-force attempt triggers verification email; spike indicates automated attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor email service logs for verification/MFA challenge sending rate per account. Alert when single account receives >N verification emails within 15-minute window; enrich with associated authentication attempt logs.

suggestion.title: Impossible Travel — Login Attempts From Geographically Scattered Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attempted logins from distant locations'—attackers using distributed proxy/botnet IPs. Same account receiving auth attempts from multiple continents in impossible timeframe.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: GeoIP-enrich login events per account. Flag when same account receives auth attempts from >2 distant geographies within 5 minutes. Whitelist known VPN/travel patterns; escalate novel geography combinations.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: Workspace membership list changes by newly granted owner
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker gaining owner role via membership injection. Post-exploitation impact includes 'now owner can perform admin actions'—need to detect rapid workspace configuration or member-list changes immediately after owner grant. Article does not specify which admin actions, but membership/role changes are high-fidelity signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate POST /workspaces/{id}/members (role=owner response 201) with subsequent GET/PUT to workspace configuration, member list, or role-change endpoints within 15 minutes from the same user/account. Flag if newly granted owner immediately enumerates or modifies other members.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: Failed login attempts before successful owner-account compromise
suggestion.rationale: Attacker must discover or guess the user_id to inject as owner (article states 'forwards the request body's user_id'). Article does not describe password-spraying or enumeration, but pre-compromise reconnaissance is implicit. Detect failed auth attempts followed by successful login from the same attacker IP.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track failed login attempts to praisonai-platform (invalid user, invalid password) from a source IP, followed within 1 hour by successful login as a different user. Escalate if that login IP later performs a POST /workspaces/*/members grant with role=owner.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: Workspace member count spike—mass role elevation
suggestion.rationale: Article vulnerability allows adding 'arbitrary user as owner'. Attacker could inject multiple users (not just one) to increase persistence or blast-radius. Article does not describe multi-user attacks, but the permission flaw is per-request; multiple requests compound the risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline workspace member count over 7 days. Alert if POST /workspaces/{id}/members succeeds 5+ times within 1 hour from the same source IP or user, particularly with role=owner or role=admin in request body.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: API token or session creation by low-privilege user followed by owner-role assumption
suggestion.rationale: Article assumes attacker is already a workspace member (require_workspace_member gate); method of member acquisition not specified. If membership is open-enrollment or unverified-invite, attacker joins first, then escalates. Detect fast token/session acquisition → immediate privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within same session or 10-minute window: user created, API token issued, workspace membership confirmed (role=member), then POST /workspaces/{id}/members with role=owner succeeds. Flag as suspicious privilege escalation chain.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: Asset exposure—CVE-2026-47413 inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article is a published CVE with GHSA advisory. Recon phase detects unpatched praisonai-platform instances. Article does not specify default ports/paths, but asset enumeration is early in kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for praisonai-platform in installed software inventory or running services (process name, http service banners, port 8000-8100 web app detection). Cross-check against CVE-2026-47413 patched-version list. Alert on unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: Suspicious JavaScript Injection via t.js Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'JavaScript injection following the t.js?site=<id> pattern' as a key fingerprint. This is a direct, observable web-layer indicator that should trigger detection when embedded in compromised sites or observed in web logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests for script injections matching the pattern t.js?site= with numeric or alphanumeric site identifiers. Look for inline script tags or external script tags loading from zTDS-owned domains. Correlate with traffic redirects to malware-delivery infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Fake Browser Update Prompts (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari, Opera, Brave, Yandex, Vivaldi)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'FakeUpdates lures contain bogus update notices for Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari, Opera, Brave, Yandex, Vivaldi, Samsung Internet, and UC Browser.' These prompts are visually detectable and often served from non-standard domains or localhost.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect fake update prompts by monitoring for suspicious download patterns: executables or ZIP archives with names containing 'update', 'browser', or version numbers originating from non-official update domains. Cross-reference domain reputation and SSL certificate issuer legitimacy.

suggestion.title: PowerShell Execution via ClickFix Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'ClickFix attacks involve PowerShell commands' that victims are tricked into copying and executing. Detection should focus on PowerShell spawned from user interaction contexts with suspicious encoded/obfuscated arguments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for powershell.exe spawned from user context (explorer.exe, browser processes, terminal) with encoded parameters (-EncodedCommand, -enc), downloaded content paths, or IEX/Invoke-Expression patterns. Correlate with recent clipboard operations or user interaction events.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Archive Extraction and Executable Launch
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'a fake Firefox update that downloaded a ZIP archive containing multiple DLLs and a malicious executable named Browser Update.exe.' This multi-stage pattern (ZIP → DLL + EXE) is anomalous and detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect archives downloaded from non-official sources followed by extraction and execution of binaries with benign-sounding names (e.g., 'Browser Update.exe', 'Security Check.exe'). Alert on ZIP/RAR extraction followed by executable launch within 1-2 seconds and from temp/download directories.

suggestion.title: Website Traffic Redirection via zTDS
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'DriveSurge hijacks thousands of legitimate, high-reputation websites and silently redirects visitors to malware' via zTDS. Detection on web servers should identify unexpected redirect rules or injected redirection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web servers for injection of redirect rules to unfamiliar domains, particularly those matching zTDS infrastructure signatures. Alert on HTTP 302/301 responses to domains not in baseline. Cross-reference redirected domains against threat intelligence feeds for known malware-delivery infrastructure.

suggestion.title: macOS Clipboard Hijacking via Obfuscated JavaScript
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'obfuscated JavaScript payload specifically designed to target macOS desktop systems, delivered via verification-themed ClickFix attacks that hijack the clipboard.' This is a platform-specific indicator absent from Windows-centric detection baselines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On macOS endpoints, monitor for JavaScript processes accessing clipboard (pasteboard) APIs with obfuscated or base64-encoded payloads. Alert on clipboard read/write patterns preceded by browser or verification-themed prompts, particularly from non-standard origins.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation from Untrusted Source
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack vector: 'Compromises Red Hat npm packages' — initial access occurs when developers or CI/CD systems install the malicious package from the registry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/require operations for packages with suspicious metadata (author account created <30 days ago, unusual download spikes, version number gaps). Correlate with known-bad package hashes or maintainer account takeovers. Flag installations outside normal development windows.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting by npm Package Process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'credential-stealing worm' — detection must identify the malware reading credential stores, environment variables, SSH keys, or API tokens after code execution within the package.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm/Node.js processes accessing credential file paths (.ssh/, .aws/, .kube/, browser credential stores, .env files). Alert on child process spawning from npm modules, especially shell invocations (cmd.exe, /bin/bash) for credential exfiltration.

suggestion.title: C2 Callback from npm Module Child Process
suggestion.rationale: Stolen credentials must be exfiltrated to attacker infrastructure. Detection captures outbound command-and-control traffic initiated by the compromised package's execution context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate npm/Node.js or child processes with outbound HTTPS/DNS to newly-registered domains, suspiciously-timed connections (off-hours for development), non-standard ports, or geolocations inconsistent with legitimate business operations.

suggestion.title: npm Registry Maintainer Account Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must gain control of package author accounts or exploit registry credentials to push malicious versions. Detection at auth layer catches compromise before package distribution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry authentication for: new login IP addresses for known maintainers, password reset events, MFA bypass or disable operations, and batch package uploads within short timeframes or from unexpected geolocations.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Metadata Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Before widespread installation, malicious packages exhibit observable registry-level anomalies: dependency injection, size changes, author field modifications in patched versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm packages with: unusual new dependencies (especially network/crypto libraries), file size deltas >20% in minor/patch versions, author or repository URL changes post-publication, or modifications to package.json timestamps suggesting republication.

suggestion.title: npm preinstall script execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'preinstall scripts automatically during npm install, before any of your own code executes'—primary execution vector. Requires process telemetry to detect node children spawned by npm with unusual command lines or credential file access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for node.exe or node processes spawned as children of npm during package installation. Correlate with subsequent file I/O to ~/.npmrc, ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, or CI/CD credential directories and environment variable reads.

suggestion.title: GitHub OIDC token request in Actions workflow
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'commits added a minimal GitHub Actions workflow that: Triggered on push to any branch. Requested a GitHub OIDC identity token via id-token: write'—ingress point for package publishing exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GitHub Actions workflows with id-token: write permissions in newly-modified workflows triggering on any branch. Correlate with subsequent npm publish commands or npm_token environment variable usage.

suggestion.title: Environment and CI credential harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Harvests secrets and credentials from the local environment and CI context: environment variables, ~/.npmrc tokens, SSH keys, GitHub tokens, and CI/CD secrets'—requires file access and env var monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file access to ~/.npmrc, ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.kube, or CI/CD secret directories by node processes. Detect reads of sensitive env vars (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, GITHUB_TOKEN, GCP_KEY, AZURE_CREDENTIALS) by unexpected processes.

suggestion.title: Cloud identity enumeration (GCP/Azure)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'pair of new collectors for GCP and Azure that enumerate every identity the infected host can assume'—novel variant capability detectable via CLI process creation and cloud audit logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for gcloud, az, or gsutil CLI invocations enumerating service accounts, IAM roles, or identity bindings from anomalous contexts (npm install, build agents). Correlate with preinstall script execution timing.

suggestion.title: Package republication with payload propagation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'queries the registry for other packages the compromised identity can publish and republishes them, carrying the same payload'—worm lateral movement via supply chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry audit logs for unexpected republications by legitimate maintainers, especially rapid burst patterns. Correlate with preinstall script additions, new dependencies, or bundle size increases in otherwise stable packages.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated JavaScript eval() chains in preinstall hooks
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unusually large, heavily obfuscated JavaScript file. The author relied on eval() and ROT-based string decoding'—defense evasion signature detectable in package manifest analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan npm package preinstall scripts for obfuscation: multiple eval() calls, ROT cipher patterns, high-entropy strings, or multi-stage decoding chains. Flag preinstall scripts >10KB or with low code coverage.

suggestion.title: Cobalt Strike Beacon Masquerading as Legitimate Web Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'Cobalt Strike profiles designed to make beacon traffic resemble legitimate web requests.' Core C2 evasion requiring detection of beacon patterns hidden within HTTP normality.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTP/HTTPS traffic exhibiting beacon hallmarks (fixed intervals, fixed payload sizes, encoded response body, atypical User-Agents, communication to content-delivery infrastructure). Correlate with Cobalt Strike JARM/JA3 signatures and process context (unexpected child processes from cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe).

suggestion.title: Telegram Bot API C2 Channel Establishment
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Telegram bot API–based external command and control (C2) mechanism that routed communication through Telegram's infrastructure.' Explicit use of messaging API for C2, bypassing traditional C2 network signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify processes initiating connections to api.telegram.org with bot token patterns, or spawning with Telegram library imports. Monitor for sustained or automated bot interactions; flag processes with no legitimate reason to contact messaging APIs (non-browser, non-messaging-app binaries).

suggestion.title: Automated Active Directory Discovery via Iterative Agent-Driven Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'automated Active Directory (AD) discovery panel' with 'collecting observations from completed tasks and selecting the next action from predefined choices.' Systematic, iterative LDAP/WMI enumeration driven by automation logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid LDAP queries with evolving filter parameters (suggesting iterative refinement), Get-ADUser/Get-ADComputer chains enumerating organizational structure, or LDAP user/computer enumeration from unusual processes. Alert on automated discovery: multiple queries from single process/user within minutes with changing search parameters.

suggestion.title: Multi-Layer Payload Encryption and Runtime Deobfuscation
suggestion.rationale: Core capability: 'wraps a raw payload in layers of encryption, evasion, and alternative execution techniques, producing custom-built executables or DLLs.' 80+ modules with runtime decryption for EDR bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for executables with abnormal entropy (indicating encryption), embedded decryption keys in .data/.text sections, or runtime deobfuscation via ROP chains. Detect memory sections with execute+write permissions, process hollowing patterns (parent terminates after spawning suspended child), and dynamic import resolution from import tables.

suggestion.title: Shellcode Injection into Legitimate Windows Executables
suggestion.rationale: Explicit: 'Python-based malware development scripts for injecting shellcode into legitimate Windows executables while preserving original functionality.' T1055.001 used operationally; process spawning hides malicious intent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect VirtualAlloc + WriteProcessMemory + CreateRemoteThread chains from suspicious parent processes. Monitor for signed system binaries executing with mismatched behavior (unexpected child processes, network activity, registry writes). Alert on process hollowing: parent exe with suspended child process, subsequent resumption without legitimate activity.

suggestion.title: Cloudflare Worker C2 Redirector Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'A Cloudflare Worker acting as a front-end redirector to obscure the actual backend C2 server.' Legitimate CDN infrastructure repurposed as C2 obfuscation layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify sustained connections to *.workers.dev or Cloudflare edge IPs with symmetric traffic patterns (C2-like request-response cycles), especially from endpoints with no legitimate reason to contact worker infrastructure. Monitor for HTTP POST/PUT with obfuscated headers, encrypted bodies, or fixed-interval communication mimicking beacon behavior.

suggestion.title: Outbound HTTPS Beaconing to Cloud Service Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'weaponizing trusted cloud infrastructure...to camouflage malicious traffic...sustain long-lived Command and Control.' HTTPS traffic to AWS, GCP, Azure, Cloudflare domains from non-browser/non-backup processes should trigger investigation. Generic beaconing hunt will drown in cloud service traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTPS outbound connections to AWS (*.amazonaws.com), GCP (*.googleapis.com), Azure (*.azure.com, *.windows.net), or Cloudflare (*.cloudflare.com) from processes not whitelisted as cloud-aware (browsers, official backup agents, OS services). Flag if connection timestamps show sub-5-minute regularity or if the source process is unusual (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rare executable).

suggestion.title: DNS Tunneling or Encoded Queries to Cloud Resolvers
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1071.004 (DNS) as active technique but provides no further detail. Attackers using cloud services for C2 often employ DNS tunneling through cloud DNS providers (Route53, Cloudflare DNS, Azure DNS). Phrase: 'T1071.004 — DNS' without further narrative suggests DNS-layer abuse not yet captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS queries to cloud DNS endpoints (Route53 resolvers, 1.1.1.1 for Cloudflare, 8.8.8.8 for GCP) with suspicious characteristics: high cardinality subdomains in single domain, TXT record queries, queries from non-standard processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe), or unusual query frequency (>100/min). Baseline by host.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Cloud Service API Calls for C2 or Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Sustaining C2 through cloud infrastructure requires API abuse. Article: 'sustain long-lived Command and Control (C2) operations' implies active API interaction (credential theft, data movement, payload staging). No specific API techniques mentioned but implied by operational pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cloud provider audit logs for anomalous API calls from compromised or stolen credentials: high-frequency GetObject/ListBucket (S3), CreateFunction/UpdateFunction (Lambda abuse for reverse shell), IAM AssumeRole from unusual principals, or large data transfer operations. Flag API calls from unexpected geographies or at off-hours.

suggestion.title: Reverse Shell or RCE via Cloud Serverless Functions
suggestion.rationale: Article focuses on 'abuse' of cloud services for C2. Modern cloud C2 chains leverage Lambda/Cloud Functions as execution vectors. Phrase: 'evade detection, and sustain long-lived Command and Control' implies active code execution, likely through ephemeral serverless compute.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Lambda/Cloud Function invocations with execution logs showing shell commands (bash, cmd.exe, powershell via subprocess). Alert on newly created functions with public HTTP endpoints or API Gateway routes. Flag functions with outbound network connectivity to non-AWS/GCP/Azure IPs. Monitor for rapid function creation/deletion patterns (indicators of staging/cleanup).

suggestion.title: Large-Volume Data Exfiltration to Cloud Object Storage
suggestion.rationale: Complete attack chain for C2 includes data movement. Article: 'malicious traffic...evade detection...C2 operations' implies full intrusion lifecycle. Attackers abuse cloud storage (S3, GCS, Azure Blob) for exfil. Phrase: 'hide malicious traffic' encompasses both ingress C2 and egress exfil.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PutObject calls to S3/GCS/Azure Blob from non-standard cloud accounts or unusual source IPs. Flag bucket ACL modifications that allow public read access. Detect unusually large uploads (>1GB) to buckets not flagged as backup/archival destinations. Monitor for cross-account or cross-tenant access patterns.

suggestion.title: Abuse of Cloud API Keys or Service Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Operational persistence in cloud C2 chains depends on credential theft/abuse. Article: 'cybercriminals are increasingly weaponizing trusted cloud infrastructure' implies attacker has valid or stolen access. No explicit credential-theft narrative, but implied by 'sustain long-lived' operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect API key or service account usage from unexpected geographies, at unusual hours, or with atypical API call patterns. Flag if a service account typically used by application X suddenly makes calls inconsistent with its role (e.g., backup service querying CloudTrail, billing service calling Lambda). Monitor for rapid credential rotation or creation of temporary credentials.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS CVE-2026-0257 Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'enables attackers to bypass authentication mechanisms' and is 'actively leveraged in real-world attacks.' No detection hunt generated for exploit attempts. Core attack primitive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS logs for exploit patterns targeting CVE-2026-0257. Look for malformed API requests, anomalous credential submissions to auth endpoints, or known exploit signatures in system logs. Correlate with inbound traffic from external sources.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass Abuse on Firewall
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim—'bypass authentication mechanisms'—has no dedicated detection use case. This is the crown-jewel exploitation outcome and requires auth-anomaly hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful administrative access without prior successful authentication, or failed auth followed by privileged session creation. Flag direct access to PAN-OS management interfaces that bypasses credential validation.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication via Application Layer Protocol
suggestion.rationale: T1071 (Application Layer Protocol) explicitly listed by article but zero detection use case generated. The six C2 IPs require protocol-level inspection to detect abuse patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect application-layer traffic to C2 IPs (104.207.144.154, 146.19.216.119-120, 146.19.216.125, 209.99.191.137, 79.130.26.202) for protocol abuse. Detect HTTP/HTTPS C2 beaconing, DNS tunneling, or application protocols repurposed for command and control.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised Firewall
suggestion.rationale: Firewall is a perimeter chokepoint. Article implies active exploitation but stops short of describing post-compromise behavior. No detection for lateral movement from PAN-OS to internal assets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unusual lateral movement originating from Palo Alto Networks management IPs. Flag RDP/SSH sessions from firewall to internal servers, or data exfiltration patterns initiated post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Oracle WebLogic T3/IIOP Unauthenticated Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'easily exploitable vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker...via T3, IIOP to compromise Oracle WebLogic Server.' These are Oracle-specific protocols requiring explicit monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound connections to WebLogic T3 (typically port 7001) and IIOP (7002) from external sources without established baseline relationships. Monitor for rapid exploitation attempts post-connection and correlate with WebLogic authentication logs showing unauthenticated access succeeding.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable WebLogic Version Detection (12.2.1.4.0 or 14.1.1.0.0)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'systems running Oracle WebLogic Server versions 12.2.1.4.0 and 14.1.1.0.0' as vulnerable. Shodan reports 1,592 exposed instances. Asset inventory must detect and alert on these versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse WebLogic startup logs, process arguments (weblogic.name), or MANIFEST.MF files to extract version. Alert if 12.2.1.4.0 or 14.1.1.0.0 detected. Correlate with patch inventory to confirm July 2024+ security patches applied.

suggestion.title: WebLogic Service Reconnaissance and Banner Grabbing
suggestion.rationale: Before exploiting CVE-2024-21182, attackers must discover and fingerprint WebLogic instances. Article notes 1,592 instances found via Shodan, implying enumeration occurs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect port scans targeting 7001/7002 from external IPs. Alert on multiple failed connection attempts followed by successful banner grab on WebLogic ports. Look for T3 protocol handshake attempts from non-approved sources.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Data Exfiltration from WebLogic
suggestion.rationale: Article states successful attacks result in 'unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle WebLogic Server accessible data.' Detection must identify exfiltration post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor java.exe (WebLogic process) for unusual outbound connections post-compromise to non-standard destinations. Alert on bulk reads from WebLogic application data directory. Correlate large egress traffic from WebLogic host during T3/IIOP exploitation window.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised WebLogic Middleware
suggestion.rationale: Article describes WebLogic as 'middleware for large, multi-tier distributed applications,' implying backend database and application server access. Compromised WebLogic enables lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new database connections, SSH/RDP sessions, or service account impersonation originating from WebLogic server host. Alert if java.exe spawns child processes for credential dumping or lateral reconnaissance tools post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2024-21182 Patch Compliance Enforcement
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes vulnerability was 'patched two years ago' (July 2024) and CISA issued mandatory patching order by June 4, 2026. Compliance verification is a detective/preventive control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query WebLogic instances for patch level via wmic, Oracle inventory scripts, or log parsing. Flag any instance running unpatched version 12.2.1.4.0 or 14.1.1.0.0. Enforce via SIEM rule that alerts if unpatched version persists >7 days from CISA directive.

suggestion.title: CVE-2022-0492 Vulnerable Asset Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states CISA KEV is 'currently being exploited' and explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' with template substitution for this CVE. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unpatched CVE-2022-0492 on Linux systems via vulnerability scanner or kernel version enumeration (uname -r). Alert on systems without patches past federal due date 2026-06-05. Correlate scanner data with patch management tools to identify remediation lag.

suggestion.title: Cgroups v1 Release_Agent Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies specific attack vector: 'privilege escalation via the cgroups v1 release_agent feature.' No behavioral detection for this mechanism exists in pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious writes to cgroups v1 release_agent paths (/sys/fs/cgroup/*/release_agent). Flag cgroup subsystem manipulation followed by unexpected process execution. Alert on userspace→kernel transitions via release_agent callback or shell script execution from cgroup operations.

suggestion.title: Patch Deadline Compliance for CVE-2022-0492
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal remediation deadline '2026-06-05'—explicit organizational priority absent from pipeline. Compliance tracking is mandatory SOC output for CISA KEV entries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track patch deployment status for CVE-2022-0492 across all Linux systems. Pre-deadline alert (≥7 days before 2026-06-05) on unpatched inventory. Post-deadline escalation for any remaining unpatched systems. Cross-validate scanner claims against actual kernel versions.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-48595 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mandates 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and lists CVE-2025-48595 under Indicators of Compromise with federal due date 2026-06-05. No use case generated despite clear instruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and patch-management systems for unpatched Android Framework instances vulnerable to CVE-2025-48595. Deadline-driven hunt with high confidence due to CISA KEV listing and specific CVE.

suggestion.title: Android Framework Code Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows for code execution'. CISA KEV designation means active exploitation in the wild, yet no detection use case was generated for the execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned from Android Framework services (system_server, framework_server). Correlate process spawning with framework crashes, integer overflow errors, or memory protection violations.

suggestion.title: Android Framework Local Privilege Escalation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'allows for local privilege escalation'. This terminal impact maps to T1068 but was not surfaced in kill-chain or use-case output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect privilege transitions from unprivileged app context to system/root following Android Framework errors. Monitor SELinux denial logs and auditd records for uid/gid escalations correlated with framework service crashes.

suggestion.title: High-volume failed authentication attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly discloses brute-force attack; password-manager platforms should detect anomalous login-attempt spikes consistent with credential-stuffing campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when failed login count against a single target (Dashlane service account or user) exceeds 3σ above baseline or exceeds 50 attempts in <5 min. Baseline should distinguish between user self-lockout and distributed attack patterns.

suggestion.title: Successful login immediately following failed-auth burst
suggestion.rationale: Brute-force attacks terminate when attacker achieves successful compromise; successful login within minutes of high-velocity failures signals account takeover.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful authentication with prior failed-attempt spike (>10 failures/min). Trigger alert if success occurs within 5–60 min post-spike, cross-referenced with geographic or device anomalies.

suggestion.title: Bulk encrypted vault download or export
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies encrypted vaults were downloaded from <20 compromised accounts; detection should identify vault backup/export API calls at unusual volume, timing, or originating from freshly compromised identities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor API endpoints handling vault export or backup (e.g., /api/backup, /export, /sync) for requests exceeding baseline frequency or triggered by accounts with recent auth failures. Flag bulk downloads >N MB within short window.

suggestion.title: Account access from impossible geographic distance or new device
suggestion.rationale: Compromised accounts show login from attacker infrastructure; geographic/device deviations post-brute-force signal abuse of stolen credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag logins from geographic location >500 km from user baseline or from never-before-seen device, especially if correlated with preceding failed-auth spike. Cross-check IP reputation against threat feeds.

suggestion.title: Account lockout storm on multi-user tenant or platform
suggestion.rationale: Brute-force attacks trigger cascading account lockouts; coordinated lockouts across service tenant or user population indicate platform-level attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when account lockout count exceeds baseline by >50% within 1 hr, especially if correlated across multiple users, departments, or originating from specific IP ranges.

suggestion.title: WinRAR Post-Extraction Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Gamaredon Exploits WinRAR to Deliver GammaWorm and GammaSteel'—no detection for suspicious process execution immediately following archive extraction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution spawned from WinRAR temp directory or invoked by winrar.exe. Cross-correlate with malware family names (GammaWorm, GammaSteel) or unusual cmdline patterns typical of post-extraction stagers.

suggestion.title: Gamaredon Malware Binary Execution (GammaWorm/GammaSteel)
suggestion.rationale: Article names specific malware families but no file-hash or behavioral signature proposed for detection of delivered payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation with image names or properties matching GammaWorm/GammaSteel families. Prioritize detections in context of recent WinRAR activity or temp directory execution.

suggestion.title: WinRAR Malicious Archive Receipt (Phishing Vector)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Exploits WinRAR to Deliver' implies archived payload delivery, likely via email phishing to Ukrainian targets, but no email-based initial-access detection proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag .rar or .7z archives received via email from external sources, especially with Ukraine-targeting campaign indicators. Alert on user opening suspicious archives or saving them to user-writable directories.

suggestion.title: Gamaredon Command-and-Control Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article does not disclose C2 domain/IP, but GammaWorm/GammaSteel are known to establish C2 post-execution. No network detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS POST requests or DNS queries from processes spawned in WinRAR extraction context. Cross-reference known Gamaredon C2 infrastructure if available; flag HTTP User-Agent or URI patterns consistent with Gamaredon beacons.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise System Reconnaissance (Gamaredon TTPs)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes payload delivery but Gamaredon historically performs whoami, systeminfo, tasklist post-execution. No discovery-phase detection proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate GammaWorm/GammaSteel execution with spawning of cmd.exe or powershell.exe executing system discovery commands (whoami, systeminfo, tasklist, net view, ipconfig, quser). Alert on rapid enumeration of local shares or AD queries.

suggestion.title: WinRAR Vulnerability Exploitation (Likely CVE-2024-21674)
suggestion.rationale: Article references WinRAR vulnerability vector but does not disclose CVE or vulnerable version ranges. Detection should flag exploitation techniques specific to WinRAR path-traversal or code-execution flaws.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WinRAR process execution for suspicious command-line flags or handling of specially-crafted archives. Flag extraction of files to parent directories or system-critical paths, or extraction of executable/script files to temp locations followed by immediate execution.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-48595 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'under limited, targeted exploitation' and attackers 'can exploit the actively abused high-severity Android Framework vulnerability (tracked as CVE-2025-48595) to gain code execution.' No detection use case exists for exploitation attempts against this specific flaw.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal Framework service processes spawned with elevated privileges or unusual syscall patterns from com.android.framework or related system processes on Android 14+. Look for exploitation indicators like memory corruption patterns or unexpected runtime behavior preceding privilege elevation.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploit Privilege Escalation on Android
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes that the Framework vulnerability 'could lead to remote escalation of privilege with no additional execution privileges needed.' This escalation post-exploitation pattern requires dedicated detection separate from initial exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid UID/GID elevation following Framework component invocation, especially system_server process attempting to gain capabilities it should not have. Flag SELinux denials on Framework context transitions that precede privilege acquisition.

suggestion.title: Qualcomm Display Component (CVE-2026-21385) Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions Google 'released patches for... another zero-day flaw in a Qualcomm display component (CVE-2026-21385).' This component-specific vulnerability should have its own detection signature distinct from Framework exploits.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal access to Qualcomm display driver components (vendor.qti.display or similar) from non-display processes, driver crashes with memory violation signatures, or GPU memory access patterns consistent with heap exploitation.

suggestion.title: Android Framework API Abuse for Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: The critical Framework vulnerability that achieves 'remote escalation of privilege with no additional execution privileges needed' implies abuse of legitimate Framework APIs. Article describes this as a primary attack vector requiring detection at the API call level.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Framework API calls with unusual parameter combinations or argument types that correlate with known exploitation patterns for Android Framework RCE. Focus on reflection-based invocation, IPC abuse through Binder, or unsafe parcelable deserialization from unexpected sources.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Gap – Unpatched Android 14+ Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Local attackers can exploit... devices running Android 14 or later' and emphasizes patch deployment delays: 'While Google Pixel devices will receive these security updates immediately, other vendors will often take longer.' Compliance detection for unpatched devices is a direct use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track Android 14+ devices lacking the June 2026 security patch level (2026-06-01 or later) as exploitable assets. Cross-correlate device inventory with patch deployment records and flag non-Pixel devices exceeding a 30-day patch lag for CVE-2025-48595 as high risk.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempt Detection – Actively Exploited Android CVE
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'One Actively Exploited' — pipeline extracted no CVE identifier or exploitation indicator. Should detect attack patterns targeting the named flaw.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Once the actively-exploited CVE is identified by version/number, monitor for network requests to known exploit infrastructure, suspicious process chains initiated by vulnerable system services, or failed/successful privilege escalation attempts following exploitation windows.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Android Device Persistence Post-Advisory
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'June 2026 Android Update' with 124 flaws — should enumerate vulnerable devices and flag non-compliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Android devices running OS build versions predating June 2026 patch. Alert on persistent vulnerable devices 14+ days post-patch availability, indicating either unmanaged endpoints or intentional adversary foothold preservation.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Indicator Correlation – Android CVE Chain
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation documented but pipeline generated no post-access detection (credential access, data exfil, C2 comms). Should detect downstream activity if exploit grants code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for privilege escalation events, unusual system API calls, or permission escalation (e.g., from system_server or zygote) immediately following vulnerable service invocation. Correlate with data exfil or C2 callbacks if exploit enables such access.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Git Tag Rewrite or Force Push to Composer Package
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'every tag across multiple composer packages rewritten'—direct indication of Git history manipulation. This is initial access / persistence mechanism that pipeline missed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for force pushes, tag rewrites, or history mutations on high-value open-source packages in trusted registries. Flag any single actor rewriting multiple package tags in short timeframe. Correlate with changes to .git/hooks or CI config files.

suggestion.title: Environment Variables / CI Secrets Accessed During Composer Install
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly frames attack as 'steal CI secrets'—attacker injects code that exfiltrates env vars during package installation. Pipeline did not create detection for this credential access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when composer install or package setup scripts read sensitive environment variables (CI_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, etc.) not normally accessed by the package. Cross-correlate with suspicious outbound DNS/HTTP from build context.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of CI Credentials to Attacker-Controlled Domain
suggestion.rationale: Attack objective is credential theft; article mentions 'steal CI secrets' but pipeline generated zero exfiltration detection. Should detect outbound connections from CI jobs to domains not in allowlist.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound connections from CI/build agents to newly registered or low-reputation domains during or immediately after dependency resolution. Baseline against known-good package CDN domains and detect anomalies.

suggestion.title: Malicious Code Injection in Composer Package Version / Tag
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: 'tags rewritten to steal CI secrets' implies code changes in version artifacts. No execution/code-injection UC generated despite this being the delivery mechanism.
log_sources: Source code/AST analysis of composer.lock versions
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare installed package code to known-good hash or published source. Alert if composer.lock references a tag/version whose source differs from upstream manifest or previous installation. Detect inline scripts or obfuscated code in dependency autoload files.

suggestion.title: Unusual Network Beacon from Build Container Executing Compromised Dependency
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack flows through package install → code execution → exfil. Pipeline missed the command-and-control / callback phase where malicious code beacons attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST requests from CI build containers to attacker C2 domains during dependency installation phase. Correlate suspicious domains with credential exfil patterns. Alert on callback patterns or data serialization (JSON/binary blobs) in request bodies.

suggestion.title: Multiple Composer Package Versions Compromised Simultaneously or Sequentially
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'every tag across multiple composer packages'—coordinated compromise of package family. Detection should flag cluster of versions/packages from same author all modified in narrow time window.
log_sources: Git commit history across package repos
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate supply-chain events: detect when multiple packages from same publisher/namespace experience simultaneous or sequential tag rewrites, code commits by unusual actors, or version publish anomalies within short time window. Cross-reference with account compromise indicators.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Code Review Bypass or Approval by Unauthorized Actors
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses 'securing code across the development lifecycle'—inherent threat is code integrity compromise when reviews are bypassed or poisoned. If article details GitHub or Azure DevOps abuse patterns, detection should monitor for unexpected approval grants or skipped reviews.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for code review policy disablement, approval grants to newly-created service principals, or commits merged without required review quorum. Flag rapid-sequence policy changes in Azure Repos or GitHub that weaken branch protection.

suggestion.title: AI Model or Training Data Poisoning Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article addresses 'securing models'—direct threat vector is adversarial input or data poisoning. If article discusses threats to model training pipelines or fine-tuning workflows, detection should track unauthorized dataset modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected dataset URI changes in Azure ML pipelines, unauthorized write access to training data repositories, or insertion of validation-set artifacts into production model registries.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Compromise via Malicious Package or Dependency Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article covers 'development lifecycle security'—standard threat is compromised open-source dependencies or internal package feeds. If content discusses supply-chain hardening, underlying attack is package metadata manipulation or unauthorized publish events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned package publications, unexpected version bumps with unusual content hash, or package metadata updates from non-standard IPs. Flag packages downloaded from secondary feeds before validation.

suggestion.title: VS Code Extension Installation from Untrusted Source or Version Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Article: '[HIGH] Nx Console VS Code Extension Compromised'—implies malicious version distributed via marketplace. Pipeline missed supply-chain compromise detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code extension directory (typically ~/.vscode/extensions/) for unexpected Nx Console plugin file creation or modification. Correlate installation with unusual publisher metadata or version anomalies. Alert on extension activation post-update with new network capabilities.

suggestion.title: Malicious Build Task Execution via Compromised Nx Extension
suggestion.rationale: Nx Console directly orchestrates build/task execution; compromised extension injects malicious steps into npm/yarn/nx workflows. Article context implies execution pipeline hijacking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned from Node.js/nx task runner with obfuscated payloads, curl/wget invocations, or powershell -EncodedCommand. Monitor for npm script execution that doesn't match source control baseline. Flag process trees where code.exe → node → shell (cmd/powershell/bash).

suggestion.title: Extension Host Network Exfiltration of Source Code or Build Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Compromised extension runs in VS Code process with full workspace access. Likely exfiltration of source, secrets, or build outputs to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS connections from code.exe or extensionHost.exe to non-allowlisted destinations. Detect POST requests with large payloads or file archives (tar, zip MIME types). Alert on connections to newly registered domains or known C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Extension Manifest or Plugin Tampering Detection
suggestion.rationale: Compromised extension must modify its code or manifest; detection of in-place code injection or unsigned module changes is critical post-compromise indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code extension package.json and main entry-point files for unexpected modifications post-installation. Detect obfuscated or minified code injected into extension bundles. Alert on permission escalation requests (fsPath, shell execution) added to extension manifest.

suggestion.title: Nx Console Command Injection via Workspace Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Build extensions parse nx.json, package.json, and CLI args; compromised extension could execute arbitrary commands via malicious workspace config without user awareness.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor nx CLI invocation for shell metacharacters (backtick, $(), pipes) in project names or task arguments. Detect extension-spawned shell processes with command substitution or environment variable injection payloads. Alert on child process execution with unusual parent (extensionHost.exe → shell).
