suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for macOS processes spawned following clicks on suspicious ad networks or landing pages known to serve malvertising. Look for process chains initiated by Safari, Chrome, or Firefox with command-line arguments indicating download of unsigned binaries or script execution via malvertising payloads.

suggestion.title: FlutterShell Backdoor Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'distributed the new backdoor FlutterShell, built using the Flutter framework.' Pipeline missed the malware name and execution phase entirely. Should detect Flutter-based malware instantiation on macOS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Flutter runtime execution on macOS (libflutter.so or Flutter framework artifacts) spawning from unexpected parent processes or download directories. Flag processes with obfuscated command lines or attempt to access system binaries post-launch (indicators of Flutter malware unpacking native payloads).

suggestion.title: Flutter-based Malware C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article describes a 'backdoor' capability but pipeline extracted no C2 infrastructure or command-and-control detection logic. FlutterShell as a backdoor implies persistent C2 communication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTPS or HTTP connections from Flutter-runtime-spawned processes on macOS to unknown or newly-registered domains. Flag atypical C2 signaling patterns: periodic beaconing, encoded parameters, or connections to IP space without corresponding WHOIS registration history.

suggestion.title: macOS Unsigned Binary Persistence via Malvertising
suggestion.rationale: Malvertising campaigns often drop unsigned binaries for persistence. Article identifies persistent backdoor ('FlutterShell') but pipeline generated no persistence detection. Should monitor for unsigned executable placement post-malvertising compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned Mach-O binaries written to standard persistence locations (~/.bash_profile, ~/Library/LaunchAgents, /tmp) following malvertising activity. Flag parent processes with unusual network connectivity immediately before binary placement.

suggestion.title: macOS Malvertising Ad Network Traffic Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malvertising campaign' — this specific initial-access vector requires detection of ad-network traffic anomalies. Pipeline missed attack surface entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for macOS processes (web browsers) connecting to newly-registered or reputation-blacklisted ad-serving domains. Flag redirect chains: legitimate ad domain → intermediate tracker → malware delivery domain. Alert on failed SSL verification or cert warnings bypassed by browser plugins.

suggestion.title: Suspicious JAR Execution from Minecraft User Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies '3,820 unique malicious JAR files' distributed via 'malicious Minecraft mods, clients, cheats, and utilities.' JAR execution from Minecraft folders is the execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect java.exe spawning from user browser or file manager with JAR arguments pointing to %APPDATA%/Roaming/.minecraft or equivalent. Correlate with outbound network connections to non-Mojang infrastructure within 5 minutes of execution.

suggestion.title: Multi-Browser Credential Enumeration by Gaming Process
suggestion.rationale: WeedHack 'targets passwords across 36 browsers' and '56 cryptocurrency add-ons' plus 'Discord, Steam, and Telegram credentials.' Single gaming process accessing credential stores across multiple browsers is anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect java.exe or Minecraft launcher accessing Chrome/Firefox/Edge user data directories, password manager vaults, and cryptocurrency wallet directories in same process session. Flag when browser profile enumeration occurs outside normal launcher startup.

suggestion.title: Webcam and Input Capture Capability Installation
suggestion.rationale: Premium WeedHack tier includes 'webcam access,' 'keylogger,' and 'remote control with input access (mouse and keyboard)' — these are post-execution collection capabilities following initial infection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Minecraft/java.exe acquiring handles to camera devices, microphone drivers, or establishing keyboard/mouse hooks via user32.dll. Detect DLL injection patterns loading input capture libraries or hook utilities.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration to Clear-Net C2 Dashboard
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'WeedHack malware platform is hosted on the clear net and provides access to anyone for free' with victim overview dashboard. Network indicators should detect HTTP/HTTPS to C2 endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Minecraft process initiating HTTPS connections to unregistered or recently-registered domains with dashboard-like URI patterns (/victims, /exfil, /api/steal). Alert on Telegram API calls from java.exe context indicating credential exfiltration to attacker channel (800+ members per article).

suggestion.title: SEO-Poisoning Landing Page Access Preceding JAR Download
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'SEO poisoning promotion' and fake sites 'displaying a security notice warning visitors' mimicking legitimate GitHub/Discord. Detect malicious landing page chains leading to JAR delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag browser downloads of JAR files from recently-registered domains with typosquatted or edit-distance-similar names to legitimate Minecraft mod projects (Meteor Client, Radium Client, Wurst Client, etc.). Correlate visit to fake security-notice page with immediate JAR file download.

suggestion.title: Minecraft Session Token and Launcher Profile Access
suggestion.rationale: WeedHack explicitly targets 'Minecraft session ID theft' and builds payloads for 'Minecraft versions 1.21.0 through 1.21.10.' Session token theft is primary credential objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect non-launcher processes accessing launcher_profiles.json, logintoken.bin, or .minecraft/launcher directory files. Flag file read attempts to Minecraft authentication token storage by unsigned or unsigned-by-Microsoft executables.

suggestion.title: Xeno RAT Process Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names Xeno RAT as the malware payload; no execution-phase detection suggested. Pipeline should flag process creation, DLL loading, or code injection associated with known Xeno RAT IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution of Xeno RAT payloads (hash or behavioral patterns: suspicious DLL injection, unsigned executables in temp directories, child processes spawned from Office or browser). Correlate with known Xeno C2 infrastructure for confirmation.

suggestion.title: Phishing Campaign to Finance Ministry
suggestion.rationale: Article title and context imply initial access via targeted phishing to Afghanistan Finance Ministry; no initial_access detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect phishing emails to finance.gov.af or similar with malicious Office attachments, suspicious macros, or links to credential harvesting sites. Monitor for Document macro execution followed by child process spawning on affected hosts.

suggestion.title: Xeno RAT C2 Command & Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: No C2 detection use case generated despite malware-specific article; pipeline should identify network-layer IOCs and communication patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound connections to known Xeno RAT C2 domains/IPs (to be extracted from article and threat feeds). Look for suspicious DNS queries, HTTP POST requests to uncommon ports, or encrypted tunnels with beacon-like patterns.

suggestion.title: Xeno RAT Persistence Registry/Autostart Modifications
suggestion.rationale: RAT implants typically establish persistence via registry keys, scheduled tasks, or startup folder writes; no persistence-phase detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for registry writes to Run, RunOnce, or Startup folders correlating with Xeno RAT process execution. Flag unauthorized .lnk files in Startup directory or modifications to shell commands (ShellExecute hooks).

suggestion.title: SideCopy Lateral Movement Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies SideCopy actor in context of targeting a government ministry; no lateral movement detection for multi-host campaigns suggested despite this being typical of group's TTPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for credential enumeration (net user, whoami) and lateral movement attempts (SMB share access, RDP logons, PsExec-like tools) originating from confirmed compromised Finance Ministry hosts, particularly targeting adjacent government or financial systems.

suggestion.title: Document Attachment Macro Execution (Xeno RAT Delivery)
suggestion.rationale: Phishing to finance ministry typically uses Office documents; no macro execution or Office child-process detection suggested despite being core Xeno delivery vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Word/Excel macro execution (VBA_MACRO events or suspicious WINWORD.EXE child processes like powershell.exe, regsvcs.exe, msiexec.exe). Flag macro-enabled files opened from Outlook or downloaded from untrusted zones.

suggestion.title: Maven Dependency Version: jqwik-engine 1.10.0 Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Package: net.jqwik:jqwik-engine Affected version: 1.10.0' and notes 'Follow-up release: 1.10.1'. Pipeline must detect exact version in manifests and lockfiles.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor build artifacts and dependency resolution logs for net.jqwik:jqwik-engine version 1.10.0. Alert on presence in pom.xml, gradle.build, or transitive dependencies during CI/CD runs. Distinguish from 1.10.1+ (patched) by examining Maven Central metadata or JAR checksums.

suggestion.title: ANSI Escape Code Anomalies in Test Output
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'prints ESC [2K followed by a carriage return, twice' and 'Watch for stray ESC[2K and carriage-return artifacts around your test summaries.' This obfuscation is the delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search CI/CD logs for ESC[2K sequences (hex: 1B5B324B) followed by carriage returns in proximity to jqwik or JUnit test summaries. Flag any raw ANSI erase-line codes in non-interactive log streams (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitHub workflows) as anomalous—they indicate obfuscation of tool output intended for agent processing.

suggestion.title: Prompt Injection in Maven/JUnit Test Output
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies the payload: 'The payload told agents to disregard previous instructions and delete all jqwik tests and code.' Detection should flag these directives in test logs fed to agents.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag test output containing prompt injection patterns targeting AI agents (e.g., 'disregard.*instruction', 'delete.*test', 'delete.*jqwik.*code'). Correlate with jqwik test runs. Monitor agent input pipelines for suspicious directives in tool output streams, especially from build/test phases.

suggestion.title: Suspicious CodingAgents Method in Compiled JAR
suggestion.rationale: Article reveals 'The malicious instruction lived in a new method called printMessageForCodingAgents() inside the net.jqwik.engine.execution.JqwikExecutor class.' Decompiled code inspection can identify this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan downloaded JARs (especially jqwik-engine 1.10.0) for method names containing 'CodingAgents', 'Agent', or 'AIAgent' in combination with print/output methods. Decompile suspected JARs and grep for printMessageForCodingAgents() in net.jqwik.engine.execution.JqwikExecutor. Compare against known safe class structures.

suggestion.title: AI Agent Rejection of Crafted Tool Output
suggestion.rationale: Article documents: 'Claude Code flagged the instruction on the first mvn test run, refused to act on it, and traced it back to its source in the JAR.' Detect when agents properly reject injected directives.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor agent execution logs for rejection events where tool output contains prompt injection patterns. Log agent refusals to act on suspicious terminal output; these are successful defenses. Correlate with source JARs to identify supply-chain attack attempts that were mitigated.

suggestion.title: Commit 9dddcb5226 jqwik Repository Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies specific commit: 'That's the code snippet from commit 9dddcb5226' containing the ESC codes. Threat intel should track suspicious repository commits.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor jqwik repository commits for methods named printMessageForCodingAgents() or similar agent-targeting patterns. Flag commits that introduce ANSI escape codes (0x1B5B324B) combined with carriage returns in output paths. Cross-reference with Maven Central release timelines (May 25, 2026).

suggestion.title: npm preinstall hook spawning child processes
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'preinstall hook on every npm install' as attack vector. No detection for arbitrary process spawning from npm install phase. Detection gap for T1546.016 (Installer Packages).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes spawned from node/npm with parent command containing 'install' or npm process event with child spawning shell/Python/Node interpreters. Preinstall hooks typically execute synchronously during npm install; children from install phase are high-risk.

suggestion.title: Process accessing credential-related environment variables
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'targets GitHub Actions secrets, AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, HashiCorp Vault, npm tokens'. No detection for environment variable enumeration or reads. Maps to T1552.001 (Credentials in Files) and T1528 (Steal Application Access Token).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detection for process reading or enumerating variables: GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, GCP_*, AZURE_*, KUBECONFIG, VAULT_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN, CIRCLECI_TOKEN. Higher confidence if sourced from preinstall hook context.

suggestion.title: HTTP metadata API access from build/CI environment
suggestion.rationale: Article lists AWS, GCP, Azure as credential targets. MITRE T1552.005 (Cloud Instance Metadata API) is mapped but no detection. Metadata services are primary lateral-movement credential vector in cloud CI/CD.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP(S) requests from npm/node processes to metadata endpoints: 169.254.169.254 (AWS IMDSv1/v2), 0.metadata.google.internal (GCP), 169.254.169.254:80/metadata/v1/instance (Azure). Especially suspicious if initiated from preinstall hook or /tmp-resident scripts.

suggestion.title: Binary execution from node_modules directory during install
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'multi-stage credential harvester' payload. Typical supply chain attacks stage binaries or wrapped scripts in node_modules. No detection for stage-2 payload execution from package installation context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of binaries (non-JS, non-shell scripts) from node_modules or .bin directories with parent process = npm/node in install context. Second indicator: execution of scripts from node_modules with arbitrary permissions or obfuscation patterns.

suggestion.title: npm package integrity mismatch (expected vs. actual hash)
suggestion.rationale: Article states specific @redhat-cloud-services versions compromised. Detection should flag when installed package hash differs from npm registry manifest or package-lock.json. Covers T1195.002 (Supply Chain compromise) detection at install time.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare SHA256/SHA1 of installed @redhat-cloud-services packages against npm registry manifest or package-lock.json checksums. Flag mismatches during npm install. Correlate with network events fetching from unexpected CDNs or mirrors.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation with Obfuscated Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords include 'obfuscation' and 'payload' in context of npm packages; supply-chain malware typically installs via npm install with hidden post-install scripts. Pipeline should detect installation of packages with suspicious post-install hooks or obfuscated code patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install / yarn add processes spawning child processes with suspicious names (powershell, cmd, bash with encoded arguments, curl/wget to external hosts). Correlate npm cache directory writes with network connections within seconds of installation.

suggestion.title: npm Package Exfiltration of Credentials or Environment Variables
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'credential harvesting' in npm context. Malicious packages commonly steal .env files, AWS keys, or CI/CD secrets during installation or at runtime.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm package processes reading .env, .aws/credentials, or CI environment files (BUILD_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN), followed by DNS queries or HTTP POST to non-package-registry domains within the same process tree.

suggestion.title: Worm-like npm Package Self-Propagation via Dependency Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article metadata explicitly cites 'worm propagation' as a threat vector. Self-replicating npm malware injects itself into dependent packages' node_modules or modifies package.json to spread laterally.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm processes that modify package.json files outside their own directory, write to parent/sibling node_modules folders, or invoke npm publish/registry commands from a package's install script. Detect version increments in dependent packages shortly after a compromised package installs.

suggestion.title: CI/CD Environment Compromise via npm Package Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'CI/CD persistence' explicitly; npm packages in CI pipelines run with elevated permissions and can persist across builds via cached artifacts or registry poisoning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm package execution in CI runners (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins) that writes to cache directories, modifies CI configuration files (.github/workflows, .gitlab-ci.yml), or exfiltrates repo secrets to external infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Registry Metadata Tampering or Typosquatting Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack on npm registry often involves fake/similar-named packages or version hijacking. Article discusses 'attack surface' of npm ecosystem, implying registry manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm install of packages with names similar to popular ones (levenshtein distance <3), packages with unusual version jumps, or packages from new publishers installing unusually large binary payloads relative to source code size.

suggestion.title: WordPress process HTTP requests to Steam profiles
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'polls Steam Community profiles for commands' and 'hides command instructions inside Steam Community profile comments'. Needs detection for w3wp.exe, php.exe, or apache processes initiating HTTP requests to steamcommunity.com URLs with repeated cadence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate outbound HTTP connections to Steam community profiles with parent process being WordPress-related (httpd, apache, w3wp, php-cgi). Legitimate WordPress does not initiate requests to Steam. Alert on repeated polling patterns (>5 requests/hour to same profile, consistent intervals).

suggestion.title: WordPress file system modifications preceding process execution
suggestion.rationale: Malware must be installed ('WordPress malware') implying file drop, plugin installation, or theme modification. Article describes two-stage attack with malware persistence on WordPress sites.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation or modification of WordPress plugin files (.php in wp-content/plugins/), theme files (wp-content/themes/), or wp-config.php within 10 minutes followed by child process spawning from web server (w3wp, httpd). Alert if files added post-deployment or modified outside change windows.

suggestion.title: Base64 or URL-encoded command injection from web requests
suggestion.rationale: Article describes commands 'hidden inside Steam Community profile comments'. Commands are likely encoded in comment text and decoded/executed by malware. Need detection for suspicious POST requests or process execution of base64-decoded payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PowerShell or cmd.exe child processes spawned with base64-encoded arguments, or monitor HTTP POST requests to Steam URLs containing base64 blocks in the request body. Correlate with web server process hierarchy.

suggestion.title: Unusual HTTP user-agent or missing headers in Steam requests
suggestion.rationale: Legitimate Steam browsing uses browser user-agents. Malware polling for C2 commands is likely to have atypical user-agent strings (or none) or absence of Referer/Accept headers typical of browser clients.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to Steam that lack browser-typical headers (Accept-Language, Referer, Cache-Control) or have non-browser user-agents (curl, wget, PowerShell, python-requests, etc.). Correlate source IPs with web servers.

suggestion.title: WordPress admin account creation or privilege escalation post-malware
suggestion.rationale: Malware infection of WordPress typically includes creation of backdoor admin accounts or modification of existing user roles to maintain access and execute commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress user creation events (wp_users table inserts) or user_meta modifications that grant admin role, especially outside change windows or from non-admin IPs. Alert on creation followed within 1 hour by HTTP requests to Steam profiles.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of WordPress database or config over Steam side-channel
suggestion.rationale: Article implies bidirectional C2 (commands in, results out). C2 side-channel over Steam comments can carry exfiltrated data such as database dumps, WordPress config, or stolen credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large POST requests from WordPress servers to Steam profiles (>100KB per request) or multiple POST requests in short window to same Steam profile. Monitor for mysqldump or wp-cli export processes preceding Steam HTTP POST activity.

suggestion.title: Dragon Weave C2 Beaconing Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'Dragon Weave' as the threat actor; typical APT campaigns involve C2 callbacks and encrypted communications that should be detectable via network signatures or behavioral patterns. No use case for C2 detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections to newly registered or bulletproof-hosted C2 domains with patterns consistent with Dragon Weave infrastructure (e.g., HTTPS on non-standard ports, beaconing intervals, TLS certificate anomalies). Correlate with regional targeting vectors against Czech/Taiwan entities.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Detection in Czech/Taiwan Government Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates breaches of Czech Republic and Taiwan—both government-sector targets. No detection logic generated for inter-host lateral movement, which is standard in APT campaigns post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag RDP/WinRM authentication chains across government networks with Dragon Weave behavioral signatures (e.g., credential reuse, traffic to unusual target hosts, off-hours activity). Combine with suspicious process launches on destination hosts.

suggestion.title: Spear-Phishing and Malicious Document Delivery for Dragon Weave
suggestion.rationale: China-aligned groups commonly use phishing as initial access; article mentions attacks on Czech/Taiwan but provides no detection logic for email-borne compromise vectors. 'Ramp up Attacks' suggests increased phishing volume.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on phishing emails targeting Czech/Taiwan government domains with Office macro payloads, suspicious file extensions, or URLs hosted on newly spun-up domains. Correlate with file execution anomalies (e.g., Office spawning cmd.exe, PowerShell).

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via Uncommon Protocols
suggestion.rationale: Article headline signals espionage against state actors; no detection logic for data staging, compression, or exfiltration. APT campaigns targeting government entities typically involve large-scale file theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual volume/patterns of outbound traffic to non-standard ports or rarely seen destinations from government systems. Detect file staging (recursive copy, compression of sensitive data) followed by transmission to likely C2 or exfil proxy infrastructure.

suggestion.title: WebLogic T3 Port 7001 Exploitation Probing
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated attacker with network access via T3' — T3 protocol (port 7001) is the primary attack surface for this CVE and must be hunted for anomalous connection or exploitation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unauthenticated or unexpected inbound connections to WebLogic T3 service (port 7001). Correlate with vulnerability scanner detections for CVE-2024-21182 and failed authentication attempts to identify exploitation or probing activity.

suggestion.title: WebLogic IIOP Port 3700 Exploitation Probing
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'network access via T3, IIOP' as dual attack vectors. IIOP (port 3700) requires equal monitoring for anomalous connections and exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound IIOP traffic (port 3700) to Oracle WebLogic Server instances, particularly from untrusted or external networks. Flag connection patterns consistent with automated exploitation probing or scanner activity.

suggestion.title: CVE-2024-21182 Scanner Detection & Unpatched Assets
suggestion.rationale: Article directly recommends 'match against your vulnerability scanner' and emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' with federal due-date 2026-06-04. Unpatched instances are immediate compromise risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner result flagging CVE-2024-21182 on Oracle WebLogic Server. Cross-reference patch history to identify systems not remediated by federal due-date; prioritize as imminent exploitation risk.

suggestion.title: WebLogic Unauthenticated Data Access or Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article states successful exploitation 'result[s] in unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle WebLogic Server accessible data' — implying post-exploitation lateral movement or data collection without legitimate credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt WebLogic audit logs for successful data access, privilege operations, or configuration changes from previously-unknown source IPs or with missing or mismatched authentication context. Flag any high-volume data read operations immediately post-exploitation window.

suggestion.title: Docker Image Pull from Untrusted/Newly-Appeared Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes poisoning Docker Hub repository and distribution of 'tainted images'—detection must flag container runtime image pull events from registries with recently-created/suspicious provenance or from repos that lack expected signer keys.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on docker pull / container image load where (registry_reputation_score < threshold OR registry_age_days < 30 OR image_signature_valid=false). Correlate against baseline image registries; flag deviation. Reference: 'poisoning a Docker Hub repository to later steal Kubernetes secrets.'

suggestion.title: Stealer/Credential-Harvester Process in Container Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'The tainted images distributed a stealer that was loaded during the KICS scanning process'—this is direct post-execution behavior. Detection must catch stealers running inside containers via process parent/child anomalies and known stealer signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor container process tree: flag execution of known credential-stealer or information-gathering tools (ProcessName matches stealer signatures) as child of scanning/build tools (gradle, maven, npm, docker build). Reference: 'stealer...loaded during...scanning process.'

suggestion.title: Kubernetes Secrets Enumeration/Access from Container
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'steal Kubernetes secrets'—this is direct credential access from within a compromised container context. Detection must identify API calls to Kubernetes secret store from pod/container not authorized to access secrets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on kubectl get secrets / kubernetes.io/secret API calls originating from a container (service account in non-privileged namespace, or process UID < 1000 in container). Cross-reference against RBAC policy; flag if caller lacks SecretRead permission. Reference: 'steal Kubernetes secrets and other sensitive data.'

suggestion.title: Container Escape via sys_admin / sys_module / sys_ptrace Capability
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE, CAP_SYS_PTRACE as privilege-escalation attack vectors. Detection must identify containers granted these dangerous capabilities and flag attempts to exploit them (e.g., ptrace syscalls from container, sysctl/module-load calls).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag pods/containers with allowPrivilegeEscalation=true OR capabilities=[SYS_ADMIN|SYS_MODULE|SYS_PTRACE]. Correlate with syscall patterns: ptrace() calls to host PIDs, sysctl writes, or module load operations from within container. Reference: 'CAP_SYS_ADMIN CAP_SYS_MODULE CAP_SYS_PTRACE.'

suggestion.title: Kubernetes API Server Authentication Failure / Anomalous API Access
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'orchestration API compromise' and 'orchestration API abuse' as attack vectors. Detection must catch failed API authentication attempts or anomalous token usage from containers/pods attempting to access kube-apiserver.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor kubernetes_audit for failed user/service-account auth (authentication_decision=deny) originating from pod IPs. Flag excessive API calls to resource types (secrets, configmaps, nodes, services) from service accounts not expected to access them. Reference: 'Exploitation of orchestration APIs.'

suggestion.title: Suspicious Dockerfile / Build Config Containing Embedded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses supply-chain compromise via container images and mention of stealer being 'loaded during KICS scanning process'—KICS scans Dockerfile/IaC for misconfigurations. Detection must catch Dockerfiles or build logs with hardcoded secrets, API keys, or credential references that pose theft risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Dockerfile content, build-time environment variables, or base images that contain plaintext secrets (AWS_KEY, password=, private-key patterns). Correlate with source code repository commits; flag if secrets added by unfamiliar actor or in recently-forked repo. Reference: 'poisoning...to later steal...sensitive data'; implies credentials in image layers.

suggestion.title: WP Maps Pro Plugin Exploitation HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies WP Maps Pro as the target ('Critical WP Maps Pro Flaw'). Pipeline produced zero IOCs or endpoint signatures. Should detect requests to vulnerable plugin paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to wp-content/plugins/wp-maps-pro/* paths for POST requests with exploitation parameters (file inclusion, template injection, RCE payloads). Correlate with 200/302 responses following reconnaissance 404s.

suggestion.title: WordPress Admin Account Creation via Unauthorized Request
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states exploitation leads to 'create admin accounts'. No detection for this persistence mechanism extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on wp-admin/user-new.php POST requests from unauthenticated or low-privilege contexts, or wp_users table INSERT events creating role='administrator' entries post-infection. Flag rapid admin user creation cycles.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP Execution in WordPress Plugin Directory Context
suggestion.rationale: WP Maps Pro exploitation implies PHP code execution within plugin space ('actively exploited'). Pipeline missed execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor child processes spawned from www-data/apache contexts following HTTP requests to wp-maps-pro paths. Alert on eval(), system(), exec() calls inferred from PHP execution chains; flag include() of attacker-controlled URLs.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via WordPress User Metadata Modification
suggestion.rationale: Creating admin accounts implies permission elevation ('create admin accounts'). No privilege-escalation detection produced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor wp_usermeta table updates setting wp_capabilities or wp_user_level to admin values; track wp_options changes to active_plugins or option_value serialized arrays. Flag modifications from external IPs or unusual user-agents.

suggestion.title: Known WP Maps Pro Plugin Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: No vulnerable version signatures extracted. Article indicates specific exploitable version(s) in active use ('actively exploited').
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Fingerprint wp-maps-pro/readme.txt or plugin.php version declarations in HTTP responses. Maintain signatures for known-vulnerable versions published post-vulnerability disclosure. Cross-reference against attacker scanning patterns.

suggestion.title: Brute Force - High-Volume Failed Logins
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'brute-force attacks that attempted logins from distant locations and unknown devices.' Direct T1110 pattern; no detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect 10+ failed authentication attempts from single source IP or account within 5-minute window. Correlate with account lockout events. Baseline per service account to reduce false positives from legitimate automation.

suggestion.title: Device Registration from Geographic Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'verification codes for legitimate account owners to register new devices' issued after brute-force from 'distant locations.' Missing detection for device enrollment anomaly spike.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on device registration/MFA enrollment attempts from countries outside user baseline geography, especially if preceded by failed authentication spike. Requires geolocation enrichment and user travel profile baseline.

suggestion.title: Account Lockout Event Spike
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'suspension of those accounts as part of Dashlane's built-in security controls.' Brute-force triggers lockout cascade; volume anomaly is strong signal of active attack in progress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on 3+ account lockouts within 1-hour window. Elevate severity if correlated with failed login spike and device registration attempts from same or related IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Unsolicited Device Registration Email Cascade
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Many users were confused...tried to confirm if the communication was part of a phishing attempt.' Bulk device-enrollment verification emails to unaware users indicate active brute-force exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect device registration / MFA challenge emails sent to 5+ users in same tenant within 1-hour window. Flag if emails reference unfamiliar devices or locations. Correlate with failed login spike from similar IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Impossible Travel / Geographic Velocity Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attempted logins from distant locations.' If single account shows authentication from City A then City B (impossible distance in time delta), it signals distributed attack or credential compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect authentication attempts from locations separated by distance impossible to travel in time delta. Weight by user's historical geography. Alert if same account or email shows rapid locale-switching across multiple IPs.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: workspace member enumeration followed by mass-grant attack
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'forwards the request body's user_id and role straight into MemberService.add()' with no validation. Attacker could iterate user_id or scrape user list, then grant owner to multiple accounts in sequence. No UC targets attacker discovering valid user IDs first.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST /workspaces/*/members requests with varying user_id values from single source within short window, followed by successful 201 responses. Correlation with user-enumeration patterns (404→200 status transitions on /users/* or /members/* list endpoints) would strengthen signal.

suggestion.title: praisonai-platform: workspace owner role abuse post-grant
suggestion.rationale: Article grants user 'owner' role; no UC tracks what owner-role accounts do afterward (workspace modifications, secret access, member list changes). Attack chain incomplete without visibility into post-exploitation workspace manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate user grants of owner role (via UC_41_2) with subsequent API calls from newly-granted account to /workspaces/{id}/secrets, /workspaces/{id}/settings, or /workspaces/{id}/members within 1 hour. Privilege escalation followed by immediate resource access suggests lateral-move intent.

suggestion.title: Malicious JavaScript Injection Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'JavaScript injection following the t.js?site=<id> pattern' and 'eight technical fingerprints' including this pattern. Observable on compromised websites.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to domains containing 't.js?site=' parameters. Correlate source IPs against known compromised site lists. Flag repeated access to injection domains from unusual geographic/ISP combinations.

suggestion.title: Fake Browser Update Prompt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'fraudulent software update prompts, usually impersonating browser updates' for Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari, Opera, Brave, Yandex, Vivaldi, Samsung Internet, and UC Browser.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected 'update' processes or downloads from domains mismatching official browser CDNs. Alert on ZIP archives containing DLLs and executables named 'Browser Update.exe' or similar. Cross-reference download source domains against zTDS infrastructure indicators.

suggestion.title: PowerShell Command Execution via ClickFix Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'ClickFix attacks involve PowerShell commands' that victims are socially engineered to copy and execute from compromised websites.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PowerShell process invocation with suspicious obfuscated or encoded command-line arguments originating from parent processes tied to web browsers. Alert on execution chains: browser → cmd/powershell → suspicious payload.

suggestion.title: macOS Clipboard Hijacking via ClickFix
suggestion.rationale: Article reveals 'obfuscated JavaScript payload specifically designed to target macOS desktop systems, delivered via verification-themed ClickFix attacks that hijack the clipboard.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for JavaScript executing in browser context with clipboard read/write system calls on macOS. Alert on clipboard modifications followed by background process creation or network connections to suspicious infrastructure.

suggestion.title: zTDS Traffic Distribution System Redirection Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'DriveSurge hijacks thousands of legitimate, high-reputation websites and silently redirects visitors to malware' using zTDS, and provides 'eight technical fingerprints' to identify infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP 30x redirects from legitimate high-reputation domains to unfamiliar targets. Identify zTDS infrastructure by profiling capabilities: track redirect logic that varies payload based on User-Agent, geolocation, or device fingerprints.

suggestion.title: Suspicious ZIP Archive Download Containing DLLs and Executables
suggestion.rationale: Report details 'fake Firefox update that downloaded a ZIP archive containing multiple DLLs and a malicious executable named Browser Update.exe' — a clear payload delivery indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ZIP downloads from non-standard update domains. Monitor extraction of mixed DLL/EXE content followed by execution of any binary inside. Correlate against known legitimate update signatures.

suggestion.title: npm Preinstall Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Each compromised release adds an install-time hook. npm runs preinstall scripts automatically during npm install, before any of your own code executes.' Zero UC generated despite explicit trigger mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for node.exe or nodejs processes spawned from npm package install contexts with parent process containing 'npm install'. Correlate with preinstall script presence in package.json. Alert on preinstall execution outside expected CI/CD environments.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated JavaScript Evaluation in npm Context
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'index.js is an unusually large, heavily obfuscated JavaScript file. The author relied on eval() and ROT-based string decoding to hide the logic.' No detection for obfuscation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect eval() calls within npm package execution contexts; monitor for ROT13/ROT47 decoding operations combined with JavaScript evaluation. Flag packages with preinstall scripts containing heavy string substitution or character rotation patterns.

suggestion.title: GitHub OIDC Token Request with Publishing Scope
suggestion.rationale: Root cause explicitly: 'added a minimal GitHub Actions workflow that...Requested a GitHub OIDC identity token via id-token: write.' No UC for supply-chain-specific token misuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions workflows in org repos for id-token: write scope requests in jobs that also execute npm publish. Alert on OIDC token requests from non-standard branches or commits lacking reviewer approval. Cross-reference with npm publish events.

suggestion.title: Credential Enumeration from npm Registry and SSH Contexts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Harvests secrets and credentials from the local environment and CI context: environment variables, ~/.npmrc tokens, SSH keys, GitHub tokens.' No UC for credential file access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Node.js processes reading ~/.npmrc, ~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.ssh/id_ed25519, or accessing environment variable lists. Monitor for fs.readFile or fs.readFileSync calls targeting credential paths from npm package contexts.

suggestion.title: Cloud Identity Enumeration (GCP/Azure)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'enumerates every identity the infected host can assume, not just static secrets. New collectors for GCP and Azure.' No UC for cloud identity discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect gcloud auth list, gcloud config list, az account show, az role assignment list commands originating from npm package install contexts or unusual processes. Monitor for cloud CLIs invoked from Node.js child processes.

suggestion.title: npm Package Republishing by Compromised Identity
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Self-propagates. It queries the registry for other packages the compromised identity can publish and republishes them, carrying the same payload.' No UC for worm propagation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on multiple npm publish commands from the same identity within hours, particularly if: (1) republishing existing packages, (2) only changing preinstall scripts, (3) originating from CI/CD contexts linked to new/orphan commits, (4) version increments are minimal or unusual.

suggestion.title: npm Preinstall Script Spawns Unexpected Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article states malicious code embedded in packages executes during install to steal credentials; detection must catch preinstall/postinstall lifecycle hooks launching processes unrelated to normal dependency setup ('silently infecting CI/CD environments')
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned from npm install contexts that execute curl, powershell, bash with external connectivity or file-system access to credential stores. Baseline normal npm lifecycle process trees and flag deviations in public/CI environments.

suggestion.title: Credential File Access from node.js Process - GitHub/Cloud Secrets
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes malicious code stealing 'credentials from GitHub, cloud platforms, and local machines'; detection must catch suspicious file reads (.npmrc, .git/config, ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.azure) during package execution
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file access events for node/npm processes reading credential files outside of normal package manager workflow. Flag access patterns originating from node_modules or install-time execution contexts to non-standard credential paths.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Republishing from CI/CD Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states campaign 'spreads like a worm by republishing trusted packages'; detection must catch unauthorized npm publish operations originating from CI/CD systems or unexpected package version increments
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm publish commands executed in CI/CD pipelines where no explicit publish step is declared in workflow config. Correlate with npm token usage and rapid version increments (e.g., +5 patch versions in <1 hour) indicating automated re-distribution.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Credentials via HTTP/DNS from Developer Workstation
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates credentials stolen from local developer machines ('local machines'); detection must identify outbound traffic from npm install processes carrying encoded credential material to attacker infrastructure
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline DNS/HTTP activity from npm contexts during install. Alert on non-package-registry egress containing base64-encoded payloads, GitHub token patterns, AWS key structures, or unusual DNS subdomains. Correlate credential file access with network egress events.

suggestion.title: @redhat-cloud-services Package Version Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states '90 versions of @redhat-cloud-services packages' were compromised; detection must flag installation of known-vulnerable version ranges or unexpected version selection in lockfiles
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain IOC list of compromised @redhat-cloud-services versions and flag installations matching those ranges. Cross-reference with package-lock.json snapshots in source control to identify first-time introductions or unplanned version downgrades within vulnerable range.

suggestion.title: Dependency Tree Mutation Post-Install in CI/CD Builds
suggestion.rationale: Implicit in worm-propagation model: if campaign injects itself into transitive dependencies or overwrites lock files, detection must catch post-install package-lock.json modifications or unexpected transitive packages from @redhat-cloud-services
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare package-lock.json at install-time versus declared dependencies. Alert on addition of @redhat-cloud-services transitive dependencies not listed in direct package.json, or version mutations not traceable to explicit version bumps.

suggestion.title: Automated AD Discovery via AI-Driven Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'AD discovery is driven by collecting observations from completed tasks and selecting the next action from predefined choices'—clear behavioral signature of programmatic enumeration orchestration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid sequential AD queries from single process (dsquery.exe, PowerShell with Get-AD* cmdlets) within short window. Monitor LDAP binds with unusual service account patterns. Correlate process tree: parent automation framework → AD discovery child processes.

suggestion.title: Cobalt Strike Beacon Masqueraded as Legitimate Web Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Cobalt Strike profiles designed to make beacon traffic resemble legitimate web requests'—direct indicator of C2 traffic obfuscation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Cobalt Strike User-Agent strings (MSIE 8.0, specific windows version patterns) mixed with legitimate traffic profiles. Correlate beacon-like callback intervals with masqueraded HTTP headers. Alert on certificate mismatches for spoofed legitimate domains.

suggestion.title: Telegram Bot API Exfiltration and C2 Channel
suggestion.rationale: Article documents 'Telegram bot API–based external command and control (C2) mechanism that routed communication through Telegram's infrastructure'—explicit alternative C2 channel.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections to api.telegram.org, particularly POST requests with bot token patterns in User-Agent or headers. Alert on uncommon endpoints (/botXXXX/sendMessage). Correlate with process execution context of malware loaders.

suggestion.title: Cloudflare Worker C2 Redirector Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'A Cloudflare Worker acting as a front-end redirector to obscure the actual backend C2 server'—explicit proxy infrastructure indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on connections to *.workers.dev subdomains with beacon-like traffic patterns (irregular intervals, POST-heavy, command echoing). Monitor for TLS/certificate anomalies. Correlate with known malware family C2 traffic signatures.

suggestion.title: Shellcode Injection into Legitimate Executables with Functionality Preservation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Python-based malware development scripts for injecting shellcode into legitimate Windows executables while preserving original functionality'—living-off-the-land evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor legitimate executables (Office, notepad, svchost) loading unusual DLL paths or inline hooks. Detect shellcode signatures (0x55 0x89 0xe5 prologues, NOP sleds) in memory. Alert on CreateRemoteThread/VirtualAllocEx from non-development processes.

suggestion.title: Modular Payload Generator with Iterative EDR Evasion Testing
suggestion.rationale: Article documents 'modular Windows payload loader generator wraps a raw payload in layers of encryption, evasion, and alternative execution techniques' tested against 70+ techniques—signature of sophisticated packer/obfuscation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect iterative file creation patterns (similar names, rapid generation). Alert on executables/DLLs with nested encryption markers, multi-stage deobfuscation. Hunt for development tooling artifacts (payload generator logs, test harnesses) in memory or disk.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing via Cloud Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'sustain long-lived Command and Control (C2) operations' and uses cloud services to 'evade detection.' Beaconing is the canonical C2 detection pattern; pipeline should have identified this from narrative keywords and generated the UC. Article even provides Splunk SPL and KQL templates as reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag periodic outbound connections from single source to single external destination (especially cloud IPs: AWS, GCP, Azure, Cloudflare) with consistent timing intervals (30–600 sec), low variance, and count > 30 per window. Correlate with process anomalies (unexpected child processes, system-process network activity, scheduled tasks).

suggestion.title: File Hash Malware Detection — Installation Phase
suggestion.rationale: Article provides MD5 IOC (1af33e1657631357c73119488045302c) under 'Indicators of Compromise' and references 'File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match' detection template. Pipeline failed to extract the IOC or generate corresponding file-matching UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for file creation, execution, or modification matching MD5 1af33e1657631357c73119488045302c across endpoints. Prioritize suspicious execution contexts: non-admin users, unconventional file paths, scheduled tasks, child processes of Office/browser, use of LOLBins (rundll32, certutil, regsvcs, wmi). Flag command-line indicators: curl, wget, powershell download patterns.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion — Malicious Traffic Masquerading via Trusted Cloud Providers
suggestion.rationale: Article core: 'weaponizing trusted cloud infrastructure... to camouflage malicious traffic, evade detection.' Masquerading (T1008) via cloud provider abuse is the attack mechanism but pipeline missed it as a distinct detection use case. T1008 not listed in techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTPS/DNS to known cloud provider infrastructure (AWS S3, GCP Cloud Storage, Azure Blob, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub) from endpoints without legitimate business use. Build per-user and per-department baselines. Alert on: encrypted tunnels to cloud IPs, SNI/Host header mismatches (domain-fronting), unusual traffic volume to cloud infrastructure, traffic from unexpected process parents.

suggestion.title: Long-Lived C2 Session Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'long-lived Command and Control (C2) operations.' Standard periodic-beaconing detection (30–600 sec intervals) misses persistent or multi-hour sessions that require connection-duration-based analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect connections open for abnormal durations (> 1 hour) to the same external IP/domain, especially cloud infrastructure. Look for bidirectional low-rate data transfer consistent with interactive command shells or command-response channels. Use payload entropy and inter-packet timing to distinguish legitimate streaming (video, backups) from encoded command traffic.

suggestion.title: DNS Protocol Abuse — Command Tunneling via Cloud Resolvers
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1071.004 (DNS) but pipeline generated no DNS-specific detection UC. Attackers may tunnel commands through DNS queries to public cloud resolvers (8.8.8.8, 1.1.1.1, Cloudflare) to evade firewall inspection, especially relevant given the 'cloud evasion' theme.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DNS queries for: unusually long or high-entropy domain names, frequent queries to random subdomains under same parent domain, queries from endpoints to public cloud resolvers (not standard corporate DNS), or DNS activity from hosts that normally don't perform external queries. Correlate query frequency/timing with suspected data exfiltration or command execution timelines.

suggestion.title: T3 Protocol Exploitation Against Oracle WebLogic
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker with network access via T3, IIOP to compromise Oracle WebLogic Server' with 1,592 exposed instances tracked by Shodan. Pipeline ignored the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for T3 protocol traffic (ports 7001–7002) to Oracle WebLogic servers, especially unauthenticated connection attempts or unusual payload patterns. Correlate source IPs with known scanner signatures and alert if destination matches vulnerable versions 12.2.1.4.0 or 14.1.1.0.0.

suggestion.title: IIOP Protocol Exploitation Against Oracle WebLogic
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names IIOP as exploitation vector alongside T3. Pipeline missed this alternate attack surface entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect IIOP traffic (ports 7002–7003) to vulnerable WebLogic servers. Flag abnormal object serialization patterns, failed handshakes, and unusual request sizes characteristic of CVE-2024-21182 exploitation.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Oracle WebLogic Asset Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies specific vulnerable versions 12.2.1.4.0 and 14.1.1.0.0 with quantified exposure (1,592 servers via Shodan). Pipeline did not generate asset-inventory detection for vulnerable software versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate WebLogic processes and extract version strings from command-line arguments, startup logs, or binary metadata. Alert if versions match 12.2.1.4.0 or 14.1.1.0.0 and flag for immediate patching per BOD 22-01 requirements.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Data Exfiltration from WebLogic
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle WebLogic Server accessible data.' Pipeline missed data-access and exfiltration detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large sequential database queries, bulk data exports, or unusual file-read activity originating from WebLogic application server processes post-exploitation. Correlate with detected exploitation attempts and alert on large outbound transfers.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Lateral Movement from Compromised WebLogic
suggestion.rationale: Article notes '12 [Oracle flaws] have been abused in ransomware attacks' and CISA warns this is a 'frequent attack vector.' Pipeline did not flag lateral-movement or credential-access use cases typical of ransomware post-exploitation chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After WebLogic compromise, detect credential dumping from Java process memory, authentication anomalies to domain controllers, unusual RDP/SSH sessions from WebLogic server, and scanning for adjacent systems. Alert on service creation or scheduled-task execution from compromised host.

suggestion.title: Child Process Execution from WebLogic Java Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'completely access to all Oracle WebLogic Server accessible data' implying code execution, but pipeline did not generate runtime-behavior detection for process spawning or injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for shell (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash) or utility process spawning from java.exe/weblogic.jar parent. Alert on process-hollowing, DLL-injection, or code-cave modification of Java runtime. Flag network-callback attempts from child processes.

suggestion.title: CVE-2022-0492 Vulnerability Detection — Scanner Hits
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mandates 'CVE: CVE-2022-0492 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' This is the primary detection signal for unpatched systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanners identifying CVE-2022-0492 on Linux systems. Article emphasizes patch lag even for known-patched systems; assume exploitable unless recently verified patched and booted.

suggestion.title: cgroups v1 release_agent Privilege Escalation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies attack vector: 'privilege escalation via the cgroups v1 release_agent feature.' Undetected, this is the path from user→root.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unprivileged processes opening /sys/fs/cgroup/*/release_agent for write, or spawning shells immediately following cgroup-related syscalls. Correlation: low-priv process → cgroup file write → root-owned child process.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure Hunt: Unpatched Linux CVE-2022-0492
suggestion.rationale: Article references asset-exposure hunt template and stresses 'patch lag is the silent killer' with CISA federal due date 2026-06-05. This is the canonical preventive detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run templated asset-exposure hunt for CVE-2022-0492: identify Linux systems with kernel versions <patched, missing recent scans, or open remediation tickets past federal due date. Cross-check against network exposure (public IPs, open SSH/HTTP).

suggestion.title: Kernel Improper Authentication via Cgroup Exploit Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'improper authentication vulnerability' enabled by cgroups mechanism. Full chain: exposed Linux → exploit kernel flaw → escalate privilege.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for low-privilege process (container, service account, web app) executing privilege-escalation sequence: stat/open cgroup v1 paths, write release_agent, trigger callback, spawn root shell. Flag anomalous kernel-boundary crossings.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation: Unexpected Root Process Ancestry
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of CVE-2022-0492 results in unauthorized privilege escalation. Detect when non-root ancestor yields root-owned child with no sudo/polkit trace.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process trees where parent UID ≠ 0 spawns child UID = 0 without setuid binary, sudo, or systemd-run in process chain. Correlate with cgroup file access in preceding 5 seconds.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Cgroup Daemon or Agent Process
suggestion.rationale: release_agent exploits kernel's ability to execute commands outside normal privilege boundaries. Detect unauthorized daemon spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process creation where cgroup subsystem triggers execution (release_agent callback), particularly if spawned binary is not a standard kernel utility or if parent PID is 1 or orphaned. Monitor for anomalous /sys/fs/cgroup file writes by non-root.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner: CVE-2025-48595 Unpatched Android Framework
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'match against your vulnerability scanner' and 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-05.' Patch lag is a named concern. Pipeline missed the canonical asset-exposure UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Android Framework instances (managed devices, containerized apps, vendor firmware) still reporting vulnerable versions of CVE-2025-48595. Cross-check against patch-management logs and OS version telemetry. Flag any device past the 2026-06-05 federal deadline.

suggestion.title: Android Privilege Escalation Detection: Suspicious LPE Behavior Post-Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows for local privilege escalation'—this is the impact phase and requires behavioral detection of abnormal elevation attempts, not just asset scanning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous privilege-escalation sequences on Android devices: unexpected spawning of UID 0 processes from user-space apps, SELinux denials followed by capability exploitation, or memory-protection bypasses. Correlate with known Android root-kit signatures.

suggestion.title: Integer Overflow Exploitation Signature: Memory Corruption Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'integer overflow vulnerability' as the exploitation vector. This specific technique should have its own detection hypothesis tied to memory-access anomalies or application crashes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag application crashes or memory-access violations (buffer overflow signatures, unaligned pointer dereferences) in Android Framework processes immediately preceding privilege-escalation events. Integer overflows often leave detectable traces in heap dumps or coredumps.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Monitoring: Post-Deadline Vulnerability Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Federal deadline '2026-06-05' is operationally critical and article emphasizes auditor/regulator scrutiny. Pipeline should generate a compliance-driven detection that flags devices not compliant by deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After 2026-06-05, any Android Framework instance still at pre-patch version triggers a high-priority alert. Correlate with risk-scoring to distinguish lab/dev instances (lower severity) from production. Report weekly non-compliance rate to CISO for federal compliance tracking.

suggestion.title: Brute Force / Credential Stuffing Against Password Manager Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Brute-Force Attack' as primary attack vector. Pipeline generated zero use cases for T1110 family. This is the foundational attack step that should trigger credential access detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Dashlane authentication endpoints for velocity anomalies: >5 failed login attempts per account within 300 seconds, or >20 failed attempts across multiple distinct accounts from single source IP within 600 seconds. Credential stuffing shows characteristic pattern of low success rate initially, then spike on valid credential match.

suggestion.title: Vault Exfiltration / Download by Compromised Account
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Encrypted Vaults...Downloaded' — describes post-compromise data extraction. Pipeline failed to surface detection use case for vault retrieval/export following brute-force success.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful authentication with immediate vault download or export API calls (within 60 minutes). Alert on vault access from unusual context: VPN/proxy IP, off-hours, device not in account history, or download size exceeding user's typical vault. Monitor for bulk API calls consistent with account enumeration.

suggestion.title: Account Takeover Detection via Login Anomaly Baseline
suggestion.rationale: Fewer than 20 users compromised indicates selective targeting. Pipeline did not identify behavioral deviation detections for detecting compromised password manager accounts post-breach.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish per-account baseline of normal login patterns (time-of-day, geography, device type, MFA method). Flag logins deviating from baseline within 72 hours of password manager breach disclosure. Correlate baseline deviations with failed login spikes from overlapping IP blocks to identify compromised credentials being exploited.

suggestion.title: WinRAR Archive Extraction Followed by Suspicious Child Process
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Gamaredon Exploits WinRAR to Deliver'—should detect WinRAR.exe spawning unexpected executables or script interpreters post-extraction, a hallmark of delivery-chain exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for WinRAR.exe (or unrar.exe) parent spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or direct .exe files with low prevalence. Look for extracted files landing in %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, or unusual archive paths followed by immediate execution within <60s.

suggestion.title: GammaWorm/GammaSteel Malware Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title names malware families explicitly (GammaWorm, GammaSteel) but pipeline extracted zero process-level IOCs. Should detect by process name, parent-child relationships, and behavioral signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for process creation with image name containing 'gamma' variants (case-insensitive) or parent-child chain consistent with WinRAR → malware droplet pattern. Monitor for suspicious command-line arguments (encoded scripts, C2 beacons).

suggestion.title: Registry Run/Startup Key Creation by Malware Dropper
suggestion.rationale: Gamaredon campaigns typically establish persistence via registry autostart; article targets Ukrainian entities (state interest in persistence) but pipeline generated no persistence-layer detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for registry modifications to HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run or HKLM variants spawned by processes originating from %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, or Downloads folders. Alert on child process execution from registry-populated paths.

suggestion.title: C2 Beacon Communication from Malware-Spawned Process
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation malware must phone home; title implies multi-stage delivery (exploit → dropper → payload) but pipeline produced no C2 detection layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious process (GammaWorm/GammaSteel) with outbound connections on non-standard HTTP/S ports or to IP space geolocated to hosting providers known to host Russian APT infrastructure. Flag connections from processes spawned by decompression or script execution chains.

suggestion.title: PowerShell Script Execution from Archive Extraction Context
suggestion.rationale: Gamaredon frequently uses PowerShell for post-compromise execution; article describes WinRAR exploit delivery but pipeline missed script execution detection use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for powershell.exe spawned by WinRAR or from %TEMP% folder paths, especially with encoded/obfuscated command-line arguments (ExecutionPolicy bypass, IEX, downloadstring patterns). Correlate timing with archive extraction events.

suggestion.title: Android Framework Component Code Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CVE-2025-48595: 'Local attackers can exploit the actively abused high-severity Android Framework vulnerability...to gain code execution and escalate privileges on devices running Android 14 or later.' No detection rule generated for the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned from Framework system services, abnormal memory access patterns in system_app context, or privilege transitions from Framework daemons to elevated credentials. Flag exploitation attempts via anomalous bytecode execution or JNI method invocations outside normal app lifecycle.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation from Unprivileged Android Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes escalation outcome: 'Local attackers can...escalate privileges on devices running Android 14 or later' and 'critical security vulnerability...that could lead to remote escalation of privilege.' No detection for abnormal privilege boundary violations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected capability escalation (CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH, CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE) granted to user-space apps or system_app processes on Android 14+. Monitor for root-level process spawning outside recovery/update contexts.

suggestion.title: Android Device Patch Non-Compliance for CVE-2025-48595
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'other vendors will often take longer to test and tweak [patches]' and establishes vulnerability window: 'devices running Android 14 or later' without June 2026 patches. No asset-based detection for unpatched inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all Android devices with OS version 14.0 or later that lack June 2026-01 or June 2026-05 security patch level. Cross-reference with MDM enrollment to identify at-risk corporate endpoints and surface them for urgent patching.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Spyware Installation Following Android Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'similar flaws have been exploited in the past by commercial spyware and by nation-state operations targeting high-profile or high-interest individuals.' No detection for persistence mechanisms or spyware installation post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious app installation events outside Google Play Store on patched/vulnerable devices. Flag creation of hidden services, unusual permission grants (LOCATION+CONTACTS+INTERNET together), scheduled background execution, or system app modifications in app-data directories.

suggestion.title: Targeted Spearphishing Delivery to High-Profile Users
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies threat targeting: 'commercial spyware and by nation-state operations targeting high-profile or high-interest individuals' with 'limited, targeted exploitation.' No detection for phishing vectors or targeting pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spearphishing emails targeting executive/high-value account holders with Android security update lures or device management enrollment links. Monitor for clicks on fake update portals preceding device compromise indicators; correlate email delivery patterns to compromised endpoints.

suggestion.title: Qualcomm Display Driver Exploitation (CVE-2026-21385)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions: 'zero-day flaw in a Qualcomm display component (CVE-2026-21385) in March, all of which were tagged as under limited, targeted exploitation.' Distinct attack surface (graphics driver) with no corresponding detection rule.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Qualcomm display driver (mdp, dpu, msm_drm) restart cycles, segmentation faults, or privilege escalation originating from GPU rendering contexts. Flag unexpected kernel module loads or privilege transitions from display service subsystems.

suggestion.title: Android Patch Compliance Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies '124 Flaws' patched in 'Google June 2026 Android Update.' Pipeline must detect non-compliance via patch deployment tracking. Article: 'Google June 2026 Android Update Patches 124 Flaws.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Android security patch dates and build numbers. Flag devices with security patch level earlier than June 2026, indicating non-deployment of critical update covering 124 vulnerabilities.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Detection Against Actively Exploited Android CVE
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly flags 'One Actively Exploited' vulnerability among the patches, indicating real-world attack campaigns. Pipeline must detect exploitation attempts. Article: 'One Actively Exploited.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous process spawning, capability escalation, memory corruption patterns, and suspicious system calls on Android devices. Correlate behavioral indicators with known Android exploit signatures and malware execution chains.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Android Vulnerability Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Patch volume of 124 flaws indicates multiple privilege escalation vectors. Pipeline should infer and detect PE techniques typical of Android vulnerability exploits.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected capability escalation, SELinux context transitions, and permission elevation. Flag processes gaining kernel-level access or running with elevated privileges from initially unprivileged contexts.

suggestion.title: Android Malware Exploitation Campaign Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article's mention of 'actively exploited' flaw indicates known malware families are weaponizing these Android CVEs in campaigns. Pipeline should correlate to threat actors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Android malware families and threat campaigns known to exploit these specific vulnerabilities. Monitor for malware hashes, behavioral signatures, and network C2 communications associated with Android exploitation.

suggestion.title: Android Sandbox Escape Post-Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: High-severity (CRIT) update with 124 patches typically includes sandbox/isolation breakout vulnerabilities. Pipeline should detect sandbox escape indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes accessing kernel memory (/dev/kmem, /proc/kcore), loading kernel modules, or reaching system files outside app sandbox boundaries. Flag abnormal kernel execution or memory access from app context.

suggestion.title: Git Repository Tag/Branch Rewrite on Trusted Packages
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Rewritten'—attacker modified version tags post-publication. Pipeline missed detection for unauthorized git history rewrites.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer package repositories for unexpected commits to existing tags, version branches, or release refs. Alert on tag deletions + recreations or commit rewrites affecting published stable versions. Correlate with unusual service-account activity or IP changes.

suggestion.title: CI/CD Credential Theft via Injected Package Code
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies attack goal was 'Steal CI Secrets'. Pipeline failed to generate a UC for credential exfiltration from compromised dependency execution in CI pipelines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP/Composer package post-install scripts or autoload files making unexpected calls to env vars (CI tokens, AWS keys, GitHub PATs). Flag exfiltration to attacker-controlled domains, unusual curl/wget from package code execution context, or env dumps to public repositories.

suggestion.title: Composer.lock Version Mismatch / Unexpected Dependency Resolution
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks succeed when developers unknowingly pull poisoned versions. Pipeline should flag UC for detecting version skew between lock file and resolved packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer install/update operations for version mismatches between declared constraints in composer.json and resolved versions in composer.lock. Flag pulls of versions not matching published semantic versioning, or installs from fork/mirror repos.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Service Account Activity on Package Repository
suggestion.rationale: Attacker needed credentials or session hijacking to rewrite tags. Pipeline should detect lateral movement or account compromise on artifact/package repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on repository service-account logins from unusual IPs, timezones, or user-agent strings. Detect high-volume tag/branch modifications in short timeframes, or API token usage outside normal CI/CD patterns.

suggestion.title: Mass Multi-Package Repository Changes in Rapid Succession
suggestion.rationale: Title emphasizes 'Multiple Composer Packages'—attacker rewrote many packages likely in coordinated fashion. Pipeline missed pattern-based UC for bulk supply-chain tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect batches of commits/tags across multiple related packages (Laravel-Lang namespace) by the same actor within minutes, with identical commit messages or patterns. Correlate timeline with known maintenance windows to flag out-of-band changes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Post-Install Script Execution in PHP Package
suggestion.rationale: Composer packages can execute arbitrary scripts on install. Article describes code injection; pipeline should flag UC for detecting malicious autoload/post-install hooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Composer post-install-cmd and post-update-cmd hooks for spawning unexpected interpreters (bash, curl, wget) or making network calls. Flag scripts writing to system paths, editing CI config, or accessing credential stores.

suggestion.title: Unusual code commit by service principal or automation account
suggestion.rationale: Article title emphasizes 'securing code...across the development lifecycle'—implies supply chain attack risk. Development automation abuse is a primary attack path into codebases. No UC generated despite this being core to agent/CICD security.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect commits or pushes originating from service principals, automation accounts, or IP ranges inconsistent with normal developer locations. Correlate with unusual code patterns (mass deletions, permission changes, secrets additions). Flag commits bypassing code review policies.

suggestion.title: Suspicious model or agent configuration deployment
