suggestion.title: npm Worm Self-Propagation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Keywords and description emphasize 'worm propagation' in npm supply chain. Pipeline missed detection for compromised packages modifying package.json or lock files to inject themselves as dependencies in downstream projects, enabling auto-propagation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized writes to package.json, package-lock.json, or .npmrc during npm execution. Detect package installation steps that append new dependencies or modify dependency versions. Correlate with subsequent package publishes by developer accounts.

suggestion.title: Device Code Phishing OAuth Token Theft
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'device code phishing, which abuses a legitimate OAuth flow to bypass MFA and passkeys entirely, has surged from a research curiosity to an industrialized PhaaS offering, with more than 18 kits being actively tracked in the wild.' This is a named, quantified, and active attack flow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect OAuth device code grant flows in sign-in logs, especially those without matching corporate device registration or from unexpected geolocations. Alert on successful device code auth immediately followed by token refresh, unusual OAuth app consent, or MFA bypass indicators. Monitor for clusters of device code attempts across multiple user accounts within short time windows.

suggestion.title: Shadow AI Tool File Exfiltration (Non-Corporate Account)
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Of file uploads to AI tools, 38% are made from personal shadow accounts rather than organizational ones' and '67% using non-corporate accounts.' Explicitly quantified exfiltration behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cloud app activity for file uploads to public AI services (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, etc.) when accessed via personal accounts on corporate devices. Correlate with clipboard paste events and document classification to infer sensitive data exfiltration. Flag accounts showing patterns of data staging and upload to out-of-policy services.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Search-Result Malvertising Click-Through
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'ClickFix is an even clearer example, where 4 in 5 payloads arrive specifically through search engine results' with 'InstallFix and ConsentFix' variants. Specific delivery mechanism and family variants named.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect search-engine-referred clicks that land on suspicious clone pages or malware-hosting domains. Flag on rapid sequential clicks to search results followed by executable download prompts, browser overlay consent dialogs, or JavaScript `document.write()` calls. Correlate referrer (search) with landing domain reputation.

suggestion.title: LLMShare Legitimate AI Link Abuse Malvertising
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'attackers were malvertising the links via search engine ads... using legitimate chatgpt.com sharing links, creating a convincing ad that is impossible to spot from just looking at the URL.' Technique leverages legitimate AI infrastructure as delivery vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for search engine referrals to known AI chat sharing domains (chat.openai.com/share, etc.) that contain embedded malicious shared chats or redirect chains. Detect via TLS inspection of shared chat content or inspection of secondary HTTP redirects from within the shared context. Flag if shared chat contains malicious prompt injection or credential harvesting mechanics.

suggestion.title: Unapproved AI Browser Extension Installation & Context Exfil
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'AI browser extensions collect browsing context from internal applications, creating a data exfiltration path that operates outside traditional DLP.' Explicitly identified as unmonitored exfiltration vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for installation of AI-labeled or AI-related browser extensions with high outbound network volume. Correlate extension network activity with browsing history (visits to internal apps, cloud services) to infer context exfiltration. Flag if extension uploads high-entropy or structured data to external hosts not on allow-list.

suggestion.title: Doko's Panel / ShinyHunters / BlackFile AitM Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article names: 'Doko's Panel and derivative kits, used extensively by ShinyHunters and BlackFile.' These are attributed, tracked threat actors with named tooling producing industrialized account takeover.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious TLS certificates on common SaaS/OAuth domains or unusual reverse-proxy patterns indicative of AitM phishing kits. Detect via certificate pinning violations, mismatched TLS issuer chains, or re-submission of credentials within a single session. Alert on IPs/ASNs known to host derivative Doko panels or ShinyHunters infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Steam Profile C2 Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'hiding command instructions inside Steam Community profile comments' and 'turning a popular gaming platform into a covert control channel'—detection must target HTTP/HTTPS connections to steamcommunity.com/profiles or /id/ endpoints with parsing of response bodies for command injection patterns, not just connection frequency.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify outbound connections to steamcommunity.com/profiles/* or steamcommunity.com/id/* URLs originating from WordPress servers, particularly with response payloads containing command-like syntax (base64, hex, script fragments). Correlate to malware execution events on same host.

suggestion.title: WordPress Malware Execution Post-Infection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'malware campaign targeting WordPress websites'—but no detection for the infection/execution phase itself. Pipeline missed T1189 (Service Exploitation) entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect WordPress child process spawning (apache/nginx → php → cmd.exe/bash), suspicious file modifications under /wp-content/, /wp-plugins/, or wp-config.php, or PHP eval() execution triggered from web requests. Correlate with outbound connections to hello-mywordl.info.

suggestion.title: Malicious Domain Registration Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'hello-mywordl.info' as malware C2 infrastructure. Pipeline must link domain registration timestamps/registrar patterns to WordPress malware campaigns and track first-contact with infected hosts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag new domain registrations matching patterns of malware C2 infrastructure (typosquatted domains, newly registered with generic registrars, bulk registration with identical privacy settings). Correlate to compromised WordPress site IPs within 7 days of registration.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from WordPress Admin
suggestion.rationale: Article implies data exfiltration via malware but does not specify mechanism. Common WordPress malware pattern is stealing admin credentials or database access. Pipeline should infer T1110 (Brute Force) or T1040 (Sniffing) variants.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple failed WordPress login attempts from single source IP followed by successful auth; or detection of database.php access patterns indicating credential exfiltration; or wp-admin POST requests with suspicious parameters typical of credential-stealing plugins.

suggestion.title: COM Hijacking Registry Modification for InprocServer32
suggestion.rationale: The malware uses COM hijacking to persist on the victim's machine, replacing the InprocServer32 entry for Windows Color System Calibration Loader DLL. This task is triggered when the user logs in, effectively allowing the malware to run at startup.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor registry modifications to HKLM/HKCU\Software\Classes\CLSID\*\InprocServer32 where data points to non-System32 locations. Correlate with DLL load events and logon timing to identify startup persistence.

suggestion.title: Base64-Encoded PowerShell Execution from Injected DLL
suggestion.rationale: natives2_blob.bin file is a DLL that executes a Base64-encoded PowerShell script when loaded. The PowerShell script performs basic checks for controlled environments before downloading Stage 2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag PowerShell invocation with Base64-encoded parameters from DLL parent process or game directory context. Include query for WMI/registry sandbox detection patterns in script content.

suggestion.title: Modified FFmpeg DLL with Malicious Native Import
suggestion.rationale: Modified FFmpeg DLL (SHA1: 42add9475e67a1ccc6a6af94b5475d3defc01b85) imported the DllGetClassObject function from natives2_blob.bin. The legitimate game requires ffmpeg.dll to run, guaranteeing execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on FFmpeg.dll file hash mismatch against known-good versions. Flag DLL import of suspicious .bin files (natives2_blob) from game process. Correlate with abnormal child process spawning.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Environment Enumeration Before Malware Activation
suggestion.rationale: The Stage1 PowerShell script performs basic checks for controlled environments before the implant downloads the Stage 2 Trojan, indicating sandbox evasion logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell queries to WMI classes (Win32_ComputerSystem, Win32_BaseBoard) or registry paths (VirtualBox, VMware, Xen) before outbound network activity. Temporal gap between execution and first C2 suggests evasion delays.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Download Several Days After Initial Infection
suggestion.rationale: After a few days, the implant downloads and executes a Trojan, resulting in full system compromise and broad remote control capabilities. Clear two-stage attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for executable downloads from persistent process (InprocServer32 context) after multi-day lag. Flag outbound connections from logon-triggered DLL execution; correlate absence of user action with network I/O.

suggestion.title: Hentai Game Archive Distribution via File-Sharing Services
suggestion.rationale: Trojanized games distributed via PixelDrain file transfer service and torrent trackers (AniRena). Archives contained legitimate game files alongside malicious DLLs, blending payload with legitimate content.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block or alert on downloads from known adult file-sharing infrastructure (PixelDrain, AniRena) of game archives. Post-extraction, scan for natives2_blob.bin or hash mismatch on bundled ffmpeg.dll.

suggestion.title: npm Preinstall Script Suspicious Child Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly references 'preinstall' attack vector; article describes malicious scripts executing during package installation. Pipeline generated zero execution-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm/node processes spawning shells (powershell.exe, cmd.exe) or curl/wget during package install phases. Preinstall scripts should have limited process spawning; flag deviations from baseline npm install behavior.

suggestion.title: Credential File Access from Package Installation Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'steals credentials from GitHub, cloud platforms, and local machines'—credential access is core objective but zero CA-phase detections exist.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm/node processes accessing ~/.git, ~/.aws, ~/.azure, ~/.ssh, HKEY_CURRENT_USER registry hives during package installation. Timestamp correlation with preinstall execution and credential exfiltration patterns.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Republishing Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack spreading 'like a worm by republishing trusted packages'—persistence and lateral-movement via supply-chain injection. Zero detections for abnormal package registry activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm publish/push API calls to registries from CI/CD or developer environments. Flag version bumps on established packages with minimal deltas, re-publishes from new accounts, or registry authentication from unusual locations.

suggestion.title: CI/CD Secret Exfiltration via npm Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack 'silently infects CI/CD environments'—no detections for env-var harvesting in CI/CD context where secrets are injected by build systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In CI/CD pipelines, detect npm/node processes accessing GITHUB_TOKEN, CI_COMMIT_TOKEN, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AZURE_CREDENTIALS, or other injected secrets, followed by unexpected outbound HTTPS connections.

suggestion.title: npm Registry Authentication Token Theft
suggestion.rationale: Republishing malicious packages requires stolen npm auth credentials. Article implies token exfiltration but pipeline captured zero credential-access detections for .npmrc files or npm auth tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor access to ~/.npmrc, in-memory reads of npm_authtoken or _authToken from npm config, and processes enumerating npm registry credentials. Correlate with subsequent npm publish operations.

suggestion.title: Abnormal package.json/lock File Modification During Installation
suggestion.rationale: Worm-like spreading implies package manifest manipulation. Pipeline should detect preinstall/postinstall scripts modifying dependency files—a clear supply-chain escalation signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag modifications to package.json, package-lock.json, or yarn.lock occurring during npm install phases. Detect when installation scripts alter manifests, add transitive dependencies, or change registry URLs.

suggestion.title: Forced NTLM Authentication via Malicious URI Scheme
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Attackers Steal NTLMv2 Hashes' via URI—classic forced-auth pattern. Pipeline missed T1187 entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Windows Search (searchindexer.exe, SearchProtocolHost.exe) initiating outbound connections to non-Microsoft hosts or making unauthenticated NTLM requests to unexpected shares/IPs. Alert on credential submission events tied to URI-handler invocations, especially if followed by NTLM Type-2/Type-3 exchanges over port 445 or 139.

suggestion.title: Windows Search Process Accessing Malicious UNC Paths
suggestion.rationale: URI vulnerability likely triggers Windows Search to access attacker-controlled UNC paths (\\attacker-ip\share). Article mentions 'URI Vulnerability' but pipeline identified no file-access baselines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Windows Search processes (searchindexer.exe, Windows.Search.exe) connecting to unknown or untrusted UNC paths, especially paths with high entropy names or IPs outside internal ranges. Baseline normal Search Index locations and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: NTLM Relay Attack from Windows Search Context
suggestion.rationale: NTLMv2 hash capture is a pre-cursor to relay attacks (T1557.002). Pipeline did not surface lateral-movement or C2 follow-on implications.
log_sources: SecurityEvent (4624: Logon, 4625: Failed Logon with NTLM)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If captured NTLMv2 hashes are relayed, watch for: (1) NTLM authentication from unexpected source IPs tied to Windows Search machine, (2) lateral logons using accounts that don't normally traverse network paths, (3) repeated NTLM auth attempts to multiple targets in short window (SMB relay footprint).

suggestion.title: Process Hooking / Handler Registration for URI Schemes
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'URI Vulnerability'—attacker likely registers malicious handler or triggers Search to parse specially-crafted URI. No detection for handler manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor modifications to HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\URL Handlers and HKCU equivalents for new or suspicious URI scheme registrations. Alert on handler commands pointing to writable paths, LOLBins, or script interpreters.

suggestion.title: Credential Material in Windows Search Cache
suggestion.rationale: Article outcome is hash theft—hashes may be cached in Search index, temp files, or event logs. Pipeline missed data-at-rest detection angle.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan Windows Search index and temporary directories for plaintext or weakly-encoded NTLM hashes, UNC paths with credentials, or auth material. Compare captured hashes against known corporate password lists to gauge breach scope.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Spawning from searchindexer.exe
suggestion.rationale: Exploited vulnerability may achieve RCE through Windows Search. Article doesn't rule out code execution; pipeline ignored execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by searchindexer.exe, Windows.Search.exe, or SearchProtocolHost.exe—especially cmd.exe, powershell.exe, net.exe, or outbound-capable tools. Baseline normal child processes and treat deviations with suspicion.

suggestion.title: Phishing to github.dev Exploitation Landing
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers to steal GitHub authentication tokens by tricking users into clicking a link' — initial vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for phishing emails/messages with github.dev URLs or redirect chains to github.dev. Alert on github.dev access from users without recent GitHub repository interaction history or from geographies inconsistent with baseline.

suggestion.title: Malicious VS Code Extension Installation via Webview Simulation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'running malicious JavaScript inside a webview to simulate keypresses in the main editor and install an extension' — core execution mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for VS Code extension installations triggered shortly after postMessage() calls from webview contexts or untrusted origins. Alert when extensions install to %USERPROFILE%\.vscode\extensions without preceding user consent dialogs or when installation follows synthetic input event sequences.

suggestion.title: GitHub OAuth Token Exfiltration from Browser Storage
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'github.com POSTing over an OAuth token to github.dev...the token...has full access to every other repo that you have access to' — describes token interception and scope abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests from Chromium/VS Code processes to github.com/github.dev containing Authorization headers or bearer tokens. Alert on unscoped or full-scope GitHub tokens transmitted to unexpected destinations immediately after webview activity.

suggestion.title: GitHub Private Repository Enumeration via API
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'queries the GitHub API to enumerate all private repositories the victim can access' — post-compromise discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub API calls to /user/repos, /user/installations endpoints from new source IPs or user-agents. Alert on bulk repository enumeration within short timeframes using full-scope tokens, especially from unexpected geographies.

suggestion.title: Synthetic Keypress Injection from Webview Context
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malicious JavaScript inside a webview to simulate keypresses' — technique abuses webview-to-parent process communication for input spoofing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for postMessage() API calls from webview frames sending synthetic keyboard/mouse event payloads to parent VS Code process. Alert when keystroke sequences match known UI navigation patterns (extension installation, authentication).

suggestion.title: github.dev Cookie/Token Persistence Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'clearing cookies and local site data for github.dev' is the recommended mitigation, indicating tokens stored in clearable browser storage despite sensitivity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for VS Code or Chromium processes accessing browser cookie/localStorage directories for github.com/github.dev domains. Alert on reads of sensitive storage locations from JavaScript contexts or unexpected processes.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Miner Process Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly discusses 'Miners Spread via Pirated Content' as impact—miners generate detectable process creation, resource exhaustion, and C2 patterns; pipeline generated zero mining-related detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation events associated with known cryptocurrency miner families (xmrig, monero miners, etc.) spawned from Minecraft or user-writable directories. Correlate with sustained high CPU usage (>80%) and network egress to mining pool IPs. Flag any Minecraft process spawning unexpected child processes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Pirated Content Download and Execution Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article describes initial access as 'Spread via Pirated Content'—should detect suspicious file sources (torrent, warez sites, forums) followed by execution; pipeline provided no initial-access or execution detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file downloads from known piracy hosting/torrent infrastructure followed within 10 minutes by execution of downloaded files. Monitor for Minecraft mod installers or 'game cracks' downloaded to AppData or Downloads, then immediately executed. Alert on parent-child relationships where browser spawns unsigned executable with randomized name.

suggestion.title: CountLoader Malware Artifact Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article headlines 'CountLoader Hits 86K'—a named malware family; pipeline extracted zero IOCs or signatures; should include file hash, registry, process-name, and C2-domain patterns for CountLoader specifically.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create malware artifact catalog for CountLoader: file names, mutation signatures, registry run-keys, mutex names, C2 domains/IPs. Hunt for process trees where CountLoader downloader creates child processes (miners, backdoors). Cross-reference file hashes against public AVs and sandbox detonations to identify variants. Escalate any direct hits or behavioral near-matches.

suggestion.title: Minecraft Process Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article focuses on 'Weedhack Attacks Minecraft Users'—pirated mods or compromised launcher; should detect anomalous Minecraft process behavior (unexpected network egress, child processes, parent process mismatches).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when javaw.exe (Minecraft launcher) initiates outbound connections to non-Mojang IPs, spawns non-Java children (powershell, cmd, miner executables), or reads/modifies registry outside game directories. Baseline Minecraft network behavior per user; flag deviations. Monitor for modified game JAR files with suspicious embedded libraries.

suggestion.title: Mining Pool Communication Detection
suggestion.rationale: Miners exfiltrate value via mining pools; article implies C2/mining-pool communication but pipeline generated no network detection; should flag connections to known Monero/Bitcoin mining pools by IP/domain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain blocklist of known Monero and Bitcoin mining pool FQDN/IP ranges (pools.supportxmr.com, etc.). Alert on any process (especially from Minecraft directory or launched by unprivileged user) connecting to mining pools. Correlate with sustained egress volume and DNS requests to mining-pool infrastructure. Exclude corporate mining operations via allow-list.

suggestion.title: Launcher/Installer Tampering via Compromised Pirated Distributors
suggestion.rationale: Article implies malware packaged in fake or compromised Minecraft installers; should detect file-replacement, directory-traversal, or supply-chain poisoning indicators in game launcher/mod directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Minecraft installation directories (.minecraft, game launcher paths) for unexpected file modifications, new DLLs, or INI/config tampering. Alert on game launcher modifications that alter CLASSPATH, JVM args, or spawn wrapper processes. Detect when game shortcut or launcher registry entry points to non-standard executable or contains malicious parameters.

suggestion.title: Telegram Bot API-Based C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Telegram bot API–based external command and control (C2) mechanism that routed communication through Telegram's infrastructure.' Pipeline extracted zero C2-related use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor processes initiating HTTPS POST requests to api.telegram.org with bot tokens or chat identifiers. Flag unusual parent processes (Python, Go, Rust binaries) making Telegram API calls, especially with repeated beacon intervals or large serialized data in request bodies.

suggestion.title: Cloudflare Worker C2 Front-End Proxy
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'A Cloudflare Worker acting as a front-end redirector to obscure the actual backend C2 server.' Proxy-layer C2 infrastructure was not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect C2 beacon patterns through workers.dev or Cloudflare-proxied domains: repeated POST/GET requests at regular intervals, characteristic request/response sizes, or anomalous data volume for legitimate Cloudflare use.

suggestion.title: Automated Active Directory Reconnaissance via Staged Agent Queries
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'an automated Active Directory (AD) discovery panel' where 'AD discovery is driven by collecting observations from completed tasks and selecting the next action from predefined choices.' Iterative reconnaissance pattern was not surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid-fire LDAP queries or PowerShell Get-AD* commands in sequence (Users → Groups → Computers → SPNs), especially when interspersed with pauses suggesting remote task coordination. Flag bulk enumeration of domain admins, service accounts, and cross-forest trusts.

suggestion.title: Python Payload Generator Spawning Rust/Go Obfuscated Executables
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'a Python tool that generates payloads, mostly in Rust and Go' and 'Close to 80 modules were generated and tested.' Parent-child process pattern (Python → compiled binary) was not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Python processes spawning Rust or Go compiled binaries, particularly from non-standard locations (temp dirs, user profiles). Monitor for unusual argument patterns, absence of expected command-line flags, or execution following file-write activity in the same directory.

suggestion.title: EDR Product Detection and Conditional Payload Selection
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates malware 'tested in virtual environments against EDR tools from Sophos, CrowdStrike, and Microsoft' with framework agents for 'testing' and 'OPSEC hardening.' Detection-aware evasion logic was not addressed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process queries of running services/drivers tied to Sophos/CrowdStrike/Defender (WmiPrvSE checking for SophosED.exe, falcon-sensor, or Sense.exe). Detect branching execution logic: processes that load different modules or DLLs conditionally based on EDR product detection.

suggestion.title: Shellcode Injection into Legitimate Windows Binaries via Python
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Python-based malware development scripts for injecting shellcode into legitimate Windows executables while preserving original functionality.' Process hollowing / code injection pattern was not surfaced as a detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python processes calling VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory, or SetThreadContext on legitimate system binaries (calc.exe, notepad.exe, explorer.exe). Flag legitimate executables spawned with empty or minimal command-line arguments when they normally require options.

suggestion.title: C2 traffic from AWS/Google Cloud/Azure/Cloudflare IP space
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'weaponizing trusted cloud infrastructure, including Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, Cloudflare, and GitHub, to camouflage malicious traffic, evade detection, and sustain long-lived Command and Control.' This is the primary attack vector. No UC addresses C2 from legitimate cloud provider ASNs and IP ranges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from endpoints to AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, and Cloudflare IP CIDR blocks with C2 indicators: small payloads, periodic intervals, anomalous ports for the provider. Baseline legitimate cloud API traffic first.

suggestion.title: DNS exfiltration via cloud DNS services
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies T1071.004 (DNS) as attack technique. Explicitly mentions DNS abuse through trusted cloud providers for command and control. No DNS-specific UC exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS queries with high-entropy domain labels, large TXT/NULL record payloads, or rapid sequential queries targeting AWS Route53, Google Cloud DNS, or Cloudflare DNS endpoints. Decode attempts should trigger alerts.

suggestion.title: HTTPS C2 via CDN/cloud proxy masquerading
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions T1071.001 (Web Protocols) combined with Cloudflare/AWS abuse. Attackers proxy C2 through CDNs to appear legitimate. No UC addresses this channel.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTPS traffic to Cloudflare, CloudFront, or Azure CDN with C2 signal: small payloads, regular timing, unusual URI paths, mismatched SNI/certificate issuer, or certificate pinning anomalies.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated payload delivery via cloud infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information) and emphasizes cloud services as delivery channel. No UC addresses obfuscated content flowing through AWS/Google Cloud/Cloudflare IPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file downloads originating from AWS/Google Cloud/Azure/Cloudflare IPs with obfuscation markers: high entropy, known packer signatures, Base64-encoded streams, or suspicious MIME type mismatches. Correlate with process execution of decoded content.

suggestion.title: Detect Exploitation Attempts on Oracle WebLogic T3 Protocol
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE-2024-21182 is exploitable 'via T3, IIOP' protocols and is 'actively exploited in attacks.' Pipeline generated no detection for this explicit attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious T3 protocol handshakes or malformed T3 packets targeting port 7001 or non-standard WebLogic ports. Baseline legitimate WebLogic-to-WebLogic T3 communication and alert on unauthenticated clients establishing T3 streams.

suggestion.title: Detect Exposed Oracle WebLogic Server Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'Shodan now tracks over 1,592 Oracle WebLogic servers exposed online' and identifies specific vulnerable versions (12.2.1.4.0 and 14.1.1.0.0). Pipeline missed inventory monitoring use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify publicly accessible Oracle WebLogic instances via port scanning telemetry, cloud security posture tools, or version fingerprinting. Correlate with Shodan/Censys data to surface unexpectedly exposed WebLogic services; flag vulnerable versions 12.2.1.4.0 and 14.1.1.0.0 for urgent remediation.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthenticated Access to Oracle WebLogic Admin Console
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'allows unauthenticated attacker with network access' to achieve 'complete access to all Oracle WebLogic Server accessible data.' Pipeline missed auth-bypass detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthenticated HTTP/HTTPS requests to /console, /consolehelp, or other WebLogic management endpoints from external IP ranges. Flag successful responses (200, 302) without prior valid session tokens; correlate with T3/IIOP traffic anomalies.

suggestion.title: Monitor for CVE-2024-21182 Specific Exploitation Signatures
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates 'Easily exploitable vulnerability' with active exploitation ongoing. No signature-based detection rule suggested by pipeline despite clear CVE identifier and exploitation status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deploy signatures or YARA rules targeting CVE-2024-21182 payload patterns in T3/IIOP streams. Monitor for known PoC payloads or characteristic bytecode sequences in network captures; correlate IDS alerts with WebLogic process injection or child-process execution anomalies.

suggestion.title: Detect Post-Compromise Data Access on Compromised WebLogic Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article states successful exploitation 'can result in unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle WebLogic Server accessible data.' Pipeline missed data-exfiltration detection for impact phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual query patterns or bulk data reads from WebLogic application logs and backend databases following a potential compromise window. Baseline normal application data-access behavior and flag high-volume exports, table scans, or lateral database queries from a single WebLogic JVM session.

suggestion.title: Detect Reconnaissance Scanning for Vulnerable WebLogic Versions
suggestion.rationale: Article cites Shodan scanning as the reconnaissance vector ('Shodan now tracks over 1,592 instances'). Pipeline failed to create detection for version-enumeration or banner-grabbing attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound network scanning or HTTP requests specifically designed to fingerprint WebLogic version (e.g., requests to /version, /console with specific User-Agent patterns, or T3 version negotiation probes). Flag external IPs that scan multiple internal WebLogic ports (7001, 7002, 8001, etc.) in rapid succession.

suggestion.title: Asset Inventory: CVE-2022-0492 Patch Compliance Check
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' with template substitution and federal due date 2026-06-05. Pipeline should have generated patch-compliance UC for vulnerability scanners and asset management logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and asset inventory for Linux systems vulnerable to CVE-2022-0492. Even patched systems warrant secondary manual verification due to patch-lag risk. Escalate any unpatched systems with public network exposure ahead of federal due date 2026-06-05.

suggestion.title: cgroups v1 release_agent Unauthorized Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'privilege escalation via the cgroups v1 release_agent feature' — this is the specific exploitation vector and requires targeted detection on the abuse mechanism itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Linux process events for writes to cgroups v1 release_agent paths (/sys/fs/cgroup/*/release_agent) from non-container, non-systemd contexts. Alert on correlations: release_agent write → fork/exec to shell with privilege escalation to root (uid=0).

suggestion.title: Kernel Privilege Escalation to Root from Unprivileged Context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes kernel-level privilege escalation outcome. Detection should capture uid/gid boundary violations (unprivileged → root) on vulnerable systems, especially those matching CVE-2022-0492 profile.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected transitions to uid=0 (root) from non-privileged parent processes on Linux systems vulnerable to CVE-2022-0492. Focus on exploit-like chains: confined process (container/sandbox) → cgroup interaction → privilege boundary violation.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Linux Systems Vulnerable to CVE-2022-0492
suggestion.rationale: Article maps T1190 'Exploit Public-Facing Application', indicating exposed Linux systems are primary targets. Detection should identify which vulnerable systems are reachable from untrusted networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify CVE-2022-0492-vulnerable Linux systems with inbound internet routes or listening on public IPs. Correlate vulnerability-scan data with network exposure metrics. Prioritize systems with oldest kernel versions. Escalate for emergency patching ahead of federal due date.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Detection: CVE-2025-48595
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'match against your vulnerability scanner' and isolates CVE-2025-48595 as the primary indicator. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this direct templated guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when vulnerability scanner detects CVE-2025-48595 on any Android Framework instance. Baseline: zero vulns across fleet. Pivot on vendor/product match (Android/Framework) to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance: CVE-2025-48595 Federal Due Date
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-05' and warns 'patch lag is the silent killer'. Pipeline omitted compliance hunt despite explicit deadline that auditors will cross-reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enforce patch deployment for Android Framework versions vulnerable to CVE-2025-48595 by federal due date. Alert on devices still running vulnerable framework after 2026-06-05. Correlate with scanner to confirm patch effectiveness.

suggestion.title: Local Privilege Escalation: Integer Overflow Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'code execution that could allow for local privilege escalation'. Pipeline kill chain was empty; this is the terminal phase and highest-impact detection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On unpatched Android Framework instances: hunt for unexpected privilege escalation events, out-of-policy native code execution from framework process, or rapid uid/gid changes post-exploitation. Integer overflow exploits often trigger SELinux denials or unusual process ancestry.

suggestion.title: Brute-force attack against password manager accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Brute-Force Attack' in title; pipeline extracted zero use cases. Detection should flag rapid failed login attempts followed by account compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a single account experiences ≥10 failed logins within 5 minutes from distinct IPs, followed by successful auth within 15 minutes. Filter for password manager vendors (Dashlane, 1Password, Bitwarden, LastPass). Baseline against organization's expected login velocity.

suggestion.title: Bulk encrypted vault download from compromised password manager session
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'encrypted vaults of fewer than 20 users downloaded.' Pipeline missed exfiltration phase entirely. Detection needed for large data egress post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag download of >100 MB from password manager endpoints (api.dashlane.com, etc.) by a single session, especially if preceded by failed-login spike or geographic anomaly. Correlate with vault sync operations to reduce FP from legitimate sync.

suggestion.title: Geographically-anomalous authentication to password manager
suggestion.rationale: Article implies unauthorized access; brute-force often succeeds from attacker-controlled infrastructure. Detection should catch logins from unexpected countries post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful login to Dashlane (or similar) from country/city never seen for that user in past 90 days, especially if login occurs during off-hours or from datacenter IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Account compromise indicator: Failed auth spike then large data transfer
suggestion.rationale: Brute-force attack (failed auths) + vault download (data exfil) chain. Pipeline should surface correlation between T1110 and T1041.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate: 5+ failed logins in 30 min on password manager account + successful login + ≥50 MB outbound data transfer within 1 hour. High confidence of account compromise; recommend immediate credential reset and vault audit.

suggestion.title: WinRAR Remote Code Execution Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Exploits WinRAR' — indicates CVE-based RCE vector (likely CVE-2023-38831 or similar). Zero initial-access or execution detection rules generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor rar.exe/WinRAR.exe for spawning unsigned or unexpected child processes, particularly from user temp or Downloads directories. Correlate archive extraction events with suspicious subprocess creation within 5-second window.

suggestion.title: GammaWorm Malware Execution and Propagation
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'GammaWorm' as primary delivered payload. No process execution, behavioral, or family-level detections created.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for GammaWorm file hashes and command-line signatures indicative of worm behavior: file enumeration, network share targeting, or rapid multi-process spawning. Alert on lateral-movement patterns consistent with autonomous propagation.

suggestion.title: GammaSteel Information Stealer Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'GammaSteel' (likely infostealer/stealer malware based on naming convention). Zero behavioral or hash-based detections for this family.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish file hashes for GammaSteel once samples available. Monitor for credential-store queries, browser-data access patterns, %APPDATA% enumeration, or suspicious registry modifications indicative of information-harvesting malware.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Archive Extraction Followed by Child Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: WinRAR exploitation delivery implies crafted archive → user extraction → malware execution. No correlation rules created to detect multi-stage delivery chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate rapid sequence: archive file written → extracted to temp/user directory → unsigned rar.exe child process. Flag if extracted filename or spawned process aligns with malware signatures or known Gamaredon campaign indicators.

suggestion.title: Gamaredon Command and Control Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: High-confidence APT campaign with two deployed malware families lacks network-based C2 detection. No domains, IPs, or behavioral C2 hunting rules generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Once Gamaredon C2 infrastructure is attributed (via OSINT, sandbox analysis, or threat feeds), create DNS/network alerts. Hunt for long-lived connections to suspicious ASNs or historical Gamaredon infrastructure IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Android Framework Privilege Escalation via CVE-2025-48595
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Local attackers can exploit the actively abused high-severity Android Framework vulnerability (tracked as CVE-2025-48595) to gain code execution and escalate privileges on devices running Android 14 or later.' Pipeline generated zero detection for this primary, actively exploited threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Android Framework components for malformed API calls or heap corruption exploits targeting CVE-2025-48595. Alert on unexpected privilege escalation from app context to system context within framework processes on Android 14+ devices; correlate with crash dumps or kernel oops.

suggestion.title: Targeted Exploitation Chain Detection (CVE-2025-48595 + Multi-Component)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'similar flaws have been exploited in the past by commercial spyware and by nation-state operations targeting high-profile or high-interest individuals.' Article also lists 18 critical vulns in System, Framework, Qualcomm. Pipeline missed detection for multi-component exploitation chains used by APTs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid-fire exploitation attempts of multiple CVEs (CVE-2025-48595, CVE-2025-48633, CVE-2025-48572, CVE-2026-21385) on single Android device within 10-minute window. Flag correlations as nation-state targeting signature.

suggestion.title: Critical Android Framework Remote Code Execution Pre-Patch
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'a critical security vulnerability in the Framework component that could lead to remote escalation of privilege with no additional execution privileges needed.' Pipeline failed to surface RCE-without-interaction detection for Framework.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Framework service crash loops preceded by inbound network traffic to vulnerable Framework APIs. Monitor for unexpected privilege context elevation in framework daemon processes following remote input without user interaction.

suggestion.title: Patch Lag Risk for CVE-2025-48595 on Android 14+ Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Exploitation for many issues on Android is made more difficult by enhancements in newer versions. We encourage all users to update to the latest version of Android where possible.' Pipeline missed detection for devices lagging June 2026 patches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Android 14+ devices with security patch level older than June 2026-06-05 as high-risk. Correlate with network segments handling sensitive data or device ownership (C-level, government, researchers).

suggestion.title: Qualcomm Closed-Source Component Exploitation Post-Framework Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'With this month's Android security updates, Google has fixed 18 critical vulnerabilities across System, Framework, and Qualcomm closed-source components.' No detection for chained Framework → Qualcomm exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor kernel module logs for abnormal Qualcomm driver access or memory operations immediately following Framework exploit indicators. Alert on attempts to load out-of-tree kernel modules or manipulate vendor partitions post-Framework compromise.

suggestion.title: Vendor Patch Delay Risk (Non-Pixel Android Devices)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'While Google Pixel devices will receive these security updates immediately, other vendors will often take longer to test and tweak them for specific hardware configurations.' Pipeline missed detection for exposure window on non-Pixel OEM devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track non-Pixel Android device patch application timelines post-June 2026-06-05 release. Flag Samsung, OnePlus, Xiaomi, etc. devices still running pre-patch levels 30+ days after vendor release window closes as vulnerable to actively exploited CVE-2025-48595.

suggestion.title: Detection of Active Android CVE Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'one actively exploited' flaw among 124 patched. Defenders must detect in-flight exploitation before patch deployment closes the window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate baseline Android process crashes, unexpected privilege escalation, or memory corruption signatures with the active CVE identifier. Flag unpatched devices showing exploitation indicators within 7 days of patch release.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Check - June 2026 Android Security Level
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes specific patch version (June 2026). Organizations must rapidly inventory unpatched Android devices to assess exposure to the one active exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all managed Android devices for Security Patch Level < June 2026. Escalate any device older than 30 days post-release without documented mitigation or exemption.

suggestion.title: Android Vulnerability Scanner Activity Post-Patch
suggestion.rationale: Active exploit implies attacker scanning. Monitor for reconnaissance targeting the specific flaw before patch adoption reaches saturation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag reconnaissance patterns (version enumeration, capability probes) targeting the active Android CVE within 2 weeks of patch release. Correlate with failed device patch deployment.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Composer Package Installation from Compromised Tag
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Rewritten' — pipeline missed detection for unexpected composer package pulls or version downgrades to malicious tags during build/CI pipelines
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect composer install/update commands pulling from laravel-lang or related packages with abnormal version numbers, unusual repo URLs, or mismatched hashes. Look for unexpected PHP process spawning with network outbound connections during or immediately after composer execution.

suggestion.title: CI Secret Exfiltration via Composer Hook Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack goal as 'Steal CI Secrets' — pipeline did not suggest detection for malicious code execution within composer post-install scripts or package autoload mechanisms that could harvest environment variables
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP/shell scripts spawned during composer autoload execution accessing CI secrets (GitHub tokens, AWS credentials, Docker registry tokens). Flag unexpected outbound DNS/HTTP from php-cgi or composer processes to non-package-repository destinations.

suggestion.title: Package Repository Tag Integrity Mismatch Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Rewritten' but pipeline extracted no IOCs for hash/signature mismatches or tag tampering that would indicate version substitution
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare composer.lock cryptographic hashes against known-good Packagist signatures. Alert on package version claims that do not match Git tag objects or have mismatched source_reference fields. Detect tag creation/modification on attacker-controlled forks.

suggestion.title: Lateral CI Pipeline Compromise via Shared Package Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: 'Multiple Composer Packages' indicates supply-chain blast radius — pipeline missed detection for cascading compromise across dependent projects when a single compromised intermediate package is installed
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track composer dependency tree and flag projects that pull transitive dependencies from laravel-lang ecosystem. Alert if multiple unrelated projects begin pulling the same suspicious package version within a narrow time window, suggesting coordinated compromise propagation.

suggestion.title: CI Environment Variable Dumping in Build Logs
suggestion.rationale: Stealing CI secrets is stated goal but pipeline provided no detection for common post-compromise behavior of exfiltrating env vars via build logs, echo statements, or artifact uploads
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan CI build logs (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins) for suspicious env var enumeration (printenv, env, compgen), credential-pattern matches (AWS_*, GITHUB_TOKEN, DOCKER_*), or encoding attempts (base64, xxd). Correlate with outbound HTTP/DNS during build execution.

suggestion.title: Composer Autoloader Backdoor Injection via Require Statement Mutation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes code rewritten in package tags — pipeline failed to suggest detection for modified composer autoload entries, require statements, or magic method hooks (__construct, __call) that could execute attacker payloads on package import
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer.json and vendor/autoload.php for suspicious entries (callable hooks, invalid namespaces, remote require statements). Flag PHP files in vendor/ with recent modification timestamps post-package-install. Detect eval(), system(), passthru() calls originating from vendor/ paths.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Nx Console Extension Installation or Update
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes Nx Console was 'compromised'—malicious version distributed via official marketplace. Pipeline should detect when extension is installed or updates to a known-bad version number.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code extensions directory for Nx Console writes, correlate timestamps with user install/update actions. Flag installations from untrusted sources or to versions not in allow-list. Splunk: (parent_image=*Code.exe OR parent_image=*code-insiders.exe) AND (file_path=*nxConsole* OR file_path=*.vscode\extensions*) AND (action=created OR action=modified).

suggestion.title: Code Execution from VS Code Extension Directory
suggestion.rationale: Compromised extension executes malicious payload when loaded. Article describes extension compromise implying code execution via extension runtime—needs detection for child processes spawned from extension paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation where parent=VS Code and child process path is outside normal whitelist, or when parent=code.exe spawns cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or network utilities. Filter known benign extensions. Splunk: ParentImage=*Code.exe (ChildImage=cmd.exe OR ChildImage=powershell.exe OR ChildImage=*curl* OR ChildImage=*wget*) AND NOT (ChildImage IN (known_extensions)).

suggestion.title: Unexpected Network Connections from VS Code Process
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack against extension likely includes C2 exfiltration or data theft. Article describes 'compromised' extension—implies malicious functionality including outbound connections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from VS Code (Code.exe, code.exe, code-insiders.exe) to non-standard ports or newly-registered domains. Baseline normal extension update/telemetry traffic, alert on deviations. Defender KQL: DeviceNetworkEvents | where InitiatingProcessFileName in ('Code.exe','code.exe') and RemotePort !in (443,80) | where RemoteUrl !in (update.code.visualstudio.com, telemetry.*, marketplace.*).

suggestion.title: Nx Console Extension Manifest or Resource Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Compromised extension implies malicious code was injected into package.json, main.js, or bundled assets. Detection should look for unexpected file modifications in extension directory post-installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file writes to .vscode\extensions\nxConsole* directory after extension install completes (baseline normal install window ~30s). Alert on package.json, index.js, or dist/ modifications outside of update windows. Correlate with process events from same parent process.

suggestion.title: VS Code Extension Auto-Start or Persistence Modification
suggestion.rationale: Compromised extension may establish persistence via VS Code settings.json, startup hooks, or launch configurations. Article does not explicitly detail persistence mechanism, but supply-chain malware commonly establishes redundancy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor modifications to .vscode\settings.json, .vscode\extensions.json, and VS Code AppData\Code\User\settings.json for new extension enables, launch args, or startup tasks. Alert if extension is re-enabled after user disable, or if new execute-before-launch tasks are added.

suggestion.title: Staged Payload Delivery via Compromised Extension Update Channel
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks often use extension update mechanism to deliver staged payloads. If article mentions multi-stage delivery or version-based rollout, should detect secondary payload downloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate VS Code extension directory writes with subsequent unexpected outbound HTTP/S requests containing base64, gzip, or obfuscated payloads. Alert on downloads to temp or AppData\Local\Temp from extension parent process, followed by execution.

suggestion.title: Malvertising-Sourced Process Execution on macOS
suggestion.rationale: Article core: 'malvertising campaign targeting macOS users… distributed the new backdoor FlutterShell.' No detection for browser-spawned process creation or unsigned binary execution following ad click.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Safari/Chrome/Firefox spawning child processes (esp. shell, curl, installer) within 5 minutes of browsing advertisement-heavy or compromised domains. Monitor for unsigned binary execution immediately following suspicious web navigation.

suggestion.title: Flutter Runtime Execution from Unexpected Parent
suggestion.rationale: Malware explicitly 'built using the Flutter framework' — no detection for Flutter interpreter or flutter.so library loaded by non-development processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Flutter runtime (flutter, dart, dartaotruntime binaries) spawned from ~/Downloads, /tmp, or browser process parents. Flag loading of libflutter.dylib or embedder dependencies outside official development directories.

suggestion.title: FlutterShell Backdoor C&C Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: BackDoor malware by definition requires persistent command channel. Article provides no detection for outbound C2 traffic or network-based indicators of compromise from FlutterShell.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for persistent or periodic outbound connections from unsigned macOS processes on non-standard ports (>1024, non-HTTP/HTTPS). Flag encrypted traffic with anomalous TLS certificates or custom protocols from processes spawned in malvertising context.

suggestion.title: LaunchAgent Persistence from Downloaded Malware
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor implies persistence installation. Article silent on LaunchAgent/LaunchDaemon abuse, standard macOS persistence vector post-execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation or modification of ~/.config/launchagents/* or /Library/LaunchAgents/* with plist files pointing to recently-downloaded or unsigned binaries. Alert on Flutter-spawned processes writing to launch service directories.

suggestion.title: Code-Signing Bypass Detection for macOS Malware
suggestion.rationale: FlutterShell as novel malware likely lacks valid Apple code signature. Article describes new backdoor with zero mention of signed executables, critical for macOS threat model.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all process execution with invalid/missing Code Signature Authority on macOS. Correlate with browser history, Downloads folder, and /tmp staging. Flag Mach-O binaries with stripped signatures or modified __SIGNATURE segment.

suggestion.title: Ad-Network Domain Redirect Chain to Attacker Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Malvertising campaign vector requires ad-to-attacker redirect. Article identifies malvertising as attack entry but pipeline surfaced zero network-layer detection for redirect chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP 302/301 redirect chains from legitimate advertising domains (doubleclick, adroll, etc.) to attacker-registered infrastructure. Flag rapid domain transitions (>3 hops in <5 seconds) or redirects to non-standard TLDs from trusted ad networks.

suggestion.title: JAR File Execution from User-Writable Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article: '3,820 unique malicious JAR files' distributed via YouTube and downloaded by victims. Attack chain: user downloads to Downloads/Temp → user double-clicks JAR → malware executes. Legitimate Minecraft does not launcher JAR files from user temp paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when java.exe spawns with parent process explorer.exe or cmd.exe and working directory is Downloads, AppData\Local\Temp, or Desktop. Exclude launcher.exe and official mod manager paths (MultiMC, CurseForge launchers). Filter known-good Java applications.

suggestion.title: Browser Credential Store Access by Java Process
suggestion.rationale: Article: malware 'targets... cookies... saved passwords across 36 browsers'. Free tier stealer immediately harvests browser credential databases. Detection targets process file I/O to Chrome/Firefox/Edge credential stores.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when java.exe or javaw.exe opens files in AppData\Local\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\Cookies, AppData\Roaming\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles, AppData\Local\Microsoft\Edge\User Data. High confidence: legitimate Minecraft launcher does not access browser storage.

suggestion.title: Minecraft Session Credential Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: free tier specifically steals 'Minecraft session ID'. Session tokens stored in AppData\.minecraft\launcher_profiles.json or cache. Detection captures this Minecraft-native credential harvesting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when processes other than minecraft-launcher.exe or official Minecraft launchers read AppData\.minecraft\launcher_profiles.json or AppData\.minecraft\launcher.json. Baseline against updates; alert on multiple sequential reads.

suggestion.title: Discord/Steam Token Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: malware steals 'Discord, Steam, and Telegram credentials'. Premium and free tiers target gaming platform auth tokens stored in AppData. Detection monitors access to these credential stores.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when java.exe or minecraft.exe accesses AppData\Roaming\discord (token, cache files) or steamapps\common\* user token files. Correlate with JAR execution within last 1 hour. Exclude legitimate Discord/Steam launchers.

suggestion.title: Webcam Device Access by Minecraft/Java
suggestion.rationale: Article: premium tier ($5/month) adds 'webcam access' feature. Users paying for surveillance capability. Detection targets camera device enumeration or opening by malware process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when java.exe or minecraft.exe attempts to open \Device\Video* or camera devices. Very high confidence finding: Minecraft has no legitimate need for webcam access. Correlate with premium tier indicators if available via process behavior.

suggestion.title: Java Process Outbound C2 to Non-Minecraft Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'dashboard' backend receives stolen credentials; C2 architecture described. '240+ distribution URLs' host payload and exfil backend. Detection captures data exfiltration from Java to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when java.exe initiates outbound TLS or HTTP connections to domains outside {launcher.mojang.com, libraries.minecraft.net, api.mojang.com, sessionserver.mojang.com, textures.minecraft.net}. Flag if domain is <30 days old, hosted on bulletproof host, or lacks legitimate web hosting reputation. Correlate with JAR execution.

suggestion.title: Xeno RAT Process Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'Xeno RAT' as the malware deployed; no execution-phase UC was generated despite this being the campaign's core payload
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Xeno RAT process signatures, including executable name patterns, suspicious command-line arguments, parent-child relationship anomalies, or service installation patterns associated with RAT persistence. Cross-reference against Xeno malware family behavioral indicators.

suggestion.title: SideCopy Spear-Phishing Delivery to Finance Sector
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies SideCopy as Pakistan-linked threat actor known for targeted campaigns against finance/government; no initial-access detection generated despite spear-phishing being the group's signature TTP
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Office macro-enabled documents or password-protected archives delivered via email to Afghanistan Finance Ministry staff. SideCopy historically uses credential-stealing lures. Flag emails with suspicious sender reputation, obfuscated attachments, or urgency language targeting finance personnel.

suggestion.title: Xeno RAT Command-and-Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: Malware name in title indicates C2 callbacks essential to campaign; no command-and-control UC generated despite this being critical for post-compromise attacker control
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections from Finance Ministry hosts to Xeno RAT C2 infrastructure. Detect patterns: non-standard HTTPS ports, DGA activity, frequent DNS failures followed by IP connections, or communications to historically compromised/malicious hosting providers linked to SideCopy.

suggestion.title: Credential Theft from Finance Ministry Systems
suggestion.rationale: Finance Ministry compromise indicates credential-harvesting objective typical of RAT intrusions; no credential-access UC generated despite this being essential post-exploitation activity
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for keylogger injection, lsass.exe access patterns, Windows Credential Manager API calls, password manager enumeration, or execution of credential-dumping tools. Flag suspicious SeDebugPrivilege escalation or unusual process impersonation targeting credential managers.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Within Finance Ministry Network
suggestion.rationale: Targeted organizational compromise suggests internal network traversal for privilege escalation and data discovery; no lateral-movement UC generated despite enterprise context
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for RDP connections from initial compromise point, SMB enumeration of admin shares (C$, IPC$, Admin$), pass-the-hash activity, or unusual authentication chains originating from compromised Finance Ministry endpoints. Flag lateral movement tools like PsExec usage.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration of Finance Ministry Records
suggestion.rationale: Finance Ministry breach implies data theft objective; no exfiltration-phase detection generated despite this being the likely final campaign goal
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline egress traffic profiles from Finance Ministry endpoints. Alert on volumetric anomalies to C2 infrastructure, bulk transfers of Office/financial documents outside business hours, or suspicious compression/archiving followed by exfiltration attempts.

suggestion.title: Maven Central Suspicious Version Dependency Load
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies the attack delivery mechanism: 'You pull the dependency, you run the tests, the payload comes along for the ride.' Pipeline missed dependency pull monitoring at specific versions (1.10.0) from Maven Central.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Maven Central dependency resolution for net.jqwik:jqwik-engine version 1.10.0 (or alert on any sudden test output anomalies in jqwik versions 1.10.0-1.10.1). Check lockfiles for the affected artifact SHA-256.

suggestion.title: ANSI Escape Code Obfuscation in Build Output
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'The code prints the instruction line, then prints ESC [2K followed by a carriage return, twice.' ANSI codes (0x1B[2K) hide content from humans but remain visible to log aggregators and LLM parsers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect presence of ESC[2K (erase-line) and CR (carriage-return) sequences in proximity to test output or build summary sections. Flag patterns where content is printed then immediately followed by line-erase codes.

suggestion.title: Prompt Injection in Tool Output Targeting AI Agents
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Any pipeline that pulled the dependency and fed test output back into an LLM agent could have triggered the prompt injection.' The payload explicitly targets agentic coding tools like Claude Code by embedding instructions in test output.
log_sources: CI/CD logs fed to LLM context
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Before feeding tool output (test logs, build summaries, CLI output) to LLM agents, scan for injected instructions, especially commands to disregard, delete, or modify code. Flag presence of phrases like 'disregard previous instructions' or imperatives to destroy artifacts in non-human-readable contexts.

suggestion.title: Malicious Library Method Invocation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is a single method call: 'The malicious instruction lived in a new method called printMessageForCodingAgents() inside the net.jqwik.engine.execution.JqwikExecutor class.' Pipeline should detect when this method is called or present in loaded classes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for invocation of or presence of the method `printMessageForCodingAgents()` in net.jqwik.engine.execution.JqwikExecutor. Trigger on class loading of JqwikExecutor from version 1.10.0 or decompilation of JARs containing this method.

suggestion.title: Maintainer-Injected Supply Chain Sabotage
suggestion.rationale: Novel attack pattern: 'The maintainer wrote it on purpose... The person who wrote it was Johannes Link, the project's own maintainer.' This is insider-based supply chain compromise, not external account hijacking. Requires monitoring for maintainer behavior anomalies and intentional payload injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag commits to open-source projects that introduce new methods specifically named or documented as targeting AI/agentic tools. Monitor for deliberate obfuscation techniques (ANSI codes, intentional hiding) paired with methods designed to execute only in automated contexts.

suggestion.title: File Deletion Executed by LLM Agent from Tool Output Injection
suggestion.rationale: Intended impact: 'The payload told agents to disregard previous instructions and delete all jqwik tests and code.' If the agent follows the injected instruction, it would delete files. Monitor for unexpected file deletions triggered by LLM agent execution of embedded commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate LLM agent processing of tool output with subsequent file deletion operations on the same system. Flag when file deletions follow agent reads of build/test output, especially deletions of test files or entire directories matching patterns in injected instructions.

suggestion.title: Preinstall Hook Triggering Credential Reads from Environment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'sophisticated multi-stage credential harvester that targets GitHub Actions secrets, AWS, GCP, Azure, Kubernetes, HashiCorp Vault, npm tokens, and CircleCI.' No UC detects the actual credential-gathering execution phase—only installation and payload download are covered.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Node or npm process spawned during preinstall hook that reads from credential files (/root/.aws/credentials, /root/.azure/config, $KUBECONFIG, env vars containing AWS_ACCESS_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, VAULT_ADDR). Look for repeated fstat/open calls on credential paths followed by child process spawns of curl, wget, or base64. File read events on cloud provider credential stores within seconds of malicious package npm install.

suggestion.title: Cloud Instance Metadata Service Access from npm Preinstall Context
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'targets...GCP, Azure' metadata and the techniques list includes T1552.005 (Cloud Instance Metadata API), but no UC detects actual metadata endpoint calls (169.254.169.254, 'metadata.google.internal', etc.) from node processes during package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Node process (spawned as child of npm/preinstall) initiating DNS queries or HTTP connections to cloud metadata endpoints: 169.254.169.254/metadata/v1/* (GCP), 169.254.169.254/api/token (Azure), 169.254.169.254/ (AWS), 'metadata.google.internal', 'instancemetadata.service.consul'. Correlation with @redhat-cloud-services package install timestamps.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Exfiltration via DNS or HTTP from Node Preinstall Process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes T1071.001 (HTTP) and T1071.004 (DNS) usage for exfil but no UC detects outbound C2 or data exfil patterns. The credential harvester must communicate stolen data; current UCs stop at execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Node or child process (spawned from preinstall hook) initiating outbound HTTP POST/PUT to anomalous domains or high-volume DNS queries (DNS tunneling signatures) within 60 seconds of credential reads. Look for command-line curl/wget with base64-encoded payloads, or node spawning bash to execute network commands. Exfil timing correlation with credential access events.

suggestion.title: npm Preinstall Script Execution with Network/File Activity Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article core threat: 'malicious payloads that fire via a preinstall hook on every npm install.' Current UCs detect installation and bun downloads separately but miss the preinstall trigger event itself—the moment npm lifecycle script execution begins.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: npm or node process invoking a script at lifecycle phase 'preinstall' (visible in command line or parent process args). Correlate with child process spawns (bash, sh, node, curl, wget) and file system writes to /tmp or node_modules within 2 seconds. Look for npm parent with --script flag or package.json preinstall entry parse patterns.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated JavaScript Payload Execution in node_modules Preinstall Context
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions T1027 (obfuscated payloads) and T1059.007 (JavaScript execution) but no UC detects highly obfuscated or minified JavaScript code being sourced and executed from package.json or installed modules during preinstall.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Preinstall hook or npm lifecycle script execution that sources obfuscated JavaScript from node_modules or installs a package whose index.js or preinstall.js contains high entropy, minified, or base64-encoded payloads (entropy > 6.5 bits/byte). Detect via file content analysis of JavaScript written to node_modules during package install, or node invocation of highly obfuscated scripts with regex `node.*-e.*[A-Za-z0-9+/=].*==` patterns.

suggestion.title: Multiple @redhat-cloud-services Packages Installed Across Dev/CI Environments
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'multiple packages in the @redhat-cloud-services npm scope'—supply chain breadth suggests hunting across multiple related packages and environments. Single-package installs miss the scope of potential exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate across multiple @redhat-cloud-services packages (host-inventory-client, notifications-client, frontend-components, rbac-client, etc.) installed in the last 7 days. Count unique hosts/users installing 3+ affected packages from the same scope. Correlate with CI/CD environment context (GITHUB_ACTIONS=true, CI=true env vars). Flag broad supply chain compromise indicator.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Post-Install Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'multi-stage attacks' and 'post-install script' vectors in npm package exploitation. Pipeline missed detection for execution of arbitrary code via install hooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for node.exe or npm.exe spawning unexpected child processes (bash, powershell, curl, wget) during package installation. Flag processes spawned from npm cache or node_modules directories with egress network activity or credential access patterns.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from npm Environment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'credential harvesting' as an attack vector. Pipeline failed to generate detection for exfiltration of npm tokens, registry credentials, or GitHub tokens from build environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect exfiltration of npm_token, NPM_TOKEN, .npmrc contents, or GitHub tokens by monitoring environment variable dumps, base64-encoded credential leakage to external domains, or authentication header anomalies in outbound HTTP traffic from CI/CD runners.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Dependency Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'supply chain' attacks and package-level compromise. Pipeline should flag detection of unexpected package.json modifications or dependency version downgrades introducing vulnerable/malicious packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized modifications to package.json or package-lock.json files, sudden introduction of unknown or typosquatted package names, or installation of packages from non-standard registries. Correlate with CI/CD pipeline triggers.

suggestion.title: CI/CD Pipeline Persistence via npm Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'CI/CD persistence' as a primary attack goal. Pipeline missed detection for installation of persistent malware disguised as legitimate build dependencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag repeated installation of the same suspicious npm package across multiple CI/CD runs, persistence mechanisms in post-install scripts (cron jobs, scheduled tasks, shell rc files), or modification of CI/CD configuration files by processes spawned from npm modules.

suggestion.title: Worm-like Propagation via npm Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'worm propagation.' Pipeline should detect when a single malicious package rapidly infects downstream consumers, indicated by cascading installations and lateral movement patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid spike in installations of a specific npm package version, followed by outbound connections from infected systems to download additional payloads or propagate to other systems. Monitor for beaconing patterns or bulk credential exfiltration across multiple endpoints simultaneously.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Payload Detection in npm Package Code
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords include 'obfuscation' and 'payload.' Pipeline should detect use of code obfuscation, string encoding, or Base64/gzip payloads embedded in node modules to evade static analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan npm package source for obfuscated JavaScript patterns (minified, base64-encoded strings, hex payloads), encrypted or gzip-compressed binaries embedded in node_modules, or dynamic code evaluation (eval, Function constructor) that loads payloads at runtime. Correlate with YARA or pattern-matching rules for known malware families.

suggestion.title: Device Code Phishing OAuth Flow Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'device code phishing...has surged from a research curiosity to an industrialized PhaaS offering, with more than 18 kits being actively tracked.' Explicit attack surface with industrial tooling documented.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on OAuth device_code grant_type flows where device code was requested but never successfully authenticated, or where authentication occurs from geographically inconsistent IP. Flag multiple failed device code attempts for same user within 1 hour or device code scopes requesting mail.read, mail.send, or files.read on first-time consent.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Browser Clipboard and Session Data Extraction
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'analyzing page behavior, script execution, and malicious mechanics (session theft, malicious copy and paste, file downloads) rather than matching domains against a feed — particularly where many attacks now take place entirely inside the browser session without touching the endpoint.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor browser process clipboard API invocations (navigator.clipboard.read* methods) in non-approved domains followed by exfiltration. Alert when script execution (eval, Function() constructor) in untrusted origins precedes clipboard access. Flag repeated clipboard reads within <5 second window.

suggestion.title: Unapproved AI SaaS OAuth Consent and Shadow Account Usage
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'average organization has 16 unique AI apps, 17 AI browser extensions, and 17 AI-connected OAuth integrations — most of them unapproved...Of file uploads to AI tools, 38% are made from personal shadow accounts rather than organizational ones.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag OAuth consent grants to ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot (personal tier) or file upload API calls to openai.com, claude.ai, google.com/colab from corporate IP ranges. Alert on sign-ins from corporate device to personal Microsoft/Google account followed by AI service access.
