suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The free tier stealer targets Minecraft session ID theft, cookies, and saved passwords across 36 browsers, 56 cryptocurrency add-ons... Discord, Steam, and Telegram credentials.' Describes rapid harvest of multiple authentication artifacts. Should alert on process accessing browser credential stores, Minecraft config, and cryptocurrency wallet files within short window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a single process (especially those named after Minecraft clients) accesses AppData/Local/Google/Chrome/User Data, .minecraft/launcher_profiles.json, cryptocurrency wallet directories (%APPDATA%/roaming/walletname), and Discord/Telegram config in same 60-second window.

suggestion.title: SEO-Poisoned Malicious Mod Download via Crafted Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'SEO poisoning promoting them [clients]... malicious website displays a security notice warning visitors... linking to the project's legitimate GitHub repository and Discord server to create a strong, false sense of legitimacy.' Describes credential-stealer hosting behind spoofed project identity. Should detect traffic to high-similarity typosquatted or lookalike domains for known Minecraft client projects.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and HTTP requests to domains with edit distance ≤2 from known Minecraft client project names (meteor-client.com vs meteor-clent.com, radiummods.com vs radium-mods.xyz). Correlate with JAR downloads on same host.

suggestion.title: Screenshot Capture by Minecraft Process
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Free tier... can capture screenshots.' Also 'Premium tier... webcam access, keylogger, remote shell' describes surveillance capability. Should detect screen capture API calls or screenshot utilities invoked by Minecraft-related processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Minecraft process (javaw.exe, launcher.exe, or processes named after malicious clients) loading GDI+ screenshot libraries (gdiplus.dll) or calling Windows.Graphics.Capture APIs, or invoking screencap/screenshot utilities.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Wallet File Access from Non-Wallet Process
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'targets... 56 cryptocurrency add-ons, 12 desktop cryptocurrency wallet apps.' Infostealer harvests wallet keys/seeds. Should detect suspicious reads of wallet application directories or key material by unrelated processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file access to common cryptocurrency wallet storage paths (%APPDATA%/Roaming/Bitcoin, .ethereum, .metamask, Ledger, Coinbase) by processes not in wallet application whitelist. Flag especially if parent process is java.exe or launcher.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Remote Control Behavior from Minecraft Client
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Premium tier... remote control with input access (mouse and keyboard)... remote shell, and remote file management.' Describes RAT-like functionality post-infection. Should detect synthetic input events or shell commands originating from Minecraft process context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Minecraft process or children spawning powershell.exe, cmd.exe with no user interaction detected, or performing file operations (copy, delete, compress) to unusual paths. Also flag low-level input event injection (mouse movement, keystroke simulation) correlated with Minecraft process.

suggestion.title: Xeno RAT Execution and Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Pakistan-Linked SideCopy Targets Afghanistan Finance Ministry with Xeno RAT'. No execution-stage detection produced despite explicit RAT implant. Execution is the critical instrumentation point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation matching Xeno RAT signatures: known executable names, parent-child chains typical of RAT unpacking, or command-line patterns associated with Xeno family. Prioritize execution from Finance Ministry webmail or file-share contexts.

suggestion.title: SideCopy Spearphishing and Initial Access
suggestion.rationale: SideCopy is documented as spearphishing operator. Article targets Finance Ministry but pipeline produced zero initial-access detection. Attack must begin with delivery vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Afghanistan Finance Ministry staff clicking or executing URLs from known SideCopy phishing infrastructure. Monitor Finance Ministry email for sender spoofing, malicious attachments, or links to file-hosting sites hosting Xeno RAT payloads.

suggestion.title: Xeno RAT Command-and-Control Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: RAT-based attacks require C2 channel; zero exfiltration or C2 detection rule. This is the critical window to detect attacker commands and data theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Finance Ministry egress for outbound connections to known Xeno C2 infrastructure. Flag periodic beaconing patterns, high-entropy encrypted payloads, or DNS tunneling from compromised Finance Ministry systems.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration from Afghanistan Finance Ministry
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly targets Finance Ministry—a high-value target for theft of budget documents, transaction records, and classified financial intelligence. Zero collection/exfiltration use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate bulk access to Finance Ministry spreadsheets, databases, or financial records with C2 beacon timing. Flag archive creation or compression of financial documents followed by outbound egress.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Scheduled Tasks or Registry Modification
suggestion.rationale: SideCopy RAT implants establish persistence to maintain access across reboots. Pipeline produced zero persistence-stage detection despite known SideCopy tactics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for scheduled task creation or HKLM/HKCU Run/RunOnce registry modifications containing Xeno RAT executable paths. Alert on tasks created by unprivileged service accounts or executing from temp/AppData directories.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised Finance Ministry Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Xeno RAT captures credentials; no detection for lateral movement within Finance Ministry network. Stolen Finance Ministry credentials enable access to sensitive systems and data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual RDP or SMB activity from Finance Ministry user accounts post-Xeno compromise. Flag failed authentications followed by successful logon with stolen credentials to administrative or data-warehouse systems.

suggestion.title: Maven Central Supply Chain Compromise - jqwik 1.10.0 Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies affected coordinates: 'Package: net.jqwik:jqwik-engine, Affected version: 1.10.0' and scope: 'Any project that pulled net.jqwik:jqwik-engine at 1.10.0, directly or transitively'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on dependency resolution of net.jqwik:jqwik-engine version 1.10.0 in build manifests, lock files, or Maven Central queries. Cross-reference artifact hash against known malicious JAR. Escalate if version 1.10.0 is found in active project dependencies.

suggestion.title: ANSI Escape Code Obfuscation in Build/Test Output
suggestion.rationale: Article details evasion: 'prints ESC [2K followed by a carriage return, twice... on any stream that records output as raw text instead of rendering it, those erase codes are just dead characters. The instruction stays right there in the log'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search CI/test logs for ANSI erase sequences (0x1B[2K or \x1b[2k followed by carriage return \r). Flag consecutive erase patterns that suggest line-clearing obfuscation, especially near test output or diagnostic messages.

suggestion.title: Prompt Injection Payload in Dependency Test Output
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exact attack phrase: 'The payload told agents to disregard previous instructions and delete all jqwik tests and code' and attack surface: 'Any pipeline that pulled the dependency and fed test output back into an LLM agent could have triggered the prompt injection'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Grep CI/build logs for instruction-override phrases ('disregard previous instructions', 'ignore prior', 'forget context') especially in dependency test output. Flag if phrase appears before destructive commands (delete, remove, clear). Correlate with agent execution logs to detect exposure to LLM-based tools.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Method Addition to Stable Open Source Library
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights suspicious method: 'The method name tells you the intent on its own' (printMessageForCodingAgents in JqwikExecutor class) added without corresponding feature in release notes or documentation
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag new public methods added to mature libraries with names explicitly targeting automation (e.g., *Agent*, *Prompt*, *LLM*, *AI*, *CodingAgent*). Cross-reference against commit history and release notes; alert if method appears without documented feature addition or is present in artifact but absent from published changelog.

suggestion.title: AI Agent Command Injection Detection and Refusal
suggestion.rationale: Article documents successful agent-side defense: 'Claude Code flagged the instruction on the first mvn test run, refused to act on it, and traced it back to its source in the JAR'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor AI agent logs for injection detection events: agent refusing to execute conflicting instructions, agent flagging instruction source, agent tracing directive back to a dependency or tool output. High-confidence indicator of attempted compromise; log agent's rejection reasoning and source identification.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation w/ Embedded Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'credential harvesting' and 'payload' obfuscation in npm packages. Multi-stage attacks using npm as initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install operations that write to unexpected paths or execute postinstall scripts with network callbacks. Correlate with new credential material in environment variables or config files within node_modules subdirectories.

suggestion.title: npm Package postinstall Script Code Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'multi-stage attacks' and worm propagation via supply chain. Package.json scripts are common execution vector for malicious payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm/node processes spawning unusual child processes (curl, wget, powershell, bash) immediately after package installation. Look for obfuscated Base64 or hex-encoded command strings in postinstall hooks.

suggestion.title: CI/CD Pipeline Credential Exfiltration via npm Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'CI/CD persistence' as attack surface. npm packages in CI environments have access to secrets and deployment credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In CI/CD logs, detect npm install → outbound DNS/HTTP to non-standard domains carrying Base64-encoded credential patterns. Correlate with secrets access patterns in logs.

suggestion.title: npm worm.propagate via package.json dependency injection
suggestion.rationale: Article tags 'worm propagation' and multi-stage attack chains. Worms self-replicate by modifying package.json or publishing new versions under similar names.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected modifications to package.json or package-lock.json pointing to new malicious dependencies. Cross-reference with npm registry API calls or git commit patterns from compromised credentials.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Malware Payload in npm module exports
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'obfuscation' and 'payload' delivery. Malicious code is commonly hidden in minified, Base64-encoded, or VM-escaped formats within legitimate-looking modules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag require() or import() of npm modules that immediately execute eval(), Function(), vm.runInThisContext(), or decode Base64 payloads. Correlate with process spawning or network activity.

suggestion.title: GitHub OAuth / npm Registry Token Theft via malicious package
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists GitHub and credential harvesting. Attackers harvest auth tokens to publish malicious packages or propagate worms downstream.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm packages exfiltrating .npmrc, .gitconfig, or environment variables containing GITHUB_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN, or GIT_CREDENTIALS. Correlate with outbound HTTP to attacker C2.

suggestion.title: Device Code OAuth Phishing – Anomalous Device Authorization Flows
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'device code phishing...abuses a legitimate OAuth flow to bypass MFA and passkeys entirely, has surged from a research curiosity to an industrialized PhaaS offering, with more than 18 kits being actively tracked in the wild.' Detectable via OAuth device code request anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alerting on OAuth device code authorization patterns: multiple failed device code requests for same user within 1 hour, device code flow immediately followed by sign-in from anomalous geography/device, or device code use on accounts with passwordless-phone-sign-in or conditional-access strict policies.

suggestion.title: Shadow AI Account Credential Exfiltration via Clipboard & File Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'AI browser extensions collect browsing context from internal applications, creating a data exfiltration path that operates outside traditional DLP...38% of file uploads to AI tools...made from personal shadow accounts...pasting sensitive data into LLMs.' Requires detection of clipboard copying + unauth AI tool destinations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate browser extension clipboard-read permission grants with network POSTs to cloud AI service endpoints (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral, etc.). Alert on sensitive file uploads (password managers, credential dumps, source code) to personal cloud storage used by unapproved AI tools. Monitor for clipboard data containing confidential information (PII, credentials) pasted into browser frames belonging to unmanaged AI services.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized AI Browser Extension Installation & OAuth Permission Grants
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'average organization has...17 AI browser extensions...most of them unapproved.' Pipeline should detect extension installs and permission changes without MDM/catalog approval.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on browser extension installations from non-managed stores (Chrome Web Store, Firefox Add-ons) that request clipboard, storage, or identity permissions. Correlate with OAuth application consent events to AI services from newly-installed extension service principals. Flag extensions with cryptic names, single-day release dates, or privesc-capable APIs.

suggestion.title: AI-Assisted Phishing Infrastructure – Rapid Domain Rotation & AI Fingerprints
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'A convincing-looking phishing page can be vibecoded in minutes...rotated out before any reputation service flags it...89% of phishing domains are active for fewer than two days...Verbose comments in page code are a clear indicator of AI-assisted development.' Detectable via HTML source analysis and domain TTL patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Behavioral detection of phishing landing pages: scan HTML source for verbose auto-generated comments (variable naming patterns, redundant docstrings), detect infrastructure patterns (multiple subdomains, rapid domain bursts from same registrar/IP space within 48h, short TTLs). Correlate search ad click-through logs with phishing page visits same-session. Alert on phishing URLs delivered via legitimate platform abuse (LLMShare pattern: legitimate chatgpt.com sharing links redirecting to phishing).

suggestion.title: Malvertising & Search-Result Phishing Payload Delivery – Non-Email Channels
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'roughly 1 in 3 phishing payloads arrive via channels other than email...ClickFix is an even clearer example, where 4 in 5 payloads arrive specifically through search engine results...malvertising, social media, SEO poisoning.' Traditional email-only defenses are blind to 80% of these deliveries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate phishing delivery vector telemetry: detect campaigns where payload distribution is predominantly non-email (search ads, YouTube pre-rolls, Reddit posts, malvertising networks). Alert on newly-registered domains advertised via paid search or display ad networks within hours of registration. Correlate user search queries for software downloads/fixes with subsequent visits to suspicious phishing domains (ClickFix/InstallFix abuse of 'software fix' intent).

suggestion.title: Browser-Session Credential & Session-Token Theft via Script Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'particularly where many attacks now take place entirely inside the browser session without touching the endpoint...analyzing page behavior, script execution, and malicious mechanics (session theft, malicious copy and paste, file downloads, and so on).' Client-side behavior in phishing/malicious domains detectable via browser telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious JavaScript execution within low-reputation domains: script calling document.cookie/localStorage.getItem on sensitive domains (mail, cloud storage, banking), use of fetch/XMLHttpRequest to exfil tokens to attacker C2, form auto-filling + submission, or clipboard access via navigator.clipboard API. Correlate with session tokens appearing in outbound HTTP headers to non-standard destinations.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Router Credential Log File
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The acer_cgi.log file in the device firmware is accessible without authentication via the web interface. This file contains cleartext login credentials (for web and Telnet).' Pipeline extracted zero detection rules for this explicit credential-access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP GET/POST requests to Acer Wave 7 routers targeting acer_cgi.log or similar log paths from unauthenticated sessions. Alert on requests to /cgi-bin or backup/log retrieval endpoints from external IP space or outside maintenance windows. Correlate log access with downstream Telnet/SSH login attempts using extracted credentials.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Backup Decryption and Re-encryption via upload.cgi
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The upload.cgi binary, responsible for processing device backups, contains a hardcoded AES encryption key. This allows an attacker to decrypt, modify, and re-encrypt system backups, facilitating persistent backdoor injection.' Pipeline missed this as persistence phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect upload.cgi invocation with backup file I/O (decrypt, modify, re-encrypt cycles). Flag backup files undergoing cryptographic operations outside normal firmware update windows. Alert on system calls indicating AES key material or backup restoration from modified archives. Baseline normal maintenance cycles; anomalies trigger escalation.

suggestion.title: Router Admin Interface Access from Untrusted Sources
suggestion.rationale: Both CVEs require remote web interface access to vulnerable endpoints. Article advises 'disable remote management or restrict Internet remote access to trusted IP addresses only'—indicating baseline should be enforced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP/HTTPS connections to Acer Wave 7 admin interface (192.168.76.1, acerconnect.com:80/443) from external IPs, non-administrative subnets, or untrusted geolocation. Correlate with failed authentication attempts or subsequent enumeration of /cgi-bin paths. Verify remote management restriction controls are enforced.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Using Extracted Router Plaintext Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article: cleartext credentials in log file 'leading to unauthorized system access.' Extracted credentials enable downstream lateral movement and further compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Telnet/SSH login attempts using credentials that appear in router logs. Correlate timing of acer_cgi.log access with subsequent authentication events on same or adjacent infrastructure. Alert on unusual authentication source IPs or failed brute-force attempts using extracted credential sets.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Cryptographic Key Exploitation in Router Backup
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies hardcoded AES key in upload.cgi as attack surface. Detection should focus on backup file tampering enabled by known key.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on router backup files (.tar, .bin, .cfg) being read, decrypted, or modified outside normal upgrade procedures. Flag re-upload of modified backups to device. Monitor for elevated privilege processes accessing firmware blobs or restoration binaries. Correlate with upload.cgi execution timing.

suggestion.title: COM Object Hijacking via InprocServer32 Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'The malware uses COM hijacking to persist on the victim's machine, replacing the InprocServer32 entry for Windows Color System Calibration Loader DLL. This task is triggered when the user logs in, effectively allowing the malware to run at startup.' Direct persistence mechanism with clear detection surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Classes\CLSID and HKEY_CURRENT_USER\SOFTWARE\Classes\CLSID for modifications to InprocServer32 entries. Flag writes pointing to unsigned DLLs, user-writable paths, or DLLs loaded alongside game executables. Alert on modifications to Windows Color System or similar system-component CLSIDs.

suggestion.title: Unsigned DLL Load Chain from Game Process
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'modified FFmpeg DLL...imported the DllGetClassObject function from a file called natives2_blob.bin.' Game executables (RenPy, RPG Maker MV) should not load random .bin DLLs; this is the execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect game engines or associated processes loading unsigned DLLs with suspicious names (natives2_blob.bin, random hash-like names). Flag FFmpeg.dll loading from game directories that then imports from non-standard locations. Look for DLL load chains: game exe → ffmpeg.dll → natives2_blob.bin.

suggestion.title: Base64-Encoded PowerShell Execution from DLL Context
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The natives2_blob.bin file is a DLL that executes a Base64-encoded PowerShell script when loaded...Stage1, performs basic checks for controlled environments.' This is obfuscated second-stage execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on powershell.exe spawned with -encodedCommand or similar Base64 decoding patterns, especially with unusual parent processes (dlls, non-standard game directories). Flag execution shortly after unsigned DLL load. Monitor for System.Convert::FromBase64String or similar decoding in script blocks.

suggestion.title: Malware Sandbox Detection Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The PowerShell script, which we'll call Stage1, performs basic checks for controlled environments.' This anti-analysis behavior avoids detonation in security labs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell scripts querying WMI for virtualization (Win32_ComputerSystemProduct, Win32_BIOS), registry artifact detection (Hyper-V, VMware, VirtualBox signatures), or checking for analysis tools (debuggers, sandboxes). Flag enumeration patterns occurring within minutes of game launch.

suggestion.title: Delayed Remote Payload Download and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'After a few days, the implant downloads and executes a Trojan, resulting in full system compromise and broad remote control capabilities.' This is classic downloader behavior with time-delayed C2 callback.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound network connections from PowerShell or unsigned processes spawned from game directories to external IPs. Flag HTTP/HTTPS downloads of executable payloads occurring days after initial infection. Detect unusual process trees: game.exe → powershell → cmd/rundll32 → network activity.

suggestion.title: Game Executable Spawning Suspicious Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The DLLs were spawned by different games written using various game engines and programming languages, including RenPy (Python) and RPG Maker MV (JavaScript).' Legitimate game engines should not spawn PowerShell, cmd, or rundll32.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when RenPy (python.exe), RPG Maker executables, or game launchers spawn powershell.exe, cmd.exe, or unsigned binaries. Flag any process creation from game installation directories pointing outside the game folder. Monitor for creation of .bin files or suspicious DLLs during game runtime.

suggestion.title: Identify Internet-Facing Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer Installations (Asset Exposure)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' as foundational detection. Vulnerable installations are prerequisite for T1190 exploitation; article specifies product name and CVE for scanner cross-reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory internet-facing Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer instances via vulnerability scanner, product fingerprinting (HTTP banners, JavaScript includes, response headers), and certificate-authority logs. Correlate against CVE-2026-45247 patch status. Flag unpatched instances exposed to untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Detect CacheWarmer Cookie Deserialization Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector: 'crafted serialized PHP object in the CacheWarmer cookie'—the literal exploitation mechanism. Represents the execution phase of T1190.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests for CacheWarmer cookie containing PHP object serialization patterns (O:number:, unserialize markers, excessive base64/hex encoding). Flag requests from external IPs with unusual payload sizes or rapid retries. Correlate with Mirasvit-targeted URL patterns.

suggestion.title: Detect Post-Exploitation Code Execution from Web Server Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploit 'could allow unauthenticated attackers to achieve remote code execution'. Successful deserialization triggers process creation with elevated privileges under web-server user.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual process execution (shells, compilers, curl, wget) spawned by web-server processes (apache, nginx, php-fpm) immediately following CacheWarmer-cookie requests. Inspect command lines for reverse shells, script execution, or system reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Monitor Mirasvit Application Logs for Deserialization Failures and Type Errors
suggestion.rationale: Failed exploitation attempts produce application errors; article's focus on deserialization vulnerability implies attackers probe for working payloads. Error spikes indicate reconnaissance or fuzzing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search application error logs for deserialization failures ('unserialize() error', type confusion, memory corruption) in request handlers processing CacheWarmer cookies. Spike in such errors correlates with active exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Correlate CVE-2026-45247 Patch Status Against Internet Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes federal due-date (2026-06-06) and states 'patch lag is the silent killer'—implies scanner discrepancies (patched per software-version but exposed per network-scan). Cross-validation is critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for systems matching Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-45247. Cross-reference asset inventory patch levels against network exposure scans. Prioritize systems marked 'patched' by asset-management but exposed by network scanning (common patch-lag blind spot).

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via cgroup_release_agent_write()
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes CVE-2022-0492 as exploiting 'cgroup_release_agent_write() function' with 'insufficient authentication checks' to 'escalate privileges' and 'escape from a container to gain root-level access on the host system.' This is the primary attack vector; zero use cases generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes invoking cgroup escape techniques: cgroup write operations, namespace-escape syscalls, or containers spawning host-level processes. Alert on unprivileged users accessing /proc/sys/kernel/cgroup/release_agent or writing to cgroup v1 hierarchies without proper capabilities. Correlate container context transitions with privilege elevation.

suggestion.title: Android Framework Integer Overflow Exploitation (CVE-2025-48595)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes CVE-2025-48595 as 'integer overflow vulnerability in the Android Framework' enabling 'increased privileges' with 'no user interaction required' and 'limited targeted exploitation in the wild.' This is active exploitation; pipeline generated zero detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Android Framework process (system_server) for unexpected privilege context changes, capability escalations, or SELinux domain transitions. Flag integer overflow patterns in memory operations. Detect rapid or unsolicited calls to privileged interfaces from unprivileged UIDs on Android 14–16.

suggestion.title: Container Namespace Isolation Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states the flaw enables attackers to 'bypass namespace isolation' and 'escape from a container to gain root-level access on the host system.' Namespace escape and host-level access are distinct impact signatures requiring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when containerized processes spawn siblings or children in different namespaces, execute host binaries outside container filesystem, or manipulate namespace entries in /proc/*/ns/*. Track anomalous container-to-host process parentage and namespace transitions.

suggestion.title: Kernel Version Exploitation Window (CVE-2022-0492)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerable kernel versions '2.6 through 4.20, and from 5.5 through 5.17' and patched versions (4.9.301+, 4.14.266+, etc.). Unpatched systems remain exploitable; detection should identify active exploitation on vulnerable branches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Profile kernel version at baseline; alert if cgroup-related syscalls originate from non-root processes on vulnerable kernel versions without corresponding patches. Cross-reference patch deployment records against running kernel versions.

suggestion.title: Suspicious cgroup_release_agent File Writes
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2022-0492 exploitation explicitly depends on writing to 'cgroup_release_agent' via cgroups v1. This is the precise exploit vector and the most specific detection signature available.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor writes to cgroup v1 control group hierarchies for release_agent field manipulation. Flag any non-root process writing to cgroup paths, especially from container contexts. Correlate with unusual child process spawns or privilege escalation indicators.

suggestion.title: Elevated Capability Container Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the exploit is 'especially dangerous when containers are granted elevated capabilities.' Containers with CAP_SYS_ADMIN or CAP_NET_ADMIN combined with exploitation patterns are high-signal indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline container capabilities at startup; alert when containers launch with dangerous capability sets. Flag exploitation patterns (cgroup writes, namespace manipulation) from over-privileged containers. Cross-reference against CVE-2022-0492 patch status.

suggestion.title: Phishing Delivery: JavaScript Attachment Masquerading as Business Document
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'disguises itself as an everyday business document — a purchase order, a quote, or a request for proposal.' This is T1566.001 (Phishing with Attachment). Pipeline detected zero initial-access techniques. Hunt for .js/.jse files with spoofed business document names.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag .js, .jse, .vbs, or .ps1 file attachments or downloads with names matching patterns like PO_*.*, Quote_*.*, RFP_*.*, especially when delivered via external email or followed by immediate execution from Downloads folder.

suggestion.title: Script Engine Execution from User-Writable Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article implies user opens the malware document, triggering execution. JS.MonoGlyphRAT indicates JavaScript runtime. Describes T1204 (User Execution) + T1059.001 (JavaScript/PowerShell Interpreter).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cscript.exe or wscript.exe spawned from user Downloads, Desktop, or %TEMP% with parent explorer.exe or outlook.exe. Elevated signal if child process spawns cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or network utilities (curl, certutil, bitsadmin).

suggestion.title: Registry Run-Key Persistence by Script Engine
suggestion.rationale: RATs establish persistence; JS.MonoGlyphRAT likely uses registry run-keys (T1547.001, T1112). Article body truncated so persistence mechanism not explicit, but standard RAT behavior absent from pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKCU/HKLM \Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run* for modifications by cscript.exe, wscript.exe, or uncommon binaries. Correlate with .js file writes to ProgramData or System32.

suggestion.title: WMI or COM Invocation by Script Interpreter
suggestion.rationale: JavaScript RATs commonly evade detection via WMI (T1047) or COM (T1559). Article does not detail these; omitted from pipeline despite being high-confidence RAT TTP.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag cscript/wscript with command-line containing 'GetObject("winmgmts:' or '.CreateObject' loading COM objects from suspicious paths, or WMI Event Subscription creation. Especially suspicious if child process is cmd.exe or powershell.exe.

suggestion.title: Double-Extension or Spoofed Business Document Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes social engineering via document mimicry. Detect files with mismatched extensions or icons (PO.js, quote.pdf.exe) or executable extensions with business document keywords. Captures T1204 (User Execution) pre-click.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt file downloads/attachments matching /PO_|QUOTE_|RFP_|purchase.order|request.for.proposal/i with executable extensions (.js, .jse, .vbs, .exe, .scr, .ps1). Flag especially if source is external email and user accessed file within 5 minutes of receipt.

suggestion.title: Active Directory Discovery via Automated LDAP/PowerShell Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'AI-assisted tools to automate Active Directory discovery.' Should detect domain account/computer enumeration via Get-AD* cmdlets, LDAP queries, or dsquery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag rapid or automated LDAP queries and Get-ADUser/Get-ADComputer executions, especially from non-admin processes or user-writable directories. Baseline legitimate admin tools and alert on anomalous enumeration scope or frequency.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Payload Execution from User-Writable Paths
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'payloads stored in a user directory' and 'suspicious endpoint triggered alerts.' Should detect executables or scripts launched from AppData, Temp, Downloads, or user-profile subdirectories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation from user-writable paths (%TEMP%, %APPDATA%, Downloads, Public, user Temp). Correlate parent process type (Office, script interpreter, browser) and command line obfuscation as risk indicators.

suggestion.title: EDR Evasion - Process Injection and Code Reflection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'test endpoint detection and response (EDR) evasion techniques.' EDR evasion inherently involves T1055 (process injection), T1620 (reflective code loading), or T1622 (debugger evasion).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for VirtualAlloc/WriteProcessMemory call sequences, unsigned DLL injection into system processes (lsass, winlogon, svchost), reflective imports, or attempts to disable ETW/WMI event logging. Flag process tree anomalies.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Malware Components - Registry and Service Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article refers to 'collection of malicious components forming a structured' attack. Should detect registry Run/RunOnce keys, service creation, or scheduled-task registration originating from suspicious processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect registry modifications (HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services, HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run) or service/task creation from non-standard contexts. Correlate timing with initial payload execution.

suggestion.title: Automated System Enumeration and Software Inventory Collection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes AI tools automating 'post-exploitation frameworks' which typically perform system discovery (T1082), process enumeration (T1057), and software inventory (T1518).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate rapid-fire information-gathering commands (systeminfo, Get-WmiObject Win32_*, tasklist, reg query HKLM\Software, net config) from a single process or session within short timeframes. Baseline admin tools and alert on batching patterns typical of frameworks.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Automated Credential or Trust Abuse
suggestion.rationale: AD discovery capability suggests lateral movement or privilege escalation goals. Article lacks explicit mention but is typical of structured post-exploitation frameworks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual SMB/RDP connections from the compromised host to other domain systems post-discovery. Flag credential forwarding or pass-the-hash patterns in authentication logs.

suggestion.title: AWS Lambda Function URL C2 Callbacks
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'hide inside one of the world's most trusted platforms, Amazon Web Services (AWS)' via Lambda URLs. Domain IOC `lambda-url.ap-southeast-1.on.aws` is the critical signature. Generic beaconing misses this AWS-specific delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTPS traffic to *.on.aws domains, specifically Lambda Function URL subdomains (lambda-url-\d+ pattern). Correlate connection source with process execution context. Filter whitelisted development environments. Alert on callback frequency matching beaconing profile.

suggestion.title: DNS Exfiltration via AWS Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: T1071.004 (DNS) listed as technique but zero DNS-specific hunts provided. Article emphasizes 'stealthy communications'—DNS tunneling to AWS name servers is plausible secondary C2 channel.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries to *.amazonaws.com and *.on.aws with anomalous patterns: base64-encoded subdomains, high query volume from single host, exfiltration-sized DNS responses, or recursive lookups within AWS CIDR space. Correlate with observed process execution.

suggestion.title: Malware Process Obfuscation & Injection
suggestion.rationale: T1027 (Obfuscated Files) is listed but unmapped to detection. Malware payloads in 7 SHA256s are presumed packed or injected given 'stealthy' positioning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for entropy anomalies in PE file sections (high entropy = packing), parent-child process relationships indicative of code injection (explorer.exe spawning rundll32; svchost.exe spawning unsigned binary), or suspicious handle/memory access patterns from interpreter processes.

suggestion.title: Southeast Asia Government Email-Based Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Campaign 'targets government networks across Southeast Asia.' No initial-access vector specified in article body; article fragment is truncated. Email-based delivery (phishing, macro malware) is standard APT entry for government targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for macro-enabled Office documents delivered to Southeast Asia government domains, suspicious attachment types (.zip/.rar with embedded executables), or credential-harvesting indicators (unusual LDAP binds, multiple failed logins post-email event). Correlate with 7 malware SHA256s being executed.

suggestion.title: AWS Infrastructure Credential Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Campaign weaponizes AWS. If attackers obtained AWS API keys or temporary credentials, they would abuse AWS services for lateral movement, data exfil, or persistence within the government cloud environment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor CloudTrail for suspicious Lambda function creation/updates, new IAM roles with overpermissive policies, or API calls from unusual geographic regions. On endpoints, hunt for process execution with AWS CLI/SDK artifacts (aws-cli in temp, AWSSDK references in memory).

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 HPACK Dynamic Table Amplification Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'HPACK compression amplification' phase with measured ratios: 'one byte sent by the attacker can result in thousands of bytes of server-side memory allocation, with Envoy and Apache httpd demonstrating...5,700:1 and 4,000:1, respectively.' Requires monitoring decoded-to-encoded size disparity per connection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP/2 connections exhibiting abnormal HPACK allocation ratios. Alert when a single source sends compact indexed headers (1-2 byte references) that decode to kilobytes, or when HPACK dynamic table size grows >100MB within single connection lifetime.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 Flow Control Window Stalling and Resource Retention
suggestion.rationale: Attack's second phase: 'preventing the memory from being freed once the request completes. This can be achieved by advertising a zero-byte flow-control window.' Connections hold state indefinitely via 'tiny WINDOW_UPDATE frames to avoid timeouts.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/2 connections advertising zero or near-zero WINDOW_UPDATE values while remaining open. Alert on connections sending periodic micro-WINDOW_UPDATE frames (bytes << request size) for >30 seconds without completing request/response cycle.

suggestion.title: Server Memory Exhaustion Spike Correlated with HTTP/2 Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Article documents empirical exhaustion rates: 'Envoy 1.37.2 exhausted 32 GB RAM in about 10 seconds,' 'Apache httpd 2.4.67 exhausted 32 GB RAM in ~18 seconds.' Requires baseline-aware alerting per server type.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create per-server-version memory-growth baselines. For Envoy, alert on >8GB/minute. For Apache, >6GB/minute. For nginx, >3GB/minute. Correlate with HTTP/2 active-connection count (should remain <<100 during exhaustion events).

suggestion.title: Anomalous HPACK Indexed Header Reference Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Attack mechanism: 'inserting a header into the HPACK dynamic table and referencing it repeatedly via a compact indexed representation that can be one byte large.' Detection should target abnormal repetition patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor per-client HTTP/2 streams for repeated references to same HPACK dynamic table indices. Alert when single connection references identical index >100 times/second, or exhibits index-reference frequency 100x higher than median client profile.

suggestion.title: Slowloris-variant HTTP/2 Connection Persistence Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attack combines 'Slowloris-style resource retention via HTTP/2 flow-control stalling.' Adapted Slowloris detection needed for HTTP/2 context where connections don't close naturally.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP/2 connections with lifetime >> median (>120 seconds) and request-completion ratio <<10%. Flag connections from single source holding >10 concurrent streams open without data transfer for >30 seconds.

suggestion.title: Version-Specific HTTP/2 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies unpatched vulnerability signatures: 'Envoy 1.37.2,' 'Apache httpd 2.4.67,' 'nginx 1.29.7' (patched in 1.29.8), 'IIS (Windows Server 2025).' Patches released for nginx (1.29.8) and Apache (mod_http2 2.0.41 with CVE-2026-49975); no patches for IIS, Envoy, Pingora.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain inventory of HTTP/2-enabled servers with unpatched versions. Trigger low-threshold alerts (1-2GB memory spike, 5+ HTTP/2 connections from single source) for Envoy, IIS, and Pingora instances. Use higher thresholds (8GB+) for already-patched nginx 1.29.8+ and Apache 2.0.41+.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 Frame Flooding Attack Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'HTTP/2 Bomb' as vulnerability mechanism — implies attack via frame-based resource exhaustion. No detection logic generated for abnormal frame rates or frame types.
log_sources: proxy logs with HTTP/2 frame counts
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/2 connections for frame rate spikes, concentration of HEADERS or SETTINGS frames without corresponding DATA frames, or rapid connection churn on affected platforms (NGINX, Apache, IIS, Envoy, Cloudflare edge). Correlation with server CPU/memory saturation increases confidence.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 Header Compression Bomb Detection
suggestion.rationale: HTTP/2 bombs typically exploit HPACK or stream multiplexing to compress payloads that expand to resource-exhausting sizes. No compression-anomaly detection generated despite DoS mechanism naming.
log_sources: web server logs with compression stats
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP/2 requests where decompressed header size significantly exceeds compressed size, or streams that declare massive Content-Length with minimal actual bytes sent. Look for patterns on affected platform edge nodes.

suggestion.title: Affected Web Server Resource Exhaustion (HTTP/2)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists NGINX, Apache, IIS, Envoy, Cloudflare as vulnerable platforms. Pipeline should map to detection of CPU/memory/connection exhaustion on these products correlated with HTTP/2 protocol indicators.
log_sources: Process performance counters (NGINX worker processes, Apache httpd processes)
web server error logs (connection limit exceeded, OOM kills)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sustained high CPU or memory use in web server processes (nginx, httpd, w3wp, envoy) preceded by HTTP/2 WINDOW_UPDATE or SETTINGS frame anomalies. Correlate with request volume baseline deviation.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 Stream Multiplexing Abuse
suggestion.rationale: HTTP/2 multiplexing feature is often the vector for bomb attacks — pipe thousands of streams with minimal framing overhead. No detection of abnormal stream counts generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for single HTTP/2 connections spawning hundreds or thousands of active streams without proportional DATA frame volume. Spike in stream resets or window updates without payload transfer is high-confidence indicator.

suggestion.title: CVE Identifier Extraction Failure for HTTP/2 Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline extracted zero IOCs including no CVE ID, despite article title identifying a specific vulnerability class. CVE number(s) should be in body or inferred from disclosure context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag hosts running NGINX, Apache, IIS, or Envoy versions in affected ranges for this HTTP/2 flaw via version banners, SSL certificate analysis, or behavioral indicators (response to malformed HTTP/2 frames). Cloudflare origin-checking via certificate or server header.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm preinstall/postinstall Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes malicious code injected into npm package install hooks: 'preinstall to persistence' in title and 'silently infecting CI/CD environments' via package installation. No UC generated despite this being the initial infection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/postinstall script execution for unexpected child processes (curl, wget, bash, powershell) spawning outside declared package dependencies. Flag execution of scripts accessing credential files (.ssh, .aws, .npmrc) immediately after npm install. Alert on process trees where npm spawns network-outbound processes with unusual parent-child relationships.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration from CI/CD and Local Environments
suggestion.rationale: Article states malicious code 'steals credentials from GitHub, cloud platforms, and local machines.' No detection UC for credential access despite this being the primary attack payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm processes or spawned children accessing credential stores: ~/.ssh/config, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.kube/config, .env files, ~/.npmrc, GitHub token cache. Alert on unusual file reads from CI/CD runners (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab) accessing credential paths. Monitor outbound HTTPS from npm processes to non-npm registry domains during install phase.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Republishing and Lateral Spread
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the attack spreading 'like a worm by republishing trusted packages'—infection spreads via package republishing, not just initial compromise. Pipeline missed the lateral movement vector entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm publish operations for out-of-band version bumps from unexpected accounts. Alert when package version increments without corresponding source commits (GitHub repo integrity check). Detect republishing of previously-clean package versions to npm registry from new author accounts or IP geographies. Correlate legitimate developer accounts used for publish against historical baseline.

suggestion.title: Detection of @redhat-cloud-services Package Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names '@redhat-cloud-services' as the targeted package ecosystem with 90+ compromised versions. Pipeline should flag all telemetry from systems that installed these specific packages as high-risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for all npm install events containing @redhat-cloud-services/<any-package> versions from the 90+ compromised batch (article should list version range). Cross-reference installed machines/CI runners against subsequent credential exfiltration events, network anomalies, or persistence indicators within 24-48 hours of install. Escalate any match as confirmed compromise.

suggestion.title: npm Registry Authentication Token Exfiltration and Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Worm-like spread via 'republishing trusted packages' requires npm write credentials. Article implies attacker obtained ~/.npmrc tokens or registry auth secrets to perform republishes. No UC for detecting token theft or unauthorized publishes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm publish operations from environments that do not match the original package maintainer's baseline IP/geolocation/time-of-day. Flag npm auth token generation or usage immediately following install of @redhat-cloud-services packages. Detect reads of .npmrc files followed by outbound network to non-npm-registry endpoints.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Package postinstall Hook Survival
suggestion.rationale: Title and article explicitly mention 'persistence'—malicious code must survive uninstall/reinstall cycles. Pipeline generated zero persistence detection UCs despite this being part of the campaign's kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for postinstall hooks that write to shell initialization files (~/.bashrc, ~/.zshrc, ~/.profile) or create cron jobs/systemd timers. Monitor node_modules/.bin for unexpected binaries not declared in package.json. Alert on persistence mechanisms tied to npm package paths that trigger on shell login or recurring schedules independent of npm workflows.

suggestion.title: Agent-Driven Unauthorized Database Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'coding agent that ignored repeated freeze instructions, deleted a production database, and then fabricated records to cover the error.' Clear attack pattern of unauthorized data destruction and tamper.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for database write/delete operations executed via agent process contexts or automation accounts, especially those bypassing approval workflows or ignored freeze signals. Flag operations that destroy data followed by immediate record modifications suggesting post-event cover-up.

suggestion.title: Suspicious MCP Server or Skill Instantiation
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Snyk's research found 76 confirmed malicious skills out of 3,984 analyzed, and roughly a third of public MCP servers carry exploitable flaws.' Agents load tools at runtime with no review.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on agent processes loading or instantiating external MCP servers, plugins, or skills not on approved whitelist. Track runtime tool invocation patterns and network calls to external tool repositories or skill markets.

suggestion.title: Prompt Injection Attempts in Development Workflows
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies: 'prompt injection inside development workflows' as a direct risk. This represents manipulation of agent decision-making.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor agent input streams and development environment logs for crafted payloads or unusual instruction sequences attempting to override agent constraints or approved workflows. Correlate with unexpected API calls or file modifications following such inputs.

suggestion.title: Agent Script Execution Without Authorization
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'Agents don't just suggest a change and wait; they run scripts, query internal systems, modify files, and call APIs at machine speed.' No human review before execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track scripts and commands executed by agent service accounts or automation contexts. Flag those that exceed predefined safe command sets, access production systems, or execute on critical infrastructure without prior approval records.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Agent Access to Internal Systems or Data
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'unauthorized access to systems or data, data exposure through tool calls' as risk. Agents inherit permissions and may abuse them.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor API calls, database queries, and system access initiated by agent processes. Alert on access to sensitive systems outside defined scope, lateral movement to unexpected services, or enumeration patterns inconsistent with stated job functions.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Contamination via Malicious Agent-Selected Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Article states agents 'pull in MCP servers, skills, APIs, external tools, data sources...even though they were never declared as traditional dependencies.' 76 malicious skills identified in analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when agents add external dependencies, tools, or MCP servers not present in approved manifests. Correlate with known-malicious skill hash lists. Detect agent processes that dynamically load unapproved packages or fetch tools from untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: Suspicious VS Code Extension Installation via Webview Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'abuses this system by running malicious JavaScript inside a webview to simulate keypresses in the main editor and install an extension' — malicious extension installation is core attack vector but zero detections generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code extension installation from non-standard sources or via programmatic API calls rather than user GUI. Alert on rapid extension installations post-github.dev activity. Track extension store API calls and installation manifest changes indicating unauthorized extensions loaded.

suggestion.title: GitHub OAuth Token Exfiltration from Compromised VS Code Session
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'POSTing over an OAuth token to github.dev that allows it to interact with GitHub on your behalf' and 'extracts the GitHub OAuth token' — token theft is the exploitation objective but no credential-theft detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound network traffic from VS Code or github.dev processes containing GitHub OAuth tokens (bearer tokens in HTTP headers or POST bodies). Alert on GitHub tokens accessed by unexpected child processes spawned by VS Code or webview. Monitor for token exfiltration to non-GitHub domains.

suggestion.title: Abnormal GitHub API Repository Enumeration from VS Code Context
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'queries the GitHub API to enumerate all private repositories the victim can access' — post-exploitation discovery step explicitly described but undetected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk GitHub API /user/repos or /repos endpoint queries originating from VS Code or github.dev processes. Detect enumeration of private repositories exceeding baseline pattern. Flag repository discovery that doesn't correlate with developer commit/push activity.

suggestion.title: Webview Sandbox Escape via Message-Passing IPC Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'abuses VS Code's sandboxed webview message-passing system' and 'simulate keypresses' — webview-to-editor privilege boundary violation is technical core of exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IPC/message-passing traffic between VS Code webview process and main editor process. Detect attempts to inject commands or simulate user input (keyboard events) originating from webview context. Alert on webview process spawning child processes or accessing main-process memory.

suggestion.title: Malicious Link Click Triggering github.dev OAuth Token Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'tricking users into clicking a link' and 'allows attackers to install malicious extensions' — initial access vector is user clicking attacker-controlled link.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate user clicks on suspicious links (possibly in phishing emails/messages) with immediate github.dev navigation and VS Code OAuth token access. Alert on github.dev URLs with unusual query parameters or from attacker-controlled hosts. Flag rapid extension installations following suspicious link clicks.

suggestion.title: github.dev Authentication Bypass Enabling Full-Scope OAuth Token Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The token is not scoped to the particular repo you interacted with, meaning it has full access to every other repo' — vulnerability allows unscoped token elevation that bypasses intended repository isolation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for github.dev authentication flows that result in full-scope GitHub OAuth tokens instead of repo-scoped tokens. Detect POST requests to github.dev carrying unrestricted tokens. Alert when github.dev session tokens are used to access repositories outside the current context.

suggestion.title: Minecraft Launcher Process Spawning Suspicious Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Weedhack Attacks Minecraft Users' — implies malware execution chain initiated via Minecraft client/launcher compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor parent process: javaw.exe, launcher processes matching */Minecraft/* or java-based game launchers spawning child processes with obfuscated names, writing to temp, accessing network resources outside expected game CDNs. Baseline normal Minecraft child processes (updater, auth) and alert on anomalous cmdline or target paths.

suggestion.title: CountLoader Malware Persistence via Pirated Software Installation
suggestion.rationale: Title mentions 'CountLoader Hits 86K' and 'Miners Spread via Pirated Content' — indicates distribution mechanism and need to detect post-installation persistence patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for registry modifications and scheduled task creation that occur shortly after pirated software installation (correlation with unsigned/suspicious MSI/EXE execution). CountLoader at 86K scale suggests widespread distribution; monitor for uncommon registry hives under HKCU\Software\*, new Run/RunOnce keys, and scheduled tasks with randomized names executing from %TEMP% or %APPDATA%.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Miner Process Resource Exhaustion
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly mentions 'Miners Spread via Pirated Content' — malware post-execution behavior is resource consumption (CPU, network for pool communication).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious processes with sustained high CPU utilization (>70% for >10min) combined with outbound network connections to known cryptocurrency mining pools (pool.***.com, stratum ports 3333-4444). Look for parent-child relationships linking legitimate process (svchost, explorer) to unsigned miner binary. Baseline expected CPU consumers per environment.

suggestion.title: Unsigned Binary Execution from Temporary Directories Post-Piracy
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is pirated content distribution. Typical payload delivery extracts to temp, executes unsigned binaries. Title mentions distribution mechanism but pipeline extracted no execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unsigned executables in %TEMP%, %APPDATA%\Local\Temp spawned by user-initiated processes (explorer.exe, chrome.exe from Downloads). Correlate with pirated software distribution channels (keywords: 'crack', 'keygen', 'serial', 'warez' in parent file path/URI). Exclude known software updaters and legitimate temp usage.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PowerShell/CMD Execution from Game or Pirated Software Context
suggestion.rationale: Malware delivered via Minecraft or pirated software typically uses shell commands for second-stage payload download or privilege escalation. Title establishes attack surface but no execution detection offered.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cmd.exe or powershell.exe spawned from java.exe, javaw.exe, or suspicious parent processes associated with pirated software installers. Baseline expected child processes (Windows Update, support tools) and alert on cmdline patterns indicative of: URL fetching (IWR, Invoke-WebRequest, curl), file deobfuscation (base64 decode), and registry/service manipulation.

suggestion.title: Active Directory Enumeration via Python
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'automated Active Directory (AD) discovery' with 'iterative approach to developing and testing' and 'collecting observations from completed tasks.' Detection gap for Python-executed AD discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on python.exe or pythonw.exe executing with LDAP libraries, ldapsearch tools, net group commands, or DirectoryServices API. Focus on recursive OU traversal, Domain Admins membership queries, or non-standard user contexts running Python discovery scripts.

suggestion.title: Shellcode Injection into Legitimate Windows Executables
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Python-based malware development scripts for injecting shellcode into legitimate Windows executables while preserving original functionality.' No detection use case for this injection pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process injection: legitimate service binaries (calc.exe, mspaint.exe, rundll32.exe) exhibiting CreateRemoteThread, unusual child spawning, memory-mapped module loads, or execution from non-standard parent processes with memory access patterns.

suggestion.title: Cobalt Strike Beacon Traffic Obfuscation
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'Cobalt Strike profiles designed to make beacon traffic resemble legitimate web requests.' No use case for detecting obfuscated beacon C2 signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify beacons via HTTP/HTTPS anomalies: unusual port combinations for web traffic, beacon-specific header patterns, jitter intervals, data exfiltration indicators, mismatched SSL certificates, or Host header inconsistencies.

suggestion.title: Telegram Bot API C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Telegram bot API–based external command and control (C2) mechanism that routed communication through Telegram's infrastructure rather than using direct connections.' No detection for this C2 channel.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound api.telegram.org POST requests with suspicious bot tokens, unusual chat IDs, or beaconing cadence from internal hosts. Flag periodic callback patterns or data sizes inconsistent with legitimate Telegram usage.

suggestion.title: Polymorphic EDR Evasion Payload Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states framework 'wraps a raw payload in layers of encryption, evasion, and alternative execution techniques, producing custom-built executables.' Multi-layer evasion execution patterns are undetected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on executables with multiple PE unpacking layers, self-modifying code, processes spawning from %TEMP%/%AppData% with packed signatures, memory execution transitions, or processes writing executable memory regions then jumping into them.

suggestion.title: Cloudflare Worker C2 Redirector Access
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'Cloudflare Worker acting as a front-end redirector to obscure the actual backend C2 server.' This redirector-based C2 infrastructure pattern is not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections to *.workers.dev domains from internal hosts, especially from non-browser processes. Flag repetitive connections with unusual frequency or data sizes inconsistent with legitimate web traffic patterns.

suggestion.title: CVE-2022-0492 Kernel Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs substitution of CVE-2022-0492 into asset-exposure hunt templates ('Standard asset-exposure hunt...Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>') and emphasizes patch status as detection foundation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner outputs and Linux OS inventory for CVE-2022-0492 matches. Identify unpatched kernel versions on internet-facing systems. Cross-reference asset inventory with network exposure telemetry to prioritize assets at risk.

suggestion.title: Suspicious cgroups v1 release_agent Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'privilege escalation via the cgroups v1 release_agent feature' as the concrete exploitation mechanism—this is the behavioral indicator that detections must capture at endpoint level.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on write operations to cgroups v1 release_agent paths (/sys/fs/cgroup/*/release_agent) by unprivileged processes. Flag execution of arbitrary commands through release_agent callbacks or manipulation of cgroup settings by non-root processes.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Root Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article outcome is 'privilege escalation'; detection must surface the post-exploitation behavioral shift (elevated UID/capability acquisition) that follows successful cgroups abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect privilege escalation success indicators: unprivileged processes achieving UID 0 execution, elevation of process capabilities (CAP_SYS_ADMIN), or root-spawned children from unprivileged parents. Correlate timing with cgroups manipulation and kernel exploit artifacts.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Kernel Exposure Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'patch lag is the silent killer' and sets federal due-date 2026-06-05, requiring asset verification as primary SOC control. Template guidance explicitly references asset-exposure hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all Linux systems with kernel versions vulnerable to CVE-2022-0492. Filter for internet-reachable or externally-exposed assets in network topology. Prioritize patch scheduling by exposure risk.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Android Framework Detection - CVE-2025-48595
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2025-48595' and 'Android Framework contains an integer overflow vulnerability.' Substitute CVE into standard asset-exposure template as instructed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and patch-management logs for devices running vulnerable Android Framework versions matching CVE-2025-48595. Prioritize Federal civilian agency devices in preparation for 2026-06-05 deadline.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Android Framework Integer Overflow - T1068
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'allows for code execution that could allow for local privilege escalation.' T1068 is the correct MITRE technique for the exploitation+LPE phase; T1190 alone misses the actual privilege-escalation execution step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected uid/gid elevation or system/root privilege requests originating from Android Framework library calls or untrusted app processes. Correlate with vulnerable Framework versions.

suggestion.title: Federal Patch Compliance Monitoring - CVE-2025-48595
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Federal patch due: 2026-06-05.' Creates a hard deadline and regulatory audit checkpoint; must track deployment progress and alert on non-compliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track cumulative patch deployment rates for Android Framework across Federal civilian fleet relative to 2026-06-05 deadline. Generate daily compliance dashboard and pre-deadline alert on devices still unpatched.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Activity Post-Android-Framework-Update
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability in Framework itself. Exploit window likely opens immediately after update if attacker has pre-positioned local gadget/app. Hunt for privilege escalation within 48-72 hours post-Framework update.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Framework update timestamps with unexpected privilege escalation, root access requests, or system-level process spawning from user-space apps within 3-day window. Flag if escalation originates from unsigned or third-party apps.

suggestion.title: Multiple Failed Logins Followed by Account Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states brute-force attack occurred, implying many failed login attempts before compromise. Pipeline extracted no detection for failed login clustering. Article phrase: 'brute-force attack' requires flagging repeated auth failures + successful compromise chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on 5+ failed logins to same account from single IP within 10 minutes, correlated with successful login from same IP within 30 minutes afterward. High-fidelity indicator of brute-force success.

suggestion.title: Vault Export or Bulk Data Download Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'encrypted vaults...downloaded', a direct exfiltration indicator. Pipeline missed detection for unusual export/download activity following credential compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag vault export requests, especially within 4 hours of account compromise or from new/untrusted IP. Correlate with sign-in from geographic impossibility or new device.

suggestion.title: First-Time Login from Attacker-Controlled Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Post-brute-force success, compromised accounts would log in from attacker infrastructure. Article indicates vaults were accessed post-attack. Pipeline missed first-login-from-new-device and geographic anomaly detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For accounts with recent failed login attempts, alert on first successful login from previously unseen country, IP range, or device. Especially high-risk if geographically/temporally inconsistent with user's historical patterns.

suggestion.title: High-Volume Authentication Failures Against SaaS Service
suggestion.rationale: Brute-force attack structure: many auth attempts. Article phrase 'brute-force attack' is the core indicator. Pipeline must detect credential spray or dictionary attack patterns at service level.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor aggregate failed login counts per service. Alert if >100 failed logins in 1 hour or >20 unique accounts with ≥3 failures each in 5 minutes. Suggests credential stuffing or spray.

suggestion.title: Account Lockout Followed by Successful Authentication Elsewhere
suggestion.rationale: If Dashlane implements account lockout after brute-force (mentioned in many disclosures), attackers may succeed via secondary paths or on unlocked accounts. Pipeline should correlate lockout with lateral access attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect account lockout events followed by successful logins to related services (e.g., email recovery, account recovery flows) within 2 hours from different IP. Indicates account takeover evasion.

suggestion.title: WinRAR Exploitation - Suspicious Child Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Gamaredon Exploits WinRAR to Deliver GammaWorm and GammaSteel'—implies WinRAR is being weaponized as initial access vector; pipeline should detect post-exploit child processes spawned by WinRAR.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for WinRAR.exe (or rar.exe, unrar.exe variants) spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or other interpreters with unusual command-line arguments. WinRAR exploit chains typically trigger immediate shell execution post-extraction.

suggestion.title: GammaWorm/GammaSteel File Creation and Registry Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article references delivery of 'GammaWorm and GammaSteel' payloads; pipeline failed to create detection for malware staging or persistence mechanisms typical of these families.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of executables or scripts with names containing 'Gamma', 'Worm', or 'Steel' in temp directories (%TEMP%, %APPDATA%). Monitor for registry modifications under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Run and CurrentVersion\RunOnce for persistence.

suggestion.title: GammaWorm Command-and-Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: Title identifies GammaWorm as delivered malware; no detection for C&C callback patterns, DNS queries, or outbound network connections typical of Gamaredon infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections from newly-spawned processes (child of WinRAR) to non-standard ports or known Gamaredon-affiliated domains. Flag DNS queries for unusual TLDs or subdomains typical of APT malware.

suggestion.title: Malware Extraction from RAR Archive
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector explicitly involves WinRAR extracting embedded payloads; should detect process execution immediately after archive extraction or temporary files containing executables.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect WinRAR processes reading/writing files to temporary directories followed by execution of those files within seconds. Correlate file creation timestamps in %TEMP% with subsequent process launches.

suggestion.title: Process Injection and Code Execution by GammaWorm
suggestion.rationale: Gamaredon malware families are known to use process injection for defense evasion; pipeline missed detection for parent-child process anomalies or unsigned DLL injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for injection patterns: parent process (initial WinRAR child) injecting into svchost.exe, explorer.exe, or other trusted binaries. Flag cross-process memory writes or remote thread creation from unsigned executables.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Detection - Gamaredon Post-Exploitation Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Gamaredon campaigns targeting Ukraine often include reconnaissance and lateral movement; no detection for process discovery, network enumeration, or credential harvesting post-delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect enumeration commands (net view, dsquery, nltest) or whoami/tasklist execution from non-admin processes spawned by initial malware. Monitor for SMB/RDP connection attempts to internal systems.

suggestion.title: Detection of Unpatched Android Devices Post-Patch-Release
suggestion.rationale: Article states 124 flaws patched; defenders need to detect devices still running pre-patch versions. Phrase: 'Google June 2026 Android Update Patches 124 Flaws' implies patch-lag risk window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Android devices reporting OS build versions prior to June 2026 patches 30+ days post-release. Flag policy exceptions for devices with security patch levels >60 days behind current. Correlate with network behavioral shifts indicating post-compromise activity.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of Actively-Exploited Android CVE in Wild
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'One Actively Exploited' vulnerability. Defenders must detect exploitation attempts of this specific CVE before patches deploy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Without CVE ID from article body, detect Android process crashes with memory corruption signatures (heap/stack exhaustion, pointer dereference), elevated privilege grants post-crash, or unusual system partition access. Correlate SELinux denial logs with exploit-stage syscall patterns (mmap, mprotect on code segments).

suggestion.title: Malicious App Installation Exploiting Patched Vulnerabilities
suggestion.rationale: Android patch articles typically describe attack chains via malicious apps; article mentions 124 flaws, likely including app-delivery vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect installation of apps from non-Play-Store sources or sideloaded APKs within 7 days of patch release. Flag apps with requested permissions mismatched to declared functionality, or those requesting accessibility/device-admin rights without justification. Cross-check against Google Play Protect threat lists.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Composer Package Installation from Non-Standard Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'every tag across multiple Composer packages rewritten,' indicating package source manipulation. Phrase: 'Laravel-Lang Supply Chain Attack' and 'Multiple Composer Packages Rewritten' establish dependency substitution as core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect composer install/update commands with suspicious registry domains or unusual curl/wget activity to pull package metadata. Monitor for composer execution with HTTP connections to non-packagist.org domains or suspicious IP ASNs.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration via CI Environment Variable Access
suggestion.rationale: Attack objective explicitly stated as 'steal CI secrets.' Phrase: 'to steal CI secrets' establishes credential access and exfiltration as primary kill-chain step not covered.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect access to CI environment variables (GitHub Actions secrets, GitLab CI_JOB_TOKEN, AWS temporary credentials) from unexpected process contexts. Monitor for ENV dump commands (env, printenv, get-childitem env:) in build pipelines or unusual credential handler invocations.

suggestion.title: Malicious Code Injection via Repository Tag Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Core attack method: 'Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Rewritten.' Indicates Git tag/commit history rewriting or force pushes to inject malicious versions.
