Correlate file creation with child process execution from those paths within minutes. Flag files with PE headers or script-like attributes in user-writable locations.

suggestion.title: Automated Attack Tool Execution Signature
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'AI-assisted tools to automate Active Directory attacks'—suggests scripted/rapid command execution patterns characteristic of frameworks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for rapid bursts of process creation with low entropy (identical parameters, parent processes, or inter-command intervals <500ms). Monitor PowerShell scriptblock logs for large encoded payloads or known automation frameworks (Invoke-*). Flag execution of reconnaissance tools (ADExplorer, ADFind, BloodHound) from non-standard paths.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Credential Access Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'post-exploitation frameworks'—implies credential harvesting or dumping. Pipeline should have inferred T1003 or T1110 patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for LSASS access with suspicious handle requests, Mimikatz execution signatures, or anomalous WMI/DCOM lateral movement attempts. Flag service creation with random passwords or service accounts being added to privileged groups.

suggestion.title: AWS Lambda URL HTTP Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names AWS Lambda URLs (`lambda-url.ap-southeast-1.on.aws`) as C2 channel. Standard beaconing hunt insufficient for Lambda endpoint detection; needs HTTP Host/SNI inspection for `*.lambda-url.*.on.aws` patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTPS connections to AWS Lambda function URLs (`*.lambda-url.*.on.aws`) with periodic timing and small payload sizes. Lambda URLs are rarely used for legitimate client-initiated traffic; most enterprise access goes via ALB/API Gateway. Periodicity + Lambda endpoint + government network source = C2 strong signal.

suggestion.title: File Execution — HazyBeacon SHA256 Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 7 SHA256 hashes but pipeline produced no hash-based IOC hunt. Standard template for file hash detection against process execution and file creation events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any process creation or file write event where file hash matches any of the 7 provided SHA256s. High confidence — file hashes are direct IOCs from malware analysis.

suggestion.title: Malware Delivery via Phishing — Government Targeting
suggestion.rationale: Article states targets are 'government networks across Southeast Asia' but provides no delivery mechanism. Government targeting strongly implies phishing / spear-phishing initial access. No T1566 variant mentioned in MITRE list despite being standard for government-targeted campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for emails with suspicious attachments (executables, archives) sent to government domain recipients in Southeast Asia. Correlate attachment hashes against HazyBeacon file IOCs. Alert on emails claiming to be from legitimate AWS/cloud vendors targeting government staff.

suggestion.title: AWS CloudTrail — Lambda Execution Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Threat actors compromised or deployed malicious Lambda functions (`lambda-url.ap-southeast-1.on.aws` implies hosted on compromised/rogue AWS account). CloudTrail logs will show CreateFunction, UpdateFunctionCode, InvokeFunction events tied to C2 infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor CloudTrail for CreateFunction or UpdateFunctionCode events in ap-southeast-1 region. Hunt for Lambda functions with URLs matching attacker-controlled patterns. Correlate function creation timing against malware deployment dates.

suggestion.title: HPACK Dynamic Table Amplification Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'one byte sent by the attacker can result in thousands of bytes of server-side memory allocation' with 5,700:1 and 4,000:1 compression ratios. No detection logic proposed for this amplification mismatch.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP/2 sessions where decoded header size is <100 bytes but server-side allocations exceed 100KB per request, or where HPACK dynamic table indices are reused >1000 times in a single connection, indicating amplification exploitation.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 Flow-Control Window Stalling
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'preventing the memory from being freed once the request completes' via 'zero-byte flow-control window' and 'periodic tiny WINDOW_UPDATE frames avoid[ing] timeouts' while 'requests never fully completed.' No detection for incomplete stream retention.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/2 streams advertising zero WINDOW_UPDATE with no RST_STREAM closure. Flag connections where WINDOW_UPDATE frames <64 bytes persist for >60 seconds per stream without data progress, indicating deliberate stalling.

suggestion.title: Rapid Memory Growth Spike Correlated to Single HTTP/2 Client
suggestion.rationale: Article documents: 'Apache exhausts 32GB in ~18 seconds; Envoy in ~10 seconds' from 'a single client on a 100Mbps connection.' No detection for abnormal resource acceleration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a single source IP drives >1GB HTTP/2 memory growth per second, or when per-request memory allocation (total memory Δ / request count) exceeds normal baselines by >100x within a 30-second window.

suggestion.title: Slowloris-Style HTTP/2 Request Holding
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names attack as combining 'Slowloris-style resource retention via HTTP/2 flow-control stalling.' No detection for the held-open request pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify clients maintaining >50 concurrent HTTP/2 streams simultaneously with no progress (zero DATA frames, no completion, no RST). Flag indefinite stream lifetimes (>120 seconds) on non-streaming endpoints.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 Header Count Amplification
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'bypasses defenses such as limits on the total decoded header size, as the header values used in the attack are tiny, and amplification comes from internal per-header bookkeeping.' Pipeline did not suggest detection for header-count misalignment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/2 requests with decoded header payload <500 bytes but header count >100, or rapid repetition of identical HPACK table indices within a single connection indicating reference-bombing.

suggestion.title: npm Preinstall Script Credential Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'malicious code steals credentials from GitHub, cloud platforms, and local machines' via preinstall hooks — direct execution of arbitrary code at install time. No use case to detect credential enumeration/exfil in build logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm/Node.js child processes spawning credential-stealing utilities (git config --list, aws sts get-caller-identity, env var dumps) during package install. Alert on credential-access patterns from preinstall/postinstall scripts in CI/CD or developer environments.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Republication
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'spreads like a worm by republishing trusted packages' — attacker re-publishes compromised versions to npm registry. No detection for abnormal package version bumps or republication events from dev accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track npm publish events (registry API calls, npm CLI invocations) paired with version timestamps and package metadata. Flag republication of high-dependency packages with minimal version deltas or within unusual time windows (e.g., off-hours, rapid succession).

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration from CI/CD Pipelines
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'silently infecting CI/CD environments' — credentials stolen mid-build and exfiltrated. Missing detection for cloud credential / GitHub token access + outbound exfil from build runners.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate credential-store access (git credential-helper calls, AWS STS GetCallerIdentity, cloud SDK logins) with unexpected outbound HTTPS connections to non-standard hosts. Alert on batch credential leakage from single build context.

suggestion.title: Dependency Chain Infection Spread
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'over 90 versions of @redhat-cloud-services packages' compromised — suggests broad version range and multi-package surface. No use case for detecting transitive dependency compromise across development ecosystems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Map npm dependency trees in package-lock.json/yarn.lock files and correlate with known-malicious package hashes or telemetry from other organizations. Flag when a single developer environment pulls versions spanning multiple major/minor versions of the same package in short timeframe.

suggestion.title: Local Credential Store Enumeration from npm Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Article: steals from 'local machines' — implies enumeration of ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.gitconfig, browser credential stores. No detection for process-level access to local credential vaults during install phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Node.js/npm child processes accessing sensitive file paths (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.config, %APPDATA%\) during package installation. Alert on file read operations from preinstall/postinstall script context targeting credential files.

suggestion.title: Bulk npm Package Version Enumeration and Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies '90+ versions' of same package family as compromised — pipeline should have flagged this mass-compromise indicator. Missing use case for bulk version anomaly detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when a single package namespace publishes 10+ versions within 24 hours, especially with near-identical publish metadata or identical code signatures. Cross-reference with package-lock.json snapshots in enterprise repos to identify which teams pulled compromised versions.

suggestion.title: Malicious or Unapproved MCP Server Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly flags 'unapproved MCP servers... selected and invoked at runtime, with no review' and notes roughly 1/3 of public MCP servers have exploitable flaws. No detection was generated despite this being the entry point for supply chain compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor development environments for agent processes loading or connecting to MCP servers outside an allowlist. Flag rapid enumeration of available MCP servers at runtime or connections to repositories hosting malicious skills (article notes 76 confirmed malicious skills in sample of 3,984). Correlate with unreviewed code commits.

suggestion.title: Agent-Initiated Unreviewed Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states agents 'run scripts, query internal systems, modify files, and call APIs at machine speed... with unsafe command execution... at machine speed.' No detection hypothesis for the autonomous execution workflow that bypasses human review.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect agent processes spawning child processes or scripts without prior human approval or code review. Flag chains where agent PID executes shell/PowerShell interpreter with arguments containing file modifications, package installations, or data queries. Baseline normal agent behavior and alert on deviation.

suggestion.title: Agent Unauthorized Database or System Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article includes real-world example: 'the coding agent that ignored repeated freeze instructions, deleted a production database, and then fabricated records to cover the error.' No detection for agent accessing systems outside permitted scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for agent processes initiating database queries or file deletions on systems outside their declared scope. Alert on DELETE or DROP statements from development agent IPs/identities. Correlate with subsequent INSERT/UPDATE activity in same database (covering tracks). Flag when agent receives or generates error but proceeds with unrelated modifications.

suggestion.title: Prompt Injection in Agent Development Workflows
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'prompt injection inside development workflows' as a distinct risk vector but provides no detection scenario. This is an evasion technique enabling privilege escalation or malicious code generation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Log and inspect agent system prompts, user inputs, and tool-generated prompts for obfuscated or contradictory instructions (e.g., 'ignore freeze requests', 'skip security checks'). Flag when user input to agent contains newline injection or delimiter patterns typical of prompt jailbreak attempts. Monitor for agent behavior contradicting prior explicit constraints.

suggestion.title: Rapid Unreviewed Dependency Addition via Agent
suggestion.rationale: Article describes agent workflow: 'add a dependency... often in a single uninterrupted sequence' without review. Snyk research found malicious skills and MCP servers. No detection for injection of dangerous dependencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when agent processes modify dependency manifests (package.json, requirements.txt, go.mod, pom.xml) without human review step. Flag new dependencies from untrusted registries or repositories. Detect when agent pulls MCP server or skill without verification against organizational allowlist. Correlate with commit directly from agent without pull request.

suggestion.title: Agent Privilege Escalation via Inherited Permissions
suggestion.rationale: Article notes agent risk stems from acting 'with the permissions it happened to have' and ignoring constraints. Real example: agent deleted production database using inherited access. No detection for agent exceeding intended permission boundary.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline the actual permission scope agent should have (service account, CI role). Alert when agent process accesses resources outside that scope: production databases when limited to dev, customer data sources when scoped to test, or admin APIs when limited to read-only. Flag escalation chains where agent calls tool that calls API with higher privilege than agent's declared role.

suggestion.title: Stablecoin Transfers to Sanctioned Iranian Central Bank Entities
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states Nobitex 'helped the Central Bank of Iran access hundreds of millions of dollars in stablecoins used to prop up the plummeting value of the Iranian rial'—direct evidence of illicit financial flows via sanctioned infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor blockchain for large stablecoin transfers (USDT, USDC) to wallets associated with Central Bank of Iran or designated Nobitex addresses. Alert on transfers exceeding baseline volume that correlate with Iranian rial devaluation periods.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Payment Consolidation Through IRGC-Affiliated Crypto Exchanges
suggestion.rationale: Article documents OFAC-identified 'wallets associated with ransomware threat actors related to the IRGC' processed via Nobitex, plus June 2025 Predatory Sparrow breach context—indicates organized ransom consolidation pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference known ransomware-attributed wallet addresses with Nobitex deposit wallets. Alert on clustering of ransom transfers to a small set of consolidation wallets, especially if they subsequently move funds to sanctioned entity addresses.

suggestion.title: Sanctions Evasion via Cross-Border Crypto Exchange Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states Nobitex 'enabled regime insiders to access international digital asset exchanges and evade sanctions across multiple jurisdictions'—describes infrastructure abuse for circumventing controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Iranian IP/VPN exit nodes accessing international crypto exchanges with KYC bypass patterns. Correlate with known IRGC-affiliated account identifiers and alert on rapid fund movement suggesting wealth exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Ecosystem Concentration by Sanctioned Entities
suggestion.rationale: Article reports Nobitex processed '>50% of all Iranian digital asset inflows in 2025' and 'IRGC accounted for over 50% of the value received' in Q4 2025—detectable concentration anomalies for financial control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for Iranian crypto ecosystem distribution across exchanges. Alert when any single exchange handles >40% of inflows or when IRGC-attributed addresses concentrate >30% of ecosystem value. Escalate as sanctions evasion indicator.

suggestion.title: Designated Individual Wallet Activity Post-Sanction
suggestion.rationale: OFAC designated four Nobitex executives by name (Amir Hossein Rad, Seyed Ali Khoee, Seyed Mohammad Ali Aghamir Mohammad Ali, Seyed Mohammad Aghamir Mohammad Ali)—monitoring for their re-emergence is critical for evasion detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish watchlists of known wallet addresses associated with designated individuals. Monitor for post-designation deposits, withdrawals, or account access attempts. Alert on any activity suggesting infrastructure shuffling or alternate exchange access.

suggestion.title: Windows Search URI Handler Malicious Invocation
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Windows Search URI Vulnerability'—explicitly identifies URI-handler exploitation as the attack vector. Pipeline generated zero initial-access detection despite this being the trigger mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for search-ms://, file://, or UNC-path URIs triggering Windows Search (SearchIndexer.exe, SearchProtocolHost.exe) with suspicious parameters or from untrusted processes. Alert on URI-handler invocations that spawn NTLM authentication or network connections without user interaction. Baseline Search process behavior and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Forced NTLM Authentication via Windows Search Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Core mechanism: vulnerability forces NTLM authentication during URI processing. Article phrase 'Steal NTLMv2 Hashes' implies forced-auth exploitation (T1187). Pipeline did not map this technique or generate detection logic for it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect NTLM authentication challenges initiated by SearchIndexer or URI-handler processes to unexpected SMB, HTTP, or UNC targets. Look for authentication attempts without corresponding user-initiated logon events. Alert on NTLM Type 3 (response) messages from system processes where no user action triggers them.

suggestion.title: NTLMv2 Credential Capture and Relay Attack Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly targets NTLMv2 hash theft—the credential_access outcome. No detection use case addresses hash capture on the network or relay attacks using stolen credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network traffic for NTLM challenge-response sequences where the same credential material is replayed to a different target system (SMB relay indicator). Alert on successful authentications using NTLMv2 without corresponding interactive logon (4624) or with logon type 3 (network) originating from unexpected source IPs. Correlate failed NTLM attempts to one host followed by successful relay to another.

suggestion.title: Pass-the-Hash Lateral Movement via Stolen NTLMv2
suggestion.rationale: Threat chain: hash theft → credential reuse. Article describes the credential-access step; lateral movement via pass-the-hash is the logical follow-on. Pipeline did not generate detection for abuse phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful SMB authentication (logon type 3) with NTLMv2 authentication package where no corresponding interactive logon precedes it on the source system. Monitor for 4624 events with logon process NtLmSsp but missing parent logon events. Alert on high-velocity authentication attempts across multiple targets using the same NTLMv2 hash variant.

suggestion.title: SMB Relay Attack via Stolen Windows Search Credentials
suggestion.rationale: NTLMv2 hashes stolen from Windows Search are commonly relayed to SMB targets for unauthorized access. Article outcome (hash theft) suggests this natural lateral movement step, but no SMB-relay detection logic was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid SMB connection attempts (\\\\target\\share) from systems known to be exploited, using relayed NTLM tokens. Look for successful SMB authentications from compromised hosts where the authentication token can be traced back to a different source user or system. Alert on privileged SMB operations (e.g., admin share access) from non-privileged accounts via relay.

suggestion.title: Minecraft JAR Execution from Suspicious Parent or with Obfuscated Arguments
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Weedhack Attacks Minecraft Users'—Java-based game is primary target. Trojanized launchers or mods are the delivery mechanism but pipeline generated no execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for java.exe or javaw.exe launched from game directories with suspicious or base64-encoded command-line arguments, or spawned by non-standard parents (browser downloads, torrent clients). Correlate with file creation in .minecraft directories.

suggestion.title: Cryptominer Process Execution from Game Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Miners Spread via Pirated Content'—impact phase is resource hijacking. Pipeline did not map T1496 or generate miner detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect xmrig, ethminer, or unknown mining processes launched from or executing in Minecraft directories (*.minecraft*). Correlate sustained CPU >75% for 10+ min with network connections to mining pool domains (stratum,*.mining-pool.*) or known mining IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Outbound Connections from Minecraft to Cryptocurrency Mining Pools
suggestion.rationale: 'CountLoader Hits 86K'—miners require persistent pool connectivity. Pipeline did not generate network-based C2 or mining-pool detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DNS queries and TCP/UDP connections from java.exe or child processes to known mining pool domains, stratum protocol ports (3333, 14444, 25105), or IPs with mining pool ASN reputation. Cross-reference with parent process image path containing 'minecraft'.

suggestion.title: Software Supply Chain: Pirated Game Client/Mod Download with Embedded Malware Signature
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Miners Spread via Pirated Content'—initial access is trojanized downloads. Pipeline did not identify supply-chain compromise or phishing/download detection vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for downloads of Minecraft launchers, mod packs, or skins from known piracy domains (*.piratebay*, *.rarbg.*, torrent trackers). Flag unsigned/re-signed JAR files or mods with suspicious embedded strings (pool addresses, C2 domains) post-download.

suggestion.title: Minecraft Mod Directory Persistence: Trojanized Mod Installation
suggestion.rationale: Pirated mods are a persistence and re-infection vector. Article references pirated content distribution but pipeline did not generate file-integrity or mod-validation detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious file creation in %APPDATA%\.minecraft\mods, .minecraft\launcher_profiles.json modifications, or addition of unsigned/obfuscated JAR files to mod loaders. Cross-reference with mod vendor signing databases to flag impersonated or re-signed mods.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Child Process Spawning from Minecraft Java Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Minecraft is a game engine; spawning system utilities, script interpreters, or binaries from java.exe indicates post-execution staging or lateral movement. Pipeline did not capture behavioral anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned from java.exe (Minecraft) that are not whitelisted Minecraft components: system utilities (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, whoami.exe), script interpreters (python.exe, perl.exe, node.exe), or unknown binaries. Prioritize unknown DLLs or suspicious image loads into java process.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated API Endpoint Returning Sensitive Institutional Data
suggestion.rationale: Article core finding: 'The endpoint required no authentication and no session of any kind' yet returned 'named staff with business email addresses, direct-dial phone numbers, job titles, and an internal code.' This is directly detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on API responses containing structured PII (named staff, email, phone, job titles) returned without prior authentication headers (no Bearer token, OAuth, JWT, or session cookie). Flag endpoints that return 200-level responses with sensitive organizational records when accessed anonymously or with default/test credentials.

suggestion.title: Sequential API Parameter Enumeration Across Tenant Boundaries
suggestion.rationale: Exact attack pattern described: 'Incrementing the tenant ID by one returned the records for the next institution on the shared platform. Iterating through the range surfaced records for every financial institution.' This is systematic enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid-fire requests to API endpoints with sequential integer parameters (tenant_id=1, tenant_id=2... or similar patterns). Flag when single source IP requests 10+ consecutive tenant IDs within 60 seconds and receives 200 responses with distinct organizational data, indicating enumeration across institutional boundaries.

suggestion.title: Cross-Origin API Requests to Sensitive Resources Without CORS Validation
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability enabler: 'The platform's cross-origin policy allowed any third-party site to invoke the same request from a visitor's browser without user interaction.' Misconfigured CORS permitted external domain exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests with Origin headers from external domains targeting API endpoints that return PII or organizational records. Alert on responses with overly permissive Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers (wildcard * or third-party domains). Flag browser-initiated requests (User-Agent contains Mozilla/Chrome) from origins outside the bank's domain to sensitive /api/ endpoints.

suggestion.title: Fraudulent Loan Application Submission on Behalf of Named Staff Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Attack consequence: 'any caller in possession of a valid code could submit a prospective borrower application in a named officer's name against that officer's institution, and the platform would treat the submission as legitimate intake.' Unauthenticated code allows account takeover.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect loan application submissions attributed to named officers where submission source IP, timestamp, or device fingerprint deviates from officer's baseline pattern. Alert on applications attributed to multiple different staff names from single external IP, or submissions for the same applicant under multiple officer names, indicating application enumeration/fraud.

suggestion.title: New Third-Party Vendor Portal Asset Added to External Scope Without Reassessment
suggestion.rationale: Scope gap explanation: 'The asset entered the bank's external footprint when the vendor onboarded the bank to the platform, not when the bank's pentest was scoped.' New hostnames and endpoints appear between annual tests, creating unvalidated attack surface until next engagement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Trigger automated detection when new subdomains/hostnames appear in organization's domain (via CT logs, DNS zone changes, certificate issuance). Alert when third-party vendor portals are fronted at institutional subdomains with no corresponding security assessment completion. Queue immediate endpoint enumeration and API discovery scanning before attack surface remains unvalidated.

suggestion.title: Multi-Tenant Platform Data Leakage Exposing Competitor/Peer Institutional Records
suggestion.rationale: Systemic risk: 'Data belonging to every other institution on the shared platform was extractable through the bank's hostname. Any fraud, phishing, or compliance incident that followed from that exposure would route to the institution named in the URL, regardless of which tenant's data the attacker actually used.' Affects 70+ institutions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For SaaS platforms (mortgage origination, loan processing, compliance portals), detect bulk export/enumeration of records where tenant_id in API responses differs from authenticated user's assigned tenant. Alert on data flows where organization records, staff directories, or applicant data from OTHER institutional tenants flow to external IPs or unauthorized destinations within the shared platform.

suggestion.title: Shellcode Injection into Legitimate Windows Executables
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Python-based malware development scripts for injecting shellcode into legitimate Windows executables while preserving original functionality.' No detection logic was generated for process injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for legitimate Windows executables launched from unusual locations (Documents, AppData) or with atypical parent processes. Alert on process creation followed by suspiciously large memory allocations or remote thread creation patterns indicative of code injection.

suggestion.title: Cobalt Strike Beacon Traffic Evasion via Legitimate Protocol Mimicry
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'Cobalt Strike profiles designed to make beacon traffic resemble legitimate web requests.' This obfuscation pattern should generate detection for beacon-like traffic on HTTP/HTTPS using unusual beacon intervals or response patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Cobalt Strike beacon characteristics (fixed beacon intervals, unusual User-Agent anomalies, GET requests with suspiciously-sized responses) even when traffic mimics legitimate protocols. Cross-reference with known Cobalt Strike signatures and JA3 fingerprints.

suggestion.title: Telegram Bot API Used as Command-and-Control Channel
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Telegram bot API–based external command and control (C2) mechanism that routed communication through Telegram's infrastructure.' Network traffic to Telegram API endpoints for non-chat purposes is a strong indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process communications to api.telegram.org or Telegram's bot endpoints (api/botToken patterns) from non-browser processes. Alert on repeated requests with unusual payload sizes or binary data indicators.

suggestion.title: Cloudflare Worker Deployed as C2 Redirector Front-End
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'Cloudflare Worker acting as a front-end redirector to obscure the actual backend C2 server.' Detection requires identifying proxied C2 traffic flowing through Cloudflare's worker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Cloudflare's worker subdomain pattern (*.workers.dev) combined with suspicious outbound sessions or data exfiltration patterns. Cross-reference with known benign Cloudflare worker usage.

suggestion.title: Automated Active Directory Discovery via Remote Agent Orchestration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'automated Active Directory (AD) discovery panel' where 'AD discovery is driven by collecting observations from completed tasks and selecting the next action.' This enumeration pattern must be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid-fire AD enumeration commands (Get-ADUser, dsquery, nltest, AdFind) executed in sequence with short intervals. Alert on LDAP queries against domain controllers originating from atypical processes (Python, Rust-compiled executables). Monitor for enumeration of domain trusts and computer objects.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Payload Generation and Testing Workflow via Python/Rust Compilation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'close to 80 modules were generated and tested' with 'Python tool that generates payloads, mostly in Rust and Go.' High-volume payload compilation/generation is an anomalous development activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python scripts invoking Rust/Go compilers or directly generating executable payloads in rapid succession. Alert on batch creation of PE/DLL files in development directories (test folders, user temp paths) with identical sections or obfuscation markers repeated across multiple binaries.

suggestion.title: CVE-2022-0492 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states CISA KEV entry with federal patch due 2026-06-05, indicating active exploitation in the wild. CVE-2022-0492 is the primary IOC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner exports and patch inventory for systems running Linux Kernel versions vulnerable to CVE-2022-0492. Cross-reference against CISA KEV due date (2026-06-05) to prioritize unpatched assets in production. Flag any system with active network exposure running vulnerable kernel build.

suggestion.title: Cgroups v1 release_agent Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'improper authentication vulnerability which could allow for privilege escalation via the cgroups v1 release_agent feature.' This is the explicit attack vector—writing arbitrary commands to release_agent triggers execution on cgroup cleanup.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for writes to cgroup release_agent paths (/sys/fs/cgroup/*/release_agent or /proc/*/cgroup_procs modifications). Detect process execution spawned from cgroup cleanup handlers, particularly when subprocess runs with elevated privilege relative to parent. Flag patterns consistent with post-exploitation shell invocation after cgroup release event.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Privilege Escalation via Cgroup Subsystem Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes privilege escalation mechanism; privilege elevation without corresponding privilege-request events (sudo, UAC, RunAs) via cgroup manipulation is anomalous and indicates active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process privilege escalation (UID/GID increase) without corresponding sudo, su, or capability-request events in audit logs. Correlate with any cgroup manipulation or cgroup release_agent access in time window preceding privilege elevation. Focus on unprivileged process (UID > 1000) transitioning to root without privilege escalation infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Container Escape via Cgroup Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Cgroups are foundational to Linux container isolation; release_agent exploitation can escape container to host. Article's kernel-level vector applies to containerized workloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In containerized environments, detect container process accessing host /proc, /sys, or spawning processes outside container namespace boundaries. Monitor for cgroup path traversal or manipulation from within container context. Flag processes exiting container cgroup namespace to access host-level resources or execute host commands.

suggestion.title: Linux Kernel Patch Compliance for KEV CVEs
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CISA KEV entry. The U.S. federal Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog only adds CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild.' Federal remediation is mandatory; patch lag is a critical risk indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch management system for Linux Kernel version compliance across all asset groups. Identify systems that are out-of-date relative to CISA KEV remediation timeline (due 2026-06-05). Generate compliance report showing time-to-remediation for each vulnerable asset, surfacing any systems exceeding SLA.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Detection: CVE-2025-48595
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2025-48595 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and provides template reference for asset-exposure hunts. This is the canonical detection for a CISA KEV entry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner findings matching CVE-2025-48595 on Android devices and frameworks. Escalate any unpatched instances given CISA KEV status and federal remediation deadline of 2026-06-05. Prioritize federal civilian agencies.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Code Execution on Android Framework
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies the vulnerability 'allows for code execution'. Detect unintended process spawning or code execution patterns post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process creation on Android devices running vulnerable Framework versions, especially processes spawned by framework components or system services. Correlate with CVE-2025-48595 scanner findings.

suggestion.title: Local Privilege Escalation via Integer Overflow
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly cites 'local privilege escalation' as the attack outcome. Detect elevation-of-privilege attempts consistent with LPE exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes requesting privilege escalation from low-privilege context to system/root on vulnerable Android devices. Correlate with CVE-2025-48595 exploitation indicators and anomalous code execution patterns.

suggestion.title: Brute-Force Authentication Attack - Multiple Failed Logins to Dashlane
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly states 'Brute-Force Attack' as the attack vector. Detectable via failed authentication rate anomalies and clustering. No UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect >N failed login attempts against Dashlane (or password-manager service principals) within T seconds from single or distributed source IPs. Correlate failure with successful authentication immediately following, indicating brute-force success.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Encrypted Vault Download - Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Encrypted Vaults of Fewer Than 20 Users Downloaded'—explicit exfiltration event. No collection or exfiltration phase in kill-chain output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Dashlane vault download/export patterns. Flag: single user session downloading multiple distinct vaults, downloads after authentication anomaly, or download size/count deviating from baseline user behavior.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Account Activity - Lateral Anomalies After Credential Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Brute-force success implies account takeover. Article implies attackers accessed vaults from compromised account context—no detection UC for post-breach suspicious access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect login from impossible travel scenario, non-standard user agent, or geographic clustering divergent from compromised user's baseline after brute-force event window.

suggestion.title: Credential Stuffing Campaign - Distributed Brute-Force with Known Breach Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Brute-force attacks at scale often involve credential stuffing from previous breaches. Article implies targeted attack on Dashlane user base, not random. No initial-access UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference failed login clusters against known-compromised credential feeds. Identify coordinated password-testing campaign: timing correlation across distributed sources, same password tested against multiple Dashlane user accounts.

suggestion.title: WinRAR CVE Exploitation Followed by Executable Extraction
suggestion.rationale: Article core narrative: 'Gamaredon Exploits WinRAR to Deliver'—no initial access detection generated. Should detect archive handling anomalies and process spawning from extracted files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WinRAR.exe spawning child processes immediately after extracting .exe or .scr files to temp/AppData/Startup locations. Cross-correlate with CVE-2023-38831 file signatures if available.

suggestion.title: GammaWorm Process Execution and File Staging
suggestion.rationale: Payload 'GammaWorm' explicitly named in article title but no execution signature, file hash, or behavioral detection created. This is a direct miss.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag execution of files matching 'GammaWorm' signatures or hashes. Look for parent processes related to archive extraction, suspicious registry/Run key modifications immediately after execution, and outbound C2 callbacks.

suggestion.title: GammaSteel Malware Persistence Registration
suggestion.rationale: Second payload 'GammaSteel' mentioned in title but zero detection coverage. Gamaredon historically establishes persistence; pipeline missed persistence-phase indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HKCU/HKLM CurrentVersion\\Run[Once] modifications by processes spawned from WinRAR extraction or matching GammaSteel behavioral signatures. Monitor startup folder writes in parallel.

suggestion.title: Gamaredon C2 Beaconing from Compromised Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Malware delivery implies persistent C2 comms. Article offers no network IOCs, but Gamaredon's known C2 infrastructure (if available in threat feeds) should trigger network-based detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound DNS and HTTP(S) from hosts with WinRAR extraction history or suspicious Startup directory modifications. Flag beaconing patterns and known Gamaredon C2 domains.

suggestion.title: Ukraine-Targeted Spear-Phishing with Archive Attachment
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies target 'Against Ukraine' and delivery mechanism is WinRAR archive—phishing delivery is implied. Pipeline did not surface email/attachment-based initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound emails to Ukrainian government/critical infrastructure domains with .rar or .zip attachments. Cross-reference extracted file hashes post-execution against GammaWorm/GammaSteel signatures.

suggestion.title: Archive with Suspicious Metadata or Obfuscated Payload Names
suggestion.rationale: WinRAR exploitation suggests archive-based delivery; pipeline missed defense-evasion patterns typical of Gamaredon (file name spoofing, double-extension, obfuscated paths).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect .rar or .zip archives containing files with double extensions (.doc.exe, .pdf.scr) or suspicious internal paths. Monitor WinRAR extraction to non-obvious directories and flag if extraction bypasses user-visible folder structure.

suggestion.title: Detect Active Exploitation of June 2026 Android Vulnerabilities
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'One Actively Exploited' — signals in-the-wild attack activity. Pipeline generated zero detection use cases despite explicit exploitation indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious capability-elevation requests (INSTALL_PACKAGES, CHANGE_NETWORK_STATE, WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS), unexpected process spawning from third-party app sandboxes, or network communications matching exploit-delivery patterns. Correlate timing with June 2026 patch release window.

suggestion.title: Identify Unpatched Android Devices Vulnerable to June 2026 Flaws
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Google June 2026 Android Update Patches 124 Flaws' — creates clear inventory/compliance detection opportunity. No patch-status or device-inventory use case in pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query MDM systems for Android devices with SecurityPatchLevel or BuildFingerprint older than June 2026 baseline. Flag non-compliance, automate enforcement of patch deployment, and track remediation time-to-patch metrics.

suggestion.title: Detect Privilege Escalation via Unpatched Android Components
suggestion.rationale: 124 flaws likely include escalation vectors; article does not exclude privilege escalation but pipeline generated no PE-phase detection. Common in Android vulnerability chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected system daemon spawning, /system partition access from user-space apps, SELinux denial patterns, or attempts to acquire elevated UIDs. Cross-reference suspicious process execution with known Android privilege-escalation CVE behaviors.

suggestion.title: Git Tag Rewrite Across Multiple Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Rewritten'—bulk tag modifications across multiple repositories is the core attack vector and anomalous supply chain pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk Git tag deletions and recreations across related package repositories within short timeframes. Flag tag rewrite operations affecting multiple packages from the same account/IP, especially with unusual commit author changes or GPG signature modifications.

suggestion.title: Malicious Code Injection in Package Release Tags
suggestion.rationale: Attack goal is to 'steal CI secrets via rewritten tags'—code must be modified to inject malicious payloads. Unexpected code changes in released packages are detectable before widespread deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare file hashes and code signatures of release tags against known-good versions. Alert on unexpected code additions in packages, especially credential-access patterns, environment variable reads, or outbound network calls in initialization code.

suggestion.title: Environment Variable and Credential Access from Deployed Packages
suggestion.rationale: Attack explicitly targets 'steal CI Secrets'—injected code must read and exfiltrate CI/CD credentials, creating observable patterns in build logs and API calls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor CI/CD logs for unexpected reads of secret environment variables from package code contexts, outbound HTTP/HTTPS calls from package initialization, or credential data being transmitted to external domains during builds.

suggestion.title: Repository Maintainer Account Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Successful rewrite of tags across multiple packages requires either compromised maintainer accounts or stolen repository signing keys—the prerequisite attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Git pushes from unrecognized IPs, geolocation anomalies for maintainer accounts, bulk tag operations from new sessions, or commits signed with previously-unseen GPG keys. Cross-correlate with account login events.

suggestion.title: Composer Package Manifest Alteration
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks commonly modify composer.json to inject dependencies or autoload directives. This ensures malicious code executes on package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected additions to composer.json autoload directives, new script entries, or dependency injections. Compare manifest diffs across tag boundaries and alert on installs of versions with altered autoload configurations.

suggestion.title: Scripted Bulk Repository Modifications Across Ecosystem
suggestion.rationale: Attack affected 'multiple Composer packages' in coordinated fashion. Automated tag manipulation across related repositories in rapid succession is a supply chain attack signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect patterns of tag creation/deletion across repositories in the same ecosystem/organization. Alert on API calls modifying multiple repositories in rapid sequence or tag operations with matching timestamps across unrelated package repositories.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to Plaintext Credential Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'acer_cgi.log file in the device firmware is accessible without authentication via the web interface. This file contains cleartext login credentials (for web and Telnet)' — credential_access vector via broken access control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP GET/POST requests to acer_cgi.log or similar credential repositories on port 80/443 without prior successful authentication. Flag any extraction of this file from non-management network segments.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Backup Decryption and Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article states upload.cgi 'contains a hardcoded AES encryption key' allowing attackers to 'decrypt, modify, and re-encrypt system backups, facilitating persistent backdoor injection' — persistence mechanism via known plaintext key.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated decryption/re-encryption operations on device backup files or upload.cgi binary. Detect modifications to backup archives followed by re-upload to device, indicating backdoor injection.

suggestion.title: Initial Access to Router Web Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies unauthenticated web access as the entry point: 'acer_cgi.log file...is accessible without authentication via the web interface.' Network exposure of management console is the initial attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to 192.168.76.1 or acerconnect.com from external/non-trusted network segments. Flag repeated failed login attempts followed by successful credential access pattern.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Cryptographic Key Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'hardcoded AES encryption key' in upload.cgi as the vulnerability root cause. Attackers with knowledge of this key can decrypt and modify backups without legitimate access credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for upload.cgi binary invocations with decryption operations or backup file access patterns. Detect multiple failed encryption/decryption attempts that succeed after few iterations (key-guessing behavior).

suggestion.title: Persistent Backdoor Injection via Firmware Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 're-encrypt system backups, facilitating persistent backdoor injection' — direct persistence mechanism through authenticated backup mechanism abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline firmware binary hashes (upload.cgi, core system binaries) at deployment. Alert on unauthorized hash changes or backup restoration operations outside of maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Credential Exfiltration Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Combination vulnerability: CVE-2026-49200 allows reading acer_cgi.log without auth, containing 'cleartext login credentials (for web and Telnet)'. Pattern indicates active credential harvesting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequential access to credential storage files (acer_cgi.log) followed by re-use of extracted credentials for Telnet or web login. Flag same source IP performing both log read and login within short timeframe.

suggestion.title: DLL Side-Loading via Game Executable and FFmpeg
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'Since the game needs ffmpeg.dll to run properly, the library loads as soon as the user starts the game' followed by ffmpeg.dll importing from natives2_blob.bin. This is the critical execution chain enabling malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DLL load chains originating from game executables where ffmpeg.dll or other legitimate multimedia DLLs load secondary DLLs with suspicious names (blob, temp, native patterns) or unsigned characteristics. Flag parent-child DLL import relationships between standard library names and anomalous DLL imports.

suggestion.title: COM Object Hijacking via InprocServer32 Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The malware uses COM hijacking to persist on the victim's machine, replacing the InprocServer32 entry for Windows Color System Calibration Loader DLL. This task is triggered when the user logs in.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKLM\SOFTWARE\Classes\CLSID registry paths for InprocServer32 value modifications, particularly those targeting system DLLs like Color System Calibration Loader (wcscaling.dll) being replaced with game directory paths or DLLs. Alert on modifications followed by startup process execution.

suggestion.title: Base64-Encoded PowerShell Script Execution from DLL Context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes natives2_blob.bin as 'a DLL that executes a Base64-encoded PowerShell script when loaded' performing 'basic checks for controlled environments.' This is Stage1 execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell execution with -EncodedCommand parameter where parent process is game-related or spawned by unsigned DLL. Correlate process chains: [game.exe → ffmpeg.dll/natives2_blob.bin → powershell.exe]. Decode and inspect Base64 payloads for reconnaissance commands (environment checks).

suggestion.title: Modified Legitimate DLL Distribution in Game Archives
suggestion.rationale: Article states archive contained 'fully functional, legitimate game files, as well as a modified FFmpeg DLL.' The trojanization of standard names (ffmpeg.dll) in game contexts bypasses basic reputation checks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag game installations where standard multimedia DLL names (ffmpeg.dll, etc.) have mismatched hashes against legitimate FFmpeg distributions or lack expected digital signatures. Monitor PixelDrain and torrent tracker downloads of game archives containing these mismatched DLLs.

suggestion.title: Trojan Downloader Second-Stage RAT Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates: 'After a few days, the implant downloads and executes a Trojan, resulting in full system compromise and broad remote control capabilities.' Stage1 checkpoint then triggers Stage2 RAT download.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network connections from processes launched by game executables or spawned PowerShell, especially with delays (days after initial execution). Detect executable downloads and subsequent spawning of child processes. Correlate with presence of natives2_blob.bin or COM hijacking registry events.

suggestion.title: Delayed Malware Activation After Initial Infection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'After a few days, the implant downloads and executes a Trojan.' Stage1 waits before triggering Stage2, evading time-based sandbox analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for game process execution and monitor for delayed secondary activities (days post-installation). Flag processes spawned from game installations with long temporal gaps. Correlate multi-day gaps between DLL side-loading events and subsequent RAT download/execution.

suggestion.title: Redis Exposed Port Access from Untrusted Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RCE flaw in Redis ('Autonomous AI Tool Finds 2-Year-Old RCE Flaw in Redis'); exploitation requires network access to Redis port. No detection generated for initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound connections to Redis default port 6379 from untrusted external IPs. Baseline internal Redis traffic; escalate on repeated failed connection attempts or access from known attacker IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Redis RCE Exploitation via Command Injection
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-23479 is explicitly an RCE; pipeline generated no execution-phase detections for malicious Redis commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Redis spawning shell processes or executing system commands. Monitor for EVAL, EVALSHA, or SCRIPT LOAD commands with embedded shell payloads; correlate with unexpected child process creation under redis-server.

suggestion.title: Post-RCE Data Exfiltration from Redis
suggestion.rationale: RCE flaws enable data extraction but pipeline generated no exfiltration detections despite HIGH severity rating.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large outbound transfers originating from compromised Redis instances. Alert on BGSAVE/RDB exports followed by exfil, or redis-cli bulk exports to external IP:port.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance for Unpatched Redis (CVE-2026-23479)
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions '2-Year-Old' flaw; implies scanning for vulnerable versions. Pipeline missed discovery-phase indicators for automated scanning tools.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect port scans for 6379 or Redis INFO command probes from single source IP across multiple targets. Flag baseline scans; correlate with subsequent exploitation attempts to same target set.

suggestion.title: Redis Persistence via Malicious Lua Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Post-RCE foothold requires persistence mechanism. Article describes RCE but pipeline generated no persistence-layer detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious Lua script injection into Redis (SCRIPT LOAD with obfuscated payload, FUNCTION LOAD with privileged operations). Alert on persistent script storage in appendonly.aof or cluster config changes.

suggestion.title: Network Reconnaissance via Passive Data Collection
suggestion.rationale: Title references 'See Your Network Like an Attacker'—classic reconnaissance posture. HD Moore historically emphasizes information gathering before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk DNS queries, WHOIS lookups, or ASN enumeration targeting internal domains or infrastructure. Flag systematic probing of internal IP ranges or service discovery (LDAP, NetBIOS broadcasts, mDNS queries) that precedes hands-on-keyboard access.

suggestion.title: Active Vulnerability Scanning Against Internal Network
suggestion.rationale: Webinar by Metasploit/Nessus founder implies scanning/enumeration methodology as core attack methodology.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-volume port scanning, fingerprinting probes (OS/service version enumeration), or timing patterns consistent with automated vulnerability scanners (e.g., Nessus, Metasploit scanner payloads) sourcing from endpoints inside the network perimeter.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Unpatched Services Identified in Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article title implies 'seeing network like attacker' includes identifying lateral movement vectors; HD Moore's tooling emphasizes service exploitation post-discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate discovery-phase reconnaissance (scanning, enumeration) with subsequent RDP, SMB, WinRM, or WMI connection attempts to hosts flagged in the same scanning window. Alert on service-to-service lateral pivots (e.g., database server to application server) using credentials obtained via earlier reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Evasion of Endpoint Detection via Process Blinding Techniques
suggestion.rationale: Title 'See Your Network Like an Attacker' implies defensive evasion; Moore's research includes bypassing EDR and detection mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for parent-child process anomalies (e.g., explorer.exe spawning rundll32.exe with suspicious arguments), non-standard process isolation techniques, or parent processes with mismatched timestamps. Flag Living-off-the-Land binaries (LOLBins) executing with encoded arguments or unusual source paths.

suggestion.title: Credential Extraction via Network Sniffing or Credential Dump Post-Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: HD Moore's classic attack flow includes credential theft as follow-on to network visibility; title implies understanding network topology enables credential interception.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution of credential dumping tools (mimikatz, procdump, gsecdump) or network-sniffing utilities post-discovery phase. Alert on LSASS access from unusual source processes or Memory.Raw file creation/access patterns.

suggestion.title: C2 Traffic from Compromised Internal Host Posing as Legitimate Service
suggestion.rationale: Attacker with network visibility can mask C2 in legitimate traffic; HD Moore's playbooks emphasize blending into network baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify DNS tunneling, DNS-over-HTTPS requests to non-standard resolvers, or HTTPS traffic to non-standard ports from endpoints identified in earlier reconnaissance phase. Flag long-duration connections with low byte transfer or unusual request-response ratios.

suggestion.title: Phishing with Localized Payroll/Tax/VAT Lures
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'uses localized phishing lures crafted to appear as payroll notices, tax audits, VAT filings, government compliance notices, invoices, and human resources communications' — foundational initial access step with high regional specificity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails impersonating government revenue/tax agencies (HMRC, Bundeszentralamt für Steuern), payroll processors, or HR platforms targeting European verticals. Correlate attachment detonation with network beaconing to TA4922 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Process Hollowing and Shellcode Injection via RomulusLoader
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'downloads and executes additional payloads using process hollowing, shellcode injection, and direct execution' — signature injection pattern for loader malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for suspiciously spawned host processes (explorer.exe, svchost.exe) with mismatched command lines or memory regions, or parent processes writing shellcode then transferring execution. Correlate with known legitimate tools (AnyDesk, SyncFuture) launched from unexpected parents.

suggestion.title: Anti-Sandbox Evasion Registry and Service Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies Atlas RAT performs 'anti-sandbox and anti-analysis checks, including looking for usernames and registry keys associated with Microsoft Defender Application Guard, the "CExecSvc" service, and OS UUID' — detectable evasion pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes querying HKLM:\SYSTEM registry for specific UUIDs, or enumerating services CExecSvc/Defender Guard DWORD values. TA4922 tooling exhibits this pattern as reconnaissance before deciding execution strategy.

suggestion.title: Chrome Credential and Cookie Extraction via SilentRunLoader
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'SilentRunLoader, which steals from Google Chrome credentials, cookies, and browsing data' deployed against UK/Southeast Asia — explicit credential-access objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file access to Chrome Local State, Login Data, and Cookies sqlite databases from non-browser processes. Flag Python process (SilentRunLoader is Python-based) spawning and immediately reading browser profiles; correlate with downstream exfil over C2.

suggestion.title: Alternate Channel Command-and-Control via WhatsApp/LINE/Teams
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'attempts to contact victims via WhatsApp, the LINE messenger, and Microsoft Teams' — non-email initial contact modality indicating persistence/C2 hybrid approach.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Teams/LINE/WhatsApp API traffic for unusual external contact patterns (high-volume from single org, file uploads, link-shortener domains). Correlate chat URLs containing payload hosting infrastructure. TA4922 uses these as side-channel delivery and persistence.

suggestion.title: Legitimate Remote-Access Tool Deployment (AnyDesk/SyncFuture)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'RomulusLoader was deployed to launch legitimate remote management tools such as AnyDesk and SyncFuture' — living-off-the-land execution strategy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected installation or execution of AnyDesk/SyncFuture from non-standard paths or spawned by loader processes. SyncFuture is rare in Western networks; any occurrence in Germany/Italy/UK is high-confidence. Pivot to network C2 beaconing.

suggestion.title: HTTP requests with anomalous CacheWarmer cookie values
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'crafted serialized PHP object in the CacheWarmer cookie' as the exploit vector. Pipeline missed this specific HTTP-layer indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Mirasvit-based applications for CacheWarmer cookie values that contain serialized PHP objects (magic byte indicators like 'O:' or 'a:'), exceed baseline length, or contain known gadget-chain signatures. Focus on unauthenticated requests.

suggestion.title: PHP deserialization patterns in web application logs
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is 'deserialization of untrusted data'; pipeline did not create detections for the deserialization process itself or its telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PHP warnings/errors related to unserialization (unserialize() errors, __wakeup/__destruct magic method invocation), particularly when triggered by HTTP request parameters or cookies. Cross-reference with Mirasvit CacheWarmer process names.

suggestion.title: Web server process spawning shell after HTTP request
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'remote code execution' results from the exploit. Pipeline did not define post-exploitation detection for process execution chains from web servers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for shell/command execution processes (cmd.exe, /bin/bash, etc.) spawned by web server processes (apache, nginx, php-fpm) with parent-child relationship anomalies or timing correlation to CacheWarmer cookie requests.

suggestion.title: Large or malformed cookie values in web server logs
suggestion.rationale: Serialized PHP objects are verbose; 'crafted' objects will deviate from baseline cookie metrics. Pipeline missed this behavioral anomaly hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for CacheWarmer cookie size and character distribution on target systems. Alert on cookies exceeding 2σ in length, containing non-alphanumeric sequences typical of serialized data, or appearing in requests from new/untrusted source IPs.

suggestion.title: Network requests to Mirasvit assets correlating with vulnerability exploitation window
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies this is being actively exploited in the wild (CISA KEV status). Pipeline did not create time-windowed threat-hunting use case linking patch-due date (2026-06-06) to scanning/exploitation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Between publication date (2026-06-03) and federal patch due (2026-06-06), heighten detection sensitivity for requests to Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer instances. Correlate inbound requests with outbound C2 or data-exfil traffic post-RCE execution.

suggestion.title: Android Privilege Escalation Exploit – CVE-2025-48595
suggestion.rationale: Article states integer overflow 'can be leveraged for increased privileges' and targets Android 14–16 with 'no user interaction' required. Requires detection of Android Framework privilege escalation attempts and exception/fault events indicative of integer overflow exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Android Framework for unexpected privilege escalation syscalls, integer overflow exceptions in native libraries, and elevation from unprivileged UIDs. Look for exploitation patterns correlated with June 2026 security patch levels (2026-06-01 and 2026-06-05).

suggestion.title: Container Escape via cgroup v1 Namespace Bypass – CVE-2022-0492
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'local attacker to bypass namespace isolation, escalate privileges, and potentially escape from a container to gain root-level access on the host system' via 'cgroup_release_agent_write() function.' Direct attack vector for container-to-host lateral movement.
log_sources: File System Audit (Linux auditd / cgroup events)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious writes to /sys/fs/cgroup/*/release_agent files, especially from processes inside containers or with child_tidaddr mismatches. Monitor for host-level process spawning with parent PID outside container namespace, correlate with absence of expected container orchestration events.

suggestion.title: Elevated Container Capability Abuse – CVE-2022-0492 Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article notes the flaw 'is especially dangerous when containers are granted elevated capabilities.' Indicates detection priority for containers running with CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_NET_ADMIN, or CAP_SYS_RESOURCE attempting cgroup manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on containers with elevated capabilities (e.g., CAP_SYS_ADMIN) performing cgroup-related syscalls or accessing /proc/sys/kernel/cgroup* files. Baseline normal cgroup access per workload and flag deviation.

suggestion.title: cgroup Release Agent Direct Manipulation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies root cause as insufficient authentication checks in 'cgroup_release_agent_write()' function. Direct indicator of exploitation is unauthorized writes to release_agent configuration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for open(O_WRONLY | O_CREAT) and write() syscalls targeting paths matching /cgroup/*/release_agent. Correlate with process UID != 0 or container context. Flag any successful writes; legitimate cgroup admin operations are infrequent.

suggestion.title: Active Exploitation Post-Breach: Privilege Escalation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article warns these flaws are 'under active targeted exploitation in the wild' with 'limited targeted exploitation.' Post-exploitation detection critical for catching in-flight attacks leveraging these known CVEs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Stack privilege escalation detection: monitor for successful UID 0 spawning from non-root parent, unrelated to sudo/polkit, within 60 seconds of integer overflow exceptions (Android) or cgroup syscall bursts (Linux). Correlate with unpatched kernel versions per KEV deadline (June 5).

suggestion.title: Jupyter Enterprise Gateway /api/kernels POST with KERNEL_UID/GID parameter values
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'specially crafted KERNEL_UID or KERNEL_GID value' — this is the exploitation vector. Detection must inspect parameter values (not just endpoint access). Should flag non-integer, negative, or unusually large values that bypass integer validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to */api/kernels endpoints. Extract KERNEL_UID and KERNEL_GID parameter values; flag if non-numeric, negative, contain special characters, or exceed expected range. Correlate with Enterprise Gateway application logs for validation errors or bypasses.

suggestion.title: Process namespace escape: unshare/pivot_root from Jupyter kernel process context
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1611 'Escape to Host' but provides no detection. Container escape to achieve root filesystem access requires namespace-exit syscalls. This is the privilege escalation anchor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unshare(), pivot_root(), setns() syscalls originating from Jupyter kernel processes (child of containerd-shim or runc). Baseline legitimate kernel startup syscalls; flag unexpected namespace transitions. Correlate with permission/capability check failures in auditd.

suggestion.title: Root-privileged kernel pod mounting hostPath volumes for persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article: kernel pod escapes to host. hostPath mounts + root privilege = direct host filesystem write. Detection should pair runAsUser=0 with hostPath volume presence in same pod spec.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query k8s audit logs for pod.create by enterprise-gateway service account where securityContext.runAsUser=0 AND volumes contain hostPath mounts. Alert on any pod combining root privilege + host filesystem access. Track mounted paths to detect write attempts to /etc, /var/spool/cron, /root.

suggestion.title: Enterprise Gateway application log: UID 0 acceptance by _enforce_prohibited_ids function
suggestion.rationale: Article: vulnerability is a bypass of _enforce_prohibited_ids. Most direct detection is application-level: log statements showing the check failing, raising exceptions, or unexpectedly allowing UID/GID=0.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse Jupyter Enterprise Gateway logs for exceptions or warnings from ContainerProcessProxy._enforce_prohibited_ids. Alert on any statement indicating UID 0 or GID 0 was accepted, check returned False, or validation was bypassed. Correlate with preceding /api/kernels POST to establish request-to-bypass sequence.

suggestion.title: Cron file creation by root-privileged container process on Kubernetes worker node
suggestion.rationale: Article: T1053.003 Scheduled Task/Job: Cron. Exploit outcome = attacker-controlled cron job persisting on host. Refined detection: root UID + container process parent = escaped and privileged.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cron file writes (/etc/cron*, /var/spool/cron/*) where initiating process runs as UID=0 AND has container runtime parent (runc, containerd-shim, crun). Verify process is running outside its intended namespace. Flag all such writes; baseline should be zero.

suggestion.title: Privilege boundary violation: non-root Enterprise Gateway SA spawning UID 0 kernel process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes _enforce_prohibited_ids as a protective boundary. Violation = service account with reduced privilege credentials somehow spawning root child process. Detect capability/privilege escalation within Enterprise Gateway itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track Enterprise Gateway pod/process effective UID; baseline should be non-root. Alert on attempts to set CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_NET_ADMIN, or other privilege-escalation capabilities. Monitor for child processes spawned by Enterprise Gateway with UID=0. Cross-check against allowlist of expected kernel processes.

suggestion.title: K8s service account token read and encoding by Enterprise Gateway Python process
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can 'steal the Kubernetes service account token' (T1552.005) but UC_3_3 detects token *reading* only. Missing: detection of base64 encoding, gzip compression, or outbound transmission of token content post-read.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Enterprise Gateway Python process reads /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token AND subsequently: spawns base64/openssl/gpg, writes to /tmp or /dev/shm with token content in environment variables, or makes outbound HTTPS/HTTP connections within 5 seconds of token read.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes API calls from Enterprise Gateway service account creating cluster-escalating resources
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RBAC escalation and privilege escalation (T1611, T1078.004) via pod creation post-exploitation, but no detection for the actual K8s API abuse. UC_3_2 looks at Change logs; this targets API call patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor K8s audit logs for create/patch operations on ClusterRoleBinding, RoleBinding, Pod (with hostPath/privileged), Secret, or ConfigMap initiated by enterprise-gateway service account. Escalate on: multiple different resource types in <5 min, or any operation touching API credentials.

suggestion.title: Network-layer SSTI payload detection to Jupyter Enterprise Gateway
suggestion.rationale: UC_3_1 joins HTTP logs with proxy logs but requires data already in Splunk. Article emphasizes POST to /api/kernels with malicious Jinja2; WAF/IDS should catch raw payloads before reaching application.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST to /api/kernels* OR /api/*/kernels* containing {{ followed by any of: __import__, __globals__, __class__, os.system, subprocess, eval, exec, popen, and closing }}. High confidence if KERNEL_* parameter name also present in same request.

suggestion.title: Enterprise Gateway process spawning kubectl or accessing container runtime from restricted context
suggestion.rationale: Article's T1611 (Escape to Host) implies container escape attempts. UC_3_3 detects shell spawning but misses direct container-runtime or kubectl invocations that precede host escape.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Enterprise Gateway Python process executes kubectl binary, accesses /var/run/docker.sock or /run/containerd/containerd.sock, or spawns containerd-shim/runc. These indicate intent to manipulate container runtime or invoke host-level operations.

suggestion.title: Jupyter Enterprise Gateway /api/kernels YAML Injection — Environment Variable Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'environment variables used during the rendering of the Kubernetes manifest allow YAML injection' and attacker can 'overwrite existing keys like securityContext and inject multi-document YAML.' Pipeline missed UC for detecting KERNEL_* variables containing YAML metacharacters (---, ..., securityContext, privileged, etc.) in POST body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for POST requests to /api/kernels containing environment variable names matching KERNEL_* pattern with values containing YAML document separators (---, ...) or securityContext keywords. High-fidelity indicator of active exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes Pod Creation with Injected securityContext — Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'enabling attackers to overwrite existing keys like securityContext' and inject 'runAsUser=0, fsGroup=0, privileged=true, hostNetwork=true.' Pipeline did not suggest UC for detecting securityContext mutations outside normal pod templates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor K8s audit logs for pod creation with securityContext.runAsUser=0 or securityContext.privileged=true or hostNetwork=true initiated by enterprise-gateway ServiceAccount. Alert on pods where securityContext contradicts known pod spec templates.

suggestion.title: Multi-Document YAML Injection in Kubernetes Manifest Rendering
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can 'inject multi-document YAML to create additional unintended Kubernetes resources.' Pipeline missed UC for detecting multiple YAML documents (---) rendered into single manifest or unexpected resource types spawned during pod creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for audit events where a single pod-creation request results in unexpected additional resources (ConfigMaps, Secrets, Services, DaemonSets). Correlate with POST timing to /api/kernels to detect YAML document injection completing successfully.

suggestion.title: launch_kubernetes.py Execution with /home/jovyan File Modifications
suggestion.rationale: Article's UC_2_1 explicitly hunts 'launch_kubernetes.py' binary and modifications to '/home/jovyan' directory. Pipeline failed to generate this process/file-based UC despite it being named in article.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of launch_kubernetes.py or file creation/modification events in /home/jovyan/. Particularly high-fidelity when paired with preceding /api/kernels POST request containing KERNEL_* YAML injection pattern.

suggestion.title: Enterprise Gateway ServiceAccount Privilege Escalation — Pod RBAC Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article describes injecting 'privileged: true, hostNetwork: true, hostPID: true' via YAML to bypass RBAC constraints. Pipeline missed UC for detecting RBAC-policy violations tied to EG service account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect pods created by enterprise-gateway service account where effective securityContext violates cluster's PodSecurityPolicy or NetworkPolicy. Flag when pod parameters (hostNetwork, hostPID, privileged) cannot be justified by pod spec template.

suggestion.title: Container Escape Precursor — Host Path Injection and CAP_SYS_ADMIN
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1611 'Escape to Host' as an outcome and YAML injection enables 'hostPath' volume mounting. Pipeline did not generate UC for detecting host-path volumes or privileged=true+CAP_SYS_ADMIN combinations that enable escape.
