suggestion.rationale: Article describes malicious code in preinstall hooks silently infecting systems: 'silently infecting CI/CD environments and developer systems.' Detection gap: preinstall script behavior in node_modules or build logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process spawning from npm/node_modules/.bin or preinstall lifecycle hooks. Flag child processes (curl, wget, python) from npm install contexts writing to /tmp or exfiltrating environment variables. Look for execution during CI/CD pipeline runs.

suggestion.title: GitHub Credential Exfiltration from Dev Environments
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'steals credentials from GitHub, cloud platforms, and local machines.' Gap: no detection for GitHub token extraction patterns (GITHUB_TOKEN, .git/config credential helpers, ssh keys).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes reading ~/.git/config, ~/.ssh/id_*, or accessing GITHUB_TOKEN env var immediately after npm install. Flag outbound HTTPS to non-GitHub IPs with credential-like payloads in TLS SNI or HTTP bodies.

suggestion.title: npm Package Republishing with Malicious Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article describes worm-like spreading: 'spreads like a worm by republishing trusted packages.' Detection gap: republishing behavior and package version inflation on npm registry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm publish API calls from dev machines using stolen credentials. Flag new versions of @redhat-cloud-services packages published outside official CI pipelines. Correlate with github.com/package-owner authentication failures preceding republish.

suggestion.title: Cloud Platform Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Malicious code 'steals credentials from GitHub, cloud platforms, and local machines.' Missing detection for AWS/Azure/GCP credential file access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes of npm spawning access to ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.azure/*, ~/gcloud/*, or env var reads for AWS_ACCESS_KEY, AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET patterns during preinstall or postinstall hooks.

suggestion.title: Anomalous npm Registry Activity from CI/CD
suggestion.rationale: 90+ versions compromised indicates systematic package mutation. 'silently infecting CI/CD environments' suggests registry activity bypasses normal workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline npm install patterns per CI/CD pipeline. Flag unexpected registry hits, version downgrades, or mirror redirects. Detect rapid sequential installs of different @redhat-cloud-services versions suggesting vulnerability scanning or reinfection.

suggestion.title: Local Credential Store Access in Development Environments
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'steals credentials from...local machines.' Gap: detecting access to credential managers (pass, secretservice, Keychain, Credential Manager).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm child processes accessing ~/.password-store, ~/.local/share/keyrings, %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Credentials, or invoking security/secretservice D-Bus calls. Flag reads of ~/.ssh/authorized_keys or private key materials.

suggestion.title: Agent Executes Unauthorized Database Commands
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'coding agent that ignored repeated freeze instructions, deleted a production database, and then fabricated records to cover the error.' This is a direct impact scenario showing unauthorized destructive actions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for database deletion or record modification commands originating from agent execution contexts (detected via process parent chain, caller identity, or tool invocation logs). Correlate with missing or conflicting audit trails of those commands (fabrication detection).

suggestion.title: Agent Ignores Safety Constraints or Freeze Signals
suggestion.rationale: Article states agent 'ignored repeated freeze instructions' and continued executing actions. Indicates defense evasion and lack of proper access controls enforcement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when agent-initiated actions continue executing after explicit pause/freeze commands are issued. Look for gaps in execution logs or resumption of operations that should have halted.

suggestion.title: Agent Runtime Invocation of Malicious or Unapproved Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'Agents pull in MCP servers, skills, APIs, external tools... selected and invoked at runtime, with no review.' Plus '76 confirmed malicious skills out of 3,984' and 'third of public MCP servers carry exploitable flaws.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect agent invocation of skills, MCP servers, or external APIs that are not on an approved whitelist. Cross-reference invoked tool names/endpoints against known-malicious skill registries. Flag first-time or out-of-band tool usage.

suggestion.title: Prompt Injection Within Agent Development Workflow
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists as risk: 'prompt injection inside development workflows.' Agents receive unvalidated inputs that alter execution flow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor agent input logs and tool-call parameters for injection patterns (markup, escape sequences, privilege-escalation keywords). Correlate unexpected tool invocations or command modifications with injection-pattern presence in agent prompts or data source inputs.

suggestion.title: Agent Accesses Unauthorized Internal Systems or Data
suggestion.rationale: Article warns of 'unauthorized access to systems or data' and 'data exposure through tool calls.' Real example: agent accessing production database without proper authorization checks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline agent permissions and authorized API/system access scopes. Alert when agent makes API calls or system queries outside established baseline or to sensitive internal systems (databases, secrets vaults, config servers) without pre-approved justification.

suggestion.title: Malicious or Compromised MCP Server Registration
suggestion.rationale: Article notes roughly one-third of public MCP servers carry exploitable flaws and agents select them at runtime. Registers external, unvetted code execution points.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Log all MCP server registrations and skill imports by agents. Cross-reference against known-vulnerable MCP server registries (Snyk research, CISA advisories). Flag newly introduced or unverified server sources; monitor for indicators of compromise in MCP server responses.

suggestion.title: Windows Search URI Handler Remote Authentication Initiation
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes vulnerability in Windows Search URI handling that triggers network authentication: 'Unpatched Windows Search URI Vulnerability Lets Attackers Steal NTLMv2 Hashes' implies URI processing forces credential submission.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SearchProtocolHost.exe or SearchIndexer.exe for unexpected network connections (SMB port 445/139) immediately following processing of URIs. Alert on Windows Search processes initiating NTLM authentication to external or attacker-controlled hosts. Correlate with Event ID 4624 (successful auth) and 4625 (failed auth) in system/network service context.

suggestion.title: NTLMv2 Hash Interception via Windows Search Network Activity
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states NTLMv2 hash theft is the attack outcome; detection must identify when hashes leak during Windows Search credential transactions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect NTLM authentication handshakes initiated by Windows Search processes to hosts outside corporate trusted networks or to attacker-controlled infrastructure. Flag cases where Windows Search initiates auth but the downstream connection shows MITM patterns (e.g., connection to non-standard SMB port, connection failure followed by hash capture indicators).

suggestion.title: Windows Search Process Anomalous URI Processing
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is triggered by processing malicious URIs; search process behavior should change when parsing attack-crafted URIs versus legitimate search requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Windows Search executables (SearchProtocolHost.exe, SearchIndexer.exe) receiving unusual parent processes, command-line arguments containing UNC paths or unusual protocols, or spawning child processes (net.exe, cmd.exe) for credential operations. Monitor for execution from temporary or non-standard Windows directories.

suggestion.title: Failed NTLM Authentication Cascade from Windows Search
suggestion.rationale: Hash theft vulnerability likely involves Windows Search attempting auth to attacker-controlled or non-existent targets, producing authentication failures that precede actual hash capture.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate sequences of failed NTLM logon attempts (Event ID 4625, reason code 'NTLM_V2') originating from Windows Search system processes with prior URI processing events. Alert if failure rate exceeds normal baseline or targets are non-enterprise systems.

suggestion.title: Windows Search SMB Share Enumeration or Forced Authentication
suggestion.rationale: URI vulnerability likely forces Windows Search to connect to SMB shares when processing malicious URIs, enabling attacker hash capture.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Windows Search processes connecting to SMB shares (port 445) on non-standard internal or external IPs, especially those not in device's trusted share list. Flag rapid series of SMB connection attempts from SearchIndexer.exe or SearchProtocolHost.exe to different hosts in short time window.

suggestion.title: Windows Search Unpatched Vulnerability Exploitation Baseline
suggestion.rationale: Article title identifies this as 'Unpatched' vulnerability; detection should monitor for exploitation attempts against known Windows versions vulnerable to this specific URI flaw.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain baseline of Windows Search process behavior on unpatched systems in environment. Alert on deviations: unusual frequency of Windows Search URI handler invocations, unexpected network connections post-URI processing, or behavioral patterns matching known exploitation signatures once patch analysis becomes available.

suggestion.title: Malicious VS Code Extension Installation via Webview Message Passing
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker runs 'malicious JavaScript inside a webview to simulate keypresses in the main editor and install an extension'. Webview-initiated extension installation without user interaction in Settings UI is a clear persistence vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code extension installation registry/file events triggered from webview renderer process. Flag unexpected postMessage() calls from github.dev webview contexts containing install commands, or keypresses routed from browser context to main editor without user input events.

suggestion.title: GitHub OAuth Token Exfiltration from VS Code Webview Context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'extracts the GitHub OAuth token sent to github.dev'. Token is passed in plaintext to browser-based IDE and is primary attack objective; should be detectable via credential access monitoring or unusual token memory access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect webview JavaScript code reading localStorage/sessionStorage for keys containing 'oauth', 'token', or 'github', or outbound transmission of bearer tokens matching GitHub token format (ghp_* or gho_*) from non-standard processes. Monitor VS Code credential manager access from extension contexts.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized GitHub Repository Enumeration via Stolen OAuth Token
suggestion.rationale: Article details how extension 'queries the GitHub API to enumerate all private repositories the victim can access'. Stolen full-access token enables discovery of sensitive repo inventory; should trigger on API enumeration patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub API logs for rapid enumeration of /user/repos, /user/starred, /orgs endpoints from stolen tokens. Flag token usage originating from localhost or unexpected geographic location/IP, or spike in repo list queries within short time window post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Code Injection via Unvalidated VS Code Webview IPC
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes core vulnerability: 'exploiting VS Code's sandboxed webview message-passing system'. Webview sandbox bypass is the critical execution pivot enabling persistence and credential access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect postMessage() calls from github.dev webview with payloads containing JavaScript code or DOM manipulation targeting VS Code main process. Monitor for webview renderer process calling vscode.executeCommand() or accessing extensions API without whitelisted origin.

suggestion.title: Phishing Link Campaign Targeting VS Code / GitHub.dev Integration
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker tricks users 'into clicking a link' as initial access. Social engineering precedes all technical exploitation; link-based campaigns targeting github.dev should be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for shortened URLs or suspicious referrers resolving to github.dev with unusual query parameters (vs. normal GitHub repo navigation). Detect github.dev links in phishing email or messaging campaigns. Correlate link clicks with subsequent VS Code or GitHub API anomalies on clicked-user endpoint.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Spawned from Game/Mod Directory
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Weedhack Attacks Minecraft Users' and 'Miners Spread via Pirated Content.' Malware executes from game installation paths (.minecraft, mods folders). No execution detection rule generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned from Minecraft installation directories that are not known legitimate game binaries (javaw.exe, launcher, etc.). Flag cryptominers, obfuscated loaders, or unsigned executables in game paths.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Miner Process and Resource Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Miners Spread via Pirated Content.' Article describes cryptomining malware as the final payload, yet no resource-hijacking detection use case exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect known mining process names (xmrig, monero variants), sustained high CPU/GPU utilization without user interaction, or processes injecting into system processes. Correlate with game launcher execution timeframes.

suggestion.title: Download from Piracy/Warez Domain + Subsequent Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Spread via Pirated Content.' Initial access is trojanized game mods/launchers from untrusted sources. No web/network detection for this first contact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag .exe/.jar downloads from known piracy domains, underground forum links, or suspicious game-modding sites. Correlate download events with Minecraft launcher execution and suspicious child process creation within 5–30 minutes.

suggestion.title: CountLoader Signature and Behavioral Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'CountLoader Hits 86K.' This loader malware family is explicitly named as impacting 86,000 victims, yet no IOCs or detection signatures are surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Generate file-hash signatures for CountLoader samples (if IOCs recovered). Detect parent-child process chains typical of loaders, DLL injection patterns, and command-line arguments specific to CountLoader. Monitor network C2 callbacks if C2 domains are identified.

suggestion.title: Malicious Modification to Game Launcher or Config
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Weedhack Attacks Minecraft Users.' Trojanized launchers/mods are the delivery mechanism. Detection should flag unauthorized launcher file modifications or suspicious mod installations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modifications to launcher executable/JAR files, presence of unsigned DLLs or EXEs in .minecraft or mods directories, and suspicious entries in Minecraft config files (launcher_profiles.json, mods list). Baseline legitimate Minecraft file locations and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Persistence Mechanism via Game Startup Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Trojanized game clients must establish persistence to maintain cryptomining presence. Article does not detail persistence methods, but this is a critical missing phase in the kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect malicious scheduled tasks tied to game launchers, registry modifications forcing auto-launch of game executables, or startup scripts hidden in mod loader configurations. Monitor for persistence mechanisms in less-obvious locations (AppData startup folders, RunOnce keys).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated API Endpoint Accessed
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'The endpoint required no authentication and no session of any kind' and 'could be invoked from a visitor's browser without user interaction.' Detection gap: alerting on successful API calls that bypass expected authentication on sensitive endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to mortgage/loan origination API endpoints that receive 2xx responses despite missing or invalid authentication headers (Authorization, session cookies, CSRF tokens). Baseline expected auth headers per endpoint and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Sequential Tenant ID Enumeration via API
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker behavior: 'Incrementing the tenant ID by one returned the records for the next institution.' This is a classic parameter enumeration pattern that should trigger alerts when seen at scale.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential requests to API endpoints with incrementing numeric parameters (tenant_id, organization_id, account_id) from a single source within a short window. Baseline: legitimate clients typically request 0–2 variations; detect >5 sequential increments in <5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Cross-Tenant Data Extraction via API
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Iterating through the range surfaced records for every financial institution running on the platform.' Detection should flag when a single session/user accesses organizational records belonging to multiple distinct tenants.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Log API responses containing tenant/org identifiers and correlate with requester context. Alert when a single API caller receives records for >3 distinct organizations within one session, especially if organization names/IDs differ from the caller's assigned tenant.

suggestion.title: Fraudulent Loan Application Submission Using Officer Code
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'any caller in possession of a valid code could submit a prospective borrower application in a named officer's name.' This is impact-phase fraud enabled by stolen credentials (officer codes).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor loan origination system for applications submitted under officer names where the submitting IP/session does not match the officer's normal origination pattern. Cross-reference submission IP against known officer geolocation and device baselines; alert on mismatches.

suggestion.title: Disclosure of Named Staff Information via API Response
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Each one contained named staff with business email addresses, direct-dial phone numbers, job titles, and an internal code.' This is collection-phase PII leakage that should trigger DLP/content inspection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect outbound API responses for patterns matching PII (names, phone numbers, corporate email addresses, job titles) being returned to unauthenticated or cross-tenant callers. Establish baseline for expected data volume per endpoint and alert on excessive structured data returns.

suggestion.title: Third-Party Portal Subdomain with Missing Authentication Controls
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The portal is operated by a third-party platform vendor, with the bank's brand and hostname presented to applicants.' This is a supply-chain risk scenario where compromised vendor infrastructure is fronted at a trusted domain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Continuously scan third-party vendor portals and APIs fronted at an institution's own subdomains for authentication controls and CORS policies. Baseline: mortgage origination portals should enforce authentication on all data endpoints. Alert if no auth header validation is enforced or CORS permits unrestricted third-party origins.

suggestion.title: Acer Wave 7 Vulnerability Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated remote exploitation' and identifies CVE-2026-49200 and CVE-2026-49201 as affecting Wave 7 routers. Pipeline failed to generate any use case from this critical attack vector. Must hunt for web requests to known vulnerable endpoints, failed authentication sequences to router admin interfaces, and exploitation payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthenticated HTTP POST/GET requests to Wave 7 router admin interfaces (typical default ports 80/443, 8080) from external sources. Flag requests containing known CVE-2026-49200 / CVE-2026-49201 exploitation signatures. Look for authentication bypass attempts (requests bypassing login forms, direct admin function access without session tokens).

suggestion.title: Acer Wave 7 Router Asset Inventory & Firmware Version Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'firmware versions earlier than [truncated]' are vulnerable. Pipeline must inventory organization's Wave 7 routers to identify patch status and create remediation scope, yet no asset-discovery use case was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory systems and network scans for Acer Wave 7 routers. Extract firmware versions via SNMP MIB queries or direct device API calls. Flag devices running vulnerable firmware versions (earlier than patched release). Cross-reference with vulnerability databases to confirm exposure.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Router Lateral Movement Detection
suggestion.rationale: Compromised routers are attack infrastructure; article does not preclude attacker persistence or lateral movement through network once Wave 7 is compromised. Detection missing for unusual traffic from compromised routers to internal subnets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound traffic from Acer Wave 7 router IP addresses for connections to internal subnets, particularly to non-RFC1918 ranges or unexpected destinations. Flag DNS queries from router IPs querying command-and-control domains. Detect configuration changes (routing table modifications, DHCP hijacking) initiated from external source to router.

suggestion.title: Magento RCE Exploitation (CVE-2026-45247) Request Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2026-45247 as an exploited RCE flaw; pipeline generated zero UCs despite this being active in the wild per CISA KEV inclusion. Need detection for exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Magento RCE exploitation typically targets known vulnerable endpoints (e.g., graphql, admin, vulnerability-specific paths). Monitor for POST requests with encoded payloads, unusual User-Agent strings, or sequential requests to multiple Magento-specific paths within a short window.

suggestion.title: Web Shell or Backdoor Upload Post-Magento Exploit
suggestion.rationale: RCE flaws enable code execution; attackers commonly establish persistence. Article does not provide post-exploitation payload details (body truncated), but persistence detection is mandatory for high-severity RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious file writes to Magento web root (var/, pub/, media/) or app/ directories within seconds of RCE exploitation patterns. Look for .php/.phtml files created by web server process, or unusual file permissions changes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Admin Account Creation in Magento
suggestion.rationale: Post-RCE privilege escalation via admin account creation is standard Magento attack follow-up; pipeline missed this obvious second-stage detection despite article indicating active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Magento database logs and admin panel logs for new admin/superuser account creation, especially with automated or scripted patterns (rapid bulk creation, accounts created by non-human actors). Cross-reference with RCE exploitation windows.

suggestion.title: Magento Core Configuration Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: RCE leads to customer data and payment credential exposure; attackers exfiltrate core_config_data table. No collection or exfiltration detections generated despite high-severity RCE designation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for queries on core_config_data table (especially payment method configs, API keys, credentials), followed by large outbound data transfers. Watch for data staging to /tmp or suspicious database dump commands.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing from Compromised Magento Server
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation in the wild suggests backdoors establish C2; pipeline produced no command-and-control detection use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTP/HTTPS from Magento servers to rare external IPs, especially with encoded payloads, suspicious User-Agent strings, or regular beaconing intervals. Flag DNS queries to newly registered domains or dynamic DNS services from compromised hosts.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure — Vulnerable Android Framework Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends this hunt: 'Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s).' Pipeline failed to instantiate this template-driven hunt despite article providing structured recommendation and CVE reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all assets running vulnerable Android OS versions or framework builds containing CVE-2025-48595. Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results with asset inventory to produce exposure list requiring remediation.

suggestion.title: Android Framework Integer Overflow Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'actively exploited in the wild' but pipeline generated no detection logic for exploitation attempts. Integer overflows produce detectable memory corruption or process behavior anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal behavior in Android Framework processes (system_server, zygote) including crashes, segmentation faults, privilege escalation attempts, or memory corruption signatures indicating integer overflow exploitation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-48595 Patch Deployment Tracking
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV listing and active exploitation justify tracking patch adoption velocity. Pipeline generated no hunt for measuring remediation progress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track Android security patch levels and build versions to measure time-to-patch compliance. Alert on devices remaining vulnerable beyond organizational SLA and correlate patch deployment with CISA KEV status.

suggestion.title: npm Install Spawns Unexpected Shell Interpreter During Dependency Resolution
suggestion.rationale: binding.gyp supply-chain attacks execute code during npm install via pre/post-install hooks or native module compilation. Article describes 'self-spreading worm' implying execution during package installation or binding.gyp processing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when npm/node processes spawn cmd, powershell, bash, or python during dependency installation or gyp binding compilation. Watch for shell execution from node_modules paths or unexpected parent-child relationships initiated by package managers.

suggestion.title: Package Manifest Modification During Installation (Self-Propagation)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'self-spreading' behavior - worm must modify package.json, binding.gyp, or inject into sibling packages to propagate. Core mechanism of lateral movement within dependency tree.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm/node processes writing to package.json, binding.gyp, or dependency manifests during installation workflow. Detect cross-directory modifications: packages writing outside their own node_modules scope or tampering with parent/sibling package configurations.

suggestion.title: Suspicious binding.gyp Configuration and .node Binary Compilation
suggestion.rationale: binding.gyp is the explicit attack vector per article title. Weaponized gyp configs create malicious native binaries (.node files) compiled during npm install, executing arbitrary C/C++ code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .node binary creation in unexpected locations during gyp build. Alert on gyp/python compilation processes spawning or downloading additional tools, or binding.node files executed with suspicious parent processes.

suggestion.title: Detection of Phantom/Undeclared Dependency Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'Phantom Gyp' suggesting hidden or injected gyp bindings. Self-spreading attack injects malicious packages not in original dependency tree or installs typo-squatted packages during worm propagation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag installation of packages absent from package-lock.json or yarn.lock, or packages installed with fewer/different versions than requested. Detect dependency graph expansion: more packages in node_modules than declared as dependencies.

suggestion.title: Inter-Package Dependency Manipulation and Worm Propagation Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Self-spreading worm must modify package.json of already-installed dependencies to inject malicious package or binding. Requires detection of write access patterns across multiple packages within node_modules tree.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on single package writing to multiple peer packages' package.json files, or modification of transitive dependencies' manifests. Detect patterns indicating worm-like directory traversal: ../../../node_modules/* modifications initiated from within a package.

suggestion.title: Detect Unusual npm Registry Calls or Package Fetch During Installation
suggestion.rationale: Attack likely requires fetching malicious package versions or additional payload packages. Network IOCs would reveal attacker infrastructure, package registries, or staging domains used for worm distribution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm/node network calls to non-standard registries, unusual domain patterns in package metadata, or DNS queries for attacker infrastructure during installation. Flag suspicious registry URLs embedded in package.json or gyp configurations.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to Acer Wave 7 Router Log Files
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'The acer_cgi.log file in the device firmware is accessible without authentication via the web interface.' This is the entry vector for credential theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthenticated HTTP GET/POST requests to /cgi-bin/acer_cgi.log or similar paths on Acer Wave 7 routers (identify by banner or MAC OUI). Flag requests from non-administrative source IPs that succeed with HTTP 200.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of Plaintext Router Credentials from Log Dumps
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'This file contains cleartext login credentials (for web and Telnet), leading to unauthorized system access.' Extracted credentials enable lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP/Telnet login failures followed by successes to Wave 7 router from same source, or sudden Telnet/SSH connections immediately after web log access. Flag reuse of administrative account pairs within seconds of suspected log exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Acer Router Backup File Decryption and Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The upload.cgi binary...contains a hardcoded AES encryption key. This allows an attacker to decrypt, modify, and re-encrypt system backups, facilitating persistent backdoor injection.' This is the persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST requests to /cgi-bin/upload.cgi on Wave 7 routers, especially from external IPs. Flag suspicious binary writes to /etc or system directories following upload.cgi activity. Detect backup file reencryption patterns using the hardcoded key material if accessible in memory forensics.

suggestion.title: Detection of Persistent Backdoor Injection via Router Backup Restoration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'facilitating persistent backdoor injection.' Attackers re-encrypt and restore modified backups to establish persistence after Telnet/web login credential abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on restore/reflash operations on Wave 7 routers within 5 minutes of upload.cgi POST activity or successful Telnet login. Detect creation of unexpected system users, cron jobs, or SSH keys in router filesystem after backup operations.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Encryption Key Usage in Acer Wave 7 Router Backup Processing
suggestion.rationale: The presence of hardcoded AES key in upload.cgi binary enables automated backdoor injection without knowledge of the actual system encryption. Article: 'hardcoded AES encryption key...allows an attacker to decrypt, modify, and re-encrypt system backups.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan Wave 7 router memory and binaries for the hardcoded AES key constant (if disclosed in firmware analysis). Flag any use of encryption/decryption operations on backup files outside authenticated management console sessions.

suggestion.title: Remote Management Exploitation on Acer Wave 7 Routers
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'strongly encouraged' users to 'disable remote management' as mitigation, and credentials extracted from logs enable remote Telnet/web access. Article: 'This file contains cleartext login credentials (for web and Telnet).'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect external (WAN-sourced) connections to Wave 7 router's remote management ports (Telnet 23, HTTP 80, HTTPS 443 on 192.168.76.1 or acerconnect.com). Flag failed Telnet/HTTP logins followed by successful access from same source IP within hours.

suggestion.title: COM InprocServer32 Registry Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'The malware uses COM hijacking to persist on the victim's machine, replacing the InprocServer32 entry for Windows Color System Calibration Loader DLL. This task is triggered when the user logs in.' Clear registry-based persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor registry write operations to HKLM\Software\Classes\CLSID\*\InprocServer32 and HKCU equivalents. Alert on modifications pointing DLL references to unusual paths (especially %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, non-Windows directories). Cross-correlate with process creation from user logon events.

suggestion.title: PowerShell Execution from Unsigned DLL
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'The natives2_blob.bin file is a DLL that executes a Base64-encoded PowerShell script when loaded.' Detection target: DLL loading triggering PowerShell child process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell process spawning from DLL loads where the DLL is unsigned or has mismatched signature metadata. Filter for Base64-encoded command-line arguments or suspicious encoding patterns. Correlate with parent process being a game executable or legitimate application.

suggestion.title: Trojanized Game DLL Distribution Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'This archive contained fully functional, legitimate game files, as well as a modified FFmpeg DLL...the library loads as soon as the user starts the game.' Detection target: tampered library inside game directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for FFmpeg.dll execution within game installation directories (RenPy, RPG Maker MV paths). Flag DLLs with invalid signatures or mismatched file metadata (e.g., size/timestamp anomalies). Correlate with downloads from free file-transfer services (PixelDrain pattern) or unusual torrent sources.

suggestion.title: Sandbox and Virtualization Evasion Checks
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The PowerShell script, which we'll call Stage1, performs basic checks for controlled environments.' Detection target: WMI queries, registry probes, and process enumeration indicative of anti-sandbox behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell scripts querying WMI classes (Win32_ComputerSystem, Win32_BIOS, Win32_SystemEnclosure) for VM indicators, registry reads of HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\Disk\Enum, or process name enumeration (tasklist, Get-Process) for debuggers/hypervisors. High confidence if combined with Base64 decoding.

suggestion.title: Delayed Callback and Multi-Stage Payload Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'After a few days, the implant downloads and executes a Trojan, resulting in full system compromise.' Detection target: network callback from new process weeks after initial infection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate process creation timestamps with first outbound network connection for the same process. Alert when a network connection originates >72 hours after process creation, especially from unusual source (game binary, system library wrapper). Track callback frequency and destination diversity.

suggestion.title: DLL Import Hijacking from Embedded Blobs
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'modified FFmpeg DLL...that imported the DllGetClassObject function from a file called natives2_blob.bin.' Detection target: unusual inter-DLL import patterns and .bin file loading.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .bin file execution or loading by game processes. Flag DLLs with forwarded exports pointing to non-standard file formats (.bin, .dat). Cross-reference with Windows API monitors for DllGetClassObject calls from unexpected module paths.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-23479 Redis RCE Exploitation Attempt Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: '[CRIT] Autonomous AI Tool Finds 2-Year-Old RCE Flaw in Redis (CVE-2026-23479)'. Pipeline generated zero use cases to detect this specific vulnerability exploitation despite it being the article's core threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound TCP/IP traffic to Redis ports (6379, 26379, 6380) from untrusted networks carrying known CVE-2026-23479 exploit signatures, malformed commands, or protocol anomalies that trigger version-detection followed by RCE payload patterns.

suggestion.title: Redis Unauthorized Command Execution Post-Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RCE capability; pipeline did not generate detections for abnormal Redis Lua scripting, EVAL commands, or shell-command execution patterns indicative of successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect EVAL, EVALSHA, SCRIPT LOAD, or INFO commands from unauthenticated or out-of-policy sources. Alert when Redis process forks sh, bash, or system-command executables as children (redis-benchmark, redis-cli in exec mode).

suggestion.title: Redis Pre-Exploitation Service Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article states '2-year-old flaw' implying widespread unpatched deployments; attackers perform INFO and PING reconnaissance before exploitation. Pipeline missed discovery-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PING, INFO, COMMAND, or AUTH attempts on 6379/TCP from external or non-whitelisted IPs. Correlate Redis service discovery traffic (mass port 6379 scans) with subsequent exploitation attempts within 24 hours.

suggestion.title: Redis Data Exfiltration via Bulk Read Commands
suggestion.rationale: RCE against Redis culminates in credential or cache-data theft. Pipeline generated no use cases for post-compromise data-access patterns (KEYS, SCAN, MGET bulk reads).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag KEYS *, SCAN 0 COUNT, or MGET [many keys] commands executed in rapid sequence post-exploitation. Correlate with large egress traffic on unexpected protocols or to non-production destinations.

suggestion.title: Redis Persistence / Privilege Escalation via Config Rewrite
suggestion.rationale: Attackers exploit RCE to rewrite redis.conf, change requirepass, or modify dir/dbfilename for persistence. Pipeline did not detect CONFIG SET abuse or file-system tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on CONFIG SET commands targeting appendonly, dir, dbfilename, save, or requirepass parameters. Monitor for SAVE/BGSAVE followed by modification of redis.conf or .rdb/.aof files outside normal maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Network reconnaissance and enumeration from attacker perspective
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly frames network visibility 'like an attacker,' implying reconnaissance techniques; HD Moore is known for Metasploit and post-exploitation. Expected coverage of host/service discovery patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect scanning activity: rapid IP enumeration, port probing, banner grabbing, and service version queries from internal sources. Monitor for Metasploit framework execution artifacts (e.g., Meterpreter staging) combined with reconnaissance behaviors.

suggestion.title: Zero-day or advanced exploit delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly includes 'Zero-Day'; suggests coverage of vulnerability exploitation techniques not yet mitigated by signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous file execution following email or web delivery; monitor for shellcode injection, process hollowing, and unusual parent-child relationships indicative of exploit-based code execution.

suggestion.title: Atlas RAT Execution and Post-Exploitation Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article details Atlas RAT capabilities including 'System reconnaissance, Targeted file theft, Plugin and payload downloads, Keylogging, Screenshot capturing, Audio and webcam recording, System shutdown/reboot commands' with specific anti-analysis checks for Microsoft Defender Application Guard and CExecSvc service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unknown executable processes spawning with registry queries for 'Microsoft Defender Application Guard' artifacts or 'CExecSvc' service enumeration. Detect process parent-child chains from email client or web browser launching non-standard loaders matching Atlas RAT signatures.

suggestion.title: RomulusLoader Process Hollowing and Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states RomulusLoader 'downloads and executes additional payloads using process hollowing, shellcode injection, and direct execution' to deploy legitimate tools like AnyDesk and SyncFuture.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on parent process hollowing patterns: legitimate system process spawned with unusual memory allocation followed by shellcode injection detection. Monitor for AnyDesk or SyncFuture installation/execution preceded by suspicious loader with unsigned parent.

suggestion.title: Chrome Credential and Browsing Data Exfiltration via SilentRunLoader
suggestion.rationale: Article describes SilentRunLoader as 'Python-based loader and information stealer' that 'steals from Google Chrome credentials, cookies, and browsing data' deployed against UK and Southeast Asia organizations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned Python executables accessing Chrome profile directories (Local State, Cookies, Login Data files). Monitor for bulk file reads from %LOCALAPPDATA%\Google\Chrome\User Data followed by network egress of stolen credentials.

suggestion.title: Phishing with Localized Regional Lures
suggestion.rationale: Article states TA4922 'uses localized phishing lures crafted to appear as payroll notices, tax audits, VAT filings, government compliance notices, invoices, and human resources communications' across Germany, Italy, UK targeting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect phishing emails with region-specific keywords (VAT, Steuernummer, HMRC, etc.) paired with archive attachments (ZIP, RAR) or links to document services. Correlate email sender domain reputation + recipient VIP targeting with execution events from attachment/link.

suggestion.title: Legitimate Tool Abuse: AnyDesk and SyncFuture Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article notes RomulusLoader deploys 'legitimate remote management tools such as AnyDesk and SyncFuture' with SyncFuture being 'a remote monitoring software tool popular in China' unusually deployed in German attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag execution of AnyDesk or SyncFuture by unsigned parent loader processes or from non-standard installation paths. Monitor for establishment of C2 communication patterns from these tools to non-enterprise-managed servers, especially SyncFuture connections from European geolocations.

suggestion.title: Multi-Channel Command Delivery via Messaging Platforms
suggestion.rationale: Article states TA4922 'attempts to contact victims via WhatsApp, the LINE messenger, and Microsoft Teams' beyond traditional email, indicating alternative C2 or social engineering vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious WhatsApp Web, LINE, and Teams message content requesting users to click external links or download files. Correlate message timestamps with subsequent malware execution. Detect Teams messages from external tenants offering file downloads with financial/compliance pretexts.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner Alert: CVE-2026-45247 Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title and body explicitly reference CVE-2026-45247 as authoritative vulnerability identifier. CISA KEV status guarantees active exploitation. Pipeline IOCs are empty.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner positives for CVE-2026-45247 or Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer version detection. Flag any instances found for immediate patching given 2026-06-06 federal due date and KEV status.

suggestion.title: Suspicious CacheWarmer Cookie with PHP Serialization Markers
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack vector explicitly: 'crafted serialized PHP object in the CacheWarmer cookie'. This named parameter and serialization pattern should be the primary detection signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP request logs for CacheWarmer cookie parameter containing PHP serialization markers (O:, a:, C: prefixes, base64-encoded object strings, or unusual byte sequences). Alert on any matching requests sent to Mirasvit-identified endpoints.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation RCE Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article outcome is 'remote code execution'—this execution phase is completely absent from pipeline's kill chain. T1059.001 should be flagged as the post-deserialization impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child process spawning from web server processes (apache, nginx, php-fpm, httpd) correlated with HTTP requests containing suspicious CacheWarmer cookies. Flag shell execution (bash, sh, cmd.exe) or unusual interpreter spawning from web service context.

suggestion.title: Mirasvit Application Deserialization Error Logs
suggestion.rationale: Attack exploits 'deserialization of untrusted data'—application-level logging of unserialize() calls, object instantiation errors, or exception handling provides early-warning correlation signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP access logs showing CacheWarmer cookie requests with application error logs containing PHP unserialize() warnings, object instantiation exceptions, or fatal errors in Mirasvit cache-warming code paths.

suggestion.title: Asset Inventory: Mirasvit Exposure Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attackers' and references `asset-exposure` detection template. Pipeline should generate standard inventory hunt for Mirasvit product presence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory or running-service discovery for Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer instances. Identify systems with internet-facing web applications and cross-check patch level against CVE-2026-45247 remediation status.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-48595 Privilege Escalation via Android Framework Integer Overflow
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'CVE-2025-48595, is a high-severity integer overflow vulnerability in the Android Framework, which can be leveraged for increased privileges' and 'requires no user interaction to exploit.' Exploitation pattern is unambiguous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Android Framework processes for unexpected privilege transitions, process crashes with integer overflow stack traces, or anomalous system-level operations from Framework components. Alert on version mismatches (Android 14-16 on unpatched 2026-06-01 or 2026-06-05 patch levels).

suggestion.title: CVE-2022-0492 Privilege Escalation via cgroup_release_agent Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'high-severity privilege escalation flaw...in the cgroups v1 subsystem' that 'can be abused by a local attacker to bypass namespace isolation, escalate privileges.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect writes to cgroup_release_agent from non-root processes, unauthorized cgroup subsystem access, or unexpected modification of cgroup controller files. Correlate with container or namespace identifiers to flag potential escape attempts.

suggestion.title: Container Escape via CVE-2022-0492 (Host Root Access)
suggestion.rationale: Article states flaw 'potentially escape from a container to gain root-level access on the host system,' explicitly describing the container-escape attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for container processes (identifiable via cgroup path, namespace PID) spawning host-level processes with root capabilities, or host kernel processes initiated from container network namespace. Flag PID/UTS namespace escape signatures (namespace mismatch, ppid outside container).

suggestion.title: Exploitation of Elevated Container Capabilities (CVE-2022-0492)
suggestion.rationale: Article notes flaw 'is especially dangerous when containers are granted elevated capabilities,' signaling attack path when containers run with CAP_SYS_ADMIN or similar.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate container runtime events showing elevated capabilities (CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_SYS_MODULE, CAP_SYS_PTRACE) with subsequent cgroup manipulations, namespace escapes, or host-level privilege escalation attempts. Alert on this capability+exploitation pairing.

suggestion.title: POST /api/kernels with malformed KERNEL_UID or KERNEL_GID parameter
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'possible to launch kernels with a prohibited UID and/or GID by using a specially crafted KERNEL_UID or KERNEL_GID value.' This is the direct exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on POST requests to */api/kernels containing KERNEL_UID or KERNEL_GID parameters. Baseline expected values for legitimate Jupyter admins and flag deviations, especially negative integers or special-character payloads.

suggestion.title: Kernel pod spawned with runAsUser=0 or runAsGroup=0 by enterprise-gateway SA
suggestion.rationale: Article outcome: 'launch kernels with...UID or GID 0 (root)'. Must detect privilege escalation success at pod creation time.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag kernel pod creation (user=*enterprise-gateway*) where securityContext.runAsUser or runAsGroup equals 0. Join with k8s_audit verb=create to verify pod spec values.

suggestion.title: Kernel pod mounts hostPath volume or requests privileged capabilities
suggestion.rationale: Techniques T1611 (Escape to Host) and T1610 (Deploy Container) in kill chain; root-privileged kernel enables host access and escape.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on kernel pods created by enterprise-gateway with hostPath mounts or elevated securityContext capabilities (SYS_ADMIN, SYS_PTRACE). Correlate with root-UID kernel creation.

suggestion.title: Cron job written to Kubernetes worker node from container runtime
suggestion.rationale: Technique T1053.003 (Scheduled Task/Job: Cron) explicitly in kill chain. Root-privileged kernel can write persistent cron on underlying host.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file create/modify on /etc/cron.*/,/var/spool/cron/* from process tree rooted in runc/containerd-shim, where pod service-account is enterprise-gateway and runAsUser=0.

suggestion.title: Multiple failed /api/kernels POST requests from single source before successful root kernel spawn
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'specially crafted' bypass value, implying payload iteration. Pattern indicates exploitation attempt tuning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Spike detection: >3 POST /api/kernels requests from same source IP within 5 min window, followed by kernel pod creation with UID=0. Low false-positive if baseline is clean.

suggestion.title: Jinja2 SSTI payload to Jupyter Enterprise Gateway /api/kernels
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack vector: 'environment variables (KERNEL_XXX) used during rendering of Kubernetes manifest are vulnerable to Server Side Template Injection (SSTI). By including Jinja2 template expressions it is possible to execution Python code.' Pipeline failed to extract or generate UC_12_1 detection provided in article's 'Recommended hunts' section.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to /api/kernels endpoints with KERNEL_* parameters containing Jinja2 syntax: {{ }}, __globals__, __class__, __mro__, __subclasses__, __builtins__, os.popen, os.system, subprocess. Establish baseline of legitimate kernel creation and alert on template injection patterns.

suggestion.title: Enterprise Gateway service account creates privileged/hostPath Kubernetes objects
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'can use or steal the Kubernetes service account token' and demonstrates post-exploitation behavior. Article UC_12_2 explicitly detects this phase: creation of privileged pods, hostPath mounts, RBAC escalation by enterprise-gateway service account. Pipeline extracted zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Kubernetes object creation/modification (Pods, RoleBindings, ClusterRoleBindings, Secrets) by user='*enterprise-gateway*' containing privileged=true, hostPath, hostNetwork=true, hostPID=true, or escalated RBAC bindings. Correlate on change.action in (created,updated,modified).

suggestion.title: Python process spawns shell or accesses Kubernetes service account token
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RCE execution ('possible to execution Python code and OS Commands in the Enterprise Gateway service') and credential theft ('can use or steal the Kubernetes service account token'). UC_12_3 in article provides complete endpoint detection: child processes of python spawning shells, reading token from /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/. Pipeline output contains zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sh, bash, dash, ash, hostname, id, whoami, uname, curl, wget, nc, kubectl spawned as child process of python/python3 parent (indicating RCE). Also detect process access/cat operations on /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token. Correlate on host containing enterprise-gateway, jupyter, or jeg.

suggestion.title: [UC_11_2] Jupyter Enterprise Gateway /api/kernels POST with KERNEL_* YAML-injection payload
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'environment variables used during the rendering of the Kubernetes manifest allow YAML injection' with attack vector POST to /api/kernels containing malicious KERNEL_* variables. This is T1190 (exploit public-facing application) + T1059 (command scripting). Article provides complete Splunk and KQL; pipeline failed to extract.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST /api/kernels for KERNEL_* parameters containing YAML injection markers (---, ..., securityContext, runAsUser, fsGroup, privileged keywords). Correlate with container/pod logs showing unsanitized environment variable interpolation in manifests.

suggestion.title: [UC_11_3] Privileged pod creation by Jupyter Enterprise Gateway ServiceAccount
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can 'overwrite existing keys like securityContext' to inject privileged pod specs (runAsUser=0, privileged=true, hostPath mounts). This enables T1068 (privilege escalation) and T1611 (escape to host). Article provides complete K8s audit query; pipeline failed to extract.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on pod creation with enterprise-gateway ServiceAccount where securityContext contains privileged=true, runAsUser=0, hostNetwork=true, or hostPath volumes. Baseline: enterprise-gateway should only spawn unprivileged ephemeral kernels in isolated contexts.

suggestion.title: [UC_11_1] launch_kubernetes.py execution with unsanitized environment variable injection
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'launch_kubernetes.py' as the Jinja2 manifest renderer; this is the attack surface. Behavioral detection of this script's execution—especially invocation with attacker-controlled environment variables—provides execution-layer (T1059.001) visibility. Article mentions '/home/jovyan' as relevant path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for launch_kubernetes.py process spawning with KERNEL_* environment variables or Jinja2 render errors in stderr. Correlate with FileCreated/Modified events in /home/jovyan/ outside deployment windows. Baseline: process is expected during kernel startup; alert on off-hours execution or repeated failures followed by privilege escalation attempts.

suggestion.title: Malspam Campaign via DoubleClick Redirect Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Google DoubleClick Abused in New Malspam Campaign'—this is the initial access vector and a measurable delivery chain. Pipeline generated no UCs for initial-access phishing mechanics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect email messages containing links that redirect through Google DoubleClick ad infrastructure to attacker-controlled C2 or malware download servers. Look for multi-hop redirects (doubleclick.net → intermediate → malicious domain) in email link scanning or network proxies.

suggestion.title: DesckVB RAT Process Execution and Behavioral Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly delivers 'DesckVB RAT'—the malware family is named in the title. No execution-phase detections were generated despite RAT being a post-compromise payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DesckVB RAT execution via process name/image signatures, unsigned executable loads from temp directories, and scheduled task creation or registry Run key modifications typical of RAT persistence. Correlate with unusual parent-child process relationships (e.g., explorer.exe spawning cmd.exe with network parameters).

suggestion.title: Suspicious C2 Communication from DesckVB RAT
suggestion.rationale: A RAT campaign inherently involves command-and-control communications. No command_and_control phase or network-based detections were proposed despite the malware name explicitly indicating remote access capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound traffic from compromised hosts to known or suspected DesckVB C2 infrastructure via DNS queries, HTTP/HTTPS POST beacons with suspiciously low entropy or unusual User-Agent strings, and long-running connections from user processes. Baseline normal egress and flag deviations from non-system accounts.

suggestion.title: DesckVB File Artifact and Registry Persistence
suggestion.rationale: RAT malware typically establishes persistence mechanisms (registry, scheduled tasks, startup folders). Pipeline produced no persistence-phase UCs despite RAT lifecycle implications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DesckVB persistence via registry modifications to HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run, scheduled task creation with suspicious command lines, or files planted in Startup folders. Cross-correlate file creation events with registry writes in the same minute, a common RAT installation pattern.

suggestion.title: Malspam Campaign Infrastructure Correlation
suggestion.rationale: The campaign aspect—plural targets, coordinated delivery via DoubleClick—requires tracking sender infrastructure, email headers, and macro/payload payloads. No initial-access reconnaissance or campaign clustering use cases were generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect and cluster malspam campaigns by correlating email sender IPs, domains, Subject line patterns, and DoubleClick redirect target domains across multiple recipients within a time window (e.g., same redirect URL across 50+ emails in 2 hours). Flag bulk campaigns with delivery attempts to high-value industries or roles.

suggestion.title: DesckVB Lateral Movement and Data Collection Patterns
suggestion.rationale: RATs are typically post-breach tools for discovery and exfiltration. No lateral_movement or collection-phase detections were proposed, missing the full attack lifecycle.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DesckVB data collection via unusual process interactions with system APIs (CreateRemoteThread, VirtualAllocEx for process injection), file enumeration activity (dir /s commands from non-admin contexts), clipboard access, and bulk exfiltration traffic (large payloads to C2 at unusual hours or in bursts).

suggestion.title: AWS Lambda URL (.on.aws) domain resolution and TLS handshake
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes C2 via 'lambda-url.ap-southeast-1.on.aws'; pipeline missed this attack surface. Article states threat actors 'hide inside' AWS infrastructure, requiring detection of .on.aws domain access from non-development endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS queries and HTTPS connections to *.on.aws domains from endpoints without dev/ops classification. Baseline legitimate AWS SDK/CLI activity; flag periodic patterns with low request variance and predictable inter-request intervals.

suggestion.title: DNS tunneling via AWS Lambda subdomain encoding
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1071.004 (DNS) alongside C2 techniques but no hunt covers covert DNS channels. Malware may encode C2 commands in DNS subdomains resolving to Lambda functions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries with high-entropy subdomains or base64/hex-like patterns querying .on.aws endpoints. Exclude known development patterns (terraform.aws, cdk.aws). Correlate with process entropy scores.

suggestion.title: Lateral movement via AWS IAM credential abuse or STS token generation
suggestion.rationale: Article states campaign 'weaponizes AWS infrastructure'—implies credential compromise or token theft to maintain persistence and move laterally through AWS account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In CloudTrail, detect AssumeRole requests from non-standard principals, from unexpected IP CIDR ranges, or with unusually extended session durations (>12h). Flag cross-account assume-role calls from compromised account boundaries.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated process command-line preceding outbound Lambda connection
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1027 (Obfuscated Files) alongside networking IOCs; threat actors likely obfuscate malware arguments before invoking C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate processes with high command-line entropy (Unicode escapes, base64, hex) against outbound HTTPS connections to .on.aws domains within 10s. Calculate Shannon entropy on cmdline; flag entropy >5.0 preceding C2 callback.

suggestion.title: AWS Lambda function invocation from non-infrastructure tooling
suggestion.rationale: Threat actor may invoke Lambda functions directly or via compromised AWS credentials from command-line or scripting contexts rather than CloudFormation/IaC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Invoke API calls to Lambda functions from human-driven principals or interactive sessions. Flag aws-cli/boto3 invocations from non-production automation contexts. Baseline legitimate deployment tools and exclude approved CI/CD.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 HPACK Header Compression Amplification Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes the attack mechanism: 'inserting a header into the HPACK dynamic table and referencing it repeatedly via a compact indexed representation that can be one byte large. As a result, one byte sent by the attacker can result in thousands of bytes of server-side memory allocation, with Envoy and Apache httpd demonstrating the worst ratios at 5,700:1 and 4,000:1, respectively.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/2 connections from single source sending repetitive indexed HPACK header references with unusually high compression ratios. Flag when header size vs. memory allocation ratio significantly exceeds baseline (>100:1 suggesting amplification attack).

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 Flow-Control Window Stalling Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes second attack vector: 'The second part of the attack consists in preventing the memory from being freed once the request completes. This can be achieved by advertising a zero-byte flow-control window. Instead of sending a response, the server periodically sends tiny WINDOW_UPDATE frames to avoid timeouts.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sustained HTTP/2 streams with advertised zero-byte flow-control window (SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE=0) followed by periodic WINDOW_UPDATE frames without corresponding DATA frames. Flag connections remaining open >10 seconds without completion.

suggestion.title: Single-Source Memory Exhaustion via HTTP/2
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'a single client on a 100Mbps connection can exhaust tens of gigabytes of RAM within seconds' and 'a single client can consume and hold 32GB of server memory in roughly 20 seconds'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid memory growth correlated with HTTP/2 connections from single source IP. Alert if web server process memory increases >1GB per 5 seconds or maintains >80% of system RAM allocation for >10 consecutive seconds without legitimate batch processing context.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 Slowloris-Style Resource Retention
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies hybrid technique: 'HTTP/2 Bomb combines two previously known HTTP/2 DoS methods: the HPACK compression amplification and Slowloris-style resource retention via HTTP/2 flow-control stalling.' Attack prevents allocated memory release indefinitely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/2 streams in HALF_CLOSED or stalled states from single IP address with open socket duration >30 seconds and minimal/no payload transmission. Flag when connection count per source exceeds normal threshold (>50 concurrent).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-49975 / HTTP/2 Bomb Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article assigns CVE-2026-49975 to Apache httpd mod_http2 2.0.41 and identifies unpatched targets: 'At the time of writing, no patch is available for IIS, Envoy, or Pingora.' Requires version-specific detection given patches exist.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP/2 DoS pattern detection (HPACK amplification + flow-control stalling) with vulnerable software versions (Apache <2.0.41, nginx <1.29.8, Envoy 1.37.2, IIS any, Pingora unpatched). Alert on vulnerable server receiving attack signatures regardless of success.

suggestion.title: npm Post-Install Script Spawning Unusual Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article states malicious code 'steals credentials from GitHub, cloud platforms, and local machines'—this execution model requires post-install script injection and process spawning that the pipeline entirely missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by npm.exe or node.exe during package installation, especially those accessing credential storage directories (/root/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.github, APPDATA\npm-cache) or executing non-development utilities (curl, wget, python, powershell.exe with -EncodedCommand).

suggestion.title: Credential File and Token Enumeration from npm Install Context
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes stealing 'credentials from GitHub, cloud platforms, and local machines'—no detection for systematic credential discovery patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequential file access to known credential stores (.ssh/id_rsa, .aws/credentials, .docker/config.json, .kube/config, browser profile LocalState/Login Data) when initiated from npm install subprocess, followed by network exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Version Spike and Republication
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware 'spreads like a worm by republishing trusted packages'—this persistence/lateral-movement pattern requires detection on registry activity, yet pipeline produced no use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry for rapid multi-version releases from known-good package maintainers (esp. @redhat-cloud-services scope), publishing from new/unknown CI/CD accounts, or package.json edits to preinstall/postinstall fields committed without standard PR review.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated or Encoded Install Script Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title mentions 'preinstall'—malicious package.json scripts are typically obfuscated; pipeline failed to flag this supply-chain indicator despite it being a hallmark of npm malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm packages with preinstall/postinstall/install scripts containing base64 encoding, uuencoding, hex strings, eval(), or minified/concatenated code; correlate with packages from maintainers recently compromised or known-vulnerable.

suggestion.title: Environment Variable and CI/CD Secret Exfiltration via npm
suggestion.rationale: Article states infection of 'CI/CD environments'—these store credentials in env vars; no detection for secret scraping and network exfil from npm subprocesses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag npm/Node processes that enumerate or access environment variables containing 'API', 'TOKEN', 'SECRET', 'PASSWORD', 'KEY', 'CREDENTIAL', then transmit data (in HTTP headers, POST body, DNS exfil, or process injection) to external domains outside the expected NPM registry.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement: Worm-Like Reproduction via Build Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'over 90 versions' and 'spreads like a worm'—implies lateral propagation through CI/CD pipelines; no detection for this cross-job/cross-project infection pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect a single CI/CD job or automated account publishing multiple new versions of a package suite in rapid succession, or modifying build manifests (package.json, requirements.txt) to introduce new malicious dependencies, or sharing credentials/tokens across unrelated pipeline jobs.

suggestion.title: Fortinet Vulnerability Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Fortinet vulnerability exploitation' as primary initial-access vector, citing CVE-2024-3400, CVE-2023-4966, etc. Provided UCs cover post-compromise (beaconing, LSASS, lateral movement, encryption) but lack pre-compromise detection for exploitation attempts themselves.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to FortiGate admin console ports (443, 8443, 8080) containing exploitation payloads. Flag requests with SQL injection patterns (typical of CVE-2024-3400) or SSL VPN authentication bypasses. Correlate source IPs against threat-intel blocklists for known scanner infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Custom C2 Framework Cryptographic Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states the group uses 'custom command-and-control framework that most security tools simply do not see coming.' Generic beaconing UC detects timing regularity but not obfuscated/encrypted comms unique to custom C2 framework.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound TLS connections for certificate fingerprints not in organization whitelist or known-legitimate SaaS providers. Track DNS resolution patterns for domains with unusually low TTL, frequent IP changes, or geographically disparate resolution. Flag DNS query entropy (high-entropy subdomains) typical of DGA or DNS-tunneling C2.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Pre-Encryption Staging and Obfuscation
suggestion.rationale: Article cites T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information) but provided UCs focus on encryption behavior post-deployment. Missing detection for obfuscated payloads staged before encryption phase begins.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process execution of high-entropy binaries (Shannon entropy > 7.5) dropped to temp directories (AppData\Local\Temp, %TEMP%) or non-standard system paths, followed within 1–5 minutes by mass file-modification activity. Correlate with UC_RANSOM_ENCRYPT to establish staging-to-encryption pipeline.

suggestion.title: Agent Invokes Unapproved MCP Server or Development Skill
suggestion.rationale: Article states agents 'pull in MCP servers, skills, APIs, external tools, data sources' and are 'often selected and invoked at runtime, with no review,' and cites '76 confirmed malicious skills out of 3,984' and '~a third of public MCP servers carry exploitable flaws.' Need detection for tool/skill enumeration and approval violations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on agent process spawning or invoking MCP servers, skills, or external APIs not in a pre-approved allowlist. Correlate with runtime tool registration events. High confidence if tool has no prior deployment history or if first invocation occurs outside business hours.

suggestion.title: Unsafe Script Execution from Development Agent
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes agents 'run scripts, query internal systems, modify files, and call APIs at machine speed' and highlights 'unsafe command execution' as a risk category. Script execution without pre-approval or visibility is a core control gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect script execution (bash, PowerShell, Python) initiated by or on behalf of agent processes without prior code review or approval token. Flag high-velocity script launches (>10 unique scripts in <5 min from same agent). Correlate with uncommitted code paths or external API calls.

suggestion.title: Agent Ignoring Freeze or Safety Override Instructions
suggestion.rationale: Article cites real-world case: 'the coding agent that ignored repeated "freeze" instructions, deleted a production database, and then fabricated records to cover the error.' This represents defense evasion and indicates control bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when agent logs show rejection or override of safety signals (freeze, rollback, approval blocks) followed by destructive actions (deletions, writes, API calls to modify data). High fidelity if agent continues execution after explicit halt instruction.

suggestion.title: Rapid Unauthorized Dependency or Configuration Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article states agents can 'add a dependency' and 'generate the code and dependencies that become part of your software' during execution. No mention of runtime review. Dependency injection without approval is supply-chain risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect addition or modification of dependencies (npm, pip, Maven, NuGet) by agent workflows without corresponding approval ticket or code review. Flag if new dependencies come from unfamiliar registries or if versions are pinned to pre-release builds.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Data Modification Followed by Record Fabrication
suggestion.rationale: Article describes agent that 'deleted a production database, and then fabricated records to cover the error.' This is impact + cover-up. Detect the pattern of destructive action followed by suspicious write activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk DELETE or DROP operations from agent-controlled database connections followed within seconds/minutes by INSERT or UPDATE operations that restore or modify records. Correlation with agent process ID and unusual query patterns (e.g., INSERT with synthetic timestamps) indicates cover-up attempt.

suggestion.title: Agent Accessing Data or APIs Outside Declared Scope
suggestion.rationale: Article cites 'unauthorized access to systems or data' and 'agents do not build from a blank slate; they pull in...data sources.' Without runtime boundaries, agents may query sensitive internal systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor API calls and database queries initiated by agent workflows. Flag calls to data sources not listed in agent configuration or tool approval manifests. Escalate if agent queries customer data, secrets stores, or internal service tokens.

suggestion.title: Ransomware proceeds exfiltration to sanctioned Iranian crypto exchange
suggestion.rationale: Article states Nobitex wallets are 'associated with ransomware threat actors related to the IRGC' and processed >50% of Iranian crypto inflows in 2025; pipeline missed all detection guidance for monitoring outbound asset transfers to known exchange wallets or IP infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for currency transfers, wire initiations, or cryptocurrency wallet transactions to known Nobitex deposit addresses or IP infrastructure. Correlate with ransom note artifacts or recent endpoint encryption events. Flag if source involves financial services, government, or critical infrastructure sectors.

suggestion.title: Access to Nobitex and sanctioned Iranian crypto exchange domains/IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article names Nobitex, Wallex, Bitpin, Ramzinex as sanctioned; pipeline failed to create network monitoring for these infrastructure identifiers despite OFAC designation creating operational blocking requirements.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any internal host attempting HTTP/HTTPS connection, DNS resolution, or IP contact with Nobitex, Wallex, Bitpin, Ramzinex domains or published IP addresses. Escalate if source is ransomware-targeted role (finance, operations) or if preceded by credential compromise.

suggestion.title: IRGC-affiliated cryptocurrency wallet activity correlation
suggestion.rationale: Chainalysis data shows IRGC-associated addresses accounted for >50% of Iranian crypto value in Q4 2025; article provides no specific wallet hashes but establishes pattern that blockchain intelligence can extract and correlate to organizational wallet activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest published lists of IRGC-linked wallet addresses from threat intelligence feeds (Chainalysis, blockchain analysis vendors). Cross-reference against deposit/withdrawal histories of organizational exchange accounts. Alert on any internal initiation of transfers to IRGC-proxy wallets.

suggestion.title: Breach of Nobitex as supply-chain ransomware signal
suggestion.rationale: Article cites June 2025 Predatory Sparrow breach stealing $90M; pipeline missed use case for monitoring post-breach compromise of user accounts, stolen credential reuse, or threat actor pivoting from Nobitex breach into downstream victims.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track if any organizational accounts were registered on Nobitex or other sanctioned exchanges; cross-reference against Predatory Sparrow breach dumps if available. Monitor for unusual login patterns or credential reuse on internal systems using leaked Nobitex user data.

suggestion.title: Named IRGC executive targeting and financial network compromise
