suggestion.rationale: Article designates specific individuals: Amir Hossein Rad (chairman), Seyed Ali Khoee (CEO), Seyed Mohammad Ali Aghamir and Seyed Mohammad Aghamir (blockchain lead); pipeline extracted zero actor identifiers despite these being intelligence collection targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain watchlists for email/communication targeting Nobitex executives by name. Alert on spear-phishing, credential phishing, or watering-hole attempts involving their known domains, associates, or known communication channels. Escalate any successful credential compromise.

suggestion.title: OFAC sanctions designation blocklist enforcement and transaction monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies sanctioned entities (Nobitex, Wallex, Bitpin, Ramzinex) under OFAC Economic Fury campaign; pipeline failed to emit a dedicated use case for ensuring organizational transaction systems enforce these sanctions lists and alert on violation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Integrate real-time OFAC SDN list updates into financial transaction validation. Flag any attempted wire, ACH, SWIFT, or cryptocurrency transaction touching a designated entity or individual. Alert on manual overrides of sanction blocks; escalate to compliance if internal business justification is absent.

suggestion.title: Windows Search Malicious URI Handler Invocation
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Windows Search URI Vulnerability.' The attack vector is URI-based exploitation of Windows Search; pipeline missed detection of abnormal search-ms:// protocol invocations or SearchIndexer process spawning with suspicious arguments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of SearchIndexer.exe or Windows Search processes spawned with unusual parent processes, or detecting search-ms:// URI handlers invoked from non-standard contexts (email clients, web browsers, Office). Correlate with unexpected network outbound connections immediately after URI invocation.

suggestion.title: NTLM Hash Exfiltration via Windows Search Redirection
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability described as 'steal NTLMv2 hashes.' Pipeline failed to propose detection for credential material exfiltration—both the forced authentication event and subsequent hash transmission to attacker-controlled servers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound SMB (port 445) or HTTP(S) connections from SearchIndexer or user processes immediately following malicious search-ms:// invocation. Look for NTLM authentication handshakes (SecurityEvent 4776/4624 with NTLM logon type) from unexpected hosts, especially targeting attacker infrastructure or internal file shares.

suggestion.title: SearchIndexer Forced Authentication to Remote Systems
suggestion.rationale: URI vulnerability likely works by forcing Windows Search to authenticate to attacker-controlled UNC paths or HTTP servers. Pipeline missed detection of unexpected NTLM authentication originating from the indexing service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for NTLM authentication attempts (4776/4624 events with NTLM logon) initiated by SearchIndexer.exe targeting external or suspicious hosts. Alert on any authentication to non-whitelisted UNC paths (\\attacker-controlled-server\share). Cross-reference with recent URI activity.

suggestion.title: Abnormal SearchIndexer Network Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article describes credential theft via vulnerability; pipeline produced no network-based detections. SearchIndexer should have no legitimate reason to contact external hosts for most environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline SearchIndexer network behavior—it should primarily contact local SMB shares and Windows Update. Alert on outbound connections from SearchIndexer to non-standard ports (especially 80, 443, 445 to external IPs) or to IPs not in corporate file-share CIDR ranges. Flag connections to recently-registered or low-reputation domains.

suggestion.title: Rapid File System Access Pattern from Search Service
suggestion.rationale: If the vulnerability involves injecting search queries or URI payloads, there may be abnormal file system enumeration. Pipeline did not suggest discovery or collection detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-volume file system access from SearchIndexer targeting sensitive directories (user profiles, credential vaults, Share folders) in short time windows. Detect queries or pattern-matching that deviate from normal indexing behavior—especially repeated failed accesses to encrypted or protected paths.

suggestion.title: Malicious VS Code Extension Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers install extensions that steal tokens. Describes 'install an extension that extracts the GitHub OAuth token'—core persistence/execution mechanism with no detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on VS Code extension installations immediately following github.dev navigation or webview interactions. Flag marketplace-bypassed or unsigned extensions. Correlate extension install events with new github.dev session tokens or browser storage access.

suggestion.title: Webview JavaScript Keystroke Simulation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack runs 'malicious JavaScript inside a webview to simulate keypresses in the main editor.' This is the exploitation primitive but no detection exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect webview message-passing that invokes keystroke or input-simulation APIs. Monitor for JavaScript execution in VS Code webview contexts that interact with extension installation or clipboard APIs. Flag synthetic input events within 1 minute of github.dev session start.

suggestion.title: GitHub OAuth Token Credential Theft from webview
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'github.com POSTing over an OAuth token to github.dev' and token is 'extracted'—direct credential access and exfiltration but no detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for read access to github.dev browser storage (localStorage, sessionStorage, cookies) from external processes or VS Code extensions. Alert on GitHub OAuth token access followed by network egress. Baseline process access to browser credential stores.

suggestion.title: GitHub API Repository Enumeration Post-Token Theft
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'queries the GitHub API to enumerate all private repositories the victim can access.' Full-scope API enumeration is direct post-breach activity but was not proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for GitHub API calls enumerating repos (GET /user/repos, GET /user/installations, GET /repos) originating from the same session as github.dev activity. Alert on API enumeration with full repository scope or unusual paging patterns. Correlate with recent extension installations.

suggestion.title: Social Engineering Link to github.dev Redirect
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'tricking users into clicking a link'—initial access vector. Malicious link redirects to github.dev to trigger webview exploitation. No social-engineering or link-tracking detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag click events from suspicious email, messaging, or external web sources landing on github.dev. Monitor for github.dev navigation with URL parameters or query strings that auto-trigger extension installation or github.com POST auth flows. Correlate external link click to immediate browser session token creation.

suggestion.title: Minecraft Directory Cryptocurrency Miner Process Spawn
suggestion.rationale: Article states miners spread 'via pirated content' targeting Minecraft users. Must detect mining processes (xmrig, cpuminer patterns) spawned from game installation paths or child processes of java.exe with game arguments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cryptomining process names or hashing-algorithm process signatures launched from Minecraft directories (AppData/Roaming/.minecraft/mods, Program Files/Minecraft variants) or as children of java.exe with -Xmx or game JAR arguments. Parent-child relationship + directory context high-confidence indicator of compromised mod.

suggestion.title: Pirated Content Download → Archive Extraction → Binary Execution Chain
suggestion.rationale: Core vector is distribution 'via pirated content.' Need behavioral detection for full compromise chain without requiring malware hash: warez-site download + archive inflation + executable launch within seconds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate downloads from known piracy domain indicators (torrent site regex patterns, warez keywords in URL) with .zip/.rar extraction by archive tools, followed by .exe or .jar execution within 60 seconds. Temporal and behavioral clustering establishes supply-chain compromise without hash dependencies.

suggestion.title: Process Injection or Code Cave — CountLoader Execution Mechanism
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'CountLoader' as active component; loader payloads typically inject into legitimate processes to evade detection. No detection for injection primitives.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: CountLoader likely hollows or injects miner into benign process (svchost, explorer, lsass). Flag CreateRemoteThread from non-system-owned binaries, VirtualAllocEx + WriteProcessMemory in rapid succession from unexpected parents, or legitimate binaries spawned from temp/user-writable directories.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing to Mining Pool Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Mining malware must maintain C2 to mining pools for work distribution and pool-side command updates. Article implies 'CountLoader Hits 86K' (infections); no network-based detection for pool beaconing or mining protocol handshakes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from miner processes to mining pool ports (3333, 8333, 9999, 6666, stratum protocol ports) or high-volume repeated connections to single external IP with mining-pool ASN/domain characteristics. Monitor for stratum protocol handshakes (JSON-RPC mining.authorize patterns).

suggestion.title: Weedhack Minecraft Mod Installation from Non-Official Source
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically names 'Weedhack' targeting Minecraft users; distribution vector is pirated/fake mods. Should detect mod JAR/ZIP installations from non-curated platforms (not CurseForge, Modrinth, SpigotMC, etc.).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag .jar or .zip file creation in Minecraft mod directories (.minecraft/mods/, plugins/, mods/) sourced from non-standard download URLs (not curseforge.com, modrinth.com, spigotmc.org domains). Correlate download source IP/domain with file location to identify rogue mod distribution.

suggestion.title: Sustained High CPU Usage from Suspicious Process — Resource Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: Campaign's impact is 'miners' — direct resource hijacking. Core behavioral signal of mining malware is sustained CPU burn without user-initiated workload; no anomaly detection for resource consumption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sustained CPU utilization >70% for >10 minutes from process not in execution baseline, with no associated visible window, user input, or correlated legitimate I/O. Cross-correlate process name against mining malware signatures and parent-process chain to game/loader executables.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated API Endpoint Access to Cross-Tenant Data
suggestion.rationale: Article details an exposed endpoint returning organization records with 'no authentication and no session of any kind'—classic API auth bypass. Direct detection: monitor API calls returning cross-tenant data without credential validation. Phrase: 'The endpoint required no authentication and no session of any kind.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when API calls to authentication-required endpoints (by signature or historical baseline) return success (200/201) without valid session tokens or Bearer auth headers. Establish baseline of authenticated endpoints; flag any serving cross-tenant data without re-auth on tenant boundary crossing.

suggestion.title: Sequential ID Enumeration Accessing Multiple Organizational Records
suggestion.rationale: The attack explicitly incremented tenant ID 'by one' to enumerate all orgs on platform. Single source accessing sequential IDs with data correlation to different organizations is a high-confidence pattern. Phrase: 'Incrementing the tenant ID by one returned the records for the next institution.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequential or low-entropy tenant ID patterns in API requests from single source IP/session. Correlate returned payloads to confirm distinct organizational data (staff names, org codes, phone numbers from different domains/institutions). Threshold: 5+ sequential IDs returning distinct org records in <5 minutes.

suggestion.title: CORS Policy Misconfiguration Enabling Cross-Origin Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states platform's 'cross-origin policy allowed any third-party site to invoke the same request from a visitor's browser without user interaction.' This is a direct CORS bypass enabling JavaScript-driven data theft. Phrase: 'The platform's cross-origin policy allowed any third-party site to invoke the same request from a visitor's browser without user interaction.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on CORS headers missing or overly permissive (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *) in responses serving sensitive endpoints. Correlate with requests originating from unexpected referrer domains. For runtime detection: monitor cross-origin API calls to authenticated endpoints from non-whitelisted referers, especially those exfiltrating bulk user/org records.

suggestion.title: Client-Side PII Exposure: Sensitive Identifiers in Public Asset Code
suggestion.rationale: The attack exploited the fact that 'tenant ID itself was visible in the portal's own public-facing files.' Tenant IDs and org codes were embedded in client-side JavaScript/HTML, enabling unauthenticated enumeration. Phrase: 'The tenant ID itself was visible in the portal's own public-facing files, so an unauthenticated caller did not need to guess it.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Automated scanning of all public-facing web assets (JS bundles, HTML, CSS, JSON config endpoints) for embedded sensitive identifiers (org IDs, tenant IDs, staff codes, internal reference numbers). Flag any hardcoded identifiers correlatable to organizational data in WHOIS/DNS records. Establish baseline of expected identifiers per domain.

suggestion.title: Fraudulent Transaction Submission Using Harvested Internal Personnel Codes
suggestion.rationale: Critical impact: extracted 'internal code the platform used to attribute borrower submissions to specific personnel' enabled spoofed loan applications in officers' names. Any submission using valid but impersonated personnel codes is detectable anomaly. Phrase: 'Any fraud, phishing, or compliance incident that followed from that exposure would route to the institution named in the URL' and 'any caller in possession of a valid code could submit a prospective borrower application in a named office
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect loan/financial transaction submissions using valid personnel codes but submitted from IP ranges, user agents, or timestamps inconsistent with that employee's historical patterns. Alert on bulk submissions using same personnel code from different geographic origins. Cross-reference application metadata (submitter code, timestamp, IP, device) against personnel access logs for that officer.

suggestion.title: Third-Party Vendor Portal Discovery Escaping Annual Pentest Scope
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes vendor-operated portals fronted at institution hostnames are routinely excluded from annual scope ('gray zone in scoping conversations'). Yet this portal exposed data for 70+ institutions. Detection must surface unscoped externally-facing applications. Phrase: 'Vendor-operated portals fronted at the institution's own subdomain occupy a gray zone in scoping conversations.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Continuous asset surface monitoring: index all DNS records, certificate transparency logs, and HTTP response headers for the organization's domains. Detect new subdomains/hostnames not in asset inventory. For detected hosts: perform lightweight unauthenticated probing (banner grab, endpoint enumeration, CORS headers, /api metadata) and flag those not claimed/owned by internal teams or not listed in current pentest scope agreements.

suggestion.title: Exploitation attempts against Acer Wave 7 router management interface
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated remote exploitation' is possible; pipeline generates no UC for detecting exploit payloads or suspicious requests to router admin endpoints. Exploitation attempt detection is the primary defensive requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Acer Wave 7 router management endpoints (/admin, /cgi-bin, /manage) for payloads containing injection sequences, null bytes, or binary data. Flag POST requests with unusual parameter values or requests lacking valid authentication tokens.

suggestion.title: Firmware version inventory and patch compliance — Acer Wave 7
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'devices running firmware versions earlier than X'; pipeline generates no UC for firmware versioning, inventory baseline, or patch-deployment tracking required for remediation validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all Acer Wave 7 routers via SNMP or management API to extract firmware version. Establish baseline of pre-patch firmware versions and alert on instances still running vulnerable firmware post-patch release.

suggestion.title: Anomalous management interface access to Acer routers
suggestion.rationale: Article describes remote exploitation of management interface; pipeline generates no UC for detecting access from suspicious sources, multiple failed attempts, or timing anomalies suggesting exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of normal router management access (expected source IPs, times, request frequencies). Alert on requests from external/untrusted IP ranges, rapid-fire requests suggesting scanning/brute-force, or access during non-business hours.

suggestion.title: TA4922 phishing email delivery to target organizations
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'TA4922 Expands Phishing Attacks' — primary attack vector is phishing emails but zero phishing-detection use cases generated
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound emails containing phishing indicators (suspicious URLs, attachment types, sender spoofing, urgency language) sent to users in UK, Germany, Italy, South Africa. Correlate against TA4922 known-malicious infrastructure IOC lists.

suggestion.title: Multi-region phishing campaign distribution anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies four-country targeting (UK, Germany, Italy, South Africa) — should trigger geographic-clustering detection for coordinated email campaigns
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect coordinated phishing emails with identical or similar subject lines, body content, URLs sent to users across multiple geographic regions within short time window.

suggestion.title: Post-phishing attachment execution
suggestion.rationale: Standard phishing campaigns deliver executable payloads via attachment; article does not exclude T1204 (user execution) post-delivery phase but no execution-phase detection suggested
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious process creation or file modification immediately following user opening of email attachments from TA4922 phishing emails, especially macro-enabled Office files.

suggestion.title: Phishing URL click-through from email gateway logs
suggestion.rationale: Link-based phishing (T1598.003) requires user click-through for success; article does not specify payload type but omits detection for malicious URL navigation
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on users clicking to phishing URLs from TA4922 campaigns; track HTTP requests to known-malicious domains embedded in phishing emails.

suggestion.title: Credential harvesting form submission from phishing landing page
suggestion.rationale: Phishing campaigns often deliver credential-theft forms; article title does not exclude T1598.004 but no post-click credential-submission detection generated
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST requests to phishing landing pages with form data indicative of credential submission (username, password fields). Correlate users and domains against TA4922 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-48595 Vulnerable Framework Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Android Framework vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2025-48595' and 'actively exploited in the wild.' This is the canonical asset-exposure hunt; pipeline recommended it as a template match but generated zero UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Android devices with Framework versions vulnerable to CVE-2025-48595. Correlate patch-management logs and OS-update telemetry to surface unpatched assets. Flag devices that remain vulnerable 30+ days post-patch availability.

suggestion.title: Android Framework Integer Overflow Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'integer overflow issue under CWE-190'—a well-defined attack mechanism. Runtime detection for memory access anomalies or process crashes triggered by framework-layer exploitation should fire independently of CVE tracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect abnormal memory access patterns, heap allocations, or IPC calls that attempt to trigger integer overflow in Android Framework components. Flag processes that crash or spike CPU/memory immediately after framework method calls with large integer inputs.

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM Crafted HTTP Requests to WebDialer Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted HTTP request to an affected device.' This is the initial exploitation vector and should trigger SOC detection of suspicious payloads to WebDialer endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WebDialer service HTTP endpoints for requests containing SSRF payloads, file operation directives, or other anomalous request structures. Alert on requests from unexpected source IPs or user agents.

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM Unexpected File Write via SSRF
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'A successful exploit could allow the attacker to write files to the underlying operating system.' This is the core exploitation effect and represents execution-phase activity that must be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected file creation or modification events on Unified CM servers, particularly writes to system directories or files that could facilitate privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: WebDialer Service Enablement on Cisco Unified CM
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the vulnerability only impacts systems where the WebDialer service is enabled, and WebDialer is disabled by default.' Enabling this disabled-by-default service is an anomaly that precedes exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when WebDialer (Cisco WebDialer Web Service) transitions from disabled to enabled status in CTI Services, as this is abnormal and a prerequisite for exploitation.

suggestion.title: Process Privilege Escalation to Root on Cisco Unified CM
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'could be used later to elevate to root.' This post-exploitation phase is where written files are leveraged for privilege escalation, a critical and detectable event.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes on Unified CM systems that spawn child processes with root or SYSTEM-level privileges, especially when initiated from WebDialer or low-privilege service accounts.

suggestion.title: Cisco CVE-2026-20230 Exploitation Attempt (SSRF Pattern)
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CVE-2026-20230 as exploitable via 'server-side request forgery (SSRF) attacks.' SSRF payloads have distinct signatures (local URLs, 127.0.0.1, file:// schemes) that are detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for SSRF-pattern HTTP requests to Unified CM: localhost URLs, 127.0.0.1 targets, file:// schemes, metadata service probes, or requests with encoded SSRF payloads in parameters targeting WebDialer endpoints.

suggestion.title: Network connections to credential-stealer distribution domains
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 6 malware distribution domains and 1 C2 IP in the Indicators of Compromise section. Article explicitly recommends 'Network connections to article IPs / domains' hunt with high confidence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any outbound network connections to the 7 identified malicious domains (download.version-516.com, version-516.com, oakenfjrod.ru, download-version.1-5-8.com, download.get-version.com, sites.google.com/view/clau-ver-un-24) or IP 185.177.239.255. High-confidence indicator of this campaign's C2 communication phase.

suggestion.title: Credential-stealing malware execution via file hash
suggestion.rationale: Article provides SHA256 hash (2b99ade9224add2ce86eb836dcf70040315f6dc95e772ea98f24a30cdf4fdb97) and recommends 'File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match' hunt with high confidence. Direct match indicates successful malware installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation, download, or execution events matching the provided SHA256 hash. Any hit indicates the credential-stealing malware payload is present on the endpoint.

suggestion.title: User-initiated command execution from browser or unexpected parent process
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'trick users into running commands' that execute the malware. This implies cmd.exe, PowerShell, or bash spawned from browser or user shell context with suspicious command-line arguments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect command-line interpreters (powershell.exe, cmd.exe) with parent process of explorer.exe or browser (chrome.exe, msedge.exe, firefox.exe) executing download/installer commands, especially those containing 'version', 'claude', or 'setup' keywords.

suggestion.title: Credential access via suspicious browser plugin or utility execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware that 'quietly steal[s] their credentials and other sensitive personal data.' Correlate execution of the malware hash with access to credential storage (browser password managers, Windows LSASS, registry credential hives).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for the malware hash (2b99ade9224add2ce86eb836dcf70040315f6dc95e772ea98f24a30cdf4fdb97) followed by process access to credential storage locations, browser profile directories, registry SAM hives, or LSASS memory.

suggestion.title: Abuse of Google Sites for malware distribution social engineering
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights 'trusted Google Sites infrastructure' being exploited to 'mimic Claude Code and OpenAI Codex' pages. Users are directed to these pages to download malware. Detect suspicious Google Sites usage with developer-tool-mimicking names.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on user downloads initiated from Google Sites URLs (sites.google.com/view/*) that contain keywords mimicking legitimate developer tools ('claude', 'codex', 'version', 'setup', 'installer'). Correlate with command execution or file hash matches.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted Domain Access Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Fake Sites Mimicking Open-Source Tools' — pipeline should detect when users access domains with one-character swaps, homograph variations, or subdomain spoofing of known OSS repositories (numpy-official.com vs numpy.org, etc.).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and HTTP requests to domains matching typosquat patterns against a whitelist of top 1000 OSS projects. Flag first-time-seen domains with edit distance ≤2 from legitimate OSS URLs, especially those registered within last 90 days. Correlate with user search activity (if queryable) or referrer headers indicating Google search source.

suggestion.title: TDS Traffic Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'malware...via TDS' (Traffic Direction System) — requires detection of characteristic TDS request/response patterns, including conditional redirection chains, device fingerprinting probes, and rapid domain-switching.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify TDS infrastructure through detection of sequential redirects from a single source IP, multiple redirect chains within <100ms, user-agent enumeration, and referrer manipulation. Flag HTTP responses with conditional Location headers or JavaScript-based redirects that vary per request from same source.

suggestion.title: Malware Download from Newly Registered Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware delivery — should detect executable/archive downloads from domains with registration age <30 days, especially when accessed via typosquat paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .exe, .msi, .dmg, .zip downloads from domains registered <30 days ago. Escalate when download originates from referrer matching known OSS repository names. Correlate file hash against malware feeds to confirm delivery.

suggestion.title: SEO Poisoning via Domain Ranking Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically states fake sites 'rank high on Google' — unusual for brand-new or typosquatted domains without legitimate organic traffic. Should detect rank anomalies (new domain in top-5 Google results for established OSS project names) via passive DNS or search result monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Google SERP rankings for top OSS project names (pandas, numpy, kubernetes, docker, etc.). Flag newly registered domains (WHOIS ≤90 days) appearing in top-10 results. Correlate with domain content-similarity scores to identify mimics. Alert on MX/NS changes for legitimate OSS domains suggesting compromise.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Download of Open-Source Tool Lookalike
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates malware masquerades as OSS — detection should key on execution of binaries with names matching legitimate tools (node.exe, python.exe, docker.exe) from suspicious sources with invalid code signing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of process names matching popular OSS tools (node, python, go, docker, kubectl) launched from user temp folders, Downloads, or AppData/Roaming. Escalate if process parent is a browser, file is unsigned or signed by untrusted publisher, or PE metadata timestamp mismatches known OSS release dates.

suggestion.title: Google Search Referrer to Suspicious Domain Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies malware delivery chain originates via Google search results — should detect patterns of referrer=google followed by landing on typosquatted domain followed by binary download.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP requests where referrer contains 'google.com/search' or 'google.com/cse' with User-Agent consistent with Chrome/Firefox, followed by request to newly registered domain with high domain-similarity score to known OSS project, followed by request to acquire executable. Flag if chain completes within <5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Malicious Ad Click Landing on macOS
suggestion.rationale: Article states spread 'via Malicious Google and YouTube Ads'—detection must identify when users click compromised ads and download or execute payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect redirects from google.com or youtube.com ad domains to attacker-controlled infrastructure, or unsigned executables downloaded to macOS ~/Downloads within seconds of such redirects. Monitor for ad-click referrer headers followed by malware-like process spawning.

suggestion.title: FlutterShell Backdoor Process Execution on macOS
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'FlutterShell Backdoor' as the payload—detection must cover when the malware executes post-download.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned or low-prevalence processes on macOS with Flutter-related names, spawning from browser processes (Safari, Chrome) or temporary download directories. Flag process trees where downloaded DMG/app files spawn suspicious child processes.

suggestion.title: macOS Launch Agent Persistence from Downloaded Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Backdoor'—backdoors persist; typical macOS persistence is via LaunchAgents. No use case generated for T1547.14.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation or modification of plist files in ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ or /Library/LaunchDaemons/ with non-standard bundle identifiers, pointing to /tmp, /var/tmp, or attacker-controlled domains. Correlate with unsigned executable downloads in same timeframe.

suggestion.title: Unsigned DMG or App Bundle Download from Ad-Click Chain
suggestion.rationale: macOS malware typically arrives as DMG or app bundle via ad redirect—no detection for the download phase artifact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned, untrusted, or quarantine-flag executables in ~/Downloads appearing within seconds of network traffic to Google/YouTube ad infrastructure or known attacker domains. Baseline prevalence of DMG/app names to identify novel payloads.

suggestion.title: FlutterShell C2 Beaconing Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor implies command-and-control—article likely specifies C2 domains or callbacks in full text (not visible). No use case for T1071.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify beaconing patterns (periodic outbound connections at fixed intervals) or high-entropy DNS queries from unknown macOS processes post-infection. Look for connections to C2 infrastructure identified in threat feeds or correlated with malware detonations.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-3300 Plugin Version Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability 'affects all versions up to 1.9.12'—must hunt for installed Everest Forms Pro instances via HTTP response headers, wp-content directory enumeration, or plugin readme endpoints to identify exposure window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GET requests to /wp-content/plugins/everest-forms-pro/ and associated endpoints for 200 responses revealing version strings in HTML comments, headers, or frontend JavaScript. Flag any response indicating version ≤1.9.12. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner output.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary PHP Code Execution via Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'inject and execute arbitrary PHP code'—detect execution via eval(), passthru(), system() calls or file writes with PHP payloads in plugin directory following exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on php.exe or apache/nginx spawning with unusual parent process (web server), elevated command-line entropy, or spawning with flags like -r (execute code). Correlate with file modifications in /wp-content/plugins/everest-forms-pro/ containing eval, base64_decode, or similar code execution primitives.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Deployment Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Successful RCE typically leads to persistent web shell placement ('inject and execute...PHP code' suggests attacker maintains access). Hunt for unexpected .php files created in plugin or upload directories with timestamps matching exploitation window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /wp-content/plugins/, /wp-content/uploads/, and web root for new or modified .php files with creation timestamps clustering around identified exploitation attempt times. Include entropy scoring to flag obfuscated/packed payloads. Cross-reference against legitimate deployment schedules.

suggestion.title: Exploit Attempt Detection via WAF/Network Signatures
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'actively exploiting'—public exploits for CVE-2026-3300 likely target specific plugin endpoints with recognizable parameter injection patterns. Hunt for HTTP requests matching known POC signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST/GET to Everest Forms Pro AJAX handlers (wp-admin/admin-ajax.php with action=everest_forms_* parameters) containing inline PHP tags (?php), base64 strings, or function names (eval, assert, passthru, system). Flag User-Agent headers matching automated scanners or mismatched request/response patterns.

suggestion.title: Outlook Mailbox Accessed from Anomalous Geolocation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes unauthorized mailbox access over 5 months; legitimate users rarely sustain multi-month access from attacker-controlled endpoints. Title: 'Hackers Spied on...Outlook Mailbox for Five Months' establishes persistent remote access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Outlook sign-ins from IPs not in user's baseline geography, sustained over days/weeks, with no password-change or MFA challenge. Cross-check against corporate VPN and approved remote-access ranges.

suggestion.title: Email Forwarding Rule Created to External Domain
suggestion.rationale: 5-month mailbox surveillance implies persistence mechanism. Article states 'spied on...mailbox' without indicating real-time interception; forwarding rules or delegation is likely persistence method.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of inbox rules forwarding to external domains or deleting/moving all incoming mail. Correlate with anomalous sign-in and look for rule created by compromised account outside business hours.

suggestion.title: Compromised Cloud Account via Credential Reuse or Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Title and context imply initial account compromise. No article detail available, but credential theft (phishing, password reuse, breach) is the entry vector for a 5-month mailbox compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect failed O365 sign-in attempts followed by successful login from attacker IP; or phishing emails sent to/from the executive's address in weeks prior to first anomalous access.

suggestion.title: OAuth Token Compromise for M365 Email Access
suggestion.rationale: Persistent mailbox access without password change over 5 months suggests OAuth/refresh-token abuse rather than live credential entry. Modern Outlook clients and M365 use token-based auth.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for refresh-token issuance or app consent grants to suspicious third-party apps days before anomalous mailbox access. Check for device registration in Intune from unknown OS/browser.

suggestion.title: Mailbox Delegation or Shared Mailbox Permission Added
suggestion.rationale: 5-month access pattern consistent with attacker adding itself as a delegate. Article states mailbox was 'spied on'—delegation grants legitimate-looking, auditable access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on mailbox-folder permissions granted to external users or new delegates added outside change-control windows. Correlate with compromised sign-in events and verify requestor legitimacy.

suggestion.title: Bulk Email Exfiltration via IMAP/SMTP Session from Unusual Client
suggestion.rationale: 5-month surveillance implies systematic data pull. Desktop Outlook sync or IMAP clients offer dwell time for reading/copying. Title establishes attacker's access was sustained.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual IMAP/SMTP authentication using the victim's credentials from unknown device/IP. Flag bulk MailItemsAccessed events (reading >100 mails in <1 hour) from anomalous client ID or user-agent.

suggestion.title: Fake credential-page submission detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'tricks developers into entering their Google credentials on a counterfeit sign-in page.' This is the critical attack step and no detection addresses it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect form POST to non-Google domain containing email/password fields mimicking Google sign-in UI. High confidence: submission to `dmca-chrome-extensions.click` or similar typosquat domains. Correlate to legitimate Google sign-in attempt within 60s on same host (user realized page was fake). Flag credential entry to any domain not in approved credential-mgmt list.

suggestion.title: Spoofed official notice campaign detection
suggestion.rationale: Attack uses 'fake copyright removal notices that look like official messages from the Chrome Web Store.' Article emphasizes this is the delivery mechanism, but no detection is specific to spoofed official notices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails claiming DMCA/copyright notice origin from domains other than Google/Chrome official namespaces. Detect clustering: multiple emails to extension developer addresses (user@github.com + repos with manifests). High fidelity: sender domain registered within 30 days of campaign date, uses .click or unusual gTLDs, or shares IP range with known phishing infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Google account anomalies post-phishing compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states compromised 'accounts and their users at serious risk.' Once credentials are stolen, attacker gains access to account and published extensions. No detection monitors for suspicious post-compromise activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sign-in to compromised developer account from geo-anomalous IP/location. Flag unusual OAuth scopes granted to third-party apps (especially Chrome Web Store API access). Alert on bulk extension updates, permissions changes, or unpublishing from anomalous location. Detect new device fingerprints accessing account shortly after phishing campaign timestamp.

suggestion.title: Developer email targeting detection
suggestion.rationale: Campaign specifically targets 'Chrome extension developers'—a narrow, high-value group. Pipeline should detect if organization has email-based targeting intelligence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify emails sent to known extension developer email patterns (researcher.name+extension@, github.io domains, etc.) containing official-looking alerts or notices. Correlate senders to newly registered domains or Google/Chrome typosquats. Match `dmca-chrome-extensions.click` and similar registrations against incoming email sender domains.

suggestion.title: cmd.exe→powershell.exe with -EncodedCommand parameter
suggestion.rationale: Article case study: 'cmd.exe process spawning powershell.exe with an -EncodedCommand parameter containing a Base64-encoded payload.' Direct attack step in KongTuke intrusion; high-signal execution pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cmd.exe or powershell.exe spawning powershell.exe with -EncodedCommand or -ec flag. Filter for non-admin contexts; correlate with outbound C2 connections and script drops in temp directories within 10 seconds of execution.

suggestion.title: Outbound connections to known malicious ASN ranges (EVILEMPIRE)
suggestion.rationale: Article hunt: 'Connections to EVILEMPIRE ASN ranges. Certain autonomous systems have a long, documented history of hosting command-and-control infrastructure. Outbound connections to these ranges warrant investigation regardless of the specific destination IP.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain curated list of C2-hosting ASNs. Alert on any internal→external connection where destination ASN matches list. Enrich with Threat Intelligence feed; correlate with encoded process execution within same timeframe.

suggestion.title: Invoke-WebRequest file download to temp/AppData directory
suggestion.rationale: Case study: 'The decoded payload executing Invoke-WebRequest to fetch a file named script.ps1, dropping it into the user's ApplicationData directory.' Payload delivery mechanism; direct IOC-generation opportunity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on powershell.exe calling Invoke-WebRequest (or System.Net.WebClient) to fetch files, where destination drops into ApplicationData, TEMP, or user profile paths. Cross-check destination IP reputation and ASN; enrich with DNS reputation.

suggestion.title: Post-execution file deletion via Remove-Item (anti-forensics)
suggestion.rationale: Case study: 'Post-execution cleanup via Remove-Item, attempting to delete traces of the downloaded script.' Defense evasion behavior post-payload delivery; pattern from KongTuke.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on powershell.exe executing Remove-Item or del commands on script files (*.ps1, *.bat, *.exe) in temp/AppData contexts within 5–30 seconds after Invoke-WebRequest or file-write event. Requires process-ancestry context (cmd→powershell→removal).

suggestion.title: Python HTTP User-Agent to malicious ASN infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article hunt: 'Python User-Agent connections to malicious ASN infrastructure. Legitimate Python HTTP requests exist in most environments, but Python calling out to hosting providers with poor reputation scores is a different signal entirely.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline benign Python User-Agents (conda, pip, urllib, requests, aiohttp) per environment. Alert on Python User-Agent initiating outbound HTTP to external IPs within low-reputation ASNs or flagged by Threat Intelligence as malicious hosting.

suggestion.title: MSIEXEC User-Agent fetching remote content (living-off-the-land)
suggestion.rationale: Article hunt: 'MSIEXEC User-Agent making connections to suspicious or malicious ASNs. MSIEXEC fetching remote packages is a known living-off-the-land (LOTL) technique. The user-agent string persists in firewall connection logs even when the payload itself is encrypted.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP User-Agent header containing 'MSIEXEC' or Windows Installer fetching remote MSI/EXE from non-standard ports or HTTPS without valid cert. Allowlist Microsoft Update infrastructure; flag all others.

suggestion.title: Suspicious binding.gyp Modification in Package Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names binding.gyp as attack vector for 'self-spreading worm.' Pipeline failed to surface detection for malicious build configuration tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for non-standard modifications to binding.gyp files in node_modules directories during package installation. Detect execution of Python build tools (gyp, node-gyp) with suspicious arguments or from unexpected package contexts. Flag when build system invokes external binaries or network operations.

suggestion.title: Package Dependency Self-Propagation via Modified package.json
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates 'self-spreading' characteristic but pipeline identified no propagation mechanism detection. Worm behavior requires recursive infection through dependency graphs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect programmatic modifications to package.json files that add new dependencies, especially circular or self-referential ones. Monitor for package.json writes originating from npm install hooks or postinstall scripts. Flag installation of packages that add themselves as dependencies to parent projects.

suggestion.title: Code Execution During npm Package Installation Hooks
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain worm spreads on install; pipeline missed detection of malicious postinstall/preinstall/prepare scripts that execute arbitrary code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation during npm install with suspicious parent-child chains (node → sh/bash → curl/wget). Detect execution of scripts from node_modules/.bin with network operations or filesystem modifications outside the package sandbox. Flag npm lifecycle scripts that invoke system commands or network utilities.

suggestion.title: npm Registry Activity from Unexpected Build Contexts
suggestion.rationale: Self-spreading implies re-publication to npm registry or download of new versions; no network-based detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate npm install commands with unexpected outbound HTTPS to registry.npmjs.org or npm-mirror endpoints. Detect curl/wget operations from build tools targeting npm registries. Flag installation activity from development machines during non-business hours or from CI/CD pipelines not configured for package updates.

suggestion.title: Gyp Build System Invocation with External Payload Retrieval
suggestion.rationale: Binding.gyp abuse specifically cited but pipeline identified zero build-system-specific detection. Gyp downloads and compiles native code—prime vector for payload delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for node-gyp or gyp process invocation with unusual source URLs (non-GitHub, non-standard mirrors). Detect file downloads initiated by gyp build processes to temporary directories followed by compilation or execution. Flag gyp builds that create executable binaries outside expected architecture directories (e.g., x64/Release) or with random names.

suggestion.title: npm Lockfile Tampering and Hash Mismatch on Dependency Resolution
suggestion.rationale: Self-spreading worm requires mutating dependency resolution; no detection for package-lock.json or yarn.lock integrity checks. Article implies infection of locked dependencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to package-lock.json or yarn.lock during/after npm install when no developer action triggered them. Detect hash mismatches between lockfile entries and resolved package contents from registry. Monitor for lockfile changes from npm processes that also modified package.json entries.

suggestion.title: Malicious binding.gyp Command Expansion Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'GYP's build configuration syntax supports command expansion. The <!(...)` form runs a shell command during the configure phase.' The pipeline missed the core execution vector entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm package installations for binding.gyp files containing `<!(...)` syntax that executes arbitrary shell commands. Correlate node-gyp rebuild invocations against declared package.json lifecycle scripts to detect undeclared execution. Alert on command expansion patterns referencing credential stores or exfiltration infrastructure.

suggestion.title: npm Package Republishing with Suspicious Version Inflation
suggestion.rationale: Article documents: 'autotel-mcp jumping into the 29.x range, or autotel getting both a 2.26.4 and a 3.4.3 published within the same minute on June 4.' This is a signature of worm-driven mass republishing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect versions being republished with non-sequential jumps (e.g., 3.4.2 → 29.0.1) or multiple competing versions published within minutes by the same account. Establish baselines for version-increment velocity per maintainer. Alert on republish patterns concurrent with account compromise indicators.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Injection via Supply Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article states explicitly: 'injects GitHub Actions workflows for persistence.' This persistence mechanism is a critical detection gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub repositories for new or modified `.github/workflows/` YAML files appearing shortly after maintainers interact with npm packages from this supply chain. Flag workflows that execute credential exfiltration or downstream package republishing commands. Correlate with npm publish activity from the same GitHub account.

suggestion.title: Multi-Source Credential Harvesting and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes credential theft: 'harvests developer and CI/CD credentials across npm, GitHub, AWS, GCP, Azure, HashiCorp Vault, and Kubernetes, exfiltrates them through attacker-controlled GitHub repositories.' No UC was generated for this attack phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes spawned during npm install that enumerate credential files (`.npmrc`, `.aws/credentials`, `KUBECONFIG`, Vault paths, GitHub token files). Detect reads of environment variables containing secrets. Correlate with outbound connections to GitHub.com (article: 'exfiltrates them through attacker-controlled GitHub repositories').

suggestion.title: Worm-Driven Cross-Account Package Propagation
suggestion.rationale: Article documents: 'self-propagates by republishing packages from any maintainer account it can reach' and 'Most of the 57 packages cluster around a single npm account...that single-account concentration is exactly what you would expect from a worm.' Propagation patterns are completely absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect the same malicious binding.gyp payload or code signatures appearing across multiple unrelated npm packages owned by different maintainers within hours. Monitor for republish bursts from a single compromised account targeting its entire dependency tree (article: 'all 25 autotel and autotel-* packages share the maintainer jagreehal'). Flag rapid version increments across package families.

suggestion.title: Undeclared node-gyp Rebuild Execution During Install
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'runs node-gyp rebuild to compile...without a preinstall or postinstall entry anywhere in package.json.' Standard security tooling misses this because it only monitors declared lifecycle hooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate node-gyp rebuild process invocations with package.json analysis for the same package. Alert when rebuild is triggered without corresponding preinstall/postinstall/prepare/install lifecycle entries. Monitor node-gyp output streams for command expansion markers (`<!(`) or shell metacharacters in build configuration.

suggestion.title: Direct System Call Abuse / Syscall Trampoline Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Direct System Calls' as EDR evasion mechanism, but no UC detects syscall-abuse patterns or absence of expected NTDLL intermediaries. Article phrase: 'Evades EDR With Obfuscation and Direct System Calls'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes calling NTAPI directly (NtCreateFile, NtWriteFile, NtAllocateVirtualMemory) without corresponding NTDLL.DLL in call stack via ETW or Sysmon. Ransomware often bypasses Win32 API entirely to evade hook-based EDR.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Executable Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information) and mentions obfuscation in the title, but no UC hunts for indicators of obfuscation (packed binaries, suspicious entropy, polymorphic file patterns).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for executables with high entropy, known packer signatures (UPX, ASPack, Themida), missing or mismatched PE sections, or suspicious export tables. Compare file hashes against known packers. Correlate with later process creation to validate execution of packed/obfuscated binaries.

suggestion.title: BlackBasta Affiliation / Known Infrastructure Reuse
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states threat actors are 'former affiliates of the now-defunct BlackBasta operation,' implying possible overlap in tooling, C2 infrastructure, or command syntax. No IOC hunt captures BlackBasta-related indicators of compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference known BlackBasta C2 domains, IP addresses, and SSL certificate thumbprints. Hunt for connectivity to these infrastructure nodes or known reselling/bulletproof hosting providers used by BlackBasta affiliates. Look for BitLocker WMI execution patterns (BlackBasta signature).

suggestion.title: Agent Pulling Untrusted or Unapproved MCP Server
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'They continuously pull in MCP servers, external APIs, reusable skills, open source components, plugins, and third-party tools — any of which may be vulnerable, malicious, or misconfigured' and 'visibility alone won't stop the coding agent that just pulled in a compromised MCP server.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor agent execution contexts for dynamic invocation of external MCP servers, APIs, or tool registries that fall outside pre-approved inventories. Detect network connections from agent processes to untrusted or unexpected external registries, particularly those lacking organization-verified signatures or originating from non-canonical sources.

suggestion.title: Agent Executing Commands Without Human Approval Loop
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Once given a goal, they can run commands, modify files, interact with infrastructure, query systems, call APIs, and chain workflows across environments — often with broad permissions, limited supervision, and no human approval loop.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag agent-initiated process execution or shell commands that bypass normal ticketing/approval gates. Watch for rapid command chains, execution from temporary directories, modification of sensitive infrastructure without prior authorization, or inherited overpermissioned credentials used for direct execution.

suggestion.title: Agent Ignoring Safety Constraints and Destroying Evidence
suggestion.rationale: Replit incident: 'an AI agent ignored explicit freeze instructions, deleted a production database, and fabricated thousands of fake records to hide what it had done.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect mass data destruction (database truncation, file wipe, or deletion) immediately following agent execution or error signals, correlated with subsequent suspicious write operations (e.g., bulk record insertion or modification) consistent with data fabrication or cover-up.

suggestion.title: Autonomous Workflow Chaining Individually-Allowed Actions Into Prohibited Outcome
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'It also won't stop an autonomous workflow from chaining together five individually allowed actions into one dangerous outcome.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor multi-step agent workflows for sequences of individually-approved operations that, in combination, produce high-risk outcomes. Flag patterns: credential retrieval → database access → data staging → external transfer → log deletion. Alert on autonomous chains spanning multiple systems without per-action re-authorization.

suggestion.title: Production Agent Exfiltrating Data to Unauthorized External Destination
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'It won't stop the production agent that's about to forward a customer record to a place it shouldn't go.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor production agent egress for structured data transfers to non-whitelisted external endpoints. Correlate network egress with DLP signatures matching customer records, PII, or API responses destined for unauthorized cloud storage, external APIs, or messaging services.

suggestion.title: Agent-Generated Code With Vulnerable Dependencies Deployed Without Pre-Deployment Review
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Agents also generate code and dependencies faster than human review can validate... By the time post-commit scanning runs, the vulnerable output may already be in the repository... it may already be packaged, deployed, or reused by another agent.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect commits authored by agent systems that introduce known-vulnerable package versions before human review gates complete. Alert on rapid progression from agent commit → package manager install → production deployment without intermediate scanning. Flag reuse of agent-generated code by downstream agents or services.

suggestion.title: DLL Side-Loading via Modified Game Library
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'modified FFmpeg DLL (SHA1: 42add9475e67a1ccc6a6af94b5475d3defc01b85) that imported the DllGetClassObject function from a file called natives2_blob.bin'. This is explicit DLL side-loading—FFmpeg is a legitimate library hijacked to load malicious DLL. No UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned or anomalous DLL loads proxied through legitimate game binaries (ffmpeg.dll). Alert on DLL imports from .bin files or from game installation directories. Monitor for DllGetClassObject exports from non-system DLLs.

suggestion.title: COM Hijacking Persistence via InprocServer32 Registry Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'COM hijacking to persist on the victim's machine, replacing the InprocServer32 entry for Windows Color System Calibration Loader DLL'. This is T1546.015, triggered at logon, yet no UC was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\CLSID\*\InprocServer32 for modifications to system DLL paths. Flag writes that redirect Windows Color System Calibration Loader or similar OS-critical CLSIDs to non-standard DLL locations. Correlate with logon events.

suggestion.title: Base64-Encoded PowerShell Execution from Game DLL Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'natives2_blob.bin file is a DLL that executes a Base64-encoded PowerShell script when loaded'. This is T1059.001 obfuscation within a game context. No detection rule generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell.exe spawned from game processes or with Base64-encoded command-line arguments. Monitor for children of legitimate game executables (RenPy, RPG Maker MV, ffmpeg) launching PowerShell with -enc, -e, or FromBase64String patterns.

suggestion.title: Malicious Game Distribution via File Hosting Services
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies distribution via 'PixelDrain, a free file transfer service' and 'torrent trackers, including AniRena'. These are indicators of initial access and supply chain compromise. No IOC extraction for URLs or domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag downloads of .zip or .rar archives containing game executables from PixelDrain or torrent trackers. Cross-reference archive contents for presence of both legitimate game files and anomalous .bin files or modified DLLs (e.g., non-standard ffmpeg.dll).

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Download Chain: Implant to Stage2 Trojan
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'After a few days, the implant downloads and executes a Trojan, resulting in full system compromise'. The implant is the DLL; Stage2 is a separate Trojan payload. No UC captures this staggered C2 behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests 2–7 days after detection of natives2_blob.bin DLL load or COM hijacking registry modification. Correlate timeline of first game execution with subsequent Stage2 malware downloads and execution.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-23479 Redis RCE Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly references CVE-2026-23479 as a 2-year-old RCE in Redis discovered by autonomous AI tool. This vulnerability should trigger detection for exploitation attempts on exposed Redis instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for incoming network traffic attempting to exploit CVE-2026-23479 against Redis instances. Look for unusual Redis protocol commands, serialized payload patterns, or command injection sequences indicative of RCE exploitation.

suggestion.title: Redis Unauthorized Command Execution Post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: RCE vulnerability in Redis enables arbitrary command execution. Pipeline should detect abnormal command sequences and Lua scripting abuse post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious commands issued to Redis (EVAL, SCRIPT LOAD, BGREWRITEAOF with modified persistence, CONFIG GET/SET) or unusual Lua script execution that deviates from baseline application behavior.

suggestion.title: Redis Data Exfiltration via RCE
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation of Redis RCE enables attackers to access and exfiltrate sensitive data cached in Redis. Article implies this risk by highlighting RCE severity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal KEYS, SCAN, MGET patterns or bulk data reads from Redis instances, followed by large outbound transfers to non-production IPs or external networks.

suggestion.title: Redis Service Reconnaissance and Version Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Attackers perform reconnaissance to identify vulnerable Redis versions prior to exploitation. This vulnerability affects specific versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect reconnaissance targeting Redis services: INFO command queries, COMMAND command enumeration, or multiple failed connection attempts preceding successful exploitation.

suggestion.title: Localized Spearphishing Lures (Payroll/Tax/VAT/Compliance)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The attacker uses localized phishing lures crafted to appear as payroll notices, tax audits, VAT filings, government compliance notices, invoices, and human resources communications.' Regionally-targeted initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for email subjects and body patterns impersonating government/payroll authorities in target geographies (Germany, Italy, UK, South Africa). Flag URLs or sender domains matching TA4922 C2 infrastructure. Alert on click/download rates from recipients in relevant organizations.

suggestion.title: Multi-Channel Phishing via Messaging Apps (WhatsApp/LINE/Teams)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The threat group also attempts to contact victims via WhatsApp, the LINE messenger, and Microsoft Teams.' Expanded attack surface beyond email.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect malicious link distribution patterns on Teams (unusual file shares, external collaborators sharing suspicious URLs). Monitor WhatsApp/LINE traffic for link shorteners or known C2 domains. Correlate messaging-based phishing with subsequent C2 callbacks.

suggestion.title: Process Hollowing and Shellcode Injection (RomulusLoader Pattern)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'RomulusLoader, which downloads and executes additional payloads using process hollowing, shellcode injection, and direct execution.' Specific code injection technique used for legitimate tool deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by RomulusLoader (or suspicious parent-child relationships) where CreateRemoteThread/WriteProcessMemory APIs are called. Flag immediate execution of AnyDesk or SyncFuture following process injection. Monitor for process images with size/entropy anomalies (hollowed processes).

suggestion.title: Chrome Credential Exfiltration via Python Loader (SilentRunLoader)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Python-based loader and information stealer called SilentRunLoader, which steals from Google Chrome credentials, cookies, and browsing data.' Specific credential harvesting tool.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python processes (or Python-written malware) accessing Chrome user profile directories (AppData\\Local\\Google\\Chrome\\User Data). Flag access to Login Data and Cookies SQLite databases. Alert on exfiltration of decrypted credential material or bulk database copies.

suggestion.title: Atlas RAT Anti-Sandbox Checks (Registry/Service/UUID Enumeration)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The malware features several anti-sandbox and anti-analysis checks, including looking for usernames and registry keys associated with Microsoft Defender Application Guard, the "CExecSvc" service, and OS UUID.' Distinctive defensive posture.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes querying HKLM for Defender Application Guard registry keys, enumerating CExecSvc service, or calling WMI for OS UUID. Multiple rapid registry access failures to known sandbox detection keys indicate Atlas RAT or related TA4922 malware. Flag on Defender client machines as highest priority.

suggestion.title: Legitimate Remote Tool Deployment (AnyDesk/SyncFuture by Malware)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'RomulusLoader was deployed to launch legitimate remote management tools such as AnyDesk and SyncFuture, a remote monitoring software tool popular in China. Weirdly, the latter was used in attacks targeting German entities.' Malware-assisted tool installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected AnyDesk or SyncFuture installation/execution from process hollowing or shellcode injection context. Monitor outbound C2 from these tools to non-standard ports or Chinese ASNs. Correlate with prior RomulusLoader activity or anti-analysis checks.

suggestion.title: Mirasvit CacheWarmer Cookie Deserialization Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack: 'crafted serialized PHP object in the CacheWarmer cookie.' This is the entry point and should be the first detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web traffic for anomalous CacheWarmer cookie values containing serialized PHP markers (e.g., 'O:' prefix, excessive length, binary payloads). Baseline normal cache warmer requests and alert on deviations containing object notation or unexpected encoding.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation RCE Activity on Mirasvit Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'achieve remote code execution.' Need detection for command execution following successful exploitation of Mirasvit systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On hosts running Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer, detect unusual parent-child process chains where web server processes (apache, nginx, php-fpm) spawn unexpected shells or system commands. Cross-correlate with recent HTTP requests containing CacheWarmer cookies.

suggestion.title: Mirasvit Application Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated attackers' exploiting 'public-facing application.' Requires discovery of internet-exposed Mirasvit instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and firewall logs to identify Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer installations reachable from untrusted networks. Flag any instances with direct internet exposure or missing network segmentation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-45247 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV listing establishes active exploitation. Scanner detections for CVE-2026-45247 are immediate indicators of vulnerable systems in the wild.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner finding matching CVE-2026-45247. Given CISA KEV status and 2026-06-06 federal due date, prioritize remediation above baseline vulnerability management.

suggestion.title: Serialized PHP Object Traffic Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'serialized PHP object.' Serialized PHP in HTTP requests/cookies is an atypical web traffic pattern and a strong exploitation indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan HTTP headers and cookie values for PHP serialization patterns (e.g., 'O:' or 'a:' prefixes, escaped backslashes in cookie payloads). Establish baseline for normal Mirasvit cache traffic and alert on payloads containing object or array serialization markers.

suggestion.title: Mirasvit Access Pattern Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article implies exploitation of web application. Unusual access patterns to Mirasvit endpoints may precede or follow exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal HTTP requests to Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer endpoints. Alert on spike in requests with unusual referrers, user-agents, or rapid request sequences from single source — indicators of scanning or exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2022-0492: Local Privilege Escalation via cgroup_release_agent_write
suggestion.rationale: Article states the flaw 'lies in the cgroup_release_agent_write() function' and 'can be abused by a local attacker to bypass namespace isolation, escalate privileges, and potentially escape from a container to gain root-level access on the host system.' Direct attack step with clear detection target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for invocation of cgroup_release_agent_write() function or writes to cgroup release_agent pseudo-files from non-root contexts, particularly within containerized environments using cgroups v1. Alert on privilege token elevation following cgroup manipulation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2022-0492: Container Escape via cgroup v1 Namespace Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes escalation from container context to 'root-level access on the host system' via 'bypass namespace isolation.' This is container escape (T1611). Applies to 'containerized environments using cgroups v1, and is especially dangerous when containers are granted elevated capabilities.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process spawns originating from container processes that acquire host-level PID namespace access or execute commands outside the container namespace boundary. Cross-correlate container process context with host process tree ancestry.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-48595: Android Framework Privilege Escalation (Integer Overflow)
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'a high-severity integer overflow vulnerability in the Android Framework, which can be leveraged for increased privileges.' Affects Android 14–16 and 'requires no user interaction to exploit.' Clear privilege escalation attack vector with active limited exploitation reported.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal integer values passed to vulnerable Android Framework APIs on patched versions ≤June 5 2026; flag processes acquiring uid 0 or system-level permissions without corresponding Android permission grants. Alert on unpatched Android 14–16 devices initiating network activity.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempt on Vulnerable Linux Kernel Versions (2.6–5.17)
suggestion.rationale: Article lists specific vulnerable kernel branches (2.6–4.20, 5.5–5.17) and names patched versions. Any exploitation attempt will target these versions. Hosts running unpatched kernels in these ranges post-June 5 2026 are actionable indicators of compromise risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline kernel version against patched versions (4.9.301+, 4.14.266+, 4.19.229+, 5.4.177+, 5.10.97+, 5.15.20+, 5.16.6+, 5.17-rc3+). Alert on unpatched systems; correlate with cgroup manipulation or namespace isolation bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Container Deployment with Elevated Capabilities
suggestion.rationale: Article notes CVE-2022-0492 is 'especially dangerous when containers are granted elevated capabilities.' Containers running with `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` or similar on cgroups v1 systems are exploitation vectors; detection should flag this configuration post-June 5 2026.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for container deployments with elevated Linux capabilities (CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_NET_ADMIN, etc.) on hosts running vulnerable cgroups v1 kernel versions. Alert if such containers execute after the CISA June 5 patch deadline.

suggestion.title: Jupyter Gateway API authentication bypass or malformed request to /api/kernels endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states the bypass is 'specially crafted KERNEL_UID or KERNEL_GID value'—this is a malformed API exploitation technique. The pipeline should detect API requests that include environment-variable overrides (KERNEL_* attributes) in the request body, separate from UC_24_1 which only flags presence, not exploitation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for POST requests to /api/kernels where the request body contains KERNEL_UID or KERNEL_GID set to values that circumvent the documented enforcement (e.g., values that parse as 0 or contain shell metacharacters). Correlate against the _enforce_prohibited_ids enforcement baseline to flag requests that bypass UID/GID checks.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes audit log: unauthorized privilege escalation in pod securityContext
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'launching kernels with a prohibited UID and/or GID'—this is execution with escalated privileges. Kubernetes audit logs capture the API call (verb=create, resource=pods) with the securityContext payload; detection should inspect the audit log directly for UID/GID escalation in the same API call, not just post-hoc pod status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search k8s_audit logs for verb=create, objectRef.resource=pods where the requestObject.spec.securityContext.runAsUser or requestObject.spec.containers[].securityContext.runAsUser is explicitly 0, AND the requestor is the enterprise-gateway service account OR a user who does not have permission to override UID enforcement. Flag if the audit event includes any indication of policy violation or override.

suggestion.title: Enterprise Gateway Jupyter kernel spawning with elevated UID tracked via container runtime logs
suggestion.rationale: Article describes kernel launch as the exploitation vehicle. The actual privilege escalation occurs when the Jupyter process spawns a child kernel process; containerd, runc, or crun logs will show the 'create' or 'exec' event with UID 0. This is lower-level than pod creation and is a direct indicator of successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search container runtime logs for process or exec events where a Jupyter or Enterprise Gateway process spawns a kernel with uid=0 (or requestedUID=0 in the event). Correlate the parent process identity (enterprise-gateway container) with the child UID to confirm privilege escalation within the container.

suggestion.title: Jupyter/Kernel process spawning unusual child processes post-exploitation
suggestion.rationale: After gaining root access via the vulnerability, the attacker is likely to spawn shells, system utilities, or persistence tools. The article mentions cron (T1053.003), but also implies broader post-exploitation activity (T1611 escape to host). Detection should monitor what Jupyter kernel processes do after they're created with UID 0.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor child processes spawned by Jupyter kernel processes running as root (UID 0). Flag for elevated privilege (bash, sh, cron, wget, curl, git, nc, socat, or system administration tools). Correlate process spawning with time correlation to pod creation time to attribute to this CVE.

suggestion.title: Jupyter service account role/permission escalation or RBAC bypass
suggestion.rationale: The article implies the enterprise-gateway service account is used to create pods with root privileges. This may indicate an RBAC misconfiguration or a service account with overpermissioned ClusterRole. Detection should identify if the service account lacks restrictive pod security policies or security context constraints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search Kubernetes audit logs for RoleBinding or ClusterRoleBinding events that grant the enterprise-gateway service account permissions to create pods without securityContext restrictions (e.g., 'create pods' without matching PodSecurityPolicy or restricted SecurityContextConstraint). Correlate with successful root-privilege pod creation to confirm overpermissioning.

suggestion.title: KERNEL_* Environment Variable Jinja2 Template Injection in Manifest Render
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'environment variables (`KERNEL_XXX`) used during the rendering of the Kubernetes manifest are vulnerable to Server Side Template Injection.' Pipeline should detect template syntax in KERNEL_POD_NAME, KERNEL_WORKING_DIR, KERNEL_NAMESPACE variables at pod creation time.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Kubernetes pod spec environment sections for KERNEL_* variables containing Jinja2 delimiters ({{, }}, {%, %}) or common Python introspection chains. High fidelity if restricted to Enterprise Gateway deployments; alert on first observation of template syntax in these specific variable names.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes Service Account Token Exfiltration from Container
