suggestion.rationale: Article: agent output 'may include vulnerabilities, unsafe dependencies, hardcoded secrets, or misconfigurations.' Detectable through secret scanning of generated code at commit time or artifact creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all agent-generated code artifacts for credential patterns (API keys, DB passwords, tokens) immediately post-generation. Alert on hardcoded secrets before artifact is committed or deployed. Track which secrets were exposed and downstream reuse by other agents or systems.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized API Data Access via Incremental Resource Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly details IDOR vulnerability: 'an API endpoint that takes an incrementing user ID parameter and returns user data, but when changing the user ID value it returns data from a different user, without appropriate authorization checks.' This pattern is directly observable when exploited against APIs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag API requests to object endpoints with sequential or enumerable identifiers (user_id, account_id) issued in rapid succession returning distinct user objects, especially when lacking proper authorization tokens or when observed across multiple distinct user accounts in short time windows.

suggestion.title: Bypassed Authentication Enforcement in API Handlers
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability pattern: 'We forgot to add any authentication or authorization checks; any user can request any other user's balance.' Application logs should reveal when sensitive operations execute without prior security validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor application logs for sensitive database queries or API operations executing without prior invocation of authentication/authorization validation routines, indicating security checks were omitted or short-circuited.

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Export from Registration Database - Beneficiary Records
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'gained access to personal data... names, ID numbers, phone numbers, and location information' from '600,000 Palestinian households.' This represents exfiltration of ~600k records; should detect via database audit logs, proxy egress, or application query logging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SELECT queries returning >100k rows from beneficiary tables, or large data transfers (>1GB) from WFP SRA servers to external IPs/cloud storage. Correlate with non-standard service accounts and timestamp around May 14 breach window.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to Self-Registration Application - Credential Spray
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies SRA as attack surface: 'self-registration application... was breached.' Initial compromise likely involved credential brute-force or vulnerability exploitation; should detect anomalous authentication patterns and failed-to-successful login sequences.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SRA login endpoints for rapid credential spray (>50 failed attempts → success within minutes), access from non-Gaza geolocations, or API calls to registration/beneficiary endpoints from anomalous source IPs. Flag successful logins using low-privilege or default credentials.

suggestion.title: Post-Breach Phishing Campaign Impersonating WFP
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly warns beneficiaries: 'be wary of anyone claiming to represent the World Food Programme and requesting information or money.' This threat of follow-up phishing attacks is actionable and distinct from the initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with WFP-impersonating sender domains (typosquatting wfp.org), requesting password resets or re-registration from beneficiaries, especially targeting compromised phone numbers. Correlate with known beneficiary email patterns and alert on unusual sender reputation.

suggestion.title: Administrative or Privileged Account Abuse Against Registration Platform
suggestion.rationale: Breach required database-level access to extract 600k records. Should detect privilege escalation, lateral movement from a compromised web tier to backend database, or stolen service account credentials used for administrative queries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on database access from service accounts outside normal business logic (e.g., direct SELECT * on beneficiary table), privilege escalation of compromised user accounts, or access to SRA database from unexpected source IPs. Baseline normal DBA and application queries.

suggestion.title: Web Application Vulnerability Exploitation - SRA Endpoint Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article states breach occurred on 'self-registration application.' Public-facing web applications are typical exploit vectors (SQL injection, auth bypass, RCE). Should detect exploitation attempts in WAF/IDS logs prior to or at breach timestamp.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate SQLi/path-traversal/auth-bypass payload attempts in WAF logs with database access anomalies on May 14. Focus on SRA API endpoints (`/api/registration`, `/beneficiary`, `/user`) and search for 400-499 errors followed by 200 responses indicating bypass.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Router acer_cgi.log
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'The acer_cgi.log file in the device firmware is accessible without authentication via the web interface. This file contains cleartext login credentials.' Attackers gaining unauthenticated access to this specific log file should be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP GET/POST requests to router management interface (192.168.76.1, acerconnect.com) targeting /acer_cgi.log or similar paths without prior authentication tokens. Flag failed authentication followed by successful log file access. Baseline normal admin credential rotation patterns and flag plaintext credential strings in HTTP traffic post-access.

suggestion.title: Suspicious upload.cgi Access or Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'The upload.cgi binary, responsible for processing device backups, contains a hardcoded AES encryption key. This allows an attacker to decrypt, modify, and re-encrypt system backups, facilitating persistent backdoor injection.' Access to or modification of backup files should trigger detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to upload.cgi endpoint without prior admin authentication. Monitor for backup file (.bin, .backup, .cfg) extraction or download attempts via router management interface. Detect file modification events on device backup partitions or firmware storage, especially writes that occur outside scheduled update windows.

suggestion.title: Extracted Plaintext Credentials Usage from Router
suggestion.rationale: Article states credentials in acer_cgi.log can be extracted leading to 'unauthorized system access.' Detection should flag use of router-extracted credentials for Telnet or web console access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unauthenticated log file access on router with subsequent Telnet login attempts or web console authentications from the same source IP or within minutes. Flag credential reuse across multiple sessions. Monitor for non-standard admin account creation post-backup access.

suggestion.title: Device Backup Decryption and Re-encryption Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the hardcoded key vulnerability: 'attacker to decrypt, modify, and re-encrypt system backups, facilitating persistent backdoor injection.' This cryptographic manipulation is a detection point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-entropy file writes to backup storage locations or temporary directories following upload.cgi access. Alert on unusual timing of backup extraction and upload operations (especially encryption operations on non-standard schedule). Flag attempts to read hardcoded keys from binary files or memory dumps of upload.cgi process.

suggestion.title: Remote Management Access Before Patches Released
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'Acer customers are advised to disable remote management or, if the firmware allows, restrict Internet remote access to trusted IP addresses.' Enabled remote management on unpatched routers is a significant risk indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Acer Wave 7 routers (T7c_GBL firmware versions ≤1.01.000055) with remote management enabled via port scans, vulnerability scans, or network telemetry. Alert on external IP ranges accessing router web interface before firmware patching completion (deadline: end of June 2026). Flag geographically anomalous access to router admin console.

suggestion.title: Modified FFmpeg DLL Execution from Game Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states trojanized FFmpeg DLL (SHA1: 42add9475e67a1ccc6a6af94b5475d3defc01b85) as vector: 'Since the game needs ffmpeg.dll to run properly, the library loads as soon as the user starts the game.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag FFmpeg.dll loads from game directories (RenPy, RPG Maker) and correlate with immediate Base64 PowerShell spawning. Unsigned or anomalous FFmpeg imports are high-signal.

suggestion.title: COM InprocServer32 Hijacking – Windows Color System
suggestion.rationale: Article directly names persistence: 'replacing the InprocServer32 entry for Windows Color System Calibration Loader DLL... triggered when the user logs in.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Classes\CLSID and HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Classes\Interface for InprocServer32 modifications. Alert on entries pointing outside System32 or to AppData/Temp paths.

suggestion.title: Base64-Encoded PowerShell Execution from DLL Load
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Stage1 behavior: 'natives2_blob.bin file is a DLL that executes a Base64-encoded PowerShell script when loaded.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell -EncodedCommand execution within 1-5 seconds of suspicious DLL loads. Filter on parent process originating from game/temp directories. Decode and scan for environment check commands.

suggestion.title: Delayed Multi-Stage Payload – DLL to Trojan Download
suggestion.rationale: Article describes sequential phasing: 'After a few days, the implant downloads and executes a Trojan, resulting in full system compromise.' This multi-day dwell pattern is an attack signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track processes spawned from game executables or Stage1 PowerShell that remain dormant for 3+ days before initiating outbound network connections or child process execution. Alert on secondary executable retrieval.

suggestion.title: Trojanized Game Archive – DLL + Binary Blob Combo
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies file pairing: 'archive contained fully functional, legitimate game files, as well as a modified FFmpeg DLL... that imported the DllGetClassObject function from a file called natives2_blob.bin.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor archive extraction (7z, zip, rar) to game directories. Alert on DLL + unnamed binary blob (.bin, .dat) pairings without legitimate game-engine associations. Check file creation timing clustering.

suggestion.title: Sandbox/VM Evasion Checks in PowerShell Stage1
suggestion.rationale: Article notes Stage1 'performs basic checks for controlled environments,' indicating explicit evasion logic deployed at execution time.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor encoded PowerShell for WMI queries (Win32_ComputerSystemProduct), CPUID probing, Registry checks for VM artifacts (VirtualBox, VMware, Hyper-V keys), and debugger detection. Alert on evasion-pattern clustering.

suggestion.title: Redis RCE via EVAL/EVALSHA Script Injection (CVE-2026-23479)
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CVE-2026-23479 as a Redis RCE flaw. RCE exploits unsafe Lua scripting (EVAL, EVALSHA commands) or serialization gadgets; pipeline produced no execution-phase detection for this primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor redis-server for unexpected child process creation or anomalous system calls. Flag RESP protocol frames containing EVAL, EVALSHA, or SCRIPT commands from external/untrusted sources. Correlate with shells (bash, sh, cmd.exe) spawned by redis-server PID following script execution.

suggestion.title: Inbound Network Exploitation of CVE-2026-23479
suggestion.rationale: A 2-year-old RCE flaw gaining sudden attention via autonomous AI discovery warrants network-layer detection. Pipeline missed reconnaissance and exploitation indicators targeting Redis ports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound connections to Redis port 6379 (or non-standard Redis ports) from external IPs attempting EVAL, EVALSHA, SCRIPT LOAD, or command-execution payloads within seconds of connection (before INFO/PING handshake). Correlate with known CVE-2026-23479 PoC signatures.

suggestion.title: Redis Authentication Bypass or Unauthenticated RCE
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-23479 likely involves bypassing requirepass authentication or targeting unprotected Redis instances. Pipeline did not detect AUTH evasion or code execution without credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on TCP connections to Redis (6379+) that skip AUTH entirely and immediately issue code-execution commands. Monitor for repeated AUTH failures followed by successful exploitation. Detect redis-cli or custom binaries connecting without credentials from non-admin subnets or external sources.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Lateral Movement from Compromised Redis
suggestion.rationale: Article frames flaw as 2-year-old and recently discovered, implying live exploitation risk. Impact phase should detect lateral movement after RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on redis-server spawning reverse shells, curl/wget, or known pivot/exfil tools post-compromise. Monitor for unusual process lineage: redis-server → bash → ssh/scp/nc. Detect redis-server making outbound connections to non-standard ports or C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Mirasvit CacheWarmer Serialized PHP Object Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies attack vector: 'crafted serialized PHP object in the CacheWarmer cookie.' This is a specific, observable behavioral signature requiring direct detection rule.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests containing CacheWarmer cookie values with PHP serialization prefixes (e.g., 'O:', 'C:', 'R:' indicating object/class/reference serialization). Flag unauthenticated requests from external sources with serialized payloads to Mirasvit endpoints.

suggestion.title: Mirasvit CVE-2026-45247 Unauthenticated RCE Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated attackers' achieving 'remote code execution'—this zero-auth RCE combination warrants distinct detection correlating HTTP exploitation attempts with post-exploit process execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP POST/GET requests to Mirasvit endpoints lacking authentication headers with subsequent child process spawning from web server/PHP parent processes. Monitor for shell execution, reverse shells, or suspicious command execution immediately following CacheWarmer cookie requests.

suggestion.title: Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer Exposed Asset Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entries target actively exploited vulnerabilities on exposed systems. Article names 'Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer' as product—requires inventory scan matching federal patch deadline (2026-06-06).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query network telemetry and vulnerability scanner results for Mirasvit Full Page Cache Warmer installations. Match on application fingerprints (HTTP response headers, cookies, server banners), cross-reference with CVE-2026-45247 patch status, flag unpatched instances on internet-facing systems.

suggestion.title: PHP Untrusted Deserialization Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability class 'deserialization of untrusted data' is a known PHP exploitation vector beyond this CVE. Generic signature detection captures variants and related exploitation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP traffic for PHP object serialization patterns in POST bodies, query strings, and cookie headers. Alert on serialized objects with gadget chain indicators or suspicious class instantiation attempts in requests to public-facing endpoints.

suggestion.title: Android CVE-2025-48595 Privilege Escalation (No User Interaction)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'high-severity integer overflow vulnerability in the Android Framework' affecting Android 14-16 with 'requires no user interaction to exploit' enabling privilege escalation. Pipeline generated zero Android exploitation detections despite active exploitation implied.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Android processes for unexpected system call sequences, integer boundary violations in framework calls, or privilege transitions (UID/GID changes) without corresponding user interaction events (input, gesture, IME). Flag suspicious behavior from apps targeting Android 14-16 with kernel-level permissions.

suggestion.title: Container Escape via CVE-2022-0492 cgroup v1 Namespace Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability where 'local attacker to bypass namespace isolation, escalate privileges, and potentially escape from a container to gain root-level access on the host system' affecting cgroups v1. This is a critical container-escape vector with zero detection rules generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect writes to cgroup_release_agent files from processes running in container namespaces, or privilege escalation (UID 0 transitions) from unprivileged container processes. Alert on host processes spawned with parent PID originating from container process namespace.

suggestion.title: cgroup_release_agent_write() Function Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article pinpoints 'cgroup_release_agent_write()' function in cgroups v1 with 'insufficient authentication checks' as exploitation vector. Specific function name and mechanism provided but zero technical detection rules derived.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for write() syscalls targeting /proc/*/cgroup or cgroup filesystem paths, specifically writes to cgroup.event_control or release_agent paths from non-root processes. Correlate with subsequent shell command execution in unrelated process context (escaping container namespace).

suggestion.title: Unpatched Linux Kernel Host Privilege Escalation (CVE-2022-0492 Versions)
suggestion.rationale: Article lists specific vulnerable kernel branches (2.6-4.20, 5.5-5.17) and patched versions (4.9.301+, 5.15.20+, etc.), enabling version-based risk scoring and behavioral thresholds. Pipeline failed to create version-aware detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Fingerprint kernel version from running host. For unpatched versions matching 5.5-5.17 or 2.6-4.20 ranges, lower detection thresholds for privilege escalation and container-escape behavioral patterns. Flag any suspicious cgroup manipulation on known-vulnerable kernels as high-confidence.

suggestion.title: Android 14-16 Framework Exploitation (Patch Levels 2026-06-01, 2026-06-05)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'June 2026 security patches (2026-06-01 and 2026-06-05 security patch levels)' as remediation. Pipeline missed opportunity to correlate unpatched device inventory with exploitation detection thresholds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Android 14-16 devices running patch levels prior to 2026-06-01 (or 2026-06-05 for specific variants) exhibiting privilege escalation activity, integer overflow symptoms in framework logs, or unexpected system capability acquisition.

suggestion.title: Jupyter Enterprise Gateway /api/kernels POST request with KERNEL_UID or KERNEL_GID in request body
suggestion.rationale: Article states bypass is 'possible to launch kernels with a prohibited UID and/or GID by using a specially crafted KERNEL_UID or KERNEL_GID value.' The hunts provided lack parameter-level specificity; should detect the actual malicious parameters, not just all POST requests to the endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to /api/kernels endpoint where request body contains KERNEL_UID=0, KERNEL_GID=0, or non-numeric bypass-attempt patterns. Correlate with subsequent pod creation as root to confirm exploitation.

suggestion.title: Kernel pod created with SYS_ADMIN or host-escape capabilities from enterprise-gateway SA
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1611 (Escape to Host) but provided hunts detect post-escape persistence, not the escape capability acquisition itself. Article narrative emphasizes container privilege context; should detect pods requesting CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_NET_ADMIN, or CAP_SYS_PTRACE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect pod creation in k8s_audit where requestObject.spec.containers[].securityContext.capabilities.add contains SYS_ADMIN, NET_ADMIN, or SYS_PTRACE, AND created by enterprise-gateway service account, AND correlates with prior /api/kernels POST.

suggestion.title: Enterprise Gateway pod escapes containment: process execution in host namespace or privileged mode
suggestion.rationale: Article technique T1611 and UC_33_3 describe escape path via hostPath volumes; should also detect active escape indicators such as container processes escaping to host PID/network namespace or requesting privileged mode.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for container processes (InitiatingProcessParentFileName in runc/containerd) executing commands outside container namespace or accessing /proc/[pid]/ns/net from host. Alternatively, detect pod creation with hostNetwork=true AND hostPID=true AND hostIPC=true.

suggestion.title: Forensic: Jupyter kernel pod environment variable inspection for KERNEL_UID bypass evidence
suggestion.rationale: Article describes bypass using 'specially crafted KERNEL_UID or KERNEL_GID value'; this would be preserved in pod spec and describe API request logs. Pipeline should suggest detection of env vars containing escape-bypass payloads or unusual UID/GID values in kernel pod configs post-creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query k8s_audit audit logs for pod creation events where spec.containers[].env[] contains KERNEL_UID or KERNEL_GID with non-standard values or special characters suggesting bypass attempt. Cross-reference with securityContext.runAsUser in same pod spec.

suggestion.title: UC_32_1: Jinja2 SSTI payload to Jupyter Enterprise Gateway /api/kernels
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'environment variables (KERNEL_XXX) used during the rendering of the Kubernetes manifest are vulnerable to Server Side Template Injection'—pipeline extracted zero use cases despite article providing complete Splunk SPL and Defender KQL for this exploit-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to /api/kernels endpoints for Jinja2 template markers ({{ }}, {%...%}) combined with Python introspection patterns (__globals__, __class__, __mro__, __builtins__, cycler.__init__) or OS command methods (os.popen, os.system, subprocess). Correlate by source IP and track timing for incident attribution.

suggestion.title: UC_32_2: Enterprise Gateway service account creates privileged/hostPath/RBAC-escalating Kubernetes resources
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'can use or steal the Kubernetes service account token'—post-exploitation phase where the compromised gateway pivots to K8s API abuse is explicitly described in article's recommended hunts but pipeline surfaced zero detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag pod, rolebinding, or clusterrolebinding creation/modification by the enterprise-gateway service account where manifests contain privileged: true, hostPath mounts, hostNetwork: true, or hostPID: true. Alert on RBAC modifications that escalate the service account's own permissions.

suggestion.title: UC_32_3: Enterprise Gateway Python process spawns shell or reads Kubernetes service-account token
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Python code execution via SSTI 'can use or steal the Kubernetes service account token'—RCE post-compromise child process and credential access are essential detections but pipeline produced zero process-level hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes (sh, bash, curl, wget, kubectl, nc) spawned under python/python3 parents, or any process reading /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token. Filter to containers with 'enterprise-gateway', 'jupyter', or 'jeg' in name. High-fidelity indicator of SSTI→RCE chain completion.

suggestion.title: Jinja2 SSTI attempt blocked or logged in WAF/API gateway (pre-exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies KERNEL_XXX environment variables as the injection point—intermediate detection of Jinja2 syntax in request payloads before reaching the templating engine provides defense-in-depth and earliest possible alerting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to Enterprise Gateway endpoints containing Jinja2 filter chains known to bypass sandbox isolation (e.g., cycler, lipsum). Baseline legitimate API schema against malicious payload patterns. Track blocked attempts separately from detected-but-allowed; the latter indicates WAF misconfiguration.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes service account token read or exfiltration from container (post-RCE)
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes that stolen tokens are 'powerful' for cluster escalation—detection of the token being read from disk or transmitted over network post-compromise is not explicitly covered in article hunts despite being critical for incident response.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for reads of /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token from non-privileged processes or processes not in the control plane. Correlate with outbound network traffic patterns (exfil). Track Kubernetes API calls authenticated with the enterprise-gateway service account from unusual source IPs or with verb/resource patterns abnormal for Enterprise Gateway workload.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes manifest with injected YAML delimiters in KERNEL_* environment
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'environment variables used during the rendering of the Kubernetes manifest allow YAML injection' and 'inject multi-document YAML.' Detection should hunt for KERNEL_* variables containing YAML document separators (--- or ...) or securityContext keys.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search Kubernetes API audit logs and Enterprise Gateway container logs for POST requests to /api/kernels where request body or environment variables contain KERNEL_* parameters with YAML delimiters (---, ...) or securityContext field references. Correlate with pod creation from the enterprise-gateway service account within seconds.

suggestion.title: Jinja2 template rendering exceptions or YAML parse failures in Jupyter Enterprise Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Malicious YAML injection may trigger template parsing errors or YAML parsing exceptions. Article describes interpolation of 'untrusted environment variables' into manifests—failed parsing is a sign of attack attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Jinja2 TemplateError, YAML ParserError, or manifest validation failures in Enterprise Gateway pod logs correlating with /api/kernels POST requests within the same time window. High precision if combined with URL pattern match.

suggestion.title: Multi-document Kubernetes manifests created by enterprise-gateway service account
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers can 'inject multi-document YAML to create additional unintended Kubernetes resources.' This is the actual impact—creation of extra pods or resources beyond the intended one.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Kubernetes API for create/patch operations on pods, deployments, or daemonsets from the enterprise-gateway service account where the manifest contains multiple YAML documents (detectable via '---' separators in requestObject). Anomaly: single API call producing multiple child resources.

suggestion.title: Suspicious securityContext escalation in pod specs from Jupyter Enterprise Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Article describes overwriting securityContext to enable privilege escalation. Detect pods created by EG with privileged:true, runAsUser:0, runAsGroup:0, hostNetwork:true, or hostPID:true—especially if these differ from prior baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Kubernetes audit logs for pod creation from enterprise-gateway service account where securityContext.privileged=true, securityContext.runAsUser=0, or hostNetwork=true. Cross-reference against enterprise-gateway's normal pod specs in the same namespace to detect deviations.

suggestion.title: Escape-to-host indicators from Jupyter Enterprise Gateway pods
suggestion.rationale: T1611 is mapped in the article but no hunt directly targets container escape. Exploit creates privileged pods that can attempt escape. Monitor for suspicious host filesystem access, privileged syscalls, or kernel module loading from EG pod context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for privileged pods created by enterprise-gateway attempting to mount host paths (/proc, /sys, /dev, /host), execute privileged operations (iptables, insmod), or issue escape-related syscalls (clone with CLONE_NEWNS/CLONE_NEWPID). Pair with pod-creation audit events.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-44182 vulnerability scan results or patch-gap assessment
suggestion.rationale: Primary recon-phase indicator: enumerate hosts running vulnerable Jupyter Enterprise Gateway versions. Article CVE and version information enable asset-scoped detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scan results, container image inventories, and application inventory for Jupyter Enterprise Gateway versions prior to the patched release. Cross-reference image digests and pod specs in audit logs to confirm runtime exposure.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with Malicious Link to TA4922 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Phishing Attacks' as attack vector; no use case generated despite this being primary initial access method for TA4922.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound emails with suspicious links pointing to TA4922-attributed domains or IP infrastructure. Look for sender spoofing patterns matching targets in UK, Germany, Italy, South Africa regions, and URL rewrite/redirect patterns common in phishing campaigns.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Phishing Landing Page
suggestion.rationale: Phishing attacks typically culminate in credential theft; article describes 'expanded' campaign suggesting credential harvesting intent, but no detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST requests to credential harvesting landing pages mimicking legitimate services targeted at the four countries. Detect form submissions with username/password pairs to suspicious infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Malware Payload Delivery Post-Click
suggestion.rationale: Article title mentions 'expands' phishing attacks; multi-stage phishing with secondary payload (malware) is standard TA4922 progression, but no malware-related detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect downloads and execution of suspicious files from phishing redirects, focusing on Office macro-enabled documents, ISO/IMG archives, or obfuscated scripts common in TA4922 campaigns targeting regional targets.

suggestion.title: TA4922 Domain Registration Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: No IOCs extracted despite article clearly identifying threat actor TA4922; domain infrastructure and registration patterns are foundational IOCs missing entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries and registrations of domains matching TA4922 known patterns (homoglyphs, typosquatting legitimate UK/German/Italian/South African entities). Cross-reference against passive DNS and WHOIS history.

suggestion.title: Geographic Targeting Signal - Regional Language Phishing Content
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names four target countries (UK, Germany, Italy, South Africa); no geo-specific detection generated to identify localized phishing content.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate incoming phishing emails with language/locale indicators, business entity spoofing, and currency/regulatory references specific to UK (GBP, FCA), Germany (EUR, BaFin), Italy (EUR, Consob), South Africa (ZAR, FSCA). Flag campaigns targeting all four simultaneously as high-confidence TA4922 indicator.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20230 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Exploit Code Goes Public' — direct signal of weaponized threat and imminent exploitation attempts against Cisco Unified CM. Pipeline generated zero detection use cases despite CRIT severity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Cisco Unified CM admin interfaces (ports 8080, 8443) for payloads matching CVE-2026-20230 signatures. Alert on HTTP 400/500 error sequences following suspicious parameter injection to known vulnerable endpoints.

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM Admin Account Persistence Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Exploit Code Goes Public' implies widespread exploitation and attacker persistence attempts. Pipeline missed persistence-phase detection for unauthorized admin account creation in Unified CM.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Unified CM audit logs for unexpected admin/super-user account creation outside change-control windows. Alert on privilege grants within 1 hour of detected exploitation attempts or reconnaissance activity against Unified CM.

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM Patch Status Verification
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Cisco Patches CVE-2026-20230' — explicit signal to track patching status. Pipeline failed to generate detection use case for patch deployment verification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Cisco Unified CM versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-20230 (versions prior to patch release date). Flag unpatched instances in production environments. Monitor version strings for obfuscation or timestamp manipulation.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance Scanning for Cisco Unified CM Instances
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Exploit Code Goes Public' establishes scanning phase precedes exploitation. Pipeline generated zero discovery-phase detections despite clear attacker motivation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect port scans targeting TCP 8080/8443 from external/untrusted sources. Alert on HTTP/HTTPS probes to /ccmadmin, /admin endpoints. Track scanning patterns consistent with Unified CM enumeration (multiple targets, repeated similar probes).

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM Configuration and Voicemail Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Exploit Code Goes Public' establishes breach probability and attacker incentive to exfiltrate sensitive voice/config data. Pipeline did not model exfiltration-phase behaviors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound SFTP/SCP/HTTP transfers from Cisco Unified CM servers to external IPs. Alert on backup/export command execution (mysqldump, tar, database exports) outside scheduled maintenance. Track large data transfers containing voice files or XML configurations.

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM Remote Code Execution via Web Application
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-20230 type vulnerabilities involve web RCE. Title establishes code execution as primary attack vector; pipeline missed execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process spawning from Cisco Unified CM application processes (Java/Tomcat). Alert on shell invocation (bash, cmd, powershell) from Unified CM service account. Correlate HTTP admin-interface access with child process creation events.

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM SSRF HTTP Request Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted HTTP request to an affected device.' WebDialer endpoints should be monitored for anomalous HTTP patterns and SSRF indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Cisco Unified CM WebDialer service endpoints for SSRF patterns (requests targeting internal addresses, unusual URIs, or suspicious headers). Focus on requests that deviate from normal dialer workflows (non-standard query strings, file:// URIs, local service probes).

suggestion.title: WebDialer Service File Write Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'A successful exploit could allow the attacker to write files to the underlying operating system that could be used later to elevate to root.' File creation by the WebDialer service should be monitored for suspicious paths and timing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation or modification by the Cisco WebDialer process (or its child processes) in sensitive OS directories (/etc, /root, /var/spool/cron, system startup folders). Alert on files that map to known privilege-escalation vectors or have suspicious ownership changes.

suggestion.title: Root Privilege Escalation via Cisco Unified CM
suggestion.rationale: Article states privilege escalation outcome: 'A successful exploit could...elevate to root.' Escalation events following WebDialer activity should be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for privilege escalation attempts (UID 0 or root group assignment) initiated by or correlated with Cisco Unified CM processes. Alert on sudo/su calls, capability escalations, or setuid binary execution that follow anomalous WebDialer HTTP activity within a short time window.

suggestion.title: WebDialer Service Enablement Indicator
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'Luckily, the vulnerability only impacts systems where the WebDialer service is enabled, and WebDialer is disabled by default.' Detection should flag when WebDialer is enabled, as it signals exposure to CVE-2026-20230.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag service enablement events for Cisco WebDialer (via service-activation logs or service-start events) as an exposure indicator. Correlate with vulnerability scanning or configuration management logs to identify at-risk systems.

suggestion.title: Malicious GitHub Issue Triggers Unauthorized Action Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'One Malicious Issue Hijack Repositories' — the attack chain starts with issue creation as entry point to trigger Claude Code action with elevated privileges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub issues created by new/external accounts immediately followed by unexpected GitHub Actions workflow execution within seconds. Correlate issue creation timestamp with action trigger timestamp; flag if payload in issue body contains shell metacharacters or command syntax.

suggestion.title: Repository Hijacking via Unauthorized Push from GitHub Action Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Title promise: 'Hijack Repositories' implies attacker achieves unauthorized commits/merges to main branch via compromised action context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag commits pushed to protected branches (main/master) by GitHub Actions service account outside approved workflow files. Detect if commit author differs from expected pipeline user or if push references were modified after initial issue/PR creation.

suggestion.title: GitHub Action Workflow File Injection via Issue Body
suggestion.rationale: Attack likely exploits unsanitized issue content to modify or create .github/workflows files, enabling persistence or lateral execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor commits that add or modify files in .github/workflows/ directory triggered within action execution context started by a GitHub issue. Alert if workflow files contain inline bash/PowerShell from issue body parameters without escaping/validation.

suggestion.title: GitHub Token Exposure via Action Environment Variable Leakage
suggestion.rationale: Malicious issue content may force action to echo or log the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable, exposing repository credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GitHub token values appearing in action logs or stdout post-execution. Cross-reference token patterns against known service account tokens; flag if token subsequently used for unexpected API calls (force-push, secret modification, workflow deletion).

suggestion.title: Repository Secrets Modification via Compromised Action Context
suggestion.rationale: Once action context is hijacked, attacker can modify repository secrets, adding persistent backdoor credentials or removing security-critical PATs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on repository secrets create/update events originating from GitHub Actions execution context, especially outside business hours or from unexpected workflows. Detect if new secrets are added with names resembling backup tokens or deployment keys.

suggestion.title: Large Data Exfiltration from Healthcare Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'stolen more than 234 GB of data'. No exfiltration detection use case generated despite this being the attack's signature artifact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag bulk data transfers from DentaQuest/Sun Life systems exceeding baseline thresholds to external IPs or cloud storage. Prioritize transfers containing PII patterns (health insurance IDs, SSNs, medical record numbers) outside business hours.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Database Access and PII Collection
suggestion.rationale: 2.6 million patient records accessed with enumerated PII fields (email, name, phone, government ID, insurance info, DOB, gender). No collection-phase detection for bulk database queries despite this being the exfiltration source.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor database logs for bulk SELECT operations against patient/member tables accessing PII columns in aggregate. Flag CSV exports, SQL dumps, or ODBC extractions from medical admin systems outside scheduled backup windows.

suggestion.title: Data Leak Site Monitoring and Extortion Communication
suggestion.rationale: Threat actor 'listed the company on its data leak site' and 'failure to reach an agreement...the data was publicly leaked'. No monitoring use cases for breach site postings or extortion demands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Automated daily scanning of known data leak boards, ransomware sites, and breach databases for organization name, executive mentions, or domain hits. Alert on extortion emails matching threat actor communication templates within 48 hours of breach detection.

suggestion.title: Initial Access and Lateral Movement to Admin Network
suggestion.rationale: DentaQuest statement: 'unauthorized access to a limited portion of our network'. No characterization of compromise vector or lateral movement paths in kill chain or detection use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Retrospective hunt for anomalous authentication, failed exploitation attempts, or unusual network flows in weeks preceding June 2 disclosure. Flag unusual VPN source geographies, credential-spray patterns, or web application probe attempts.

suggestion.title: Compromised Service Account Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Access to 2.6M patient records including government IDs requires elevated database read permissions; no detection use case for credential compromise or service account abuse during data transfer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk successful authentications from anomalous sources preceding large data transfers. Flag service accounts (reporting, analytics, admin) being used outside normal business hours or from unexpected geographic locations.

suggestion.title: Ongoing Data Breach Exposure and Credential Reuse Risk
suggestion.rationale: '66% of the exposed records were present in its database from past incidents'—indicates DentaQuest customer data already in dark web repositories. No proactive dark web monitoring or credential-reuse alerting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Integrate HIBP, darknet feeds, and breach database monitoring to alert when organization or employee data appears in public searchable breach collections. Correlate leaked credentials against company email domains for account compromise risk.

suggestion.title: Malware Download from Typosquatted Open-Source Tool Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article core narrative: 'Fake Sites Mimicking Open-Source Tools...Deliver Malware.' Pipeline generated zero delivery-phase detection. Users will download executables/scripts from domains impersonating tools (Python, Node, npm, Rust, etc.)—this is the attack climax and should anchor at least one detection rule.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP(S) file downloads from domains morphing legitimate open-source tool names (edit distance ≤2 from canonical name, e.g. pytohn, npmjs-official, cargo-rs). Flag .exe, .msi, .zip, .tar.gz, .ps1 downloads. Baseline against expected package-manager traffic; alert on anomalies and sandbox-detonation positives.

suggestion.title: Traffic Direction System (TDS) Redirection Chain Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names TDS as delivery mechanism: 'Deliver Malware via TDS.' Pipeline failed to surface TDS as a technique or detection angle. TDS exhibits characteristic behavior: single request → conditional redirect chain → malware/exploit-kit. No detection whatsoever despite this being the mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify TDS-like patterns: HTTP(S) GET to typosquatted domain returns 302/307 redirect to multiple distinct IPs/ASNs within 2–5 seconds, with final destination hosting malware family or exploit kit signature. Correlate redirect chain termination with suspicious content types (PE headers, shellcode patterns) or detonation alerts.

suggestion.title: Google Search Result Click to Impersonated Tool Site
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Rank High on Google to Deliver Malware.' SEO poisoning is the lure; users arrive via legitimate search. Pipeline did not model initial-access via search-referrer clicks to suspicious domains. This is the user-facing attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on clicks originating from search.google.com, bing.com, etc., landing on domains with high string similarity to open-source tool names. Cross-check domain age (WHOIS), SSL trust history (CT logs), and reputation. Combine with subsequent malware/exploit-kit detections on that domain within 30 seconds.

suggestion.title: Process Execution from Downloaded Malware (Impersonated Tool)
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain concludes with execution of malware delivered via fake tool sites. Pipeline generated zero execution-phase use cases despite this being essential to the attack's impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor execution of processes spawned from files downloaded from typosquatted tool domains. Baseline expected parent-child relationships for legitimate tools; flag anomalies (e.g., npm spawning cmd.exe, cargo spawning rundll32). Include network I/O and child-process execution for C2 indicators.

suggestion.title: Newly Registered Typosquatted Open-Source Tool Domain
suggestion.rationale: Attack infrastructure precondition: register fake domains mimicking tools (Python, Node, Go, etc.). Pipeline did not suggest proactive domain-registration monitoring or CT log hunting for lookalike TLDs or morphed names.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest CT logs and WHOIS feeds to identify newly-registered domains with high edit distance to popular open-source tool names. Flag typos (pytohn, npmjs-registry), homoglyphs (0→O, 1→l), and suspicious TLDs (.xyz, .top, .click). Cross-reference with malware families and passive DNS sinkhole activity.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Redirect Chain from Search Result to Exploit Kit
suggestion.rationale: Full attack flow: Google search → fake tool site → TDS redirection → malware delivery. Pipeline did not create a composite detection spanning search referrer + suspicious redirect + exploit-kit indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate three signals within 10 seconds: (1) HTTP Referer from search engine, (2) request to typosquatted tool domain, (3) 30x redirect to infrastructure associated with known malware or exploit kits. Build correlation rule across proxy and network logs; alert on high-confidence hits.

suggestion.title: Executable Download from Ad-Network Domain to Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'spreads...via Malicious Google and YouTube Ads'; pipeline did not identify initial-access detection for ad-click-driven payload delivery, the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect executable or DMG downloads originating from Google Ads redirect chains or YouTube domains; correlate with script execution or process launch from browser contexts or temporary download directories on macOS.

suggestion.title: Process Execution from Browser Parent on macOS
suggestion.rationale: Malicious ads are clicked by users, triggering downloads and execution; pipeline missed execution-phase detection for browser-spawned processes, a primary infection mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process launch with parent Safari, Chrome, or Firefox; particularly sensitive to child processes named pkg, dmg, or shell scripts, or processes executing from /tmp or ~/Downloads.

suggestion.title: macOS Launch Agent Persistence by FlutterShell
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor malware always establishes persistence for callback capability; title implies active spread requiring sustained access, but pipeline omitted persistence-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file creation/modification in ~/Library/LaunchAgents and /Library/LaunchDaemons following executable download or installation from ad networks; correlate with suspicious plist content pointing to temporary or obfuscated executable paths.

suggestion.title: FlutterShell C2 Callback Detection
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor name in title establishes command-and-control phase; pipeline extracted zero network IOCs or C2 behavioral signatures despite this being core malware functionality.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound network connections from newly-installed processes on macOS to non-standard ports or known FlutterShell C2 domains; flag connections initiated within minutes of suspicious installer execution.

suggestion.title: Unsigned macOS Installer Execution
suggestion.rationale: Ad-delivered malware typically circumvents code-signing; pipeline failed to generate detection for unsigned executables from web-origin sources on macOS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution of unsigned or self-signed binaries delivered via HTTP/HTTPS from non-App Store sources, particularly when downloaded and executed within short time window on macOS.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance Process Execution Post-Infection
suggestion.rationale: Backdoors perform discovery after installation (process enumeration, system profiling); article title implies FlutterShell establishes active persistence, but pipeline missed discovery-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of ps, system_profiler, or file enumeration commands (find, ls, stat) shortly after suspicious installer or process launch from browser context on macOS.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated request to AVideo YPTSocket plugin endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Unauthenticated remote attacker' with 'Exploit Public-Facing Application (T1190)'. Initial access phase requires detection of unauthenticated access to the vulnerable endpoint before payload delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to /plugin/YPTSocket/ endpoints that do not carry valid authentication tokens or session cookies. Establish baseline of authenticated vs. unauthenticated access patterns. Flag spikes in unauthenticated requests, especially with query parameters (webSocketSelfURI, page_title).

suggestion.title: Stored DOM XSS payload in YPTSocket WebSocket broadcast metadata
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Stored DOM Cross-Site Scripting via Per-Client Metadata Broadcast'. Requires detection within the WebSocket layer or broadcast inspection, not just HTTP GET/POST parameters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WebSocket traffic to /plugin/YPTSocket/ for page_title metadata containing HTML event handlers (onerror, onload, onclick) or script tags in broadcast frames. Alert on payload persistence across multiple client connections, indicating storage in backend.

suggestion.title: Administrator session hijacking via XSS cookie exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'execute arbitrary JavaScript in the authenticated origin of every administrator currently viewing'. Requires detection of abnormal admin session behavior post-XSS, including impossible travel, lateral movement, or credential access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for admin-authenticated sessions that suddenly access endpoints from new IP/geolocation, or for extraction of sensitive admin operations occurring outside normal admin behavior windows. Flag re-use of admin session tokens in unusual contexts (e.g., automated API calls vs. interactive web sessions).

suggestion.title: Everest Forms Plugin Exploitation Attempt — CVE-2026-3300
suggestion.rationale: Article states hackers are 'actively exploiting' but pipeline generated zero hunts for exploitation traffic itself. Attackers must send crafted requests to vulnerable plugin endpoints—requires HTTP request pattern detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web server logs for HTTP requests to Everest Forms plugin paths (*/wp-content/plugins/everest-forms/*) with anomalous payloads, parameter injection attempts, or rapid fuzzing patterns from single source IPs. Flag unauthenticated requests attempting to bypass form validation or exploit known parameter injection vectors.

suggestion.title: Malicious PHP File Creation in Web Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'inject and execute arbitrary PHP code' and 'malicious PHP code injection'—this directly implies post-exploitation file creation. Pipeline generated no detection for web shell or backdoor deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect .php file creation or modification in web directories (wp-content/plugins, DocumentRoot, /var/www) with timestamps matching or shortly following successful exploitation attempts. Correlate parent process (apache, nginx, php-fpm, www-data) with anomalous file ownership or executable flags.

suggestion.title: Web Process Spawning System Commands
suggestion.rationale: RCE payload execution—'execute arbitrary PHP code' necessitates runtime detection. Attacker-injected PHP will spawn child processes for interactive shell or reconnaissance—no process-level detection in pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on web server processes (apache, nginx, php-fpm) or CGI-spawned children launching shell interpreters (bash, sh, cmd, powershell) or utilities (curl, wget, nc, find) outside normal maintenance windows. Parent process must be web daemon; process arguments containing shell metacharacters or network operations = high confidence.

suggestion.title: PHP Shell Command Execution via HTTP
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation—attacker controls injected code and uses it for command execution. Article's 'malicious PHP code' implies web shell interaction via HTTP POST/GET, but pipeline found no web request pattern detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to suspicious .php files (created in recent days, owned by web process, in unexpected locations) containing parameters matching web shell execution patterns (cmd=, exec=, system=, base64 payloads). Alert on POST requests followed by process creation or file writes by web daemon.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Form Submission Spike to Everest Forms
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability requires no authentication—article explicitly states 'unauthenticated attackers.' Pipeline missed baseline/anomaly hunt for form endpoint access, which is the attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate unauthenticated POST/GET requests to Everest Forms submission endpoints. Alert on spike in volume, unique source IPs, geographic anomalies, or requests from IP ranges known for vulnerability scanning. Pair with User-Agent analysis (curl, wget, scanners).

suggestion.title: Plugin Reconnaissance and Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'widespread' exploitation, implying active scanning phase. Pipeline reported 'Kill chain phases observed: none detected'—missed entire reconnaissance phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for requests to common WordPress plugin enumeration paths (wp-content/plugins/everest-forms/readme.txt, plugin metadata queries, HEAD requests to static assets). Flag high-frequency requests from single IPs, automated scanner signatures (nmap, nikto, metasploit), or bulk parameter fuzzing.

suggestion.title: Unusual OWA Login Location and Bulk Mailbox Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states hackers maintained access for five months—requires sustained remote session or token reuse. 'Spied on a Stock Exchange Executive's Outlook Mailbox for Five Months' establishes collection phase involving email monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on OWA logins from geographically impossible locations or high-risk IPs, followed within minutes by bulk mailbox search/read operations. Correlate login IP reputation and user's historical login geography.

suggestion.title: Email Forwarding Rule Added to External Account
suggestion.rationale: 'Spied on...for Five Months' implies sustained exfiltration of messages. Email forwarding is standard persistence technique for mailbox surveillance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Mailbox_Audit log for SMTP forwarding rule additions targeting external domains. Alert if rule created by non-owner principal or outside normal admin workflow.

suggestion.title: Credential Compromise via Phishing or Session Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates successful mailbox compromise; initial access vector not specified. Five-month dwell suggests weak detection. Common vectors: phishing, brute force, OAuth token theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful logins to executive's account from non-corporate IP ranges or suspicious ISPs. Flag if login is followed immediately by forwarding rule changes, delegate additions, or bulk data access with no subsequent legitimate user activity.

suggestion.title: Mailbox Delegate Access Grant to Attacker-Controlled Account
suggestion.rationale: Five-month persistence window unlikely via password alone; attackers typically add delegate access or linked mailbox accounts for sustained access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on mailbox delegation grants to unfamiliar service principals or guest accounts. Cross-reference against approved delegation list and check if granted by non-admin user.

suggestion.title: Anomalous IMAP/POP3 Access to Cloud Mailbox
suggestion.rationale: Sustained mailbox monitoring for five months may involve legacy protocols. 'Hackers Spied on...Outlook Mailbox' suggests repeated access, consistent with IMAP archival or syncing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for IMAP/POP3 logins to O365 mailbox from non-standard clients or multiple simultaneous connections. Alert on IMAP access from VPN/proxy IP ranges or countries outside normal baseline.

suggestion.title: Insider Threat Signal: High-Value Target Account Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Stock exchange executive is high-value target for espionage or insider trading. Title specifies this targeting: 'Hackers Spied on a Stock Exchange Executive.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain lower alert thresholds for credentials of high-value financial targets (executives, traders, compliance officers). Flag any login anomaly, unusual country origin, or failed MFA events for immediate investigation.

suggestion.title: Base64-Encoded PowerShell via cmd.exe Spawn
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly documents: 'cmd.exe process spawning powershell.exe with an -EncodedCommand parameter containing a Base64-encoded payload.' Unambiguous execution pattern with low false-positive rate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cmd.exe spawning powershell.exe with -EncodedCommand flag. Log decoding of base64 payload. High-confidence indicator when immediately followed by Invoke-WebRequest or outbound network connection to known-bad ASN.

suggestion.title: Invoke-WebRequest Download to ApplicationData with Cleanup
suggestion.rationale: Article documents payload fetch: 'The decoded payload executing Invoke-WebRequest to fetch a file named script.ps1, dropping it into the user's ApplicationData directory' followed by 'Post-execution cleanup via Remove-Item, attempting to delete traces.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Invoke-WebRequest or similar download cmdlet from PowerShell targeting ApplicationData or temp paths. Flag subsequent Remove-Item targeting the same directory within 5-minute window. Combine with outbound network context for validation.

suggestion.title: curl.exe Process Communicating to Known C2 with Network Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'A separate curl.exe process making requests to the same C2 infrastructure the firewall had flagged.' Demonstrates process-to-IP correlation across EDR and firewall domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline curl.exe usage per environment and user context. Cross-validate EDR process execution with firewall connection logs to confirm curl connecting to known C2 ASNs or malicious IPs (144.31.221.82 and similar).

suggestion.title: MSIEXEC User-Agent to Suspicious ASN (Living-Off-Land)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'MSIEXEC User-Agent making connections to suspicious or malicious ASNs. MSIEXEC fetching remote packages is a known living-off-the-land (LOTL) technique. The user-agent string persists in firewall connection logs even when the payload itself is encrypted.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP User-Agent headers containing 'MSIEXEC' in firewall logs making outbound connections. Correlate destination ASN reputation with threat intel feeds. Low false-positive rate; MSIEXEC HTTP requests rare in legitimate environments.

suggestion.title: Python User-Agent to Malicious ASN Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'Python User-Agent connections to malicious ASN infrastructure. Legitimate Python HTTP requests exist in most environments, but Python calling out to hosting providers with poor reputation scores is a different signal entirely.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of Python HTTP clients (User-Agent matching 'python-*' or 'python/*') per environment. Flag connections to ASNs with known C2 hosting history or poor reputation. Use threat intel feeds to identify high-risk autonomous systems.

suggestion.title: TDS Redirect Pattern Detection via Firewall URL Path
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies: 'Cisco Secure Firewall telemetry recorded outbound ConnectionEvents to "144.31.221.82" on port 6060, with a URL path of /capcha9856. This pattern is consistent with a Traffic Direction System (TDS) infection, where a compromised website redirects visitors through a chain of intermediate servers.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections with suspicious URL paths (captcha, verification, check, etc.) to non-standard ports (e.g., 6060). Cross-reference source with known-compromised website traffic or ad-tech redirect chains. Correlate with subsequent payload delivery.

suggestion.title: NPM Post-Install Script Execution with File Writes to System Paths
suggestion.rationale: Article describes npm package attack that spreads via binding.gyp during install. Pipeline missed: npm install / postinstall script triggering abnormal file writes or process execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution spawned during npm install operations (node, npm parent) that write to system directories, create executables, or establish network connections outside expected package manager repos. Flag when post-install scripts invoke shell commands or spawn processes not typical for the declared package.

suggestion.title: Suspicious binding.gyp Execution in node_modules
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector explicitly uses binding.gyp (node-gyp build manifest). Pipeline failed to flag: gyp build system executing arbitrary code during dependency installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on node-gyp or python build processes spawned from node_modules with unusual command-line arguments, obfuscated payloads, or outbound network activity. Correlate binding.gyp file modifications with process execution in the same parent package.

suggestion.title: Self-Propagating Package Dependency Modification
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates 'self-spreading worm'—attack replicates to other packages. Pipeline missed: detection of package.json or package-lock.json writes that inject new dependencies or version bumps during build.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file modifications to package.json or package-lock.json initiated by post-install or build processes, especially additions of transitive dependencies or pinned versions not declared in the original manifest. Cross-reference with npm registry queries to identify non-existent or newly-registered malicious packages.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Network Activity from npm/Build Processes
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks typically exfiltrate data or phone home. Pipeline produced no detection for command & control or data exfiltration during npm operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DNS queries or HTTPS connections initiated by npm, node, or build processes to domains not in the npm registry allowlist. Alert on non-standard ports, TLS-only obfuscation, or connections to newly-registered domains queried during post-install execution.

suggestion.title: Package Manifest Tampering and Duplicate Registration
suggestion.rationale: Phantom/typosquatting tactics mentioned in title ('Phantom Gyp'). Pipeline missed: detection of identical or near-identical package names registered to different maintainers in short time windows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry API logs for rapid package registrations with similar names to popular packages, registration from new or suspicious accounts, and dramatic version jump patterns. Correlate with package download anomalies and user reports of unexpected updates.

suggestion.title: CI/CD Pipeline Compromise via Transitive Dependency Injection
suggestion.rationale: Self-spreading nature implies lateral movement through dependency trees in CI systems. Pipeline missed: detection of unexpected packages appearing in lock files or CI build logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In CI/CD systems, detect npm install or yarn install commands that pull packages not in the committed lock file, or changes to lock files without corresponding developer commits. Alert on builds that run new post-install scripts or trigger unsigned binaries.

suggestion.title: npm Preinstall Script Execution of Embedded ELF Binary
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Rust ELF binary executed via preinstall, pushing malicious commits'. This is the execution pivot but pipeline missed it entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when npm install triggers unexpected process creation of ELF/native binaries from node_modules/.bin or package preinstall hooks. Focus on unsigned or unusual binary origins executed during install phase.

suggestion.title: Mass Credential and Environment Variable Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article core finding: 'targets 86 environment variables (key-value pairs) and 20 credential files that may contain OpenAI, AWS, Anthropic, and npm credentials, vault configuration files, SSH keys, and Exodus cryptocurrency wallet files.' Pipeline has no detection for this credential collection phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect single process enumerating multiple credential file paths (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.anthropic keys, vault configs) or bulk getenv/environ access. Alert on cardinality >10 distinct credential paths accessed within short time window from process without legitimate cause.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Artifacts as Covert C2 Exfiltration Channel
suggestion.rationale: Novel detection gap: 'writes it to a file with a harmless-looking name, as if it were lint or formatting output' then 'uploading the file as a build artifact, which can be downloaded by anyone with access.' Pipeline completely missed this C2 mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag GitHub Actions workflows uploading artifacts with benign naming patterns (*.lint, *.format, *.cache) from CI runs that do not legitimately produce such outputs. Cross-correlate with environment variable dumps or credential access in workflow logs.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Trusted Publishing Credential Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Attack mechanism: 'self-propagates by using stolen credentials for publishing on npm; this includes secrets associated with npm's Trusted Publishing workflow.' Pipeline should flag anomalous publishing patterns using these elevated permissions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate npm package publication workflows per account/CI environment. Alert on: new packages published via Trusted Publishing from unusual OIDC issuer origins, high-velocity publishes from compromised accounts, or publishing of versions with suspicious preinstall scripts.

suggestion.title: eBPF Kernel Rootkit Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Defense-evasion persistence mechanism: 'eBPF kernel rootkit'. This kernel-level component should trigger on BPF syscall usage from unprivileged or CI contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bpf() syscall (SYS_BPF=357) execution, particularly from npm preinstall context, CI/CD runners, or unprivileged users. Cross-correlate with module loading or kernel version queries that may probe rootkit defenses.

suggestion.title: Timestomped Git Commits During Recent Repository Activity
suggestion.rationale: Explicit evasion technique: 'timestamps point to several years ago, up to 13 years in some cases, even though they were pushed in the past few days. This is likely to evade investigation.' Pipeline missed this forensic red flag.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Git commits with author date >90 days older than push date. Especially flag when pushed by recently-flagged accounts, during compromise windows, or alongside preinstall script modifications to published packages.

suggestion.title: binding.gyp GYP Command Expansion Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'GYP's build configuration syntax supports command expansion. The <!(...)form runs a shell command during the configure phase'. This is the novel attack vector bypassing preinstall/postinstall monitoring. No detection logic captured it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor node-gyp rebuild execution during npm install without matching preinstall/postinstall lifecycle hooks. Flag binding.gyp files containing <!(command) syntax patterns. Detect spawning of non-standard interpreters (Bun, bash, sh) or credential-store access from node-gyp context.

suggestion.title: Multi-Vault Credential Harvesting During npm Install
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'harvests developer and CI/CD credentials across npm, GitHub, AWS, GCP, Azure, HashiCorp Vault, and Kubernetes'. Pipeline missed detection of file/environment access for ~/.npmrc, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh/config, ~/.kube/config, GITHUB_TOKEN, VAULT_ADDR during install-time code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate npm/node process spawned from install with reads of credential files or access to CI/CD credential environment variables. Cross-reference child processes and file I/O with malicious package versions. High-confidence signal if Bun subprocess accesses multiple credential locations.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Injection for Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'injects GitHub Actions workflows for persistence'. No detection for unexpected .github/workflows file creation/modification originating from npm install process or malware payload payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag file creation/writes to .github/workflows/ directory from npm, node, or Bun process context. Monitor for workflow.yml commits pushed without user interaction. Correlate with known malicious package installations and credential exfiltration timing.

suggestion.title: npm Package Mass Republishing from Compromised Account
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'self-propagates by republishing packages from any maintainer account it can reach' with 'single-account concentration' (jagreehal publishing 25 packages). Shows inflated versions (autotel-mcp 0.1.14→29.0.1 in same minute). No detection for account takeover or abnormal publish patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on single npm account publishing dozens of packages within hours. Flag version number inflation (jumping from stable to 20+.x.x). Correlate with GitHub commit timestamps for package.json version bumps and binding.gyp modifications. High-fidelity if combined with credential exfiltration evidence.

suggestion.title: Bun Interpreter Execution from npm Install Context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'multi-stage Bun-based loader'. No detection for Bun executable invocation during package installation without explicit Bun devDependency or node-gyp native build context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Bun interpreter (bun.exe, /usr/local/bin/bun) spawned from npm/node process during install. Flag if Bun not in package.json dependencies. Inspect Bun command-line arguments and child process spawning for credential access or exfiltration operations.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration via GitHub Repository Git Operations
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exfiltrates them through attacker-controlled GitHub repositories'. Pipeline did not detect npm install process performing git operations, creating/modifying repositories, or pushing sensitive data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate npm install spawning git, curl, or wget with GitHub/gitlab API endpoints or 'git push' operations. Flag commits containing credential patterns (AWS keys, GitHub tokens, VAULT_* values). Monitor for write access to unexpected GitHub repositories from dev/CI/CD contexts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Service Creation / Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly claims T1569.002 (Service Execution) but zero detection use case covers service creation or execution. Ransomware uses services for lateral movement and persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for non-system accounts creating or starting Windows services, especially via wmic, sc.exe, or PowerShell. Ransomware frequently pivots by installing services on remote hosts. Look for services created post-initial-compromise with random/obfuscated names.

suggestion.title: Direct Syscall / Process Injection Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Evades EDR With Obfuscation and Direct System Calls' — direct syscall obfuscation is the primary evasion vector claimed, but no use case detects this. T1027 coverage is indirect only.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process memory injection patterns (early exit hooks, DLL hollowing, EWOP) via behavioral signals: processes with abnormal module load order, unsigned DLL injection into legitimate processes (explorer, winlogon), or unusual API call patterns bypassing EDR hooks.

suggestion.title: EDR Evasion / Process Termination
suggestion.rationale: Title emphasizes ransomware 'Evades EDR' as a primary feature, but no use case targets EDR evasion attempts. Ransomware often kills EDR agents or disables EDR callbacks before encryption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process termination of common EDR/security vendors (MsMpEng, MsSense, CrowdStrike falcon, Sentinel agent, etc.), registry modifications disabling ETW/Sysmon, or loading of kernel-mode drivers by non-administrative processes post-compromise.

suggestion.title: File Hash IOC Endpoint Detection (high-fidelity)
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 2 SHA256 hashes but pipeline output is empty. Use case exists in narrative but pipeline failed to surface. Add explicit file hash correlation rule.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match file creation or process execution against the 2 provided IOC hashes (335ad12a950f..., d68ce82e82801...). High-fidelity indicators; alert immediately on match. Prioritize for host isolation and forensic preservation.

suggestion.title: Atlas RAT / RomulusLoader / SilentRunLoader / ValleyRAT Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names four malware families: 'deploying a growing arsenal of malware, including Atlas RAT, RomulusLoader, SilentRunLoader, and ValleyRAT.' Thirteen SHA256 hashes provided. Pipeline generated zero execution-phase hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file execution or hash match against the 13 provided SHA256s. Monitor for process creation exhibiting RAT behavioral indicators (network outbound to C2, registry persistence writes, credential access API calls). Flag obfuscated loader command lines launching LOLBins.

suggestion.title: Network Connections to TA4922 C2 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Five IPv4 addresses and three domains identified as C2 infrastructure. Article describes 'campaigns' deployed using these. T1071 identified but no network-phase hunts generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt outbound connections to 206.238.115.58, 154.211.86.110, 43.156.77.97, 103.214.172.33, 18.139.83.110 (all destination contexts), and DNS/HTTPS queries to aeya388.club, ws.ztts88.cyou, nwphotoblog.com. Prioritize non-business-context endpoints and repeated/automated connection patterns.

suggestion.title: RAT Registry Persistence Mechanisms
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'sophisticated cybercrime group' with 'level of planning.' RATs require persistence. No persistence-phase hunts generated despite this being standard post-execution behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on registry.exe or reg.exe modifications to Run/RunOnce keys, services registry hive, or scheduled task creation initiated by processes matching known loader hashes or exhibiting process injection patterns. Correlate with hash IOCs to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from RAT-Compromised Systems
suggestion.rationale: Targets listed as 'organizations in Japan, the United Kingdom, Germany, and across Southeast Asia.' Financially-motivated group targeting enterprises suggests post-compromise lateral movement. No lateral_movement-phase detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for RDP, WMI, PSEXEC, or SSH connections originating from endpoints recently matched against RAT SHA256 IOCs. Flag anomalous lateral moves to servers or credential-rich systems (domain controllers, Exchange, file shares) within 48 hours of initial infection.
