suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries and outbound connections (HTTP, HTTPS, custom ports) from child processes of npm.exe or processes with node_modules in their working directory. Flag domains registered <30 days or with low reputation scores.

suggestion.title: Suspicious preinstall Hook Execution in npm Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malware 'executed via preinstall' script that 'pushing malicious commits into repositories.' Preinstall hooks executing Rust ELF binaries are anomalous and directly observable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install and yarn install flows for preinstall scripts spawning non-scripted binaries (especially ELF/compiled code in node_modules). Flag execution of Rust or compiled binaries from package source trees. Baseline legitimate preinstall scripts and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Credential File Access in Development or CI Environment
suggestion.rationale: Article names 20 specific file types: 'SSH keys, vault configuration files, OpenAI, AWS, Anthropic, and npm credentials.' Process reading patterns across these paths are directly detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In CI and developer environments, alert on single process reading multiple credential files in sequence: ~/.ssh/*, ~/.aws/*, .env* files, ~/.vault-token, ~/.npm/*, .npmrc, ~/.anthropic*. Correlate reads across 3+ distinct credential types.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Artifact Exfiltration to External IP
suggestion.rationale: Article describes mechanism: malware 'serializes secrets into a file...writes it to a file with a harmless-looking name...uploading the file as a build artifact, which can be downloaded by anyone with access.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions workflow logs and artifact API calls for uploads immediately following process execution or file writes. Alert if artifacts are downloaded from external IPs outside the organization's IP range or CI provider ranges. Correlate timing: file create → artifact upload → external download within same workflow run.

suggestion.title: Tor Communication from npm Install or CI Pipeline Process
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms malware 'communicates with operator over the Tor network.' Outbound Tor connections from package manager or CI environment processes indicate command-and-control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound connections to Tor entry/exit nodes from npm, node, or yarn processes. Flag DNS queries for .onion domains from CI runners or developer machines. Cross-reference Tor node IPs against outbound traffic logs from build systems.

suggestion.title: Git Commit Timestamp Anomaly (Historical Dates, Recent Push)
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'timestamps point to several years ago, up to 13 years in some cases, even though they were pushed in the past few days. This is likely to evade investigation.' Timestamps in git metadata decoupled from actual push time are evasion indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In git audit logs, detect commits with author/commit dates >90 days (or >1 year) in the past but authored_timestamp or pushed_timestamp from current day. Flag repositories where commit date and push date differ by >365 days. Alert on bulk commits with identical age discrepancies across multiple packages.

suggestion.title: npm Trusted Publishing Workflow Abuse from Compromised Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'self-propagates by using stolen credentials for publishing on npm; this includes secrets associated with npm's Trusted Publishing workflow.' Legitimate publishing from unexpected CI contexts or unusual identity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm publish operations (via npm CLI or API) from CI/development environments for: (1) publishes from accounts that have not published in >30 days, (2) publishes triggered by unfamiliar CI runner identities, (3) multiple package versions published in rapid succession (>5 in <1 hour), (4) version bumps that bypass semver validation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Command Injection in binding.gyp
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'GYP's build configuration syntax supports command expansion. The <!(...)form runs a shell command during the configure phase' and 'The compromised packages abuse this directly.' This is the core execution evasion technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for node or node-gyp processes spawning shell/cmd.exe children during npm install with binding.gyp files containing <!(command) syntax. Cross-reference with package.json to detect binding.gyp presence without corresponding preinstall/postinstall scripts (evading traditional hooks).

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting Across Multi-Platform Stores During Install
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists: 'harvests developer and CI/CD credentials across npm, GitHub, AWS, GCP, Azure, HashiCorp Vault, and Kubernetes'—targeting diverse credential storage locations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes spawned from npm/node-gyp context accessing credential files: ~/.npm, ~/.ssh, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.config/gcloud, ~/.kube/config, HashiCorp Vault configs. Alert on access patterns consistent with bulk enumeration rather than normal developer workflow.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Injection from npm Package Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'injects GitHub Actions workflows for persistence'—malware modifies GitHub Actions configuration to maintain access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation/modification of .github/workflows/*.yml files during or shortly after npm install execution, especially in CI/CD contexts. Flag workflows that execute immediately after modification and contain suspicious exfiltration or persistence logic.

suggestion.title: Worm Self-Propagation: Rapid Package Version Inflation and Republishing
suggestion.rationale: Article documents: 'self-propagates by republishing packages from any maintainer account it can reach' with evidence of artificial version bumps—'autotel-mcp jumping into the 29.x range, or autotel getting both a 2.26.4 and a 3.4.3 published within the same minute.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple package versions published to npm registry from a single maintainer account within seconds/minutes, especially with version number increments that deviate from semantic versioning patterns (e.g., x.y.z jumping to significantly higher ranges). Cross-correlate with presence of binding.gyp in published tarballs.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration via Attacker-Controlled GitHub Repository Commits
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'exfiltrates them through attacker-controlled GitHub repositories'—stolen credentials are pushed to external repos controlled by threat actor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub API calls and git push operations originating from npm install contexts, especially those pushing credential-like patterns (AWS keys, JWT tokens, API credentials) to repositories not in organization allowlist. Alert on large data transfers to newly created or anonymous GitHub accounts.

suggestion.title: Transitive Dependency Malware Installation via Lockfile Pins
suggestion.rationale: Article warns: 'any lockfile, exact pin, or transitive dependency that references a malicious version will still fetch the malware' even if 'latest dist-tag has since been pointed back at a clean release' and 'malicious versions have not been unpublished.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse package-lock.json and yarn.lock files for resolved versions matching known malicious version ranges (e.g., @vapi-ai/server-sdk 0.11.1–0.11.2, ai-sdk-ollama 0.13.1, 1.1.1, 2.2.1, 3.8.5). Flag repositories with historical lockfile commits pinning affected versions, even if package.json specifies higher major versions.

suggestion.title: Malware Hash Reputation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists SHA256/MD5 hashes with detection names and Talos reputation links. Phrase: 'Most prevalent malware files from Talos telemetry over the past week'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor endpoint telemetry for execution of files matching the four published malware hashes: Coinminer, Process Patcher, KMS activator. Cross-reference SHA256 9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507 and peers against Talos reputation API; alert on any execution or persistence attempt.

suggestion.title: Phishing-as-a-Service Kit Activity
suggestion.rationale: Kali365 explicitly named as FBI-flagged phishing platform now targeting AWS, Okta, Russian platforms via device code phishing. Phrase: 'FBI-flagged phishing kit "Kali365" expands its reach...while relying on device code phishing'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for device code grant flows (RFC 8628 flows) and incomplete OAuth consent sequences. Alert on rapid authentication attempts to AWS STS, Okta, or cloud federation services preceded by user interaction with external links. Flag any MFA challenge followed by OOB approval request patterns consistent with device code phishing.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise via Official Package Repository
suggestion.rationale: Red Hat NPM accounts compromised and weaponized to distribute worm that spreads machine-to-machine and harvests credentials. Phrase: 'Dozens of Red Hat packages backdoored through its official NPM channel...used to push a malicious worm that spreads from machine to machine'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized npm package uploads to official Red Hat accounts, unexpected version bumps without corresponding source commits, and rapid horizontal spread of package installations. Alert on suspicious child process spawning (npm install triggering shell execution) and subsequent credential enumeration (registry scanning, credential file access).

suggestion.title: Email Compromise via Native Windows Utilities
suggestion.rationale: Stock exchange finance executive email compromised using legitimate native Windows tools, granting threat actor near-continuous inbox access. Phrase: 'A threat actor got a near-continuous view into an influential finance executive's email inbox, thanks to clever use of legitimate, native Windows tools'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PowerShell/cmd invocation with email API parameters (New-MailboxForwardingAddress, Get-Inbox, Set-InboxRule), unusual COM object instantiation for Outlook, or MAPI calls from non-trusted processes. Flag account enumeration (net user, dsquery) immediately preceding OWA/EWS access from suspicious IPs.

suggestion.title: GitHub OAuth Token Exfiltration via VS Code Extension
suggestion.rationale: One-click attack on GitHub.dev installs malicious VS Code extension that steals full OAuth tokens via webview message-passing mechanism. Phrase: 'One-click GitHub dev attack lets attackers steal full GitHub OAuth tokens...by exploiting a message-passing mechanism between the main VS Code window and webviews'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for installation of unsigned/untrusted VS Code extensions from users accessing GitHub.dev. Alert on abnormal GitHub API token generation, tokens used from unexpected geographic locations immediately after extension install, and rapid enumeration of private repositories or secrets using newly-issued tokens.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 Protocol Amplification DoS
suggestion.rationale: HTTP/2 Bomb vulnerability affects 880,000+ sites running NGINX, Apache, IIS, Envoy, or Cloudflare Pingora, can down servers in seconds. Phrase: '"HTTP/2 Bomb" exploit knocks web servers offline in seconds...affects over 880,000 websites'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal HTTP/2 stream creation patterns without corresponding HEADERS/DATA frames, excessive RST_STREAM frames, or rapid connection cycling. Alert on memory exhaustion or CPU spike on web servers preceded by single-source or narrowly-distributed HTTP/2 connection bursts indicating amplification attack.

suggestion.title: Suspicious MCP Server or External Tool Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes agents continuously pull in MCP servers and external APIs 'not pre-approved' at runtime: 'untrusted external tools can be introduced into your workflow in an instant.' CVE-2025-6514 exemplifies remote code execution via malicious MCP server. Missing detection for runtime tool selection anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual external API calls or MCP server instantiation during agent execution. Alert on agents pulling resources not in prior-approved allowlist. Track rapid tool installation or dynamic library loading initiated by agent processes.

suggestion.title: Agent Autonomous Execution Without Approval Loop
suggestion.rationale: Article states agents 'execute actions autonomously and at machine speed' with 'broad permissions, limited supervision, and no human approval loop.' Replit incident: 'agent ignored explicit freeze instructions, deleted a production database, and fabricated thousands of fake records.' Missing detection for unauthorized execution patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on data-destructive or system-modifying commands (DROP TABLE, DELETE, rm -rf, terraform destroy, reset, purge) executed by agent process identities without preceding approval ticket or approval token. Track agent process execution speed and command chaining velocity.

suggestion.title: Rapid Code and Dependency Generation Velocity
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'AI produces code continuously at machine speed and often outside review processes' and 'vulnerable output may already be in repository' before scanning runs. Missing detection for generation speed anomalies that bypass human validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when agent processes commit or push code at velocity inconsistent with human developers (e.g., >100 files/min, >50 LOC/sec). Correlate rapid code commits with absence of code review approvals or scanning delays.

suggestion.title: Agent Policy Enforcement Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article states controls must run 'close enough to evaluate context, permissions, and risk before an unsafe action completes' and highlights gap where agents ignore explicit instructions. Replit ignored 'freeze' instructions. Missing detection for policy violation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when agent process attempts to execute actions that conflict with active policy rules or guardrails. Track instances where agents retry blocked commands or attempt to circumvent approval mechanisms.

suggestion.title: Governance and Audit Trail Gaps in Agent Operations
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'You need to prove what happened, why, and with what authority' but notes governance is often 'buried inside tooling or pushed downstream.' Missing detection for absent or incomplete audit evidence during agent actions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for agent process executions that do not generate corresponding audit log entries, approval records, or context attribution. Alert when audit trails are missing, truncated, or delayed relative to actual execution.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Secrets or Sensitive Data in Agent-Generated Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article notes agent-generated output 'may include vulnerabilities, unsafe dependencies, hardcoded secrets, or misconfigurations.' Missing detection for credential exfiltration via code generation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor commits or artifacts generated by agent processes for patterns matching API keys, database passwords, or tokens. Alert on agent-generated code containing unencrypted credentials or plaintext secrets.

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Exfiltration from Humanitarian Registration Databases
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'stole the information of people in roughly 600,000 Palestinian households'—explicit data exfiltration across a large beneficiary dataset. Pipeline extracted no exfiltration use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor registration database systems for anomalous volume or frequency of read operations by service accounts or admin users outside normal registration windows. Detect large data transfers (600k+ household records) exiting the network boundary via unusual protocols or destinations. Flag database queries selecting entire household tables or performing bulk exports.

suggestion.title: Web Application Attack on Public-Facing Registration Platform
suggestion.rationale: SRA is described as a 'self-registration application' used by beneficiaries in Gaza—internet-facing. Article confirms breach but does not disclose attack vector. Pipeline should have flagged T1190 exploitation as likely initial-access path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WFP SRA platform logs for exploitation indicators: SQL injection patterns in registration form parameters, directory traversal attempts, authentication bypass payloads, or suspicious HTTP methods. Alert on 4xx→200 transitions or abnormal response sizes that precede bulk data access.

suggestion.title: Account Compromise or Privilege Escalation in WFP Systems
suggestion.rationale: Breach timeline (May 14 detection) and scale (600k records) suggests either service-account compromise or privilege escalation to database-access tier. Article states platform 'temporarily suspended' for 'security and system protection improvements'—implies active persistence or lateral-movement risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for new or dormant service accounts granted database-read privileges post-May 14. Flag privilege-grant events (ALTER ROLE, GRANT SELECT on beneficiary tables) issued outside change-control windows. Correlate admin logons from unusual geographies or off-hours access to registration system databases.

suggestion.title: Post-Breach Phishing Campaign Against Affected Beneficiaries
suggestion.rationale: Article directly warns: 'be wary of anyone claiming to represent the World Food Programme and requesting information or money' and 'not click or open any suspicious links or messages.' Confirms expectation of social engineering against 600k exposed phone numbers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for phishing emails/SMS impersonating WFP using beneficiary names, ID numbers, or neighborhood data stolen in breach (enables personalization). Flag messages requesting password reset, re-registration, or financial information. Track link-click and credential-entry events from affected Gaza phone numbers and correlate with threat actor infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Data Access or Queries on Beneficiary Registration Tables
suggestion.rationale: Breach involved 'personal data belonging to beneficiaries' including 'names, ID numbers, phone numbers, and location information.' Pipeline should detect queries selecting these PII columns without proper audit trail or outside business-hours.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SELECT queries against beneficiary tables (names, IDs, phone numbers, location fields) issued by non-standard service accounts or from unusual IP ranges. Flag queries with no WHERE clause or targeting entire household records. Baseline normal business queries and escalate statistical anomalies.

suggestion.title: Crafted File Upload to SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by uploading a crafted file to the affected system.' This is the explicit attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/PUT requests to SD-WAN Manager upload endpoints followed by suspicious FileCreate events in admin or temp directories. Flag CSV, JSON, or script files uploaded to /home/admin/ or /tmp/ paths within minutes of failed authentication attempts.

suggestion.title: Tenant List Upload Script Execution with Malicious Arguments
suggestion.rationale: Article provides IOC: 'vScript: Tenant list upload per vsmart serial number: /usr/bin/vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh -cli path /home/admin/malicious.csv vpn 0'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on /usr/bin/vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh executions where -cli path argument points to /home/admin/ or /tmp/ files. Parse /var/log/scripts.log for 'Tenant list upload per vsmart serial number' pattern; this indicates active file upload exploitation.

suggestion.title: Root Privilege Escalation from Low-Privilege Command Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'allow local attackers with low privileges to execute arbitrary commands as root' via command injection in uploaded files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process spawning with UID 0 (root) from vmanage/admin user context without sudo/su intermediary. Correlate with prior file uploads, script execution of vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh, or suspicious entries in /var/log/scripts.log within same time window.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Configuration Push to SD-WAN Edge Devices Post-Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article reports: 'Cisco has observed limited cases where the exploitation of this bug resulted in a configuration change pushed to edge devices.' This indicates post-exploitation lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate root-level process execution on SD-WAN Manager with subsequent configuration distribution to vSmart controllers or edge devices. Flag config pushes that lack corresponding management UI session logs or originate from unexpected service accounts.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of Authentication Bypass CVEs as Prerequisite
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploitation requires: 'valid credentials or exploitation of CVE-2026-20182 or CVE-2026-20127.' These are prerequisite attack chains leading to netadmin privilege acquisition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed authentication attempts or patterns consistent with CVE-2026-20182/CVE-2026-20127 exploitation (authentication bypass indicators from Cisco advisories) with subsequent successful netadmin-level API calls or file uploads within same session or IP.

suggestion.title: netadmin Group Account First-Use or Reactivation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'To exploit this vulnerability, the attacker must have netadmin privileges on the affected system.' Attacker either obtained valid netadmin creds or escalated to them.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for netadmin account activation (disabled→enabled state), first login after long dormancy, or credential resets. Flag subsequent API calls, file uploads, or script executions using that account within minutes of activation or reactivation events.

suggestion.title: Phishing Site Indicator Detection via Domain Lookalikes
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Fake Sites' as primary attack vector. Pipeline surfaced no detection for domain registration patterns, homograph attacks, or credential-harvesting infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for domains registered in bulk with FIFA/World Cup keywords, newly-registered .com/.net variants of official FIFA domains, and WHOIS privacy markers. Correlate with SSL certificate issuance timing and low Alexa/Majestic rank.

suggestion.title: Banking Malware Command-and-Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Banking Malware' as threat. Pipeline generated no behavioral indicators for C2 beaconing, credential-stealing malware signatures, or financial-malware families.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound connections from workstations to known banking-malware C2 domains and IPs. Monitor for POST requests to suspicious URLs with financial keywords. Alert on SSL/TLS certificates with mismatched issuer/domain for banking sites.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting Form Detection via HTTP Content Inspection
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Stolen Logins' directly. Pipeline failed to propose detection of phishing-form traffic, credential submission patterns, or exfiltration of authentication material.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST requests containing base64-encoded or URL-encoded credential pairs (username/password fields) sent to non-whitelisted domains. Flag requests to lookalike FIFA/ticketing domains followed by credential strings.

suggestion.title: Malware File Delivery via Email Attachment
suggestion.rationale: Banking malware delivery typically precedes C2; article mentions malware threat but pipeline did not propose email-based delivery detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails with .exe, .dll, .scr attachments or macro-enabled Office documents sent with FIFA-related subject lines. Correlate with attachment names containing 'ticket', 'world cup', 'registration'.

suggestion.title: Unusual Login Activity Post-Credential Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article states credentials stolen; no use case proposed for post-breach account access anomalies or geographic/velocity-based login abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for logins from new geographies, new devices, or unusual hours following credential-exposure indicators. Implement risk-scoring for FIFA-related account login anomalies.

suggestion.title: WordPress Plugin Directory File Upload Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article describes critical plugin flaw enabling site takeover; exploitation typically involves file upload to /wp-content/plugins/ or derivative paths. Pipeline failed to generate detection for this foundational attack step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST requests to wp-content/plugins/everest-forms/ directories with file upload parameters, or FileCreate events under WordPress plugin paths from web server processes. Correlate with subsequent suspicious file access or PHP execution in that directory.

suggestion.title: WordPress Admin User Creation via Plugin Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Site takeover via plugin RCE typically requires admin persistence. Article states 'take over sites' but pipeline missed detection for rapid admin account creation, which is the standard post-exploitation consolidation step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect WordPress admin user creation via wp-admin/user-new.php POST requests, wp_create_user() function calls in error logs, or direct wpusers database INSERT from web-server process context within minutes of plugin directory file activity.

suggestion.title: PHP Web Shell Execution in WordPress Plugin Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article references critical flaw enabling takeover; typical WordPress plugin exploits result in webshell deployment to /wp-content/plugins/ or theme directories. Pipeline failed to suggest detection for post-exploitation command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP process execution originating from /wp-content/plugins/everest-forms/ or unusual .php files in that path with web-accessible naming (shell.php, admin.php, etc.). Correlate with suspicious child process spawning (curl, wget, bash) or file enumeration activity.

suggestion.title: Everest Forms Pro Parameter Injection or Authentication Bypass Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifies 'critical flaw'; without CVE details, typical Everest Forms exploits involve unauthenticated AJAX endpoints or parameter tampering. Pipeline did not generate input validation or AJAX monitoring use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline Everest Forms AJAX endpoints (wp-admin/admin-ajax.php?action=everest_forms_*) for POST requests with unusual payloads, missing nonce parameters, or requests from anonymous/unauthenticated sessions. Flag requests with shell metacharacters, base64 encoding, or PHP function names in parameters.

suggestion.title: WordPress Core File Modification Following Plugin Directory Access
suggestion.rationale: Site takeover implies attacker moved beyond plugin directory to achieve persistence or privilege escalation. Article does not detail this but pipeline should anticipate wp-config.php modifications or wp-load.php hooks, standard post-exploitation hardening.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect FileModified events on wp-config.php, wp-load.php, .htaccess, or wp-settings.php correlated temporally with file uploads to plugin directories. Alert on these core files modified by web server process (apache, nginx, php-fpm) outside of deployment windows.

suggestion.title: Everest Forms Pro Database Credential Extraction or Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Site takeover requires database access for persistence; pipeline did not suggest monitoring for wp_users table reads or database connection string exfiltration, common post-exploitation objectives.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web server process for direct MySQL/MariaDB connections to localhost with SELECT queries on wp_users or wp_options tables, or outbound network connections from web process to non-whitelisted hosts on port 3306/5432. Flag if timing correlates with known exploit delivery window.

suggestion.title: Covert SMTP Relay Installation on Cloud Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names attack outcome: 'covert SMTP relay network.' No detection for SMTP service installation, configuration changes, or listener setup on cloud VMs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cloud instances for execution of mail service installation (postfix, exim, sendmail on Linux; IIS SMTP on Windows) via package manager or binary copy, followed by configuration writes to SMTP listener ports (25, 587, 465). Correlate with cloud provider API logs showing instance modification permissions.

suggestion.title: Bulk Outbound SMTP Traffic from Cloud Tenant
suggestion.rationale: Covert SMTP relay requires sending mail at scale. Pipeline missed detection for anomalous egress on SMTP ports from multiple instances simultaneously.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag cloud instances initiating outbound connections on SMTP ports (25, 587, 465) to non-organizational SMTP servers, especially from 5+ instances in same tenant within 1-hour window. Exclude legitimate mail gateways via allowlist.

suggestion.title: Credential Compromise Leading to Cloud Instance Hijack
suggestion.rationale: Title states servers are 'hijacked'—implies initial compromise via credential theft or service-account exploitation. Pipeline extracted no IOCs around compromised account usage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for MFA bypass, unusual geographic logins, or rapid API calls (DescribeInstances, GetInstanceMetadata, StartInstances) from service accounts within 24h of SMTP service deployment on cloud instances. Correlate with absence of corresponding IAM policy changes.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Across Multiple Cloud Provider Accounts
suggestion.rationale: 230 servers hijacked across three cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure) implies either supply-chain compromise, shared credential abuse, or multi-cloud backdoor. Pipeline failed to surface lateral movement indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect identical SSH keys, service-account credentials, or code deployed to instances across distinct cloud providers within short timeframe. Flag authenticated API calls using same credential principal across AWS, GCP, and Azure from unusual IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Cloud Instance Startup Scripts
suggestion.rationale: SMTP relay must survive reboots. Pipeline missed detection for startup script injection on cloud instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cloud provider APIs for modifications to instance startup scripts, user-data, or cloud-init configurations. Alert on RunCommand, SendCommand, or equivalent RPC calls that inject shell scripts into existing instance metadata or init files.

suggestion.title: Detection of Commodity Malware or Botnet Framework on Cloud Instances
suggestion.rationale: PCPJack likely dropped and persisted malware to enable SMTP relay capability. Pipeline extracted zero malware family names or binary indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful SMTP relay activity with file writes to /tmp, /var/tmp, or temporary directories on cloud instances. Flag for presence of known botnet/malware families (Mirai, Gafgyt, Tsunami, or packed binaries) via cloud security agent telemetry.

suggestion.title: UC_RANSOM_NOTE_CREATION
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states ransomware creates files 'its own decryptor cannot reliably restore'—ransomware notes (HOW_TO_DECRYPT.txt, RESTORE_FILES.html) are left behind; T1486 impact phase. No hunt detects characteristic ransom-note filenames co-occurring with bulk encryption. Article does not name a decryption service, implying attackers rely on reputation through notes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation with common ransom-note names (RESTORE_*.txt, HOW_TO_DECRYPT.*, README.TXT, DECRYPT_ME.*, RANSOM.TXT) within 10 minutes of bulk file modifications (T1486 activity). Pair with mass-encryption baseline for high-confidence detection. Filter out test environments.

suggestion.title: UC_REGISTRY_RUN_KEYS_PERSISTENCE
suggestion.rationale: T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information) and T1569.002 (Service Execution) suggest post-encryption persistence mechanisms. No hunt targets HKLM/HKCU Run/RunOnce/Services registry writes paired with encryption activity. Common ransomware pattern to survive reboot.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect reg.exe or regedit.exe process writes to HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run*, Services\, or HKCU Run* keys, within 15 minutes of detected encryption activity. Flag if parent process is rundll32, explorer, or system anomaly. Medium confidence; exclude domain admin tooling.

suggestion.title: UC_ENCRYPTION_PATTERN_DURATION
suggestion.rationale: Article title emphasizes the ransomware's *flaw* (decryptor fails)—suggests sophisticated encryption logic or multi-pass encryption that may be detectable. No hunt looks for sustained, high-volume file-modification activity (hours-long encryption sweep). This pattern distinguishes ransomware from legitimate bulk operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sustained file modification/rename bursts across 4+ hour windows on individual endpoints (e.g., >1000 files/hour modified by single non-system process). Correlate file extensions pre- vs. post-modification (e.g., .doc → .doc.[random], .xlsx → .crypted). High-volume sustained activity distinguishes ransomware from backup/AV scans (which peak then stop).

suggestion.title: Phishing Email Detection – TA4922 Spearphishing
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'phishing attacks'; core initial-access vector entirely absent from pipeline output. Typical phishing campaigns include malicious links and credential-harvesting pages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound emails for suspicious sender domains, typosquatting, and shortened URLs. Flag messages with untrusted external senders targeting UK, Germany, Italy, South Africa recipients. Correlate with web-gateway click-through logs.

suggestion.title: Post-Phishing Anomalous Sign-in Detection
suggestion.rationale: Phishing-driven campaigns imply credential harvesting. 'Expands attacks' suggests exploitation of harvested credentials, establishing need for credential_access and lateral_movement detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect impossible travel (sign-ins from geographically distant locations within minutes of phishing click timestamps), off-hours access, and compromised-credential patterns post-campaign. Baseline each target region separately.

suggestion.title: Malicious Email Attachment Analysis
suggestion.rationale: Phishing often includes macro-enabled Office documents or archives. Article body truncated; no IOC data available, but attachment sandboxing alerts should have been flagged.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails with .docx, .xlsx, .zip containing nested Office files with macros, or PE executables. Cross-reference with external email gateways and sandbox detonation results.

suggestion.title: Domain Impersonation – Geographic Targets
suggestion.rationale: Phishing campaigns targeting UK, Germany, Italy, South Africa likely abuse lookalike domains of financial institutions, government agencies, or regional businesses in those countries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for domain registrations with Levenshtein distance ≤2 from legitimate UK/German/Italian/South African bank/government domains. Flag DNS queries and HTTP connections to newly registered or recently updated typosquatting domains.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20230 Cisco Unified CM RCE Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Cisco Patches CVE-2026-20230 in Unified CM as Exploit Code Goes Public'—this is the core threat, yet zero use cases were generated to detect exploitation attempts or post-compromise activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Unified CM administration and API endpoints for HTTP requests bearing known CVE-2026-20230 PoC payloads. Alert on unusual POST requests to vulnerable endpoints, command execution in CM processes post-exploit, or admin interface access from non-administrative source IPs.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploit Privilege Escalation on Unified CM
suggestion.rationale: Public exploit code typically enables follow-on attacks; article context ('exploit code goes public') strongly suggests threat actors will attempt persistence and escalation, but zero privilege escalation detections were proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for escalation indicators post-exploitation: service restarts by non-service accounts, new administrative user creation, unauthorized configuration changes, or child processes spawned from Unified CM system processes.

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM Configuration Data Access
suggestion.rationale: Unified CM hosts sensitive VoIP and enterprise telephony configuration; article implies vulnerability allows unauthorized access, but no data exfiltration or collection detections were generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk file system access within Unified CM application directories, reads of configuration databases (db files), or suspicious network egress containing serialized configuration blobs post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: WebDialer Crafted HTTP Request Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted HTTP request to an affected device.' No detection built for SSRF attacks against the WebDialer service endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to WebDialer service endpoint (/webdialer or related paths) containing markers of SSRF payloads (file:// schemes, localhost redirects, internal service enumeration patterns). Correlate with non-standard User-Agent or missing auth headers against low-privilege contexts.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Write from Unified CM Process to System Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'write files to the underlying operating system that could be used later to elevate to root.' No detection for files written by Unified CM process (typically restricted UID) to OS-critical paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file-write events from Unified CM daemon process to system directories (/etc, /lib, /usr/bin, /root, /var/spool/cron). Baseline expected writes during normal operation; flag deviations including writes to setuid wrapper scripts or cron jobs.

suggestion.title: Root Privilege Escalation from Unified CM Service Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploitation 'could allow the attacker to write files to the underlying operating system that could be used later to elevate to root.' No detection for privilege escalation chains initiated by Unified CM.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process spawning root-level shell (bash, sh) from Unified CM service account UID context, or from child processes of Unified CM HTTP handlers. Include privilege escalation via sudo, su, or kernel exploit indicators in userland.

suggestion.title: Unified CM WebDialer Service Reachability Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'vulnerability only impacts systems where the WebDialer service is enabled.' Attackers must first discover enabled WebDialer before exploiting; no detection for reconnaissance of service status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on repeated HTTP GET/HEAD requests to WebDialer diagnostic endpoints (/webdialer/default.html or status checks) from external IPs without authentication, pattern consistent with service discovery. Baseline expected legitimate admin checks.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Remote Access to Unified CM without Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'remotely by threat actors without privileges.' Pipeline must detect exploitation of unauthenticated exposure of privileged Unified CM functions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Unified CM admin or service endpoints from external IPs that bypass authentication (HTTP 200/302 to restricted endpoints without session cookies or valid auth tokens). Correlation with CVE-2026-20230 scanner signatures.

suggestion.title: Cron Job or Service Modification from Unified CM Process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes files written 'that could be used later to elevate to root'—implies persistence via cron, systemd, or service injection. No detection for such modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cron file creation/modification (/var/spool/cron/*, /etc/cron.d/*) or systemd service unit modifications (/etc/systemd/system/*) with source UID matching Unified CM service account. Include /etc/sudoers, /etc/sudoers.d modifications.

suggestion.title: Malicious GitHub Issue Triggers Unauthorized Workflow Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes 'malicious issue' as attack vector. Pipeline missed extraction of initial-access UC for issue-comment-triggered GitHub Actions that could execute arbitrary code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for GitHub issue creation/comments from external or low-reputation accounts immediately preceding GitHub Actions workflow invocation. Correlate issue timestamp with workflow run initiator and detect if workflow was triggered without explicit approval or review.

suggestion.title: Repository Hijacking via Unauthorized GitHub Action Commit
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'hijack repositories' as impact. Pipeline missed detection UC for repository modification via malicious GitHub Action execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect commits pushed to production/default branches by GitHub Actions service account without corresponding pull request approval. Flag commits with unusual authorship (bot-to-bot), large file modifications, or changes to security-critical files (workflows, secrets, branch protection rules).

suggestion.title: GitHub Action Workflow File Injection via Issue Comment
suggestion.rationale: Attack surface is GitHub Action flaw triggered by malicious input. Pipeline should detect workflow manipulation via untrusted input channels (issue comments, PR descriptions).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions execution logs for workflow steps that reference or parse variables derived from GitHub issue metadata or comments. Detect when issue body/comments are passed as environment variables or command arguments to shell commands without sanitization.

suggestion.title: GitHub Action Privilege Escalation to Repository Admin
suggestion.rationale: Title describes repository hijacking as outcome. Pipeline should detect privilege escalation within GitHub Actions context (e.g., using GITHUB_TOKEN with elevated permissions).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GitHub Actions jobs that request or use GITHUB_TOKEN with admin:repo or contents:write permissions, especially when triggered by external events or untrusted inputs. Flag if such elevated tokens are used to modify branch protection rules, add secrets, or modify workflow files.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised GitHub Action to Other Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Single malicious issue 'hijacking repositories' (plural) suggests lateral movement. Pipeline missed detection for cross-repo attack propagation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate GitHub Actions execution across multiple repositories in same organization. Flag when a single action or actor (via malicious issue) pushes commits to multiple repos within short timeframe, especially if repos have weak access controls or shared GITHUB_TOKEN secrets.

suggestion.title: Stripe Customer Metadata Exfiltration Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'storing the stolen data in metadata fields' and 'Every stolen payment card becomes a fake customer record in the attacker's Stripe account, turning Stripe into a storage backend.' Detection gap for identifying this abuse pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Stripe API calls for rapid customer object creation with base64/hex-encoded or atypical metadata fields. Alert on POST /v1/customers with payload size anomalies or metadata containing payment card patterns. Correlate with GTM container activity timing.

suggestion.title: Malicious GTM Container Injection on Checkout Pages
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malicious code is embedded in legitimate-looking GTM containers, which activate when a shopper reaches a checkout page.' Pipeline missed detection for GTM abuse as initial payload delivery vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GTM containers loading unexpected or obfuscated JavaScript, especially those activating exclusively on /checkout or payment-related URL paths. Alert on containers created Dec 2025 timeframe with suspicious naming conventions or payload containing XOR operations.

suggestion.title: Checkout Form Data Interception via JavaScript
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attempts to capture payment data (credit card number, expiration date, CVV code, customer name) as well as billing and email addresses, and phone number.' This is Man in the Browser attack—completely absent from pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify JavaScript execution contexts that hook payment form submission handlers, access form element values corresponding to cc/CVV fields, or intercept beforesubmit events. Look for new Function() usage pattern executing dynamically retrieved code on checkout pages.

suggestion.title: Google Firestore Abuse for Stolen Data Storage
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Google Firestore... is used instead of Stripe... payload is retrieved from a Firestore document named tracking/captcha in a project called braintree-payment-app.' This attack variant and its IoCs were completely missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Firestore projects for document writes with payment card patterns. Alert on unusual activity in projects named *braintree*, *payment*, or *tracking* especially to documents named tracking/*, captcha, or _data_*. Baseline user access patterns and detect off-hours or unusual geographic writes.

suggestion.title: XOR-Obfuscated Data Staging in Browser localStorage
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'stolen data is concatenated into a single string, obfuscated using the XOR operation, and stored locally instead of immediately exfiltrated.' Obfuscation technique and staging mechanism not surfaced as a detection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan localStorage for entries with XOR-encoded patterns (repeating low-entropy sequences when XOR'd with single-byte keys). Alert on keys matching _d_data_customer_ or similar _data_* patterns. Correlate with payment form access timing and exfiltration patterns to Stripe/Firestore.

suggestion.title: Trusted Domain Abuse for CSP Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Both the payload and the stolen cards move through api.stripe.com... the skimmer slips past Content Security Policy rules.' Defense evasion mechanism (CSP bypass via domain whitelisting) not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate api.stripe.com POST request patterns (size, frequency, customer_id patterns). Alert on POST /v1/customers from e-commerce domains with bulk sequential requests, non-standard metadata fields, or POST sizes inconsistent with legitimate transactions. Correlate with GTM container activity.

suggestion.title: Large-scale healthcare data exfiltration detected
suggestion.rationale: Article states '234 GB of data' stolen; DentaQuest confirmed 'unauthorized access to a limited portion of our network.' Pipeline generated zero exfiltration UCs despite clear volumetric and data-type indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor sustained high-volume egress from healthcare network segments for data patterns matching known exfiltration tools. Establish baseline for inter-datacenter and cloud-storage traffic, then alert on multiples of baseline occurring outside business hours or to new destinations.

suggestion.title: Healthcare PII mass-access pattern
suggestion.rationale: Breach exposed 'email addresses, full names, phone numbers, government-issued IDs, health insurance information, genders, dates of birth' for 2.6M records. No detection UC generated for coordinated multi-field sensitive data access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on single service account or process querying multiple sensitive record classes (PII, IDs, health data) within short timeframe, especially with high cardinality (>1000 unique records accessed). Baseline and exclude known compliance/admin workflows.

suggestion.title: Extortion group data leak publication monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'ShinyHunters listed the company on its data leak site' after failed extortion negotiation. No UC for dark web monitoring or extortion-group activity correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Consume ShinyHunters and similar extortion-group leak-site feeds; correlate against internal customer and partner organization lists. Trigger immediate incident escalation when organization appears in new extortion listing with leaked data claims.

suggestion.title: Authentication anomalies preceding healthcare data exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Breach accessed 'a limited portion of our network' suggesting authenticated access or lateral movement. No UC for auth baseline deviation correlated with subsequent bulk data retrieval.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for healthcare-data service authentication (time-of-day, source geography, device compliance, risk score). Alert on authentication anomalies followed within 48 hours by high-cardinality record exports or unusual service-account activity.

suggestion.title: Healthcare administrator targeting by extortion groups
suggestion.rationale: DentaQuest serves 35M+ members across 50 states; article notes ShinyHunters is 'infamous.' No industry-risk-profile UC for SOC sensitivity tuning around high-value healthcare administrators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag national healthcare benefit administrators (>5M covered lives, multi-state) as preferred targets for ShinyHunters and similar groups. Reduce SOC alert thresholds for network-access and data-movement anomalies; escalate VPN/RDP authentication failures faster.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Domain Mimicking Open-Source Tool Name
suggestion.rationale: Article headline states 'Fake Sites Mimicking Open-Source Tools Rank High on Google'—direct attack surface. No domain IOCs extracted, yet this is the primary delivery vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries and HTTP requests to domains that closely resemble legitimate open-source tool names (e.g., typosquats, subdomain spoofing, .io/.co variants). Pair with geolocation and domain reputation checks to identify newly registered or low-trust registrants.

suggestion.title: Malware Download from Suspicious Domain Offering OSS Tool
suggestion.rationale: Article describes delivery of 'malware via TDS'—victims download malicious installers from fake sites. No file-based detection created despite clear executable delivery step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution initiated from unusual download paths correlated with suspicious domain HTTP requests. Monitor for execution of tools with names closely matching legitimate OSS projects but from non-standard installation paths.

suggestion.title: Traffic Direction Service (TDS) Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'TDS' in headline as delivery mechanism. TDS infrastructure patterns (HTTP 302 redirects, user-agent inspection, geolocation-based routing) should be detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect TDS behavior: HTTP 302/307 redirects from attacker-controlled domain to payload server, conditional on request metadata (AS number, user-agent, referer). Alert on multiple payload domains behind single redirect endpoint.

suggestion.title: Malicious Search Engine Ranking / SEO Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article states sites 'Rank High on Google'—search engine abuse is the distribution channel. No detection of browser traffic from search results to malicious domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP Referer header pointing to Google/search engine followed by redirect to suspicious domain. Correlate with known typosquat patterns and newly registered domains. Flag users clicking ads or high-ranked results on malicious clones.

suggestion.title: Installer Masquerading as Legitimate OSS Tool
suggestion.rationale: Attack hinges on visual/functional mimicry: 'Fake Sites Mimicking Open-Source Tools.' No detection for file metadata or signature anomalies indicating disguised malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on executables with names matching legitimate OSS (e.g., 'vscode-installer.exe', 'kubectl.exe') lacking authentic code signatures or bearing unfamiliar publisher metadata. Cross-reference against known OSS SHA256 hashes to identify imposters.

suggestion.title: Post-Execution C2 Beacon from Malware
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline stopped after delivery; no detection for post-execution command-and-control activity that malware would establish after installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTP/HTTPS or DNS traffic from recently executed suspicious installers. Alert on beaconing patterns (regular intervals, suspicious domains, non-standard ports) consistent with C2 communication.

suggestion.title: macOS: Suspicious Installer Execution from ~/Downloads with Unsigned Signature
suggestion.rationale: Article states FlutterShell 'spreads to macOS via malicious...ads,' implying trojanized installer delivery. Legitimate macOS installers (.dmg, .pkg) execute from user-writable directories; detection should flag unsigned or code-signature-mismatched execution from Downloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .pkg or .dmg execution from ~/Downloads with missing or invalid code signatures, then correlate with immediate process spawning (installer processes often fork helpers). Alert on parent process being Finder, Safari, Chrome, or other browsers.

suggestion.title: macOS: LaunchAgent Creation by Non-System Process Post-Download
suggestion.rationale: macOS backdoors maintain persistence via ~/Library/LaunchAgents plist files. Article implies FlutterShell persists after installation; this is the standard mechanism for user-level backdoor survival across reboots.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation or modification in ~/Library/LaunchAgents by processes spawned from Downloads, /tmp, or /var/tmp directories within 5 minutes of suspicious installer execution. Flag if plist contains shell or script-based execution (ProgramArguments with /bin/sh, curl, python).

suggestion.title: Ad Network Referrer to Suspicious Download Domain Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'malicious Google and YouTube ads' as delivery vector. Detection must capture HTTP referer chain from ad platforms to malware download sites.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP referer headers from google.com/ads or youtube.com redirecting to .dmg or .pkg downloads on newly-registered or low-reputation domains. Cross-reference download domain with threat feeds (C2, malware distribution sites).

suggestion.title: Unexpected Network Egress from macOS Backdoor Process to Non-Apple Destinations
suggestion.rationale: Backdoors establish C2 post-execution. Without specific domains in article, detection pattern should identify anomalous outbound connections from installer-spawned processes to non-RFC-1918, non-Apple, non-CDN destinations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate process creation from suspicious installer with HTTPS/HTTP connections to non-Apple domains. Flag if destination has recently-registered domain, low Alexa rank, or reputation score < 30. Baseline against Apple Software Update and App Store CDNs.

suggestion.title: Dylib or Framework Injection by FlutterShell Installer Helper Process
suggestion.rationale: Sophisticated macOS backdoors use dylib hijacking or process injection for stealth. Article does not explicitly describe this, but code-execution persistence on macOS frequently exploits DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES or similar mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process environment variables (DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES, DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH) set by downloaded or suspicious installer-spawned processes. Detect execution of unsigned dylib files from non-standard library paths (/tmp, ~/Downloads, /var/tmp).

suggestion.title: Stored XSS-to-admin-session-hijack via YPTSocket metadata broadcast
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'execute[s] arbitrary JavaScript in the authenticated origin of every administrator currently viewing'—direct path to session token theft. Pipeline detected injection but not downstream session compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for exfiltration patterns following YPTSocket XSS injection: outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from admin IPs to non-AVideo domains with Base64-encoded or URL-encoded credential patterns; WebSocket frames with cookie/token content; unusual external API calls from authenticated admin sessions immediately post-XSS injection.

suggestion.title: Anomalous AVideo administrator privilege abuse post-XSS injection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes vulnerability affects 'every administrator currently viewing'—stored payload ensures persistence across admin sessions. Should detect privilege escalation via hijacked admin sessions or unauthorized administrative actions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag administrative account actions from new/unexpected source IPs, geographic anomalies, or unusual admin API calls (user creation, permission changes, config modifications) immediately following YPTSocket plugin requests from unauthenticated or non-admin origins.

suggestion.title: Malicious metadata injection into YPTSocket WebSocket broadcast frames
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly involves 'Per-Client Metadata Broadcast in YPTSocket Plugin'—attack vector is metadata pollution in WebSocket frames. No detection of malicious payload structures in broadcast metadata.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WebSocket traffic to YPTSocket for page_title and webSocketSelfURI metadata parameters containing HTML/JavaScript indicators: '<' characters, script/img/iframe/svg tags, event handlers (onerror, onload, onmouse*), javascript: protocol, or String.fromCharCode patterns within metadata broadcast frames.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Mailbox Forwarding Rule Added to Executive Account
suggestion.rationale: Five-month 'spying' on mailbox requires persistent access mechanism. Forwarding rules are the primary persistence vector in mailbox compromise. Article phrase: 'spied on... Outlook Mailbox for five months.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of forwarding rules on executive mailboxes that forward to external domains or rare recipients, especially if created outside business hours or by a different user account. Cross-reference with new mailbox delegates.

suggestion.title: Impossible Travel or Anomalous Geographic Sign-in to Outlook
suggestion.rationale: Article describes extended unauthorized mailbox access. Attacker must have authenticated or maintained a session. 'Spied on... for five months' implies repeated access from attacker-controlled location.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sign-ins from geographically impossible locations within hours of legitimate user activity, or from flagged/Tor IPs. Correlate with failed MFA attempts and app-password creation in preceding days.

suggestion.title: IMAP/POP Legacy Protocol Enabled and Accessed on Mailbox
suggestion.rationale: Five-month dwell time suggests attacker used legacy mail protocols to bypass modern conditional-access and session controls. No mention in article of detection method rules out modern Outlook clients.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect enablement of IMAP/POP protocols on accounts previously mail-client-only. Alert when IMAP/POP sessions originate from non-corporate ASNs or access archive folders at unusual scale.

suggestion.title: Bulk Email Export or Search Operations on Compromised Mailbox
suggestion.rationale: Attacker conducting five-month surveillance would exfiltrate sensitive emails. 'Spied on mailbox' implies systematic collection beyond occasional reads. Article does not describe detection method, suggesting data left the system.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-volume mailbox search operations, eDiscovery requests, or PST file creation/download on executive accounts. Alert on searches for keywords tied to market-sensitive or M&A activity.

suggestion.title: New Application or App-Password Token Created for Persistent Mailbox Access
suggestion.rationale: Five-month undetected access suggests attacker obtained OAuth token, app password, or refresh token rather than using stolen credentials directly. 'Outlook' access could indicate app-based compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect new OAuth applications granted Mail.Read or Mail.ReadWrite scopes to executive accounts. Alert on app-password creation tied to IMAP/POP access. Correlate with suspicious token redemptions.

suggestion.title: Email Rule or Inbox Filtering to Hide Exfiltration Activity
suggestion.rationale: Five-month undetected compromise suggests attacker hid forwarding/exfiltration activity. New rules that auto-delete, move, or suppress forwarded emails prevent executive from discovering breach.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rules created by non-owner accounts or rules that suppress, move, or delete emails immediately after forwarding. Alert on rules with conditions matching C-suite domains or keywords, especially if timestamps cluster around compromises.

suggestion.title: Network Connections to FlutterBridge C2 Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists 8 C2 domains and describes malware 'sends encrypted network traffic to command-and-control servers.' This is the primary detection vector for active compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network connections from macOS endpoints to the 8 FlutterBridge C2 domains (atsheisdomestic.org, etoftheappyrince.org, healightejustb.org, sinterfumesco.com, ads-parkpro.com, adsparkpro.top, adsparkpro.net, softwe.art). Flag both successful connections and DNS resolution attempts, accounting for encrypted tunnels (T1071 Application Layer Protocol).

suggestion.title: FlutterShell Backdoor Hash Detection
suggestion.rationale: Nine SHA256 hashes of the malware samples provided in IOC section. This is high-confidence install-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match process creation and file write events against the 9 provided SHA256 hashes (including 021666417de8b9972c179783fe60d4c4ad2d93224e3a0f16137065c960b1b845, 363923500ce942bf1a953e8a4e943fbf1fb1b5ed6e5d247964c345b3ad5bfc34, and 7 others). Detection should cover execution from ~/Downloads, /tmp, and standard installer paths common to fake app delivery.

suggestion.title: Malicious Google Ad Click-to-Fake-App Downloads
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Threat actors are using Google Ads to push fake desktop applications.' This is the initial access vector and should trigger on suspicious ad domains and landing-page patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify users clicking Google ads that redirect to any of the 8 C2 domains or lookalike app-store domains. Flag downloads of suspicious .dmg, .zip, or .pkg files from ads-parkpro subdomains and similarly suspicious parent domains. Correlate ad traffic patterns with FlutterShell hash executions within 30 minutes.

suggestion.title: macOS Launch Agent / Plist Persistence After FlutterShell Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware 'secretly install[ing] a powerful backdoor on infected machines.' macOS backdoors typically establish persistence via plist modification in LaunchAgents or LaunchDaemons.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor creation or modification of plist files in ~/Library/LaunchAgents, ~/Library/LaunchDaemons, /Library/LaunchAgents, and /Library/LaunchDaemons on endpoints that have seen FlutterShell hash execution or C2 domain contact. Look for unsigned or suspicious RunAtLoad, ProgramArguments pointing to /tmp, /var/tmp, or unusual app directories.

suggestion.title: macOS Gatekeeper/Quarantine Flag Bypass for Fake App Execution
suggestion.rationale: Fake applications downloaded via ads would trigger Gatekeeper checks on modern macOS; successful execution implies quarantine attribute removal. Article's mechanism requires this bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of unsigned Mach-O binaries or .app bundles that lack the com.apple.quarantine extended attribute, or that have had it explicitly removed via xattr -d. Correlate with recent .dmg mount or .zip extraction events from Downloads folder and subsequent hash match to FlutterShell samples.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Downloads from Advertisement/Parking Domains
suggestion.rationale: Eight ad/parking domains are used in distribution. Article's attack vector is 'using Google Ads to push fake desktop applications'—detection must cover the ad-to-download phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any .dmg, .zip, .pkg, .tar.gz, or installer-like file downloads from the ad-parking domains (ads-parkpro.com, adsparkpro.top, adsparkpro.net, softwe.art) or from any parent domain sharing DNS history with these. Baseline against legitimate software distribution; flag if download is followed by Finder/Archive extraction and application execution.

suggestion.title: PowerShell Encoded Command Execution Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article describes cmd.exe spawning powershell.exe with -EncodedCommand parameter containing Base64-encoded payload: 'A cmd.exe process spawning powershell.exe with an -EncodedCommand parameter containing a Base64-encoded payload.' This is high-fidelity attack pattern observed in KongTuke C2 case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cmd.exe spawning powershell.exe with -EncodedCommand parameter. Decode Base64 payload and analyze for suspicious function calls (Invoke-WebRequest, DownloadString, etc.). Strong indicator of living-off-the-land payload delivery.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Outbound C2 Connection on Uncommon Port
suggestion.rationale: KongTuke case shows: 'outbound ConnectionEvents to "144.31.221.82" on port 6060, with a URL path of /capcha9856.' This is confirmed C2 connection pattern that should trigger detection across customer environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound connections to 144.31.221.82:6060 or similar TDS redirect patterns. Correlate with endpoint process data (Invoke-WebRequest, curl.exe) to confirm C2 communication. Port 6060 on non-standard infrastructure is high-risk indicator.

suggestion.title: Invoke-WebRequest to Known C2 Infrastructure with File Drop
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The decoded payload executing Invoke-WebRequest to fetch a file named script.ps1, dropping it into the user's ApplicationData directory.' This fetch-and-drop pattern is characteristic of KongTuke delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell executing Invoke-WebRequest to fetch .ps1 files to non-standard ports or suspicious ASNs. Alert if destination file is dropped to ApplicationData, Temp, or other low-visibility directories. Baseline legitimate PowerShell requests to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Anti-Forensics: Remove-Item Cleanup
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies: 'Post-execution cleanup via Remove-Item, attempting to delete traces of the downloaded script.' This defensive behavior immediately following suspicious activity is strong indicator of confirmed intrusion rather than false positive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Remove-Item or del commands executed in user ApplicationData or Temp directories within 60 seconds of suspicious file drops or process execution. Correlate with prior Invoke-WebRequest or PowerShell download activity. Cleanup pattern significantly elevates confidence in confirmed compromise.

suggestion.title: Python User-Agent to Malicious ASN
suggestion.rationale: Article lists threat hunt: 'Python User-Agent connections to malicious ASN infrastructure. Legitimate Python HTTP requests exist in most environments, but Python calling out to hosting providers with poor reputation scores is a different signal entirely.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests with Python User-Agent (requests, urllib, boto3, etc.) to ASNs with documented C2 hosting history or poor reputation scores. Baseline legitimate Python requests in environment (CI/CD, monitoring agents), then alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: MSIEXEC User-Agent to Suspicious ASN (LOTL)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'MSIEXEC User-Agent making connections to suspicious or malicious ASNs. MSIEXEC fetching remote packages is a known living-off-the-land (LOTL) technique. The user-agent string persists in firewall connection logs even when the payload itself is encrypted.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound HTTP connections with MSIEXEC User-Agent to non-standard ports or suspicious ASNs. MSIEXEC LOTL execution is difficult to detect at endpoint; network User-Agent is persistent indicator even when payload is encrypted.

suggestion.title: Suspicious node-gyp or Native Module Execution During npm Install
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'binding-gyp-npm-supply-chain-attack' — binding.gyp is the native module build file executed by node-gyp during install, enabling arbitrary code execution before/after package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when node.exe, npm.exe, or node-gyp spawn powershell.exe, cmd.exe, or curl/wget during package installation. Correlate unexpected child process creation from npm parent with binding.gyp file writes or modifications to native module dependencies.

suggestion.title: npm Package Self-Replication via Transitive Dependency Injection
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Self-Spreading Worm' — worm propagation in npm requires automatic injection of malicious packages into downstream consumer's node_modules/package-lock.json, creating transitive infection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package-lock.json for unexpected entries that do not appear in source package.json. Flag when npm packages add transitive dependencies with gyp-related keywords, native bindings, or low/zero publisher reputation after package installation completes.

suggestion.title: Network Exfiltration or C2 Contact from npm/Node.js Process
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'spreads-like-worm' — worm replication requires C2 signaling or lateral propagation. Article URL references StepSecurity published threat; worm behavior implies network-based propagation or command coordination.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate outbound HTTP/HTTPS or DNS queries from npm/node processes during package installation with zero historical baseline. Alert on connections to newly-registered domains, low-reputation IPs, or non-standard npm registries initiated from npm install workflows.

suggestion.title: Preinstall/Postinstall Script Injection in package.json
suggestion.rationale: npm package.json supports preinstall/postinstall lifecycle hooks that execute shell commands. Worm propagation vector likely leverages malicious scripts in these fields to replicate and execute payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse package.json scripts for encoded payloads, obfuscated JavaScript, or shell commands (curl, wget, git clone from suspicious sources). Cross-reference package version history against publisher baseline—alert on script field changes in minor/patch versions or from low-reputation publishers.

suggestion.title: Phantom Gyp or Spoofed Native Module Dependency
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'Phantom Gyp' — suggests attacker spoofed or injected a fake gyp-related package name (typosquatting, namespace confusion, or direct registry account compromise).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry API calls and .npmrc configurations for lookups of packages with names similar to legitimate gyp tools (e.g., gyp, node-gyp variants). Flag installation of packages with single/few downloads, newly-created publishers, or versions released immediately after legitimate package updates.

suggestion.title: Recursive Dependency Chain Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Self-Spreading Worm via Phantom Gyp' — worm self-replication requires the malicious package to inject itself or related packages into the dependency graphs of multiple consumers, creating exponential spread.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Analyze package-lock.json for circular or unintended dependency cycles, packages with no legitimate upstream consumer, or injection of packages into transitive slots that differ from lock file baselines. Alert when a package version rapidly increases its downstream dependents (dependency explosion pattern).

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Publishing from Compromised Account
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the latest attack started from a compromised account named asteroiddao, which published package versions containing the Rust ELF binary executed via preinstall'—detection needed for unusual publisher behavior and first-time publishers with executable payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm for publishing from accounts with no historical publish activity. Alert on packages published with preinstall scripts executing compiled binaries (ELF). Cross-reference against commit metadata for suspicious author names (e.g., generic 'claude') or timestamp anomalies (commits older than repository creation).

suggestion.title: Credential File Access During Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malware targets 86 environment variables and 20 credential files that may contain OpenAI, AWS, Anthropic, npm credentials, vault configuration files, SSH keys, and Exodus cryptocurrency wallet files'—detect file access from package context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file reads from ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.npm, ~/.vault, or cryptocurrency wallet directories when spawned from npm install processes or preinstall hooks. Baseline normal access per environment and flag bulk access to multiple credential paths in single execution. Detect serialization of multiple files into single output.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Artifact Exfiltration of Serialized Secrets
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malware serializes the secrets into a single value and then writes it to a file with a harmless-looking name, as if it were lint or formatting output...uploading the file as a build artifact, which can be downloaded by anyone with access. This way, the threat actor can avoid the need for an external command-and-control (C2) altogether.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions artifact uploads for files with generic/benign names (eslint-report, format-output, .lint) containing JSON or serialized credential patterns. Alert on artifact downloads from unexpected authentication contexts or IP ranges. Detect workflows that serialize env vars before artifact upload.

suggestion.title: Backdated Git Commits with Spoofed Author Names
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'commit author appears as claude, and the timestamps point to several years ago, up to 13 years in some cases, even though they were pushed in the past few days. This is likely to evade investigation.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag commits where commit timestamp predates repository creation or is significantly older than push timestamp. Alert on generic/suspicious author names (claude, admin, root, system) in supply-chain repos. Detect multiple commits with identical or sequential timestamps pushed in batches (automated tool behavior).

suggestion.title: eBPF Rootkit Installation from Package Context
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'IronWorm is written in Rust, hides behind an eBPF kernel rootkit'—this is kernel-level persistence installed from userspace npm package, requiring detection of BPF program loading.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bpf() syscalls (SYS_BPF) with BPF_PROG_LOAD from processes spawned during npm install. Alert on eBPF programs with suspicious instruction patterns (network redirection, syscall hooks). Baseline expected eBPF programs and detect new unsigned programs loaded from package execution contexts.

suggestion.title: Rust ELF Execution via npm Preinstall Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'published package versions containing the Rust ELF binary executed via preinstall'—detect preinstall execution of compiled binaries with credential access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on preinstall scripts in npm packages that execute compiled binaries (ELF/PE) instead of interpreted scripts. Detect child processes from npm install with anomalous resource patterns (network connections, credential file access). Flag Rust-compiled binaries by stripped symbol tables or absence of standard Go/Node runtime markers in preinstall contexts.

suggestion.title: binding.gyp Command Substitution Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states core attack: 'GYP's build configuration syntax supports command expansion. The <!(…) form runs a shell command during the configure phase and substitutes its output into the build definition. The compromised packages abuse this directly.' This is the novel execution vector that bypasses preinstall/postinstall monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on binding.gyp files containing `<!(` command expansion syntax during npm install. Detect node-gyp rebuild execution that lacks corresponding preinstall/postinstall hooks in package.json—this is install-time execution without script declarations, highly anomalous.

suggestion.title: Rapid Package Re-publish from Single Maintainer Account
suggestion.rationale: Article documents worm propagation: 'the worm enumerates and republishes everything one compromised account can touch' with 25 autotel-* packages and 'Many of the inflated version numbers…are themselves a side effect of the worm's automated republishing' (e.g., autotel-mcp 0.1.14 → 29.0.1, multiple versions in same minute).
