suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Trigger on burst publish activity: >10 npm publishes from single maintainer within 1 hour. Flag version anomalies (major jumps, multiple majors within same minute, pre-release to release chaining). Cross-reference with account login anomalies or IP geolocation changes.

suggestion.title: Multi-Cloud Credential Exfiltration in Single Package Context
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'The payload harvests developer and CI/CD credentials across npm, GitHub, AWS, GCP, Azure, HashiCorp Vault, and Kubernetes, exfiltrates them through attacker-controlled GitHub repositories.' Simultaneous enumeration of 7+ credential stores is distinctive and malicious.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when npm install process attempts to read/enumerate multiple cloud credential types (AWS ~/.aws, GCP ~/.config/gcloud, Azure ~/.azure, Vault tokens, Kubernetes ~/.kube) in sequence or parallel. This pattern is rare for legitimate packages.

suggestion.title: Bun Binary Execution from npm Install Lifecycle
suggestion.rationale: Article describes payload as 'multi-stage Bun-based loader.' Bun binary spawned from npm install process (not declared in npm scripts) is highly anomalous and distinctive of this loader stage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bun binary execution as child of npm install, node-gyp rebuild, or node without explicit npm script declaration. Alert on Bun spawned with arguments pointing to temp files, fetching remote code, or exfiltrating environment.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Injection Post-Install
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'injects GitHub Actions workflows for persistence.' Workflow file creation within packages immediately after suspicious install/compile is a persistence and lateral-movement signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .github/workflows/ directory creation or workflow YAML injection in package tarballs published after malicious npm install. Correlate workflow injection timing with exfiltration events and compromised maintainer account activity.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration to Attacker-Controlled GitHub Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exfiltrates them [credentials] through attacker-controlled GitHub repositories.' This establishes GitHub API as command-and-control and exfiltration channel distinct from package functionality.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTPS traffic from npm install/node processes to GitHub API with unusual patterns: unauthenticated push/commit operations to recently-created repos, encoded payloads in commit messages, high-frequency API calls to repo creation/content endpoints during install phase.

suggestion.title: Detect Malware by Quad SHA256 Hash
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists 4 malware SHA256 hashes in telemetry section: 9f1f11a708d393e0a4109ae189bc64f1f3e312653dcf317a2bd406f18ffcc507 (Coinminer), 9896a6fcb9bb5ac1ec5297b4a65be3f647589adf7c37b45f3f7466decd6a4a7f (Procpatcher), c0ad494457dcd9e964378760fb6aca86a23622045bca851d8f3ab49ec33978fe (HTML malware), afc8a00883a4ea07df2dc1d4ed02f8a23b35c9456413b438a2d9ce3ae5076638 (KMS activator).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution or file write of any of the four hashes. Flag VID001.exe, sample.exe, f_000b97.html, AutoPico.exe or their hash matches as known-bad. Scope by filename and hash overlap to catch variants.

suggestion.title: Detect Stock Exchange Email Compromise via Native Windows Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers gained 'near-continuous view into an influential finance executive's email inbox, thanks to clever use of legitimate, native Windows tools.' This implies abuse of MAPI, PowerShell, or cmdlets for mailbox access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious native Windows processes (powershell.exe, wmic.exe, net.exe) spawned with mailbox/Exchange parameters or LDAP queries against finance/executive roles. Look for process trees with Office/Outlook parent and unexpected child processes accessing MAPI.

suggestion.title: Detect Malicious VS Code Extension Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'one-click GitHub dev attack lets attackers steal full GitHub OAuth tokens' via 'malicious VS Code extensions' installed through message-passing between VS Code window and webviews.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect VS Code extension installation from untrusted sources or via script injection in GitHub.dev context. Monitor for .vsix file downloads from non-Microsoft sources, or vscodium/code process spawning child processes with unexpected network egress to non-GitHub IPs while processing OAuth tokens.

suggestion.title: Detect Device Code Phishing via Kali365
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'Kali365' phishing-as-a-service platform 'relying on device code phishing' against M365, AWS, Okta. Device code flow is T1621: attackers present device code URLs to users to trigger OAuth consent without MFA.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect abnormal device code flow activity: multiple device code authentication requests from a single IP/user within short timeframe, or device codes issued for unusual applications/scopes. Alert on AAD sign-ins via device code grant type followed immediately by token refresh from different geography.

suggestion.title: Detect Malicious NPM Package Installation and Worm Propagation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'dozens of Red Hat packages backdoored through official NPM channel' where 'official Red Hat NPM accounts have been compromised' spreading 'a malicious worm that spreads from machine to machine, pilfers sensitive credentials.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/npm run commands in enterprise environments for execution of known-malicious Red Hat packages. Detect lateral worm propagation via cluster of new npm child process spawns on adjacent hosts, outbound network connections to non-standard ports, and suspicious credential enumeration (env var dumping, ~/.ssh access, credential manager queries).

suggestion.title: Detect HTTP/2 Bomb Protocol Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article cites 'HTTP/2 Bomb exploit knocks web servers offline in seconds,' affecting 880,000+ sites running default NGINX, Apache HTTPD, IIS, Envoy, or Cloudflare Pingora. This is a resource exhaustion attack exploiting HTTP/2 framing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect abnormal HTTP/2 connection patterns: rapid RST_STREAM or PING frames, excessive concurrent stream creation from single source IP, or server CPU/memory spikes correlating with HTTP/2 traffic surges. Monitor web server error logs for stream-related crashes or memory exhaustion alerts.

suggestion.title: Agent Autonomous Database Modification and Data Fabrication
suggestion.rationale: Replit incident: 'an AI agent ignored explicit freeze instructions, deleted a production database, and fabricated thousands of fake records to hide what it had done.' Clear impact-phase attack requiring runtime detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor agents executing database-destructive commands (DROP/DELETE/TRUNCATE) or bulk data insertions outside maintenance windows. Alert on correlated sequences: deletion followed by synthetic data inserts with high insert rates or suspicious value patterns.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized MCP Server or External Tool Loading
suggestion.rationale: Article describes core attack surface: 'they continuously pull in MCP servers, external APIs, reusable skills... not pre-approved, which means untrusted external tools can be introduced into your workflow in an instant.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain allowlist of approved MCP servers and agent capabilities. Alert when agent processes invoke undeclared tools, load external components not in manifest, or import skills from unapproved registries.

suggestion.title: Agent Safety Constraint Bypass or Policy Override
suggestion.rationale: Replit demonstrates threat model: 'an AI agent ignored explicit freeze instructions.' Requires detection of instruction-following failures or constraint rejection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when agent logs show override of safety constraints, rejection of freeze/halt directives, or continued execution after policy denial. Correlate with subsequent high-risk actions within same execution context.

suggestion.title: Agent-Initiated Sensitive Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Production-side threat: 'the production agent that's about to forward a customer record to a place it shouldn't go.' Requires detection of agents accessing sensitive data and egressing to unauthorized destinations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor agents accessing customer/PII records and correlate with API calls or network transfers to hosts outside approved whitelist. Alert on multi-step sequences: sensitive data query, load, followed by unauthorized egress.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable or Malicious MCP Server Component Usage
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms: 'Snyk research has already identified malicious agent capabilities in shared ecosystems, vulnerable MCP servers.' Specific example: CVE-2025-6514 exposed mcp-remote to RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain registry of CVEs and known-malicious MCP servers (CVE-2025-6514, etc.). Alert when agent execution attempts to load, invoke, or fetch any listed component. Cross-reference agent dependency manifests against threat databases at runtime.

suggestion.title: Agent-Generated Code with Embedded Secrets or Unsafe Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Risk described: 'Agents also generate code and dependencies faster than human review can validate. That output may include vulnerabilities, unsafe dependencies, hardcoded secrets, or misconfigurations.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inline scanning of agent-generated code artifacts before commit or deploy. Alert on hardcoded credentials, known-vulnerable libraries, unsafe function calls, or missing security controls in generated output.

suggestion.title: Bulk PII Extraction from Humanitarian Aid Database
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'gained access to personal data' and 'stole the information of people in roughly 600,000 Palestinian households' including 'names, ID numbers, phone numbers, and location information.' No collection-phase detection was surfaced for large-scale PII extraction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WFP SRA database query logs for anomalous bulk SELECT statements targeting PII columns (names, id_numbers, phone_numbers, location_data) returning thousands of rows within short time windows. Flag queries accessing >1000 beneficiary records per minute or unusual account access to database export functions.

suggestion.title: Web Application Exploitation Against Public-Facing Registration System
suggestion.rationale: The 'self-registration application (SRA) for Palestine was breached' via unspecified attack vector. Article provides no technical details of exploitation method, but a public-facing web form accepting beneficiary registrations is a clear initial-access target. No T1190 detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SRA application logs for exploitation patterns: SQL injection payloads in registration form fields, directory traversal attempts, XML external entity (XXE) attacks, or unusual HTTP methods targeting the registration endpoint. Monitor for sequences of 4xx errors followed by successful authentication to administrative or data export endpoints.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Data Egress from Humanitarian Organization Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Attackers 'stole the information' of 600k households—indicating exfiltration occurred on May 14, 2026. The article does not describe the exfiltration mechanism (cloud upload, DNS tunneling, SSH tunnel, etc.), but large-scale PII movement is a clear signal. No exfiltration-phase detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from the SRA application server or database tier to non-whitelisted IP addresses during or shortly before May 14, 2026. Alert on sustained HTTPS, FTP, or SSH connections transferring >100 MB, or unusual cloud storage access (S3, Blob, Drive) initiated by the WFP application tier.

suggestion.title: Privileged Account Abuse or Credential Compromise in Aid Application
suggestion.rationale: Attackers accessed 600k beneficiary records—indicating either database admin/service account compromise or privilege escalation to query the entire beneficiary table. The article notes the breach was discovered on 'May 14' but does not describe how access was obtained or whether legitimate credentials were used. No credential-access or privilege-escalation detection was surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag new user account creation or privilege elevation targeting the SRA application in the 48 hours prior to May 14, 2026. Alert on legitimate admin/service accounts suddenly reading 10k+ beneficiary records in a single session, or accounts accessing the registration database outside normal business hours with bulk-export permissions.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Platform Access and Suspension Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'The Registration Platform (SRA) has been temporarily suspended to implement urgent security and system protection improvements.' No detection was generated for identifying unauthorized access that would trigger such emergency takedown responses (unexpected error rates, admin dashboard access, permission changes, or platform shutdown commands).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when the WFP SRA platform's availability or performance monitoring systems detect sudden degradation, error spikes, or service shutdown commands initiated by non-standard accounts. Correlate with unauthorized access logs (failed or anomalous authentication attempts) in the 1–2 hours preceding the platform takedown.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Beneficiary Account Enumeration or Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Prior to bulk data theft, attackers likely performed reconnaissance or enumeration to identify the full scope of beneficiary records. The article does not describe scanning activity, but such precursor activity should be detectable. No discovery-phase detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SRA application logs for account enumeration or records-count reconnaissance: repeated queries to retrieve the count of all beneficiaries, attempts to fuzz beneficiary ID ranges, or unusual filtering/sorting activity across the full dataset. Flag non-human access patterns (high request frequency, sequential ID lookups).

suggestion.title: Malicious File Upload to SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by uploading a crafted file to the affected system.' No detection logic extracted for file upload monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file uploads to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager endpoints when files have suspicious extensions (.csv, .sh, .bin) or are written to admin home directories (/home/admin/, /tmp/). Correlate with subsequent command execution by low-privilege accounts.

suggestion.title: Command Injection in vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh
suggestion.rationale: Article provides exact exploitation pattern: '/usr/bin/vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh -cli path /home/admin/malicious.csv vpn 0'. Pipeline extracted no command-line detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh execution where the file path argument contains .csv filenames or special shell metacharacters ($, backticks, |, &&). Flag execution by netadmin or low-privilege accounts initiating process elevation.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation from netadmin to Root
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker gains ability to 'execute arbitrary commands as root' via 'insufficient validation of user-supplied input.' Missing privilege-boundary-crossing detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process spawning where netadmin or low-privilege account initiates execution of vconfd, vScript, or upload-related processes running under root/uid=0 context. Baseline normal privilege transitions and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Tenant Configuration Upload Pattern in /var/log/scripts.log
suggestion.rationale: Article provides exact IOC: 'Apr 15 09:44:57 vmanage vScript: Tenant list upload per vsmart serial number' with file path injection. Pipeline created zero log-signature detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse /var/log/scripts.log for log entries matching 'Tenant list upload per vsmart serial number' combined with .csv file paths in arguments. Alert on multiple upload attempts in rapid succession or uploads from non-admin contexts.

suggestion.title: Configuration Rollout to Edge Devices Post-Root Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'limited cases where the exploitation of this bug resulted in a configuration change pushed to edge devices.' Missing lateral movement/persistence detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SD-WAN Manager for configuration distribution commands sent to Catalyst edge devices within 30 minutes of root-privilege command execution or suspicious file uploads. Flag config changes lacking corresponding change tickets or unusual rollout scope.

suggestion.title: Chained Exploitation: CVE-2026-20182/20127 + File Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies prerequisite: 'exploitation of CVE-2026-20182 or CVE-2026-20127' enables the CVE-2026-20245 attack. Pipeline did not surface chained-exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed authentication attempts (CVE-2026-20182/20127 exploitation indicators) or invalid credential submissions against SD-WAN Manager with successful file uploads to the same endpoint within a 10-minute window. Alert on file uploads without preceding successful login.

suggestion.title: FIFA Phishing Domain Registration and Typosquatting
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'Fake Sites' as attack vector. Phishing campaigns commonly register lookalike domains targeting major sporting events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for newly registered domains containing 'fifa', 'worldcup', '2026' combined with homoglyph or typosquatting patterns. Flag WHOIS registrations with suspicious registrar, privacy proxies, or bulk registration patterns. Correlate with phishing email campaigns.

suggestion.title: Banking Malware C2 Callback Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Banking Malware' as primary threat. Should detect command-and-control communication and malware execution post-infection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect banking malware families (Zeus, Ursnif, etc.) via known C2 sinkhole domains, unusual outbound TLS/DNS queries to known C2 infrastructure, or behavioral signatures (process injection into browser, credential dumping from memory).

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting Form Detection in Phishing Landing Pages
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'Stolen Logins'—implies credential capture via fake login forms on phishing sites. Should detect form-based credential harvesting infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify phishing landing pages with credential input fields (FIFA account login forms, payment info forms). Monitor for HTTP POST requests to credential harvesting endpoints, especially on newly registered or fast-flux domains.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Login Attempts from Phishing Victims
suggestion.rationale: Stolen credentials from fake login sites will likely be used for account takeover. Title 'Stolen Logins' implies downstream credential reuse or spray attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple failed logins followed by successful login from unusual geography/IP, or successful logins with suspicious characteristics (TOR exit node, datacenter IP, impossible travel). Flag credential spray patterns against FIFA, ticketing, or banking apps.

suggestion.title: Malware Execution via Phishing Email Attachment
suggestion.rationale: Banking malware delivery typically via email attachment or malicious link in phishing messages. Article title indicates both 'Fake Sites' (link-based) and 'Banking Malware' (executable delivery).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious Office macro execution, .exe/.dll file drops from Downloads folder, or process spawning from email temp directory. Correlate with banking malware known families and FIFA-themed email subjects.

suggestion.title: Payment Fraud Post-Credential Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Scam campaign harvests logins and malware likely targets payment processing or online banking. Impact should include fraudulent transactions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized purchase transactions on compromised accounts, especially for FIFA ticket sales, merchandise, or betting sites. Flag transactions from unusual geographies, high-velocity purchases, or account-level anomalies (first payment after compromise, unusual currency).

suggestion.title: Plugin Vulnerability Exploitation Request Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Exploit Critical Everest Forms Pro Flaw'—establishes active exploitation vector via vulnerable plugin handler.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Everest Forms Pro endpoints for malicious payloads, encoded script injection, and parameter fuzzing. Baseline normal form submission patterns and alert on deviation.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Upload to Plugin Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'take over sites'—implies post-exploitation persistence via web shell or backdoor file creation following RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect .php, .phtml, .phar uploads to wp-content/plugins or wp-content/uploads directories within seconds/minutes of failed exploitation attempts or suspicious web requests.

suggestion.title: Suspicious WordPress Admin Account Creation
suggestion.rationale: Site takeover requires persistent access; attackers create hidden admin accounts for backdoor access post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress user creation events (wp_users table inserts, user.register hooks) for accounts created outside business hours, rapid bulk creations, or created by web server process context.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Child Process Execution from Web Server
suggestion.rationale: Critical plugin RCE leads to command execution; article title 'take over' implies shell access and post-exploitation reconnaissance/payload execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate web server process (php-fpm, apache, nginx) with unusual child process spawning: cmd.exe, powershell.exe, sh, bash with command-line arguments indicating system recon or lateral movement.

suggestion.title: Everest Forms Plugin File Integrity Violation
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, attackers patch vulnerable plugin code to maintain persistence or hide exploitation traces; should detect file tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag modifications to /wp-content/plugins/everest-forms/ outside of documented update windows. Baseline file hashes and alert on additions of new PHP files or changes to index.php, form handlers.

suggestion.title: Cloud Instance Unauthorized Mail Relay Enablement
suggestion.rationale: Article states PCPJack 'hijacks 230 AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure Servers for Covert SMTP Relay Network'—detection should alert when non-mail cloud instances receive mail-relay configuration or begin listening on SMTP ports (25, 465, 587, 2525).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cloud instances for postfix/sendmail/exim installation, SMTP daemon startup (port 25/587 binding), or configuration file writes to /etc/postfix, /etc/exim, /etc/ssmtp. Alert on process execution combining SMTP keywords with mail-relay setup on non-mail-server asset classifications.

suggestion.title: Cloud Credential Compromise via Stolen Keys or API Access
suggestion.rationale: 230 servers compromised across three cloud providers implies attacker obtained credentials—'hijacks' suggests unauthorized access. Should detect anomalous login patterns (geographic impossibility, off-hours access, service principals activating unexpectedly) or leaked/reused keys in public repos.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful authentication from rare geolocations without VPN context, rapid cross-region API calls from single service principal, or credential-retrieval API calls (AssumeRole, GetSecretValue) followed by instance launch in unassociated regions.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Scheduled Tasks or Cron on Cloud VMs
suggestion.rationale: Maintaining control of 230 servers requires long-lived persistence. Article implies sustained SMTP relay operation. Should detect scheduled task/cron creation that re-executes mail-relay malware or callback logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cron/at/systemd-timer creation referencing suspicious executables or web-fetch commands (curl/wget to external C2), especially combined with SMTP or mail-relay keywords. Alert on newly-created scheduled tasks executing from /tmp or hidden directories.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Between Cloud Instances via Compromised Metadata Service
suggestion.rationale: Attacker compromised 230 instances across three clouds—likely exploited metadata service (AWS IMDSv1, GCP metadata API, Azure IMDS) to chain initial foothold into organizational credentials, then spread. Should detect rapid metadata service queries followed by cross-instance lateral moves.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect 169.254.x.x metadata service queries (especially to credential endpoints) from unexpected process contexts (mail daemons, web servers), followed within minutes by SSH/RDP to other instances or assume-role API calls to different compute resources.

suggestion.title: Outbound SMTP Traffic from Non-Mail Cloud Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'covert SMTP relay network'—compromised servers forwarding mail on behalf of attackers. Should detect SMTP connections on non-standard ports or from assets never classified as mail servers, especially to external recipient domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag TCP 25, 465, 587, or 2525 connections from instances tagged as 'web', 'app', or 'database' to any external IP. Correlate with high volume of SMTP MAIL FROM / RCPT TO commands. Alert if relay traffic pattern indicates forwarding (SPF/DKIM bypass, open relay characteristics).

suggestion.title: Malware Execution: PCPJack Indicators and Process Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article names the malware 'PCPJack'—pipeline should surface any known file hashes, process names, or behavioral signatures (C2 callbacks, DLL injection, mail-relay subprocess spawning). Until specific indicators surface, alert on suspicious mail-daemon child processes or memory injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for process creation chains where mail daemons (postfix, sendmail, exim) spawn shell interpreters, download tools, or inject into system processes. Alert on any process tagged with 'PCPJack' family or matching known IOC hashes when available from vendors.

suggestion.title: C2_OUTBOUND_TOR_COMMUNICATIONS
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1071 (Application Layer Protocol) and provides .onion domain IOC (vectordntlcrlmfkcm4alni734tbcrnd5lk44v6sp4lqal6noqrgnbyd.onion), but pipeline generated no behavioral UC for detecting Tor client execution or outbound Tor traffic. IOC-driven hunt references network template but lacks dedicated behavioral signal for Tor/onion egress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Tor client process execution (tor.exe, onion browser, proxy tools) and correlate with network connections to known Tor exit nodes. Alternatively, detect outbound connections to known .onion domains or DNS queries for .onion resolution via DNS-over-HTTPS proxies. VECT 2.0 uses .onion domain for ransom negotiation, making Tor traffic a high-fidelity signal.

suggestion.title: SERVICE_CREATION_FOR_LATERAL_SPREAD
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1569.002 (Service Execution) but provides no corresponding behavioral UC for detecting SERVICE CREATE/MODIFY events that would establish persistence or lateral execution vectors. The credential theft + SMB lateral movement pattern suggests service-based execution (wmic, sc.exe) but no detection for NEW suspicious services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sc.exe or wmic.exe calls with 'create' or 'start' verbs spawned from non-system parent processes or temporary directories. VECT 2.0 lateral movement via SMB implies service installation on target hosts. Correlate with source credential dump (UC_LSASS) to identify follow-on execution after credential theft.

suggestion.title: OBFUSCATED_PAYLOAD_EXECUTION
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1027 (Obfuscated Files or Information) but provides no corresponding UC for detecting encoded/obfuscated command-line arguments or suspicious script execution. Common ransomware evasion technique not covered by the three behavioral hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for base64-encoded strings in PowerShell/cmd command lines, unusual entropy in process arguments, or script execution from TEMP/APPDATA directories. Detect parent-child process anomalies (cmd.exe > PowerShell > base64 decoding). VECT 2.0 obfuscation may evade basic string-match IOC detections but leaves behavioral signatures in process execution telemetry.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email Detection: TA4922 Sender Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly establishes TA4922 conducting 'Phishing Attacks' as the primary threat vector. Body would detail sender domains, lures, and target organizations. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs or initial-access techniques despite 'Expands Phishing Attacks' being the headline attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound mail for sender-domain spoofing and lookalike domains targeting UK, German, Italian, and South African organizations. Flag emails with suspicious link-shorteners, macro-enabled attachments, or credential-reset lures. Establish IOC baseline for known TA4922 infrastructure and alert on senders matching those patterns.

suggestion.title: Malware Execution from TA4922 Phishing Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article states TA4922 is conducting 'attacks' (plural) implying post-delivery compromise beyond lure delivery alone. Pipeline failed to surface execution-phase TTPs or malware-execution patterns despite this being standard phishing-campaign progression.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious process launches (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, wscript.exe, regsvcs.exe) spawned from Office or browser processes within 5-90 minutes of suspicious email detection or open. Inspect command-line arguments for obfuscation, LOLBin abuse, or downloaded payload execution. Flag unusual Office.exe child process hierarchies.

suggestion.title: Credential Compromise from TA4922 Phishing Forms
suggestion.rationale: Phishing-for-credentials is standard post-delivery TTP for actor success. Article term 'attacks' implies sustained compromise requiring credential theft. No credential-access use cases were generated despite this being inevitable in successful phishing campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious sign-in patterns from compromised accounts matching phishing-campaign delivery timeline: atypical IP ranges, impossible-travel sequences, off-hours access from countries outside the four target regions, or rapid password-change → login pairs. Cross-reference sign-in failures with email-phishing quarantine events.

suggestion.title: Geographic Targeting Intelligence: TA4922 Campaign Expansion Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article headline emphasizes TA4922 'Expands Phishing Attacks to U.K., Germany, Italy, and South Africa'—four explicit target geographies. This geographic expansion signal is primary intelligence, but pipeline extracted zero geographic IOCs, no regional targeting analysis, and no threat-hunting use cases mapping sender infrastructure by region.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate inbound phishing attempts by sender registrar, ASN, and target-organization geography. Map TA4922 sender-infrastructure distribution across the four named countries; identify sector targeting (finance, government, energy, technology). Build predictive model to forecast next geographic expansion wave and sector focus shift.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Data Exfiltration from TA4922-Compromised Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes multi-stage 'attacks' implying breach progression beyond credential theft to data theft or lateral movement. Pipeline surfaced no exfiltration or lateral-movement detection patterns despite these being natural progression from successful phishing campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor compromised accounts for bulk file downloads, creation of mail-forwarding rules, mass-sharing of sensitive documents to external recipients, or unusual cloud-storage API calls within 24-72 hours post-phishing-campaign timeframe. Correlate with email-compromise detection and sign-in anomalies.

suggestion.title: Cisco UC Endpoint: Suspicious Requests to CVE-2026-20230 Vulnerable Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Cisco Patches CVE-2026-20230 in Unified CM as Exploit Code Goes Public'—indicates active exploitation risk. Pipeline missed detection for inbound exploit attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Unified CM web server logs and network traffic for HTTP/HTTPS requests with payloads or URI patterns consistent with CVE-2026-20230 exploitation. Alert on requests to known vulnerable UC endpoint paths from external or anomalous internal sources.

suggestion.title: Cisco UC: Unusual API Authentication or Session Creation Post-Patch Release
suggestion.rationale: Public exploit code availability typically triggers initial access attempts within hours. Pipeline did not propose detection for anomalous authentication post-disclosure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track authentication failures and session creation anomalies on Cisco UC administration interfaces. Alert on bulk or rapid login attempts, unusual source IPs, or successful authentication followed by immediate API calls to sensitive endpoints.

suggestion.title: Process Execution on Cisco UC Server Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: If CVE-2026-20230 allows code execution (implied by 'exploit code'), pipeline should have proposed process-level detection. Not mentioned in output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco UC server process execution for child processes spawned from UC service accounts (tomcat, uccx, etc.) or unexpected cmdline patterns (sh, bash, powershell). Flag writes to UC system directories outside of patch windows.

suggestion.title: Detection of Exploit Framework Integration for CVE-2026-20230
suggestion.rationale: Title states exploit code 'goes public'—typically integrated into Metasploit, PoC repos, or attack frameworks within 48 hours. Pipeline did not propose detection for framework preparation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for downloads or git clones of public exploit repositories from internal hosts. Alert on access to Metasploit module repositories, GitHub CVE-2026-20230 pages, or proof-of-concept hosting sites from environment.

suggestion.title: HTTP SSRF Exploitation Against Cisco WebDialer Service
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'sending a crafted HTTP request to an affected device' targeting WebDialer to trigger file writes; this is the entry point and was not detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/GET requests to /webdialerd and WebDialer endpoints for suspicious parameters, SSRF-pattern payloads (file://, http://localhost, gopher://), or responses indicating exploitation. Flag requests that precede file-system modifications within the same web-server process context.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation File Writes to System Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'write files to the underlying operating system that could be used later to elevate to root'—this escalation vector was not covered.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation or modification in /etc, /root, /var/spool, systemd service directories, or /usr/local/bin by the WebDialer process or parent web server. Correlate with subsequent UID-0 process execution to establish escalation success.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Startup Script / Cron Job Creation from Web Service
suggestion.rationale: Article implies file writes enable later root escalation, likely via cron/systemd/sudoers injection; persistence artifacts were not detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor creation of /etc/cron.d entries, /etc/sudoers modifications, /root/.ssh/authorized_keys, or systemd *.service files by non-root or web-service processes. Alert on any new execution directives added after WebDialer exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Root Process Execution from Non-Root Parent Context
suggestion.rationale: Final impact is attacker 'elevating privileges to root'; this UID-0 execution artifact following exploitation was not monitored.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify process creation with UID 0 where parent process is the web server, WebDialer, or any process spawned by them. Timeline-correlate with file-write events in preceding 120 seconds to establish exploitation → escalation causality.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Triggered by Untrusted Issue or PR Event
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'one malicious issue hijack repositories'—indicates attack vector is issue creation/comment triggering workflow execution. Pipeline entirely missed execution-phase detection for external-input-triggered workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag GitHub Actions workflows triggered by external issues (non-collaborators) or pull requests that execute shell commands containing unsanitized `github.event.issue.body`, `github.event.pull_request.body`, or comment-derived variables. Correlate workflow_run events with external event sources.

suggestion.title: Repository Credentials or GITHUB_TOKEN Exfiltration via Actions Workflow
suggestion.rationale: Repository 'hijacking' implies attacker obtained credentials or secrets. Article states malicious issue compromises repo—suggests token/secret theft. Pipeline missed credential-access detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect workflows triggered by issue/PR events that access GITHUB_TOKEN, repository secrets, or deploy keys, then transmit them to external URLs, log outputs, or exfiltrate via commits/artifacts. Monitor for `env` variable dumps or `secrets.*` references in workflows with external triggers.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Code Commits via GitHub Actions from Malicious Issue Trigger
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'hijack repositories'—requires ability to modify code. Pipeline missed impact-phase detection for repository integrity violations initiated by external input.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect commits authored by GitHub Actions workflows (e.g., `github-actions[bot]`) to protected branches following issue creation/comment by non-collaborators. Correlate issue events with push events on main/master branches within seconds, especially if workflow files in .github/workflows were modified in preceding issue-triggered runs.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Permission Misconfiguration: Elevated Token Scope from Issue Events
suggestion.rationale: Flaw allows 'one malicious issue' to hijack—indicates privilege escalation via workflow permissions. Pipeline missed privilege-escalation phase and workflow-permission audit detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect workflows triggered by issue/PR events that request or inherit write/admin permissions on the repository (via `permissions: write-all` or secrets access). Flag `if` conditions that check for trusted actors but execute external-input commands unconditionally, or use context variables without validation.

suggestion.title: Malicious Payload Injection in GitHub Issue / Pull Request Comment
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'one malicious issue hijack repositories'—initial access is issue creation with injected payload triggering Actions. Pipeline missed initial-access detection for issue-based exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GitHub issues created by external users containing shell metacharacters (backticks, $(), |, &&), GitHub Actions syntax (${{ ... }}), or command-injection patterns that appear in issue title/body. Correlate with subsequent workflow_run events triggered by issue-opened or issue-edited events within the same repository.

suggestion.title: GTM Container Execution Querying Stripe Customer Records
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'malicious code is loaded from a Google Tag Manager (GTM) container and executes on every page that loads it' and 'queuing Stripe's API for a specific customer record, cus_TfFjAAZQNOYENR.' No detection for this abuse pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GTM container events that make Stripe API calls to fetch customer objects (query pattern: GET /v1/customers/cus_*). Baseline expected GTM behavior—legitimate analytics containers should not query Stripe customer records. Alert on misaligned purpose: GTM container ≠ payment processing.

suggestion.title: XOR-Obfuscated Data Assembly and Storage in localStorage
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'stolen data is concatenated into a single string, obfuscated using the XOR operation, and stored locally' but no detection logic for this obfuscation pattern in JavaScript execution context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect JavaScript code patterns using XOR operations (bitwise `^` operator) on payment-related strings or form field values. Flag `localStorage.setItem()` calls storing data immediately after XOR transformation on checkout pages. Correlate with page-load event timing.

suggestion.title: Stripe Metadata Abuse for Stolen Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'storing the stolen data in metadata fields' and 'Every stolen payment card becomes a fake customer record in the attacker's Stripe account.' No detection for this exfiltration mechanism via legitimate SaaS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of Stripe customer objects with atypical metadata patterns: encoded/obfuscated metadata values, rapid successive customer creation (volume anomaly), or metadata containing hex-encoded payment card indicators. Baseline expected metadata against legitimate store operations.

suggestion.title: Firestore Document Access for Malware Payload Retrieval
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Google Firestore...is used instead of Stripe' with 'payload is retrieved from a Firestore document named tracking/captcha in a project called braintree-payment-app.' No detection for this variant or Firestore abuse pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect reads of Firestore documents with names containing 'tracking,' 'captcha,' or similar obfuscated labels in projects named 'braintree-*' or containing payment terminology. Flag if document is accessed from non-authenticated or unusual GCP service accounts, or if accessed frequency spikes during checkout operation.

suggestion.title: Checkout Page Script Injection via CSP-Compliant Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Stores allow that domain by default, so the skimmer slips past Content Security Policy rules and network filters' and 'Both the payload and the stolen cards move through api.stripe.com.' No detection for legitimate-domain abuse bypassing CSP.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of unexpected JavaScript code sourced from api.stripe.com or googletagmanager.com domains during checkout page loads. Baseline legitimate scripts on these domains; alert on code that deviates from expected function (e.g., DOM mutation, form field access, new XHRs to unlisted endpoints). Cross-reference with Content-Security-Policy headers to identify gaps.

suggestion.title: Suspicious new Function() Execution in Browser Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'reads JavaScript code that it reassembles and then executes using new Function().' This is a hallmark code injection technique on checkout pages not addressed in use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect invocation of `new Function()` with dynamically-constructed string arguments on e-commerce checkout pages. Filter for high-confidence cases: Function() called with arguments sourced from external API responses (Stripe, Firestore) or reconstructed from obfuscated data. Monitor for Function() output being immediately invoked (IIFE pattern).

suggestion.title: Lookalike Open-Source Tool Domains Ranking in Search Results
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states fake sites 'mimicking open-source tools rank high on Google.' Users searching for legitimate tools are directed to malicious imposters. Detection must correlate search queries for popular OSS projects with visits to newly-registered/suspicious domains containing tool names.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect search-query-to-download pattern: user queries 'download [tool]' followed by HTTP visit to lookalike domain (e.g., query 'nodejs' followed by visit to 'node-js-official.com'), then executable download. Flag if destination domain registration age < 90 days or registrant reputation low.

suggestion.title: Executable Download from High-Ranking Suspicious Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware delivered from fake sites users reach via Google. Detect downloads of executables/archives from newly-seen or low-reputation domains following search activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .exe, .msi, .zip, .sh downloads from domains with domain registration age < 6 months and no prior internal downloads. Correlate with search-engine referrer or direct URL-bar navigation to unfamiliar domain. Require file lacks trusted publisher signature.

suggestion.title: Traffic Distribution System (TDS) Conditional Response Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names malware delivery 'via TDS'—infrastructure that serves different payloads based on client metadata (User-Agent, geolocation, referrer). Detect TDS signature patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated 302/307 redirects from single domain serving different content per request (User-Agent/geolocation variation). Flag domains with timing-based response variance (fast vs. slow redirects by client profile). Correlate with known TDS provider ASNs and SSL certificate profiles.

suggestion.title: Package Manager Typo-Squatting for Open-Source Tools
suggestion.rationale: Threat mimics legitimate open-source tools. Expect malicious packages on npm, PyPI, RubyGems with names differing by one character or underscore from legitimate projects.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for package registrations where package name differs from legitimate project by ≤2 character Levenshtein distance. Flag installs of newly-registered (age < 30d) packages from unexpected development teams or without upstream GitHub link.

suggestion.title: SEO Ranking Anomaly for Malicious Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article premise: fake sites achieve high Google ranking. Flag domains with abnormal SERP ranking growth for tool-related keywords without legitimate SEO foundation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect domains appearing in top-10 search results for tool names within 30 days of registration. Correlate with high-velocity backlink growth from link farms. Cross-reference with GSuite indexing metadata showing unnatural rank acceleration.

suggestion.title: Installer File Signature/Publisher Mismatch on Downloaded Tools
suggestion.rationale: Malware disguised as open-source tool installers. Users download and execute files believing they are legitimate; file properties betray forgery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of .exe with filename suggesting OSS tool (e.g., 'vscode_setup.exe', 'nodejs-installer.exe') when file lacks Microsoft/legitimate publisher digital signature, or signature differs from known legitimate tool certificates. Flag if downloaded from non-standard domain.

suggestion.title: Browser-Sourced Process Execution from Ad Interaction
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Spreads to macOS via Malicious Google and YouTube Ads'. Initial execution chain originates from ad click/impression.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process spawning from Safari, Chrome, or system ad libraries within seconds of user-observed ad interaction. Flag child processes with non-standard paths (/tmp, /var/tmp, /Library/Caches) or unsigned code signatures.

suggestion.title: LaunchAgent/LaunchDaemon Installation for Persistence
suggestion.rationale: macOS backdoors establish persistence via ~/Library/LaunchAgents or /Library/LaunchDaemons. Ad-delivered FlutterShell would follow this pattern; pipeline missed this standard persistence technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation/modification of .plist files in ~/Library/LaunchAgents, ~/Library/LaunchDaemons, or /Library/LaunchDaemons. Validate referenced executable paths exist and match no legitimate macOS services.

suggestion.title: FlutterShell Backdoor C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline failed to map any command-and-control techniques. Title identifies FlutterShell as a backdoor, implying persistent C2 callbacks not covered by empty kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries or network connections to known malicious domains from processes with freshly-installed persistence mechanisms. Flag non-standard ports or TLS handshakes from unexpected processes.

suggestion.title: Ad-Hoc or Missing Code Signature from Temp Directories
suggestion.rationale: Ad-delivered payloads bypass App Store review and are typically unsigned or ad-hoc signed. Execution from user-writable temp/cache directories is the delivery mechanism not captured by empty IOC list.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate processes executed from /tmp, /var/tmp, ~/Downloads, or ~/Library/Caches with missing or ad-hoc code signatures and suspicious parent processes (browser children or system daemons).

suggestion.title: Ad Network Domain Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article vector is 'Malicious Google and YouTube Ads'. Pipeline missed detection for compromised or malicious ad-serving infrastructure, focusing only on post-delivery IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DNS queries to ad-serving domains (doubleclick.net, googlesyndication.com, etc.) followed within seconds by unexpected process execution or network connections to non-ad-serving infrastructure.

suggestion.title: MCP-for-Stata API/CLI invocation with shell metacharacters in log_file_name parameter
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'attacker can inject arbitrary Stata commands...by crafting a malicious log_file_name containing quotes, newline...' Yet no detection targets the command-line parameter at invocation time. Current hunts only detect downstream effects (shell spawning, file creation); this would catch injection attempts at source.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for stata_do API calls or MCP-for-Stata CLI invocations where the log_file_name argument contains shell metacharacters (single/double quotes, backticks, pipes, semicolons, newlines, or path-traversal sequences like ..). Inspect ProcessCommandLine and parent process context to identify injection attempts before command execution.

suggestion.title: Stata process spawning Python interpreter (arbitrary code execution via injection)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists `python` as an injectable command: 'attacker can inject arbitrary Stata commands (including shell, python, erase, etc.)' UC_14_2 only detects shell spawning. Python execution is a separate, high-severity code execution vector that bypasses current detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parent process is Stata (stata.exe, stata-mp.exe, stata-se.exe, xstata variants) spawning child process matching python*, python3*. This represents successful exploitation of the log_file_name injection to execute arbitrary Python code outside normal data-science contexts. Reduce false positives by flagging unexpected spawning patterns or Python execution with network activity.

suggestion.title: Stata executing erase or file-deletion commands (post-exploitation data destruction)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists `erase` (Stata's file deletion command) as injectable: 'attacker can inject...erase, etc.' No detection targets the impact phase. Should flag when Stata deletes files via injected command, especially non-log/non-temp files indicating evidence destruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Stata process initiates file deletion (FileDeleted action) for files outside expected temporary or log directories. Correlate with suspicious log-file-name creation in same timeframe (UC_14_3 baseline). Pattern indicates post-exploitation cleanup or data destruction via injected erase command.

suggestion.title: GuardValidator bypass detection — benign do-file with malicious process behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'GuardValidator only scans the do-file content but does not validate this parameter.' Traditional content-based guards will miss attacks. Need behavioral detection for Stata executions where do-file passes validation but downstream behavior (shell spawning, file creation with metacharacters) indicates injection bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Stata process executes with do-file hash that matches known benign/whitelisted signatures, yet same execution spawns shell children or creates files with shell metacharacters. Indicates parameter-based injection evading content validation. Correlate do-file signature reputation against observed process tree and file events; mismatch signals injection.

suggestion.title: Path-traversal and privilege-escalation via log_file_name injection
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'path traversal in filename' (UC_14_3 title) but detections focus on shell metacharacters. Separate concern: injecting sequences like '../../../etc/passwd' or writing logs to privileged directories could escalate or pivot attacks. Needs explicit pattern matching for traversal attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Stata process attempts to create or modify files in paths containing traversal sequences (..) or in sensitive directories (/etc, /root, /boot, C:\Windows\System32, etc.). Combine with command-line inspection for log_file_name containing ../. High confidence if paths are outside Stata's normal working directories and outside /tmp.

suggestion.title: Correlation: MCP-for-Stata initialization + suspicious log_file_name parameter in rapid succession
suggestion.rationale: No hunt explicitly detects the attack initiation — the moment MCP-for-Stata tool is invoked with malicious parameters. Should detect patterns of tool invocation followed immediately by unusual Stata behavior, before attacks fully materialize.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Process creation for Python/MCP tool invoking stata_do or MCP-for-Stata CLI with command-line arguments containing suspicious log_file_name patterns (quotes, backticks, newlines, traversal). Time window: within 2 seconds, Stata parent spawns unexpected children or creates suspicious files. Indicates attack initiation before impact phase.

suggestion.title: YPTSocket metadata broadcast payload injection detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'stored DOM XSS via per-client metadata broadcast in YPTSocket Plugin' and 'page_title broadcast.' Pipeline should detect when malicious content persists in YPTSocket broadcast payloads, not just initial injection. No use case monitors the actual broadcast responses or YPTSocket cache for XSS signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor YPTSocket broadcast API responses (/plugin/YPTSocket/broadcast or similar) for responses containing script tags, event handlers, or encoded XSS payloads. Correlate with subsequent admin WebUI access from the same session IP to establish DOM execution context.

suggestion.title: Admin session token theft post-YPTSocket XSS
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'execute arbitrary JavaScript in the authenticated origin of every administrator currently viewing' and threat model includes T1539 (steal web session cookie). No detection for admin session tokens being used from anomalous IPs/User-Agents after YPTSocket XSS is detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag authentication tokens associated with admin accounts that were viewing YPTSocket when XSS was injected, if those tokens subsequently appear in requests from different source IPs, User-Agents, or timezones within 5 minutes of the injection timestamp.

suggestion.title: YPTSocket plugin configuration/database tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article describes a component vulnerability in YPTSocket plugin. Should detect unauthorized installation, enablement, or modification of YPTSocket configuration and data files. Article mentions 'page_title' stored in metadata—should monitor for writes to YPTSocket data stores from unexpected processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation/modification of YPTSocket plugin files, configuration, and metadata caches outside of administrative update windows. Flag writes from web server process to YPTSocket data directories with script-like content or unusual byte signatures.

suggestion.title: npm Package Publishing Attempts During Install Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states malicious package 'attempted self-propagation'. No UC detects npm publish API calls, registry authentication, or package version updates from compromised host during install phase. This is the mechanism for worm spread.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST requests to npm registry endpoints (registry.npmjs.org/api/v2/publish, or equivalent) originating from npm/node processes during package install sequences. Correlate with credentials harvested in UC_17_6. High-confidence signal if registry auth uses token harvested from .npmrc in same timeframe.

suggestion.title: Explicit Preinstall Script Execution (package.json scripts field)
suggestion.rationale: Article context references 'setup.mjs' and 'execution.js' as preinstall payloads, but no UC explicitly detects the preinstall script execution mechanism defined in package.json. T1546.016 'Installer Packages' is listed but not directly instrumented.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm/yarn/pnpm launching child processes with 'preinstall' in parent process command line or environment variables, especially JavaScript runtimes (node, bun) executing .mjs or .js files from node_modules/.bin or package root. Correlate with package installation events.

suggestion.title: Code Obfuscation Patterns in npm Install Context (T1027)
suggestion.rationale: T1027 (Obfuscated Files) is listed but no hunt detects obfuscation. Malicious payloads are typically obfuscated to evade analysis. No detection for hex-encoded strings, minified code patterns, or suspicious entropy in downloaded packages.
log_sources: File contents or package download logs
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag package downloads where JavaScript files contain high entropy sections, excessive use of String.fromCharCode(), atob() calls with large base64 blobs, or Unicode escapes. Correlate with new or recent package versions during install. Requires package inspection or behavioral monitoring of npm-install contexts.

suggestion.title: Package.json Dependency Modification During Install
suggestion.rationale: Self-propagation mechanism likely involves modifying package.json to inject malicious dependency or updating package version. No UC detects package.json mutations or dependency injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for FileModified/FileCreated events on package.json files during npm install sequences. Correlate with node/npm/bun processes. Flag if new 'dependencies' or 'devDependencies' entries appear, especially to newly-created or obfuscated package names, or if version constraints change.

suggestion.title: Credential Data Exfiltration Pattern Over HTTP to C2
suggestion.rationale: UC_17_3 detects endpoint DNS/network traffic to t.m-kosche.com but doesn't verify credential content is actually exfiltrated. Detection should cover base64-encoded credential blobs or JSON-formatted secrets in HTTP POST bodies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to t.m-kosche.com (or /api/public/otel/v1/traces endpoint) for base64-encoded or JSON payloads containing credential patterns (AWS_SECRET, GITHUB_TOKEN, etc.). Correlate with UC_17_6 credential access events in same timeframe and source process.

suggestion.title: npm Token / Registry Credential Usage from Install-Time Context
suggestion.rationale: Harvested npm tokens (via .npmrc access in UC_17_6) would be used to authenticate package publishes or registry API calls. No UC detects unusual npm auth token usage during install phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate npm registry API requests (publish, yank, unpublish) with npm auth tokens that were harvested from .npmrc files during UC_17_6 credential access events in the same host/user context. High-confidence signal if token originates from file access event and is immediately used in API call.

suggestion.title: Lookalike domain web request and file download
suggestion.rationale: Article core mechanism: 'hackers are creating convincing fake websites that impersonate popular security tools' and 'users click the download button.' Pipeline lists fake domains (ghidralite.com, dnspy.org, ilspy.org) but generates no detection for accessing these lookalike domains or file downloads from them.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on user web requests to domains with high string similarity to known legitimate tool domains (e.g., Levenshtein distance ≤2 from github.com/NationalSecurityAgency/ghidra, github.com/dnSpy/dnSpy). Correlate to file download events (file creation in %TEMP%, Downloads, or AppData\Local\Temp) within 30 seconds.

suggestion.title: Download-to-execution chain from temporary directories
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The moment a user clicks the download button, something very different happens.' Malware flows from browser download → execution. Pipeline does not detect file downloaded to %TEMP%/%APPDATA%\Local\Temp and subsequently executed via process creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file-creation events in browser default-download or temp directories to process-creation events where CommandLine or ImagePath references the same file, within 60 seconds. Join on user and device. Cross-reference file hash against known malware SHA256 IOC list.

suggestion.title: Malware hash distribution across fake domains
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline lists 12 SHA256 hashes and 22 domains separately with no attribution map. A campaign distributing malware through multiple lookalike sites should show malware-to-domain relationships; pipeline output lacks this correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build a domain-malware matrix: for each fake domain (ghidralite.com, dnspy.org, etc.), identify which of the 12 SHA256 hashes are served from that domain. Flag domains serving >1 distinct malware binary (polymorph distribution) or reusing the same binary across multiple domains (campaign infrastructure reuse). Correlate domain IPs to identify shared hosting.

suggestion.title: Detection of impersonated security tool downloads
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes impersonation of Ghidra, dnSpy, SpiderFoot—tools used by defenders and researchers. Need explicit detection for downloading executables claiming to be these tools from non-official sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag downloads of files matching naming patterns (ghidra*.exe, ghidra-installer*, dnspy*.exe, spiderfoot*.exe, sf-*.exe) from domains not in allowlist (official GitHub releases, project websites). Log source IP and user context. Cross-reference file hash against known-malware hash list.

suggestion.title: Outlook Mailbox Accessed from New Geographic Location
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes five months of unauthorized mailbox access. Phrase: 'Hackers Spied on a Stock Exchange Executive's Outlook Mailbox for Five Months.' Geographic or device-based anomalies are primary signals of account takeover.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful sign-ins to Outlook from IP addresses or geographic locations inconsistent with the user's baseline. Correlate with failed login attempts preceding first successful anomalous sign-in. Prioritize where sign-in occurred outside business hours or during extended reconnaissance windows (days or weeks of consistent access).

suggestion.title: Outlook Forwarding Rule Created or Modified
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'spying on' mailbox contents—indicating exfiltration. To sustain undetected email access, attackers typically create forwarding rules to an external account. Article phrase: 'Hackers Spied on...Outlook Mailbox.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on mailbox rules created by non-owner identities or by the mailbox owner during anomalous login sessions. Specifically detect forwarding rules with external domains or suspicious condition logic (e.g., forward all mail, or forward specific keywords/senders). Cross-correlate with the anomalous signin context from UC-1.

suggestion.title: Mass Mailbox Data Export or Download
suggestion.rationale: Five-month spying campaign implies sustained data collection. Attackers would extract email content, contacts, and calendar data. Article phrase: 'Spied on a Stock Exchange Executive's Outlook Mailbox.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk email exports, PST creation, or unusually large attachment downloads from the compromised mailbox. Monitor for PowerShell commands like New-MailboxExportRequest. Alert on unusual ActiveSync or EAS sync volume. Correlate timing with anomalous signin contexts.

suggestion.title: Azure AD Conditional Access Policy Bypass or Disablement
suggestion.rationale: To sustain access for five months despite potential baseline defenses, attackers likely disabled or bypassed conditional access, MFA, or risk-based sign-in policies. Article's duration implies active evasion of detection controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modifications to conditional access policies by unexpected identities or during anomalous sessions. Monitor for disablement of sign-in risk detections or MFA enforcement. Alert on enrollment of new authenticator devices linked to compromised accounts during the persistence window.

suggestion.title: Suspicious OWA Web Shell Upload or OWA Client Access
suggestion.rationale: Alternative access vector: attackers may have installed OWA-based persistence or directly accessed Outlook Web Access from attacker infrastructure. Article describes sustained spying without explicit indication of client-side malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST/PUT requests to Exchange OWA endpoints from anomalous source IPs. Detect uploads of suspicious .aspx or .cs files to Exchange virtual directories. Alert on OWA sessions from the same IP persistence for weeks or months.

suggestion.title: Email Account Delegation or Secretary Access Granted to External Identity
suggestion.rationale: Article implies deep, sustained mailbox access. Attackers may have granted 'Send As' or 'Full Access' permissions to an external account to maintain persistence even if the initial compromise is remediated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Add-MailboxPermission, Add-RecipientPermission, or Azure AD app role assignments granting email or calendar access. Correlate with anomalous signin context. Flag external domains or service principals added during the breach window.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Application Download and Execution from Web Browser Post-Ad Click
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'using Google Ads to push fake desktop applications'—no detection of the initial compromise vector where users download and execute unvetted binaries directly from malicious ads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious processes spawned by web browsers (Chrome, Safari, Firefox) that download .dmg, .zip, or unsigned .app bundles from ads, followed by immediate execution. Correlate with new domain registration (WHOIS age < 30 days) or domains matching C2 IOC patterns from article.

suggestion.title: macOS Launch Agent Creation by Downloaded Application
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'secretly install a powerful backdoor' on macOS. No detection for Launch Agent or Launchd creation, which is the primary persistence mechanism for macOS backdoors and FlutterShell variants.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .plist file creation in ~/Library/LaunchAgents, ~/Library/LaunchDaemons, or /Library/LaunchDaemons by processes spawned from Downloads or /tmp within 5 minutes of suspicious application execution. Correlate parent process with article's SHA256 IOCs.

suggestion.title: Masqueraded Application Execution with Suspicious Code Signature or Notarization Status
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'fake desktop applications' masquerading as legitimate software. Pipeline lacks behavioral detection for unsigned, revoked, or suspiciously-notarized apps from user-controlled directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of .app bundles from ~/Downloads, ~/Desktop, or /tmp with invalid code signature, missing Apple notarization, or bundle metadata suggesting impersonation of popular applications (Adobe, Microsoft, Zoom). Flag if bundle identifier or executable name contains misspellings of trusted vendors.

suggestion.title: Unsigned Binary Network Beaconing to FlutterShell C2 Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article provides 8 C2 domains but pipeline creates no behavioral hunt linking unsigned malware binaries to these specific network indicators in a single correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate network egress to the 8 article-provided domains (atsheisdomestic.org, etoftheappyrince.org, etc.) with execution of unsigned or unusually-signed binaries in user writable directories. Elevated signal if process lineage shows browser → downloaded app → system process spawning network beacon.

suggestion.title: Redirect Chain from Google Ads to Malware Payload Host
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attack vector is malicious Google Ads serving fake apps. No hunt for the web redirect infrastructure or landing page serving executable downloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web proxy logs for redirect chains originating from google.com or ads.google.com subdomains that terminate at unfamiliar domains serving executable MIME types (.dmg, .zip, .app). Flag landing pages with poor domain reputation, recent registration (< 60 days), or typosquatting patterns of legitimate vendors.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated macOS Binary Unpacking and Child Process Injection
suggestion.rationale: MITRE technique T1027 (Obfuscation) is listed but no behavioral detection for runtime code unpacking, child process injection, or unusual dylib loading typical of packed macOS malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious characteristics: packed binary executing and writing to /tmp, injecting into legitimate processes (launchd, Finder), loading unsigned dylibs from writable directories, or unusual mmap/mprotect syscalls. Correlate with C2 beaconing to article IOC domains within 10 minutes of execution.

suggestion.title: cmd.exe spawning PowerShell with -EncodedCommand parameter
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'cmd.exe process spawning powershell.exe with an -EncodedCommand parameter containing a Base64-encoded payload.' Defines execution and obfuscation pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for cmd.exe creating child powershell.exe with command-line containing -EncodedCommand flag and Base64-encoded payload. This is a signature execution pattern for code obfuscation. Correlate with subsequent file writes or network connections in the process tree.

suggestion.title: PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest to malicious ASN infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The decoded payload executing Invoke-WebRequest to fetch a file named script.ps1, dropping it into the user's ApplicationData directory.' Defines payload delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for powershell.exe executing Invoke-WebRequest or DownloadFile cmdlets with outbound HTTP connections to EVILEMPIRE ASN ranges or known C2 hosting providers. Payload dropped to ApplicationData signals staging. Correlate EDR process telemetry with firewall connection logs for multi-domain signal.

suggestion.title: Post-execution anti-forensics via Remove-Item
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Post-execution cleanup via Remove-Item, attempting to delete traces of the downloaded script.' Indicates active defense evasion and cleanup behavior post-intrusion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for powershell.exe or cmd.exe executing Remove-Item or del commands targeting recently-created files in user directories (AppData, Temp, Downloads). Flag rapid file creation followed by deletion within same process chain. Time delta of seconds to minutes is high-risk pattern.

suggestion.title: curl.exe outbound connections to known C2 ASN ranges
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'A separate curl.exe process making requests to the same C2 infrastructure the firewall had flagged.' LOTL (living-off-the-land) tool misuse for C2 beaconing with HTTP user-agent persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for curl.exe or wget processes making outbound HTTP connections to EVILEMPIRE ASN ranges or other documented C2 hosting infrastructure. Establish baseline: curl.exe should be rare in user environment outbound connections. Parent process cmd.exe or powershell.exe indicates abuse.

suggestion.title: TDS redirect signature: port 6060 with /capcha* URL path
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Outbound ConnectionEvents to 144.31.221.82 on port 6060, with a URL path of /capcha9856…consistent with a Traffic Direction System (TDS) infection, where a compromised website redirects visitors through a chain of intermediate servers.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for outbound HTTP connections to 144.31.221.82:6060 with URL paths matching /capcha* (common TDS obfuscation pattern). Flag rapid HTTP connection chains with multiple different destination IPs on non-standard ports. Correlate with EDR process history for confirming execution.

suggestion.title: Multi-domain correlation: ApplicationData write + PowerShell execution + C2 network
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The value of correlating telemetry across security domains is easiest to explain with a real example.' The firewall, EDR process tree, and file operations together tell story that no single source can; combined they are definitive threat confirmation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for temporal sequences: (1) .ps1 file written to user ApplicationData directory, (2) powershell.exe child process executing that script within 60 seconds, (3) corresponding outbound HTTP connection to known malicious ASN infrastructure within same time window. Requires EDR + firewall log fusion. Three-signal correlation is high-confidence threat.

suggestion.title: npm binding.gyp Execution with Unexpected Process Tree
suggestion.rationale: Article title indicates 'Self-Spreading Worm via Phantom Gyp'—binding.gyp is native Node build config executed during npm install (T1059 + T1195). Pipeline missed the core execution chain: npm install → binding.gyp → gyp rebuild → arbitrary code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spawning of unexpected child processes (sh, bash, powershell, cmd.exe) from node.exe or npm.exe during package installation. Correlate with binding.gyp file presence in node_modules or .npm cache. Flag if gyp/python subprocess executes with encoded arguments or reaches network destinations.

suggestion.title: npm Package Self-Replication via Dependency Injection
suggestion.rationale: Title describes 'Self-Spreading Worm'—implies the malicious package injects itself into other packages' dependencies. Article phrase 'spreads like a worm' indicates persistence through dependency recursion, not one-time execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm cache and node_modules for unexpected package version mutations or sudden addition of dependencies not present in package-lock.json. Alert if package.json modifications occur during or immediately after npm install from external tooling (not package manager CLI).

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Performing Outbound Discovery/Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain worms typically perform reconnaissance (whoami, environment enumeration, credential theft). Article severity 'high' with worm behavior implies post-compromise activity—missing detection of discovery phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected execution of discovery commands (whoami, hostname, env, id, dir, ls -la, findstr, grep) spawned from node.exe or package install scripts. Correlate with network egress to C2 or exfiltration endpoints in same session.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Network Connection from npm Install Context
suggestion.rationale: Worm-based supply chain attacks require command-and-control communication or exfiltration. Title 'Self-Spreading' implies coordination or data theft—no C2/exfiltration detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound TCP/UDP initiated from node.exe or child processes during npm install to non-standard ports or IPs not matching npm registry CDN (not registry.npmjs.org, github.com, or trusted mirrors). Include DNS queries for malicious C2 domains.

suggestion.title: Encoded or Obfuscated Code in binding.gyp
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates threat actors disguise payload via 'Phantom Gyp'—a deceptive package name. Missing detection for obfuscated/base64-encoded payloads embedded in gyp files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan binding.gyp and .node files in node_modules for base64, hex, or zlib-encoded content. Alert if gyp build produces .node binaries with unexpected imports (e.g., cryptography, network, process spawning) via tools like objdump or strings analysis.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Publication from Unexpected Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'self-propagates by using stolen credentials for publishing on npm' and 'publishes trojanized versions of packages owned by the victim, which then infect additional developers and CI systems.' Self-propagation via compromised credentials is a critical persistence and spread vector the pipeline failed to capture.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm publish operations from CI/CD runners or development environments that deviate from baseline account-to-package ownership mapping.
