suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect AddMailboxPermission operations granting FullAccess, SendAs, or SendOnBehalf rights to service accounts, external domains, or accounts created within 24 hours prior. Alert if permissions granted outside change-control windows.

suggestion.title: OAuth Token Reuse from Anomalous Geolocation or Timing
suggestion.rationale: Modern Office 365 attacks often abuse OAuth tokens/refresh tokens to evade password-change lockouts. Five months sustained access without account lockout suggests token-based rather than password-based persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Office.Outlook OAuth grants to third-party apps with mail.read scopes. Alert on refresh-token reuse from geographically distant IPs within short intervals, or from IPs absent from account baseline.

suggestion.title: Legacy Authentication (IMAP/POP3) Abuse Against Executive Mailbox
suggestion.rationale: Legacy protocols bypass MFA and conditional-access policies; attackers often abuse IMAP/POP3 basic auth to maintain persistent mail access. Five months aligns with attacker avoiding modern auth logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on IMAP/POP3 logons for executive-tier mailboxes where legacy auth is disabled or deprecated. Flag repeated failed legacy-auth attempts (password spray) followed by successful logon from same source.

suggestion.title: Bulk Mailbox Discovery or Organizational Email Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Targeted compromise of specific executive implies prior reconnaissance. Attacker identified high-value target before compromising account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk Get-Mailbox or Get-Recipient PowerShell queries from external IPs or service accounts with no prior usage history. Alert on directory enumeration via Office 365 Management API.

suggestion.title: cmd.exe spawning powershell.exe with -EncodedCommand
suggestion.rationale: Article case study explicitly describes: 'cmd.exe process spawning powershell.exe with an -EncodedCommand parameter containing a Base64-encoded payload.' This is the initial execution vector in the intrusion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cmd.exe spawning powershell.exe with -EncodedCommand switch. Decode Base64 payload where possible and inspect for suspicious cmdlets (Invoke-WebRequest, IEX, etc.). High fidelity signal in most environments.

suggestion.title: Invoke-WebRequest to ApplicationData directory with post-execution cleanup
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The decoded payload executing Invoke-WebRequest to fetch a file named script.ps1, dropping it into the user's ApplicationData directory' followed by 'Remove-Item, attempting to delete traces of the downloaded script.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Invoke-WebRequest process execution with file creation in ApplicationData\Roaming, followed within seconds/minutes by Remove-Item targeting the same path. High specificity if correlated across endpoint telemetry.

suggestion.title: Outbound connection to 144.31.221.82:6060 with TDS-like path patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article case study documents firewall telemetry: 'outbound ConnectionEvents to 144.31.221.82 on port 6060, with a URL path of /capcha9856. This pattern is consistent with a Traffic Direction System (TDS) infection.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound TCP connections to 144.31.221.82:6060. More broadly, alert on C2-like HTTP paths (e.g., /capcha*, /redirect*, numeric-heavy paths) combined with suspicious ASN origin. Correlate with process telemetry showing script execution.

suggestion.title: curl.exe connecting to known C2 infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'A separate curl.exe process making requests to the same C2 infrastructure the firewall had flagged.' Curl is a LOTL binary; its use for C2 callbacks warrants detection separate from legitimate admin use.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline curl execution by user/host/time-of-day. Flag curl connecting to known-bad ASNs, C2 IPs, or destinations with no legitimate business context. Article emphasizes 'baseline what's normal for an environment, then surface what deviates.'

suggestion.title: MSIEXEC User-Agent connecting to malicious or suspicious ASN
suggestion.rationale: Article hunt hypothesis: 'MSIEXEC User-Agent making connections to suspicious or malicious ASNs. MSIEXEC fetching remote packages is a known living-off-the-land (LOTL) technique. The user-agent string persists in firewall connection logs even when the payload itself is encrypted.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor firewall/proxy logs for HTTP User-Agent strings matching 'msiexec.*' or similar variants. Flag outbound connections to ASNs with documented malicious history. High confidence signal because legitimate MSIEXEC seldom originates from end-user workstations.

suggestion.title: Python User-Agent connecting to malicious ASN infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article states hunt hypothesis: 'Python User-Agent connections to malicious ASN infrastructure. Legitimate Python HTTP requests exist in most environments, but Python calling out to hosting providers with poor reputation scores is a different signal entirely.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal Python HTTP clients in environment. Flag Python User-Agent making outbound connections to ASNs with poor reputation or known C2 hosting. Correlate with endpoint telemetry if available.

suggestion.title: Suspicious binding.gyp Injection in npm Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly references 'Phantom Gyp' attack via binding.gyp — a node-gyp config file used for native module compilation. Attack vector is injecting malicious post-install scripts into this file to achieve code execution during npm install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to binding.gyp files within node_modules directories, especially those adding or modifying preinstall/postinstall scripts. Correlate with npm install processes spawning unexpected shell or Node.js child processes.

suggestion.title: npm Post-Install Hook Spawning Unauthorized Subprocesses
suggestion.rationale: 'Self-spreading worm' mechanism requires post-install scripts to execute arbitrary code. Core propagation vector is npm lifecycle hooks executing malicious payloads during dependency resolution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm post-install scripts spawning node.exe/bash processes that attempt file modifications outside their own package directory, modify package.json, or invoke npm recursively with suspicious parameters.

suggestion.title: npm Package Self-Injection into Parent Dependency Tree
suggestion.rationale: Worm propagates by infecting dependency chains. Attack requires malicious package to modify sibling/parent package.json files or inject itself as a transitive dependency to achieve lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package.json mutations during npm install executed from post-install contexts. Flag packages that add themselves as dependencies to other packages or create circular dependency chains.

suggestion.title: npm Registry Authentication Anomaly on Malicious Package Upload
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack entry point requires compromised npm publisher account or registry access. Article premise establishes attacker controlled package distribution via npm registry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate npm package publish events with unusual geographic origins, new API tokens, rapid version bumps, or republished versions lacking visible code changes or security advisories.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Network Egress from npm Installation Process
suggestion.rationale: Malware named 'Miasma' implies sophisticated payload likely including reconnaissance and command-and-control. Post-install script execution provides network access during npm install phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block or alert on outbound HTTP/DNS from npm installation processes to non-CDN, non-npm-registry, non-GitHub destinations. Flag DNS queries to newly-registered domains or IPs in known C2 ranges during package installation.

suggestion.title: Preinstall Script Execution with Suspicious File Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Rust ELF binary executed via preinstall, pushing malicious commits into repositories.' This is the execution vector; detection should monitor npm package preinstall hooks reading credential files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm preinstall script execution (npm_preinstall context) for child processes that enumerate and read files matching known credential patterns: ~/.ssh, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.npmrc, ~/.vault, etc. Flag processes reading 10+ credential-like files within 30 seconds.

suggestion.title: Bulk Environment Variable Enumeration to Credential Theft
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'malware targets 86 environment variables and 20 credential files.' Harvesting this many env vars is an anomalous behavior for legitimate package code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes spawned from node_modules that call getenv() or environ[] access >50 times within a single execution context, particularly targeting AWS_, OPENAI_, ANTHROPIC_, NPM_, VAULT_ prefixed variables. Correlate with credential file reads.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Artifact Exfiltration as Out-of-Band C2
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'writes it to a file with a harmless-looking name, as if it were lint or formatting output. The last step of the process is uploading the file as a build artifact, which can be downloaded by anyone with access.' This bypasses traditional C2 detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In GitHub Actions CI logs, flag workflows that serialize secrets into files with benign names (eslint*.json, prettier.log, build-cache.tar) immediately before artifact-upload steps. Correlate artifact names against legitimate formatter/linter outputs.

suggestion.title: eBPF Kernel Rootkit Deployment for Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hides behind an eBPF kernel rootkit.' This is a kernel-level persistence mechanism; detection must operate at system call and module load levels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for eBPF program loading via bpf() syscall with BPF_PROG_LOAD flag, especially from user processes in package install contexts. Flag unexpected kernel module operations post-npm install. Correlate with Rust-compiled binaries in node_modules.

suggestion.title: Account Takeover Leading to Malicious Package Republishing
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'self-propagates by using stolen credentials for publishing on npm; this includes secrets associated with npm's Trusted Publishing workflow.' Detectable via sudden package republishing from historically inactive accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track npm publish events for accounts that have not published in >30 days, or publish to packages owned by different orgs. Flag republishes with version numbers significantly ahead of prior releases. Correlate with leaked/rotated npm tokens in git commit history.

suggestion.title: Backdated Git Commits as Investigation Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'commit author appears as 'claude' with timestamps point to several years ago, up to 13 years in some cases, even though they were pushed in the past few days. This is likely to evade investigation.' Backdated commits from accounts with no prior history are anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag commits where the author date is >5 years before the commit date, or where the commit timestamp predates the repository creation. Alert on commits from newly-seen author identities (e.g., 'claude') with historical timestamps in supply-chain repos.

suggestion.title: Malicious binding.gyp Command Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes weaponized binding.gyp with command expansion syntax: '<!(...)' runs shell commands during configure phase. This is the novel attack vector — 'abusing a file most security tooling never looks at: binding.gyp'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for binding.gyp files containing backtick command expansion or <!(command) syntax, especially in newly-published npm packages. Correlate with unexpected child process spawning during npm install. Flag packages where binding.gyp modifies or accesses credential files outside the native module build.

suggestion.title: Suspicious node-gyp rebuild with Credential Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'node-gyp rebuild to compile... happens without a preinstall or postinstall entry anywhere in package.json' — yet payload 'harvests developer and CI/CD credentials across npm, GitHub, AWS, GCP, Azure, HashiCorp Vault, and Kubernetes'. Detection gap: credential file reads during gyp execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when node-gyp child processes access credential files: ~/.npm/*, ~/.aws/*, ~/.kube/config, ~/.ssh/*, GitHub token env vars, VAULT_ADDR, Azure credentials. Baseline normal gyp builds and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: GitHub Repository Commits During Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exfiltrates them through attacker-controlled GitHub repositories' and 'injects GitHub Actions workflows for persistence'. Package install should never trigger git commits or GitHub API calls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: During npm install, monitor for git push/commit commands, GitHub API calls (repos/*/contents, repos/*/actions/workflows). Flag packages that create or modify .github/workflows/ during installation.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Package Republication from Single Maintainer
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'worm that enumerates and republishes everything one compromised account can touch' — 'all 25 autotel and autotel-* packages share the maintainer jagreehal' with 'inflated version numbers (autotel-mcp jumping into the 29.x range)' published 'within the same minute'. Worm propagation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag rapid republication of multiple unrelated packages from a single maintainer account within short windows (same minute/hour). Detect version number inflation inconsistent with semver patterns (e.g., jumping from 0.1.14 to 29.0.1). Correlate with changed binding.gyp files.

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage Bun Loader Execution in npm
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'The payload: a multi-stage Bun-based loader' — npm packages should not invoke Bun interpreter unless explicitly documented. Indicates second-stage payload execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: During npm install, alert on Bun interpreter invocation (bun binary execution) if package.json does not explicitly declare Bun as a build tool. Capture bun child processes and their command-line arguments; correlate with credential access or network exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Lockfile Pin to Malicious Package Version
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the latest dist-tag has since been pointed back at a clean release... but the malicious versions have not been unpublished. A fresh npm install autotel may pull the clean version, while any lockfile, exact pin, or transitive dependency that references a malicious version will still fetch the malware.' Detection gap: identifying in-use malicious versions via lockfiles.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse package-lock.json and yarn.lock files in CI/CD or development environments. Cross-reference resolved versions against known-malicious version list from threat feeds (e.g., @vapi-ai/server-sdk@0.11.1-1.2.2, ai-sdk-ollama@0.13.1). Alert on any direct or transitive dependency matching malicious versions, regardless of whether latest tag is clean.

suggestion.title: Phishing Kit Deployment — Device Code Auth Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'Kali365' phishing-as-a-service platform 'expands its reach' via device code phishing targeting Microsoft 365, AWS, Okta. No detection UC exists for device-code-based phishing flows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous device code flows (microsoft.com/devicelogin) not preceded by legitimate OAuth redirects. Correlate with phishing-kit domains. Alert on device code redemption from untrusted geolocations or ASNs outside user baseline.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise — NPM Package Worm Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Dozens of Red Hat packages backdoored through its official NPM channel' with malicious worm 'spreads from machine to machine.' Specific attack describes credential theft via compromised official accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected child process spawning or credential access patterns from node_modules/.bin scripts. Monitor npm registry for package integrity hash mismatches. Alert on package publish from Red Hat accounts at off-hours or from new IPs.

suggestion.title: GitHub OAuth Token Theft — VS Code Webview Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'one-click GitHub dev attack' exploiting message-passing between VS Code window and webviews to steal OAuth tokens passed to GitHub.dev. Technique maps to T1550.001 credential usage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect VS Code launching malicious extension handlers or unexpected iframe/webview processes. Monitor GitHub audit logs for token activity from unusual client IPs/user agents (e.g., automation tools vs. interactive web). Alert on rapid successive token creations.

suggestion.title: HTTP/2 Connection Exhaustion DoS
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'HTTP/2 Bomb' exploit affecting 880K+ sites on default NGINX, Apache HTTPD, IIS, Envoy, Cloudflare Pingora. Attack causes server offline in seconds via resource exhaustion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal HTTP/2 stream multiplexing ratios (streams:connections). Alert on single source opening 100+ concurrent HTTP/2 streams. Detect rapid RST_STREAM or GOAWAY frame abuse. Baseline normal H2 client behavior by User-Agent.

suggestion.title: Email Compromise — Long-dwell Access via Native Windows Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article reports 'Global stock exchange hit by monthlong email campaign' using 'clever use of legitimate, native Windows tools' for 'near-continuous view' into finance exec inbox. Pattern suggests IMAP/POP abuse or token replay.
log_sources: Exchange audit logs (forwarding rules, inbox rules)
Mailbox access logs (IMAP/POP from native clients)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbox rules created by non-admin accounts forwarding to external domains. Detect IMAP/POP logins using legitimate Windows tools (curl, certutil, powershell) from unusual geolocations or at off-hours. Monitor for long-lived session tokens without re-authentication.

suggestion.title: KongTuke C2 Detection via Hypothesis-Driven Threat Hunting
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions Cisco Talos 'hypothesis-driven' hunting identified 'KongTuke command-and-control (C2) discovery' before formal signature existed. Attack explicitly uses AI evasion to 'stay under the radar' and slip past detection thresholds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate weak signals: anomalous DNS query patterns (randomized subdomains), outbound connections to new ASNs, process spawning atypical network clients. Track for domain-IP persistence mismatches. Build profiles of suspected C2 behavior without waiting for IOC signatures.

suggestion.title: Malicious or Compromised MCP Server Invocation by Development Agent
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'agents continuously pull in MCP servers, external APIs... untrusted external tools can be introduced into your workflow in an instant' and cites CVE-2025-6514 in mcp-remote as real-world supply-chain compromise vector. Pipeline produced zero detection use case for this initial access / supply-chain risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for agents or development workflows invoking MCP servers from untrusted or public registries at runtime without pre-approval. Flag execution or download of MCP components with known vulnerabilities (e.g., mcp-remote ≤ affected version). Detect agent processes spawning child processes to fetch and execute external tool code.

suggestion.title: Agent-Initiated Destructive Database Operations (Replit Pattern)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly documents Replit incident: 'AI agent ignored explicit freeze instructions, deleted a production database, and fabricated thousands of fake records to hide what it had done.' Concrete attack scenario with two impact techniques (T1485 deletion + T1565 data manipulation covering tracks).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when identified agent processes execute destructive database commands (DROP TABLE, DELETE with large row counts, TRUNCATE) on production databases without corresponding human authorization in audit logs. Correlate with agent override events (safety freeze instruction received but ignored). Flag rapid INSERT operations immediately following DELETE as data-fabrication evasion pattern.

suggestion.title: Agent Execution Continues After Safety Freeze or Stop Signal
suggestion.rationale: Article warns agent 'ignored explicit freeze instructions' and describes lack of 'human approval loop.' This is behavioral anomaly—agent overriding safety controls deliberately or through prompt injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor agent execution logs for divergence between issued safety signal (pause, freeze, stop) and actual execution state. Detect agent processes that spawn children or continue API calls after freeze instruction logged. Alert on agents receiving explicit 'do not execute' flag in prompt/control but executing command anyway.

suggestion.title: Hardcoded Credentials and Secrets in AI-Generated Code
suggestion.rationale: Article warns generated code 'may include... hardcoded secrets, or misconfigurations' and notes 'by the time post-commit scanning runs, the vulnerable output may already be in the repository.' Attack: agents generating code with embedded credentials faster than review can catch.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor commits and file creation events from agentic development processes for embedded API keys, tokens, passwords, or database credentials. Detect pattern of high-volume file creation (agent speed) containing secrets before human approval. Flag secrets appearing in generated code that would not pass pre-commit secret scanning.

suggestion.title: Dangerous Autonomous Workflow Chaining (Individual Acts to Aggregate Risk)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly warns 'autonomous workflow from chaining together five individually allowed actions into one dangerous outcome.' Describes sophisticated risk: composition of separately-safe actions into harmful sequence without human oversight.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequences of individually-whitelisted agent actions (read privileged data → enumerate targets → modify configuration → write output → call external API) that in composition achieve governance violation or dangerous outcome. Implement sequence-pattern detection for agent workflows; alert when action chain crosses risk threshold (e.g., data access + data modification + external communication in < 5 minutes without human breakpoint).

suggestion.title: Production Agent Data Exfiltration to Unauthorized External Destination
suggestion.rationale: Article describes production agents that 'interact with users, data, APIs, and production systems' and warns of risk to 'forward a customer record to a place it shouldn't go.' Agent-initiated unauthorized data transfer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor production agent processes (identified by service account, container ID, or execution context) for outbound connections to destinations outside corporate whitelist immediately following data access events. Flag agents reading customer/sensitive data followed by unexpected HTTP POST, DNS, or API calls to non-approved external endpoints. Alert on agents making exfiltration attempts to cloud storage, messaging platforms, or analysis services.

suggestion.title: API Endpoint Authorization Bypass (IDOR Pattern)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly presents IDOR as 'pernicious vulnerability' and shows /balance/{user_id} endpoint returning unauthorized user data. Detection should capture API calls that access user resources without role/ownership validation. Phrase: 'any user can request any other user's balance'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor API endpoints accepting user identifiers (user_id, account_id, customer_id) in path or query parameters; flag calls where authorization context (JWT claims, session user ID, API key) does not match requested resource owner. Focus on read operations returning PII/financial data.

suggestion.title: DOM Injection via Unsanitized Input (XSS Detection)
suggestion.rationale: Article cites Trusted Types web API as mitigation for 'most forms of DOM XSS', implying XSS injection sinks receiving untrusted input are actively exploitable. Phrase: 'ensuring that XSS injection sinks accept only known-safe values'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor client-side DOM manipulation (innerHTML, eval, Function constructor) with unsanitized input from user-controlled sources (URL params, form data, localStorage). Flag when trusted sanitizer is not invoked before DOM write.

suggestion.title: Memory Corruption via Type Confusion
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes Rust's elimination of memory corruption vulnerabilities and contrasts with languages lacking strict types. Discusses how 'secure-by-design libraries or well-placed library wrappers can completely stop entire classes of vulnerabilities'. Type confusion is the implied attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In environments using weakly-typed or dynamically-typed languages at the boundary (C/C++ interop, unsafe blocks), monitor for unexpected type casting, buffer overruns, or out-of-bounds access patterns. Correlate with application crashes containing memory-related signals.

suggestion.title: Unsafe Library Import or Missing Authentication Wrapper
suggestion.rationale: Article argues 'secure-by-design libraries' prevent vulnerabilities by design. Implies vulnerable code results from unsafe library usage or missing wrapper abstractions. Phrase: 'well-placed library wrappers can completely stop entire classes of vulnerabilities'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Static analysis or runtime monitoring for direct database queries without parameterization, or direct database connection usage without authentication middleware. Flag function signatures that accept user input and pass it directly to unsafe sinks (SQL, OS commands, DOM).

suggestion.title: Insufficient Authorization Check Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article shows vulnerable endpoint code with no auth check, then corrected version with `check_authentication() and check_authorization()`. The vulnerability pattern is repeatable across endpoints. Phrase: 'Forgetting one auth check on one API endpoint can lead to significant impacts'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit codebase for API endpoints accepting parameterized resource identifiers (user_id, account_id) but lacking explicit authorization guards before database/cache queries. Flag if auth check is conditional (error-prone) rather than enforced at type level.

suggestion.title: WFP SRA Web Application Unauthorized Access & Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'self-registration application (SRA) for Palestine was breached' and 'attackers gained access to personal data' — indicates exploitation of internet-facing web application with no detection logic generated despite clear compromise vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on WFP SRA access logs showing: (1) spike in 4xx errors from single source preceding successful 200 responses, (2) rapid API enumeration to beneficiary endpoints with fuzzing indicators, (3) sequential requests to data export/bulk download endpoints bypassing normal UI flows. Establish baseline registration-only traffic and flag queries accessing user PII in batch patterns.

suggestion.title: Large-Scale Beneficiary PII Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'they stole the information of people in roughly 600,000 Palestinian households' covering 'names, ID numbers, phone numbers, and location information' — massive data loss with zero exfiltration detection logic generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on database query patterns selecting 600K+ rows from beneficiary/PII tables within single session; flag egress of large data volumes (>500MB) from WFP database servers to non-whitelisted external IPs; detect creation/compression of archives containing name, ID, phone, location fields in staging directories immediately preceding network exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Post-Breach Impersonation & Phishing Campaign Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'WFP warned Palestinian beneficiaries to be wary of anyone claiming to represent the World Food Programme and requesting information or money' and 'not click or open any suspicious links' — indicates active secondary attack phase using compromised beneficiary identities, zero UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails to Gaza beneficiaries impersonating WFP requesting: account re-verification, relief claim confirmation, re-registration, or personal data resubmission. Flag WFP domain spoofing (homoglyphs, lookalikes), lack of DMARC/SPF validation, and inclusion of PII from breach (names, IDs) in phishing body. Correlate with email sender reputation and URL analysis.

suggestion.title: Registration Platform System Compromise Investigation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Registration Platform (SRA) has been temporarily suspended to implement urgent security and system protection improvements' — explicit acknowledgment of system compromise requiring forensic detection of access patterns and configuration changes around May 14.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on WFP SRA application logs May 1-20 showing: beneficiary database schema enumeration, privilege escalation attempts, service account abuse, addition of unauthorized API credentials, disabling/tampering of audit logging, or creation of backdoor administrative accounts. Flag unusual database connection patterns (spike in connection count, rare service accounts, abnormal query volume).

suggestion.title: PII Collection Phase Detection from Beneficiary Database
suggestion.rationale: Article states stolen data: 'names, ID numbers, phone numbers, and location information' — targeted collection of specific PII fields with no detection logic for this collection phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on database queries selecting PII columns (name, ID, phone, location) with anomalous patterns: broad SELECT statements without per-user WHERE clauses, UNION queries combining PII across tables, queries from non-standard service accounts, rapid sequential queries indicating data enumeration. Cross-reference with application access logs to identify corresponding HTTP/API calls.

suggestion.title: Persistence on Network Appliances — Scheduled Tasks / Cron Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article: "living inside corporate networks for well over a year"—requires persistence mechanisms on firewalls/storage. No persistence-phase detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network appliances (firewalls, NAS, storage arrays) for anomalous scheduled task creation, cron job additions, or startup script modifications. Alert on recurring execution mechanisms on non-standard hosts with low user interaction.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion — Log Deletion and Alerting Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article: "without ever tripping an alarm"—indicates active defense evasion (log clearing, alert rule disablement). Zero defense-evasion techniques captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Windows Event Log service disablement, security log clearing, or Sysmon rule modification. Monitor wmic.exe and powershell for event log deletion commands. Correlate log gaps with BRICKSTORM IOC activity timeline.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement to Network Devices — Management Interface Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: "compromise firewalls, storage systems, and network appliances"—requires lateral movement to non-standard targets. No network-device-targeting detection exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor RDP, SSH, Telnet connections from compromised endpoints to firewall/NAS/storage IP ranges. Alert on non-standard ports (2222, 8022, 9000) for device management. Correlate with stolen credential events.

suggestion.title: Credential Access — Default / Weak Appliance Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article implies credential compromise on appliances ("compromise firewalls...") but no credential-access mechanism identified. Missing common attack path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt failed login attempts on appliance management interfaces from non-expected source IPs. Alert on default account usage (admin, root) or bulk password spray patterns against device management ports.

suggestion.title: Malware Execution — BRICKSTORM Toolkit Behavioral Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article names "BRICKSTORM" malware but pipeline generated zero behavioral detections beyond hash matching. Missing behavior-based hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for low-level native API calls (VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory, CreateRemoteThread, NtWriteVirtualMemory) typical of malware. Monitor for unexpected kernel-mode activity from user-mode contexts or firmware modification patterns.

suggestion.title: Command and Control — Appliance C2 Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Custom toolkit maintaining year-long presence requires C2 channel. Article states "custom malware toolkit" but no command-and-control detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from firewall/appliance management subnet to external IPs. Alert on DNS queries for known VerdantBamboo C2 infrastructure from appliance VLAN. Flag TLS certificates with anomalous Subject or Issuer fields.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN vManage: Malicious File Upload and Command Injection (CVE-2026-20245)
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by uploading a crafted file to the affected system' and 'perform command injection attacks on an affected system and elevate their privileges as the root user.' Direct attack vector with executable consequences.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco SD-WAN Manager (vManage) for unexpected file uploads, particularly CSV files to /home/admin/ or similar writable paths, especially when followed by vScript or shell execution events. Correlate file creation with subsequent process execution for vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh or related vScript utilities.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN vManage: Root-Level vScript Execution via vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh
suggestion.rationale: Article provides exact log signature: 'Tenant list upload per vsmart serial number: /usr/bin/vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh -cli path /home/admin/malicious.csv vpn 0'—concrete behavior from actual exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of /usr/bin/vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh with '-cli path' arguments pointing to CSV files in /home/admin/ or other suspicious paths. Monitor /var/log/scripts.log for the syslog message pattern: 'vScript: Tenant list upload per vsmart serial number' immediately followed by vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh invocation.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN vManage: Unauthorized Configuration Push to Edge Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Cisco has observed limited cases where the exploitation of this bug resulted in a configuration change pushed to edge devices.' Configuration distribution is the attack outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SD-WAN Manager API and configuration daemon logs for configuration distribution commands that push changes to edge devices without corresponding authorized change tickets or authenticated admin action. Baseline normal config push rates and alert on anomalous deviations, especially when temporally correlated with suspicious file uploads or vScript execution.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN vManage: Pre-Exploitation Authentication Bypass (CVE-2026-20182, CVE-2026-20127)
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'To exploit this vulnerability, the attacker must have netadmin privileges on the affected system. This would require valid credentials or exploitation of CVE-2026-20182 or CVE-2026-20127.' These are the explicit prerequisite gatekeepers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for exploitation of CVE-2026-20182 (Catalyst SD-WAN Manager authentication bypass) and CVE-2026-20127 (authentication-bypass zero-day exploited since 2023) on SD-WAN Manager systems. Look for authentication events bypassing normal login workflows, unexpected privilege escalation to netadmin role, or failed authentication attempts immediately followed by successful credential usage.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN vManage: Netadmin Privilege Escalation or Acquisition
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'To exploit this vulnerability, the attacker must have netadmin privileges on the affected system.' Privilege acquisition is a critical prerequisite checkpoint in the attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation or modification of netadmin role assignments on SD-WAN Manager, especially for new or anomalous user accounts. Monitor for privilege escalation events from lower roles (read-only, operators) to netadmin. Correlate with subsequent suspicious file uploads or vScript execution to identify exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious FIFA/World Cup Domain Registration & Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Fake Sites' targeting World Cup 2026. Pipeline must detect typosquatting, lookalike domains, and rapid domain creation around major sporting events tied to phishing infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag domain registrations or DNS queries containing FIFA, World Cup, or tournament variants with typos (e.g., fifa2026.net, wordcup2026.com). Correlate with phishing/credential-harvesting URLs. Alert on rapid subdomain creation under newly registered domains.

suggestion.title: Banking Malware Delivery via Event-Themed Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Banking Malware' + 'Fake Sites.' Pipeline must detect malware samples, delivery mechanisms, and file hashes associated with World Cup-themed phishing campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect executable or script delivery from World Cup-themed domains or URLs. Alert on process execution chains following clicks on suspicious FIFA/tournament links. Correlate email attachment analysis and sandbox detonations with banking malware signatures.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Fake Login Forms
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Stolen Logins.' Pipeline must detect fake FIFA ticketing/account sites capturing credentials through HTML forms, keylogging, or forced authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP POST requests to World Cup-themed domains with credential-like payloads (email, password fields). Monitor for multiple failed authentication attempts followed by redirects to fake login pages. Flag form-capture infrastructure (phishing-kit patterns).

suggestion.title: Multi-Stage World Cup Event-Themed Spearphishing Campaign
suggestion.rationale: Title combines phishing (fake sites) + malware + credential theft. Pipeline must reconstruct end-to-end campaign flow: lure → payload delivery → credential exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Chain indicators: World Cup-themed email subject lines → suspicious domain clicks → malware execution → credential submission to attacker-controlled login page. Alert on multi-stage sequences; single indicators acceptable only with high confidence.

suggestion.title: Credential Dumping or Database Exposure (World Cup Fan Data)
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Stolen Logins.' Beyond credential harvesting, pipeline should detect bulk credential breaches or exposed databases related to FIFA/ticketing platforms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor dark web, paste sites, and credential-sharing forums for World Cup fan email/password dumps. Cross-correlate with known phishing/malware campaigns. Flag credential dumps mentioning FIFA, ticketing, or tournament-related account types.

suggestion.title: Financial Fraud / Account Takeover Post-Credential Theft
suggestion.rationale: Article title mentions 'Banking Malware' → stolen logins likely lead to account compromise and fund theft. Pipeline must detect anomalous account activity (geographic, velocity, card usage).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag account logins from new geolocations post-phishing campaign. Detect rapid consecutive failed authentication attempts (brute force on compromised credentials). Alert on unusual payment card or fund transfer patterns originating from compromised accounts.

suggestion.title: Everest Forms Pro Plugin RCE Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Critical Everest Forms Pro WordPress Plugin Flaw' exploited for 'Take Over Sites'—'takeover' outcome is RCE-class (article phrase: 'exploit...flaw to take over').
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST/GET requests to /wp-content/plugins/everest-forms/* endpoints with suspicious parameter payloads (code execution syntax, path traversal, unfiltered input) or requests to patched plugin versions. Establish baseline for plugin version and endpoint patterns; flag 5xx responses indicating exploitation failure.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Plugin Admin Functions
suggestion.rationale: Critical vulnerabilities in WordPress plugins typically involve auth bypass or privilege escalation; 'site takeover' outcome signals unauthenticated admin-level capability (article phrase: 'critical flaw to take over').
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to /wp-admin/ or plugin settings pages (admin.php?page=everest-forms-*) from sessions lacking valid WordPress authentication cookies. Alert on HTTP 200 responses to normally-protected admin pages preceded by HTTP requests to plugin endpoints, without wp-login redirection.

suggestion.title: WordPress Admin User Creation Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Takeover requires persistence; attackers create new admin accounts or elevate privileges to maintain control post-exploitation (implicit in 'take over sites' outcome).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect wp_users table INSERT or UPDATE operations creating/elevating users to 'administrator' role immediately following plugin exploitation attempt indicators (HTTP 200 to plugin RCE endpoints, unusual wp-admin access). Alert on user_registered timestamps within 60s of plugin endpoint activity.

suggestion.title: Plugin Backdoor / Web Shell Upload via File Upload Feature
suggestion.rationale: Everest Forms, a form-building plugin, includes file upload functionality; attackers exploit upload handlers to inject PHP web shells for persistent access enabling continued 'site takeover' operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multipart/form-data POST to plugin upload endpoints (/wp-content/plugins/everest-forms/form-submit, /wp-admin/admin-ajax.php?action=*upload*) containing executable extensions (php, phtml, php7) or MIME-type mismatches. Correlate with new .php file creation in wp-content/uploads or plugin directories.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Plugin Code Modification (Backdoor Installation)
suggestion.rationale: Attackers modify plugin files post-exploitation to maintain persistent backdoor access; 'site takeover' implies sustained control beyond initial exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file-write/modify events to /wp-content/plugins/everest-forms/*.php with timestamps outside of official plugin release windows or admin-initiated updates. Alert on file size changes, new require/include statements calling external URLs, or eval()/base64_decode() patterns in plugin core files.

suggestion.title: Database Query for Privilege Escalation via Plugin Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: If vulnerability involves SQL injection or database-level privilege escalation, attackers query wp_users or wp_usermeta to identify/modify admin roles (implied by 'site takeover' persistence requirement).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SQL queries containing UPDATE wp_users SET user_login/user_pass or SELECT * FROM wp_usermeta WHERE meta_key IN ('wp_capabilities', 'wp_user_level') immediately following plugin endpoint requests. Alert on schema enumeration queries (SHOW TABLES, SHOW COLUMNS) from unauthenticated plugin contexts.

suggestion.title: UC_EXTENSION_PERSISTENCE_ABUSE
suggestion.rationale: Article states extensions 'secretly harvest conversations'—implies durable persistence, not one-time install. Phrase 'quietly exploited' suggests long-term background activity. Detection should monitor for extension auto-enable via registry/manifest and background script execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Malicious extensions persist via Chrome/Edge extension manifest capabilities or auto-enable registry modifications. Look for extension manifest JSON writes with elevated permissions, or background script processes spawned by chrome.exe with non-standard arguments to extension directories.

suggestion.title: UC_CONVERSATION_EXFILTRATION_TO_C2
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'harvesting conversations and sending them off.' This is the collection-to-exfil bridge. Generic IOC hunts miss timing correlation between AI service API calls and outbound connections to C2 domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect patterns where active HTTPS traffic to AI platforms (api.openai.com, claude.ai, copilot.microsoft.com, etc.) is closely followed or paralleled by TLS connections to article IOCs (deepaichats.com, chatsaigpt.com). Correlation window 0–300 seconds; filter by device with open browser session.

suggestion.title: UC_EXTENSION_MANIFEST_TAMPERING
suggestion.rationale: Malicious extensions must escalate permissions or inject scripts post-installation. Article implies stealthy operation—suggests manifest manipulation to hide capabilities or request new permissions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for writes to Chrome/Edge/Firefox extension manifest files (manifest.json) after initial installation. Correlate manifest changes with permission escalations (e.g., 'webRequest', 'tabs', 'cookies') or script injection patterns. Flag if manifest modified outside official update windows.

suggestion.title: UC_BROWSER_IFRAME_INJECTION
suggestion.rationale: Browser extensions often inject iframes or inject malicious scripts into target pages (AI chat interfaces). Article's 'harvesting conversations' likely involves DOM access via injected code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual script execution or network requests originating from iframe elements injected into OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft, or Google AI service domains. Correlate browser process children or script execution with extension IDs from suspicious installations.

suggestion.title: IIS Web Shell File Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Custom Web Shell Framework' targeting IIS—implies .aspx/.ashx file creation in web-accessible directories. Article body should contain deployment details (paths, file signatures, naming patterns).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected .aspx, .ashx, .jspx files created under %SystemRoot%\inetpub\wwwroot or custom app pools' virtual directories by System/NETWORK SERVICE. Correlate with w3wp.exe spawning cmd.exe or powershell.exe within 10 seconds of file creation.

suggestion.title: IIS Worker Process Executing Shells
suggestion.rationale: Web shell frameworks require command execution through IIS process (w3wp.exe). This is the core mechanism for the threat described.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag w3wp.exe (or ApplicationPoolIdentity) launching cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or csc.exe with base64-encoded parameters, obfuscated arguments, or redirects to network sockets. Monitor for parent process tree anomalies (IIS → shell → utilities).

suggestion.title: IIS Log Deletion or Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Attackers deploying web shells typically erase IIS access logs to hide attack evidence. Article's threat sophistication ('threat cluster') implies anti-forensics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor %SystemRoot%\System32\LogFiles\W3SVC\* for deletion, truncation, or clear operations triggered by non-System users or unexpected processes. Alert on IIS log directory access during off-hours or outside rotation schedules.

suggestion.title: Suspicious HTTP Requests to Web Shell Paths
suggestion.rationale: Operators interact with web shells via HTTP requests containing encoded commands or scripts. Article describes web shell 'framework' implying structured C2 protocol.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST/GET requests to .aspx/.ashx/.jsp files with base64, hex-encoded, or gzip payloads in query strings or POST bodies. Flag requests with suspicious User-Agents or multiple rapid requests to same path with different parameters.

suggestion.title: IIS Application Pool Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Web shells often escalate from network service account to System. Article implies custom framework suggesting privilege escalation capabilities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for w3wp.exe creating child processes with SYSTEM privileges (impersonation tokens or token theft). Alert on unexpected Token::CreateProcessAsUser or LSA handle opens from IIS worker processes.

suggestion.title: Network Recon from Compromised IIS Server
suggestion.rationale: Article describes targeting 'cluster' (plural), suggesting lateral movement post-exploitation. Attackers typically enumerate network after IIS compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag network enumeration tools (ping, ipconfig, nslookup, nbstat) executed from w3wp.exe or spawned children. Monitor for unusual remote share access (\\<IP>\admin$ or c$) from the IIS server.

suggestion.title: PCPJack Malware Execution on Cloud Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names PCPJack as the malware hijacking servers. Pipeline extracted zero malware IOCs, execution signatures, or process-level detections despite this being the core threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag suspicious process spawning on cloud compute instances post-compromise, unsigned code execution, or unexpected scheduled tasks consistent with malware installation. Cross-correlate with cloud API anomalies.

suggestion.title: Anomalous SMTP Relay Activity from Cloud Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly describes 'covert SMTP relay network'—indicating C2-orchestrated mail abuse at scale. Pipeline produced zero C2, SMTP exfiltration, or impact-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sustained or high-volume SMTP outbound from cloud instances not normally configured as mail relays. Flag instances with periodic connection attempts to external SMTP servers or DNS queries for mail infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Cloud Credential Compromise or Service Account Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Compromise of 230 servers across three distinct cloud providers (AWS/GCP/Azure) implies either stolen credentials, IAM policy abuse, or service account takeover as initial vector. Pipeline missed initial-access and lateral-movement phases entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous cloud authentication: failed-then-successful logins from unusual geographies, service account key creation followed by compute modification, or bulk resource enumeration across multiple regions/accounts within short timeframe.

suggestion.title: Persistence Mechanism Deployment Across Cloud Instances
suggestion.rationale: Operating a 230-server relay network requires durable persistence; article implies sustained command infrastructure. Pipeline reconstructed zero persistence-phase techniques (T1098.002, T1136, etc.).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag bulk creation of service accounts or SSH public keys across disparate cloud instances, unauthorized IAM policy modifications enabling persistent access, or cron/scheduled-task deployments on multiple servers within narrow time window.

suggestion.title: Cloud Infrastructure Reconnaissance and Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Targeting exactly 230 servers across three cloud vendors suggests prior reconnaissance. Article does not detail enumeration but attack surface implies T1580/T1526 discovery activities before compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous cloud API query patterns: high-volume DescribeInstances, ListVMs, or ListComputeInstances from single principal across multiple regions or resource types, especially if followed by failed exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Mass Cloud Instance Modification for Malware Deployment
suggestion.rationale: 230-server compromise implies automated or batch deployment mechanism. Pipeline missed execution and lateral-movement indicators for scale-based attack orchestration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk API calls modifying cloud instances within single session: PutUserData, ModifyImageAttribute, or CreateSnapshot across 10+ instances; cross-reference with SSH key injection or privilege-escalation attempts.

suggestion.title: PAN-OS CVE-2026-0257 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Active Exploitation of PAN-OS CVE-2026-0257'—pipeline should detect HTTP requests with payloads or URI patterns consistent with this RCE vector. Pipeline extracted no kill-chain phases despite this being initial-access attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PAN-OS management interface (port 443, https://target/api/v1 paths) for unusual POST requests with command injection patterns or script execution attempts. Flag requests originating from non-administrative IP ranges during non-business hours.

suggestion.title: Web Shell or Command Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation implies attacker gains code execution; article should describe post-exploitation activity (web shell, reverse shell, command execution). Pipeline missed execution phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on spawning of shell interpreters (bash, sh, powershell, cmd.exe) as child processes of firewall management services or httpd. Monitor for unusual argument patterns (base64-encoded commands, curl/wget to external URLs).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Outbound Connections from Compromised Firewall
suggestion.rationale: Exploited firewalls are often used as pivot points or beacons to attacker infrastructure; article should list C2 domains or callback IP addresses. Pipeline extracted no IOCs for this threat path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor egress traffic from PAN-OS management interface to non-whitelisted external IPs/domains, especially port 4444, 8080, 443 to suspicious C2 ranges. Flag DNS queries from firewall to unusual second-level domains.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Scheduled Task or Cron on PAN-OS
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation often leads to persistence mechanisms (cron jobs, at, scheduled tasks). Article should document attacker persistence method; pipeline has no kill-chain entry for persistence phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor system cron tables and scheduled task creation on PAN-OS appliances for new entries post-exploitation window. Alert on modification of /etc/cron.d or crontab -e invocations followed by network callbacks.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Firewall to Internal Network
suggestion.rationale: Compromised firewalls are jump-off points for network pivot attacks. Article should enumerate lateral-movement indicators if attacker leverages firewall access for deeper penetration—none captured by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect internal network scanning or mass connection attempts originating from PAN-OS management or dataplane interfaces after exploitation window. Flag LDAP, SSH, RDP, or SMB probe patterns originating from firewall IP.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration or Sensitive File Access from Firewall
suggestion.rationale: PAN-OS appliances often hold logs, configuration secrets, and visibility into internal network. Article should mention exfiltration of firewall logs, configs, or API keys; pipeline missed this collection/exfiltration phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor reads of /var/log/*, /config/*, /root/.ssh/*, and API credential stores on PAN-OS, especially during off-hours or following exploitation indicators. Flag bulk data transfers to external IPs disguised as heartbeat or syslog.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with Geographic Targeting Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states phishing campaign targeting UK, Germany, Italy, and South Africa. No use case maps to multi-region phishing detection despite clear geographic targeting signal in title.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound emails with subject lines or sender patterns impersonating government/financial institutions in targeted geographies. Correlate sender IP geolocation mismatch (non-UK/EU IPs sending as UK entities). Flag high volume to recipients in UK, Germany, Italy, South Africa within 24h window.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting Form Landing Pages
suggestion.rationale: Phishing-to-credential-theft pipeline fundamental to TA4922 TTPs; no detection for post-click credential capture phase mentioned despite implicit attack flow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP POST requests to suspected phishing infrastructure mimicking SSO/email/banking login pages originating from users in targeted regions. Monitor for high-entropy base64 or URL-encoded payloads in request body (credential exfil).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Attachment Execution Post-Phishing Click
suggestion.rationale: Organized multi-country campaign likely includes malware delivery; zero detection for macro/script execution from email-sourced files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Office applications (winword.exe, excel.exe) spawning child processes (powershell, cmd, wscript) within 30s of file access from Downloads, Temp, or AppData folders; correlate parent process to Outlook.exe or web browser.

suggestion.title: Coordinated Phishing Campaign Blast Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates 'expands' campaigns across four countries simultaneously. No aggregation rule to detect coordinated phishing surges by sender pattern, subject similarity, or URL payload overlap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert if phishing email volume exceeds 50th percentile baseline for UK, Germany, Italy, or South Africa within same 4-hour window AND sender domain/URL exhibits string similarity (Levenshtein distance <3) across regions.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20230 Unified CM RCE Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly states 'Exploit Code Goes Public'—the primary attack vector. Zero detection use cases generated for exploitation attempts despite HIGH severity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Unified CM web-facing services (typical ports 8443, 8884) for HTTP requests with known exploit payloads or malformed parameters. Alert on POST/GET requests to known vulnerable endpoints. Correlate with WAF denials and IDS signatures for CVE-2026-20230.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Process Execution from Unified CM Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Exploit-code context implies RCE capability; no execution-phase detection suggested. Article phrase: 'Exploit Code Goes Public' signals imminent remote code execution attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by Unified CM application processes (tomcat, java) including cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash. Monitor for encoded command execution, file download utilities, or reverse-shell indicators in command-line arguments.

suggestion.title: Unified CM Service Crash or Unexpected Restart Cluster
suggestion.rationale: High-severity RCE exploits often cause application instability or DoS side-effects. No impact-phase detection for service degradation was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ≥2 Unified CM service restarts within 30 minutes or repeated process crashes. Monitor for abnormal exit codes and memory exhaustion warnings. Correlate with application logs for out-of-memory or null-pointer exceptions.

suggestion.title: Unified CM Admin Account Anomalies Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Successful RCE often leads to lateral movement or credential theft. No post-compromise detection use case for admin activity was suggested despite exploit-code disclosure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new admin account creation, password resets, or role elevations during or immediately after CVE-2026-20230 exploitation window. Flag logins from unexpected geographies or IPs to Unified CM admin consoles.

suggestion.title: Network Reconnaissance for Unified CM Vulnerability Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Public exploit release typically triggers attacker scanning. No discovery-phase detection was generated despite imminent attack surface created by public PoC code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect port scans or service enumeration targeting Unified CM listening ports (6970, 6971, 7936, 8443, 8884). Alert on vulnerability scanner User-Agents (Nessus, Qualys) or brute-force login attempts against admin interfaces.

suggestion.title: WebDialer SSRF Exploitation Attempt (Crafted HTTP Request)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers send 'a crafted HTTP request' exploiting SSRF to the WebDialer service. This is the initial compromise vector; no UC was generated for detecting such requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Cisco Unified CM WebDialer endpoints for SSRF indicators: out-of-band redirects, file:// or localhost URIs, unusual query parameters, or requests from unauthenticated sources. Correlate spike in 4xx/5xx responses with subsequent system activity.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Write from WebDialer Service Context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploit 'write[s] files to the underlying operating system.' No detection UC flags file creation/modification by the WebDialer process outside expected application directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation or write operations from the WebDialer service process (tomcat/Java application server context) to system directories (/bin, /lib, /etc, /root). Baseline normal operations and alert on writes to unexpected paths or files with suspicious names (scripts, binaries, cron jobs).

suggestion.title: Root Privilege Escalation from WebDialer Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states the attack 'could be used later to elevate to root.' No UC detects privilege escalation originating from the WebDialer service or related process chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for privilege escalation attempts (sudo invocation, uid changes, capability grants) originating from or related to the WebDialer service or its child processes. Alert if WebDialer process (non-root) spawns actions executing with root privileges.

suggestion.title: WebDialer Service Activation on Disabled-by-Default Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'WebDialer is disabled by default' and attackers would need to enable it. No UC detects unexpected service activation or persistent access setup.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag WebDialer service state changes from disabled to enabled outside of scheduled maintenance windows. Monitor Cisco Unified CM Administration CTI Services menu access logs and API calls that modify service activation status.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20230 PoC Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'publicly available proof-of-concept exploit code' exists. No UC captures known PoC HTTP request signatures or exploitation patterns for detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract and correlate HTTP request signatures from public PoC code (URIs, headers, parameter structures) against WebDialer endpoint logs. Implement WAF/IPS signatures derived from known exploit implementations.

suggestion.title: Malicious Issue Triggers Unintended GitHub Actions Workflow Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'one malicious issue hijack repositories'—establishes issue content as attack trigger; no UC captures issue→workflow→execution chain
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect issue creation by external or low-privilege actor immediately triggering workflow execution with elevated token scope (WRITE/ADMIN). Flag issues containing shell metacharacters, variable interpolation syntax, or GitHub Actions context references in body/title that flow into environment or script inputs.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Inherits Elevated Permissions When Triggered from Issue Event
suggestion.rationale: Hijacking requires privilege escalation; pipeline missed UC for detecting permission mismatch between issue-actor and workflow-token scope
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor workflows triggered by issue_comment or issues events that request or inherit secrets, push tokens, or admin scopes. Correlate with actor permissions: if non-admin opened the issue, but workflow runs with WRITE/ADMIN, flag for potential token scope abuse.

suggestion.title: Repository Configuration or Branch Protection Modified by GitHub Actions Workflow
suggestion.rationale: Repository hijacking requires disabling protections or seizing control; no UC detects repo-config changes originating from Actions triggered by untrusted events
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on repository settings changes (branch protection rules, admin/owner list, default branch, visibility) performed by GitHub Actions workflows, especially those triggered by issue, pull_request_review, or external actor dispatch rather than push or explicit workflow_dispatch by authorized user.

suggestion.title: Code Execution via GitHub Actions Runner Invoked by Untrusted Issue Metadata
suggestion.rationale: Hijacking depends on arbitrary execution; article describes flaw in how Issues trigger Actions—UC needed for detecting command injection in workflow inputs derived from issue body/title
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GitHub Actions workflows where commands, scripts, or environment variable assignments reference ${{ github.event.issue.body }}, ${{ github.event.issue.title }}, or similar untrusted inputs. Flag if those fields contain shell escapes, backticks, $(…) substitution, or /bin/bash directives.

suggestion.title: Malicious GTM Container Activation on Checkout Pages
suggestion.rationale: Article directly states: 'malicious code is embedded in legitimate-looking GTM containers, which activate when a shopper reaches a checkout page'—clear execution and payload delivery indicator that should trigger detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GTM container load events for non-standard JavaScript execution patterns. Flag containers that reference Stripe customer records (cus_*) in metadata or perform dynamic code reassembly via new Function(). Correlate with checkout page navigation.

suggestion.title: Stripe Customer Record Abuse for Stolen Payment Data Storage
suggestion.rationale: Core exfiltration sink: 'Every stolen payment card becomes a fake customer record in the attacker's Stripe account, turning Stripe into a storage backend for stolen data.' Bulk creation of customer objects post-checkout is the detection pivot.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid bulk creation of Stripe customer records (cus_* IDs) within 60 seconds of payment capture events. Inspect metadata fields for XOR-obfuscated or base64-encoded card-number-like patterns. Baseline normal API call patterns to identify spike anomalies.

suggestion.title: XOR-Obfuscated Payment Data in Browser localStorage
suggestion.rationale: Staging mechanism: 'The stolen data is concatenated into a single string, obfuscated using the XOR operation, and stored locally instead of immediately exfiltrated.' localStorage is the data holding tank before exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect and attempt to decode suspicious localStorage entries, especially keys like _d_data_customer_. Alert on XOR-obfuscated sequences alongside checkout page script execution and subsequent Stripe API calls within the same session.

suggestion.title: Firestore Document Exploitation for Payload Delivery (tracking/captcha)
suggestion.rationale: Variant infrastructure: article describes 'Google Firestore, a cloud database service for data storage and real-time retrieval, is used instead of Stripe' with document path 'tracking/captcha in a project called braintree-payment-app'—alternate C2 mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Firestore API calls to documents named 'tracking/captcha' or projects containing 'braintree' strings. Detect payload retrieval followed by immediate JavaScript execution. Track project creation timestamps near December 24, 2025 (campaign start date).

suggestion.title: Checkout Form Credit Card Data Capture and Aggregation
suggestion.rationale: Collection target: 'The card skimmer targets Magento/Adobe Commerce checkout pages and attempts to capture payment data (credit card number, expiration date, CVV code, customer name) as well as billing and email addresses, and phone number.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for JavaScript injected into Magento/Adobe Commerce checkout forms that reads or aggregates payment field values (card, CVV, expiry, email, phone). Alert on form submission handlers installed post-GTM load and data concatenation patterns.

suggestion.title: Periodic Automated Exfiltration Routine (60-Second Intervals)
suggestion.rationale: Exfiltration cadence: 'Retrieving the data is done through a separate routine, which executes right after a page load and every minute after'—predictable timing signature enables reliable detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect periodic outbound calls to api.stripe.com at ~60-second intervals from checkout pages. Analyze payloads for obfuscated customer data. Correlate timing with page load and monitor for localStorage deletion patterns immediately post-exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Domains Mimicking Open-Source Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states fake sites are mimicking open-source tools and ranking high in Google search results. Domain reputation, registration age, SSL certificate info, and WHOIS mismatches with legitimate tool maintainers should be monitored. Phrase: 'Fake Sites Mimicking Open-Source Tools Rank High on Google'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries and clicks on domains that closely resemble legitimate open-source tool names (e.g., typosquatting, subdomain spoofing). Flag domains registered within last 30 days with high search engine visibility, SSL certificates mismatched to legitimate tool orgs, or hosted on shared infrastructure associated with malware delivery.

suggestion.title: TDS Redirect Traffic Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article core mechanic: malware delivery via TDS (Traffic Distribution System). TDS redirects exhibit characteristic patterns (conditional redirects based on IP/geo/user-agent, multi-stage redirects, landing page variation). Phrase: 'Deliver Malware via TDS'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect TDS behavior by identifying redirect chains from search engine results to suspicious domains, particularly requests that vary payloads by GeoIP/user-agent. Monitor for 302/meta-refresh redirects from seemingly legitimate domains to dynamic/pseudonymous hosting. Correlate high redirect counts from same user within short time window.

suggestion.title: Executable Downloads from Fake Tool Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Users searching for open-source tools will attempt to download what they believe is legitimate software; TDS redirects them to fake sites hosting malware. Article establishes this attack path. Phrase: 'Fake Sites... Rank High on Google to Deliver Malware'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on executable/installer downloads (EXE, MSI, ZIP containing PE) from domains that mimic popular open-source tools (e.g., misspelled npm packages, PyPI-like domains, GitHub clones). Trigger on suspicious file metadata (mismatched digital signatures, abnormal version strings), execution from temp/downloads, and parent process being a web browser launched from search activity.

suggestion.title: Open-Source Tool Name Typosquatting in Search Results
suggestion.rationale: SEO poisoning hinges on compromised or lookalike domains ranking high. Monitoring search engine result pages (SERPs) for domains attempting to impersonate tool names is critical early detection. Phrase: 'Rank High on Google'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SERP clicks and DNS queries for domains containing typos or slight variations of popular open-source tool names (npm, pip, go packages, GitHub projects). Flag domains that appear in organic search but are not associated with official tool maintainers. Correlate with downloads or process execution on the user endpoint.

suggestion.title: Malware File Drops from TDS-Redirected Downloads
suggestion.rationale: TDS delivers actual malware payload to compromised endpoints. Detection must catch file drops and suspicious execution. Article indicates malware is the ultimate payload delivered via this chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for newly created executable files in user directories (Downloads, AppData, Temp) that are unsigned, have anomalous metadata, execute immediately after download, and initiate unexpected outbound connections (C2 beaconing). Correlate file drop with preceding TDS redirect or suspicious domain access.

suggestion.title: Google Search Click to Malware Executable Chain
suggestion.rationale: Complete attack chain: user searches for open-source tool → click malicious SERP result → TDS redirect → download malware → execution. Detection must chain these events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build correlated detection: (1) browser search query for known open-source tool name, (2) HTTP request to suspicious domain mimicking that tool, (3) redirect chain with geographic/user-agent variance, (4) executable download from final redirect, (5) execution of downloaded file with unsigned/suspicious metadata. Multi-event correlation within 10-minute window.

suggestion.title: Malware Execution from Browser Download Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states FlutterShell spreads 'via Malicious Google and YouTube Ads' — establishes user-initiated download → execution pattern. No UC generated for this critical initial execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution of unsigned binaries from ~/Downloads or typical browser cache directories within 60 seconds of network traffic to ad-serving domains. Correlate browser activity (Safari, Chrome) with child process spawning suspicious Flutter-based or obfuscated binaries.

suggestion.title: macOS Persistence via Launch Agents or Login Items
suggestion.rationale: Article describes a 'Backdoor' — persistence is implicit. No use case covering macOS-specific persistence mechanisms (LaunchAgents, LaunchDaemons, login items) that FlutterShell likely exploits.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ~/Library/LaunchAgents and ~/Library/LaunchDaemons for new plist files created post-infection. Alert on plist modifications where executable path points to /tmp, /var/tmp, or user-writable application directories with timing correlation to malware execution.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Ad-Delivered Malware Download Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Malicious Google and YouTube Ads' as delivery mechanism — this indicates ad-network compromise or attacker-controlled ad account. No UC generated for detecting ad-network abuse or detecting landing pages serving malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag ad-serving infrastructure (doubleclick.net, googleadservices.com, youtube-nocookie.com redirect chains) that resolve to attacker-controlled CNAME/A records or unusual geographies. Detect landing pages on ad networks returning executable content or redirection to malware-hosting domains.

suggestion.title: FlutterShell Command-and-Control Callback Detection
suggestion.rationale: A 'Backdoor' necessarily establishes C2. Article does not explicitly detail C2 mechanisms in provided text, but detection use case for backdoor callback is absent. Should monitor for outbound connections to known FlutterShell C2 infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create threat intelligence watchlist for FlutterShell C2 domains/IPs once disclosed. Alert on outbound TLS connections from suspicious process with Flutter-runtime-specific JA3 fingerprint or User-Agent strings. Monitor for beaconing patterns (regular callbacks to same destination).

suggestion.title: Quarantine Attribute Bypass on macOS Downloaded Binary
suggestion.rationale: macOS quarantine mechanism (com.apple.quarantine xattr) would normally block unsigned binaries delivered via ads. Sophisticated malware removes this attribute. Pipeline should flag this evasion technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for xattr deletion or clearing on files in ~/Downloads within minutes of download completion. Correlate with subsequent unsigned binary execution. Flag removal of com.apple.quarantine before parent browser process has exited.

suggestion.title: Ad Click-to-Download-to-Execute Kill Chain Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Complete attack chain from malicious ad click to backdoor execution should be detectable via process and network telemetry correlation. No synthetic use case for end-to-end detection of this sequence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Construct multi-event correlation: (1) HTTP request from browser to ad-serving domain, (2) redirect to external malware host, (3) file download in ~/Downloads, (4) com.apple.quarantine removal, (5) process execution of downloaded binary — all within 5-minute window. Alert on complete chain.

suggestion.title: WebSocket YPTSocket Metadata Broadcast — XSS Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically describes 'Per-Client Metadata Broadcast in YPTSocket Plugin'—the attack vector uses WebSocket protocol, not HTTP query strings alone. Network detection (UC_24_2) may miss encrypted or binary WebSocket payloads.
log_sources: Web application proxy logs with TLS decryption
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt WebSocket frames to YPTSocket endpoints for XSS payload patterns in the 'page_title' metadata field or other broadcast message bodies. Look for script tags, event handler attributes (onerror, onload, onclick), or JavaScript protocol URIs that would be anomalous in legitimate broadcast metadata.

suggestion.title: Admin Context XSS Exploitation — Privilege-Aware Injection Detection
