suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'execute arbitrary JavaScript in the authenticated origin of every administrator currently viewing'—detection should filter for admin-only sessions and endpoints, not generic web traffic, to reduce noise and identify high-value compromise attempts.
log_sources: Web application logs with role/privilege metadata
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Refine UC_24_2 to fire only when XSS injection attempts target admin-scoped endpoints (e.g., /admin/*, /dashboard/*, configuration APIs) AND the session is authenticated with elevated privileges. Separate these high-risk attempts from generic web injection noise and correlate with admin user IDs.

suggestion.title: Post-XSS Session Hijacking — JavaScript Context Cookie/Token Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Given 'arbitrary JavaScript' execution in admin context, attacker can steal session cookies, OAuth tokens, or auth headers via document.cookie/localStorage APIs. This is the critical next step not covered by current UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unusual outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from the AVideo application to external/untrusted domains within seconds of XSS injection detection (potential exfiltration beacons). Also hunt for XSS payloads themselves containing credential-stealing patterns such as document.cookie, localStorage.getItem(), sessionStorage, or fetch() calls to external URLs.

suggestion.title: AVideo Admin Configuration Tampering Post-XSS Compromise
suggestion.rationale: JavaScript execution in admin context enables attacker to modify application settings, disable security controls, create backdoor accounts, or modify plugins. This post-exploitation objective is not addressed by any current UC.
log_sources: Web application logs for /admin/ and API endpoints
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for admin configuration API calls (plugin enable/disable, user creation, permission elevation, debug feature toggling) that originate from sessions coinciding with or shortly after detected XSS injection. Look for unusual request patterns, bulk changes, or modifications to normally-locked settings.

suggestion.title: npm package publish / self-propagation from compromised dev machine
suggestion.rationale: Article states malicious package 'attempted self-propagation.' No UC detects the worm re-publishing itself or modifying package.json to inject the compromised package into downstream dependencies. This is a critical missing link in the attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm cli commands (npm publish, npm ci) executed by npm or node processes during or shortly after preinstall hook execution. Correlate with dev-environment machine identities. Look for package.json writes that add @cap-js/openapi as a dependency to unrelated projects.

suggestion.title: npm registry authentication using stolen tokens post-compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies npm tokens are harvested. No UC detects these tokens being used to authenticate to npm registry from anomalous geographic location, IP, or user-agent. Stolen tokens enable attackers to publish malicious versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry API calls (registry.npmjs.org) for authentication with stolen tokens or API keys. Flag publishes of packages under previously uncompromised accounts. Correlate publish operations with prior credential-file access detected in UC_22_6.

suggestion.title: Compromised @cap-js/openapi v1.4.1 package installation detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies the malicious version is @cap-js/openapi@1.4.1. No UC directly detects package lock file or npm ls output showing this exact version installed. This is the most direct artifact-based IOC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for package-lock.json, yarn.lock, or pnpm-lock.yaml files containing '"@cap-js/openapi": "1.4.1"' or npm ls output showing this version. Correlate filesystem writes to node_modules/@cap-js/openapi/ on or after 2026-05-19 with process execution in that directory.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration correlation: credential file read → network connection to t.m-kosche.com
suggestion.rationale: Article describes a payload that harvests credentials and sends them out. No UC correlates the two events in time. Current UC_22_3 and UC_22_6 detect in isolation; missing is the causality chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For each machine: within a 5-minute window, if node/npm process accesses ≥2 credential files (UC_22_6) AND the same or parent process initiates connection to t.m-kosche.com (UC_22_3), escalate to critical. This temporal causality is harder to explain as legitimate.

suggestion.title: Unusual child process spawning from npm preinstall (beyond Bun)
suggestion.rationale: Article doesn't specify Bun; mentions only 'JavaScript' execution and 'setup.mjs loader.' Worm could spawn any runtime (deno, node child process, native binary). UC_22_4 over-specifies Bun. Need broader hunt for any non-standard child process from npm preinstall hook.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process spawn from npm/node where the child process is NOT (node, npm, npx, yarn, pnpm, python, perl, bash, sh, powershell) and parent command line contains 'preinstall', 'setup.mjs', or 'postinstall'. Include YARA/signature match for binary payload execution from node_modules.

suggestion.title: DNS/WHOIS reconnaissance on t.m-kosche.com prior to installation
suggestion.rationale: Threat actor may have tested the C2 domain before injecting it. Article provides domain as primary IOC but no UC detects machines that resolved or pinged the domain *before* the May 19 installation window, indicating prior threat reconnaissance or testing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any DNS query or network connection to t.m-kosche.com on or after 2026-05-15 (before the May 19 package publish, to catch attacker setup) from non-cloud-provider IPs. Correlate with subsequent npm install activity on the same machine.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Email Forwarding Rule Creation
suggestion.rationale: Five-month mailbox access suggests exfiltration; attackers typically create forwarding rules or delegate access. Article title states 'spied on...mailbox,' indicating adversary mail collection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for New-InboxRule or Set-InboxRule PowerShell activity from non-standard sources, or API calls to create forward-to-external-email rules. Correlate with suspicious login events from the same time window.

suggestion.title: Impossible Travel to Email Login
suggestion.rationale: Executive account compromise over five months implies attackers authenticated from attacker-controlled infrastructure. Article establishes geographic/temporal persistence gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag sign-in events for the target mailbox that occur from IP space inconsistent with historical user behavior, especially if preceded by failed auth attempts. Correlate distance/time between consecutive logins.

suggestion.title: Mailbox Delegation to Attacker-Controlled Account
suggestion.rationale: Five-month spying suggests persistent access mechanism. Delegation or application impersonation is quieter than repeated logins and commonly abused in targeted campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Add-MailboxPermission, Set-Mailbox -GrantSendOnBehalfOfPermissions, and OAuth app consent grants (especially those requesting Mail.Read, Mail.ReadWrite) in the target's mailbox.

suggestion.title: Bulk Email Download or PST Export
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'spied on...mailbox for five months'—implies adversary exfiltrated mail contents, not just read metadata. Export operations leave forensic traces.
log_sources: Network traffic (TLS handshakes to odd destinations)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual IMAP/POP3 bulk downloads, PST export attempts via Outlook or eDiscovery APIs, or abnormally large email folder access (reads >X messages in <Y minutes) from the compromised account.

suggestion.title: Credential Validation via Outlook Web Access
suggestion.rationale: If attackers accessed via OWA over five months, successful login patterns would differ from the executive's baseline. OWA logs are gold for persistence validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search OWA access logs for the target mailbox from atypical user agents, geolocations, or times. Correlate OWA logins with absence of Outlook MAPI/EAS sync from expected devices; suggests attacker-side browser access.

suggestion.title: Long-Dwell Mailbox Access Without MFA Challenge
suggestion.rationale: Five months of undetected access implies either MFA bypass, legacy protocol abuse (IMAP without MFA enforcement), or unmonitored access path. Article's 'spied' language suggests surveillance, not detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag mailbox access events where MFA was NOT challenged over a 30+ day window. Compare to baseline: legitimate user logins should trigger MFA challenges at intervals. Anomaly = non-MFA paths (IMAP, SMTP AUTH, app passwords) or policy gaps.

suggestion.title: Encoded PowerShell execution via cmd.exe spawning
suggestion.rationale: KongTuke case study explicitly states: 'cmd.exe process spawning powershell.exe with an -EncodedCommand parameter containing a Base64-encoded payload.' Direct attack pattern requiring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when cmd.exe or explorer.exe spawns powershell.exe with -EncodedCommand (-Enc, -EC) flags. Base64 payloads indicate obfuscation. Correlate parent process with suspicious network outbound connections on ports 6060 or non-standard HTTPS ranges.

suggestion.title: Invoke-WebRequest to ApplicationData staging with Remove-Item cleanup
suggestion.rationale: Case study shows exact execution chain: 'Invoke-WebRequest to fetch script.ps1, dropping into ApplicationData' followed by 'Remove-Item attempting to delete traces.' File staging + anti-forensics pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Invoke-WebRequest or DownloadFile targeting %APPDATA%, %TEMP%, or user profile subdirectories. Alert when Remove-Item or del.exe targets recently-modified scripts in these paths within 10 minutes of fetch. High confidence when network connection to known-bad IP precedes script staging.

suggestion.title: Outbound curl/wget to EVILEMPIRE ASN ranges
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names EVILEMPIRE as 'autonomous systems with documented history of hosting command-and-control infrastructure' and case study shows 'curl.exe making requests to same C2 infrastructure.' User-Agent persistence through encryption noted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain blocklist of EVILEMPIRE ASN ranges. Alert on outbound connections from curl, wget, Python http.client, or Invoke-WebRequest to these ASNs regardless of destination IP. User-Agent string in firewall logs provides signal even when payload encrypted.

suggestion.title: Traffic Direction System (TDS) redirect chain to C2
suggestion.rationale: Article describes KongTuke initial compromise: 'compromised website redirects visitors through chain of intermediate servers before landing on malicious payload host' via path '/capcha9856.' TDS is signature attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP 30x redirect chains (2+ hops) from legitimate-appearing domains to suspicious IPs/ASNs. Flag paths matching CMS evasion patterns (/capcha*, /index*.php?param=). Correlate with PowerShell execution or binary downloads within 5 minutes on same endpoint.

suggestion.title: Domain Generation Algorithm (DGA) via entropy and n-gram analysis
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Algorithmically generated domains have statistical properties (character distribution, entropy, n-gram frequency) that distinguish them from human-registered domains.' Concrete ML-based hunt hypothesis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Score DNS queries by character entropy, n-gram frequency, and syllable uniformity. Flag queries scoring >0.85 Shannon entropy or with character distributions matching generated-domain statistical profiles. Suppress legitimate high-entropy technical domains (e.g., hashes in subdomains). Pair with reputation lookup on resolved IPs.

suggestion.title: MSIEXEC User-Agent outbound connections to suspicious ASNs
suggestion.rationale: Article hunting hypothesis: 'MSIEXEC User-Agent making connections to suspicious or malicious ASNs. MSIEXEC fetching remote packages is a known living-off-the-land technique.' User-Agent persistence critical for detection when payload encrypted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound network events with User-Agent 'msiexec.exe' or 'Windows Update' variant connecting to non-Microsoft IPs. Baseline legitimate MSI deployments in environment, then surface deviations. Port 6060 and 8080 particularly suspicious in msiexec context.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Installation with Phantom Gyp Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'Phantom Gyp' as attack mechanism—binding.gyp is used to compile native modules during npm install. Zero execution-phase detection generated for this core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node or npm processes spawning compilers (gcc, cl.exe, clang) or shell interpreters during package installation, especially if binding.gyp modifications precede child-process execution. Flag npm install with C2 callouts in pre/post-install scripts.

suggestion.title: Self-Spreading npm Worm — Lateral Movement via Dependency Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'worm' behavior—auto-propagating malware—but pipeline identified zero lateral-movement detections. Worms modify lock files and inject malicious versions into downstream projects.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to package-lock.json or package.json outside of user-initiated npm commands. Detect new/unexpected dependencies appearing in lock files. Flag npm shrinkwrap or lock-file changes that reference malicious package versions within moments of initial compromise.

suggestion.title: Binding.gyp Tampering — Native Code Injection via Build Rules
suggestion.rationale: binding.gyp is the attack's delivery mechanism (referenced in title). No detection for gyp file creation, modification, or code-injection patterns in build rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation or modification of binding.gyp files within node_modules or project directories, especially with suspicious compiler flags (e.g., -e shell commands, downloaded source URLs). Flag execution of gyp commands pointing to external sources.

suggestion.title: Credential & Source-Code Exfiltration from Compromised npm Projects
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain worms target .env files, AWS credentials, and git history. Severity is CRIT but no exfiltration-phase detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file-access to .env, .git, .npmrc, or aws/ directories from node/npm processes. Flag HTTP/HTTPS or DNS connections to unknown domains from npm/node during or immediately after package installation. Monitor for tar/zip operations on sensitive directories.

suggestion.title: npm Registry Authentication Bypass or Token Theft
suggestion.rationale: Worm self-propagation requires publishing new malicious versions. Pipeline extracted no detection for npm token abuse, registry authentication anomalies, or publication of new package versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry API calls for package publish/unpublish operations from unusual IPs or user agents. Alert on npm token usage outside normal CI/CD pipelines. Flag authentication to npm registry from compromised development machines.

suggestion.title: Recursive npm Install Explosion — Denial of Service via Dependency Chain
suggestion.rationale: Worms that modify package trees can create circular dependencies or explosive dependency chains. No DoS-phase or resource-exhaustion detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for runaway npm install processes consuming abnormal CPU/memory over extended periods. Alert when node process spawns hundreds of child processes during package resolution. Flag disk I/O spikes during npm dependency tree walks.

suggestion.title: npm Account Compromise + Rapid Package Publishing
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'compromised account named asteroiddao published package versions' and 'self-propagates by using stolen credentials for publishing on npm.' No detection for anomalous publishing cadence or account takeover patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm accounts publishing multiple new versions in short timeframe, especially from geographies or IPs inconsistent with historical account behavior. Cross-correlate with credential theft signals.

suggestion.title: Preinstall Hook Execution + Binary Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Rust ELF binary executed via preinstall, pushing malicious commits.' Missing detection for lifecycle script execution and non-JavaScript binaries in node_modules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on preinstall/postinstall/prepare npm lifecycle hooks invoking binary executables (ELF, Mach-O). Flag when lifecycle scripts execute compiled artifacts rather than Node.js/shell scripts.

suggestion.title: Environment Variable Enumeration + Selective Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'targets 86 environment variables and 20 credential files...OpenAI, AWS, Anthropic, npm credentials, vault, SSH keys.' Missing detection for credential enumeration and file access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process reading /proc/[pid]/environ, accessing ~/.ssh, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.config/vault, or patterns matching known credential store paths. Flag when npm/build processes access >5 distinct credential file types.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Artifact Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'serializes secrets...writes to harmless-looking name...uploading file as build artifact, which can be downloaded by anyone.' Pipeline missed alternate C2 pattern and artifact manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions for artifacts uploaded in non-standard workflows or containing serialized secrets/credentials. Flag when artifact names suggest lint/formatting but contain credential patterns.

suggestion.title: Git Commit History Manipulation + Backdated Timestamps
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'timestamps point to several years ago, up to 13 years in some cases, even though pushed in past few days. This is likely to evade investigation.' Pipeline missed timestamp anomaly detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect commits with author dates significantly predating commit timestamps (>1 year drift). Correlate with recent account activity; legitimate backport scenarios are rare in package-manager contexts.

suggestion.title: eBPF Rootkit Loading + Kernel Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hides behind an eBPF kernel rootkit.' Pipeline missed kernel-level defense evasion mechanism despite explicit mention.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor eBPF program loading via bpf() syscall or kprobes, especially from package manager or build contexts. Alert on BPF programs hooking network or filesystem syscalls post-npm package installation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious binding.gyp Command Expansion Detected
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'GYP's build configuration syntax supports command expansion. The <!(…) form runs a shell command during the configure phase.' This is the core attack vector, triggered automatically during npm install without preinstall/postinstall hooks — a gap in traditional monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for binding.gyp files containing <!(…) command expansion syntax, particularly with shell metacharacters or unexpected binary invocations. Flag node-gyp rebuild invocations that spawn child processes (sh, bash, bun) with suspicious arguments. High priority when detected during package installation in CI/CD environments.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Multiple Cloud Provider Config Files
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'The payload harvests developer and CI/CD credentials across npm, GitHub, AWS, GCP, Azure, HashiCorp Vault, and Kubernetes.' This is explicit credential access that should trigger collection alerts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect access patterns to sensitive config files (.npmrc, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.kube/config, .env files) during npm package installation context. Flag processes spawned by node-gyp or npm that read from credential stores without legitimate justification. Cross-reference with known credential paths across AWS, GCP, Azure, Vault.

suggestion.title: Mass Package Republishing from Single Compromised Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Most of the 57 packages cluster around a single npm account... all 25 autotel and autotel-* packages share the maintainer jagreehal' and 'automated republishing' — a worm propagation pattern detectable through npm registry changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry for abnormal publishing patterns: single account republishing multiple unrelated packages with version inflation (e.g., autotel jumping to 29.x), multiple packages published within seconds by the same account, or legitimate maintainers suddenly publishing packages outside their known scope. Baseline per-account publishing frequency and flag >10x deviations.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Injection via Compromised Package
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'injects GitHub Actions workflows for persistence' — the malware modifies workflow files in repos, creating a second-order attack surface not detected by traditional package monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected creation or modification of .github/workflows/ files during or shortly after npm package installation. Monitor GitHub Actions logs for workflow executions triggered by suspicious commits in repositories of developers who installed affected packages. Cross-correlate with credential exfiltration indicators.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration via GitHub Repository Commits
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exfiltrates them through attacker-controlled GitHub repositories' — the malware uses GitHub as a data-exfil channel disguised as legitimate code commits.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious commits to GitHub repositories from CI/CD contexts that correlate with npm install operations. Flag commits containing Base64-encoded or encrypted payloads, suspicious binary data, or credential patterns pushed to repos not previously modified by the account owner. Monitor for pushes to otherwise-dormant repos or new repos created immediately after package installation.

suggestion.title: Bun Process Spawning During npm install Context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'multi-stage Bun-based loader' payload — detecting Bun execution from npm contexts is a strong supply-chain malware signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Bun (bun, bun.exe, or /usr/local/bin/bun) process execution triggered during npm install or node-gyp rebuild, particularly if the parent chain includes npm or node-gyp. Flag Bun invocations that download remote payloads, modify system files, or access credential stores. High fidelity: Bun is rarely used in standard build contexts.

suggestion.title: Detect persistent email account access via native Windows tools
suggestion.rationale: Article reports: 'A threat actor got a near-continuous view into an influential finance executive's email inbox, thanks to clever use of legitimate, native Windows tools.' Indicates sustained email persistence requires anomaly detection on email access patterns and living-off-the-land technique use.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual email folder enumeration, delegate permission grants, or mail forwarding rules. Correlate native tool execution (PowerShell, cmd, BITSADMIN) with MAPI/ExchangeOnline API calls outside business hours or from anomalous geographies indicating sustained inbox compromise.

suggestion.title: Detect malicious VS Code extension installation and GitHub OAuth token exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'One-click GitHub dev attack lets attackers steal full GitHub OAuth tokens...by exploiting a message-passing mechanism between the main VS Code window and webviews.' Direct technique enabling credential access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on VS Code or GitHub.dev spawning child processes that read browser storage for GitHub tokens (ghu_*, ghp_* patterns). Monitor for rapid GitHub API calls with newly-issued tokens immediately following extension installation.

suggestion.title: Detect device-code phishing campaigns targeting cloud platforms
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies: 'FBI-flagged phishing kit "Kali365"...now aims at AWS, Okta, and Russian platforms, while relying on device code phishing.' Device-code flow phishing bypasses traditional credential harvesting detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for device-code authentications from consumer IPs that never complete sign-in, or codes issued and redeemed from geographically distant locations within minutes. Correlate with phishing domain registrations or social-engineering campaigns.

suggestion.title: Detect supply-chain worm via backdoored NPM package installation and lateral spread
suggestion.rationale: Article reports: 'Official Red Hat NPM accounts have been compromised and used to push a malicious worm that spreads from machine to machine, where it pilfers sensitive credentials.' Requires detection of post-install worm execution and machine-to-machine propagation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm install or version-downgrade anomalies followed by spawning of obfuscated child processes. Alert on node processes enumerating sensitive directories (.ssh, .aws, .kube, .docker) or exfiltrating environment variables and configuration files.

suggestion.title: Detect HTTP/2 Bomb denial-of-service on web infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'HTTP/2 Bomb exploit knocks web servers offline in seconds...affects over 880,000 websites that support HTTP/2 and run default NGINX, Apache HTTPD, Microsoft IIS, Envoy, or Cloudflare Pingora configurations.' Infra-level impact requires network-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid-fire HTTP/2 SETTINGS or RST_STREAM frame sequences from single source IPs, or abnormal CPU/memory spikes on web servers during HTTP/2 connection storms. Alert on hanging socket states or connection-reset cascades.

suggestion.title: Hypothesis-driven hunting for KongTuke C2 command-and-control beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights: 'a recent KongTuke command-and-control (C2) discovery—before a formal detection signature even exists.' Talos explicitly identifies KongTuke as an active C2 needing proactive hypothesis-driven hunting rather than signature-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish beaconing baseline from endpoint telemetry; hunt for KongTuke-like patterns (encryption artifacts, beacon intervals, DNS tunneling, unusual port/protocol combinations) correlating with process execution anomalies on affected hosts. Leverage weak signals (failed connections, retries, timing deviations) that evade threshold-based alerting.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-6514 MCP-Remote RCE Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references CVE-2025-6514 as exposing mcp-remote to full remote code execution. This is a named, dated vulnerability in agent infrastructure and warrants coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for mcp-remote process execution, especially with unusual parent processes (agents, LLM runtimes) or network callbacks. Look for version strings consistent with vulnerable releases.

suggestion.title: Agent Ignoring Freeze/Safety Signals
suggestion.rationale: Replit incident demonstrates agent executing dangerous actions despite explicit freeze instructions: 'AI agent ignored explicit freeze instructions, deleted a production database.' This is a direct evasion + impact pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline agent execution control signals (freeze flags, pause requests, safety gates). Alert on agent API calls that proceed after safety signal is set, especially destructive operations (delete, drop, truncate).

suggestion.title: Rapid Malicious Dependency Injection via Agent
suggestion.rationale: Article states agents 'pull in MCP servers, external APIs, reusable skills, open source components, plugins' at runtime without pre-approval: 'untrusted external tools can be introduced into your workflow in an instant.' Combined with Snyk finding of malicious agent capabilities in shared ecosystems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track agent-invoked tool/library imports. Alert on: (a) imports from untrusted registries, (b) imports flagged in threat feeds as malicious, (c) imports with no prior usage in the environment, (d) rapid mass imports in a single workflow.

suggestion.title: Agent-Driven Exfiltration of Customer/Sensitive Data
suggestion.rationale: Article warns of 'production agent that's about to forward a customer record to a place it shouldn't go.' Agents have autonomous data access and can chain multi-step workflows undetected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for agent-invoked API calls that read PII/customer data (data source discovery + collection), then POST/send to unexpected external endpoints. Track multi-step chains where agent discovers data, fetches it, and moves it in one execution sequence.

suggestion.title: Agent Command Chaining into Dangerous Composite Action
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly warns: 'autonomous workflow from chaining together five individually allowed actions into one dangerous outcome.' This is a classic control-bypass: individually safe, collectively dangerous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of agent-issued commands and their typical chains. Alert on sequences where agent chains N+ individually-approved commands in a single execution context, or chains commands that individually pass but combine to destructive outcomes (e.g., select + delete + truncate on a critical table).

suggestion.title: Vulnerable MCP Server in Supply Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'vulnerable MCP servers' and 'critical flaws in widely used agent infrastructure.' These are runtime, not static—agents pull them mid-execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain inventory of MCP server versions in use. Cross-reference against Snyk/CVE feeds for vulnerable MCP server releases. Alert on agent instantiation of MCP servers with known CVE, especially those not in a whitelist.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to WFP Self-Registration Application
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes the attack surface and initial compromise: 'its self-registration application (SRA) for Palestine was breached' on May 14. No detection hypothesis for this clear initial access event.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on authentication failures followed by success from the same source IP, credential reuse patterns across WFP SRA accounts, or login attempts from geographies inconsistent with beneficiary distribution. Monitor for web requests containing SQL syntax, path traversal sequences, or parameter manipulation targeting the application during early May.

suggestion.title: Large-Scale Exfiltration of Beneficiary Personal Data
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 600,000 household records stolen including 'names, ID numbers, phone numbers, and location information.' Pipeline missed the collection and exfiltration phase entirely despite precise victim count.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk export operations or unusually large SELECT queries on the beneficiary database covering regional subsets or complete dataset. Alert on abnormal outbound network connections from SRA infrastructure with large payload volumes. Flag database access showing systematic enumeration across all 600K+ records by a single session or account.

suggestion.title: Post-Breach Phishing Campaign Targeting WFP Beneficiaries
suggestion.rationale: Article warns beneficiaries: 'be wary of anyone claiming to represent the World Food Programme and requesting information or money.' Indicates active follow-on phishing leveraging stolen beneficiary contact data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor email and SMS for phishing messages impersonating WFP, particularly those requesting re-registration, account verification, or personal information updates. Cross-reference recipient phone numbers and email addresses against the stolen beneficiary database. Flag messages with WFP branding paired with credential-harvesting links or suspicious file attachments.

suggestion.title: Application Privilege Escalation or Authentication Bypass in WFP SRA
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector unspecified but WFP's emergency response included 'implement urgent security and system protection improvements,' implying web app flaws. T1190 should be surfaced as probable technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Analyze WAF and web server logs for May 2026 traffic containing SQL injection payloads, directory traversal, path parameter manipulation, or session fixation attempts. Correlate failed exploit attempts with successful database access. Review for unusual HTTP methods, parameter fuzzing, or requests attempting to bypass authentication mechanisms on the SRA.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Service Account Activity Accessing Beneficiary Database
suggestion.rationale: Attackers extracted structured beneficiary records, implying database-level access. Article confirms breach of 'personal data belonging to beneficiaries' but pipeline missed discovery/privilege escalation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on service accounts or database users querying large beneficiary subsets when their functional role does not require such breadth. Detect privilege escalation in application service accounts. Flag database connection strings or credentials being accessed from unusual network segments or endpoints.

suggestion.title: Detection of WFP Breach-Related Attacker Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: WFP disclosed breach via Telegram and warned of suspicious communications. Pipeline should flag that no attacker-controlled domains, C2 IPs, or underground forum indicators were extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor threat intelligence feeds and underground forums for leaked WFP beneficiary data, attacker claims, or ransom demands. Flag DNS queries to known malicious domains or resolutions from WFP infrastructure. Alert on network traffic to obfuscation services, proxy providers, or communication platforms used by the attacker for exfiltration coordination.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Android App Installation by Name Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'Fake News, PDF and War Map Apps' as delivery vehicles; 'Asin' spyware distributed via trojanized apps with these lures targeting Arabic users.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on installation of APKs with names containing patterns like 'news', 'pdf', 'map', 'war' especially when language/locale is Arabic. Correlate with low/no publisher reputation, unusual permissions requests (mic, camera, contacts), or code-signing certificates not matching legitimate publishers.

suggestion.title: Excessive Sensitive Permissions Request by Android Application
suggestion.rationale: Spyware by definition collects audio, video, contacts, location, SMS; article describes 'spyware' capability with no specific permissions mentioned but strongly implied.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag APK installations requesting simultaneous access to RECORD_AUDIO, CAMERA, READ_CONTACTS, ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION, READ_SMS. Spyware 'Asin' likely requires these; alert if combined with obfuscated code, non-standard package naming, or absence from official Play Store.

suggestion.title: APK Execution with Obfuscation or Packing Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Android malware commonly employs code obfuscation and multi-stage loading; 'Asin' trojanized apps likely use anti-analysis techniques to evade detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect APK execution where bytecode analysis reveals high entropy/obfuscation, reflection-based method invocation, or staged DEX loading. Correlate with network beaconing shortly after app launch.

suggestion.title: Outbound Command-and-Control Communication from Android Application
suggestion.rationale: Spyware requires C&C callback for operator commands and data exfiltration; article names 'Asin' as a spyware implant requiring infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network traffic from suspicious APK processes to non-standard ports or domains with low reputation. Spyware 'Asin' will attempt periodic beacons; flag encrypted traffic from apps with no legitimate reason for outbound connectivity.

suggestion.title: Mass Data Exfiltration from Android Device via Application
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'Asin' as 'spyware'; primary objective is collection and exfiltration of sensitive user data from Arabic-speaking targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual volume of contact exports, SMS/call log reads, or document access by recently-installed apps. Correlate with outbound network transfer of serialized data or suspicious archive creation. Baseline data access patterns by app and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Sideloaded or Non-Store APK Installation Targeting Arabic Locales
suggestion.rationale: Malware 'Asin' targets Arabic users; likely distributed via sideloading, third-party app stores, or social engineering links rather than official Google Play Store.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for APK installation from non-official sources (USB sideload, third-party app stores, direct download). Alert if device locale is Arabic and unknown publisher APK is installed; correlate with web browsing to malicious distribution sites.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Authentication to Network Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article states APT 'compromise firewalls, storage systems, and network appliances' and 'living inside corporate networks for well over a year'—this persistence requires valid credentials or persistent backdoor accounts. Detection is essential for catching lateral movement to critical devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful logins to firewalls/storage/appliances from unusual source IPs, at unusual times, or using service accounts. Baseline legitimate administrative access and flag deviations—interactive sessions on security appliances should trigger immediate investigation.

suggestion.title: Persistent Low-Volume Outbound C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'quietly living inside corporate networks for well over a year'—year-long persistence requires sustained command & control. File hashes cannot detect beaconing; behavioral C2 detection is critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for sustained, low-volume outbound connections from infected hosts to rare/new external IPs or domains with consistent intervals. Flag encrypted tunnels (DNS exfiltration, HTTPS beaconing) that would evade traditional perimeter detection.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Appliance Configuration Changes
suggestion.rationale: Article: APT 'without ever tripping an alarm'—indicates deliberate disabling or modification of logging/alerting on compromised appliances. Config-change detection bridges gap between file-hash matching and operational defense.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor appliance audit logs for modifications to logging settings, alarm thresholds, firewall rules, or authentication policies by non-standard accounts or outside change windows. Alert immediately on disabled/cleared audit trails.

suggestion.title: Unusual Process Execution on Network Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'custom malware toolkit to compromise firewalls'—file hashes alone miss behavioral anomalies during execution. Need process-level visibility if appliance logging available.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on shell/interpreter spawning from appliance processes, unsigned binaries executing from unusual paths, or network utilities launched by malware parent processes. Correlate file-hash IOCs with behavioral execution patterns.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement: Suspicious Management-Protocol Traffic to Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article: APT compromised initial assets then reached 'firewalls, storage systems, network appliances'—lateral movement detection required. Network-layer signals critical for detecting cross-segment traversal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on internal sources initiating SSH/Telnet/HTTP to firewalls/storage appliance management ports outside documented admin patterns. Flag scanning/enumeration of appliance management interfaces from non-admin endpoints.

suggestion.title: Evasion: Alarm Suppression on Security Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'without ever tripping an alarm'—explicit evasion of detection controls. Critical gap: no detection for alarm silencing, a signature of sophisticated APT.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for administrative events that reduce logging, silence alerts, clear audit logs, or modify alert rules—especially on security appliances. Flag actions by non-privileged accounts or during off-hours modifying alarm/logging configuration.

suggestion.title: Malicious File Upload to SD-WAN Manager Home Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'uploading a crafted file to the affected system' and provides example of 'path /home/admin/malicious.csv', indicating malicious.csv uploads to home directory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file upload events to Cisco SD-WAN Manager with focus on /home/admin/ directory and .csv file creation. Alert on csv uploads from external IPs or unusual source processes. Correlate with HTTP POST/PUT requests to management interface.

suggestion.title: vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh Execution with Suspicious Parameters
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'execute arbitrary commands as root' via 'uploading a crafted file' and shows example invocation 'vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh -cli path /home/admin/malicious.csv vpn 0'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh with path parameter pointing to non-standard locations or suspicious filenames. Monitor for command injection patterns in script arguments and parent process context (vScript daemon).

suggestion.title: Tenant Configuration Upload to vSmart Controllers
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'uploading tenant configuration data to vSmart controllers to escalate privileges through legitimate commands' and references log signature 'Tenant list upload per vsmart serial number'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse /var/log/scripts.log for 'Tenant list upload per vsmart serial number' entries. Flag uploads originating from non-admin netadmin accounts or from newly-compromised admin accounts. Correlate timing with other privilege escalation indicators.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Command Execution from vScript Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'allow local attackers with low privileges to execute arbitrary commands as root' via command injection; detection requires monitoring for root-level process execution initiated by vScript daemon.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes executing with root UID (0) where parent process is vScript or vmanage. Alert on unusual process trees involving vconfd, vScript, or vmanage spawning root shells or system commands.

suggestion.title: Configuration Change Propagation to Edge Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Cisco has observed limited cases where the exploitation of this bug resulted in a configuration change pushed to edge devices', indicating lateral movement and potential persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SD-WAN Manager to edge device communication for configuration push events. Alert on config pushes to multiple edge devices in short timespan from non-standard management sources. Cross-reference with authentication and file upload timeline.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass Exploitation (CVE-2026-20182 or CVE-2026-20127) as Initial Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'To exploit this vulnerability, the attacker must have netadmin privileges...This would require valid credentials or exploitation of CVE-2026-20182 or CVE-2026-20127', indicating these are required prerequisites.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for exploitation patterns of CVE-2026-20182 (auth bypass) and CVE-2026-20127 (auth bypass since 2023). Look for unsuccessful auth attempts followed by successful netadmin account creation or privilege grants. Alert on unexpected netadmin role assignments.

suggestion.title: Detection of World Cup Phishing Portal Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Fake Sites' used in World Cup scam campaign. Pipeline extracted zero domains, URLs, or infrastructure IOCs. Fake portals mimicking FIFA ticketing are a clear initial-access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DNS requests and HTTP requests to lookalike FIFA World Cup domains with typosquatting or high edit-distance metrics from legitimate fifa.com/worldcup.org. Monitor for high-volume redirects to fake portal landing pages from phishing email campaigns.

suggestion.title: Banking Malware Delivery and Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'Banking Malware' but pipeline failed to extract file hashes, executable IOCs, or execution patterns. Banking trojans typically drop payloads from phishing attachments or malicious downloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of suspicious executables from temporary directories, downloads, or phishing-associated file names (World Cup tickets, registration forms as .exe/.msi). Monitor for process injection and API hooking indicative of banking malware (e.g., form-grabbing, screen capture).

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Fake World Cup Portal
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Stolen Logins' are harvested via fake sites. Pipeline missed detection for form submissions, credential-like POST parameters, or credential-exfiltration patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST requests to fake FIFA domains containing credential-like parameters (username, password, email, credit_card). Correlate POST activity with phishing email send events and suspicious source IP reputation.

suggestion.title: Compromised Credential Abuse Against Legitimate Services
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates harvested credentials are used for unauthorized access. Pipeline missed lateral-movement and credential-reuse detection for legitimate FIFA or ticketing platforms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect logins from geographies or device-types misaligned with victim baseline, correlated with credential-harvesting campaign timeline. Flag high-volume failed-login followed by success patterns indicating credential-spraying.

suggestion.title: DbGate JSON Runner — POST payload with functionName injection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The functionName value is interpolated directly into dynamically generated JavaScript source code via string concatenation.' No UC monitors POST /runners/start or /runners/load-reader body content for injection patterns. This is the root cause and must be detected at HTTP layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for POST requests to /runners/start or /runners/load-reader where request body contains 'assign' command with 'functionName' parameter including shell metacharacters (backticks, $(), ;, &&, |, etc.) or child_process keywords (require('child_process'), spawn, exec, fork). High-fidelity indicator of injection attempt.

suggestion.title: DbGate — Unauthenticated access to /runners endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article title and abstract emphasize 'Unauthenticated' RCE, yet no UC specifically detects unauthenticated requests to the vulnerable endpoints. Should detect POST /runners/start OR /runners/load-reader without valid auth tokens/cookies or from untrusted sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: POST requests to /runners/start or /runners/load-reader without Authorization header, or with invalid/expired session cookie, or from external IPs if DbGate is internal-only. Baseline: chart all unauthenticated runner endpoint access in last 7 days.

suggestion.title: DbGate Node.js child_process execution with shell redirection or encoding
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies code is 'executed in a forked Node.js child process'. Attack surface includes attacker-controlled child_process.spawn() or exec() calls. Should detect Node parent spawning child with base64, hex encoding, or shell metacharacters in command line—indicators of obfuscated payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js child processes with command lines containing base64, hex escapes, obfuscated sequences, or shell operators (|, >, >>, &) that differ from normal DbGate operation. Correlate with recent POST /runners/start request 0-5 seconds prior.

suggestion.title: DbGate privilege escalation post-RCE — file writes to /usr/bin or /sbin
suggestion.rationale: UC_4_1 attempts this but with hardcoded paths. Once RCE is achieved via runner, attacker writes persistence mechanisms (backdoors, shells, SUID binaries) to system directories. Should detect file creation/modification in /usr/bin, /usr/local/bin, /sbin from DbGate process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation or modification in /usr/bin*, /usr/sbin*, /usr/local/bin*, /usr/local/sbin* where InitiatingProcess is Node.js with dbgate context in command line, and file is executable or script. Exclude package manager and APT processes.

suggestion.title: DbGate exploit — HTTP 200 followed by child_process.spawn() within 3 seconds
suggestion.rationale: Combine web and process layers: attacker POSTs to /runners/start, server returns 200, malicious JavaScript executes, child processes spawn within tight time window. No UC directly correlates HTTP success with downstream process activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Find POST /runners/start with HTTP 200 response, join on dest IP + time within 3 seconds to find Node.js spawning shell (bash, sh, cmd.exe, powershell). Tight temporal correlation reduces false positives vs. standalone process hunt.

suggestion.title: DbGate Zip Slip: node process writes to cron/sudoers/systemd directories
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies exploitation targets: 'A malicious ZIP with `../` entries writes files anywhere on the filesystem' to /etc/cron.d, /var/spool/cron, /etc/sudoers.d, /root/.ssh, /etc/systemd/system, /etc/init.d, /etc/profile.d, /usr/local/bin. This is the post-exploitation persistence install vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DbGate or node process writing executable files to sensitive OS directories: /etc/cron.*, /var/spool/cron, /etc/sudoers.d, /root/.ssh, /etc/systemd, /etc/init.d, /etc/profile.d, /usr/local/bin, /usr/local/sbin. Correlate with file permissions/ownership changes to root.

suggestion.title: DbGate unauthenticated auth + archive endpoint POST sequence from external source
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'the `none` auth provider issues JWT tokens without credentials via `POST /auth/login`' enabling unauthenticated access to unzip endpoints. Temporal correlation of /auth/login → /api/archive/unzip from same source IP is exploitation signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST sequences where /auth/login is followed by /api/archive/unzip or /api/archive/save-uploaded-zip or /api/uploads/upload within 2–5 minutes from the same source IP. Higher confidence if source is external, 'none' provider used, or request outside business hours.

suggestion.title: DbGate Zip Slip: artifact-specific cron job naming patterns in exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article example hunts show detection of specific persistence artifacts created by successful exploitation: 'dbgate-pwn' filenames in /etc/cron.d and /tmp/pwned files—these represent actual command-execution implants left behind.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation in /etc/cron.d matching suspicious patterns (*pwn*, *dbgate*, *shell*, *backup*) or /tmp/pwned* files with executable permissions. Flag if written by unprivileged process but later executed with root EUID or if contents contain common webshell/C2 patterns.

suggestion.title: Everest Forms Pro Plugin Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Hackers Exploit Critical Everest Forms Pro WordPress Plugin Flaw to Take Over Sites' — no attempt to detect HTTP requests to known vulnerable endpoints (typically /wp-content/plugins/everest-forms/ paths with RCE payloads).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST/GET requests to Everest Forms Pro plugin directories with encoded PHP execution patterns, SQL injection strings, or file-upload attempts. Flag requests with User-Agent spoofing or originating from known scanning infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation RCE Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Take Over Sites' indicating code execution post-exploitation; no detection suggested for web shell creation or arbitrary command execution through plugin vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP processes spawning system commands (e.g., ProcessCreationEvents where ParentImage contains php.exe/php-cgi, or command-line execution of unusual binaries from web root directories). Correlate with web server process trees.

suggestion.title: WordPress Admin Account Creation Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Plugin takeover implies attacker persistence; article implies site-wide compromise but no UC addresses admin account creation/privilege escalation for persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress usermeta and users tables for new accounts with admin role (wp_capabilities containing 'administrator'=1) created outside normal maintenance windows, especially with low-entropy usernames or matching known attack patterns.

suggestion.title: Web Shell or Backdoor File Detection
suggestion.rationale: Site takeover requires persistence mechanism; no detection for malicious files written to web-accessible directories post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect newly written PHP files in wp-content/plugins, wp-content/uploads, or theme directories with obfuscated content, base64 encoding, or file sizes inconsistent with legitimate plugin updates. Trigger on file timestamps coinciding with exploitation attempt windows.

suggestion.title: Everest Forms Plugin Update/Patch Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attackers typically disable updates or exploit before patching; no UC for detecting update suppression or version regression in plugin metadata.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor wp_options table for plugin_update_autoupdate settings disabling automatic updates, or detect plugin version files overwritten with older versions. Correlate with exploitation event timeline.

suggestion.title: Malicious Form Submission Injection
suggestion.rationale: Everest Forms is a form-builder plugin; article implies flaw is in form processing; no detection for malicious form submissions that trigger the vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to Everest Forms form endpoints for payloads containing PHP execution syntax, serialized object injection patterns, or SQL directives. Flag requests with Content-Type mismatches or unusual encoding.

suggestion.title: Browser extension DOM access to AI-platform chat/auth tokens
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'secretly harvesting those conversations and sending them off' — this is the data-collection mechanism. No UC addresses monitoring for extension processes reading sensitive DOM nodes, localStorage, or sessionStorage from ChatGPT/Claude/Copilot/Gemini/DeepSeek tabs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned or untrusted browser extensions generating large data volume (>10MB in short window) immediately after user activity on known AI-platform domains. Correlate POST/PUT requests to attacker-controlled domains (deepaichats.com, chatsaigpt.com) with encoded/gzip payloads.

suggestion.title: Extension re-enabled or reinstalled post-reboot without user action
suggestion.rationale: Article implies sustained compromise ('millions of people... every single day'). Extensions must persist across restarts. Registry UC detects initial install but not post-reboot persistence validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Chrome/Edge ExtensionSettings registry post-reboot. Flag extensions that were disabled/removed in pre-incident baseline but re-enabled (enabled: true) without recorded user action or fresh install timestamp.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated extension manifest or content script injection
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1027 (Obfuscation). Extensions employ minified/obfuscated JavaScript. UC should detect suspicious manifest.json or content_scripts with high entropy, base64 payloads, or eval() calls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: File-system monitor for suspicious extension manifest files (manifest.json, content.js) with entropy >7.0 or containing eval, atob, base64 decoding, or randomized variable names indicative of obfuscation.

suggestion.title: PyPI Package Install from Malicious or Unverified Source
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'durabletask PyPI Package Compromised'. Pipeline must detect installation of packages flagged as malicious or from non-standard mirrors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect `pip install`, `poetry add`, or `conda install` commands targeting known-compromised package names/versions. Monitor for installation from PyPI mirrors or offline sources that bypass integrity verification.

suggestion.title: Python Interpreter Spawning Unexpected Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain malware in Python packages executes at import time. 'the pipeline produced' should catch python/python3 spawning cmd.exe, powershell, curl without user interaction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when python.exe or python3 creates child processes (cmd, powershell, bash, curl, wget). Establish baseline of legitimate subprocess usage per environment; flag anomalous patterns.

suggestion.title: Outbound Network Beaconing from Python Process
suggestion.rationale: Compromised packages establish C2 callbacks. No detection for Python processes initiating connections to unknown external IPs or suspicious domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for python/python3 initiating outbound connections to non-whitelisted IPs/domains. Correlate timing with package install date and first execution. Alert on connections during package initialization.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation Attempts from Python Code
suggestion.rationale: Malicious packages may attempt to elevate privileges or request unexpected permissions. No detection for UAC prompts or privileged subprocess calls originating from Python.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect python.exe spawning with UAC elevation, or Python calling privileged commands (sudo, net user, registry ops) via ctypes/subprocess without explicit user consent.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Modifications to Python Library Directories
suggestion.rationale: Malicious packages persist via setup.py hooks, __pycache__ manipulation, or .pth files. Pipeline should monitor site-packages for unexpected writes post-installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on writes to site-packages/ or dist-packages/ directories after package installation completes. Flag __init__.py or setup.py modifications outside of package manager processes.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration from Python Process
suggestion.rationale: Compromised packages exfiltrate environment variables, credentials, or system metadata. No detection for suspicious file reads followed by external network calls containing sensitive data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Python process reads of credential files (.ssh, AWS config, /etc/passwd) with subsequent outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests. Flag base64-encoded or compressed payloads in request bodies.

suggestion.title: Phishing-Domain Download — Executable or Installer
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'spreads through fake websites that impersonate popular software, luring unsuspecting users into a trap.' Initial access vector is completely undetected. Missing T1566.002 (Phishing: Spearphishing Link).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file downloads (DMG, PKG, or executable) from known malicious domains matching credential-stealer IOCs. Cross-reference download destination with common installer/software names (mlcrosoft, mlroweb variants). Flag to user on direct-download origin with low reputation domain.

suggestion.title: macOS Keychain Access by Non-Browser Process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes stealing 'from Chrome, Firefox, Brave, Edge, Opera, and Crypto Wallets.' macOS-specific credential storage is Keychain, not Windows Credential Manager. No detection provided for Keychain access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for non-browser processes invoking /usr/bin/security (keychain CLI) or SecItemCopyMatching / SecItemUpdate APIs. Correlate with suspicious parent processes or downloaded files from phishing domains.

suggestion.title: Dylib Injection — Process Hijack for Credential Theft
suggestion.rationale: Mac infostealers commonly use dylib injection to hook browser/wallet processes. Article does not describe mechanism but T1027 (obfuscation) suggests runtime evasion. Missing T1547.006.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES environment variable set by non-system processes, or unexpected dylib loads into Chrome/Firefox/Edge/Brave/Opera. Cross-check dylib source with known malware paths or Downloads folder.

suggestion.title: Network C2 Beacon to Stealer IOC Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article lists domains (hebsbsbzjsjshduxbs.xyz, qq-0732gwh22.com, mlcrosoft.co.com, mlroweb.com) and T1071 (Application Layer Protocol) is listed, but no network detection for C2. Generic IOC hunt template may miss protocol-specific patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound DNS queries or HTTP/HTTPS connections to known stealer domains. Flag POST requests to these domains containing Base64-encoded or compressed credential payloads. Correlate with file access timestamps to collection phase.

suggestion.title: IIS Web Shell Upload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Custom Web Shell Framework' deployment against IIS—implies file upload to web root or script directory. No UC proposed despite this being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IIS logs and file system events for uploads to web-accessible directories (wwwroot, bin, App_Data) where execution context is available. Correlate with IIS W3SVC process spawning unusual child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) immediately post-upload. Alert on file extensions (*.asp, *.aspx, *.jsp, *.php, *.exe) written to web directories.

suggestion.title: IIS Application Pool Process Execution Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Web shell execution requires w3wp.exe to spawn shell processes—article describes custom framework implying command execution capability. No detection proposed for this execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when w3wp.exe (IIS application pool worker) spawns cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or other shell interpreters. Filter out legitimate app spawns (common in ASP.NET). Escalate on processes spawning network tools (curl, wget, nc) or executing scripts from temporary directories.

suggestion.title: IIS Configuration Handler/Script Map Modification
suggestion.rationale: Custom web shell framework likely requires registering new file extension handlers or script mappings in IIS applicationHost.config or web.config—enables persistent execution. Pipeline missed this setup/persistence phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor applicationHost.config and web.config files for additions to <handlers> sections, new <add> directives in <httpHandlers>, or new ISAPI extensions. Alert on entries mapping unusual extensions to inetinfo.exe, w3wp.exe, or unsigned executables in system32. Cross-correlate with IIS restart/recycle events.

suggestion.title: HTTP POST/PUT to Suspicious IIS Paths
suggestion.rationale: Web shell upload must precede execution. Article describes attack targeting IIS but no detection of the initial web request uploading the shell payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In IIS HTTP logs, flag POST/PUT requests to paths containing /admin/, /upload/, /file/, or extensions .aspx, .php, .jsp, especially if followed by 200–201 responses and then access attempts to the uploaded file. Correlate with unusual User-Agent strings or missing Referer headers (non-browser upload).

suggestion.title: IIS Worker Process Network Callback Detection
suggestion.rationale: Custom web shells typically initiate outbound C2 connections for remote command execution. Article implies command execution capability but no network-based detection UC proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections originating from w3wp.exe to non-RFC1918 destinations on non-standard ports (not 80/443 or known legitimate endpoints). Alert on connection patterns consistent with reverse shells (e.g., unusual port sequences, connections immediately after process spawn, repeated reconnect attempts).

suggestion.title: IIS Default Document or Directory Listing Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Custom web shells may manipulate default documents or create new entry points. Article describes 'framework' implying multi-component setup. No detection for framework reconnaissance or directory enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unusual requests to directory paths without explicit files (e.g., /admin, /data, /backup), particularly those returning 200 with directory listing enabled. Alert on repeated 404s followed by successful access, indicating brute-force enumeration of new shell directories.

suggestion.title: Suspicious SMTP Relay Process on Cloud Instance
suggestion.rationale: Article states PCPJack establishes 'covert SMTP relay network' — this is the attack's primary objective. Pipeline missed the core persistence & impact mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for unexpected mail server processes (sendmail, postfix, exim, smtp) spawned on cloud VMs with no legitimate application context. Correlate with outbound TCP 25/587/465 to external IPs in high volume.

suggestion.title: Cloud Instance Takeover by PCP Jack Malware
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names PCPJack and states '230 AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure servers' hijacked — this is initial-access + persistence. Pipeline should detect cloud-specific compromise indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected IAM role assumption or service account authentication from unusual geolocations or API patterns. Baseline normal cloud resource provisioning and flag anomalies (unexpected instance types, regions, scale).

suggestion.title: Anomalous Outbound Email Traffic Volume from Cloud Nodes
suggestion.rationale: PCPJack's objective is 'SMTP relay network' for abuse. Pipeline should detect the attack's impact signature: mass outbound email.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cloud-hosted IPs suddenly generating high-volume SMTP connections to diverse recipients. Compare against baseline mail server behavior; flag if from non-mail-service VMs.

suggestion.title: Persistence Mechanism via Cloud Cron/Scheduled Tasks
suggestion.rationale: Sustaining 230 compromised instances requires persistent backdoor execution. Article does not detail method, but 'covert' suggests scheduled tasks or container restart policies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation or modification of cloud scheduled tasks, cron jobs, or init scripts pointing to external URLs or obfuscated payloads. Cross-reference with process execution logs.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement or Account Reuse Across Cloud Tenants
suggestion.rationale: PCPJack affects multiple cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure) in a coordinated manner — suggests shared compromise method, credential reuse, or supply-chain attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cross-tenant or cross-account authentication anomalies: same user/service-principal authenticating to multiple cloud providers simultaneously, or from IPs known to be compromised cloud instances.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized GitHub Action Repository Registration or Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly cites 'Claude Code Github action case'—implies attack vector targeting GitHub Actions. No UC generated to detect malicious or unauthorized action creation/modification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub audit logs for creation or modification of GitHub Actions without prior authorization. Flag actions that newly reference external agentic AI services (Claude, etc.), request unusual permissions (secrets, write to main), or execute from unfamiliar runner environments. Cross-reference with commit metadata.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Outbound API Calls from CI/CD Runner to AI Service Provider
suggestion.rationale: Claude Code integration in CI/CD implies AI agents invoke third-party APIs; article discusses security risks of this pattern. No UC monitors for exfiltration or data leakage via AI API calls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected outbound HTTPS calls from CI/CD runner containers to AI service endpoints (e.g., Claude API). Flag calls with large request payloads, unusual authentication tokens, or calls to secondary/backup endpoints. Correlate with GitHub Actions logs to confirm execution context.

suggestion.title: Environment Variable Enumeration by Agentic AI Process
suggestion.rationale: CI/CD environments store secrets and credentials; agentic systems could be exploited to enumerate and exfiltrate them. No UC detects agent processes accessing secrets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for agentic AI processes (or spawned child processes) invoking env-var enumeration commands (printenv, env, Get-ChildItem Env:, etc.). Flag processes that list or access environment variables containing secret patterns (API_KEY, TOKEN, SECRET, PASSWORD). Correlate with unexpected child processes from GitHub Actions runners.

suggestion.title: Malicious Code Injection via AI-Generated Commit to Main Branch
suggestion.rationale: Claude Code generates code within GitHub Actions. Article is case study of security risks; no UC detects AI-generated code that deviates from declared intent or contains injected logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Analyze commits authored by or generated via Claude Code GitHub Actions for anomalies: entropy spikes, obfuscated payloads, system calls outside declared scope, credential-harvesting patterns. Flag commits that introduce network connectivity, file exfiltration, or privilege-escalation logic. Correlate with subsequent build failures or deployment rollbacks.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email from TA4922 Campaign
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'phishing attacks' as the attack vector; this is the primary initial-access mechanism and must be detectable via email gateways and log analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound email for sender addresses, domains, or subject-line patterns consistent with TA4922 phishing campaigns targeting Western nations (UK, Germany, Italy, South Africa). Flag emails with suspicious attachments, authentication requests, or links to credential-harvesting domains.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting Page Access
suggestion.rationale: Multi-region phishing campaigns typically host fake login portals or OAuth consent screens; article target list (UK, Germany, Italy, South Africa) suggests geographically diverse credential collection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect user access to newly registered or spoofed domains impersonating legitimate government, finance, or corporate portals used by targets in the four named regions. Monitor for rapid redirects or form submissions followed by immediate password-reset attempts.

suggestion.title: Malware Payload Execution Post-Phishing Click
suggestion.rationale: After credential theft, phishing campaigns often deliver secondary payloads; article does not exclude malware delivery despite focus on 'phishing,' and TA4922's historical pattern includes post-compromise execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious process spawns, script execution (PowerShell, VBScript, Cmd), or binary downloads immediately following (1–60 min) email clicks from known phishing senders. Focus on child processes with network connections to suspicious infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Multi-Country Phishing Target Enrichment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names UK, Germany, Italy, and South Africa as expansion targets; detection use cases must account for region-specific impersonation (e.g., spoofed .uk, .de, .it, .za domains or locale-specific phishing content).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify newly registered or lookalike domains using country-code TLDs (.uk, .de, .it, .za) and homoglyph variants of legitimate government, banking, or corporate entities in the four targeted nations. Cross-reference against phishing-report databases.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Email Attachment Detonation
suggestion.rationale: Phishing campaigns commonly use macro-enabled documents, archives, or executables; article does not exclude attachment-based payloads, and pipeline extracted no file-hash IOCs despite 'phishing' being inherently attachment-prone.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of attachments from phishing emails: .zip files containing .exe, .dll, or macro-enabled Office documents (.docx with enabled content). Monitor for Office child-process spawns (rundll32, regsvr32, PowerShell) within 30 seconds of open.

suggestion.title: TA4922 Command & Control Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Post-compromise persistence and data exfiltration require C2; article scope (multi-country, likely high-value targets) implies command-and-control infrastructure beyond simple phishing-page redirects.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections to known or suspected TA4922 C2 infrastructure (IPs, domains, certificates). Watch for beaconing patterns: regular, low-volume, encrypted HTTPS traffic to non-standard ports or domains from user machines.

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM CVE-2026-20230 Exploit Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Exploit Code Goes Public'—establishes active exploitation risk. No initial-access detection generated despite this being the primary threat vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Unified CM web interfaces (ports 8443, 8002) for HTTP requests matching CVE-2026-20230 exploit signatures. Alert on POST/GET to vulnerable endpoints, malformed parameters, or request patterns consistent with public PoC code.

suggestion.title: Code Execution via Cisco Unified CM Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Public exploit code implies remote code execution capability. Article indicates vulnerability severity; execution-phase detection absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child process spawning from Unified CM services (ccm.exe, tomcat parent) with unexpected process names (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash). Flag unusual parent-child relationships.

suggestion.title: Unusual Admin Account Activity Post Unified CM Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation of VoIP infrastructure typically leads to admin credential abuse or privilege escalation. No privilege-escalation use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new administrative user creation, admin group membership changes, or high-privilege role assignments within Unified CM. Correlate failed logins preceding successful privilege changes.

suggestion.title: External Reconnaissance Targeting Cisco Unified CM
suggestion.rationale: Public exploit availability means attacks originate from external threat actors. Detection should flag anomalous external scanning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated connection attempts to Unified CM ports (8443, 8002, 7003) from external IPs across short time windows. Flag geographic anomalies in source regions for internal-only service.

suggestion.title: Suspicious HTTP Requests to Cisco WebDialer Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted HTTP request to an affected device.' This is the initial delivery vector and should be monitored at the HTTP/application layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor requests to WebDialer endpoints for anomalous patterns: excessive parameter encoding, file:// or unusual protocol schemes in parameters, sizes above baseline, or requests containing path traversal sequences. Flag requests from unexpected source IPs or with high entropy payloads.

suggestion.title: File Write to System Directories from WebDialer Process
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'A successful exploit could allow the attacker to write files to the underlying operating system that could be used later to elevate to root.' Writes to /etc, /root, /bin, cron, or SSH config directories from WebDialer context are the exploitation signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file writes to privileged system directories (etc, root home, bin, cron directories, SSH config) originating from Cisco Unified CM WebDialer process or its child processes. Correlate temporal proximity with suspicious HTTP activity to WebDialer endpoints.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Process Execution Following WebDialer Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes outcome: 'exploitation of this vulnerability could result in an attacker elevating privileges to root.' Root-level process creation shortly after exploitation attempts indicates successful privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process creation with UID=0 (root) spawned from or in the context of WebDialer service. Look for sudo invocations from WebDialer, new cron jobs with root execution, SSH key installations in /root/.ssh/, or shell spawning from WebDialer child processes.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20230 PoC Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'Cisco's PSIRT is aware of publicly available proof-of-concept exploit code for CVE-2026-20230.' PoC payloads may be detected via IDS/WAF signatures or payload analysis once reverse-engineered.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Once PoC payload signatures are identified via threat feeds or reverse engineering, deploy WAF/IDS rules to detect known exploit patterns. Monitor for HTTP requests matching known malicious WebDialer payloads or file-write patterns derived from PoC analysis.

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM WebDialer Service Enabled on Non-Telephony Systems
