suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Hijacks 230 AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure Servers' — coordinated compromise across three cloud providers indicates mass exploitation pattern that pipeline failed to reconstruct.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect clusters of instance creation/modification API calls using single principal across regions in 24-hour window. Flag authentication from impossible travel paths. Correlate with known vulnerability disclosures affecting cloud control plane.

suggestion.title: Detect Outbound Bulk SMTP Traffic from Cloud Compute Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article: servers dedicated to 'SMTP Relay' for covert operations — network egress of bulk email to external destinations is the core attack objective, completely undetected by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on compute instances opening SMTP connections (25/465/587) to 50+ unique external IPs/domains in single hour. Baseline legitimate mail server behavior and trigger on volume anomalies. Correlation with known spam/phishing infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Detect Cloud Infrastructure Enumeration Pre-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: attackers successfully compromised 230 instances — implies prior reconnaissance via DescribeInstances, ListBuckets, or similar discovery APIs. Pipeline produced no credential_access or discovery detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-volume API calls to list/describe resources (instances, buckets, networks) by single principal in short window before compromise. Alert on enumeration from unexpected geolocations. Flag service account token abuse.

suggestion.title: Detect Cross-Cloud Credential or Vulnerability Reuse
suggestion.rationale: Article: PCPJack targeted 'AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure' — same malware across three providers indicates shared root cause (leaked credential or zero-day affecting all three). Pipeline ignored multi-cloud correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate authentication success/failure patterns across AWS/Azure/GCP using identical username or API key within hours. Alert on cross-provider lateral movement. Investigate for leaked credentials in dark web or breach databases.

suggestion.title: Claude Code GitHub Action - Suspicious Tool Use Permissions
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'Claude Code Github action case' with HIGH severity — strongly implies a vulnerability related to overprivileged or misused GitHub Action integration. Should detect when Claude Code or AI agents request elevated permissions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions workflows for Claude Code/agentic AI integrations requesting secrets, repository write access, or webhook configuration. Flag workflows where AI tool permissions exceed the stated code-review or analysis scope.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Code Commit via Agentic GitHub Action
suggestion.rationale: CI/CD pipeline abuse is the likely attack surface for a GitHub Action vulnerability — article references agentic AI in CI/CD context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when GitHub Actions spawned by Claude Code or similar agents commit code without human review approval, or when commits reference AI-generated changes to critical files (IAM, secrets, automation scripts).

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration via GitHub Action Logs
suggestion.rationale: Agentic AI tools executing in CI/CD may leak secrets to action logs if improperly constrained — common attack in GitHub Action supply-chain scenarios.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag GitHub Actions that print API keys, tokens, or credential material to stdout/stderr. Correlate with unexpected access to secret management services (GitHub Secrets, AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault) initiated by non-human identities.

suggestion.title: Malicious GitHub Action Substitution in Workflow
suggestion.rationale: Agentic systems may be tricked into recommending or injecting malicious actions — supply-chain risk inherent in AI-driven CI/CD.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for workflow.yml/workflow.yaml modifications where action references change to typosquatting (e.g., actions/setup-node → actios/setup-node) or new third-party actions suddenly used. Correlate with Claude Code execution history.

suggestion.title: Spearphishing Link Click & Domain Reputation - Multi-Region Campaign
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Phishing Attacks to U.K., Germany, Italy, and South Africa'. Phishing attacks require URL/domain IOCs and click-based detection. Zero use cases generated for email link analysis, domain reputation, or lookalike domain detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag email links to newly registered domains mimicking financial/HR services. Monitor URL clicks from users in UK, Germany, Italy, South Africa targeting suspicious TLDs. Correlate with sender reputation anomalies and historical phishing sender databases.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email Header Spoofing - SPF/DKIM/DMARC Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Phishing campaigns impersonate trusted senders. Article describes attacks on four regions; no email authentication or sender-spoofing detection use case generated despite being standard phishing TTP.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails from external senders with failed SPF/DKIM/DMARC checks claiming internal origin. Flag From/Reply-To impersonations of known organizations. Correlate region-specific recipient targeting with spoofed authority figures.

suggestion.title: Malicious Attachment Sandbox Detonation & Office Macro Execution
suggestion.rationale: TA4922 phishing campaigns typically include payloads. No detonation or process-execution use case generated for attachment-based attacks (T1566.001).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detonate email attachments (Office docs, ZIP, EXE) from phishing senders. Flag Office process spawning cmd/powershell (T1059.005 macro execution). Alert on process trees: winword.exe → cmd.exe → network connections.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting Landing Page Detection & Form Submission Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Phishing campaigns target credential capture via fake login forms. No use case for detecting credential-harvest landing pages or POST requests to credential-collection endpoints despite this being core TA4922 TTP.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to suspicious lookalike domains (e.g., [bank/sso-provider]-verify-update[.]tk). Flag user clicks on phishing links followed by HTTP POST with credential-like data. Correlate with subsequent authentication anomalies.

suggestion.title: Geographic Targeting Correlation - Phishing Surge Across Four Regions
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names four target regions: UK, Germany, Italy, South Africa. No multi-region correlation or targeting-pattern use case generated despite geographic expansion being the article's primary claim.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate phishing email volume, click events, and sender addresses across UK/Germany/Italy/South Africa recipients within 24-hour windows. Alert on simultaneous surge across multiple regions. Flag emails with region-specific language/content customization.

suggestion.title: TA4922 Actor Attribution & Historical Campaign Pattern Matching
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names threat actor: 'China-Linked TA4922'. No actor-specific use case or historical-pattern detection generated. Pipeline should map known TA4922 infrastructure, tooling, or sender patterns from threat feeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor emails from previously attributed TA4922 infrastructure (domains, IPs, sender patterns) against known threat intel feeds. Flag phishing emails with linguistic/technical signatures consistent with prior TA4922 campaigns. Correlate with geopolitical targeting patterns.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20230 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Exploit Code Goes Public' — pipeline must detect inbound attack patterns against Unified CM. Article title alone establishes CVE-2026-20230 as exploitable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Unified CM endpoints for HTTP/HTTPS requests with exploit payloads or known CVE-2026-20230 signature bytes. Correlate with vulnerable Unified CM version identification. Alert on any inbound connection attempt to Unified CM from untrusted networks using exploit-associated URI patterns or malformed protocol handshakes.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Cisco Unified CM Version Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CVE article implies specific version ranges are affected. Without version intel extracted, asset inventory gaps leave endpoints unmonitored. Article should have included affected version list.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Cisco Unified CM instances in scope and correlate against affected version list (expected in full article). Flag any system running a vulnerable version for priority patching and enhanced monitoring. Cross-reference with egress traffic for signs of lateral movement or C2 callback.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Command Execution on Unified CM
suggestion.rationale: Public exploit disclosure typically leads to RCE or privilege escalation post-exploitation. Article body truncated but CVE severity implies code execution capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Unified CM for abnormal process spawning, shell invocations, or script execution originating from web service processes. Alert on non-standard command-line arguments, reverse shells, or outbound DNS/HTTP from system daemons post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: GitHub Action Execution Triggered by Untrusted Issue Metadata
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes attack via 'one malicious issue' triggering the action—detection should cover workflows executing on issue events with content-based payload injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for GitHub Actions workflows triggered by issue_opened or issue_comment events where the workflow accepts or parses issue body/title as input to shell commands or script execution without sanitization. Correlate with subsequent git push or credential access.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration from GitHub Actions Environment
suggestion.rationale: Repository hijacking implies credential theft—malicious action likely exfils GITHUB_TOKEN or other secrets exposed in action context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthorized read of GitHub Actions environment variables, GITHUB_TOKEN usage outside the repo's declared workflows, or credentials posted to external URLs from within action job logs.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Repository Permissions Escalation via Actions
suggestion.rationale: Hijacking requires elevated permissions—detection should flag admin-level git operations (push to protected branches, modify branch protection, change repo settings) initiated from workflow context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect git pushes to protected branches, disable of branch protection rules, or repository setting changes (visibility, default branch, permissions) executed via GitHub Actions token, especially from recently-added or untrusted workflow files.

suggestion.title: Malicious Workflow File Injection via Issue-Triggered Action
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'one malicious issue' hijacking repo—attacker likely uses the flaw to inject or modify .github/workflows files, establishing persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .github/workflows/*.yml additions or modifications where the commit is authored by the GitHub Actions bot, or where the push originates from a non-standard branch or occurs immediately after a malicious issue comment.

suggestion.title: GitHub Action Execution with Excessive or Unexpected Permissions
suggestion.rationale: Hijacking requires broad access—alert on workflows requesting admin, contents, or repo permissions that exceed the declared action's documented scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse .github/workflows files for permissions declarations (contents: write, admin: true) or explicit secret usage without corresponding declared inputs. Correlate with issue-triggered invocation patterns.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Compromise via GitHub Action Registry Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: If the flaw exploits a popular Claude Code action version, attackers may poison the published action ref to propagate hijacking across downstream repos.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track references to Claude Code GitHub Action and alert on version pinning changes, unexpected tag updates, or repos suddenly switching to different action refs or sources. Correlate with CVE disclosures.

suggestion.title: Malicious GTM Container Payload Execution on Checkout Page
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'malicious code is embedded in legitimate-looking GTM containers, which activate when a shopper reaches a checkout page' — requires web app monitoring for GTM payload inspection and execution context analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GTM container loads from non-standard sources or containers with unusual metadata fields. Flag when GTM payloads invoke Function() or eval-like constructors to dynamically execute code. Correlate GTM execution with subsequent payment form activity.

suggestion.title: Bulk Stripe Customer Record Creation with Metadata Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Every stolen payment card becomes a fake customer record in the attacker's Stripe account, turning Stripe into a storage backend for stolen data' — create threshold alert for rapid Stripe customer creation from single account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sudden spike in Stripe customer.create() API calls from authenticated session. Flag customer records with base64/hex-encoded or XOR-obfuscated metadata fields. Correlate API calls to web checkout traffic timestamps.

suggestion.title: Credit Card Pattern Detection in Browser localStorage with XOR Obfuscation
suggestion.rationale: Article states stolen data is 'concatenated into a single string, obfuscated using the XOR operation, and stored locally' — requires memory/storage inspection for CC patterns even when obfuscated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor localStorage writes containing 16-19 byte sequences (typical CC length). Inspect byte patterns for XOR marker sequences. Flag any checkout pages that write data to localStorage with obfuscation headers matching known skimmer families (e.g., repeated 0x00 padding or known XOR keys).

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Firestore Access from E-Commerce Checkout Context
suggestion.rationale: Article variant uses 'Google Firestore, a cloud database service' with document 'tracking/captcha' in project 'braintree-payment-app' — monitor for unusual Firestore queries from checkout pages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Firestore document writes from web browsers (non-server-side). Flag access to 'tracking/' or 'captcha' paths that deviate from legitimate bot-protection patterns. Correlate Firestore writes to payment page load events within 1-second window.

suggestion.title: Periodic Data Exfiltration Loop Synchronized to Page Reload
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'executes right after a page load and every minute after' — data exfiltration on predictable 1-minute intervals is anomalous for legitimate traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeating API calls to api.stripe.com or Firestore at exactly 60-second intervals from same client during checkout session. Correlate intervals with localStorage reads and metadata field writes. Alert if pattern persists across multiple checkout pages.

suggestion.title: Content Security Policy Bypass via Trusted Domain Abuse (Stripe/GTM)
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'Stores allow that domain by default, so the skimmer slips past Content Security Policy rules and network filters' — abuse of trusted Stripe/GTM domains for C2 channels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for data exfiltration POST requests to api.stripe.com or firestore.googleapis.com that carry base64/binary-encoded payloads in customer metadata or document fields. Flag if payload size exceeds normal payment API calls (>1KB). Inspect request bodies for patterns consistent with credit card data.

suggestion.title: Detect large-scale data exfiltration from healthcare networks
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states '234 GB of data' exfiltrated from DentaQuest network. Pipeline generated zero exfiltration detection despite high-volume data theft being the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sustained outbound transfers from healthcare databases >100 GB/day window outside business hours. Correlate with admin/service-account activity, unusual DNS queries to external CDNs or cloud storage, and connection patterns to IP space not in whitelist.

suggestion.title: Monitor ShinyHunters threat actor leak site for victim postings
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'infamous extortion group ShinyHunters' and describes data posted to 'data leak site' after ransom negotiation failed. Zero threat-actor tracking or impact-phase detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor known ShinyHunters leak site domains for new victim postings with organizational names or data descriptions matching DentaQuest breaches. Alert on publication timelines correlating with internal breach discovery and public statement dates.

suggestion.title: Detect unauthorized network access preceding healthcare data exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthorized access to a limited portion of our network' but provides no IOC or initial-access detection. Should flag anomalous login patterns and network segmentation breaches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag successful admin logins from unusual geographies or off-hours immediately followed by database/share enumeration. Alert on lateral movement from internet-facing systems to internal healthcare databases within hours of initial compromise.

suggestion.title: Alert on post-breach credential harvesting and phishing spike targeting exposed identities
suggestion.rationale: Article warns: 'leaked data increases the risk of social engineering and phishing attacks' and lists exposed full names, phone numbers, email addresses. No post-breach attack-surface detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Spike detection on phishing emails targeting exposed employee email addresses with dental/health insurance pretexts. Monitor for credential-harvesting landing pages using exposed names/phone numbers for social engineering. Track domain registrations mimicking DentaQuest or major health plans.

suggestion.title: Detect sensitive PII/healthcare data bulk collection and staging for exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Breach exposed email, name, phone, government IDs, health insurance data, DOB, gender—234 GB total. Article implies bulk data collection; zero collection/staging-phase UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk read/copy operations from healthcare databases containing PII (SSN, government ID, health records). Flag unusual archive or compression activity (tar, zip, 7z) on sensitive shares. Correlate off-hours access with admin/service account anomalies.

suggestion.title: Track extortion communications and ransom negotiation timelines
suggestion.rationale: Article describes ransom negotiation: 'failure to reach an agreement with the company, the data was publicly leaked.' No impact-phase UC for detecting extortion infrastructure or threat communications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound ransom email templates or messaging from ShinyHunters infrastructure. Flag suspicious external emails claiming data access or demanding payment. Track Bitcoin/Monero addresses linked to threat actor, and monitor for leaked negotiation screenshots on breach forums.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted OSS domain access from search-engine referrer
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Fake Sites Mimicking Open-Source Tools Rank High on Google'—users click fake domains found via search. Defenders must detect high-similarity domain visits with Google/Bing/DuckDuckGo HTTP Referer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound HTTPS connections to domains with edit distance ≤2 from popular OSS projects (kubernetes.io → kubenetes.io, docker.com → dokcer.io) preceded by HTTP Referer header from search engines. Correlate domain first-seen timestamp with user search behavior. Flag if followed by file download (.exe, .msi, .zip, .tar.gz).

suggestion.title: TDS redirect chain detection for malware delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Deliver Malware via TDS'—Traffic Direction System performs intermediate HTTP redirects. Defenders must detect 302/307 chains from fake OSS domains to attacker C2 or payload hosts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid redirect chains (HTTP 302/307) where initial request lands on typosquatted domain and subsequent requests go to infrastructure with different IP geoLocation or certificate issuer. TDS systems use fingerprinting; same User-Agent + Cookie combination should redirect consistently—flag deviation. Alert if destination resolves to bulletproof hosting or known malicious ASNs.

suggestion.title: Certificate transparency logs: OSS tool domain variants
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must obtain SSL certificates for fake domains to avoid browser warnings. CT logs reveal newly registered typosquatted domain infrastructure before they rank in search results.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query CT log aggregators (crt.sh, certstream) for wildcard or multi-SAN certificates issued to domains matching common OSS projects. Use fuzzy string matching (Levenshtein ≤2) against curated list of high-value targets (kubernetes, terraform, nodejs, python, docker, npm, golang). Alert on bulk issuance to single registrant within 24-hour window. Cross-reference issuer and registrar against known attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Bulk domain registration anomalies for OSS variants
suggestion.rationale: Achieving 'Rank High on Google' at scale requires registering many typosquat domains. Passive WHOIS and registrar logs reveal clusters of suspicious registrations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate newly registered domains against OSS project name variants. Flag registrant accounts that register >5 similar domains within 7 days, use privacy/proxy services, or share nameservers with known malicious domains. Alert if domains resolve to shared hosting or fast-flux patterns where A-records change hourly.

suggestion.title: Malware download from fake OSS package sites
suggestion.rationale: Users may download installers (.exe, .msi) or archives from fake sites. Defenders must detect downloads from typosquatted domains and subsequent execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on executables or archives downloaded from domains with high string similarity to legitimate OSS projects. Cross-reference filename against legitimate project conventions (e.g., 'node-v18.0.0.msi' from domain ≠nodejs.org). Flag if file is written to temp directories (%TEMP%, /tmp), executed immediately, or has digital signature mismatch to legitimate publisher cert.

suggestion.title: Search result rank anomalies: counterfeit vs. legitimate OSS domains
suggestion.rationale: Attackers boost fake domain ranking to appear above legitimate projects. Statistical analysis of search traffic volume and ranking position reveal SEO manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate user web proxies with search engine results. Alert if user searches for 'kubernetes download' and visits non-kubernetes.io domain, or visits typosquat site immediately after search. Baseline: legitimate OSS domains should receive higher search-referrer traffic fraction than newly appeared clones. Flag if typosquat domain search traffic grows >50% week-over-week or ranks in top-3 results for generic searches (e.g., 'install docker').

suggestion.title: Suspicious macOS Process Execution from Ad Network Origins
suggestion.rationale: Article states threat 'spreads via Malicious Google and YouTube Ads'—ad clicks must trigger execution via browser or downloader child processes. No detection was generated for this initial execution step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned by Safari, Chrome, or other browsers with parent process showing recent ad-network traffic or unusual download activity. Flag non-whitelisted executable downloads and execution within seconds of browser activity.

suggestion.title: FlutterShell Backdoor C&C Beacon Detection
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor malware must establish command-and-control post-infection. Article explicitly names 'FlutterShell Backdoor' but no C&C/C2 detection use case was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor macOS network traffic for known FlutterShell C&C domains and IP addresses. Flag unusual HTTPS or DNS queries to infrastructure patterns consistent with bot beaconing from macOS hosts.

suggestion.title: macOS LaunchAgent/LaunchDaemon Persistence Installation
suggestion.rationale: Backdoors persist via LaunchAgent or startup scripts; article describes persistent 'backdoor' implant but no persistence detection was created.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor creation of plist files in ~/Library/LaunchAgents, /Library/LaunchAgents, /Library/LaunchDaemons with suspicious command payloads or execution patterns. Flag modifications to existing LaunchAgent/Daemon entries.

suggestion.title: Malicious Download from Ad Network Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article's attack vector is 'Google and YouTube Ads'—these ads serve malware payloads. Pipeline missed initial download/infection signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag downloads initiated from ad network domains (doubleclick.net, googlesyndication.com, youtube ad serving infrastructure) to macOS endpoints. Correlate with suspicious file types or execution within minutes.

suggestion.title: Unsigned or Gatekeeper-Bypassed Executable Execution on macOS
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor delivery via ads typically bypasses or spoofs macOS code-signing. No detection for unsigned/suspicious code execution was surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor execution of unsigned binaries or scripts on macOS with csFlags indicating Gatekeeper bypass. Flag shell script invocation with suspicious inline payloads from recent downloads.

suggestion.title: Trojanized Mobile App Installation via Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes distribution via 'Fake News, PDF and War Map Apps'—this is initial access via app impersonation, a primary mobile attack vector the pipeline did not surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for installation of apps with names matching news, PDF reader, or map utilities from untrusted sources or side-loading paths. Cross-reference app package hashes against known-malicious app repositories. Alert on mismatched publisher names or suspicious installation patterns in Arabic-targeted demographics.

suggestion.title: Spyware Runtime Behavior: Permission Abuse and Data Staging
suggestion.rationale: Spyware 'Asin' inherently performs surveillance—credential theft, call/SMS interception, location tracking. Pipeline did not propose behavioral detections for privilege escalation or sensitive data access typical of Android spyware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on apps requesting CALL_LOG, READ_SMS, ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION, or RECORD_AUDIO permissions post-installation with abnormal frequency or timing. Detect abnormal file staging in /sdcard or /cache consistent with data exfiltration prep. Flag apps spawning shell processes or accessing system binaries.

suggestion.title: Android C2 Callback Over Covert Channels
suggestion.rationale: Spyware requires command & control—article does not detail C2 infrastructure, but detection pipeline should have flagged for post-deployment C2 communication analysis once IOCs emerge.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS and HTTP/HTTPS traffic from known-compromised app package UIDs for beaconing patterns, unusual TLD frequency, or domain generation algorithms. Correlate C2 domains (once IOCs available) with Arabic geo-targeting signals.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion: App Obfuscation and Anti-Analysis Detection
suggestion.rationale: Modern Android spyware employs code obfuscation and anti-emulation checks. Pipeline did not propose detection for sandbox evasion or dynamic code loading behavior characteristic of Asin-family threats.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect dynamically loaded DEX files, reflection-based method invocation, or runtime code patching. Flag apps that query for debugger presence, detect emulation, or check for known security tools. Alert on native library loading from app-writable directories.

suggestion.title: Targeted Credential Harvesting: Arabic Media Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Asin specifically leverages 'fake news' and 'war map' apps to target Arabic speakers—this is credential collection via contextual social engineering. Pipeline should detect post-compromise credential harvesting UI overlays or keylogging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for accessibility service registrations by non-system apps, especially those spoofing news/media utilities. Detect window event capture or input device hooking. Alert on keyboard handler registration or suspicious event listener attachment post-install.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration via Native Protocol Abuse: SMS/Call Logs to Attacker Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Spyware Asin almost certainly exfiltrates SMS, call logs, and credentials. Pipeline identified no exfiltration detection for mobile-specific data channels (SMS to short codes, covert call forwarding).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual SMS sends to non-contacts, especially premium or regional short codes. Detect call forwarding activation via *21# or equivalent USSD. Monitor for bulk export of call/contact/SMS data to app-accessible storage followed by network exfil.

suggestion.title: Egnyte Storage Sync Compromise via Credential Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Explicit attack vector: 'VerdantBamboo compromised an Egnyte Storage Sync system and accessed it periodically through the victim's web SSL VPN.' This was the initial foothold for 18+ months of undetected access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate SSL VPN access logs with Egnyte authentication events. Alert on VPN sessions with subsequent Egnyte API calls outside business hours, from geographically anomalous IPs, or accessing sensitive shares repeatedly over extended periods. Detect credential reuse across VPN and storage systems.

suggestion.title: WebSocket C2 Traffic Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Plenet and Brickstorm both 'us[ed] the WebSocket protocol for C2 communications and a multiplexing library for simultaneous data streams.' Non-standard C2 protocol requiring explicit detection rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP 101 Upgrade responses (WebSocket handshake) to suspicious domains. Flag WebSocket streams with encrypted payloads, multiplexed frames, or connections to infrastructure taken offline during Sept 18-23 timeframe referenced in article. Correlate with process execution on compromised hosts.

suggestion.title: Malware Deployment to Storage Appliances (Synology NAS)
suggestion.rationale: Re-compromise phase: 'deployed additional custom malware to a Synology NAS device' and later 'deployed the custom malware Plenet to a Synology NAS appliance.' Unique attack surface often lacking EDR coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected binary execution on Synology NAS, unauthorized SSH/telnet sessions to NAS management, suspicious cron job creation, or writable directory access in /usr/local/bin or similar privilege paths. Detect connections from compromised internal gateways (pfSense, Egnyte) to NAS management ports.

suggestion.title: BSD Brickstorm on pfSense Firewall Detection
suggestion.rationale: Critical finding: 'VerdantBamboo had planted a BSD variant of Brickstorm on a pfSense firewall' compromised '18 months earlier.' Firewall backdoor bypasses all network-layer defenses downstream.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Implement file integrity monitoring on pfSense binaries and configuration files. Detect unauthorized package installs, unexpected firewall rule additions, or suspicious outbound connections originating from the firewall itself. Monitor SSH/https access to firewall management console for unusual credentials or source IPs.

suggestion.title: AgentPSD Python Reverse Shell Fallback Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Secondary persistence mechanism: 'AgentPSD is a simple Python-based reverse shell utility' deployed as 'fallback persistence mechanism if other malware was no longer accessible.' Indicates multi-layer persistence strategy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python interpreter (python/python3) spawning reverse shell patterns (socket.socket, subprocess.Popen, os.dup2). Alert on Python processes with hardcoded IP addresses or domains (article notes AgentPSD used 'different domain than the one Brickstorm used'). Monitor for Python package imports of socket, pty, or subprocess in suspicious contexts.

suggestion.title: Re-compromise Post-Remediation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Post-remediation re-entry: 'VerdantBamboo breached the organization again after the researchers completed the remediation efforts,' using 'stolen credentials to enable and configure SSL VPN access on the victim's firewall.' Indicates multiple backdoors or persistence mechanisms survived initial cleanup.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-incident, baseline normal credential usage and firewall rule modifications. Alert on re-authentication from previously suspicious IPs/geolocations within 30 days of incident closure. Detect SSL VPN or firewall rule changes shortly after remediation—indicators of retained backdoor access or missed compromise. Correlate with new process execution on infrastructure.

suggestion.title: BRICKSTORM file hash detection (installation/execution)
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 12 file hash IOCs (4 SHA256, 4 SHA1, 4 MD5) as 'high-fidelity' but pipeline extracted zero and generated no use case. Hash matching is the minimum viable detection for known malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation, process execution, or module load events matching any of the 12 BRICKSTORM hashes. Prioritize system-owned appliance processes and network service accounts on Windows, Linux, and proprietary appliance OSes.

suggestion.title: Persistence on network appliances and firewalls
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes malware maintained presence 'for well over a year' on 'firewalls, storage systems, and network appliances' — the attack's defining characteristic — yet no persistence detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unauthorized admin account creation on appliances, modification of startup scripts or cron jobs, unexpected scheduled tasks, or firmware backdoors. Correlate suspicious config changes with T1027 obfuscation indicators and file hash IOCs.

suggestion.title: Defense evasion via obfuscation bypass and alert suppression
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states threat evaded detection alerts entirely ('without ever tripping an alarm'). Pipeline identified T1027 but generated no detection for obfuscation patterns, logging disablement, or alert rule tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-entropy binaries, packed code, or reflective injection on appliances. Correlate with indicators of logging disabled, firewall rules modified to permit C2, or IDS/IPS signatures altered or silenced.

suggestion.title: Lateral movement from initial access to network appliances
suggestion.rationale: Explicit targeting of 'firewalls, storage systems, and network appliances' indicates pivoting from initial compromise point. No lateral movement detection generated despite clear infrastructure-specific attack flow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound connections from compromised endpoints or admin stations to appliance management interfaces (SSH 22, HTTPS 443/8443, vendor-specific ports). Correlate with process execution from SYSTEM/admin accounts and T1027 obfuscation signals.

suggestion.title: Command and control beaconing from network infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Multi-year persistent dwell requires active C2 channel, yet article provides no C2 IOCs (IP, domain, port) or behavioral signatures. Infrastructure-based beaconing detection critical for this threat profile.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for beaconing patterns (regular intervals, small payloads) from appliance management daemons to external or atypical internal infrastructure. Inspect for encrypted tunnels (suspicious TLS/SSH) from non-user-interactive processes on network devices.

suggestion.title: Serv-U POST Requests with Content-Encoding Deflate Header
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'specially crafted POST requests that crash the Serv-U service without authentication using Content-Encoding: deflate'. This is the direct attack signature and should be primary detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to Serv-U endpoints with Content-Encoding: deflate header. High-volume or rapid-fire such requests indicate exploitation attempts. Correlate timing with subsequent Serv-U service crashes or restarts.

suggestion.title: Serv-U Service Process Termination Following HTTP Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacks 'crash the Serv-U service'. Detection should correlate unexpected Serv-U process termination with preceding HTTP POST requests to identify DoS impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Serv-U process unexpected termination within minutes of abnormal HTTP POST request activity. Flag if process restart cycle indicates repeated exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempts Against Internet-Exposed Serv-U Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'Shodan currently tracks over 12,000 Serv-U servers exposed online' with 'no information on how many have already been patched'. This exposure creates immediate attack surface for CVE-2026-28318.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for incoming HTTP connections to public-facing Serv-U instances from untrusted sources. Flag POST requests with unusual or Content-Encoding headers.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Serv-U Version Asset Inventory (< 15.5.4 Hotfix 1)
suggestion.rationale: Patch released June 5, 2026 for version 15.5.4 Hotfix 1. Article warns 'there is no information on how many have already been patched', indicating urgent need for asset visibility.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Continuous asset inventory scanning identifying Serv-U installations with version < 15.5.4 Hotfix 1. Alert on any new instances; prioritize internet-facing deployments.

suggestion.title: Resource Exhaustion Indicators on Serv-U Hosts
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-28318 stems from 'uncontrolled resource consumption weakness'. Detection should identify abnormal resource usage consistent with DoS exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Serv-U hosts for CPU/memory spikes coinciding with HTTP POST request floods. Flag high-frequency POST requests (>100/min) to Serv-U. Correlate resource exhaustion with availability loss.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-28318 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and identifies CVE-2026-28318 as primary indicator. Pipeline generated zero UCs despite this clear directive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner detections of CVE-2026-28318 affecting SolarWinds Serv-U instances. Cross-reference with patch-management data to flag unpatched systems. Escalate any instance unpatched past federal deadline 2026-06-19.

suggestion.title: Serv-U Service Crash Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability 'allows specially crafted POST requests using the Content-Encoding: deflate header to crash the Serv-U service without authentication.' Pipeline missed the DoS impact phase and associated monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SolarWinds Serv-U for unexpected service crashes, restarts, or resource exhaustion spikes. Correlate with HTTP POST requests to exposed Serv-U endpoints. Alert on service availability deviations preceded by anomalous HTTP traffic patterns.

suggestion.title: Content-Encoding: deflate POST Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector: 'specially crafted POST requests using the Content-Encoding: deflate header.' This technique is distinctive enough for direct detection rules on exposed Serv-U endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests with Content-Encoding: deflate header targeting publicly exposed SolarWinds Serv-U instances. Baseline normal content-encoding patterns and flag anomalies or repeated attempts from untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: Unpatched SolarWinds Serv-U Compliance Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and establishes federal remediation deadline 2026-06-19. Pipeline should surface compliance-tracking UC alongside vulnerability detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain continuous inventory of all SolarWinds Serv-U instances and their patch levels. Flag any running vulnerable versions. Generate compliance report showing patch status against federal deadline. Escalate instances still unpatched beyond 2026-06-19.

suggestion.title: SD-WAN Manager Malicious File Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by uploading a crafted file to the affected system.' File upload is the execution vector but zero detection UC generated for it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file uploads (HTTP POST, multipart) to Cisco SD-WAN Manager web interface with suspicious file extensions (.csv with shell metacharacters) or destinations under /home/admin/. Correlate with immediate execution of vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh.

suggestion.title: Command Injection via vconfd_script Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article documents exact vulnerable script path and parameter pattern: 'vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh -cli path /home/admin/malicious.csv'. Injection point is detectable but not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of /usr/bin/vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh with -cli path parameter containing user-controlled input, paths under /home/admin/, or shell metacharacters (pipe, semicolon, backticks, $()). Monitor parent process context (vScript or vManage user).

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation from netadmin to root
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'local attackers with low privileges...execute arbitrary commands as root' requiring 'netadmin privileges.' Process-tree privilege transition is detectable but no UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for UID 0 (root) process spawning initiated from vconfd, vScript, or vmanage processes running under netadmin context. Alert on sudo/su transitions or direct capability escalation without expected sudo entries. Baseline normal root-spawning processes first.

suggestion.title: Suspicious SD-WAN Manager Log Entries
suggestion.rationale: Article provides concrete IOC: 'check their SD-WAN /var/log/scripts.log file' with example log 'Apr 15 09:44:57 vmanage vScript: Tenant list upload per vsmart serial number'. Log signature is actionable but not extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /var/log/scripts.log for entries containing 'Tenant list upload per vsmart serial number' followed by vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh with paths pointing to /home/admin/. Baseline expected timestamps and sources; alert on off-hours or suspicious parameter combinations.

suggestion.title: Configuration Changes Pushed to Edge Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Cisco has observed limited cases where the exploitation of this bug resulted in a configuration change pushed to edge devices.' Post-compromise lateral spread via config distribution is documented impact but no detection UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate root privilege escalation indicators with unexpected vsmart controller configuration pushes (policy updates, VPN/interface/route changes). Alert on config changes originating from root-privilege vManage processes or pushed at anomalous times outside change windows.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20182 or CVE-2026-20127 Exploitation Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE-2026-20245 requires 'valid credentials or exploitation of CVE-2026-20182 or CVE-2026-20127.' Detecting prerequisite vulns signals elevated risk of full chain exploitation but no chaining UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for exploitation attempts against CVE-2026-20182 (auth bypass) or CVE-2026-20127 (auth bypass) targeting Cisco SD-WAN Manager. Upon successful exploitation, escalate sensitivity/lower thresholds for file-upload and command-injection detections specific to CVE-2026-20245.

suggestion.title: Phishing emails with FIFA World Cup 2026 ticket-purchase lures
suggestion.rationale: Title phrase 'Fake Sites' and 'Stolen Logins' establishes phishing as primary attack vector targeting ticket buyers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with World Cup 2026, ticketing, or sports-betting keywords directing to unverified domains. Flag sender domain spoofing of FIFA/official ticketing platforms. Alert on emails with shortened URLs or redirects to credential harvesting infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted FIFA and World Cup ticketing domain infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Fake Sites' indicates fraudulent domains impersonating FIFA/ticketing platforms for credential harvesting and malware distribution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS/HTTP traffic to domains typosquatting FIFA, ticketing authorities, or World Cup infrastructure. Detect registration anomalies: newly registered, bulk registrations, WHOIS privacy abuse, shared hosting with known phishing/malware infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Banking malware execution and command-and-control communication
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'Banking Malware'. Detection must cover execution, lateral movement, and C2 exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious process execution: unsigned executables in TEMP, explorer.exe→malware spawning, DLL injection patterns. Monitor C2 patterns: POST requests to malicious IPs, DNS tunneling, encrypted outbound to known trojan C2 ranges.

suggestion.title: Phishing form and credential-harvesting kit detection
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Stolen Logins' indicates fraudulent ticketing/banking forms capturing credentials at scale.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POSTs to phishing infrastructure with form field patterns matching FIFA account, banking, or ticketing credentials. Monitor for pages with FIFA/official branding but non-official backend infrastructure. Flag credential submission spikes from single source IPs.

suggestion.title: Anomalous World Cup ticket purchases and account takeover fraud patterns
suggestion.rationale: Compromised credentials from phishing/malware lead to unauthorized high-volume ticket purchases and account abuse—indicates impact phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk/rapid ticket purchases from single account, geographic impossibilities, sequential purchases via different payment methods, credential changes following transactions, account lockouts post-purchase.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated POST to DbGate /api/auth/login without valid credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article states the 'none auth provider issues JWT tokens without credentials via `POST /auth/login`'—this is the initial access mechanism that must be detected before the ZIP payload exploitation. Currently no UC hunts for tokens being issued to unauthenticated requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to /api/auth/login endpoints on DbGate instances that return successful auth tokens (HTTP 200, JWT in response body) without corresponding valid credentials in request. Track source IPs making this request; these are attack initiation points.

suggestion.title: Malicious ZIP with path-traversal entries uploaded to DbGate unzip endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'A malicious ZIP with `../` entries writes files anywhere on the filesystem.' No UC hunts for detecting these ZIP payloads in flight. This is the execution phase of the attack and should be detected at upload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to /api/archive/unzip with ZIP file bodies. Inspect ZIP central directory for entries containing `../` path traversal sequences. Alert on any ZIP upload attempting to write outside the intended extraction directory (e.g., entries with absolute paths or excessive traversal).

suggestion.title: DbGate process spawning shell or privilege-escalation commands post-exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article notes DbGate runs as root; exploitation allows writing to sensitive paths (cron, sudoers, ld.so.preload). Post-write, persistence mechanisms are triggered (cron job execution, ld.so.preload injection). No UC detects the subsequent child-process execution from these persistence layers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned from node (DbGate) after suspicious file writes to /etc/cron.d, /etc/init.d, /etc/systemd/system/, or /etc/ld.so.preload. These child processes indicate the persistence payload triggered. Alert on any shell, curl, wget, or outbound-network child of node in this context.

suggestion.title: Web shell or reverse-shell payload execution via DbGate web root write
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1505.003 (Server Software Component: Web Shell) as a technique but no UC hunts for web shell execution. If DbGate writes a shell script to the web root or application directory, we should detect HTTP requests to that shell and execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After detecting suspicious file write to web-accessible paths (detected in UC_14_2), monitor for HTTP GET/POST to that newly created file. Then correlate with shell-execution events (bash, sh, curl commands) launched from the web server context.

suggestion.title: Node process reading or sourcing newly written configuration or shell scripts
suggestion.rationale: After zip-slip writes files to /etc/profile.d, /etc/init.d, /etc/systemd/system, or shell rc files, those scripts are sourced or executed on next system event or session. Article describes '...leading to RCE' but doesn't explicitly cover detection of these sourcing events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file-open or file-read events where the node process (or child processes) opens files in /etc/profile.d, /etc/init.d, /etc/systemd/system/, or similar shell initialization paths immediately after those files are written. This indicates the persistence payload is being loaded.

suggestion.title: DbGate /runners/load-reader endpoint access by authenticated user
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'any user with valid DbGate credentials can execute' — requires authentication as prerequisite. Missing hunt for anomalous login-to-exploitation correlation: user login followed by suspicious POST to /runners/load-reader within minutes. Article states authenticated access requirement but no detection rule addresses this multi-event sequence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful user logon to DbGate service with POST request to /runners/load-reader endpoint within 5–30 minutes. Focus on accounts with no prior /runners/load-reader access history or accessing DbGate from unusual network location/time-of-day. Exclude service accounts and known DevOps workflows.

suggestion.title: Dynamic import() and function instantiation patterns in DbGate traffic
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically identifies 'require = null mitigation is trivially bypassed via dynamic import()' as the attack mechanism. Pipeline should detect the functional bypass pattern itself: presence of 'import(' in POST bodies to /runners/load-reader. This is the core exploitation technique and deserves dedicated detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for POST requests to /runners/load-reader with functionName parameter containing JavaScript patterns: 'import(', 'eval(', '(async', 'Function(', or backticks followed by shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, $()). Correlate with absence of User-Agent or User-Agent inconsistent with DbGate client libraries.

suggestion.title: Root-level process execution spawned from Node.js DbGate service
suggestion.rationale: Article states commands execute 'as root' — this is privilege-escalation intent. Detect when DbGate node process (typically unprivileged service account) spawns child processes running as root/UID 0. This indicates successful exploitation leading to privilege escalation, not just benign process spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Filter for ProcessIntegrityLevel=System OR AccountName=root OR UID=0 where InitiatingProcessParent is node/dbgate service account. Exclude DbGate startup sequences and scheduled maintenance jobs. Flag interactive shell spawns (sh -i, bash -i) or reverse-shell patterns (/bin/bash -c, nc, socat) from node parent.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated newline injection in functionName parameter
suggestion.rationale:
Article shows newline injection bypasses: '
var', '%0Avar', '%0Aawait'. Pipeline should generalize beyond these 3 variants to detect other Unicode/encoding schemes: 
, \x0A, 
 in various encodings, multi-byte 
 sequences. Current UCs only match literal strings, missing polymorphic payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST to /runners/load-reader where functionName parameter contains encoded newline variants: %0A, %0D%0A, \u000A, \u000D, or raw bytes 0x0A/0x0D. Flag if followed by shell metacharacters or eval-like patterns. Allow-list known-safe client versions; flag all others as suspicious.

suggestion.title: DbGate credential reuse and session anomaly (authentication-to-RCE pipeline)
suggestion.rationale: Article vulnerability requires 'valid DbGate credentials' but doesn't describe how attackers obtain them. Missing detection for credential compromise signals: failed login attempts preceding successful login, geographically-impossible login patterns, login from known compromised IP ranges, credential reuse across multiple DbGate instances in short timeframe.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline DbGate login patterns by user: typical login times, geographies, source IPs. Flag logins deviating from baseline (e.g., user never logs in before 08:00 now logs in at 02:00). Flag N successful logins within M minutes from distinct IPs but same account. Correlate with /runners/load-reader requests within 30 minutes of anomalous login.

suggestion.title: File creation outside ait-bsc configured log root
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'log to arbitrary filesystem paths'—must detect actual impact. Current UCs miss post-exploitation file-write signals by focusing only on request patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track files created or modified by ait-bsc process (or child processes). Alert when file path escapes /var/opt/ait-bsc/logs or administrator-configured log root. Correlate with POST to /start in same time window.

suggestion.title: HTTP API calls to BSC without authentication headers
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated HTTP API'—legitimate clients should provide session/auth headers. Absence of Authorization, X-API-Key, or session cookie is anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to /*/start endpoints. Alert when POST lacks Authorization header, X-API-Key, Cookie, or equivalent auth mechanism present in baseline.

suggestion.title: Rapid multiple path-traversal attempts to single BSC handler
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'blindly trusts path fields'—attackers will probe different traversal payloads (../, %2e%2e, %252e%252e, ../../) to identify target filesystem layout.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect 5+ POST requests to same /[handler]/start endpoint within 60s containing distinct path-traversal encoding variants (/, %2e%2e, %252e%252e, unicode escapes). Indicates scanning for exploitability.

suggestion.title: Outbound DNS/HTTP from ait-bsc for exfiltration staging
suggestion.rationale: If attacker appends data to attacker-controlled destinations (e.g., writable SMB shares, HTTP callbacks), ait-bsc process will resolve or connect externally—a true post-exploitation signal missing from current hunts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate ait-bsc process execution with outbound DNS queries to non-baseline domains or HTTP connects to suspicious IPs. Focus on connections initiated within 30s of successful path-traversal POST.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized role creation from non-privileged user
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Any authenticated user could load the page and use its public actions to create new roles' — direct privilege escalation action the network-layer UC cannot detect.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful role creation operations (HTTP 200/201 responses to POST Settings/Team/Index or createRole action) from user accounts lacking admin or role-creator privileges. Baseline admin-only operations and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Admin user deletion by non-admin authenticated user
suggestion.rationale: Article states compromised users could 'delete other users, including administrators' — specific privilege escalation attack vector via Settings/Team/Index.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor user deletion operations targeting admin or privileged accounts initiated from non-admin authenticated sessions. Alert on any deletion of admin users by standard user accounts.

suggestion.title: Permission read/write mismatch in RolePermission endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'RolePermission gated write actions on the read-only view_users permission' — indicates permission validation bypass allowing read-permission holders to modify permissions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PATCH/PUT operations to RolePermission endpoints from users whose role only includes view_users permission. Cross-reference user assigned permissions against actual write actions performed.

suggestion.title: Livewire component mount() bypass in Settings.Team
suggestion.rationale: Article root cause: 'Settings/Team/Index had no mount() authorization' — Livewire's component lifecycle check is missing, allowing unauthenticated or under-privileged access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag POST requests to /livewire/update or /livewire/message/settings.team with actions like createRole, deleteUser, or updatePermission from non-admin users. Livewire component calls bypass higher-level authorization when mount() checks are absent.

suggestion.title: HTTP POST to Everest Forms Plugin Endpoint with Exploit Signatures
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Hackers Exploit Critical Everest Forms Pro WordPress Plugin Flaw'—initial access vector is direct exploitation of the plugin via POST request; detection must cover malicious form submissions and injection payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to /wp-content/plugins/everest-forms* endpoints. Alert on requests containing SQL injection markers, command injection syntax, file inclusion patterns (../, etc), or base64-encoded payloads. Correlate with subsequent successful responses and file creation events.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Deployment via Vulnerable Plugin
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'Take Over Sites'—full site takeover implies persistence mechanism; threat actors deploy web shells or backdoors post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PHP file creation in wp-content/plugins/everest-forms/ or adjacent directories by web server process. Flag new .php files in WordPress root or upload directories with suspicious names (shell.php, admin.php, etc). Correlate creation time with exploitation attempts (POST spike).

suggestion.title: Web Server Process Child Spawning (RCE Post-Exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation of plugin vulnerability should result in arbitrary code execution; attackers execute system commands via web context to establish foothold.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for web server processes (apache, www-data, iis apppool) spawning child processes: shells (bash, sh, cmd.exe, powershell), system utilities (curl, wget, nc, ncat), or compilers (gcc, cc). Trigger alerts with 100% confidence; web servers should not spawn these normally.

suggestion.title: Everest Forms Pro Plugin Installation or Modification Baseline Violation
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerable 'Everest Forms Pro' plugin must be inventoried and monitored; article implies active exploitation requiring vulnerable version to be present and accessible.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any WordPress instance where Everest Forms Pro plugin is installed with version below current/patched release. Alert on unauthorized plugin file modifications (permissions change, binary modification, new files in plugin directory without corresponding version bump).

suggestion.title: Large Volume of Form Data POST Requests Targeting Single Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Plugin exploitation often involves repeated probe/exploit attempts; 'Critical Flaw' suggests unauthenticated endpoint vulnerability susceptible to rapid-fire exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spike in POST requests to Everest Forms form submission endpoints from single source IP within short time window (e.g., >50 requests/minute). Correlate with 5xx errors or successful responses followed by persistent connections (web shell callback).

suggestion.title: PyPI Typosquatting Package Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article core: 'deceptive Python package... crafted to look almost identical to the widely used parsimonious library. The single missing letter was no [...].' This is the attack mechanism — detection should hunt for packages with names similar to popular libraries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Python package installations via pip/conda, flag when newly-installed package name Levenshtein-distances ≤2 from known popular packages. Cross-reference package hash against blacklists. Alert on first execution of recently-installed packages from untrusted sources.

suggestion.title: Malicious Python Package File Hash Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article provides SHA1 hash `a01c2a21f24db63cb01a67016519aebeca438089` and explicitly recommends 'File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match' hunt. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this directive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match SHA1 hash `a01c2a21f24db63cb01a67016519aebeca438089` against file activity (pip cache, site-packages, /tmp) and process execution context. Correlate file hash with Python interpreter invocation to detect when malicious package bytecode executes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Python Module Import Post-Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article states package 'quietly made its way into the PyPI repository' and would execute when imported. Detection gap: no hunt for post-installation execution patterns of recently-installed Python packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Python subprocess spawning or network I/O immediately after pip install completes. Flag unexpected child processes, network connections, or file modifications triggered by package __init__.py or setup.py execution.

suggestion.title: Package Repository Upload Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Attack surface: malicious package was 'published' to PyPI. Detection should cover repository-side signals: new accounts uploading packages with typosquatted names, bulk uploads from single source, packages that mimic maintenance patterns of legitimate libraries but differ in metadata or dependencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query package repository logs for uploads where package name similarity score to established libraries exceeds threshold; flag if uploader is new account or country of origin differs from maintainer baseline. Flag packages with identical or near-identical version numbers to legitimate packages.

suggestion.title: File hash match — Hola Browser malware payload
suggestion.rationale: Article lists four file hashes for malware 'me.exe'; foundational hash-based detection missing from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution or file creation matching any of the four provided hashes: 174086534a2de730058465a4a4e231ce3778ab17ebebfd7f62b3bf9750bc7bdb, e3541caf708c075f0bb22fc68b03acd8457fea7cf0732ea935b1eb016d1c7721, 8046735d354814bf9ef9a053cb9cad8cfec261f2, 8462f61e68b37d220eab2462b3cbcec8.

suggestion.title: Cryptominer resource hijacking behavior
suggestion.rationale: Payload explicitly identified as cryptominer; detection must hunt resource exhaustion signatures (sustained CPU/memory abuse, pool connectivity) beyond file presence alone.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate sustained elevated CPU/memory usage from low-reputation or unsigned processes with outbound connections to known cryptomining pool infrastructure or hosting ASNs.

suggestion.title: Installer-spawned unsigned executable execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'me.exe' distributed within Hola Browser installer; detection gap for installers spawning unexpected unsigned binaries outside known vendor post-install patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor processes matching setup/installer/update pattern names for spawning unsigned executables or shell interpreters (cmd, powershell, rundll32, regsvr32, mshta, wscript) not in vendor baseline.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated/packed binary distribution indicators
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline cited T1027 (Obfuscated Files) as a technique but generated no detection for obfuscation signals such as entropy analysis, packing signatures, or anomalous PE metadata.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect files exhibiting high entropy (packed/compressed), anomalous PE section structure, or signatures of known packing tools distributed through software delivery infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Installation & Post-Install Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly: 'Hit npm in Supply Chain Attacks'. Worms exploit package.json postinstall hooks to execute arbitrary code. Pipeline should detect npm.exe/node.exe spawning unexpected child processes (powershell, cmd, curl) immediately after npm install or package-lock.json modification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm.exe or node.exe executing powershell.exe, cmd.exe, curl.exe, or bash with suspicious arguments (downloading, encoding, exfiltrating) within 30 seconds of package-lock.json write or 'npm install' command. Flag especially if target directory is not a known development workspace or if child process opens outbound network connections.

suggestion.title: Worm Self-Propagation via Rapid Project Discovery & Reinfection
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Worm Variant'—implies automated self-replication across targets. Article likely describes filesystem enumeration seeking additional project directories, repeated npm install across non-owned paths, or registry manipulation. Pipeline should detect patterns of rapid sequential package operations on multiple directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node.exe or npm.exe process spawning multiple instances in parallel or in rapid succession targeting different directories, reading package.json across unrelated project paths, or modifying node_modules/.bin executables. Alert if a single npm install triggers 10+ child processes or file modifications across sibling/parent directories in under 1 minute.

suggestion.title: Credential & Secrets Exfiltration from npm Compromised Host
suggestion.rationale: Worm attack on development/build infrastructure. Article likely describes theft of .env files, .npm tokens, .ssh keys, or source repos. Pipeline should detect node.exe reading sensitive files followed by HTTP POST/PUT to external infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node.exe or child process (spawned by npm) reading .env, .npmrc, .ssh/id_rsa, .git/config, or AWS credential files, immediately followed by DNS resolution and HTTP/HTTPS POST request to an external IP or newly registered domain (not in org allowlist). Payload likely base64, gzip, or JSON-encoded.

suggestion.title: C2 Beacon from Compromised npm Host
suggestion.rationale: Worms maintain persistence & receive updates via C2. Title/article should identify attacker infrastructure. Pipeline should detect node.exe establishing outbound TLS sessions or DNS queries to suspicious domains, especially with retry/beaconing patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node.exe initiating outbound HTTPS/TLS to external domain/IP not in org allowlist, especially with high-entropy subdomain patterns or dynamic DNS indicators. Alert on repeat connection attempts (every 30–300s) indicating beaconing. Flag connections from build/CI runner containers or dev machines to infrastructure with short WHOIS registration date.

suggestion.title: Modification of Package Metadata for Persistence & Re-infection
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain worms persist by tampering with package.json (adding malicious dependencies), .bin scripts, or CI/CD config files. Article should describe these modifications. Pipeline should detect file writes to package.json, node_modules/.bin, or .github/workflows outside of normal deployment windows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modification of package.json (new 'postinstall'/'preinstall' scripts, new dependencies added), creation of unsigned executables in node_modules/.bin, or modification of CI/CD workflow files (.github/workflows/*.yml) by a process running under npm or node context. Alert if modifications occur outside scheduled deployment windows.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Attack Detection: Typosquatting or Dependency Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: Common npm worm vector: malicious packages with typosquatted names or legitimate package version hijacking. Pipeline should detect installation of packages not in organization's approved software catalog, or installations of unusual package versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm install requests for package names that differ by 1–2 chars from popular packages (e.g., 'lodash' vs 'loddash'), packages from newly created npm authors, or packages with zero GitHub stars installed in production environments. Cross-reference against org-maintained allowlist and flag mismatches.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Browser Extension Installation via Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malicious Google Chrome extensions is secretly harvesting'. Installation is the persistence mechanism. Corresponds to article's explicit recommended hunt UC_BROWSER_EXT: 'Registry.registry_path contains Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor registry paths *\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\, *\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\, *\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\ for writes from non-system processes. Alert on new extension registrations not matching known-good baseline.

suggestion.title: Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'harvesting those conversations' requires extraction of session tokens and login context. Directly corresponds to UC_BROWSER_STEALER: non-chrome/edge/firefox processes reading Login Data, Cookies, logins.json, cookies.sqlite files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file-system access to browser credential databases by processes outside the browser binary and its child processes. Correlate with extension host processes or unusual script interpreters.

suggestion.title: Network Traffic to Extension Command-and-Control Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'sending them off [conversations]' to external servers. IOCs deepaichats.com and chatsaigpt.com represent C2 infrastructure for data exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DNS queries and network connections to deepaichats.com and chatsaigpt.com. Include TLS SNI inspection and DNS-over-HTTPS tunneling detection.

suggestion.title: Execution of Known Malicious Extension Binaries
suggestion.rationale: Article provides three SHA256 hashes as IOCs. File hash matching at process/file-system level for malware identification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match hashes 524c953e23ff8b768206cf33a529c11ac5510e47cbf6246db79ee671d1231716, c984787ccd787629542da68302ed4ceb48fc7e458eab1c15bf45c3070883d26a, f8cbe44fde6914bc8d06426c03c92ed536c891470292e567a586b54af29c2442 against process creation, module loads, and file writes.

suggestion.title: UPnP Stack Buffer Overflow Exploitation Attempts on DD-WRT
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malware 'exploits a stack buffer overflow flaw in the UPnP service of affected routers' — this is the attack vector but no detection logic exists for it. Critical gap: no hunt for oversized UPnP packets or service crashes on port 1900.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag abnormally large UPnP payloads (UDP/1900) exceeding 512-byte threshold, especially those with memcpy-like patterns. Correlate with immediate UPnP service restarts, kernel panic logs, or dmesg 'segmentation fault' messages on DD-WRT routers within 5 minutes of packet arrival.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Command Execution Without Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article stresses 'gain full access without any credentials' — implies immediate post-exploitation privilege escalation. Missing detection for unauthenticated root spawned from network service contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Linux routers, detect processes with UID 0 spawned from UPnP/network daemon contexts without preceding login events (no setuid transition, no su/sudo audit trail). Flag unexpected /bin/sh or busybox execution from httpd or upnpd parent process.

suggestion.title: Multi-Architecture Botnet Payload Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'multiple Linux architectures' and 'modular propagation' but no detection hunt for multi-variant binary execution. Article implies ARM/MIPS/x86 variants spread within same campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference the 12 provided SHA256 hashes against executed binaries. Alert if 2+ hashes from different ELF machine types (ARM, MIPS, x86) are seen executing on the same router or within same /24 network segment. Check ELF e_machine header values in binary analysis.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication to Extracted IP Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: MITRE T1071 (Application Layer Protocol) indicates C2 callback. Three IPs extracted (85.215.131.70, 217.160.125.125, 176.100.37.91) but no detection use case specifies how to hunt them. Gafgyt typically uses HTTP/IRC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections from DD-WRT routers to the three IPs on ports 80, 443, 6667, 8080. Flag connections with short-lived patterns, POST requests with binary payloads, or IRC protocol sequences. Correlate timing with UPnP exploitation window.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Firmware or Startup Script Modification
suggestion.rationale: Botnet must persist across reboots. Article mentions 'modular propagation' implying installed components but no detection for DD-WRT firmware changes, cron jobs, or rc.local injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /etc/rc.local, /etc/init.d/, crontab entries for modifications post-compromise. Flag firmware file writes (nvram changes on DD-WRT), unexpected busybox/dropbear instances, or cron entries spawning shells. Use file integrity monitoring on /etc and /lib directories.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Binary Execution from Network Origin
suggestion.rationale: MITRE T1027 (Obfuscation) noted in techniques. Article hashes suggest packed/obfuscated malware but no detection for suspicious ELF characteristics like stripped symbols, UPX-packed sections, or unusual entropy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of stripped ELF binaries (no symbol table) or those with high entropy sections indicating packing/encryption. Cross-reference with downloaded/modified files from network sources. Flag process command lines invoking binaries from /tmp or /var/tmp.

suggestion.title: C2 beacon to Firebase command domain
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'uses Stripe... as both its command center and its data dump' with explicit IOC braintree-payment-app.firebaseio.com. Pipeline extracted neither IOC nor matching C2-detection use case despite article recommending 'Network connections to article IPs / domains' hunt at High confidence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTPS to braintree-payment-app.firebaseio.com and related Firebase domains from web servers and browsers. Legitimate ecommerce systems do not beacon to attacker-controlled Firebase projects. Correlate with website code changes, unusual JavaScript execution, or payment form interception.

suggestion.title: Payment card data exfiltration via Stripe abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'uses Stripe... as... its data dump.' Exfiltration of stolen card data is the core attack payload; pipeline mapped only T1071, missing T1041 (exfil over C2 channel) and T1567 (exfil over web service).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt Stripe API logs for anomalous account activity: bulk tokenization, unusual geographies, or card data patterns inconsistent with site's legitimate business. Monitor webhook endpoints for suspicious data payloads. Correlate with website compromise signals or C2 beacon to Firebase.

suggestion.title: Malicious JavaScript injection on ecommerce payment forms
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'credit card skimming malware... hiding inside... trusted payment platform.' This describes browser-level form hijacking via script injection; pipeline missed T1005 (data from local forms) and T1189 (drive-by compromise).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned or dynamically-loaded JavaScript on ecommerce pages accessing payment form fields (form.onsubmit handlers, HTMLFormElement.submit interception, input.value reads). Hunt for XSS payloads, malicious third-party widget injection, or obfuscated data exfiltration code. Correlate with C2 beacon or form access anomalies.

suggestion.title: Stripe account abuse and compromise for C2 infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'uses Stripe... as both [command center] and [data dump].' This implies attacker control of a Stripe account; pipeline did not infer account-compromise patterns or infrastructure-abuse use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Stripe API keys and webhooks for unusual access patterns, unexpected geographies, or spike in token creation.
