suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Whitelist legitimate Firebase domains per organization; alert on connections to Firebase subdomains outside the whitelist or without matching business application context. Inspect Firebase Realtime Database traffic for JSON payloads with command/control semantics.

suggestion.title: SMTP Relay Configuration on Non-Mail Cloud Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article states PCPJack 'hijacks' servers 'for covert SMTP relay network'—attackers modified instance configs to send mail. Should detect SMTP daemon installation or postfix/sendmail process start on VMs not tagged as mail servers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for postfix, sendmail, or exim processes starting on non-designated mail relay VMs. Correlate with unusual administrative access (SSH/RDP) in same session window. Flag instances with outbound SMTP traffic on high ports (587, 2525) not matching baseline.

suggestion.title: Credential Reuse Across Multi-Cloud Instances
suggestion.rationale: 230 servers across AWS, GCP, Azure suggests attacker used shared or overprivileged credentials to persist. Article implies lateral movement across cloud boundaries. Need detection for same credential/key used on instances across different providers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-correlate authentication logs from AWS, GCP, Azure for same user/service principal/SSH key used within short time window across separate cloud accounts/subscriptions. Establish baseline of legitimate cross-cloud access patterns and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: SSH Public Key Injection on Cloud Instances
suggestion.rationale: Persistence across 230 heterogeneous cloud VMs most likely via SSH key implants (T1098.004). Title says 'hijacks' (active compromise), implying ongoing access mechanism needed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ~/.ssh/authorized_keys modifications on cloud instances, especially bulk changes affecting multiple VMs in parallel or same-minute timestamps. Alert if new keys added from unfamiliar source IPs. Correlate file modification events with SSH session logs to detect key injection outside normal change-control windows.

suggestion.title: Initial Compromise: Public-Facing Service Exploitation or Credential Stuffing
suggestion.rationale: Article does not detail initial access method but compromising 230 cloud instances suggests either exploiting a known weakness (T1190) or reusing stolen credentials (T1110/T1078). Without specifics in body, detection should cover both vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track failed-then-successful SSH/RDP authentication against cloud management APIs. Flag rapid credential attempts against multiple instances from same source (credential stuffing). Monitor API calls creating/modifying IAM roles or service principals that later access instances.

suggestion.title: Bulk Infrastructure Modification: Widespread Persistence Across Multiple VMs
suggestion.rationale: 230 servers suggests coordinated, scripted deployment of malicious SMTP relay—not manual. Detect batch execution of configuration changes (systemd units, cron, startup scripts) across instance fleet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk cron job additions, systemd service file writes, or shell script executions affecting 10+ instances within 1-hour window. Correlate with administrative credential usage from single source IP or service principal. Baseline normal patch/config deployment cadence and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Outbound SMTP Traffic from Non-Mail Cloud Instances
suggestion.rationale: Covert SMTP relay means instances sending mail to external recipients on ports 25/587/2525. Title explicitly states relay network purpose—detect egress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound SMTP connections from non-mailserver instances. Flag high-volume SMTP egress to suspicious domains or new destinations. Correlate with process telemetry (postfix, sendmail, custom SMTP clients). Establish baseline for legitimate outbound mail and alert on deviations >10x baseline.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized GitHub Action Execution via Prompt Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly references 'Claude Code Github action case' and keywords include 'Frontier AI models' and 'Vulnerability'—indicating agent-driven CI/CD compromise via prompt/injection attack. Pipeline missed the core execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious GitHub Actions runtime invocations (scheduled or on-demand) spawning unexpected child processes, network calls to non-standard registries/artifact stores, or encoded command sequences. Flag when action logs contain LLM-generated or obfuscated task definitions.

suggestion.title: CI/CD Supply Chain Artifact Injection
suggestion.rationale: Keywords include 'Supply chain' and 'Vulnerability' in context of CI/CD. Article discusses securing CI/CD in agentic world—implies compromise of build artifacts or dependencies injected during pipeline execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package repositories, artifact registries (npm, PyPI, Maven), and container registries for unexpected package versions, author changes, or metadata alterations. Correlate with GitHub push events from service accounts or unusual repository branches.

suggestion.title: Anomalous GitHub Service Account Activity
suggestion.rationale: CI/CD platforms use service accounts with broad access. Article covers securing CI/CD—pipeline should flag unauthorized account creation, token exfiltration, or repository permission escalation in GitHub.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub API calls creating or modifying org-level secrets, adding SSH keys to runner accounts, or cloning private repos to external URLs. Flag token usage from non-CI/CD infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Suspicious GitHub Workflow File Modification
suggestion.rationale: Attack surface in agentic CI/CD is the workflow YAML itself. If Claude Code action or similar agent can author/modify .github/workflows files, detect persistence via workflow injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for direct file modifications to .github/workflows/ by non-human actors or automation outside normal CI/CD gates. Detect workflow additions containing exfiltration, credential harvesting, or reverse-shell payloads.

suggestion.title: Claude Code GitHub Action Endpoint Substitution
suggestion.rationale: Named vulnerability 'Claude Code Github action case'—likely involves supply-chain risk from compromised or forked action. Detect when workflows reference action from unexpected repository, tag, or commit hash.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline the canonical Claude Code action repository and version in use. Alert on workflows that reference forks, alternative paths, or untagged commits. Correlate modified workflow files with first execution of substituted action.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration via Authorized CI/CD Log Access
suggestion.rationale: CI/CD runners have access to build logs, secrets, and artifacts. Article severity 'HIGH' suggests data exfiltration risk. Detect unusual log collection or artifact download patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor CI/CD runner egress for unexpected archive downloads (tar.gz, .zip of entire repo/logs), uploads to personal cloud storage, or base64-encoded secrets in HTTP POST bodies.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Authentication Dialog from External JavaScript Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Starting in late May 2026, the polyfill[.]io domain became active again and started responding with HTTP 401 authentication requests. User browsers visiting pages...interpret that as a request for a username and password, so they serve a login prompt.' Core observable is browser showing native login dialog sourced from untrusted external domain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP 401 responses from external JavaScript CDN domains (especially polyfill.*, cdn.*, ajax.*) delivered to corporate or e-commerce domains. Browser-native auth dialogs sourced from third-party infrastructure indicate HTTP 401 spoofing. Correlate with known-good domains (Toshiba, Muji, Samsung, etc.) to identify victims.

suggestion.title: Script Inclusion from Compromised Polyfill.io CDN
suggestion.rationale: Article documents 'The login pop-ups were generated by the external service hosted at polyfill[.]io' and 'remnants of Polyfill code remained' on sites that failed to remove the service over two years. This is explicit script inclusion from compromised infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to polyfill.io (and variants: polyfill.*.com, polyfill.*.io) containing script tags or JavaScript execution. Cross-reference with site ownership databases to identify unpatched pages still including the malicious CDN. Alert on any polyfill.io resolution or connection post-May 2026.

suggestion.title: Expired Domain Reregistration by Malicious Actor
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'when the domain expired, it could be claimed by anyone' and 'starting in late May 2026, the polyfill[.]io domain became active again.' This is classic supply-chain attack via domain lifecycle exploitation by 'a Chinese entity.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track WHOIS changes on high-value JavaScript CDN domains (especially those with historical supply-chain exposure). Alert on re-registration after expiration, especially to registrars or entities in high-risk jurisdictions. Monitor DNS resolution changes for domains known to be referenced in legacy code.

suggestion.title: Bulk Credential Harvesting via Spoofed Browser Auth Dialog
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'if you do see it, please select "Cancel" without entering any information' and advises users 'who entered their account login data in the authentication screens to change their passwords.' This indicates multi-victim credential harvesting at scale (Toshiba, Muji, Samsung, Zojirushi, FiNC, Ishiyaku, Hobonichi).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected password-entry events triggered by non-origin HTTP 401 responses. Cross-check browser security logs for authentication dialogs rendered by third-party scripts. Correlate with known-good site access; password changes following suspicious auth prompts on retail/tech sites indicate credential compromise.

suggestion.title: Detection of Unpatched Script Inclusions from Malicious CDN
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'some sites using the service failed to clean all their pages over the past two years, so remnants of Polyfill code remained.' This describes persistent presence of legacy malicious script references in site markup.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan production site markup and git history for script tags referencing polyfill.io, polyfill.io/*.js, and renamed variants. Identify pages that were not updated when the domain was known to be compromised (2024). Alert on any page serving these references post-remediation date.

suggestion.title: TA4922 Phishing Email Detection by Domain Typosquatting
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'TA4922 Expands Phishing Attacks'—core attack vector is phishing emails; pipeline generated zero detection rules for email-borne threats
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound email for sender domains resembling legitimate targets in UK, Germany, Italy, South Africa. Detect newly-registered or typosquatted domains. Alert on emails with attachment+urgent-language lures typical of TA4922 past campaigns. Correlate with external threat feeds for known TA4922 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Login After Phishing Email Click
suggestion.rationale: Phishing campaigns harvest credentials; article targets multiple countries suggesting credential theft objective; no detection rule for post-compromise login anomalies
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed/successful logins within 2–6 hours of phishing email delivery. Flag impossible travel (user IP geolocation inconsistent with typical location). Alert on bulk account enumeration or credential spray from suspicious IPs.

suggestion.title: Outbound Data Transfer from Phishing-Exposed Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Multi-region phishing campaign suggests data exfiltration intent; pipeline missed detection for abnormal data movement or forwarding rule creation post-compromise
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbox forwarding rule creation by newly-compromised accounts. Alert on unusual cloud-storage uploads or email attachment downloads from compromised mailboxes. Correlate with known TA4922 C2 IP ranges and exfiltration domains.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20230 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Cisco Patches CVE-2026-20230' and 'Exploit Code Goes Public', indicating active exploitation risk. Pipeline failed to generate any detection for exploitation attempts against this specific vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Unified CM ingress for malformed requests, known payload signatures, or HTTP verb anomalies targeting Unified CM APIs or web interfaces. Correlate with failed authentication followed by successful access within short timespan to identify post-exploitation activity.

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM Authentication Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Public exploits targeting Unified CM typically abuse authentication mechanisms. Article describes a patched vulnerability in 'Unified CM' but pipeline generated zero use cases for credential-less or mis-credentialed access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on authentication failures followed by privilege escalation actions (config changes, account creation, admin API calls) within the same session or correlated source IP. Monitor for session tokens issued without corresponding successful login events.

suggestion.title: Unified CM Unauthorized Administrative Action
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of Unified CM typically leads to privilege escalation or lateral movement within the phone system. Pipeline did not suggest detection of post-exploitation persistence or admin-level changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of new administrative accounts, modification of existing admin accounts, changes to device permissions, or installation of software on Unified CM servers without change ticket correlation. Focus on configuration deltas in the 2–4 hours post-patch availability (exploitation window).

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM Process Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Exploit code execution on Unified CM implies RCE capability. Pipeline failed to suggest detection of abnormal process trees, child process execution, or resource consumption anomalies on Unified CM servers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Unified CM process execution for unexpected child processes spawned by Unified CM daemon/service accounts, especially shell interpreters (bash, perl, python) or network utilities. Alert on processes with parent PID mismatches or unusual working directories.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised Unified CM
suggestion.rationale: Unified CM is a critical network appliance with access to internal directory, VoIP protocols, and call data. Article does not detail post-exploitation but pipeline should have anticipated lateral movement risk given the 'exploit code public' context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor egress from Unified CM servers to internal services (LDAP, SMB, SSH, RDP) at unusual times or targeting non-standard hosts. Alert on DNS resolution of internal hostnames from Unified CM context or unexpected SMB shares enumeration.

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM Export or Exfiltration of Call Records
suggestion.rationale: Unified CM stores sensitive call metadata and user credentials. Compromised systems often lead to data collection. Pipeline did not suggest detection of unusual data access or export patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk queries against Unified CM database (CDRs, user configs, device lists) or export of call detail records outside normal maintenance windows. Monitor for database connections from non-standard service accounts or unusual query volume.

suggestion.title: Malicious GitHub Issue Triggers Unauthorized Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states a single 'malicious issue' can 'hijack repositories'—this is the attack's core execution vector. No detection UC exists for suspicious command injection in issue bodies paired with Claude Code GitHub Action execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect issue creation containing shell metacharacters, base64 payloads, or URL-encoded commands in repositories with Claude Code GitHub Action enabled. Correlate with unexpected workflow trigger events in the same 5-minute window.

suggestion.title: GitHub Action Privilege Escalation via Issue Input
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates 'repositories' are 'hijacked'—implying unauthorized operations at the repo level. No UC for detecting Action runtime escalations triggered by untrusted issue data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions logs for repo-level operations (branch protection changes, secret access, workflow modifications, protected branch pushes) executed by GitHub Action identities in response to issue-triggered workflows.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Code Commit via Hijacked Action Identity
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifies repositories are 'hijacked'—commits or file modifications must result. No UC detects code landing in the repo from GitHub Action identities without explicit prior human authorization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on commits to protected branches or sensitive files (src/, .github/workflows/) authored by GitHub Action service identities, especially within 10 minutes of issue creation on the same repo.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Repository Secrets via GitHub Action Context
suggestion.rationale: Hijacked Actions have access to repository secrets and environment variables. Article does not detail credential theft but is the natural post-exploitation step from the described flaw.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect base64-encoded, hex-encoded, or URL-encoded output in GitHub Actions logs; unusual HTTP/DNS exfiltration to external hosts from Action runners; or environment variable names matching known secret patterns (.*TOKEN, .*KEY, .*SECRET) appearing in logs.

suggestion.title: GitHub Workflow Persistence via Action Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Attacker would modify or inject .github/workflows files to ensure persistence. Pipeline omitted detection for workflow file changes triggered by issue-linked Actions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to .github/workflows/ or action.yml files by GitHub Action identities or by users with zero prior commit history to the repo, especially within 15 minutes of issue creation.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Repository Dependency Injection
suggestion.rationale: A compromised repo could poison dependency files (package.json, requirements.txt, go.mod). Article title implies full repository control; downstream consumers would fetch malicious dependencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modifications to package manifest files (package.json, requirements.txt, Gemfile, go.mod, etc.) in public/popular repositories triggered by GitHub Actions within hours of a newly created issue. Cross-reference against known dependency repositories for subsequent poisoning campaigns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Stripe API Customer Record Creation Burst
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Every stolen payment card becomes a fake customer record in the attacker's Stripe account' and describes exfiltration routine 'creating a new Stripe customer object.' Pipeline missed this primary exfiltration mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Stripe API endpoints (POST /v1/customers) for anomalous burst creation patterns. Baseline normal customer creation rates per integration account. Alert on customer records created with metadata fields containing serialized binary/obfuscated data rather than legitimate business information.

suggestion.title: XOR-Obfuscated localStorage Exfiltration to Payment APIs
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states stolen data is 'obfuscated using the XOR operation, and stored locally' then exfiltrated via Stripe API. No detection for this specific obfuscation pattern in browser exfiltration context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect XOR-encoded payloads in network traffic destined to api.stripe.com with characteristic patterns. Correlate localStorage write operations (especially _d_data_customer_ key) followed within 60 seconds by POST/PUT calls to Stripe endpoints with base64/hex-encoded bodies.

suggestion.title: Google Tag Manager Container Executing Stripe-Sourced JavaScript
suggestion.rationale: Article describes payload 'loaded from a Google Tag Manager (GTM) container' that 'reads JavaScript code...from metadata fields of the record, it reassembles and then executes using new Function().' This GTM+Stripe+new Function() execution chain requires dedicated detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for GTM container initialization followed by HTTP GET requests to api.stripe.com/v1/customers/{cus_*}. Flag containers that parse HTTP response metadata fields and pass them to new Function() or eval(). Legitimate GTM should not query Stripe customer objects.

suggestion.title: Firestore Document Access from Checkout Context (braintree-payment-app Pattern)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes variant: 'payload is retrieved from a Firestore document named tracking/captcha in a project called braintree-payment-app.' Firestore exfiltration path with payment-processor-mimicking project names should be explicitly detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Firestore document access from browser/web context to projects with names imitating payment processors (e.g., *braintree*, *stripe*, *payment*). Flag reads from 'tracking/captcha' or 'tracking/*' document paths. Monitor for Firestore collection writes containing serialized credit card metadata.

suggestion.title: Magento Checkout Page Unauthorized Script Execution with Form Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'The card skimmer targets Magento/Adobe Commerce checkout pages and attempts to capture payment data (credit card number, expiration date, CVV code...)' but pipeline did not map this to detection scenarios.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Magento checkout endpoints (/checkout/cart, /checkout/onepage) for unexpected JavaScript execution contexts. Alert on scripts that access HTMLInputElement objects on payment forms followed by exfiltration to non-payment-processor domains. Correlate form data harvesting with API calls to api.stripe.com or Firestore.

suggestion.title: Trusted Payment Domain Abuse for CSP Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes that attackers use api.stripe.com because 'Stores allow that domain by default, so the skimmer slips past Content Security Policy rules and network filters.' This trusted-domain bypass pattern deserves explicit detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for normal api.stripe.com traffic (token creation, charge endpoints). Flag anomalous Stripe API usage: customer record CRUD operations from checkout contexts, metadata-heavy payloads that deviate from payment transaction structure, requests originating from unexpected geolocations relative to account registrant.

suggestion.title: Detect Bulk Data Exfiltration from Customer PII Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article states ShinyHunters 'stolen more than 234 GB of data' containing 'email addresses, full names, phone numbers, government-issued IDs, health insurance information.' Detection should trigger on abnormal volume or velocity of PII extraction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on large-volume outbound network transfers originating from DentaQuest customer-database servers (>100 MB in short windows to external IPs). Pair with database query logs showing bulk SELECT or EXPORT operations on PII tables outside maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthorized Access to Customer Master Data Tables
suggestion.rationale: Breach exposed records for '2.6 million accounts' with specific PII fields. Detection should identify role-anomalous access to centralized customer repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag database queries or system calls from service accounts or user credentials accessing customer PII in patterns inconsistent with job function (e.g., developer accounts querying customer SSNs, batch-job accounts doing row-by-row exports outside scheduled windows).

suggestion.title: Monitor ShinyHunters Leak Site Postings for Organizational Claims
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'ShinyHunters listed the company on its data leak site' following negotiation failure. Threat-actor disclosures are early-warning indicators of compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest known ShinyHunters leak-site feeds (via OSINT or threat-intel partners) and alert when any organization name appears in new breach postings. Cross-correlate with prior compromises to assess breach credibility.

suggestion.title: Detect Anomalous Lateral Movement or Privilege Escalation Post-Breach Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'upon discovery of the initial incident, we took immediate action to secure our environment'—implying initial breach was not immediately detected. Detection should surface credential compromise or suspicious access that may have enabled lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on off-hours or geographic-anomaly authentication events for service accounts or user credentials. Flag failed login attempts followed by successful authentications from the same source within minutes.

suggestion.title: Detect Initial Compromise via Exploitation of Internet-Facing Application
suggestion.rationale: Breach vector unspecified; DentaQuest operates 'programs in 50 states' with customer-facing portals. Exploitation of web apps is common attack vector for healthcare-benefits firms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web-application logs for exploitation attempts (SQL injection, path traversal, RCE payloads targeting common frameworks). Correlate with successful post-auth privilege escalation or access to restricted databases within hours of exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: Detect Data Staging (Compression, Staging Directories) Prior to Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: 234 GB of data required staging before transfer. Attackers typically compress and move data to intermediate locations before exfil.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of large archive files (ZIP, RAR, 7Z) containing database-dump filenames or PII-related keywords. Flag bulk file moves to writable network shares or temp directories followed by network anomalies.

suggestion.title: Domain Homograph Detection - Open-Source Tool Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'fake sites mimicking open-source tools'—this indicates typosquatting or homograph attacks. No detection UC was generated despite this being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on domains registered with names similar to popular open-source projects (Golang, Python, Node.js tools, etc.) with Levenshtein distance < 3 or homograph variants. Correlate with recent registration dates (< 30 days) and suspicious WHOIS profiles.

suggestion.title: Malware Delivery via TDS Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware is delivered 'via TDS' (Traffic Distribution System). Pipeline missed this command-and-control / malware-staging technique entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS traffic to newly registered or spoofed domains serving binary payloads. Alert on user downloads from suspicious domains followed by process creation matching common malware staging patterns.

suggestion.title: Search Engine Result Poisoning - SEO Abuse Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes fake sites 'rank high on Google'—this indicates SEO manipulation or search-result poisoning. No detection for search ranking abuse or crawler metrics anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify domains with high organic search traffic (from referrer logs showing Google) but with low legitimate service history, mismatched domain age vs. authority score, or indicators of link-scheme abuse.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Executable Download from Browser - Malware Delivery Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article implies users download malware after clicking fake sites in search results. No UC for browser-initiated executable downloads from untrusted sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when browser process (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari) downloads an executable (.exe, .msi, .dmg, .deb) from a newly registered domain or IP not in allowlist, especially if downloaded folder shows no prior activity.

suggestion.title: Typosquatting Domain Infrastructure Acquisition
suggestion.rationale: No detection for bulk domain registration patterns used in open-source tool impersonation campaigns—common precursor to this attack type.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect batches of newly registered domains with high similarity to legitimate open-source tool names across multiple registrars, correlated by shared infrastructure (nameservers, hosting provider, WHOIS email).

suggestion.title: Browser Process Child Spawning After Malware Download
suggestion.rationale: No UC for post-download execution chain—the critical indicator that a downloaded file from the fake site was executed maliciously.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious child processes (cmd.exe, PowerShell, bash) spawned by browser processes within 5 minutes of a file download event from untrusted domain, especially if download was of executable type.

suggestion.title: Suspicious APK Installation from Non-Play-Store Source
suggestion.rationale: Article states spyware delivered via 'Fake News, PDF and War Map Apps' — typical Android spyware lures. Pipeline should have flagged APK installation vectors and deceptive package names from the article body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for APK installation attempts (Android InstallReferrer, PackageManager) with package names matching spyware indicators (fake news/map/PDF apps). Flag installs originating from sideload sources rather than official Play Store distribution.

suggestion.title: Command-and-Control Egress Detection for Spyware Callbacks
suggestion.rationale: Spyware 'Asin' implies persistent C2 communications. Article should enumerate IOCs (domains, IPs); pipeline should have proposed callback detection rules. No IOC extraction suggests parsing failure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTPS/HTTP POST callbacks from suspicious APK packages to attacker-controlled domains. Flag periodic beacons (hourly, daily) or large encrypted payloads consistent with data exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Overlay and Accessibility Service Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Android spyware uses UI overlay attacks and accessibility service permissions to intercept user input. Article body unavailable, but targeting Arabic-language users suggests credential theft. Pipeline missed this attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW and ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE permission requests by apps installed from untrusted sources. Flag rapid permission grant sequences post-installation. Correlate with screen-unlock events and keyboard input capture.

suggestion.title: Bulk Contact/SMS/Location Data Exfiltration by Spyware
suggestion.rationale: Spyware targeting Arabic users (geo-political context) implies targeted collection of contact lists, SMS, call logs, and location. Article should specify data-exfiltration IOCs; pipeline produced none.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious read access to /data/data/com.android.contacts and com.android.telephony.provider by non-system packages. Correlate bulk content provider queries with large encrypted network transfers to C2 addresses.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Deployment of Malware to Network Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes Brickstorm deployed to Egnyte Storage Sync and retired Linux archive server, Plenet to Synology NAS. These are high-value persistence points. Article: 'Brickstorm was then deployed to the victim's Egnyte Storage Sync appliance and to a retired Linux GroupWise email archive server' and 'they deployed the custom malware Plenet to a Synology NAS appliance.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious process execution, network connections, or file modifications on network appliances (Synology NAS, Egnyte Storage Sync, retired archive servers, pfSense firewalls) that deviate from baseline administrative activity. Flag child processes spawned by system daemons or unusual listening ports on non-standard services.

suggestion.title: Suspicious SSL VPN Credential Enablement on Firewalls
suggestion.rationale: Attackers used stolen credentials to enable SSL VPN access on victim's firewall. Article: 'attackers used stolen credentials to enable and configure SSL VPN access on the victim's firewall, then connected to internal systems.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor firewall logs for SSL VPN service enablement by non-administrative accounts or from unusual source IPs. Alert on VPN access configuration changes followed by connections to internal systems. Correlate with failed or anomalous credential usage.

suggestion.title: WebSocket-Based C2 Communication from Network Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Brickstorm and Plenet both use WebSocket protocol for C2 communications, which is uncommon malware C2 pattern. Article: 'using the WebSocket protocol for C2 communications and a multiplexing library for simultaneous data streams to the server.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP/WebSocket traffic from non-web servers (appliances, servers) to external domains, especially with established multiplexed connections. Flag WebSocket upgrade requests from unexpected endpoints, particularly from network infrastructure devices.

suggestion.title: Python Reverse Shell Execution with Hardcoded C2 Domain
suggestion.rationale: AgentPSD deployed as fallback persistence mechanism, described as 'Python-based reverse shell utility.' This is a common persistence pattern. Article: 'AgentPSD is a simple Python-based reverse shell utility that Volexity believes VerdantBamboo used as a fallback persistence mechanism.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for python.exe spawning with suspicious command-line arguments (socket, subprocess, base64, reverse shell indicators). Alert on python processes making outbound network connections, especially to non-standard ports or with encoded payloads.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Managed Services Provider Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Attackers compromised MSP's pfSense firewall with BSD variant of Brickstorm, then pivoted to victim organization. This is a trusted-relationship attack vector. Article: 'Volexity found that VerdantBamboo had planted a BSD variant of Brickstorm on a pfSense firewall... pivoted from the MSP into the victim organization's environment.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious outbound connections from MSP-managed infrastructure to client environments that deviate from known management channels. Alert on unusual patterns of administrative access from MSP IP ranges to client networks, especially after baseline changes on MSP-controlled appliances.

suggestion.title: Infrastructure Takedown/Indicator Removal Following Detection
suggestion.rationale: After researchers identified C2 infrastructure fingerprint, threat actor took all servers offline within 5-day window. This evasion tactic indicates awareness of investigation. Article: 'Between September 18 and September 23, all of the servers previously matching this pattern turned off their services on port 443.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate C2 domain/IP indicators published in threat reports with prior network traffic. Flag sudden, coordinated takedown of known C2 infrastructure (multiple IPs/domains going offline simultaneously). Alert on any-to-any traffic patterns to those indicators post-publication to identify previously undetected beacons.

suggestion.title: Detect POST requests with Content-Encoding: deflate to Serv-U
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'specially crafted POST requests that crash the Serv-U service without authentication using Content-Encoding: deflate.' This is the exact exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS proxies and network sensors for POST requests targeting Serv-U services (ports 80, 443, 2121) carrying Content-Encoding: deflate headers. Legitimate Serv-U requests do not require this encoding per vendor guidance.

suggestion.title: Detect Serv-U service crash or unexpected restart
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacks 'crash the Serv-U service.' Impact must be detectable on the endpoint via service termination or restart events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected termination or restart of Serv-U process (serv-u.exe on Windows, serv-u on Linux). Correlate with timing of suspicious POST requests to establish causality.

suggestion.title: Detect reconnaissance scans for Serv-U CVE-2026-28318 exploitation
suggestion.rationale: CISA flagged as 'actively exploited in the wild.' Attackers will probe external perimeter; article mentions 12,000+ instances exposed on Shodan, implying scanning is happening.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of POST requests with Content-Encoding: deflate across multiple external IPs or rapid-fire requests to a single Serv-U endpoint, indicating active scanning or exploitation campaigns.

suggestion.title: Identify unpatched Serv-U installations (version < 15.5.4 Hotfix 1)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'SolarWinds released Serv-U 15.5.4 Hotfix 1 on Thursday to patch this denial-of-service vulnerability.' Enumeration of vulnerable versions is critical for asset inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query endpoint software inventory for Serv-U versions below 15.5.4. Cross-reference with patch management to identify systems not yet updated. Flag for urgent remediation per CISA BOD 22-01 deadline (June 19).

suggestion.title: Monitor for HTTP 500 or service errors following deflate POST requests
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of the resource-consumption flaw would produce characteristic error responses or service unavailability before a full crash.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate POST requests with Content-Encoding: deflate to Serv-U with subsequent HTTP 500 errors, connection timeouts, or rapid drop in legitimate traffic to the service.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U POST with deflate Content-Encoding
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector: 'specially crafted POST requests using the Content-Encoding: deflate header' — this is the precise exploitation signature and a direct detection opportunity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST requests to SolarWinds Serv-U listening ports with Content-Encoding: deflate header. Correlate with service availability or restart logs to confirm impact. No authentication required, making this detectable on external-facing instances.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U Service Crash or Restart
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows...to crash the Serv-U service' — service crashes are directly observable in application logs, event logs, and monitoring platforms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Serv-U service unexpected termination or rapid restart cycles. Establish baseline for service uptime and flag deviations. Cross-reference with POST request anomalies from same source IP/subnet.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-28318 Vulnerable Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status confirms active exploitation 'in the wild'; article references 'federal due-date 2026-06-19'. Standard vulnerability presence hunt for unpatched Serv-U instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner (Nessus, Qualys, etc.) for CVE-2026-28318 matches. Cross-reference with firewall/network discovery to confirm Internet-facing Serv-U instances. Prioritize remediation against 2026-06-19 federal due date.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Serv-U Service Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article notes exploitation 'without authentication' — absence of auth requirement is an access control failure enabling external reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for scanning activity targeting Serv-U ports (typical: 22, 990, 991) from untrusted networks. Deflate-header POST requests from IPs with no prior authentication context are high-fidelity indicators.

suggestion.title: Malicious CSV File Upload to SD-WAN Manager Home Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker uploads crafted CSV file: 'attacker could exploit this vulnerability by uploading a crafted file' and log shows path /home/admin/malicious.csv
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SD-WAN Manager for unusual file uploads to /home/admin/ with CSV extension, particularly correlated with vScript process spawning. Alert on CSV files containing suspicious command patterns or shell metacharacters.

suggestion.title: vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh Execution with Suspicious Arguments
suggestion.rationale: Article provides explicit log signature showing command injection vector: '/usr/bin/vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh -cli path /home/admin/malicious.csv' — suspicious .csv argument and unusual path parameter
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh is invoked with CSV file paths in arguments, especially those not matching expected deployment configs. Correlate with preceding file upload events.

suggestion.title: Tenant Configuration Upload to vSmart Controller Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack chain requires 'exploitation of CVE-2026-20182 or CVE-2026-20127' followed by tenant data upload; log entry references 'Tenant list upload per vsmart serial number'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences where auth-bypass exploitation (CVE-2026-20182/20127 indicators) is followed within minutes by tenant configuration uploads to vSmart controllers. Alert on uploads with non-standard serial number patterns or from unexpected internal hosts.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Configuration Changes Pushed to Edge Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Cisco has observed limited cases where the exploitation of this bug resulted in a configuration change pushed to edge devices' — indicates lateral movement/impact phase
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for configuration pushes to Catalyst edge devices originating from compromised SD-WAN Manager instances. Flag pushes that occur outside maintenance windows or correlate with vScript command injection activity.

suggestion.title: /var/log/scripts.log vScript Tenant Upload Activity
suggestion.rationale: Cisco provided explicit IOC: 'check their SD-WAN /var/log/scripts.log file for attempts to upload tenant configuration data to vSmart controllers' — concrete log source and attack indicator
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search /var/log/scripts.log for entries containing 'vScript: Tenant list upload' combined with vSmart controller IP or serial number references. Pattern match on vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh execution with -cli and path arguments.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass Chain to Privilege Escalation (CVE-2026-20182 → CVE-2026-20245)
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploit requires 'valid credentials or exploitation of CVE-2026-20182 or CVE-2026-20127' as prerequisite; these are critical auth bypasses enabling the command injection chain
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create detection chain: flag CVE-2026-20182 exploitation indicators (auth bypass attempt patterns), then monitor same source IPs for subsequent netadmin privilege use or suspicious file uploads within 5-minute window.

suggestion.title: Phishing Site Masquerading as FIFA World Cup Ticketing
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Fake Sites' and 'Stolen Logins' — phishing infrastructure mimicking legitimate FIFA World Cup 2026 ticket vendors. Pipeline generated zero IOCs or detections for this initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS requests and HTTP connections to domains containing 'fifa', 'world cup', '2026', 'ticket', 'qualify', or similar keywords combined with suspicious TLDs (.tk, .ml, fresh registrations <30 days). Flag user clicks on external phishing links from emails mentioning World Cup events in security awareness telemetry.

suggestion.title: Banking Malware Execution via World Cup Lure
suggestion.rationale: Article headline references 'Banking Malware' but pipeline extracted no techniques, no process execution patterns, no IOCs. No detection use case for malware delivery chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious process trees where user double-clicks archived attachment (ZIP, RAR) from phishing email containing World Cup lure, spawning execution of executable or script. Flag process injection into legitimate banking applications (browser, banking software) from suspicious parent processes.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Fake Banking Login Pages
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'Stolen Logins' and 'Banking Malware' — indicates credential phishing via fake login forms. Pipeline identified zero credential access techniques or detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify user submissions of credentials to non-banking domains. Detect HTTPS POST requests to phishing domains containing patterns like 'login', 'authenticate', 'verify', 'confirm', or credential field names (username, password, pin, otp). Correlate with simultaneous legitimate banking login within 5 minutes (failed auth attempt → redirect to phishing → credential entry).

suggestion.title: Command and Control Callbacks from Banking Malware
suggestion.rationale: Banking malware requires C2 communication for command execution and data exfiltration. Article references 'Banking Malware' but pipeline generated no C2 detection logic or IOC extraction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections from processes executing from user temp/downloads folders to non-whitelisted external IPs/domains. Flag unexpected HTTP/HTTPS POST requests from banking malware processes exfiltrating stolen credentials, session tokens, or banking data to remote servers.

suggestion.title: Domain Registration Pattern: World Cup Phishing Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Threat actors register lookalike domains for FIFA World Cup to host phishing/malware. Pipeline extracted zero domain IOCs despite article explicitly mentioning 'Fake Sites'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query threat intelligence feeds and WHOIS for recent domain registrations containing 'fifa', 'worldcup2026', 'qualify', 'ticket' with registration dates within 90 days before article publication. Flag domains with identical or near-identical SSL certificates to legitimate FIFA domains. Cross-reference with URLhaus, PhishTank for reported phishing pages.

suggestion.title: Anomalous File Download and Execution from World Cup Themed Email
suggestion.rationale: Malware delivery mechanism combines social engineering (World Cup event) with executable attachment. Pipeline failed to model the attachment → download → execution chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with World Cup/sporting event keywords and archived attachments (ZIP, RAR, 7Z) containing executable or script files. Flag users who extract and execute these files within minutes. Alert if process spawning indicators align with known banking malware families (memory injection, browser hooking, credential dumping).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Authentication Followed by Root Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Any user with valid DbGate credentials can execute arbitrary OS commands as root.' Pipeline omitted detection of authentication anomalies (failed login attempts, lateral auth from unusual IP/time) immediately preceding RCE. Missing initial-access pairing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate DbGate failed authentication events or successful logins from anomalous geography/time with subsequent high-privilege process spawning (EUID=0) within 60 seconds. Attacker may brute-force credentials before exploiting loadReader endpoint.

suggestion.title: Dynamic import() Function Calls in Node.js Request Context
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'The require = null mitigation is trivially bypassed via dynamic import().' No UC hunts the actual attack vector—JavaScript dynamic import patterns in request handlers. This is the core exploit technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Node.js application logs and WAF request payloads for import() calls, Function() constructors, eval() invocations, or child_process references appearing in HTTP request context to POST /runners/* endpoints. Flag payloads containing newlines/encodings (\n, %0A) suggesting multi-statement injection.

suggestion.title: Service Account–to–Root Privilege Escalation Spike
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RCE executing 'as root.' Attackers escalate from DbGate service account (likely non-privileged) to root via exploited endpoint. No UC hunts for process-parent privilege-level transitions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process spawned by non-root service account (e.g., _dbgate, www-data, nobody) that immediately spawns or modifies process with IntegrityLevel=SYSTEM or UID=0. Focus on child_process calls within 5 seconds of initial RCE.

suggestion.title: Configuration/Credential File Access from RCE Shell
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'execute arbitrary OS commands as root.' No UC hunts post-RCE data exfiltration (credential harvesting, config theft). Attackers would read /root/.dbgate, /etc/shadow, database creds, SSH keys.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file-read operations from shell processes (sh, bash, python) spawned post-RCE, targeting sensitive paths: /root/.*, /etc/shadow, /etc/passwd, database config directories, SSH keys. Pair with outbound network egress from node/DbGate process for exfiltration detection.

suggestion.title: DbGate Installation Directory Modification (Persistence)
suggestion.rationale: Article: RCE runs 'as root' with arbitrary command execution. No UC hunts persistence mechanisms (e.g., modifying DbGate startup, installing systemd backdoors, modifying app config).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for file creates/modifications to DbGate installation paths (/app/packages/api/*, /dbgate/*, /opt/dbgate/*) or system startup mechanisms (systemd units, cron, init.d) with timestamp immediately after RCE shell spawning. Suspicious parents: bash/sh spawned from node.

suggestion.title: Nested Command Execution via Child Process API
suggestion.rationale: Article: attacker injects code calling 'child_process' and 'execSync' methods. No UC specifically hunts for child_process module usage patterns from web request context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Node.js process-spawn syscalls (execve, clone, fork) initiated by HTTP request threads within DbGate API service. Correlate request timestamp to /runners/load-reader with process-spawn events appearing in the same microsecond window. Flag arbitrary shell invocations (bash, sh, cmd.exe) with unconstrained arguments.

suggestion.title: Shopper: User deletion or role creation by non-admin account
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Any authenticated panel user could load the page and use its public actions to create new roles and delete other users, including administrators.' — application logs must capture privilege escalation when non-privileged accounts execute admin actions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Shopper audit logs for user deletion or role creation events where the acting user account lacks admin/owner role. Correlate account's assigned roles against action permissions. Critical: flag deletion of administrator accounts by standard users.

suggestion.title: Shopper: Permission mapping changes without authorization
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Settings/Team/RolePermission gated its write actions on the read-only view_users permission' — modifications to role-permission associations by accounts lacking permission-management privileges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect write operations to role_permission records where the acting account does not hold the edit_role_permissions or admin capability. Focus on changes to sensitive permissions (user_deletion, role_creation, account_management).

suggestion.title: Shopper: HTTP 200 to /settings/team/* from non-team-member accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Settings/Team/Index had no mount() authorization.' — successful HTTP access to team-settings pages by accounts lacking explicit team-admin role or team membership.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference HTTP 200 responses to /settings/team/* endpoints with user's assigned roles and team memberships. Baseline: only team admins + members should reach HTTP 200; all other users should receive 403 Forbidden or redirect. HTTP 200 for non-members indicates authorization bypass.

suggestion.title: WordPress Plugin RCE Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Exploit Critical...Flaw to Take Over Sites'—direct evidence of RCE via plugin. No use case generated despite this being the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST/GET requests to /wp-content/plugins/everest-forms/* endpoints with payloads characteristic of RCE attempts (shell metacharacters, PHP evaluation patterns, script tags). Correlate with 4xx→2xx transitions indicating exploitation success.

suggestion.title: Everest Forms Pro Post-Exploitation Admin Creation
suggestion.rationale: 'Take Over Sites' implies post-RCE lateral privilege escalation. No detection for admin account creation or privilege escalation post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect wp_users table INSERT or UPDATE for user_role='administrator' events occurring shortly after suspicious HTTP activity to the plugin folder. Baseline on admin creation frequency by site.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Upload via Everest Forms Handler
suggestion.rationale: Plugin RCE typically leads to web shell placement for persistence. Article describes takeover capability but no detection for shell upload/execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /wp-content/plugins/everest-forms/ and /wp-content/uploads/ for unexpected .php, .phtml, .phar file creation post-exploit window. Alert on execution (apache/nginx process spawning with new .php files as argument).

suggestion.title: Everest Forms Database Exfiltration Query
suggestion.rationale: Plugin RCE can query arbitrary database. No detection for data exfiltration behavior that 'site takeover' would entail (credentials, customer data, etc.).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on large SELECT * FROM wp_users, wp_usermeta, wp_postmeta queries originating from the plugin execution context. Pair with outbound data volume anomalies from the compromised WordPress server in the post-exploit window.

suggestion.title: Python Package Installation — Typosquatting Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack vector: 'parsimonius' mimicking 'parsimonious' with 'single missing letter.' Pipeline generated zero use cases for package-name similarity despite this being the delivery mechanism affecting 'thousands of developers.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor pip install for package names with Levenshtein distance ≤2 from known legitimate libraries. Alert on installation of near-duplicate package names. Cross-reference installed packages against typosquatting watchlists and new PyPI publishers.

suggestion.title: File Hash Detection — Known Malicious Package
suggestion.rationale: SHA1 a01c2a21f24db63cb01a67016519aebeca438089 provided in IOC section but not extracted by pipeline (output empty). Standard file-hash endpoint detection absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hash .py, .pyc, .pyd files in site-packages. Alert on SHA1 a01c2a21f24db63cb01a67016519aebeca438089. Maintain daily IOC feed updates with known-malicious package hashes.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise — PyPI Repository Threat
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malicious package quietly made its way into PyPI repository' before removal. Kill chain was empty; this is T1195 initial-access compromise requiring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTPS traffic to pypi.org for unusual batch package downloads outside deployment windows. Alert on new packages flagged by threat intel. Block based on publisher reputation and account age.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Execution — Runtime Code Surveillance
suggestion.rationale: Article implies malicious code executes upon import, 'putting thousands at risk.' No execution-phase detection for import-time side effects or suspicious subprocess/network activity from Python processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor child process creation and DNS/HTTP from python.exe immediately after suspicious package imports. Alert on unexpected subprocess spawning or outbound connections from pip install or Jupyter contexts.

suggestion.title: Cryptominer Registry Persistence via Installer
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies payload as 'cryptominer' but does not detail persistence mechanism. Standard practice for cryptominers is Registry modification for autostart (T1547.001) or scheduled task. Article phrase: 'distributing an unexpected executable file alongside its legitimate installer' — cryptominers must survive reboot. Hunt for registry/run-key modifications by installer or me.exe process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modification of HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run or HKCU equivalents during Hola installer execution or by me.exe process. Cryptominers require autostart for impact.

suggestion.title: Cryptominer Network Beacon Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies payload is 'cryptominer' but omits C2/mining pool communication. Cryptominers must exfiltrate mining results and receive work (T1041). Hunt for outbound connections from me.exe to known mining pools or unusual external IPs with sustained connectivity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sustained outbound TCP/UDP connections from me.exe process to non-standard ports (typically 7777-9999, or HTTPS to unknown domains). Filter for connection duration >5min and high byte transfer rates typical of mining pool communication.

suggestion.title: Hola Browser Installer Hash Mismatch Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article premise is 'delivery pipeline compromised' — the installer itself is malicious or tampered. Hunt for Hola Browser installer with unexpected file hash compared to known-good versions from official sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect installation of Hola Browser (setup.exe, installer) with SHA256 matching the IOC hashes provided in article. Correlate with download source (if not from official hola.org domain). Flag as compromised supply chain.

suggestion.title: Unusual File Alongside Legitimate Installer
suggestion.rationale: Article states me.exe was 'distributed alongside' the legitimate installer — spatial/temporal co-location. Hunt for any executable written to same directory or extracted from same archive as known Hola installer during installation window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation events (me.exe or similar executables) in %TEMP%, %AppData%\Local\Temp, or Program Files\Hola directory within 60 seconds before/after Hola installer execution. Flag if created by system process rather than user action.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Installer Execution from Non-Standard Source
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'compromised delivery pipeline' — the installer should originate from official channels. Hunt for Hola Browser installer downloaded from non-standard URLs or with unusual download parent process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect download of Hola Browser installer (setup.exe, hola_installer*.exe) from domains other than official hola.org, mirrors, or known CDNs. Flag unusual referrers or unusual user-agents (e.g., wmi, powershell instead of browser).

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Installation from Known Threat List
suggestion.rationale: Article title identifies 'IronWorm and New Miasma Worm Variant' as npm supply chain threats. No detection rule generated for identifying installation of these or related malicious packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install, yarn add, pnpm install commands. Cross-reference package names against threat-intel feeds for IronWorm, Miasma, and related malicious npm packages. Alert on installations from non-standard registries or by unexpected user/service accounts.

suggestion.title: Code Execution via npm Postinstall/Preinstall Lifecycle Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain worms execute via package manager hooks during installation—article mentions 'Worm Variant' indicating self-propagating code. No detection rule for malicious script execution in npm lifecycle events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on shell (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash) child processes spawned from npm.cmd or node.exe during package installation context. Flag execution of curl/wget/python to retrieve and run remote code during postinstall phase.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Outbound Connections from node.js During Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Worms establish C2 during installation. Article describes attack but no use case generated for detecting command-and-control traffic or data exfiltration from npm processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound HTTP/HTTPS or DNS from node.exe/npm.exe to newly-registered or suspicious domains during npm install timeframe. Correlate against known C2 infrastructure lists and malware sinkhole feeds.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Modification of package.json or .npmrc Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Malware may modify package manifests to add dependencies, establish persistence, or route future installs through compromised registries. No file-integrity rule generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file writes to package.json, .npmrc, .yarnrc outside legitimate package manager operations. Alert on addition of suspicious dependencies, changes to npm registry URLs, or modifications by unexpected users.

suggestion.title: Extraction and Execution of Binaries from npm Package node_modules
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain malware bundles native executables or archives within packages for obfuscation and evasion. No detection for payload extraction or execution from node_modules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor extraction of .exe, .bin, .so, .zip, .tar from node_modules/ or npm cache directories followed by process spawning. Flag npm packages containing binary or archive files in atypical directories.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized npm Registry Publishing or Account Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Worms may republish themselves or trojanize legitimate packages to propagate laterally. No detection for npm publish or registry authentication anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm publish, npm login, or yarn publish commands from unexpected accounts or machines. Alert on publishing of packages with typosquatted names or sudden version bumps to popular packages.

suggestion.title: Extension-driven data exfiltration to C2 domain
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states extensions 'secretly harvesting those conversations and sending them off' to external C2. No exfiltration detection was proposed. Core attack step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Browser process (chrome.exe, msedge.exe) initiates outbound connection to deepaichats.com or chatsaigpt.com with encrypted payload; flag sustained C2 communication or large data volumes within hours of extension installation.

suggestion.title: Extension DOM scraping — large data reads from protected pages
suggestion.rationale: Extension harvests AI platform conversations (ChatGPT, Claude DOM content). Article: 'harvesting those conversations.' DOM access via content scripts is invisible to traditional process-level monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor extension JavaScript execution for repeated DOM queries to AI service iframes/divs (contenteditable divs, message containers); correlate with egress to C2.

suggestion.title: Malicious extension — manifest permissions overprivilege or C2 hardcoding
suggestion.rationale: Extensions must declare broad permissions (all_urls or specific AI domains) to intercept/harvest conversations. Manifest inspection was not suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extension manifest.json declares all_urls permission, *://*/* pattern, or contains hardcoded C2 domain strings; inspect at install time via file enumeration of browser extension directories.

suggestion.title: Browser extension network beaconing — suspicious domain resolution post-install
suggestion.rationale: C2 communication from extension process. Article mentions 'sending them off' to external command-and-control servers. No network IOC hunt was generated despite 2 domains being present.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: DNS resolution or TLS/HTTP connection from browser process to deepaichats.com or chatsaigpt.com following suspicious extension installation; timeline-correlate to establish causality.

suggestion.title: Asset exposure - DD-WRT devices vulnerable to UPnP stack overflow CVEs
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploit targets 'known vulnerability in DD-WRT router firmware' — 'stack buffer overflow flaw in the UPnP service' without credentials. This is the precursor attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on network assets running DD-WRT firmware versions matching CVE-2021-27137, CVE-2015-2051, CVE-2022-35914, CVE-2016-15047, CVE-2025-34054. Correlate asset inventory against public DD-WRT security advisories and patch status.

suggestion.title: C2 callback detection - connections to C0XMO infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies three IPs as infrastructure used by the botnet. The article emphasizes 'modular propagation' implying sustained command and control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from Linux/router-class devices to 85.215.131.70, 217.160.125.125, 176.100.37.91 over any port. Prioritize connections from UPnP services or early-stage processes. Monitor for DNS queries resolving to these IPs.

suggestion.title: Modular payload installation - SHA256 file hash matching
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references 12 distinct SHA256 hashes with emphasis on 'modular propagation' — indicating multi-stage infection chain with separate components.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation, download, or execution of any file matching the 12 provided SHA256 hashes. Prioritize detection in /tmp, /var, or root-writable directories on Linux devices.

suggestion.title: Network scanning for replica propagation targets
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'modular propagation across multiple Linux architectures' — botnet must perform active scanning to identify and exploit additional vulnerable routers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect network scanning tools (nmap, masscan, custom probes) spawned from compromised router processes. Flag multiple connection attempts to port 49152/TCP (UPnP) across subnet ranges. Correlate with failed UPnP exploit signatures.

suggestion.title: Router persistence via cron and init script modification
suggestion.rationale: Gafgyt family historically persists via cron/init — modular design implies need to re-infect on reboot. No narrative detail but expected for botnet family.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected modifications to /etc/cron.d, /etc/rc.d, /etc/init.d on DD-WRT systems. Flag suspicious symlinks in startup directories or unexpected processes spawned by cron daemon targeting remote downloads.

suggestion.title: Secondary payload staging and download behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'modular' design with 12 hashes but provides no details on deployment flow. Multi-component malware typically downloads stages post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/S requests with suspicious User-Agents from UPnP/system processes on Linux routers. Detect file write attempts following inbound network activity. Correlate DNS requests for file-delivery domains with subsequent SHA256 hash execution.

suggestion.title: Credit Card Data in Network Exfiltration to Firebase/Cloud Storage
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'stolen card data' dumped via Stripe using Firebase endpoint. Article phrase: 'Stripe, the widely used online payment service, as both its command center and its data dump.' Need detection for PII/card data in outbound flows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound traffic containing credit card number patterns (Luhn-validated), CVV, or cardholder data matching to non-standard Stripe endpoints, Firebase Realtime Database instances (*.firebaseio.com), or unexpected cloud infrastructure. Correlate with payment processing servers as source.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Stripe API Credential Extraction or Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Attacker must steal or create Stripe API credentials to use Stripe as C2. Article phrase: 'uses Stripe...as both its command center and its data dump.' Detect credential compromise enabling this abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Stripe API key extraction, unauthorized Stripe SDK authentication, or bulk Stripe API calls (payouts, refunds, balance reads, charge queries) from non-standard source IPs, user agents, or authentication chains. Alert on API keys found in process memory or logs.

suggestion.title: Malicious JavaScript Injection into Payment Forms (Magecart)
suggestion.rationale: Magecart attacks inject malicious client-side JavaScript into e-commerce checkout pages. Article phrase: 'malware...hiding inside...payment platforms.' This is the execution vector for client-side card harvesting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized modification or injection of JavaScript on payment checkout pages (file integrity monitoring, CDN/script source anomalies). Alert on payment form pages serving scripts from attacker-controlled or Firebase domains. Monitor for script DOM manipulation targeting card input fields.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise — Malicious Stripe/Payment SDK Update
suggestion.rationale: Magecart typically compromises third-party payment libraries, SDKs, or integrations. Article phrase: 'hidden inside one of the most trusted payment platforms.' Attacker likely poisoned a payment processing dependency.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected or unauthorized updates/modifications to Stripe SDKs, payment processing libraries, and checkout JavaScript components. Alert on code changes not corresponding to official releases, unsigned script modifications, or dependency downloads from non-official sources.

suggestion.title: Stripe Webhook Registration to Attacker-Controlled Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Using Stripe as C2 likely involves registering malicious webhooks or modifying webhook endpoints to exfiltrate stolen data or receive commands. Article phrase: 'command center and data dump' implies bidirectional data flow via Stripe.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Stripe API logs for unauthorized webhook creation, modification of webhook URLs to non-standard ports/IPs, or callbacks to Firebase/external cloud storage. Alert on webhooks pointing to private IP ranges, attacker IPs identified in threat feeds, or suspicious cloud service endpoints.

suggestion.title: Input Capture on Payment Forms — Credit Card Field Interaction
suggestion.rationale: Injected JavaScript harvests card data by monitoring form field interactions. Article phrase: 'credit card skimming malware...stolen card data.' Detection must trigger on abnormal form-field monitoring code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on JavaScript code in payment pages that attaches event listeners to payment input fields (oninput, onchange, onkeypress, onfocus). Flag suspicious key-logging behavior, card data regex patterns in memory, or script exfiltration of form values to non-whitelisted domains.

suggestion.title: IIS Web Shell File Creation via Unusual Extension Drop
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'custom web shell framework' as the attack vector. Pipeline should detect ASPX, ASHX, or JSP files written to IIS directories (e.g. wwwroot, inetpub). Title states this is the core persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious file creation in IIS application directories with extensions .aspx, .ashx, .jsp with low frequency prevalence or obfuscated names. Correlate with IIS application pool identity to detect out-of-band file placement.

suggestion.title: IIS Process Spawning PowerShell or cmd.exe Post-Web Access
suggestion.rationale: Web shells typically execute commands via PowerShell or cmd. Article describes custom framework suggesting post-exploitation command execution. Gap: no detection rule for IIS→shell spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when w3wp.exe or iisexpress.exe spawns powershell.exe, cmd.exe, or rundll32.exe. Filter for known legitimate IIS extensions (app compilation, diagnostic scripts) but maintain low threshold for child process creation outside scheduled maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Anomalous HTTP POST/PUT to IIS Followed by File System Modification
suggestion.rationale: Web shell upload sequence: HTTP POST to IIS + file drop to disk. Article mentions IIS targeting, implying web-accessible endpoints. Pipeline missed this execution-to-persistence chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate IIS access logs showing POST/PUT requests to suspicious paths (.aspx, .config, .ashx uploads) with subsequent file creation events in inetpub or application root within 5-second window. Exclude known application update processes.

suggestion.title: IIS Application Pool Accessing Registry or WMI Unexpectedly
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation web shells often enumerate system via WMI (T1047) or registry (T1012). Title implies custom framework suggesting lateral movement/discovery post-shell. No detection for privilege escalation or C2 setup via IIS process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when IIS worker processes (w3wp.exe) invoke WMI queries, access HKLM registry hives, or execute wmic.exe / powershell Get-WmiObject. Correlate with suspicious child processes or outbound network activity.

suggestion.title: Outbound HTTPS from IIS Process to Non-Microsoft Domains
suggestion.rationale: Web shells establish C2 callbacks. Title mentions custom framework (implying attacker control). No detection for command-and-control traffic from web server.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTPS outbound from w3wp.exe or iisexpress.exe to destinations outside established Microsoft/CDN IP space. Prioritize rare or newly-seen domains; correlate with POST/PUT activity timestamps from same server.

suggestion.title: Compressed or Encrypted Data Transfer from IIS to External Host
suggestion.rationale: Web shells exfiltrate data or receive staged payloads. Article's 'custom framework' language suggests multi-stage operations. Missing exfiltration/C2 staging detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on high-entropy outbound traffic (gzip, encryption signatures) from IIS processes to rare/new domains, or large data transfers (>100 MB) from application pool identity in short windows.

suggestion.title: Unusual SMTP Outbound from Cloud Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article states 230 cloud servers were 'hijacked for covert SMTP relay network'—instances normally handling non-mail workloads would not initiate SMTP connections on ports 25, 465, 587 to external domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cloud instance egress for SMTP ports (25, 465, 587) to external IPs, especially from non-mail-server instance types (compute, database, app-tier). Cloud-native approach: filter CloudTrail for EC2/GCP/Azure network policy changes allowing outbound SMTP that violate baseline.

suggestion.title: Mail Service Installation on Non-Mail Cloud Instances
suggestion.rationale: To establish SMTP relay, attackers must install or enable mail relay software (Postfix, Exim, SendGrid, etc.) on compromised instances. Article phrase 'hijacks servers for covert SMTP relay' implies software deployment or configuration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution or package installation (apt, yum, npm) of mail relays (postfix, exim, sendmail, nodejs smtp libraries) on instances not tagged/classified as mail infrastructure. Cross-reference instance metadata (instance type, application tag) to baseline.

suggestion.title: Cloud Instance Credential Compromise or Unauthorized Root/Admin Access
suggestion.rationale: Hijacking 230 instances across three cloud providers suggests either mass credential compromise or exploitation of a shared vulnerability. Article implies unauthorized administrative access to deploy relay software.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for spike in failed then successful authentication attempts on cloud instances; unusual geographic/IP origins of successful logins; root/admin activity creating new users or SSH keys; changes to security groups/network policies enabling inbound administrative access from unusual sources.

suggestion.title: Cloud API Anomalies: Mass Instance Modification or Metadata Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Deploying SMTP relay to 230 instances likely involved bulk API operations—instance reconfiguration, security group rule additions, or cloud-init script injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk ModifyInstanceAttribute, CreateSecurityGroup, or AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress calls in short timeframe; RunInstances with suspicious user-data scripts; GCP operations on compute instances in patterns inconsistent with deployment baseline; Azure runCommand or CustomScript extensions executed on multiple VMs.

suggestion.title: SMTP Relay C2 Domain Communication from Cloud Instances
suggestion.rationale: Relay network 'hijacked for covert SMTP' implies attacker-controlled C2 or relay coordination domain. Instances must communicate with attacker infrastructure to receive phishing/spam targets or relay policy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate DNS queries from compromised instance IPs to known C2 or free-domain registrars; monitor for DNS beaconing patterns; alert on HTTP/HTTPS to attacker-controlled domains from non-web-server instances; monitor cloud instance DNS/HTTP logs for communication to relay aggregation domains.
