suggestion.title: Lateral Movement / Privilege Escalation Across Cloud Tenant or Project
suggestion.rationale: Compromising 230 instances across distinct cloud accounts/projects implies cross-tenant lateral movement or a shared identity/SSO compromise enabling privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for service account token abuse (AssumeRole, AssumeServiceAccount) across projects; unusual cross-account CloudTrail activity; GCP service account activity in unexpected projects; Azure cross-subscription role assignments; unexpected API calls from single identities spanning multiple environments.

suggestion.title: Agentic AI Malicious Code Generation in CI/CD
suggestion.rationale: Article focuses on 'Claude Code GitHub action' security; no UC was generated for detecting AI agents creating suspicious code patterns, unusual imports, or obfuscated payloads injected into repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions logs and local workflow executions for unusual code generation patterns, suspicious variable names, API calls to install malicious dependencies, or script content that differs from historical agent behavior. Flag when generated code contains credential enumeration, exfiltration logic, or persistence mechanisms.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized GitHub Secrets Access by Agentic Workflows
suggestion.rationale: Article implicit threat: compromised AI agent reading CI/CD secrets. No UC for detecting bulk enumeration or misuse of repository credentials outside expected contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Trigger when a single GitHub Actions run accesses >3 distinct secrets, requests secrets not referenced in the workflow definition, or attempts to export/read secrets in commands outside the official secretManager API. Correlate secret access timing with unusual agent behavior.

suggestion.title: Suspicious GitHub Workflow Modification by AI
suggestion.rationale: Article threat model: agentic system modifying CI/CD pipelines. No detection for unusual .github/workflows file changes that expand permissions, add new runtime actions, or inject external script downloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag commits to .github/workflows/ that: (a) increase permissions from read-only to write/admin, (b) add external action calls from newly-registered orgs/users, (c) inject curl/wget to untrusted domains, or (d) disable branch protection checks. Pair with committer identity anomalies (AI service account making unusual edits).

suggestion.title: Repository Credential Lateral Movement via Agent
suggestion.rationale: Article's implicit attack surface: AI agent obtaining deploy keys or GITHUB_TOKEN and using it outside intended CI context. No UC for detecting cross-repository secret reuse or out-of-band credential usage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GITHUB_TOKEN or deploy key usage from non-GitHub IP ranges, unusual frequency of API calls to list/access private repos, or credential reuse across unrelated repositories. Correlate with GitHub Actions job IP context.

suggestion.title: AI-Generated Dependency Injection via Package Manager
suggestion.rationale: Attack surface implicit in agentic CI/CD: malicious package installation or manifest modification. Pipeline missed detection for unusual dependency resolution or supply-chain compromise via dependency scripts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm/pip/cargo install operations in CI workflows for: (a) packages added by agent without corresponding requirement file edit, (b) install hooks executing unusual commands, (c) version pinning removed to allow pre-release/malicious versions, or (d) mirror/registry changes from default. Flag when package metadata and execution diverge.

suggestion.title: Malicious polyfill[.]io Domain Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'starting in late May 2026, the polyfill[.]io domain became active again and started responding with HTTP 401 authentication requests.' This is a directly-named, actionable malicious domain IOC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any DNS resolution to polyfill[.]io or HTTP/HTTPS traffic to that domain. Cross-reference with website source code to identify pages still embedding the legacy domain. Flag as supply-chain indicator: domain confirmed malicious in 2024 (Chinese entity injection) and May 2026 (HTTP 401 abuse).

suggestion.title: HTTP 401 Authentication Prompts from External CDN Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'User browsers visiting pages such as Toshiba's and MUJI's interpret that as a request for a username and password, so they serve a login prompt'—HTTP 401 responses from untrusted external domains abused as phishing vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP 401 Unauthorized responses originating from external CDN or third-party domains in web proxy logs. Correlate response source with page script inclusions. Alert on 401 from domains outside authorized identity-provider whitelist (Auth0, Okta, internal IdP, etc.). Credential-harvesting indicator.

suggestion.title: Unremediatedlacy Polyfill.io Script Includes Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'some sites using the service failed to clean all their pages over the past two years, so remnants of Polyfill code remained'—supply-chain risk persistence via un-removed malicious script dependencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Source-code analysis for script includes from polyfill[.]io or legacy polyfill domain variants. Identify pages that load external JavaScript from the compromised CDN. Flag as supply-chain technical debt and re-exploitation risk.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Authentication Prompts on Unauthenticated Pages
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'suspicious sign-in screens popping up on their websites could collect credentials' on non-login pages (Toshiba homepage, Muji storefront). Anomalous authentication behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on authentication dialog/prompts (HTTP 401, JavaScript window.alert for login) appearing on pages that should not require authentication. Correlate with external script sources (CDN domains). Credential-interception indicator.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Attack Infrastructure Re-Activation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the domain was purchased by a Chinese entity' (2024, 100k+ sites impacted), domain deactivated, then 'starting in late May 2026, the polyfill[.]io domain became active again'—indicates threat actor re-engagement or domain seizure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor historical threat feeds and domain registration databases for re-activation of previously-dormant malicious domains. Cross-reference polyfill[.]io registration history (2024 compromise, May 2026 re-activation) with threat-actor infrastructure. Alert on unexpected activity from known supply-chain attack domains.

suggestion.title: Phishing email targeting UK/Germany/Italy/South Africa regions
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states geographic expansion of phishing attacks; campaign targeting specific countries is a foundational detection use case. From title: 'Expands Phishing Attacks to U.K., Germany, Italy, and South Africa'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for phishing emails with TA4922 indicators (sender reputation, URL patterns, subject line themes) targeting recipient orgs in specified geographies. Correlate email gateway logs with failed security checks (DMARC/SPF failures, malicious URL detection) and subsequent suspicious login attempts within 24-48 hours of delivery.

suggestion.title: Suspicious attachment delivery from TA4922 phishing campaigns
suggestion.rationale: Phishing campaigns typically involve malicious attachments (Office macros, executables, archives). Article confirms attack expansion but pipeline extracted zero IOCs, including file hashes or attachment signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on phishing attachments with executable or macro-enabled suffixes (.exe, .docm, .xlsm, .zip containing PE files) delivered to users in targeted geographies. Correlate with process creation events (WinWord, Excel spawning cmd.exe or PowerShell) within 30 minutes of attachment open.

suggestion.title: Credential harvesting post-phishing delivery
suggestion.rationale: Phishing campaigns typically follow with credential theft; article describes TA4922's geographic expansion but pipeline missed detection for post-compromise credential access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect login attempts 1-72 hours after phishing email delivery using credential pairs not previously seen for those users. Flag impossible travel (email recipient in UK, login from unrelated geography). Monitor for MFA bypasses or token theft patterns post-phishing.

suggestion.title: TA4922 infrastructure reconnaissance and domain acquisition
suggestion.rationale: Campaign expansion to new geographies implies new malicious infrastructure setup. Article does not mention specific domains/URLs but pipeline should flag infrastructure-related MITRE techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and HTTP traffic for newly registered domains matching TA4922 phishing infrastructure patterns (look-alike domains, newly created registrations <30 days old). Flag C2 beaconing patterns and bulk email sending to newly acquired domain reputation baseline.

suggestion.title: Malicious URL click-through and landing page access
suggestion.rationale: Phishing campaigns rely on URL clicks leading to credential harvesting pages. Article does not provide specific URLs but this is a standard phishing kill-chain detection gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on users clicking embedded URLs in emails flagged as high-risk phishing. Correlate with landing-page patterns (HTTP 200 response, form submission detection, unusual redirect chains). Block second-stage payload delivery or credential submission.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20230 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Exploit Code Goes Public'—this is the primary attack vector and should trigger immediate detection logic for exploitation attempts against Cisco Unified CM.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Cisco Unified CM administrative endpoints with payloads matching known CVE-2026-20230 exploitation patterns. Track requests containing known malicious parameter patterns or POST bodies targeting vulnerable code paths. Correlate with version detection to confirm unpatched instances are being targeted.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Cisco Unified CM Administrative Access
suggestion.rationale: High-severity vulnerability implies potential auth bypass or privilege escalation. Article does not specify attack mechanics but exploitation would likely require elevated access to impact the system.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on admin-role access to Unified CM from non-whitelisted source IPs, or rapid successful authentications following multiple failed attempts. Flag access outside known maintenance windows or access to sensitive endpoints like configuration exports that do not correlate with known administrative activity.

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM Process Execution Anomalies Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation of a Unified CM vulnerability would likely result in code execution or process injection. Article confirms active exploitation is occurring, necessitating runtime detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual child processes spawned from Unified CM application processes (tomcat, ucmanager, etc.), particularly those invoking shell interpreters (cmd.exe, /bin/sh). Detect process execution from unexpected working directories or with suspicious command-line arguments that deviate from normal Unified CM operational patterns.

suggestion.title: Cisco Unified CM Patch Status Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Cisco Patches CVE-2026-20230'—organizations must track patch deployment to distinguish vulnerable from patched instances and prioritize triage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Continuous assessment of Cisco Unified CM version numbers across infrastructure. Alert if unpatched versions running in production are detected post-patch-release date. Cross-reference with active exploitation indicators to identify systems at imminent risk of compromise.

suggestion.title: Suspicious GitHub Action Workflow Trigger from Issue
suggestion.rationale: Article title directly states 'malicious issue hijack repositories' — pipeline failed to detect the initial-access vector: a crafted GitHub issue triggering an Action workflow
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions workflows triggered by issue comments/creation from external or low-reputation users. Flag if workflow modifies protected branches or accesses repository secrets within 5 minutes of issue creation.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Code Push via GitHub Action Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes repository hijacking — pipeline missed detection for workflow execution resulting in unexpected commits to main/protected branches
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect commits pushed by GitHub Actions service account that were not triggered by a verified source (PR approval, scheduled task, signed webhook). Alert on code changes in protected branches within GitHub Action context.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Workflow Environment Secrets Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Hijacking implies access to secrets/tokens — pipeline should detect workflows unexpectedly accessing GITHUB_TOKEN or custom repository secrets
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Actions workflows that export, log, or exfiltrate repository secrets (GITHUB_TOKEN, deploy keys, API tokens) to external endpoints or artifacts. Flag if triggered by untrusted PR or issue.

suggestion.title: GitHub Action Workflow File Modification Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector likely involves modifying .github/workflows YAML files — pipeline failed to surface detection for workflow definition changes
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any modifications to .github/workflows/ files (*.yml, *.yaml) committed without approval from repository admins. Correlate with issue/PR creation in same commit window.

suggestion.title: External Data Exfiltration via GitHub Action Artifact Upload
suggestion.rationale: Hijacked repository control could enable data theft — pipeline missed detection for Actions uploading unexpected artifacts to external storage
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions workflows for artifact uploads to non-standard storage (S3 buckets, blob storage) with unfamiliar credentials. Flag if Action runtime accesses source code or secrets before upload.

suggestion.title: Malicious GTM Container Executing Inline Payload from Metadata
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malicious code is embedded in legitimate-looking GTM containers, which activate when a shopper reaches a checkout page' and 'reads JavaScript code that it reassembles and then executes using new Function()' — pipeline should detect GTM instances executing code sourced from external metadata fields.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GTM containers for instances that retrieve and execute code via new Function() with arguments sourced from external APIs (Stripe metadata, Firestore documents). Baseline: GTM should execute pre-packaged analytics, not dynamically load and run external payloads on checkout pages. Flag container activation on checkout URL patterns with code-execution indicators.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Stripe Customer Record Creation for Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'creating a new Stripe customer object, and storing the stolen data in metadata fields' and 'Every stolen payment card becomes a fake customer record in the attacker's Stripe account' — legitimate checkout processes payment intents, not dynamic customer record creation as a storage backdoor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST /v1/customers requests from web application contexts with metadata fields containing structured payment data. Look for high-volume customer creation without corresponding order records, or metadata patterns matching credit card format (16-digit sequences, MM/YY expiration, 3-4 digit CVV). Correlate with checkout page load frequency.

suggestion.title: XOR-Obfuscated Credit Card Data in Browser Storage
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'stolen data is concatenated into a single string, obfuscated using the XOR operation, and stored locally' — detection must identify XOR byte-stream patterns in localStorage/sessionStorage consistent with encrypted payment data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan localStorage keys (especially '_d_data_customer_' or generic '_data' patterns) for values with high byte-level entropy and consistent cipher bias (XOR signatures). Correlate with credit card capture events (form inputs with 15-19 digit numeric sequences, MM/YY patterns in adjacent fields, CVV capture near card number). Flag if wiped immediately after exfiltration attempt.

suggestion.title: Firestore Document Access from E-Commerce Checkout Contexts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes variant: 'Google Firestore, a cloud database service for data storage and real-time retrieval, is used instead of Stripe' with payload retrieved from 'tracking/captcha' in 'braintree-payment-app' project — legitimate payment flows have no reason to access Firestore.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any Firestore read/write access (firebase.google.com API calls, includemasked_ips) from e-commerce checkout pages. Specifically monitor for reads from document paths like 'tracking/captcha', 'tracking/*', or projects named 'braintree-*', 'payment-*'. Legitimate Firestore use in payment flows is exceptional; baseline should reflect zero normal use.

suggestion.title: Content Security Policy Bypass via Trusted Domain Payment Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Stores allow that domain by default, so the skimmer slips past Content Security Policy rules and network filters' — data exfiltration through api.stripe.com and googletagmanager.com POST requests with payment data payloads bypasses CSP whitelisting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to api.stripe.com and googletagmanager.com for payload sizes and patterns inconsistent with normal analytics or payment operations. Baseline legitimate requests: small structured data (event tags, transaction IDs). Flag: large or irregularly-formatted POST bodies, metadata fields with >256 byte values, multiple credit card-like structures in single request.

suggestion.title: Stripe API Customer Record Queries from Non-Backend Contexts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'queuing Stripe's API for a specific customer record, cus_TfFjAAZQNOYENR, in this case' and 'From the metadata fields of the record, it reads JavaScript code' — browser-initiated Stripe API queries for customer metadata retrieval is abnormal and indicates payload retrieval.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GET /v1/customers/{id} or /v1/customers/{id}/metadata requests originating from client-side JavaScript (User-Agent contains Chrome/Firefox/Safari, origin from checkout domain). Legitimate payment flows query customers from backend only. Flag if customer ID matches known attacker accounts (cus_TfFjAAZQNOYENR) or if metadata fields contain base64/hex/XOR-like encoded values.

suggestion.title: Large-Scale Network Data Exfiltration Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states '234 GB of data' stolen from networks; detection should alert on sustained bulk outbound transfers matching threat actor operational patterns
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cumulative outbound transfer volume exceeding 50 GB to non-whitelisted external IPs within 48-hour windows. Correlate with unusual logon times and disabled security controls.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to Healthcare Data Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms 'unauthorized access to a limited portion of our network' with targeting of insurance records, government IDs, PII; detect anomalous queries/exports from healthcare databases
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk exports, iterative enumeration, and sequential rapid-fire queries to insurance and PII tables outside business hours or from unusual service accounts. Flag access patterns consistent with data staging.

suggestion.title: ShinyHunters Leak Site Activity Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'ShinyHunters listed the company on its data leak site'; SOC should track threat actor leak platforms for new victim postings matching customer roster
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Automated scanning of known ShinyHunters leak sites, forums, and pastebins for organization names; trigger alert matching detected company name with breach claim + extortion language within 72 hours of network compromise discovery.

suggestion.title: Post-Breach Organization Notification Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: DentaQuest 'confirmed on its website' breach 'On June 2'; monitor customer-facing breach advisories as leading incident indicators
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest organization breach notifications from websites and press releases; correlate with threat actor leak activity and internal IR timeline. Alert on confirmation statements with specific damage metrics (records, GB size).

suggestion.title: Healthcare PII Pattern Matching in Public Breaches
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exposed: 'government-issued IDs', 'health insurance information', 'dates of birth'; create pattern signatures for healthcare-specific PII combinations in leaked datasets
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Regex/ML patterns for healthcare PII (insurance ID + birthdate + full name + government ID) in public paste sites and leaked datasets; match against internal customer/employee rosters to confirm data presence and notify breach response teams.

suggestion.title: Fraudulent Open-Source Tool Domain Registration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Fake Sites Mimicking Open-Source Tools'. Pipeline missed typosquatting detection for domains impersonating legitimate tools (npm, docker, nginx, etc.). Should flag newly-registered domains with edit-distance similarity to known OSS projects.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DNS queries and HTTP requests to domains with string similarity (Levenshtein distance ≤2) to canonical open-source tool names. Cross-reference against WHOIS age; alert if registration <30 days and resolves to hosting provider (not legitimate maintainer infrastructure). Correlate with zero historical reputation in URL reputation services.

suggestion.title: Search Engine Result Injection / SEO Poisoning
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Rank High on Google to Deliver Malware'. Pipeline found no detection for search-based initial access. Should detect HTTP referer headers from search engines routing to newly-observed/low-reputation domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests with referer=google.com/bing.com/etc. pointing to domains registered <60 days, with WHOIS registrant privacy enabled, or hosted on disposable IP ranges. Identify search keywords in referer URL and correlate against SEO fraud signatures (keyword stuffing in page titles, suspicious inbound link patterns).

suggestion.title: Traffic Distribution System (TDS) Command-and-Control
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'Deliver Malware via TDS'. TDS infrastructure exhibits rapid-redirect chains, geographically-diverse destination IPs, and sub-second response times. Pipeline entirely missed C2 reconstruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP 301/302/307 redirect chains (≥3 hops) originating from single IP to geographically-disparate destinations within 500ms. Flag response times <150ms for redirect-only pages. Alert on single-IP TDS infrastructure serving >100 unique destinations within 24h, characteristic of commercial TDS providers.

suggestion.title: Malware Delivery from Fake Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware delivery endpoint. Pipeline should detect downloads of suspicious executables from fake tool domains, followed by process execution, especially for common OSS distribution archives (setup.exe, .tar.gz from unverified sources).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP downloads from low-reputation/newly-registered domains with subsequent process creation of unsigned binaries, .NET/PowerShell runners, or legitimate-tool masqueraders (e.g., nginx.exe spawned from user temp directory). Flag archive extractions followed by execution within 60 seconds of download.

suggestion.title: Lookalike Repository Mirror Detection via HTTP Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Attackers cloning legitimate repository layouts (GitHub, PyPI, npm homepages). Article phrase: 'Mimicking Open-Source Tools'. Should detect pages with stolen/repurposed legitimate website HTML/CSS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP responses from low-reputation domains serving HTML with identical or near-identical CSS/JavaScript to legitimate repositories (GitHub, PyPI, docker.io). Flag SSLMITMs, certificate transparency logs showing certs issued to typosquat domains within 24h of legitimate domain activity.

suggestion.title: User-Agent and Referrer Consistency Anomalies from TDS
suggestion.rationale: TDS systems forward user traffic through multiple proxies, creating inconsistent HTTP headers and referer chains indicating traffic manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests where User-Agent indicates legitimate browser but referer chain shows intermediary/proxy domains, or where multiple requests from same source IP show wildly different User-Agents within 10 minutes. Alert on Accept-Language/Charset mismatches with geographic source, indicating traffic forwarding.

suggestion.title: Malicious Ad Network Click-to-Executable
suggestion.rationale: Article states threat spreads via 'Malicious Google and YouTube Ads'—initial access vector; pipeline did not generate detection for ad-driven downloads or suspicious landing pages from ads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution spawned from Safari/Chrome download of unsigned Mach-O binaries originating from ad redirect chains. Correlate clicks on Google/YouTube ad URLs with suspicious file writes to ~/Downloads within 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Unsigned macOS Binary Execution from Temp/Download Directories
suggestion.rationale: FlutterShell on macOS implies unsigned or code-signing-bypassed executable being run; article specifies macOS target but pipeline did not generate gatekeeper-bypass or unsigned-binary-execution detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag execution of Mach-O binaries from ~/Downloads, /tmp, /var/tmp lacking valid Apple code signature or showing xattr com.apple.quarantine removal. Correlate with parent process chrome/safari.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Bundle Loading and Injection
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor persistence on macOS commonly relies on dylib injection or bundle loading; article title references backdoor but pipeline did not suggest detection for suspicious library loads or process injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned dylib loads from non-standard paths (/tmp, ~/Library/Caches, /var/tmp). Flag DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES env var usage or plist modifications under ~/Library/LaunchAgents pointing to unsigned binaries.

suggestion.title: FlutterShell C2 Beaconing (Generic Backdoor Pattern)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'backdoor'—implies C2 communication; pipeline extracted zero IOCs (no C2 IPs/domains) and zero network-based detection rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Without known C2 indicators, flag unusual DNS queries from unsigned processes, long-lived connections to non-whitelisted IPs on non-standard ports, and beaconing patterns (regular outbound attempts at fixed intervals).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Tree: Ad Click → Download → Execution → Daemon Launch
suggestion.rationale: Kill-chain reconstruction was empty; article implies multi-step attack from ad click to backdoor persistence but pipeline did not model parent-child process relationships.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Construct process tree: browser process → child download process → launch of unsigned executable → launch of LaunchAgent/LaunchDaemon. Flag if chain occurs within 10 minutes with no user-visible UI.

suggestion.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Unauthenticated Access Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Actively Exploited' and 'No Patch Available'—indicates known abuse of a pre-auth or low-privilege path. Article body corrupted but exploit pattern demands detection of unauthorized Manager API/web access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco SD-WAN Manager for HTTP/HTTPS requests to sensitive endpoints (e.g., /api/admin, /login, /.well-known) originating from non-whitelisted IPs or with suspicious user-agents. Alert on 401/403 errors in clusters, or successful access from previously unseen sources.

suggestion.title: SD-WAN Manager Configuration Exfiltration or Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article title emphasizes active exploitation; typical SD-WAN Manager post-compromise activity is policy/config theft or rogue device onboarding. No reference to specific exfil in title but is standard attack goal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large outbound data transfers from Catalyst Manager processes, especially to non-corporate IPs. Alert on config-backup exports outside change-control windows. Monitor for rapid policy/template modifications by API without human admin audit trail.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised SD-WAN Manager to Edge Devices
suggestion.rationale: SD-WAN Manager controls fabric of edge routers; compromise typically leads to backdooring managed devices. Article title does not provide specifics but exploitation of management plane universally risks fabric takeover.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Manager-originated configuration pushes during non-maintenance windows. Detect new device registrations or re-registrations to Manager from unexpected source IPs. Flag policy updates that bypass approval workflows.

suggestion.title: Cisco CVE-2026-20245 Exploitation Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: CVE ID in title is the primary threat indicator. Pipeline failed to extract it. Detection rule must key on known exploit payload patterns or behavioral signatures if available via threat feeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest CVSS/CVE-2026-20245 signature rules from Cisco, IDS vendors, or public POC repositories (GitHub, Metasploit). Flag HTTP requests matching known payload patterns or regex for command injection / path traversal typical of Cisco web-app flaws.

suggestion.title: Persistence via SD-WAN Manager Web-Shell or Admin Account Creation
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation with no patch means attacker retention is critical. Web-shell placement on Manager or rogue admin account is standard post-exploit tactic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Catalyst Manager filesystem for unexpected .php, .jsp, .asp files in web-accessible directories. Alert on new admin user creation outside provisioning workflows. Detect password changes on system accounts via API without normal approval.

suggestion.title: Trojanized Android App Installation from Untrusted Source
suggestion.rationale: Article core: 'Targets Arabic Users via Fake News, PDF and War Map Apps'—attacker distribution is app-based social engineering. No use case generated for detecting installation of these trojanized APKs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for installation of APKs from unofficial sources or bundled with decoy app names (Fake News, PDF Reader, War Map). Detect package installation attempts from non-Play-Store URLs or side-loaded APKs. Correlate with user interaction on suspicious links or email attachments.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Android Capability Request - Location + Camera + Contacts
suggestion.rationale: Spyware implicitly requests permissions to collect user data. Article describes 'spyware' but no UC for detecting over-broad permission grants typical of Asin family.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Android apps requesting multiple sensitive permissions in rapid sequence (location, camera, microphone, contacts, messages) without corresponding functional justification. Asin-family malware typically requests full data-exfiltration permissions upfront.

suggestion.title: Asin Spyware C2 Beacon to Known Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies malware 'Asin' by name but pipeline did not extract any IOCs (domains, IPs, package names). No network-based detection generated for C2 communication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTPS/HTTP to Asin-attributed command-and-control servers. Detect beacon patterns from Android devices running trojanized news/PDF/map apps, especially with geotags from MENA region. Flag repeated connections from same device to C2 IPs.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Sensitive Data to External C2
suggestion.rationale: Spyware payload inherently exfiltrates data. Article context strongly implies data theft but no detection use case for mobile exfiltration channels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk uploads of contact lists, SMS history, photos, or location logs from mobile devices. Monitor for encrypted outbound tunnels or unusual traffic volume on ports 443/8443 from devices running Asin samples.

suggestion.title: Android App Masquerading - Name vs Bundle ID Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Asin disguises itself as legitimate news/PDF/map apps. Article structure ('Fake News App', 'PDF app', 'War Map app') indicates brand-spoofing but no UC captures app-identity fraud.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on APKs with legitimate-looking display names (e.g., 'Al Jazeera', 'Google Maps', 'Adobe Reader') that have suspicious or unfamiliar package identifiers (com.example.fakemaps). Cross-reference against Google Play app metadata.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Scheduled Task or Boot-Complete Receiver
suggestion.rationale: Spyware requires persistence mechanisms. Standard Android malware uses broadcast receivers or JobScheduler. Article does not detail but should be assumed; no persistence-phase UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for apps registering BOOT_COMPLETED or persistent JobScheduler tasks that run hidden services. Flag APKs that declare no user-visible components but spawn background threads immediately after installation.

suggestion.title: M365 Access Blending with Stolen Credentials and Proxy Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Brickstorm proxying features and stolen credentials' to 'blend in with legitimate network traffic and evade Conditional Access policies.' Detection should focus on sign-ins that exhibit proxy/spoofing of legitimate IP ranges combined with policy bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on M365 sign-in events using stolen credentials (low-risk user, admin account, dormant account) that originate from IPs exhibiting proxy/VPN fingerprints, especially when signing in from geographic impossibilities. Correlate with disabled or bypassed Conditional Access policies.

suggestion.title: WebSocket C2 Communication with Multiplexing Library
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies Plenet uses 'WebSocket protocol for C2 communications and a multiplexing library for simultaneous data streams.' This is distinct from HTTP/S C2 and requires protocol-level detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP Upgrade requests (101 Switching Protocols) to port 443 or alternate ports initiated by non-browser processes. Monitor for WebSocket frames carrying binary serialized data consistent with command multiplexing. Flag internal systems opening WebSocket connections to unknown external IPs.

suggestion.title: .NET Assembly Execution on Network Appliances (Plenet Deployment)
suggestion.rationale: Article: Plenet 'deployed to a Synology NAS appliance' and is '.NET-based backdoor.' Runtime execution of .NET on non-workstation appliances is inherently anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .NET runtime (dotnet.exe, mono, csc.exe) process spawning on Synology, pfSense, NAS, or legacy Linux systems. Monitor for .dll/.exe files written to Synology /volume1 directories or Linux /tmp paths from unexpected sources. Flag non-standard CLR host processes.

suggestion.title: Python Reverse Shell Execution as Secondary Persistence (AgentPSD)
suggestion.rationale: AgentPSD described as 'Python-based reverse shell utility' deployed as 'fallback persistence mechanism.' Python process establishing outbound sockets is a clear fallback indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect python.exe or python3 processes with command-line arguments containing socket, subprocess.socket, or paramiko imports. Alert on Python spawning /bin/bash or cmd.exe. Correlate with outbound connections to hardcoded IPs/domains and absence of legitimate development context.

suggestion.title: Firewall VPN Configuration Followed by Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Article: attackers 'enable and configure SSL VPN access on the victim's firewall, then connected to internal systems.' Firewall config changes (especially enabling access) followed by unusual internal movement is a kill-chain indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on firewall CLI commands or web UI access enabling VPN/remote access outside scheduled maintenance. Correlate with subsequent SSH/RDP/SMB connections from the VPN subnet to internal servers. Flag admin account usage on firewall during off-hours.

suggestion.title: Legacy/Unsupported System Targeting (No EDR Coverage)
suggestion.rationale: Article: VerdantBamboo 'targets systems that do not support endpoint detection and response (EDR) solutions.' Malware deployment to pfSense, Synology, GroupWise archive indicates deliberate targeting of EDR-blind infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized file writes or process execution on network appliances (firewalls, NAS, legacy email servers). Alert on binary execution on Synology devices outside vendor patch schedules. Flag credential reuse to non-EDR infrastructure, especially for dormant admin accounts.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U Internet-Exposed Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies vulnerability in public-facing instances with CISA patch due 2026-06-19. Asset exposure is prerequisite for remediation and detection. Article phrase: 'allow specially crafted POST requests...to crash the Serv-U service without authentication' — requires exposed listening port.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Serv-U instances (FTP/SSH, ports 22/23/3389) reachable from internet. Correlate vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-28318 against externally-facing assets. Flag unpatched instances against CISA remediation deadline 2026-06-19.

suggestion.title: Malformed POST Request with Deflate Content-Encoding
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies precise exploitation technique: 'specially crafted POST requests using the Content-Encoding: deflate header'. This HTTP pattern is the attack fingerprint and highly tunable for WAF/proxy detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests with Content-Encoding: deflate header targeting Serv-U endpoints (admin/service URIs). Monitor for HTTP status anomalies or connection resets following deflate-encoded POSTs. Flag clusters of deflate requests to same host within short time window as DoS probe pattern.

suggestion.title: Serv-U Process Crash and Service Unavailability
suggestion.rationale: Article describes impact: 'crash the Serv-U service without authentication'. Service termination is observable post-exploitation indicator. Article phrase: uncontrolled resource consumption implies T1499 endpoint DoS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Serv-U process termination (Sysmon EventCode 5 or ProcessTerminated) preceded by anomalous HTTP traffic. Monitor for CPU/memory exhaustion spikes or connection pool depletion in Serv-U logs. Correlate service restart loops with inbound HTTP patterns.

suggestion.title: Deflate Content-Encoding Anomaly Baseline
suggestion.rationale: Content-Encoding: deflate is legitimate HTTP compression, but rarely seen in POST requests to Serv-U service endpoints. Baseline normal usage (expected low/zero) to detect malicious payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate deflate encoding in environment (most applications use gzip, not deflate). Alert on any deflate-encoded POST to Serv-U, or spike in deflate usage targeting file-transfer/admin endpoints. Cross-reference with CVE-2026-28318 context.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN vManage Malicious File Upload + vScript Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers exploit by 'uploading a crafted file to the affected system' followed by 'command injection attacks.' Provides concrete IOC: Apr 15 log entry showing `/usr/bin/vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh` execution with `/home/admin/malicious.csv`. No detection logic for this core attack step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious .csv or script file creation in /home/admin/ directory on vManage systems, immediately followed by execution of vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh or other vScript engine processes. Correlate file write + process execution within 60 seconds.

suggestion.title: Root Privilege Escalation from Netadmin Context
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states flaw 'can allow local attackers with low privileges to execute arbitrary commands as root' and 'elevate their privileges as the root user.' Missing detection for privilege escalation outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of system commands (UID 0) originating from vManage script execution contexts or uploaded files. Alert on subprocess elevation: netadmin-context process spawning root-level child process or executing commands via sudo/su.

suggestion.title: vSmart Controller Configuration Exfiltration / Push
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'limited cases where exploitation resulted in a configuration change pushed to edge devices' and describes 'uploading tenant configuration data to vSmart controllers.' Missing detection for lateral movement to controller devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vManage→vSmart network traffic for unusual volume, frequency, or size of configuration distribution. Correlate with prior evidence of file upload or privilege escalation. Alert on config push operations initiated during suspicious script execution windows.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20182/20127 Authentication Bypass Followed by CVE-2026-20245 Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE-2026-20245 requires 'netadmin privileges' which can be obtained via 'valid credentials or exploitation of CVE-2026-20182 or CVE-2026-20127.' Missing detection for chained exploits: auth bypass → file upload → privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create multi-stage correlation: detect failed/atypical authentication attempts → successful session creation without credentials → file upload activity within 10 minutes. Single IOC weak; sequence is high-confidence indicator of exploit chain.

suggestion.title: Netadmin Account Anomalous Activity & Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker 'must have netadmin privileges on the affected system.' Missing detection for netadmin account enumeration, off-hours access, geographic anomalies, or unusual command execution patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of normal netadmin activity. Alert on: netadmin login from new geography/IP, off-hours access, account enumeration attempts, service account testing, or netadmin executing administrative commands outside normal workflows.

suggestion.title: /var/log/scripts.log Injection Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article provides exact IoC pattern: 'vScript: Tenant list upload per vsmart serial number' entries in /var/log/scripts.log, with example showing malicious .csv path. Pipeline missed this specific, concrete log signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Direct log pattern match: alert on entries in /var/log/scripts.log containing substring 'vScript: Tenant list upload per vsmart serial number' combined with suspicious file references (/home/admin/*.csv, /tmp/*, malicious extensions) or uncommon vsmart serial identifiers.

suggestion.title: Phishing Domain Detection — World Cup Event Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Fake Sites' as attack vector; likely FIFA/World Cup domain typosquats or lookalike registrations used for credential harvesting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries and HTTP requests to domains similar to FIFA, World Cup, or ticket-resale sites. Flag registrations with creative misspellings (e.g., 'fifa2026-tickets.com' vs 'fifa.com'), newly registered domains (<30d age) resolving to non-endemic hosting, and HTTPS certificates issued to suspicious registrants. Correlate against phishing intelligence feeds for known World Cup scam infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Banking Malware Behavioral Detection — Credential Capture & C2
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'Banking Malware' as delivered payload; expected behaviors include keylogging, API hooking, process injection targeting financial software.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag suspicious code injection into banking applications, registry modifications targeting credential stores, and unsigned executable launches with banking-app names. Monitor for processes spawning with obfuscated command lines, DLL side-loading patterns common in banking trojans, and hook-insertion syscalls targeting winsock/CNG (crypto APIs).

suggestion.title: Stolen Credential Usage — Anomalous Post-Breach Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Stolen Logins' as outcome; detection should focus on credential reuse patterns that diverge from legitimate account behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous login patterns post-credential-dump: geographic impossibility (same account logging in from Brazil and Russia within seconds), failed login bursts followed by success (spraying), logins from new devices/ISPs without corresponding MFA challenges, and login times outside user's typical patterns. Correlate with known World Cup scam infrastructure IPs.

suggestion.title: Command & Control Communication — Banking Malware Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Banking malware inferred from title requires C2 infrastructure for credential exfiltration and operator control; article likely describes backend infrastructure or command domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections to newly registered or low-reputation domains from hosts running suspicious processes. Flag DNS requests for common C2 domains (fast-flux patterns, DGA-like naming), HTTPS connections with certificate anomalies (self-signed, mismatched CN), and exfiltration over HTTP POST with large payloads disguised as benign traffic.

suggestion.title: Malware Delivery via Phishing Attachment or Link — World Cup Campaign
suggestion.rationale: Implied delivery chain: fake World Cup site → banking malware download. Article likely describes email or drive-by-download vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with World Cup or FIFA-themed subject lines linking to phishing domains or triggering file downloads. Monitor for execution of files downloaded from suspicious World Cup/sports betting sites. Flag macro-enabled Office documents or executables masquerading as PDF/tickets.

suggestion.title: DbGate JSON payload structure — functionName injection in /runners/start POST body
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'code injection in the `functionName` parameter of JSON script `assign` commands. The `functionName` value is interpolated directly into dynamically generated JavaScript source code via string concatenation.' Current UCs hunt downstream shell spawning, but none hunt the actual malicious JSON payload structure in the POST body. Detection requires application logs or WAF logs capturing request body content.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for POST requests to `/runners/start` or `/runners/load-reader` endpoints where JSON body contains `functionName` parameter with JavaScript code syntax (backticks, semicolons, require/import statements). Flag when functionName value deviates from simple alphanumeric identifiers. Requires body inspection from reverse proxy or WAF.

suggestion.title: DbGate forked child process creation from bundle.js parent
suggestion.rationale: Article describes execution: 'The generated code is then executed in a forked Node.js child process.' Current detections hunt for shell spawning by child, but don't specifically catch the fork pattern itself. A child_process.fork() or spawn() call is the immediate indicator of code execution success.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child process creation where parent process is `node` or `node.exe` with command-line containing `bundle.js`, `dbgate`, or `.dbgate/run/`, and child process has a randomized or temporary name (GUID-based, temp file name, or short-lived PID). Baseline legitimate Node.js child creation to reduce FP.

suggestion.title: DbGate: Unauthenticated JWT token issuance via POST /auth/login
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'none auth provider issues JWT tokens without credentials via POST /auth/login.' This auth bypass is the prerequisite for exploitation; pipeline never surfaced it as a detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to /auth/login endpoints that return HTTP 200 (successful token issuance) without credential submission in the request body. Look for DbGate instances with auth provider configured as 'none'.

suggestion.title: DbGate: Command execution via shell interpreter spawn after Zip Slip file write
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'allows arbitrary file write leading to RCE.' Article headlines RCE but pipeline did not map T1059.001. Successful Zip Slip exploitation often results in written shell scripts being executed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Node process spawning bash, sh, or other shell interpreters shortly after (within seconds) of file creation events to /etc, /var/spool, or /root directories. Correlation: node process ID in both file-write and process-spawn events.

suggestion.title: DbGate: Cron job persistence via Zip Slip arbitrary file write
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies T1053.003 (Cron) but provides no specific detection for cron-file writes via the Zip Slip. Article: vulnerable file write to '/etc/cron.d/*', '/var/spool/cron/*'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Node process (dbgate) creating or modifying files in /etc/cron.d/, /etc/cron.*, /var/spool/cron/ directories. High confidence if process is initiating the writes (not PID 0 or system service) and the request source is external network traffic.

suggestion.title: DbGate: LD_PRELOAD hijacking via /etc/ld.so.preload write
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions /etc/ld.so.preload in the detection hunts but never explains the attack vector. This is library hijacking for privilege escalation or persistence—a missing technique T1574.008.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Node process writing or modifying /etc/ld.so.preload file. /etc/ld.so.preload is a sensitive system file that preloads shared objects into all binaries—writes here indicate attempts to achieve persistence or privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: DbGate: SSH key injection via /root/.ssh/authorized_keys write
suggestion.rationale: Detections reference /root/.ssh/* paths (UC_17_2) but pipeline never surfaced this as a lateral-movement or credential-access technique. Article: Zip Slip can write arbitrary files including SSH keys.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Node process (dbgate) creating, appending to, or modifying /root/.ssh/authorized_keys or ~/.ssh/authorized_keys in any user home directory. Successful write enables SSH access without password.

suggestion.title: DbGate /runners/load-reader POST with code injection patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states exploitation occurs via 'unsanitized functionName parameter' in POST requests. Pipeline must hunt the specific parameter name and payload patterns (import(), require, child_process) at the HTTP request body level, not just URL patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST /runners/load-reader endpoint for requests containing 'functionName' parameter with values including import(, require(, child_process, execSync, or eval. The article identifies dynamic import() as the specific bypass mechanism—this should be the primary signature, checked in decoded/unencoded request body.

suggestion.title: Bypass of require=null mitigation via dynamic import
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically highlights that 'require = null mitigation is trivially bypassed via dynamic import()'. This is the core technical vulnerability. Hunts must look for import() or import ( used within the functionName payload as the evasion technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect exploitation attempt signatures that use import() syntax within the functionName parameter. The whitelist bypass (require=null) is bypassed by using dynamic imports—monitor for code patterns that load child_process, os, or other RCE-capable modules via import() instead of require().

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation: node process executing commands as root
suggestion.rationale: Article states RCE allows execution 'as root'—this indicates unauthorized privilege escalation from the node application context to root OS-level execution. Should detect when node spawns processes with elevated UID/GID.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when a node.js or DbGate process (typically running as non-root user) spawns child processes that execute with UID 0 (root) or with setuid/setgid bits. Monitor for token elevation or privilege inheritance anomalies.

suggestion.title: Authentication + authorization baseline for /runners/load-reader
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes this is 'Authenticated RCE'—requires valid DbGate credentials. Hunts should establish baseline of legitimate /runners/load-reader access and flag deviations: multiple auth failures, unusual user accounts, accounts from unexpected networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline the set of authenticated users who legitimately access /runners/load-reader endpoint. Flag authentications from new user accounts, service accounts, or off-hours access. Correlate successful auth + subsequent malicious payload attempt.

suggestion.title: DbGate application error/exception logs for code injection context
suggestion.rationale: Injection attempts will likely generate error traces in application logs (JavaScript syntax errors, eval() exceptions, or namespace collisions). Application logs are the highest-fidelity source for detecting malformed payloads and injection intent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DbGate application error logs for exceptions or stack traces containing 'functionName', 'import', 'ReferenceError', or 'SyntaxError' in contexts related to the loadReader handler. Error logs will show failed injection attempts.

suggestion.title: HTTP POST to /*/start endpoint with path-traversal payloads in request body/query
suggestion.rationale: Article states BSC 'blindly trusts path-related form fields' and vulnerability uses 'path traversal'—the actual exploitation signal is POST bodies/queries containing encoded traversal sequences (.. / %2e%2e / %252e%252e) targeting parameters like log_dir_path, file_name_pattern, path. No hunt currently detects this in-flight.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST requests to URI paths matching `/{name}/start` where request body or query string contains path-traversal indicators (.., %2e%2e, %252e, encoded variants) co-occurring with file/directory parameters (log_dir_path, file_name_pattern, path, root_dir). High confidence if destination path contains sensitive prefixes (/etc, /var, /root, /home/*/.ssh, /usr/bin).

suggestion.title: File writes outside configured log_root by ait-bsc process
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'bypass the configured log root and direct BSC to log to **arbitrary filesystem paths**'—exploitation manifests as files created/appended outside expected BSC log directories. Requires baselining log_root configuration but directly maps to impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of ait-bsc/Python process file writes to configured log_root (typically /var/opt/ait-bsc/logs or /opt/ait-bsc/logs). Alert on writes/appends to files outside this perimeter, especially in system directories (/etc, /root, /home, /var), or with path-traversal indicators in the file path. Correlate with prior HTTP POST activity.

suggestion.title: ait-bsc or Python child processes spawning shell interpreters or network tools
suggestion.rationale: Article capability to append to arbitrary files could enable writing to executable paths or scripts. If exploitation escalates to code execution (RCE), attacker may spawn /bin/sh, /bin/bash, or nc/curl for reverse shell. No hunt for execution phase escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ait-bsc or python processes (especially those with HTTP context) spawning child processes matching /bin/(sh|bash|ksh|csh) or network tools (nc, netcat, curl, wget, python -m socket). Flag if spawned from processes not normally expected to fork shells, or if command line contains obvious reverse-shell patterns (>&, /dev/tcp, mkfifo).

suggestion.title: Unauthorized modifications to ait-bsc configuration (bsc.yaml) or installation paths
suggestion.rationale: Article describes dynamic handler creation and path configuration. Attackers may modify bsc.yaml to persist changes, alter logging behavior, or change listening ports. No hunt for configuration tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor modifications to bsc.yaml, bsc.config, or files in /opt/ait-bsc, /home/*/ait-venv (if development environment) for write/modify events outside of expected deployment/upgrade windows. Alert on modifications by non-service accounts (e.g., ait user, root outside of deploy) or by HTTP-handling processes.

suggestion.title: Repeated failed and successful HTTP attempts to /*/start with payload mutations
suggestion.rationale: Attacker may probe and iterate on payload encoding (double-encoding, case variation, null bytes) before successful exploitation. Baselining benign /start requests and detecting anomalous attempts reveals reconnaissance/exploitation in flight.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Profile baseline /start POST request patterns (successful requests, normal path arguments). Alert on statistically significant increases in POST rate to /*/start, or request patterns with suspicious mutations: repeated attempts with varying encodings (%2e vs . vs %252e), increasing path depth, or requests from single source with multiple distinct payload variations within short window.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized role creation by non-admin user
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Any authenticated user could load the page and use its public actions to create new roles.' Core attack step missing from pipeline output. Requires privilege_escalation phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on role creation when initiator's role does not include role-management or admin capability. Cross-check authorization context against role CRUD permissions in application ACL.

suggestion.title: Administrator or privileged account deletion by low-privilege authenticated user
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'delete other users, including administrators.' Second explicit attack step. Represents account removal and privilege escalation combined.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect user deletion initiated by authenticated accounts without user-management permissions. Escalate if target account is admin-role. Correlate with prior suspicious role creation or privilege grants.

suggestion.title: Permission policy gating mismatch: sensitive action guarded by read-only permission
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'RolePermission gated its write actions on the read-only view_users permission.' Root cause: authorization check was insufficient. Detectable via policy audit or post-incident code review, but operational detection should monitor for write actions succeeding after read-level permission checks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor application permission-check logs for pattern: state-modifying action (write to role, delete user) preceded only by read-permission validation. Mismatch between checked permission scope and action sensitivity indicates potential bypass.

suggestion.title: WordPress Plugin Exploit Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article claims 'hackers exploit critical...flaw' but pipeline extracted zero exploitation patterns. Need baseline detection for Everest Forms Pro endpoint abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/GET requests to Everest Forms Pro plugin directories (wp-content/plugins/everest-forms/) for exploitation attempts. Watch for suspicious parameter patterns, path traversal attempts, or authentication bypasses targeting form processing endpoints.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Activity Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article title claims 'take over sites' implying persistent access, but no detection strategy for post-exploitation web shells or backdoors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of new .php files in wp-content/plugins/everest-forms/ or wp-uploads/ directories with execution attempts. Monitor for base64-encoded PHP execution or obfuscated script patterns commonly used in web shells.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized WordPress Admin Account Creation
suggestion.rationale: Site takeover typically requires persistence via admin account; article mentions takeover but pipeline extracted no account creation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor wp_users table INSERT statements or wp-admin.php?action=createuser requests for unexpected admin account creation, particularly accounts created outside normal business hours or by non-admin users.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Modifications in Everest Forms Directory
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability exploitation typically results in plugin file modification for persistence. Pipeline should surface file integrity alerts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected modifications to Everest Forms Pro core plugin files (especially form processing, upload handlers, or shortcode handlers). Flag write operations to plugin PHP files after known vulnerability disclosure dates.

suggestion.title: Database Direct Access Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Site takeover may involve direct database manipulation; article provides no detection for database exfiltration or malicious queries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor database audit logs for unexpected database user authentication from web-process accounts (www-data, apache). Alert on SELECT queries to wp_users table followed by INSERT/UPDATE operations or large data extractions to external destinations.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PyPI Package Upload with Typosquatting Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malicious package 'parsimonius' mimicked 'parsimonious' with 'single missing letter'—classic typosquatting supply-chain compromise. No hunt exists to detect package uploads with suspiciously similar names to known legitimate libraries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PyPI uploads for package names with edit distance 1-3 from known popular packages. Flag when upload account metadata, author field, or keywords diverge significantly from legitimate package. Alert on rapid-succession uploads or uploads from dormant/new accounts.

suggestion.title: Malicious Python Package Execution on Developer Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'thousands of developers at risk' from package installation/use—standard Python supply-chain attack executes attacker code at import time. No hunt covers suspicious spawning of child processes during pip install or suspicious site-packages modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Python processes spawning unexpected children (subprocess, os.system calls) during pip install or package import. Monitor site-packages __init__.py for recent modifications containing network I/O, credential harvesting, or system commands. Correlate with installation of packages with low download counts or recent creation dates.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package Repository Account Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: malicious package 'quietly made its way into' PyPI—suggests account compromise or permission abuse. No hunt covers abnormal PyPI account activity (login anomalies, upload frequency spikes, account reactivation).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PyPI account logins for geographic distance anomalies or new device fingerprints. Alert on upload frequency spikes from previously dormant accounts. Flag packages with suspicious patterns: version 0.0.1, no prior release history, or author metadata mismatches vs. legitimate package.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation with Postinstall Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'npm in Supply Chain Attacks'—attacks via npm typically exploit postinstall hooks to execute arbitrary code during package installation. Pipeline failed to generate any detection for this core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node.js or npm processes spawning unusual child processes (shells, powershell, curl, wget) during or immediately after npm install operations. Monitor for postinstall script execution from package manager cache directories. Flag installations where the package.json scripts section contains obfuscated or URL-fetching commands.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized npm Registry Authentication or Credential Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks on npm registries often involve compromised or stolen credentials to publish malicious packages. Pipeline did not surface credential-related detection despite 'supply chain' context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry API calls (registry.npmjs.org, private registries) for authentication from unexpected IP ranges, user-agents, or time-of-day patterns. Alert on package publish/update operations from accounts with no prior publication history or after access token generation.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Metadata and Version Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Title mentions 'New Miasma Worm Variant'—typosquatting and version inflation are standard npm supply chain tactics. Pipeline did not generate detection for suspicious package metadata patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect package names similar to popular libraries (typosquatting), packages with large or unusual version jumps, and packages with short descriptions or empty maintainer fields. Flag packages published by newly-created accounts that immediately depend on suspicious external URLs or C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Development Environment Compromise via Package Dependency Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article implies npm developers are targets of supply chain attacks. Pipeline missed detection for injected or modified dependencies in lock files and CI/CD environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected changes to package-lock.json or yarn.lock (integrity hash mismatches, missing entries). Alert on package.json modifications committed outside normal development workflows. Flag lock-file updates that add transitive dependencies not declared in the primary package.json.

suggestion.title: IronWorm/Miasma Malware Behavioral Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline extracted zero threat-actor or malware-family IOCs despite explicit naming in article title. Should have surfaced IronWorm and Miasma as indicators to hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for process names, command-line patterns, or behavioral signatures associated with IronWorm and Miasma (e.g., specific file paths, registry keys, HTTP user-agents, or C2 beacon patterns documented in the source article). Cross-reference with malware sandboxes and feed intelligence.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Network Egress from npm-Installed Code
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain malware in npm packages often exfiltrates data or calls home to C2. Pipeline did not suggest network-based detection despite impact-phase implications in title.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTP/HTTPS/DNS requests initiated by node.js or npm child processes to non-whitelisted domains. Alert on IP geolocation anomalies for connections from package-manager processes. Flag DNS queries for suspicious domains (malware C2, data exfiltration endpoints) resolved during or after npm install.

suggestion.title: Browser extension suspicious network beaconing to C2 domains
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states extensions 'send conversations off' to attacker infrastructure. IOCs deepaichats.com and chatsaigpt.com are C2 domains. No detection suggested for outbound HTTP/HTTPS from browser processes to these or pattern-matching attacker domains. This is the exfiltration phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound connections from chrome.exe, msedge.exe, or firefox.exe to domains matching article IOCs or pattern-matching suspicious C2 infrastructure (newly registered, poor reputation, keywords like 'chat', 'gpt', 'deepai'). Correlate with extension installation within 24 hours prior.

suggestion.title: Anomalous cross-platform AI service authentication patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes threats target ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, Gemini, AND DeepSeek. Malicious extension would need to harvest or replay sessions across multiple AI platforms. No UC suggested for detecting single user/session accessing auth endpoints of multiple competing AI services in short window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when any single IP or user-agent pair authenticates or initiates sessions with 3+ different AI platform APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft, Google, DeepSeek endpoints) within 1 hour. Extension attempting to consolidate stolen credentials will trigger this pattern.

suggestion.title: Browser extension DOM access to sensitive AI platform input fields
suggestion.rationale: Article states extensions are 'harvesting those conversations'—implying real-time DOM inspection of user-entered prompts and AI responses. This is web-application-layer credential access, distinct from cookie/password DB theft. No DOM-level inspection or content-injection detection rule suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual size or frequency of POST requests from browser to external C2 domains containing serialized JSON/base64 payloads that decode to conversation content. Pair with extension installation analytics and tab-access permissions in manifest.

suggestion.title: Malicious extension manifest and update-check anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article does not describe installation mechanism (Chrome Web Store vs. sideloaded vs. social engineering). Regardless, malicious extensions must hide their true C2 endpoint. No hunt suggested for manifest.json content anomalies, obfuscated permission strings, or update callbacks to non-official sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan extension manifest files in Chrome/Edge/Firefox extension directories for: unusual permission combinations (tabs + cookies + webRequest + activeTab together), Base64-encoded strings, hardcoded IP addresses, or update URLs pointing to attacker infrastructure rather than Chrome Web Store or official CDNs.

suggestion.title: Network Connections to Suspicious Firebase Domain from Payment Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names braintree-payment-app.firebaseio.com as C2. Pipeline generated zero IOC-driven hunts despite this being the primary indicator and the briefing calling out 'Network connections to article IPs / domains' as a standard hunt template.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections from payment-processing systems (Stripe integration points, checkout flows) to braintree-payment-app.firebaseio.com or similar Firebase domains. Correlate with sessions handling payment card data. Firebase is high-signal for exfil staging in financial-sector Magecart attacks.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized JavaScript Injection into Payment Processor Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'malware hidden inside one of the most trusted payment platforms' and 'injected code.' This is the core attack vector in Magecart/supply-chain attacks but pipeline did not surface code-injection detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unexpected script modifications or injections in Stripe/payment-gateway script loading and initialization. Look for tampering with payment.js or checkout endpoint responses. Cross-reference CDN cache-busting indicators and unexpected script hashes in frontend code.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Payment Card Data to Attacker-Controlled C2
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attack 'uses Stripe... as both its command center and its data dump' and mentions 'stolen card data.' Pipeline missed the exfiltration phase of the kill chain despite clear language.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk exfiltration of card numbers, expiry dates, CVV, and cardholder names out of payment-processing systems. Baseline normal Stripe API traffic and alert on anomalous POST requests to external domains, especially Firebase-hosted endpoints, during periods of high transaction volume.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise of Third-Party Payment Service
suggestion.rationale: Magecart attacks are definitionally supply-chain compromises (T1195). Article describes attack hiding 'inside one of the most trusted payment platforms'—this indicates compromise of the supply chain layer, not direct merchant compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Stripe/payment-processor dependency integrity: monitor for unexpected commits, deployments, or script modifications in trusted payment libraries. Implement code-signing verification and track script hash changes in production payment endpoints.

suggestion.title: Anomalous API Calls to Payment Processor from Legitimate Merchant Domains
suggestion.rationale: Magecart typically does not directly touch backend systems but manipulates frontend code to exfiltrate card data during checkout. Pipeline should identify API anomalies where legitimate merchant domains trigger unusual Stripe calls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for non-standard Stripe API calls (custom fields, unusual customer data queries, token-creation patterns) initiated from checkout pages or payment forms, especially those that occur before or after the legitimate payment flow.

suggestion.title: Fake software distribution — typo-domain downloads + non-standard installer execution
suggestion.rationale: Article core narrative: 'spreads through fake websites that impersonate popular software.' Article explicitly names lookalike domains mlcrosoft.co.com, mlroweb.com. No initial-access detection present despite this being the infection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP downloads from domains with known typos of legitimate vendors (mlcrosoft → microsoft, mlroweb → microsoft). Correlate with execution of unsigned .dmg, .zip containing unsigned Mach-O binaries, and lack of notarization metadata. Reaper distribution observed via software impersonation.

suggestion.title: macOS persistence — suspicious LaunchAgent or daemon creation
suggestion.rationale: Article: malware 'runs silently' on system, implying persistence mechanism. No detection for how Reaper maintains access across reboots. macOS persistence primarily via ~/.LaunchAgents/ plist files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation/modification of ~/.LaunchAgents/*.plist files referencing browser, wallet, or network processes. Flag unsigned LaunchAgent payloads, scripts launched from /tmp or world-writable paths, and agents executing with unusual privileges.

suggestion.title: C2 beaconing and stolen-data exfiltration to known domains
suggestion.rationale: Article technique T1071 (Application Layer Protocol) for C2 listed but not mapped to detection. Recommends IOC hunts but doesn't specify detection of *exfiltration channels* or beaconing patterns to mlcrosoft.co.com, mlroweb.com, qq-0732gwh22.com, hebsbsbzjsjshduxbs.xyz.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DNS queries and HTTP/HTTPS connections to IOC domains, especially with high frequency, unusual byte counts (exfiltration), or non-standard ports. Reaper variant uses T1071 for C2, likely exfiltrating stolen credentials and wallet data over encrypted channels.

suggestion.title: Use of harvested credentials — cross-system authentication with stolen creds
suggestion.rationale: Article describes stealing browser login data and wallet credentials but lacks post-breach detection for *use* of stolen credentials for lateral movement, privilege escalation, or account takeover.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect authentication attempts from compromised Mac using credentials observed in browser/wallet theft indicators. Alert on cross-machine SSH, SMB, or cloud-service logins using harvested plaintext passwords or browser autofill data within hours of data exfiltration.

suggestion.title: IIS w3wp.exe Child Process Execution Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'custom web shell framework' targeting IIS; web shells execute attacker commands by spawning children from w3wp.exe. No execution-phase UC was generated despite this being the core attack mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Web shells spawn cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or other interpreters from w3wp.exe. Alert on w3wp.exe creating child processes outside normal patching windows, especially with command-line arguments containing encoded payloads, pipes, or redirects. Baseline expected children per IIS application pool.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Script Upload to IIS Content Root
suggestion.rationale: Title mentions 'custom web shell framework'—implies initial payload delivery via file upload. Pipeline missed persistence-phase detection for malicious .aspx/.jsp/.jspx files written to web-accessible directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inetpub\wwwroot and IIS content directories for creation of web-script files (.aspx, .jsp, .jspx, .php). Alert on files written by service accounts, SYSTEM, or w3wp.exe itself. Correlate with IIS HTTP POST requests to those paths in preceding minutes.

suggestion.title: IIS HTTP POST with Oversized or Encoded Request Body
suggestion.rationale: Web shell exploitation occurs via HTTP POST with command payloads; article emphasizes custom framework targeting public-facing IIS. No HTTP anomaly detection proposed despite this being initial-access vector.
