suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track IIS POST request body sizes and payload entropy. Alert on requests >5 KB to non-standard paths, Base64-encoded parameters, or suspicious parameter names (cmd, exec, shell, payload). Correlate sc-status 200 with subsequent w3wp.exe process creation.

suggestion.title: w3wp.exe Outbound Network Connection to Suspicious IP/Domain
suggestion.rationale: Web shell framework must beacon to attacker C2 for command delivery. Article provides no IOCs, but pipeline should generate network-based detection for IIS process making outbound connections outside normal dependency ranges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: IIS/w3wp.exe should not initiate outbound connections to arbitrary external IPs. Alert on new outbound TCP/UDP connections from w3wp.exe to non-infrastructure IPs, especially on ports 443, 8080, 4444, or other C2 beaconing patterns. Baseline legitimate dependencies (package managers, license servers).

suggestion.title: IIS Log Volume Spike on Single Handler
suggestion.rationale: Web shell operation generates anomalous request patterns (reconnaissance, enumeration, command batching). No volume-based anomaly for IIS logs was proposed despite 'custom framework' implying complex command flow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline POST-request frequency per IIS handler. Alert on 5–10x deviation within 10-minute windows, especially from single source IP or with sequential/predictable parameter values (time-based tokens, incrementing IDs). Correlate with sc-status 200 (successful shell command execution).

suggestion.title: OP-512 Threat Cluster Behavioral Profile
suggestion.rationale: Article title identifies threat cluster OP-512; no actor-specific threat profile, TTPs, or signature artifacts were extracted. Custom framework likely exhibits recognizable command syntax, request headers, or timing patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Profile OP-512's web shell framework for signature artifacts: specific HTTP parameter names, header patterns, response encoding, request/response timing intervals, or error-message templates. Once baseline established, create behavioral rule to detect matching patterns on any IIS server, especially coupled with process-execution and file-write detections.

suggestion.title: Suspicious process execution on cloud instances
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 230 servers were 'hijacked' — requires command execution or script injection on victim VMs. Title directly states compromise occurred but pipeline captured no execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous process creation on cloud-hosted VMs with indicators: parent process legitimacy mismatch, unusual outbound network from new processes, or execution of known malware downloaders. Alert on processes with names/parents suggesting installer behavior (setup.exe, msiexec) spawning network-capable children outside business hours.

suggestion.title: SMTP relay abuse from cloud server pool
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Covert SMTP Relay Network' as the attack objective. Pipeline generated no detection for outbound mail abuse despite this being the operational impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-volume outbound SMTP/TCP 25 or 587 traffic from cloud VMs to non-whitelisted relays. Correlate with process execution of mail utilities (sendmail, swaks) or PowerShell Send-MailMessage. Alert on spike in unique destination ports 25 or 587 from instances with no historical mail-sending role.

suggestion.title: Cloud credential compromise via unauthorized login
suggestion.rationale: Hijacking 230 servers across AWS, GCP, Azure requires initial credential compromise or exploitation of cloud-native services. Article describes breach but pipeline did not surface credential-access-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on failed login attempts followed by successful logins from new IPs/devices to cloud service principals or VM management portals. Look for sign-in patterns anomalous to baseline: time-of-day drift, impossible travel, or sign-ins from IP ranges hosting known botnet C2.

suggestion.title: Botnet-like communication pattern from cloud instances
suggestion.rationale: PCPJack malware must establish C2 or coordination mechanism to deploy SMTP relay payload across 230 servers. No command-and-control detection rule generated despite implied C2 phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect periodic, high-volume outbound connections from cloud instances to rare/unknown destinations at regular intervals (C2 heartbeat). Correlate with process creation from system processes (svchost, lsass parent anomalies). Flag instances communicating to IPs with reputation as malware hosting or botnet C2.

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation on compromised cloud VMs
suggestion.rationale: Article title states servers were 'hijacked' — typically requires elevation from initial access context to system/administrator. No privilege-escalation-phase detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for use of privilege-escalation utilities (sudo, runas, UAC bypass) or token-manipulation processes. Alert on suspicious service creation or scheduled tasks spawning with SYSTEM context. Correlate with suspicious parent-child process pairs where unprivileged process spawns admin-context child.

suggestion.title: HTTP 401 Authentication Prompt Injection from Third-Party Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'polyfill[.]io domain became active again and started responding with HTTP 401 authentication requests. User browsers visiting pages such as Toshiba's and MUJI's interpret that as a request for a username and password, so they serve a login prompt.' This is credential phishing via HTTP status code abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP 401 responses originating from external domains injected into legitimate retail/corporate websites. Correlate 401 failures with subsequent user credential submission attempts. Flag 401s from domains not in the site's known third-party allowlist, especially those matching known-compromised CDNs.

suggestion.title: Malicious JavaScript CDN Domain Inclusion Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'external service hosted at polyfill[.]io, which in 2024 introduced malicious code...impacted more than 100,000 websites.' and 'some sites using the service failed to clean all their pages over the past two years, so remnants of Polyfill code remained.' Supply chain software compromise persisting across 100K+ websites.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor JavaScript <script> tag sources pointing to known-compromised CDN domains. Scan for lingering references to polyfill.io or other deactivated malicious CDNs. Cross-correlate multiple unrelated legitimate sites loading from the same compromised external domain to identify coordinated supply chain compromise.

suggestion.title: Coordinated Malicious 401 Responses Across Enterprise Websites
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Toshiba and mega-retailer Muji warned...Zojirushi, FiNC Technologies, Ishiyaku Publishers, and online publishing brand Hobonichi were also impacted by the same issue...Samsung Smart TVs and websites also displayed a login prompt on June 1.' Multiple high-profile organizations hit simultaneously.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when multiple distinct organizations' websites simultaneously report or serve authentication prompts from the same external domain. Correlate incident timing, affected domains, and source CDN. Escalate when cluster size exceeds threshold (e.g., 3+ Fortune 500 sites in 7 days).

suggestion.title: Masquerading Authentication via Browser Native Dialog
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'User browsers...interpret that as a request for a username and password, so they serve a login prompt.' Attack leverages browser native UI to spoof legitimate authentication, avoiding detection of JavaScript-based fake login forms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for user credential entry immediately following HTTP 401 errors from unexpected external domains. Flag instances where authentication dialog timing does not align with expected login workflows. Detect cases where legitimate shopping/info-gathering sessions unexpectedly transition to authentication requests.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Third-Party Include Persistence Post-Incident
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'When the domain expired...While the deactivation of the service at polyfill[.]io stopped the redirections, some sites using the service failed to clean all their pages over the past two years, so remnants of Polyfill code remained.' Malicious includes persisted undetected for 2 years after initial incident.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Periodic source code scanning for script includes referencing deactivated or known-compromised domains. Flag any page serving JavaScript from polyfill[.]io, polyfill.com (if compromised), or other known-incident CDNs. Track remediation completion across website inventory to ensure no orphaned malicious includes remain.

suggestion.title: Serv-U Service Crash or Unexpected Termination
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'enables unauthenticated attackers to crash the service' — pipeline captured no impact detection despite this explicit DoS capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal Serv-U process termination, rapid restarts, or elevated error rates coinciding with external connection attempts. Establish baseline service uptime and alert on deviation from SLA.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Exploitation Attempt Against Serv-U CVE-2026-28318
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'unauthenticated attackers' exploiting the flaw — pipeline missed detection for the initial exploit vector itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect malformed or suspicious unauthenticated requests to Serv-U service ports (typically 22 for SSH/SFTP, 21 for FTP). Flag requests with crafted payloads, oversized inputs, or protocol violations characteristic of DoS fuzzing.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-28318 Patch Deployment Verification
suggestion.rationale: Given CISA KEV status and active exploitation, detection should include confirmation of patched systems — none recommended by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Asset inventory query for Serv-U installations; identify systems running vulnerable versions prior to published patch release date. Correlate with patch-deployment logs to track remediation.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager CVE-2026-20245 Exploit Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'actively exploited'—baseline exploitation detection is mandatory for active CVEs. No use case exists to detect attack attempts against the vulnerable management interface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST/GET requests to Cisco SD-WAN Manager management UI targeting known vulnerable endpoints. Correlate with 4xx/5xx error responses and repeat requests from external networks to identify exploit probing or active exploitation.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Unexpected Remote Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: If CVE-2026-20245 enables RCE (standard for 'high' SD-WAN vulnerabilities), post-exploitation command execution on the management appliance is probable attack path not covered by generated use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned by Cisco SD-WAN Manager service account (e.g., bash, sh, curl, wget). RCE exploits often execute shell commands to download/execute payloads or establish persistence. Baseline legitimate process trees from SD-WAN Manager are typically limited.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Lateral Movement via Stolen Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'no patch available'—organizations must rely on detection. Compromised SD-WAN managers have access to network overlay configuration and credentials to branch appliances. Missing UC for credential harvesting/lateral movement risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect attempts by SD-WAN Manager process to exfiltrate config files or authentication material (e.g., reads of /opt/cisco/dpm/certs, /opt/viptela/etc files). Correlate with DNS requests to external C2 or unexpected SSH/SNMP sessions initiated from the manager to branch devices outside normal change-control windows.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Version Inventory & Vulnerability Status
suggestion.rationale: Without patch, version identification becomes critical control. Pipeline generated no baseline asset-inventory use case to identify vulnerable SD-WAN Managers in the environment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scrape Cisco SD-WAN Manager web interface HTTP headers (e.g., Server, X-Version, or /api/system endpoint) to extract version. Flag any version <CVE-2026-20245 remediation threshold as vulnerable. Cross-reference against internal asset management to identify unpatched systems requiring compensating controls.

suggestion.title: Installation of Asin Spyware via Trojanized Apps
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes malware delivered through fake news, PDF, and war map applications. Pipeline should extract malicious APK names, package identifiers, and file hashes from article narrative and IOC sections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect installation of APKs matching Asin malware signatures, family package identifiers, or developer certificates. Alert on side-loaded installs of apps claiming to be news readers, PDF viewers, or map applications from untrusted sources targeting Arabic-speaking users.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Permission Requests from Fake Content Applications
suggestion.rationale: Spyware requires excessive permissions for surveillance. Fake 'content apps' requesting camera, contacts, location, microphone, and call logs indicate malicious intent—critical detection gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag runtime permission grants to news/PDF/map apps requesting sensitive data access (camera, contacts, call logs, location, microphone). Generate alerts when permission patterns misalign with app functionality.

suggestion.title: Command and Control Beaconing from Asin Spyware
suggestion.rationale: Spyware must exfiltrate collected data to C2. Article likely documents C2 domains or IP addresses in technical sections—these should be surfaced as network IOCs for firewall and DNS detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTPS/HTTP traffic from infected devices to known Asin C2 domains or IPs. Detect abnormal data volume bursts or encrypted tunneling (VPN, DNS) consistent with exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Keylogging and Input Capture
suggestion.rationale: Fake news/PDF/map apps are classic fronts for credential interception. Article likely documents keylogging or accessibility service abuse—critical for detection but entirely missing from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect keystroke logging, accessibility service registration abuse, or overlay attacks from installed apps. Monitor for abnormal input capture during credential-entry contexts (login screens, password fields).

suggestion.title: Android Persistence via Broadcast Receiver Registration
suggestion.rationale: Spyware must survive reboots. Android persistence mechanisms (BOOT_COMPLETED broadcasts, hidden services) should be extracted and mapped to T1402 persistence techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect native code execution triggered by system broadcasts (BOOT_COMPLETED, CONNECTIVITY_CHANGE). Monitor for hidden broadcast receiver registration or scheduled job execution from suspicious app contexts persisting across reboots.

suggestion.title: Targeted Phishing Campaign Against Arabic-Speaking Users
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies Arabic user targeting, indicating culturally-tailored social engineering. Phishing emails, SMS, or malicious URLs hosting APK downloads should be detected and attributed to Asin campaign infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify phishing messages with Arabic content or Middle East–themed lures directing installation of fake news/PDF/map apps. Correlate APK download events from Arabic-speaking geographic regions with subsequent Asin installation.

suggestion.title: Brickstorm Backdoor Execution on Non-EDR Targets
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'deployed Brickstorm to the victim's Egnyte Storage Sync appliance and to a retired Linux GroupWise email archive server.' Brickstorm is the primary persistence mechanism across multiple infrastructure targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Golang/Rust process spawning WebSocket-based outbound connections to suspicious C2 infrastructure. Focus on appliance-class targets (Egnyte, pfSense, NAS devices) where EDR is unavailable. Monitor for malware implants reaching back to attacker infrastructure on port 443 with WebSocket multiplexing patterns.

suggestion.title: SSL VPN Authorization Abuse via Compromised Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the attackers used stolen credentials to enable and configure SSL VPN access on the victim's firewall, then connected to internal systems.' Clear credential-driven persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag VPN authentication events preceded by unusual credential access patterns or successful auth from non-standard geolocations. Detect firewall configuration modifications enabling VPN access outside normal change windows. Correlate VPN sessions with subsequent lateral movement within 24 hours.

suggestion.title: Egnyte Storage Sync Persistence Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'compromised an Egnyte Storage Sync system and accessed it periodically through the victim's web SSL VPN.' Egnyte appliance was the initial foothold for weeks before M365 pivot.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious Egnyte sync authentication or file access patterns coinciding with VPN sessions. Monitor Egnyte appliance logs for repeated access from internal IPs after-hours or unusual file access sequences. Alert on Egnyte device becoming a bridge to cloud services (M365).

suggestion.title: Plenet (.NET Backdoor) Deployment to NAS Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'deployed the custom malware Plenet to a Synology NAS appliance. Plenet...offers interactive shell access, remote command execution.' Second-stage malware deployed to non-standard targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor NAS appliances (Synology, etc.) for unexpected .NET CLR process spawning or shell activity. Detect C2 beacons from NAS devices over WebSocket or non-standard protocols. Flag interactive shell sessions from NAS with exfiltration patterns.

suggestion.title: Python Reverse Shell Fallback Mechanism Detection (AgentPSD)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'AgentPSD is a simple Python-based reverse shell utility that Volexity believes VerdantBamboo used as a fallback persistence mechanism if other malware was no longer accessible.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python interpreter execution spawning reverse shell child processes (bash/cmd/powershell). Correlate Python execution on non-standard systems (NAS, appliances) with outbound socket connections to alternate C2 domains not seen before in environment.

suggestion.title: Long-Dwell Undetected Persistence Detection (18-Month Dwell Time)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'An investigation into the incident revealed that the threat actor had gained access to the victim network at least 18 months before detection' and 'the threat actor took the infrastructure offline before the researchers could reveal other systems.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate service account behavior (Egnyte sync, VPN access patterns, email archive access). Detect sustained, low-volume anomalies over months: periodic VPN sessions, Egnyte sync patterns, or M365 logins at unusual times. Prioritize detection of proxy/multiplexing C2 channels designed to evade CAP (Conditional Access Policies).

suggestion.title: POST Request with Content-Encoding: deflate to Serv-U
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names the attack signature: 'specially crafted POST requests that crash the Serv-U service without authentication using Content-Encoding: deflate.' This is the exact exploitation method.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST requests to Serv-U endpoints (ports 989, 990, 443, 21) containing Content-Encoding: deflate header. Article notes 'Serv-U does not require this functionality,' making any occurrence suspicious. Correlate repeated requests from single source IP within minutes as attack pattern indicator.

suggestion.title: Serv-U Service Crash or Unexpected Restart Spike
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability outcome: 'crash the Serv-U service.' Service termination is the direct impact indicator and detection opportunity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Serv-U service unexpected stops, crashes, or rapid restart sequences. Establish baseline for normal restarts per environment. Alert when restart frequency exceeds baseline or when restarts correlate temporally with POST request spikes in network logs within preceding 2-minute window.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Serv-U Version Inventory Alert
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerable scope: 'Serv-U 15.5.4 Hotfix 1' is the fix. Patch status = exploitability. Article implies 'no information on how many have already been patched' requiring inventory visibility.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset management for Serv-U versions <15.5.4 Hotfix 1. Flag any detected instance. Cross-reference with network-exposure data (Shodan: 12,000+ instances) to identify internet-facing unpatched targets. Alert on new deployments without patch or documented mitigation (limiting POST access).

suggestion.title: High-Volume POST Requests to Serv-U Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of 'uncontrolled resource consumption' weakness requires repeated requests to exhaust resources or trigger crash. Volumetric pattern is behavioral fingerprint of CVE-2026-28318 exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST request rate anomalies to Serv-U endpoints: flag single source IP sending >10 POST requests/minute or >50/hour to same target. Optionally filter to only Content-Encoding headers for high-confidence alerts. Baseline by environment and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Serv-U Reconnaissance Activity from External Scanners
suggestion.rationale: Article notes Shodan tracks 12,000+ exposed servers; attackers enumerate targets before exploitation. External scanning activity precedes active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound connection attempts to Serv-U ports (989, 990, 443 with Serv-U banner) from external IPs. Alert on enumeration patterns (rapid sequential connections across port ranges). Cross-reference source IPs against CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog feeds and threat intel on Serv-U scanner infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: SolarWinds Serv-U Instances (CVE-2026-28318)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Anything in CISA KEV is *currently* being exploited' and 'it's worth one quick check across your fleet'; mandatory inventory of public-facing Serv-U instances given federal patch due-date.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management system and network scanner output for SolarWinds Serv-U instances. Cross-reference patch status against CVE-2026-28318. Flag unpatched instances on internet-facing assets or DMZ for immediate escalation given CISA KEV status.

suggestion.title: HTTP POST with Deflate Encoding to Serv-U (CVE-2026-28318)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector: 'specially crafted POST requests using the Content-Encoding: deflate header to crash the Serv-U service without authentication'; requires network-level behavioral detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP traffic for POST requests with Content-Encoding: deflate targeting Serv-U endpoints. No authentication required. Correlate with Serv-U service crashes. Low FP risk: deflate is uncommon in modern web apps; flag all instances.

suggestion.title: Serv-U Service Crash or Restart Spike (CVE-2026-28318 Impact)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes impact as 'crash the Serv-U service'; consequence-based detection catches exploitation when POST logs unavailable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid Serv-U process termination and restart cycles (3+ restarts in 10 minutes). Monitor for CPU/memory exhaustion preceding crash. High confidence if preceded by external HTTP POST traffic or deflate-encoded requests.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-28318 Vulnerability Scan Match
suggestion.rationale: Article mandates federal patch due-date 2026-06-19; compliance requires scanner integration and alerting on new detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on CVE-2026-28318 detections in vulnerability scanner output. Track remediation against regulatory timeline. Escalate any findings on internet-facing or critical production systems immediately.

suggestion.title: Suspicious vScript Tenant Configuration Upload to vSmart
suggestion.rationale: Article provides explicit exploitation IOC: 'Tenant list upload per vsmart serial number: /usr/bin/vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh -cli path /home/admin/malicious.csv vpn 0'. This is the direct exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /var/log/scripts.log for vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh execution with file paths containing shell metacharacters, .csv uploads from /home/admin/, or command separators in parameters. Alert on any invocation with '-cli path' containing untrusted input.

suggestion.title: Netadmin Privilege Escalation via Authentication Bypass (CVE-2026-20182/20127)
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers require 'netadmin privileges' achieved via 'valid credentials or exploitation of CVE-2026-20182 or CVE-2026-20127'. These auth bypass CVEs are mandatory precondition steps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect authentication to vManage followed by immediate role escalation to netadmin without corresponding ticket/authorization. Flag repeated failed auth attempts or unusual auth patterns consistent with bypass exploitation.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Command Execution from vManage File Upload Handler
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability: 'insufficient validation of user-supplied input' allows 'arbitrary commands as root' via file upload. Article explicitly describes command injection leading to privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on root-level process spawning from vManage web service or tenant file handlers. Correlate with prior file upload activity or vScript execution. Flag shell commands (sh, bash, python) executed with UID 0 from vManage processes.

suggestion.title: Configuration Push to Edge Devices Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Cisco has observed limited cases where the exploitation of this bug resulted in a configuration change pushed to edge devices.' Post-exploitation impact indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect configuration push events from vManage to Catalyst edge devices. Flag pushes occurring within hours of detected exploit attempts, or pushes containing unusual/suspicious configuration parameters (new users, firewall rules, route changes).

suggestion.title: Malicious File Upload Targeting vManage Administrative Directories
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires 'uploading a crafted file' with example showing CSV file upload to /home/admin/. Indicates web-facing upload handler is vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vManage upload endpoints for .csv, .sh, .py files. Alert on uploads to /home/admin/ or other protected directories. Detect multi-part uploads with embedded shell commands, base64 payloads, or command separators.

suggestion.title: FIFA 2026 Phishing Domain Access Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly states 'Fake Sites' as primary attack vector. Pipeline failed to generate initial-access detection. Article establishes phishing to fraudulent FIFA-themed domains as entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and successful HTTP connections to newly-registered domains containing FIFA, World, Cup, 2026, or ticketing keywords with <30 day domain age. Flag access from corporate users; correlate against phishing report feeds and WHOIS bulletproof-hoster patterns.

suggestion.title: Banking Malware Execution Post-Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Article title cites 'Banking Malware' as explicit payload. No use case for malware execution detection despite clear attack stage. Common banking trojans exhibit file-system and browser injection patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect banking malware through behavioral signals: process hollowing, credential-store access (LSASS, browser-profile scraping), WebAuthn interception, legitimate-process injection, and C2 beaconing to non-standard ports. Alert on file downloads from phishing domains matched against banking malware signatures.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting Form Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly mentions 'Stolen Logins' as outcome. Pipeline missed detection for phishing kit infrastructure (fake login forms, POST credential exfiltration). Phrase 'Fake Sites' establishes credential-capture motive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for credential-stuffing POSTs to suspicious FIFA-related domains. Detect credential-form patterns in HTTP responses from newly-registered domains. Alert on users submitting passwords to domains flagged as phishing or unregistered 24 hours prior.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Banking Account Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Scam campaign establishes stolen login credentials; no detection for downstream banking abuse (unauthorized transfers, account takeover indicators). Article describes theft → malware → financial impact chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag successful bank logins from FIFA phishing referral IPs or within 1 hour of credential-form submission to phishing infrastructure. Alert on rapid fund-transfer initiation post-login, bot-like session patterns (WebDriver, headless browser signatures), or new device enrollment on compromised accounts.

suggestion.title: FIFA 2026 Typosquat Domain Registration Campaign
suggestion.rationale: Scam infrastructure relies on bulk domain registration for typosquats. No use case for detecting malicious domain registration patterns despite article establishing 'Fake Sites' as attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor domain registrations for FIFA, World Cup 2026, ticketing keywords using privacy registrars, bulletproof hosters, or newly-created registrant accounts. Correlate multiple domains sharing infrastructure (IP, registrar WHOIS email, nameserver) to identify registration campaign clusters.

suggestion.title: Malware Distribution from Phishing Pages
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes causal chain: 'Fake Sites' → 'Banking Malware.' No detection for file downloads from phishing domains or malware delivery via scam pages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on executable/script downloads from FIFA-phishing domains. Detect malware delivery via emails spoofing FIFA/ticketing services with malicious attachments. Match downloaded file hashes against banking malware family signatures and behavioral indicators.

suggestion.title: DbGate /runners/start JSON request body inspection for code injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'functionName value is interpolated directly into dynamically generated JavaScript source code via string concatenation.' Detection must decode and parse JSON POST bodies to /runners/start looking for JavaScript fragments in the functionName field (require, eval, spawn, exec, child_process). Current UC_21_3 detects the endpoint but not the payload.
log_sources: network proxy logs with request body capture
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: POST requests to /runners/start carrying JSON with JavaScript indicators (require, eval, Function constructor, child_process keywords) in the functionName or other parameters represent code injection attempts. Baseline: legitimate /runners/start requests should use simple function names, not function declarations or require statements.

suggestion.title: DbGate Node.js process spawning with stdout/stderr redirected to network sockets or temp files
suggestion.rationale: Article describes egress via 'shell/LOLBin children'—once code executes in Node.js, child processes must exfiltrate data. Look for node process spawning shell children AND immediately following creation of pipe/socket/file descriptors for data movement. UC_21_2 detects spawning; this adds the exfiltration connection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Node.js child processes (bash, sh, curl, wget) created within 10 seconds of a connection to external IP or opening /tmp temporary files indicate exfiltration. Alert if child_process stdout is redirected to a file descriptor bound to a socket.

suggestion.title: DbGate unauthenticated API request without valid session token
suggestion.rationale: Article states endpoint allows 'unauthenticated remote code execution.' Detection should baseline the presence/absence of authentication headers (Authorization, X-Auth-Token, session cookies) on requests to protected endpoints like /runners/start. Article mentions auth-bypass but doesn't detail whether normal deployments require auth headers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: POST requests to /runners/* endpoints from unknown source IPs WITHOUT valid Authorization header or session cookie are anomalous. Establish baseline of legitimate /runners/start traffic (with credentials) vs. unauthenticated POST payloads.

suggestion.title: UC_15_2: Unauthenticated POST to AIT-BSC /<name>/start with path-traversal form fields
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'remote client can Bypass the configured log root and direct BSC to log to arbitrary filesystem paths' via HTTP POST with attacker-controlled form fields containing path-traversal sequences (.., %2e%2e, /etc/, /home/, /root/, /var/, /tmp/, /usr/)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to endpoints matching */start with URI query or form parameters containing path-traversal strings. Aggregate by source IP, destination host, and URI path to identify scanners and exploitation attempts against vulnerable AIT-BSC instances.

suggestion.title: UC_15_3: ait-bsc process outbound TCP to public/non-baseline destination
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability allows arbitrary filesystem write via path traversal; attacker may exfiltrate captured packets or establish C2 by writing payloads to log-path destinations controlled by form fields
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ait-bsc or python processes (command-line indicators: ait-bsc, ait.core.bsc, ait_bsc, StreamCaptureManagerServer, bsc.yaml) for outbound TCP to non-RFC1918, non-loopback destinations. Flag connections to public IPs, especially non-standard ports or sustained data volume.

suggestion.title: UC_15_1: Behavioral hunt—CVE-2026-47731 exploitation artifact creation
suggestion.rationale: Article names specific POC executables (python_poc.py, attacker_tcp.py, dmc.py) and paths (/home/elias/ait-venv/, /var/opt/ait-bsc/logs) that exploitation would write via path-traversal; these artifacts have high fidelity as compromise indicators
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for process execution or file creation/modification of python_poc.py, attacker_tcp.py, dmc.py or writes to ait-venv/site-packages/ait/core/ paths. Cross-correlate with preceding HTTP POST to /start endpoint to establish full exploitation chain.

suggestion.title: WordPress Plugin Exploitation via Unauthenticated Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes 'Hackers Exploit Critical...Flaw' — indicates CVE-driven RCE or auth-bypass in plugin code path. No detection UC generated despite direct exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web server access logs for POST/GET requests to Everest Forms Pro plugin paths (/wp-content/plugins/everest-forms/) containing suspicious query strings or unusual payloads. Correlation with error_code 200 + subsequent unexpected database writes increases fidelity.

suggestion.title: Unexpected WordPress Admin User Creation
suggestion.rationale: 'Take Over Sites' explicitly indicates administrative compromise. No persistence-phase detection for account creation, which is the foothold post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on WordPress user creation events (wp_users INSERT) occurring outside business hours or from non-admin source IPs, particularly if preceded by failed/successful exploitation attempts to plugin endpoints within 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized WordPress Option / Database Modification
suggestion.rationale: Plugin exploitation will likely modify WordPress options table (admin_email, siteurl, etc.) or inject malicious content. Article's 'Take Over Sites' implies data modification for persistence. No UC captures post-exploitation database tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress wp_options table for modifications to security-critical keys (admin_email, siteurl, active_plugins) outside scheduled maintenance windows. Cross-reference with web access logs to identify the HTTP request that triggered the write.

suggestion.title: Everest Forms Pro Plugin Activity Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically names 'Everest Forms Pro' as attack vector. Pipeline should have generated a behavioral baseline detection for unusual plugin function calls, scheduled tasks, or file writes tied to the plugin directory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file writes to /wp-content/plugins/everest-forms/ outside of automated updates or deploy windows. Alert on execution of PHP scripts within the plugin directory that are not in the plugin's known code manifest.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Python package installation — typosquatting variant
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'package was crafted to look almost identical...single missing letter.' Attack vector is installation of deceptive package. No detection generated for install-time typosquatting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag pip install commands where package name has edit-distance-1 from known legitimate libraries (parsimonius ↔ parsimonious). Correlate with publisher reputation, account age, and installation velocity across fleet.

suggestion.title: PyPI supply-chain malicious package distribution
suggestion.rationale: Core attack pattern: 'deceptive Python package quietly made its way into PyPI repository, putting thousands of developers at risk.' This is supply-chain compromise, yet no T1195.001 technique was flagged and no distribution-phase detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PyPI package download/install events for: new publishers uploading packages, rapid adoption spike (thousands of installs in hours), packages with names one character away from established libraries, and unusual geographic/organizational distribution.

suggestion.title: Malicious Python package execution in development environment
suggestion.rationale: Article describes package achieving 'thousands of developers at risk,' implying execution when imported. Execution phase should trigger detections on module load, process spawning, or network connections from Python interpreters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Python interpreter process creation (python.exe, python3) for unsigned child processes, outbound network connections, or file writes to sensitive directories immediately following pip install of newly-registered packages.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Post-Install Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks on npm typically execute malicious code via postinstall hooks. Article title explicitly references npm worms and supply-chain compromise, which rely on script execution during package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm, yarn, or pnpm spawning unexpected child processes (bash, cmd, powershell) immediately after package installation. Flag processes launched from node_modules/.bin or similar package execution paths with suspicious command lines (curl, wget, python execution, registry modification).

suggestion.title: npm Dependency Tree Poisoning via Version Confusion
suggestion.rationale: Miasma and IronWorm variants described as 'new' suggests version-confusion or similar npm-specific supply-chain technique (e.g., typosquatting, dependency confusion). Article phrase 'supply chain attacks' implies dependency injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm install/update commands pulling from unexpected or newly-registered package registries, or package versions significantly older than expected. Cross-reference against known npm package databases (e.g., registry.npmjs.org) for unexpected latency or domain mismatches.

suggestion.title: Detection of Known Malware Package Names in Dependency Manifests
suggestion.rationale: IronWorm and Miasma are named malware families explicitly referenced in article title. Presence of these packages in package.json or lock files is a direct compromise indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create IOC list from article (IronWorm, Miasma, and any variant package names). Monitor package.json, package-lock.json, yarn.lock for exact matches. Alert on any npm install/download commands referencing these packages.

suggestion.title: Abnormal npm Registry Download Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks often involve mass or unusual package download patterns. Article contextualizes multi-malware infection vector (two worm families), suggesting widespread distribution pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTPS traffic to registry.npmjs.org (or private registries) for sudden volume spikes, rapid sequential package requests from non-development IPs, or downloads of packages not in organization's approved list.

suggestion.title: npm Package with Suspicious Metadata or Binary Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Worm variants in npm often bundle pre-compiled binaries or obfuscated code. Article's 'new variant' language suggests novel evasion techniques that would manifest as anomalous package contents.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Analyze package contents (via npm view, tarball inspection) for suspicious indicators: compiled binaries in unexpected directories, minified/obfuscated code without source maps, large file sizes relative to declared functionality, or .node files (native modules) that execute arbitrary code.

suggestion.title: Client-side JavaScript injection into payment form pages
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'malware has been discovered hiding inside one of the most trusted payment platforms.' Requires detection of unexpected or obfuscated JavaScript injected into payment domain responses that executes in user browsers during checkout.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate payment JavaScript libraries (Stripe.js, Braintree.js) by hash/fingerprint. Alert on supplementary or obfuscated JavaScript payloads served from payment domains, inline event handlers on form elements, or script injections detected by Content-Security-Policy violations.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of cardholder data to attacker-controlled Firebase project
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'uses Stripe...as both its command center and its data dump.' Explicit exfiltration phase sending stolen card data to firebaseio.com subdomain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on POST/PUT requests from payment pages to non-standard Firebase subdomains. Flag high-entropy payloads or base64-encoded data transferred from payment processing endpoints to cloud destinations. Monitor for batched exfil patterns.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized command-and-control via compromised Stripe infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'uses Stripe...as its command center'—attacker abuses legitimate payment service for C2 rather than external hosting. Implies unusual API calls or transaction manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Stripe/Braintree API call patterns for anomalies: unexpected source IPs, auth tokens used outside normal geographic/temporal windows, API calls not correlating with user session activity, unusual request sequences.

suggestion.title: Form data harvesting via malicious event handlers or memory access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'credit card skimming malware'—malware must read cardholder PAN, expiration, CVV from form inputs before encryption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect JavaScript accessing credit card input fields (by ID/name patterns like 'card', 'cc_number', 'cvv'), hooking form submit events, or reading localStorage/sessionStorage on payment pages. Alert on unusual event listeners added to payment forms post-load.

suggestion.title: Persistence of malicious code in payment service assets or CDN
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hiding inside...the most trusted payment platforms.' For malware to persist across users/sessions, code must be baked into served JavaScript or back-end components.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track cryptographic hashes of payment JavaScript assets. Alert on unexpected file modifications, new files in asset directories, CDN origin changes, or suspicious commits to payment infrastructure repositories. Monitor for backdoors in library dependencies.

suggestion.title: IIS Web Shell Deployment via Suspicious Script Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly mentions 'Custom Web Shell Framework'—the core persistence mechanism. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IIS application directories (e.g., wwwroot, inetpub) for suspicious file creation of scripting file types (.aspx, .asp, .ashx, .asmx) by unexpected processes or from external sources. Correlate with unusual IIS request patterns shortly after file creation.

suggestion.title: IIS w3wp.exe Spawning Unexpected Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: Web shells typically invoke cmd.exe or powershell.exe via IIS worker process. Article mentions 'custom framework' implying command execution capability—pipeline missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on w3wp.exe or iisexpress.exe spawning system utilities (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe, certutil.exe). Baseline legitimate child processes per application and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Anomalous POST Requests to IIS Handlers / Web Shell Comms
suggestion.rationale: Web shells receive commands via HTTP POST to scripting endpoints. Article specifies 'framework' pattern but pipeline generated no command-and-control detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag POST requests to .aspx/.asp files from non-standard User-Agents or with suspicious parameter patterns (base64, hex, obfuscated payloads). Correlate POST spike to persistence timeline if available.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of IIS Public-Facing Applications
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Targets Microsoft IIS Servers'—implies initial compromise of accessible IIS instance. Pipeline did not map to exploitation techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IIS logs for known vulnerability patterns (unusual HTTP methods, oversized payloads, encoded paths, multiple 4xx/5xx followed by successful requests). Flag requests that precede web shell file creation events.

suggestion.title: Registry Modification by IIS Worker Process
suggestion.rationale: Web shell frameworks often modify registry for persistence or configuration. Article mentions 'custom framework' but no defense-evasion detections proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on w3wp.exe or iisexpress.exe writing to HKLM or HKCU registry, especially Run keys, CLSID entries, or IIS configuration keys. Baseline application-specific registry access.

suggestion.title: Cloud Instance Malware Execution Detection (PCPJack)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'PCPJack Hijacks 230 AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure Servers' — indicates malware execution on cloud compute resources; pipeline surfaced no execution detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual process execution patterns on cloud VM instances, particularly execution of downloaders, obfuscated scripts, or SMTP-relay daemons. Monitor for process names or command lines consistent with mail-relay setup (postfix, sendmail, msmtpd spawned from unexpected parents). Correlate with cloud instance creation or security group rule modifications.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Outbound SMTP Relay Traffic from Cloud Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Covert SMTP Relay Network' — compromised servers are actively relaying SMTP traffic; no network detection use case for relay abuse was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag cloud instances initiating SMTP connections (port 25, 587, 465) to external IPs not whitelisted as corporate mail servers. Spike in outbound SMTP volume from instances previously showing no mail relay activity. Correlate with malware execution or persistence indicators.

suggestion.title: Cloud Credential Compromise or Overprivileged Access Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates attackers gained control of 230 instances across three cloud providers; suggests either credential compromise or exploit of existing access; no IAM-abuse detection included.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual API calls indicative of instance compromise: rapid EC2/VM creations, security group rule modifications, or IAM role assumption from anomalous source IPs. Alert on instances compromised from non-standard login paths or lateral-movement patterns within cloud account.

suggestion.title: Cloud Instance Security Configuration Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: 230 servers hijacked suggests security controls were either absent or bypassed; no detection for misconfigured or altered instance security posture.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on disabled or modified cloud security features: disabling CloudTrail, GuardDuty, or Cloud Logging; removing EDR agents; opening security groups to 0.0.0.0/0; or disabling firewall rules on multiple instances within a time window.

suggestion.title: Multi-Cloud Cross-Provider Attack Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically targets AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure; no correlation rule for simultaneous or rapid compromise across cloud providers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious authentication, API activity, or infrastructure changes across AWS, GCP, and Azure accounts in the same organization. Flag if the same source IP, user agent, or credential variant is observed compromising instances across multiple cloud providers within hours.

suggestion.title: SMTP Relay Infrastructure Persistence Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Covert SMTP relay implies persistent relay configuration (software install, cron jobs, systemd service); no persistence-layer detection included.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for installation or modification of mail relay services (postfix, sendmail, exim, msmtpd) on instances without corresponding change tickets. Alert on cron jobs, systemd timers, or rc.local entries that execute relay daemons or connectivity scripts at startup. Correlate with unauthorized package installations or binary modifications.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Modified by Malicious Agent Output
suggestion.rationale: Article addresses 'agentic world' and Claude Code GitHub action integration—implies AI models generating or suggesting workflow YAML modifications. No detection logic for agent-injected task definitions or action invocations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions workflow files (.github/workflows/*.yml) for inline command execution patterns or step definitions that invoke external scripts; correlate with agent-generated PR commits or comments. Flag runs where workflow modification precedes unexpected process spawning or credential access.

suggestion.title: Agent-Generated Code Access to Repository Secrets
suggestion.rationale: CI/CD security with agentic AI inherently risks malicious code accessing GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_KEY, or other injected secrets. No detection for exfiltration or anomalous secret usage post-agent-modification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag GitHub Actions jobs where environment variables (GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS credentials) are logged to stdout/stderr, or where agent-modified steps invoke external endpoints (curl, wget) immediately after secret-injection statements.

suggestion.title: Malicious PR Comments Injecting Code via Agent Invocation
suggestion.rationale: Article context (GitHub + agents) suggests attackers may use PR comments to trigger agent re-execution with malicious prompts. No detection for suspicious comment patterns or re-trigger patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub PR comments containing commands (e.g., '@claude-code fix this', 'generate deployment script') followed by new workflow runs or code commits within seconds. Prioritize first-time commenters or accounts with no prior repo activity.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Attack via Compromised Agent Model Output
suggestion.rationale: Agentic systems generating code for CI/CD implies downstream users will execute that code. A compromised or poisoned agent output could affect all consumers. No detection for poisoned artifact signatures or hash mismatches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track cryptographic signatures of generated artifacts (compiled binaries, container images) and alert on signature anomalies. Cross-reference agent invocation timestamps with artifact generation times; flag cases where generation occurs outside normal change windows.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Stolen GitHub Action Runner Tokens
suggestion.rationale: Article addresses CI/CD security; runners execute with elevated permissions. Agent-injected code could exfiltrate runner authentication tokens for lateral movement to other pipelines or services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for GitHub runner tokens used from IPs outside the organization's CI/CD provider. Alert on token reuse across unrelated repositories or multiple organizations within short time windows.

suggestion.title: Agent-Generated Secrets Leakage via Logging
suggestion.rationale: Agentic systems may inadvertently output secrets in generated code comments, debug logs, or error messages. No detection for structured secret patterns in GitHub commit history or action logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Regex-scan agent-generated code (commits, workflow files) for AWS key patterns (AKIA*), GitHub tokens (ghp_*), API key prefixes. Correlate with secret rotations and alert on hardcoded secrets appearing in any agent output.

suggestion.title: FFmpeg Memory Corruption Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states '21 Zero-Days in FFmpeg' but pipeline provided no use case for detecting exploitation. FFmpeg zero-days typically trigger via malicious media files causing crashes or memory access violations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for FFmpeg process crashes with abnormal exit codes (memory violation signatures). Detect FFmpeg spawning unexpected child processes immediately after processing untrusted media files. Alert on exception handling patterns consistent with buffer overflows or heap corruption.

suggestion.title: Chrome Sandbox Escape and Privilege Escalation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Chrome Patches Record 429 Bugs' but pipeline failed to surface detection rules. Chrome zero-days often include sandbox escape chains leading to SYSTEM-level code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect chrome.exe spawning processes with elevated privileges or unusual parent chains (chrome spawning cmd/powershell/rundll32 at higher integrity). Monitor for token impersonation attempts originating from chrome child processes. Alert on writes to system directories from chrome namespace.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Software Version Inventory and Enforcement
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies specific vulnerable software (FFmpeg, Chrome) but pipeline extracted no IOCs (CVE numbers, affected versions). Detection must enumerate and block known-vulnerable versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query installed FFmpeg and Chrome versions at startup or via EDR inventory. Cross-reference against published CVE version ranges from the disclosure. Block execution of unpatched versions or alert SOC for immediate patching.

suggestion.title: Malicious Media File Delivery and Processing Chain
suggestion.rationale: FFmpeg zero-days are triggered by processing malicious media files. Article context implies delivery mechanism (email, web, USB) but pipeline provided no detection for file-to-process correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious file downloads (unusual extensions, from external sources) with immediate FFmpeg execution. Flag media files from phishing emails or untrusted cloud shares processed by FFmpeg within <2 min. Alert on FFmpeg crashes within 10 seconds of file opening.

suggestion.title: Zero-Day Patch Compliance Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Record 429 Bugs' in Chrome patches. Pipeline should track patch deployment velocity and flag non-compliant endpoints to prevent exploitation window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Chrome and FFmpeg auto-update channels. Alert on endpoints failing to apply patches within 24-48 hours of release. Detect suspicious disabling of auto-update features (registry edits, policy bypass) or rollback to older versions post-patch.

suggestion.title: Heap/Buffer Overflow Behavioral Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: FFmpeg zero-days are memory-corruption vulnerabilities (heap/stack overflows). Pipeline offered no detection for exploitation behavior (crash patterns, exception codes, memory access violations).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create YARA/behavioral signatures for crash dumps or memory exception patterns. Detect unusual system call sequences (mmap/mprotect chains, ROP gadget setup) preceding FFmpeg crashes. Flag unhandled exceptions with specific fault addresses consistent with heap corruption.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article headline states vulnerability is 'actively exploited.' Pipeline extracted zero detection logic. Title alone establishes T1190 (exploit public-facing application) attack vector against Serv-U service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Serv-U ports (typically 22, 3389, or custom) with payloads containing known exploit signatures or abnormal request patterns (oversized Content-Length, encoded directives, SQL injection attempts). Correlate with subsequent failed authentication spikes or privilege-escalation indicators.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U Service Denial of Service Activity
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability described as 'DoS Flaw' in title. Pipeline failed to surface detection for availability impact phase. T1499 is core to this attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sustained connection floods to Serv-U endpoints, abnormal bandwidth consumption to affected host, or rapid service restart/hang patterns. Baseline normal connection/request rates and spike detection with 5-minute rolling window.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable SolarWinds Serv-U Instance Discovery
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV catalog addition implies organizations must identify exposure. Pipeline omitted discovery/inventory phase detection. No coverage for passive fingerprinting or banner-grabbing reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag successful Serv-U service identification via port scanning, SSH banner enumeration, or version-disclosure responses. Correlate scanner tools (Shodan queries, Nessus, Qualys) with enterprise IPs or external reconnaissance infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Serv-U Process Abnormal Behavior Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: If DoS includes service crash/hang or code-execution vector, behavior baseline is needed. Title does not exclude RCE pathway. Pipeline missing post-initial-access detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Serv-U process spawning unusual child processes, writing to unexpected directories, or executing scripts/binaries. Alert on service crash with memory dumps or core files in temp directories.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager CVE-2026-20245 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'actively exploited' — HTTP-based exploitation attempts against the management interface should be detectable via request pattern anomalies and payload inspection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Cisco SD-WAN Manager (typically port 8443) for requests matching known exploit patterns, unusual parameter combinations, or requests that bypass expected authentication sequencing. Correlate external IPs sending exploitation attempts with subsequent process creation or outbound C2 traffic from the SD-WAN Manager host.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation RCE Execution from SD-WAN Manager Process
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation means code execution is occurring post-vulnerability trigger — detect child process spawning or shell invocation under the SD-WAN Manager application context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any bash, sh, cmd.exe, or powershell.exe spawned as a child of the Cisco SD-WAN Manager process (java.exe, vmanage, etc.). Flag any process creation with suspicious parent-child relationships or from legitimate application PIDs running unusual command-line payloads.

suggestion.title: SD-WAN Manager Vulnerability Scanning and Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must first discover vulnerable SD-WAN Manager instances before exploitation — reconnaissance probes (version leaks, endpoint enumeration) precede active attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential probes against Cisco SD-WAN Manager endpoints (/api/version, /status, /login) from single source IPs. Flag unusual User-Agent strings, missing Host headers, or automated scanning patterns. Correlate reconnaissance activity with subsequent exploitation attempts from the same source.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised SD-WAN Manager to Branch/Hub Nodes
suggestion.rationale: SD-WAN controller compromise enables movement across the fabric; attackers leverage centralized management access to pivot to connected infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor the compromised SD-WAN Manager host for outbound management traffic (SSH, Telnet, IPSec, NETCONF) to branch routers, firewalls, and hub appliances not previously contacted. Flag configuration pushes or firmware updates initiated outside maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: SD-WAN Manager Data Exfiltration: Network Configuration and Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Compromise of a management plane exposes all network configurations, topology maps, and potentially stored credentials for connected devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large data transfers from the SD-WAN Manager process to external IPs, or bulk exports of configuration databases. Monitor for access to credential stores, configuration backups, or topology files followed by file compression or remote staging.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Cisco SD-WAN Manager Inventory Alert
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'no patch available' — asset inventory must flag all vulnerable instances until mitigation is deployed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Generate immediate priority alerts for any Cisco SD-WAN Manager instance matching CVE-2026-20245 vulnerable software versions. Escalate instances exposed to untrusted networks or the Internet for emergency segmentation or out-of-band access controls.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Free App Install on Smart TV Device
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: 'free apps are quietly turning smart TVs into web-scraping proxies'. Detection must cover app installation events. Smart TV app stores are a trusted delivery channel (T1199) being abused.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor app installation package manifests on Smart TV devices for unusual permissions (network proxy, background service, content scraping APIs). Flag apps requesting both HTTP/proxy permissions AND persistence mechanisms (boot triggers). Cross-reference app publisher reputation against known benign vendors.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Outbound Web Scraping from Smart TV
suggestion.rationale: Core mechanism: 'turning smart TVs into web-scraping proxies'. Detection needs network signal. Article indicates bulk requests to websites for AI training data harvest.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Smart TV devices making high-volume, repetitive HTTP requests to distinct content domains (news, articles, media sites) without user interaction patterns. Look for user-agent strings spoofing browsers, systematic crawl patterns (sequential page requests, robots.txt queries), or requests originating from background processes rather than the TV UI.

suggestion.title: Persistence Mechanism on Smart TV via Service or Autostart
suggestion.rationale: For web-scraping proxy to remain active across TV restarts, malicious app must establish persistence. 'Quietly' implies background/hidden execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of background services, launch daemons, or autostart executables spawned by third-party apps on Smart TV OSes (Android TV, Tizen, WebOS, RokuOS). Monitor for processes started outside user interaction windows or by system services that child off unexpected binaries related to HTTP/network operations.

suggestion.title: Command & Control Communication from Smart TV to Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Proxies require control. Article implies apps phone home to AI companies or scraping operators for job dispatch and data exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and HTTP POST/GET requests from Smart TV devices to unusual infrastructure (CDN backends, non-media domains, known cloud proxy providers). Correlate outbound connections with app lifecycle: app install → immediate C2 beaconing. Flag encrypted tunnels (VPN, proxy) initiated by apps.

suggestion.title: High Bandwidth Exfiltration of Web Content from Smart TV
suggestion.rationale: Scraped content must leave the device. Article describes data being harvested for AI training — large volume of page/media assets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sustained elevated outbound bandwidth from Smart TV devices, especially when paired with background process activity. Look for data exfiltration to IP ranges owned by AI/LLM companies or hosting providers in bulk-data-handling business. Correlate with web-scraping request patterns (incoming HTTP traffic mirror in outgoing flows).

suggestion.title: Resource Exhaustion on Smart TV (CPU/Memory/Network)
suggestion.rationale: Continuous web scraping is computationally expensive. Users may notice 'quiet' malicious activity through device slowdown, fans, heating.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on anomalous sustained CPU, memory, and network I/O consumption from third-party apps on Smart TVs, especially during user-inactive periods (night, weekend). Correlate spikes with app installation dates. Compare baseline resource usage post-app install vs. pre-install.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthorized Changes to GitHub Repository Branches
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes worm hitting '73 Microsoft GitHub Repositories' — implies malicious code commits or branch modifications. Pipeline failed to surface detection for repository tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub audit logs for unexpected commits, branch deletions, or merge operations from accounts without typical contribution history. Correlate with unusual times-of-day and IP geolocation anomalies. Alert on commits introducing known malware signatures or obfuscated payloads.

suggestion.title: Detect Suspicious Package Artifacts in Microsoft-Controlled Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack context implies malware distributed through compromised packages. Title mentions 'worm' payload in repositories — should detect binary/executable artifacts in source control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on executable, DLL, or compiled artifacts committed to Microsoft GitHub repositories outside of expected build directories. Cross-reference against repo's historical file types. Flag commits with no associated pull request or code review.

suggestion.title: Detect Abuse of GitHub Deploy Keys or CI/CD Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Successful compromise of 73 repositories suggests credential theft or deploy key abuse. Article doesn't describe attack vector but supply chain context implies automated access. Pipeline missed this critical access control angle.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub for deploy key creation, API token generation, or SSH key additions outside normal deployment windows. Correlate with failed authentication attempts and access from non-corporate IP ranges. Alert on deploy keys used from geographic locations inconsistent with maintainer history.

suggestion.title: Detect Mass Repository Modification Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies '73' repositories affected — indicates coordinated, bulk attack. Pipeline should have generated use case for detecting synchronized anomalous activity across multiple repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect patterns of commits pushed to multiple repositories within a short time window (e.g., >5 repos in 1 hour) from single account or API token. Baseline normal contribution patterns per developer. Flag when commit messages, file types, or code style deviate from repository norms.

suggestion.title: Detect Download or Execution of Binaries from Compromised GitHub Releases
suggestion.rationale: Worm distribution through GitHub implies build artifacts or release binaries were compromised. Detection should cover downstream consumption of malware via release pages and package managers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PowerShell/curl downloads of binaries from Microsoft GitHub release pages. Correlate with failed code signature validation and execution from temp directories. Cross-reference downloaded hashes against known Miasma malware signatures.

suggestion.title: Detect GitHub OAuth Token Leakage and Malicious Use
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks often pivot through leaked credentials. '73 repositories' scale suggests either shared infrastructure compromise or token harvesting. Pipeline should detect abnormal token usage patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub API token usage from non-standard clients, unusual geographies, or API calls inconsistent with token owner's role (e.g., admin actions from read-only token). Flag tokens accessing >10 repositories in 24 hours.

suggestion.title: Sideloaded Android App Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references malware distributed via 'Fake News, PDF and War Map Apps'—masqueraded as legitimate applications to drive installation. Title establishes app-as-vector but pipeline captured nothing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for installation of APK files from non-standard sources (Downloads folder, email attachments, WebView). Flag app installation events where package name contains lookalike strings (e.g., 'news', 'pdf', 'map' with typos or suffixes). Correlate against Google Play signatures.

suggestion.title: Excessive Android App Permission Requests
suggestion.rationale: Spyware classification ('Asin Targets Arabic Users') implies data collection—requires permissions for contacts, location, call logs, message access. Pipeline did not surface permission-granting as a detection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on app permission grants for PERMISSION_ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION, READ_CONTACTS, READ_CALL_LOG, READ_SMS, RECORD_AUDIO when granted to applications with recent install dates or non-standard publisher certificates. Baseline expected permissions per app category.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Network Beaconing from App UIDs
suggestion.rationale: Spyware must exfiltrate collected data; article title implies collection of sensitive data from Arabic users. Pipeline omitted command-and-control detection despite 'spyware' classification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network traffic initiated by recently-installed or suspicious app UIDs for unusual patterns: C2-like domains (low reputation, newly registered, no legitimate sinkhole history), suspicious ports (non-standard for app category), high-frequency beaconing, or encrypted tunnels to unknown ASNs.

suggestion.title: Malicious App Binary Obfuscation & Entropy
suggestion.rationale: Android spyware typically employs packing/obfuscation to evade static analysis. Article provides no IOCs (signature hashes, domains); pipeline should have flagged when these are absent but threat is confirmed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On app installation, compute entropy of DEX sections and native libraries. Flag entropy >7.5 (high obfuscation) combined with app requesting sensitive permissions. Cross-reference against known packers (UPX, YGuard, ProGuard anomalies).

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Contact & Geolocation Data
suggestion.rationale: Spyware explicitly targets users for data collection; article should enumerate what is stolen (contacts, location, messages, call history). Pipeline generated zero collection-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk reads from contacts database (ContentProvider queries to com.android.contacts) or GPS location APIs (FusedLocationProvider, LocationManager) followed by network writes to non-standard endpoints. Correlate timing and volume with known C2 intervals.

suggestion.title: Brickstorm Backdoor C2 Activity Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states Brickstorm 'undetected in environments of various targets...for more than a year.' Describes it as 'advanced malware implant' with Golang and Rust variants. Specifically notes researchers 'created a fingerprint to identify IP addresses and domains Brickstorm used for C2 communication' and deployed to Egnyte, pfSense, Linux systems. Phrase: 'Between September 18 and September 23, all of the servers previously matching this pattern turned off their services on port 443.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for WebSocket protocol anomalies on non-standard ports from infrastructure appliances (Egnyte, Synology, firewall) without EDR; fingerprint Brickstorm's TLS certificate/cipher suite patterns observed during investigation; correlate successful Golang/Rust process execution on infrastructure with outbound HTTPS connections to known C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Plenet/.NET Backdoor Execution on NAS Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies Plenet as 'cross-platform .NET-based backdoor' offering 'interactive shell access, remote command execution, file manipulation' and states 'deployed the custom malware Plenet to a Synology NAS appliance' after re-establishing access. Notes it uses 'WebSocket protocol for C2 communications and a multiplexing library for simultaneous data streams.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .NET assembly execution or loading on Synology/Linux-based appliances (anomalous for patched systems); detect WebSocket library imports (System.Net.WebSockets) compiled into executables on infrastructure; monitor SSH/Telnet sessions spawning shells or downloading binaries to NAS devices.

suggestion.title: SSL VPN Firewall Configuration Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'used stolen credentials to enable and configure SSL VPN access on the victim's firewall' and deployed Brickstorm to MSP's pfSense firewall compromised 'at least 18 months earlier.' Represents infrastructure-level persistence mechanism distinct from endpoint malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect firewall administrative access and SSL VPN configuration changes outside maintenance windows using historical baselines; alert on new VPN user accounts created with non-standard naming or linked to compromised credentials; monitor for firewall certificate replacements or route modifications following access logs from multiple IP geographies.

suggestion.title: Conditional Access Policy Evasion via Proxy Relaying
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Volexity assesses with high confidence that this was done to blend in with legitimate network traffic and evade Conditional Access policies' using Brickstorm's 'proxying features' to access Microsoft 365. Attackers used 'stolen credentials' through this proxy layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate M365 sign-in events originating from homogeneous source IPs (internal VPN) with impossible-travel patterns or ASN mismatches; detect successful Conditional Access exemptions or policy modifications; monitor for sign-in anomalies (unusual time-of-day, geo, user-agent) immediately following Brickstorm C2 activity windows.

suggestion.title: Multi-Vector Infrastructure Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attack spans appliance types: 'Egnyte Storage Sync system...accessed it periodically through the victim's web SSL VPN,' then 'deployed additional custom malware to a Synology NAS device' and 'Brickstorm was then deployed to the victim's Egnyte Storage Sync appliance and to a retired Linux GroupWise email archive server.' Targets 'systems that do not support endpoint detection and response (EDR) solutions.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for malware staging/deployment chains across heterogeneous infrastructure (storage, firewall, NAS, archive servers); detect living-off-the-land tool usage (curl, wget, bash, ssh) to download payloads to systems assumed to have minimal access controls; baseline legitimate file writes to appliances and alert on suspicious binary/script creation.

suggestion.title: AgentPSD Python Reverse Shell Fallback Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies AgentPSD as 'simple Python-based reverse shell utility' deployed as 'fallback persistence mechanism if other malware was no longer accessible' and 'configured to connect to a different domain than the one Brickstorm used.' Indicates intentional redundancy in persistence strategy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python interpreter (python.exe, python3, python2.7) with network socket operations or subprocess spawning (/bin/bash, cmd.exe); monitor for scheduled persistence (crontab entries, Windows scheduled tasks) executing Python scripts; correlate AgentPSD C2 domain connections with secondary ASN or geolocation distinct from primary Brickstorm infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Detect HTTP POST with Content-Encoding: deflate to Serv-U Services
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'specially crafted POST requests that crash the Serv-U service without authentication using Content-Encoding: deflate.' This is the attack signature; detection baseline is mandatory.
