suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Populate signatures database with Miasma worm indicators: file hashes, process command-line patterns, C2 domains, and execution artefacts from incident disclosures. Flag process creation or downloaded artifacts matching known Miasma infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Installation of durabletask PyPI Package
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly concerns compromised durabletask package on PyPI. Must detect suspicious or malicious version installs: 'Microsoft's durabletask PyPI Package Compromised'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor pip install, python -m pip, and setuptools execution for durabletask package requests, especially targeting version ranges that overlap the compromise window. Alert on installation of versions outside normal enterprise distribution practices.

suggestion.title: Malicious Code Execution from Installed durabletask Package
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks inject executable code that runs at import or install time. Article describes package compromise implying code execution: 'Compromised in Supply Chain Attack'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of Python interpreters with unusual parent processes (pip/setuptools), unusual child processes spawned by Python, or unexpected network connections from python.exe shortly after package installation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Imports from Compromised durabletask Module
suggestion.rationale: Malicious PyPI packages typically execute on import. Must track import patterns from the compromised namespace.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Python process AST or import hooks for 'from durabletask' or 'import durabletask' statements in non-development environments. Cross-reference source file locations against known package directories to detect trojanized imports.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Network Activity from Python Process Post-Installation
suggestion.rationale: Compromised packages often establish command-and-control callbacks. Article describes attack implying callback infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Python process execution (post-durabletask installation) with outbound network connections to non-standard ports or newly registered domains. Alert on connections from processes without prior network baseline.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Writes to Python Site-Packages Directory
suggestion.rationale: Package installation modifies site-packages; monitor for post-installation tampering or lateral writes: 'compromised' implies file modification
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag file creation or modification under Python site-packages (or .local/lib/python*) directories outside normal pip/setuptools processes, especially targeting durabletask namespace or __init__.py files.

suggestion.title: PyPI Repository Audit — Unauthorized Package Versions
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks alter version metadata or inject malicious versions. Article title indicates package was compromised on PyPI itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PyPI API calls and package repository logs for unauthorized version uploads, metadata tampering, or version yanks on durabletask. Cross-check against expected release schedules.

suggestion.title: Android APK Installation - Spoofed News/Map App Package
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes delivery via 'Fake News, PDF and War Map Apps.' Pipeline generated zero detections for suspicious APK installation patterns despite this being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for APK installations with package names matching common news/map/PDF readers but with atypical publishers or installation source (sideload, non-Play Store). Correlate to device enrollment and geolocation targeting Arabic-language-configured devices. Flag installations from unsigned or self-signed certificates.

suggestion.title: Android Excessive Permission Requests - Contact/Call Interception
suggestion.rationale: Spyware designation implies collection of contacts, call logs, and messages. Article describes 'spyware' functionality but pipeline generated no detection for the permission-acquisition stage preceding data theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on apps installed in the past 7 days requesting READ_CONTACTS, READ_CALL_LOG, READ_SMS, or RECORD_AUDIO permissions. Correlate to process execution invoking TelephonyManager or ContactsProvider APIs immediately post-install. Flag if permissions are granted without user interaction logs or are granted to non-Play-Store-verified apps.

suggestion.title: Android Network Exfiltration - Anomalous C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Spyware must maintain persistent communication with command infrastructure for telemetry and tasking. Pipeline identified no C2-related kill-chain phase or detection use case despite this being implicit in the threat description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for network connections initiated by newly installed news/map/PDF apps to non-standard ports (not 80, 443, or common app CDN ranges). Flag DNS queries for domains with low or zero historical reputation, particularly those serving Arabic regions. Correlate to data exfiltration volumes (contact count * bytes) within 24-48h post-installation.

suggestion.title: Android Sideloaded APK - Missing Play Store Signature Verification
suggestion.rationale: Delivery via fake app stores or direct sideload implies signature-bypass or unsigned APK installation. Article specifies 'Fake News' apps but pipeline generated no detection for out-of-band APK deployment mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect APK files written to device storage or installed via `pm install` without Play Store signature verification chain. Alert if installation source is third-party app store, direct .apk file, or MDM bypass. Correlate to device reaching out to non-Google package-distribution infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Android Spyware - Delayed Malicious Payload Execution
suggestion.rationale: Android spyware commonly delays capabilities (sleep, anti-analysis) post-install. Article contains 'spyware' but pipeline provided no detection for dormancy-then-activation patterns that distinguish targeted malware from commodity adware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for apps installed 3-14 days prior that suddenly activate network egress, file I/O, or permission-gated API calls (contacts, call logs) without user-visible UI. Flag if activation is triggered by geolocation change (e.g., entering specific Arabic-speaking country) or calendar-based timers rather than direct user action.

suggestion.title: Arabic-Localized Malware Distribution - Fake App Store Network
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Arabic Users' targeting and 'Fake' app delivery. Pipeline did not reconstruct the social-engineering campaign or distribute-via-fraudulent-marketplace attack pattern that contextualizes threat scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Arabic-language phishing campaigns or fake marketplace referrals (fake Play Store clone URLs, Telegram/WhatsApp links) hosting the malicious APKs. Monitor for domains mimicking legitimate app stores with high registration-to-delivery velocity. Correlate user clicks on Arabic-language news or geopolitical content to subsequent APK installs within 48h.

suggestion.title: Detect WebSocket C2 Communications from Brickstorm/Plenet
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'using the WebSocket protocol for C2 communications and a multiplexing library for simultaneous data streams to the server.' No detection use case generated for protocol-based C2 identification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound WebSocket connections (ws:// or wss://) from servers lacking legitimate WebSocket dependencies. Monitor for multiplexed stream patterns, connection cycling, and correlation with known APT infrastructure IPs or suspicious destination geographies.

suggestion.title: Detect Python Reverse Shell Execution (AgentPSD Fallback)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'AgentPSD is a simple Python-based reverse shell utility that Volexity believes VerdantBamboo used as a fallback persistence mechanism.' No detection for Python reverse shells or script-based backdoors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on python/python3 spawning with network libraries or reverse-shell indicators. Monitor execution from temp directories and correlate with outbound network connections to attacker-controlled ranges. Flag AgentPSD-configured C2 domains if available.

suggestion.title: Detect Cross-Platform Malware Deployment to Network Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Brickstorm was then deployed to the victim's Egnyte Storage Sync appliance and to a retired Linux GroupWise email archive server' and 'planted a BSD variant of Brickstorm on a pfSense firewall.' No detection for appliance-targeted backdoors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected binary deployment to pfSense, Synology NAS, Egnyte, and email appliances outside patching windows. Alert on Golang/Rust/BSD executables, compilation artifacts, or shell execution on appliances. Correlate with VPN session and administrative access timelines.

suggestion.title: Detect MSP-to-Victim Lateral Movement via Compromised Shared Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'Volexity concluded that this firewall, like the victim organization's Storage Sync system, had also been compromised at least 18 months earlier' and 'The researchers have medium confidence that the attacker pivoted from the MSP into the victim organization's environment.' No detection for supply-chain pivot vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect administrative access from MSP infrastructure to customer environments using shared credentials, especially outside business hours or from hosting-provider IP ranges. Alert on firewall configuration changes immediately after MSP VPN login. Monitor for credential spraying patterns across MSP-managed client bases.

suggestion.title: Detect Stolen Credentials Enabling VPN Reconfiguration for C2 Evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'attackers used stolen credentials to enable and configure SSL VPN access on the victim's firewall' and 'From this foothold and using Brickstorm proxying features and stolen credentials, the threat actor accessed the organization's Microsoft 365 environment' to 'blend in with legitimate network traffic and evade Conditional Access policies.' No detection for credential-driven firewall/VPN changes enabling evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on VPN reconfiguration or SSL VPN access changes performed by valid accounts outside normal administrative windows. Correlate with M365 access attempts using the same credentials from the newly-enabled VPN IP. Flag accounts used for both VPN configuration and Conditional Access policy bypass attempts.

suggestion.title: Detect .NET Backdoor Deployment to NAS Storage (Plenet/Grimbolt)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'they deployed the custom malware Plenet to a Synology NAS appliance. Plenet, also tracked as 'Grimbolt' by Google, is a cross-platform .NET-based backdoor that offers interactive shell access, remote command execution, file manipulation.' No detection for .NET malware on non-standard platforms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unexpected .NET runtime or CLR assembly execution on NAS systems that do not normally run .NET code. Alert on Synology/storage appliances executing binary types outside their firmware baseline. Monitor for cross-platform .NET binaries with socket or network capabilities deployed post-compromise.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U POST Request with Content-Encoding Deflate Header
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'specially crafted POST requests that crash the Serv-U service without authentication using Content-Encoding: deflate.' This is the primary attack signature and sole technical IOC provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on POST requests to Serv-U listening ports (default 21, 990, 443, 80) containing 'Content-Encoding: deflate' header, especially from untrusted sources. Correlate with Serv-U process crashes, service restarts, or latency spikes on target hosts. Baseline legitimate Content-Encoding usage first.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U Unexpected Process Termination or Service Restart
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'crash[es] the Serv-U service' — direct impact is DoS via service failure; this is detectable via process/service monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected crashes or rapid restarts (>3 in 10 minutes) of Serv-U service processes. Alert on correlated HTTP POST traffic with unusual header combinations immediately preceding crashes. Flag multiple crashes across fleet as distributed DoS campaign.

suggestion.title: Inventory: SolarWinds Serv-U Version <15.5.4 Hotfix 1
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies patched version (15.5.4 Hotfix 1) released June 5, 2026; CISA mandated patch deadline is June 19. Unpatched instances are exploitable targets currently under active attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset management/CMDB or software inventory tools for Serv-U installations with version <15.5.4 Hotfix 1. Cross-reference with Shodan/Shadowserver internet-facing asset lists. Escalate to patch management immediately given active exploitation and mandatory compliance deadline.

suggestion.title: HTTP POST Requests to Serv-U with Anomalous or Missing User-Agent
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'low-complexity attacks' via unauthenticated POST — implies potential use of automated tools or legitimate-looking requests; User-Agent anomalies may indicate scanner/exploit tools.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to Serv-U ports for missing, suspicious, or scanner-like User-Agent headers (e.g., curl, Nmap, Metasploit variants). Establish baseline of expected User-Agents for Serv-U clients; alert on deviations combined with deflate or other unusual Content-Encoding values.

suggestion.title: Serv-U POST Request with deflate Content-Encoding
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'specially crafted POST requests using the Content-Encoding: deflate header'. This is the attack signature—the mechanism by which the vulnerability is exploited.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for HTTP POST requests to Serv-U endpoints (port 22, 3389, or known Serv-U listeners) containing header Content-Encoding: deflate from non-whitelisted sources. Flag any requests originating from internet-facing IPs. Correlate with subsequent service restart or crash events.

suggestion.title: Serv-U Service Crash or Abnormal Termination
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'crash the Serv-U service without authentication'. Post-exploitation impact is immediate service denial, detectable via process termination or restart logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Serv-U process (srvuserv.exe / srvuagent.exe) unexpected termination or rapid restart cycles within short time windows. Cross-correlate with network logs to confirm POST requests preceded the crash. High-confidence indicator of exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: Serv-U HTTP 5xx Error Spike
suggestion.rationale: Article describes resource consumption causing service crash. Crashed or unstable service generates HTTP 5xx responses; 'uncontrolled resource consumption' will manifest as degraded performance before full crash.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Serv-U-facing web server logs for sudden increase in HTTP 500/503 responses. Set baseline for normal error rate; alert on deviation >3σ within 5-minute window. Correlate spike with POST requests from external IPs.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Serv-U Exploitation Attempt (No Auth Session)
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'without authentication'. Normal legitimate traffic involves session establishment; exploitation POCs will attempt POST directly without prior login/auth token.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to Serv-U endpoints that lack valid session cookies or authentication tokens. Flag requests from sources with no prior successful login in the current session or historical access logs.

suggestion.title: Suspicious vScript File Upload Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by uploading a crafted file to the affected system.' No detection for file uploads preceding privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file uploads to Cisco SD-WAN vManage system, especially to admin directories (/home/admin/*) followed by execution of vScript commands. Cross-correlate file creation timestamps with script invocation logs.

suggestion.title: vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh Execution with Anomalous Arguments
suggestion.rationale: Article provides log signature: 'Tenant list upload per vsmart serial number: /usr/bin/vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh -cli path /home/admin/malicious.csv vpn 0'. No detection for this specific script execution pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of /usr/bin/vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh with file paths pointing to /home/admin/ or non-standard vpn arguments. Requires parsing vmanage vScript log entries for script invocation anomalies.

suggestion.title: Tenant Configuration Upload to vSmart Controllers
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'uploading tenant configuration data to vSmart controllers to escalate privileges through legitimate commands' and 'configuration change pushed to edge devices.' No detection for unauthorized config transfers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /var/log/scripts.log for 'Tenant list upload' entries correlating netadmin-privilege actions with subsequent vSmart controller communication. Alert on config data transfers from vManage to edge devices initiated by non-administrative processes.

suggestion.title: Root Command Injection via Malicious CSV Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exploit this vulnerability by uploading a crafted file...perform command injection attacks...elevate privileges as root user.' No detection for file content inspection or post-upload command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file uploads with names matching *malicious* or unusual CSV patterns to subsequent execution of commands under root context. Look for shell metacharacters or command separators in uploaded file metadata parsed by vScript.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Edge Device Configuration Push
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Cisco has observed limited cases where exploitation resulted in a configuration change pushed to edge devices.' No detection for suspicious config modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on configuration pushes from vManage to Catalyst SD-WAN edge devices immediately following successful privilege escalation indicators. Baseline legitimate config change frequency and flag anomalous bulk pushes.

suggestion.title: Low-Privilege Netadmin Behavior Anomaly Leading to Root Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attacker must have netadmin privileges...execute arbitrary commands as root.' No detection for privilege escalation from low-privilege authenticated role.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag sequences where netadmin-authenticated sessions execute commands or upload files followed by shell commands executing as root (uid=0). Establish baseline of normal netadmin activities and detect privilege boundary violations.

suggestion.title: Suspicious FIFA 2026 Ticketing Domain Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Fake Sites' luring users to phishing endpoints. Article: 'Fake Sites, Banking Malware, and Stolen Logins'—fake domains are initial attack vector for credential theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and web proxy logs for domains mimicking FIFA.com, fifa2026.com, or regional ticketing sites. Flag newly registered domains with FIFA keywords registered within 90 days. Correlate with SSL certificate issuance for lookalike domains.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting Form Submission to Fake FIFA Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Stolen Logins'—pipeline should detect credential entry on malicious sites. Fake FIFA ticketing sites are designed to harvest email and password credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to fake FIFA domains containing form-encoded credentials (username/password fields). Correlate with user login attempts to legitimate services within 24 hours using the same credentials, indicating credential stuffing or account takeover.

suggestion.title: Banking Malware Execution Post-Download from Malicious FIFA Site
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists 'Banking Malware' as delivery vector. Pipeline should create detections for malware execution following fake site compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation and DLL injection patterns consistent with banking trojans (e.g., Emotet, IcedID, Qbot) following downloads from newly registered or flagged domains. Flag code signing anomalies (unsigned or invalid certificates) on executables from FIFA scam sites.

suggestion.title: Credential Misuse Post-Theft (Impossible Travel / Out-of-Region Login)
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Stolen Logins'—compromised credentials will be used from attacker infrastructure, enabling detection via behavioral anomaly. Success requires detecting login anomalies after credential theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After credential compromise, detect logins from IPs/geolocations impossible given user's baseline. Trigger alerts for first-time logins from Tor, residential proxies, or foreign infrastructure within 12-48 hours of credential harvesting. Correlate with failed MFA attempts.

suggestion.title: Banking Data Exfiltration via Banking Malware C2 Channel
suggestion.rationale: Article implies banking malware—standard banking trojans exfiltrate account credentials and session tokens. Pipeline should detect data theft post-execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTPS/TCP traffic from infected hosts to known banking malware C2 IP ranges or domains. Flag abnormal certificate pinning bypass attempts. Detect beaconing patterns (periodic, small-volume encrypted outbound traffic) consistent with malware callback.

suggestion.title: Suspicious SSL Certificate for FIFA Lookalike Domains
suggestion.rationale: Fake FIFA sites require HTTPS (modern browsers require it). Monitoring CT logs and certificate issuance for FIFA keyword domains enables early detection before credential harvesting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Certificate Transparency logs for newly issued certificates containing 'FIFA', 'World Cup', '2026', or domain permutations. Flag certificates issued by known-abused CAs (especially free tier). Alert on certificates for domains registered within 48 hours of issuance.

suggestion.title: DbGate unauthenticated endpoint access — successful POST /runners/start without auth token
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution' and attack vector is 'POST /runners/start'. Pipeline should detect successful (HTTP 200–299) requests to this endpoint without authentication credentials or with anonymous/default credentials, which is the initial-access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for POST requests to /runners/start or /runners/load-reader that return HTTP 200–299 status, originating from public IPs or untrusted networks, to instances where DbGate is exposed. Correlate with absence of Authorization or authentication headers in proxy/WAF logs.

suggestion.title: JSON payload injection — 'functionName' parameter in /runners/start POST body
suggestion.rationale: Article core: 'functionName value is interpolated directly into dynamically generated JavaScript source code via string concatenation.' The injection point is the JSON payload structure, not just the HTTP method/URL. Pipeline missed detection of the actual malicious payload syntax.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to /runners/start with JSON body containing 'assign' commands and 'functionName' fields with shell metacharacters, command substitution syntax ($(..),`..`), or script injection patterns. Requires WAF/proxy logging that captures request bodies.

suggestion.title: Node.js child_process module execution via code injection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies the RCE mechanism: 'executed in a forked Node.js child process.' This is distinct from generic shell-child-spawning and relates to Node.js runtime abuse (require/import of child_process module). Detection should look for Node.js process spawning children via child_process.spawn() or .exec().
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Node.js processes with command-line arguments containing 'child_process', 'spawn', 'exec', or 'fork' (if captured in process command line), or Node.js spawning atypical children (shells, compilers, interpreters) within seconds of receiving an HTTP POST to /runners/start.

suggestion.title: DbGate bundle.js or .dbgate runtime directory writes post-compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions paths like '/home/dbgate-docker/bundle.js' and '/.dbgate/run/' as DbGate runtime locations. Post-exploitation, adversary may persist or deploy tools by writing to these directories. Detection should monitor for unauthorized file creation/modification in these locations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file-creation or file-modification events in DbGate directories (/home/dbgate*, /.dbgate/run/*, ~/.dbgate/*) where the initiating process is NOT the legitimate DbGate daemon or package manager.

suggestion.title: Egress command execution — Node.js spawning wget/curl/nc immediately post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation resulting in Node.js child process spawning 'LOLBin' utilities for egress. UC_28_2 covers this but assumes immediate child spawn; missed is the temporal signature: egress tool execution within T seconds of exploit POST request, linking the HTTP request to process spawning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful POST /runners/start requests with Node.js spawning wget, curl, nc, bitsadmin, or certutil within a 30-second window on the same host. Include egress connections (non-local IP) initiated by the spawned child process.

suggestion.title: DbGate unauthenticated auth endpoint enumeration (CVE-2026-47669 initial access)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'the none auth provider issues JWT tokens without credentials via POST /auth/login'—yet no UC detects this anomalous behavior. Unauthenticated token issuance is the gateway for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to /api/auth/login returning HTTP 200 without corresponding Authorization header, client certificate, or credential submission. Baseline legitimate DbGate auth patterns and alert on requests from external/untrusted networks or high-volume enumeration.

suggestion.title: ZIP file upload + extraction correlation with /api/archive/unzip (CVE-2026-47669 exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'POST to /api/archive/unzip with malicious ZIP'—detections should look for Content-Type: application/zip or multipart uploads immediately followed by unzip operations, not just endpoint correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP POST with Content-Type header matching 'zip' or 'application/x-zip-compressed' to /api/archive/unzip with subsequent filesystem activity (file creation/writes) by the node process within 2 seconds. Focus on writes to directories outside the expected extraction path (e.g., /var/lib/dbgate/uploads/*).

suggestion.title: Node process shell invocation post-ZIP extraction (CVE-2026-47669 persistence/RCE)
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability enables 'arbitrary file write leading to RCE'—if a cron job or shell script is extracted, it will be executed. Detection should observe node spawning bash/sh/python after unzip operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when node process (parent or child) creates or spawns shell processes (bash, sh, python, perl) within 5 seconds of ZIP extraction activity. Look for suspicious command lines referencing /tmp, /etc, or /root directories.

suggestion.title: Extracted executable in system-critical directory execution (CVE-2026-47669 impact)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes files written to /etc/cron.d, /root/.ssh, /etc/init.d—these are persistence/privilege-escalation mechanisms. Detection should observe execution from these paths shortly after extraction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when executables in /etc/init.d, /etc/systemd/system, /etc/profile.d, or /usr/local/{bin,sbin} are created by node process and subsequently executed within 10 seconds, especially if parent process is not a standard system service manager.

suggestion.title: DbGate POST /runners/load-reader with Code Injection Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'unsanitized functionName parameter in the /runners/load-reader endpoint' exploited via 'dynamic import()'. HTTP detection layer required to catch exploitation attempts. Article provides search: 'url=*child_process* OR url=*import(* OR url=*execSync* OR url=*\nvar*'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to endpoints matching */runners/load-reader containing JavaScript injection patterns (import(), require, execSync, child_process keywords in request body or URL parameters). Require authentication context (authenticated user) to reduce false positives from scanning/public analysis.

suggestion.title: Node Process Spawning Shell Interpreter Child (DbGate RCE Post-Exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'execute arbitrary OS commands as root' via spawned processes. Describes 'node OR dbgate parent process launching sh, bash, cmd.exe, powershell'. This is the post-injection execution artifact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation where parent is node, node.exe, dbgate, or dbgate.exe spawning interactive shell interpreters (sh, bash, dash, cmd.exe, powershell.exe, pwsh) with non-system service accounts. Filter out legitimate dbgate administrative shells via process path and argument whitelisting.

suggestion.title: DbGate Authentication + Suspicious File Activity Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RCE as authenticated attack. Detection should pair successful DbGate auth events with suspicious filesystem activity (temp file creation in /tmp/_rce_*, modification of /root/.dbgate, /etc/shadow access) occurring within bounded time window post-auth.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful DbGate authentication (HTTP 200 + valid credentials) with subsequent filesystem modification events in /tmp or /root directories. Flag creation/modification of files named poc.py, bundle.js, or paths matching /tmp/_rce_*, /root/.dbgate within 5 minutes post-authentication.

suggestion.title: HTTP 4xx/5xx spike to ait-bsc /start endpoint (path-traversal filtering)
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'blindly trusts path-related form fields'—defensive filtering would reject malformed traversal patterns with HTTP errors. Spike in 4xx/5xx to this endpoint could indicate reconnaissance or fuzzing. Not covered by UC_21_2 which only hunts successful POST.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sustained increase in HTTP 4xx or 5xx responses to URI paths matching `*/start` on systems running ait-bsc. Baseline noise; alert on anomaly. Correlate with distinct source IPs and user-agents to identify reconnaissance vs. misconfiguration.

suggestion.title: File write to non-baseline path by ait-bsc process (post-exploitation impact)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes impact as 'arbitrary file append'—actual exploitation succeeds when attacker-supplied path is written to. Need endpoint-layer detection of ait-bsc writing outside expected log directories. UC_21_2 hunts the HTTP request; this hunts the filesystem impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for FileCreated or FileModified events where InitiatingProcessName matches ait-bsc and FolderPath does NOT match baseline log directory (e.g., `/var/opt/ait-bsc/logs`). Alert on writes to /etc, /home, /root, /usr, /var outside baseline. Baseline deviation suggests successful path-traversal exploitation.

suggestion.title: ait-bsc process spawning subprocess or executing shell (post-write code execution)
suggestion.rationale: If attacker writes Python script via path traversal and BSC loads/executes it (e.g., in a handler initialization), this would manifest as subprocess creation. Article doesn't explicitly describe this, but arbitrary file append + process execution is a credible post-exploitation path. Current UCs don't cover this vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation where ParentProcessName=ait-bsc or ParentProcessName=python and ProcessName matches shell interpreters (bash, sh, python). Unusual for packet-capture daemon to spawn subprocesses; baseline legitimate spawning and alert on deviation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious parameter mutations in POST /start requests (polymorphic traversal encoding)
suggestion.rationale: UC_21_2 uses static regex for `..`, `%2e%2e`, etc. Attackers may use double-encoding (`%252e%252e`), Unicode normalization, or other obfuscation. Need behavioral detection for malformed or anomalous parameter structure in URI_QUERY.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag POST requests to `*/start` where uri_query parameters are unusually long, contain URL-encoded sequences stacked (e.g., `%25` near `2e`), or contain null bytes / control characters. Supplement regex-based detection with entropy/length anomalies.

suggestion.title: Everest Forms Pro Plugin Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Hackers Exploit Critical Everest Forms Pro WordPress Plugin Flaw' — indicates active CVE or 0day in the plugin; should trigger detections on plugin upload, activation, or suspicious parameter injection to plugin endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST/GET requests to Everest Forms Pro endpoints (/?p=* or plugin path) containing shell code, serialized PHP objects, or encoded payloads. Flag unexpected plugin file uploads or modifications to everest-forms directory in wp-content/plugins/.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation WordPress Admin Account Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article phrase 'take over sites' implies attacker gains administrative control; typical post-exploitation step is creating a rogue admin account or modifying user roles.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on wp_users table INSERT or UPDATE operations that create new administrator accounts with suspicious usernames (e.g., 'admin2', 'wp-support', 'backup'). Monitor wp_usermeta for role changes elevating subscriber/contributor to admin.

suggestion.title: Suspicious WordPress Core/Plugin File Modification
suggestion.rationale: Site 'takeover' implies persistent backdoor installation via shell injection in wp-config.php, theme files, or plugin loader. Article does not provide truncated body detail but exploitation patterns typically involve file-write access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file modifications to WordPress root (wp-config.php, index.php), theme folder (wp-content/themes/*/), or everest-forms plugin directory with new shell code, base64 blobs, or remote include statements. Correlate with HTTP requests to those modified files.

suggestion.title: Everest Forms Pro Plugin Vulnerability Scanner / Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Prior to exploitation, attackers scan for the vulnerable plugin version; should detect probes to /?p=* and version disclosure endpoints before exploit delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests enumerating Everest Forms Pro version strings, checking plugin readme.txt, or probing known vulnerable endpoints with timing/error-code analysis (e.g., 404 vs 500 response patterns).

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution via Plugin Parameter Injection
suggestion.rationale: Critical 'flaw' in plugin implies unauthenticated or poorly-validated parameter passing; article title indicates RCE capability ('take over').
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Everest Forms endpoints containing PHP code patterns (<?php, system(), exec(), passthru()), shell metacharacters (|, ;, &, $(), backticks), or serialized object injection markers (O:, a:, s:) in GET/POST/cookie parameters.

suggestion.title: Python Package Installation — File Hash Match (PyPI Supply Chain)
suggestion.rationale: Article provides SHA1 hash a01c2a21f24db63cb01a67016519aebeca438089 and describes package-download execution vector; pipeline output shows empty IOCs despite mentioning this hash in recommendations, failing to generate correlating use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on pip install or package-manager operations that download files matching known-malicious PyPI package SHA1 hashes. Correlate with subsequent python.exe process spawning or import statements.

suggestion.title: PyPI Typosquatting Detection — Near-Match Package Names
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'crafted to look almost identical to the widely used parsimonious library, the single missing letter was'—core attack is name masquerade, not obfuscation. T1036.005 applies, not T1027.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag pip install queries and PyPI searches for package names within edit-distance 1–2 of legitimate popular packages (parsimonious→parsimonius). Correlate with first-time account creation or rare geographies.

suggestion.title: Malicious Python Package Execution — Post-Install Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector requires developer execution: 'thousands of developers at risk'—implies successful import and code execution of the malicious payload after installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor python.exe child-process spawning within seconds of pip install completion. Flag children that initiate network connections, write to temp/user profile, or execute encoded commands.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Compromise — PyPI Upload Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'deceptive Python package quietly made its way into the PyPI repository'—primary attack surface is unauthorized upload to trusted package index.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PyPI API for new package uploads with metadata timestamps clustering near legitimate package updates, account-creation velocity spikes, or from IPs not associated with known maintainers.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'IronWorm and New Miasma Worm Variant Hit npm'—attack vector is compromised npm packages. Installation is the entry point for supply chain compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/update commands targeting packages known to be compromised. Alert on installation of packages with typosquatted names, unusual maintainers, or from non-standard registries. Track package integrity via hash mismatches.

suggestion.title: Code Execution via Malicious npm Package Import
suggestion.rationale: Once installed, worm code executes when the package is require()'d or imported by downstream applications. 'Worm variant' indicates active code execution and replication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Node.js processes executing unusual scripts or binaries from node_modules directories, especially those spawning additional processes, making network connections, or accessing credential stores. Flag obfuscated or base64-encoded code in package contents.

suggestion.title: npm Worm Lateral Movement to Downstream Packages
suggestion.rationale: Worms by definition self-propagate. Supply-chain worms spread by injecting themselves into package.json files or modifying dependencies of downstream projects, causing reinfection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected writes to package.json from Node.js processes. Detect addition of new dependencies not initiated by package manager user interactions. Flag rapid creation of similar package names across multiple registries.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing from npm Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Worms require command & control to coordinate propagation and receive updated payloads. Article refers to 'worm variant,' implying active C2 infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTPS/HTTP connections from Node.js processes to newly-registered or untrusted domains. Monitor for unusual port usage (non-80/443) from npm processes. Flag connections to infrastructure hosting known malware C2.

suggestion.title: Credential/Source Code Exfiltration from npm Processes
suggestion.rationale: Worms harvest environment variables, .env files, SSH keys, and source code from compromised projects for secondary monetization or espionage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large data transfers initiated by Node.js processes to external IPs. Detect file-read operations on sensitive paths (.env, ~/.ssh, ~/.aws) followed by network transmission. Alert on encoding/compression of source directories in process context.

suggestion.title: Persistence via npm Package Pre-install/Post-install Hooks
suggestion.rationale: npm packages support lifecycle scripts (preinstall, postinstall, preuninstall) that execute with high privilege. Worms use these hooks to survive package updates and establish persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package.json for unusual or obfuscated lifecycle scripts. Detect execution of scripts in .npm cache or node_modules/.bin directories not matching known package names. Flag script invocations with curl/wget to external URLs.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Card Data Exfiltration to Payment Service Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'data dump' and stolen card data being exfiltrated. 'uses Stripe, the widely used online payment service, as both its command center and its data dump.' Pipeline missed the exfiltration detection vector entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal outbound connections from web servers to Firebase, Stripe, or other trusted payment/cloud domains on non-standard ports. Correlate with POST requests containing high-entropy payloads consistent with encrypted card data. Flag deviations from baseline payment processor communication patterns.

suggestion.title: JavaScript Injection in Payment Forms Leading to Magecart Skimming
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'credit card skimming malware' and 'hiding inside' Stripe platform. This suggests malicious JavaScript injection into payment flows. Pipeline missed the execution/injection phase entirely despite this being the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized JavaScript includes or mutations in payment form DOM. Hunt for script tags pointing to Firebase or other CDNs on payment pages, inline DOM-manipulation scripts that capture form field input, or suspicious XHR callbacks during checkout flow. Compare against known-good Stripe integration scripts.

suggestion.title: Abuse of Trusted Services (Firebase) for Malware C2
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: Stripe/Firebase misused as 'command center.' Pipeline identified C2 phase in narrative but generated no hunt for this abuse pattern. Firebase is legitimately used, but exfiltration-to-Firebase combined with command polling is anomalous for e-commerce contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual Firebase Realtime Database access patterns: high volume of writes from a single merchant/website, writes containing base64/hex-encoded data, polling patterns (frequent rapid GET/POST cycles) inconsistent with legitimate payment processing, Firebase credentials or API keys embedded in obfuscated JavaScript.

suggestion.title: Malicious Stripe Integration Script Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is injection of malicious code into Stripe integration layer. Article states malware 'found hiding inside' Stripe but pipeline generated no detection for compromised payment scripts or API key exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan Stripe integration code for unauthorized API calls, exfiltration endpoints, or script sources. Monitor for Stripe public key usage outside authorized domains, API requests originating from unexpected geographic locations, or Stripe.js versions that have been replaced with backdoored copies. Alert on Stripe account access from non-registered IPs.

suggestion.title: Payment Card Data Collection and Staging to Attacker Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes data being collected and dumped. 'stolen card data' and 'data dump' appear in narrative. Pipeline did not generate collection-phase hunts despite this being explicitly stated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for JavaScript event listeners on payment form fields (onchange, onkeyup, onfocus) that capture card number, CVV, or expiry fields. Detect in-memory staging of credit card data followed by encryption and transmission. Monitor for KeyLogger-like behavior in checkout contexts. Correlate card data exfiltration with legitimate payment processing to identify interception points.

suggestion.title: IIS Unusual .ASP/ASPX File Creation in Web Root
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'custom web shell framework' targeting IIS servers—implies ASP-based implant. No UC generated despite this being the primary persistence vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IIS application directories (wwwroot, web apps) for .asp, .aspx, .asmx, or .ashx file creation outside of maintenance windows. Correlate with IIS process events. Flag new web-executable files with low file age and unusual names.

suggestion.title: IIS w3wp.exe Spawning Command Shells
suggestion.rationale: Web shells execute commands via IIS worker process. Article explicitly discusses web shell framework but pipeline captured no execution detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on w3wp.exe (IIS worker process) directly spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or cscript.exe. Filter known application-legit child processes. Web shells do not typically invoke these directly—legitimate IIS apps delegate to service accounts or scheduled tasks.

suggestion.title: Suspicious IIS HTTP Request Patterns (Command Injection in URL/POST)
suggestion.rationale: Web shell interaction is command execution via HTTP. Pipeline missed HTTP/application layer detection despite this being the primary attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search IIS logs for requests to newly-created .asp/.aspx files with encoded commands in query parameters or POST bodies (e.g., cmd=, exec=, command=). Look for command metacharacters (|, &, &&, ;, $()), Base64-encoded payloads, or PowerShell download patterns in HTTP POST data.

suggestion.title: IIS Application Pool Recycling or App Domain Unload Events
suggestion.rationale: Web shells often modify IIS configuration for persistence. Article title suggests 'custom framework' implying configuration-level implants, but no detection for IIS state changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IIS applicationHost.config, web.config, and ISAPI/CGI filter registry keys for unexpected modifications. Alert on unusual IIS module registration (applicationInitialization, FastCGI, etc.) outside change control windows.

suggestion.title: OP-512 Threat Actor Identification (Clustering)
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'OP-512' but pipeline output includes no actor attribution, campaign ID, or threat intelligence linking. This is foundational context missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest OP-512 campaign indicators (domains, registrant patterns, certificate serial ranges, malware signatures) into threat feeds. Pivot on observed web shell hashes, C2 endpoints, or staging infrastructure to identify related intrusions. Cross-reference with existing incident data for pattern continuity.

suggestion.title: Cloud Credential Compromise & Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'hijacks 230 AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure servers' — hijacking of multiple disparate cloud accounts/subscriptions requires either stolen credentials, compromised service principals, or exploited IAM misconfigurations. Pipeline should detect unusual cloud IAM activity, cross-account assume-role calls, or bulk lateral movement across cloud infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous cloud API calls such as bulk AssumeRole, CreateAccessKey, or AttachUserPolicy actions; flag rapid authentication across multiple cloud tenants or regions from single source; alert on service principal token grants to previously-unused applications.

suggestion.title: Rogue SMTP Relay Service Activation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'covert SMTP relay network' — implies SMTP service activation or mail-forwarding rules configured on compromised servers. Should detect unauthorized Postfix/Sendmail/Exim activation, SMTP listener startup, or email forwarding rule creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual startup or installation of SMTP daemons (postfix, sendmail, exim, sendgrid agents); flag creation of mail forwarding rules; monitor for unexpected listening on ports 25, 587, 465; detect bulk email transmission from previously-quiet cloud instances.

suggestion.title: Cloud Metadata API Exploitation & Container Escape
suggestion.rationale: Hijacking 230 servers across three cloud providers within single campaign suggests a common exploit vector — likely cloud metadata service (169.254.169.254) abuse or container escape (Kubernetes or container breakout). Article implies infrastructure-wide compromise method.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTP(S) requests to cloud metadata IP ranges (169.254.169.254, 0xA9FEA9FE); flag curl/wget commands targeting metadata endpoints; alert on containers spawning unexpected child processes or attempting to break out of cgroup restrictions; monitor for sudden privilege escalation within containerized workloads.

suggestion.title: PCPJack Malware Execution & Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Title names 'PCPJack' as the attack actor/malware family. Pipeline should flag any artifact (file hash, command-line pattern, registry key, scheduled task) associated with PCPJack deployment and persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Generate file-hash signatures and command-line heuristics for PCPJack (to be extracted from full article/threat intel feeds); detect process execution with characteristic command patterns; flag creation of scheduled tasks or cron jobs matching known PCPJack persistence behaviors.

suggestion.title: Multi-Cloud Infrastructure Reconnaissance & Targeting
suggestion.rationale: Campaign specifically targeted AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure — article implies attacker conducted reconnaissance to identify cloud-hosted assets, enumerate accounts, or map multi-cloud deployments. Should detect advanced reconnaissance patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on batch cloud CLI commands enumerating instances, VPCs, security groups across multiple cloud providers; flag API calls to DescribeInstances, ListBuckets, or equivalent across disparate cloud tenants; detect tooling (Prowler, Pacu, cloud-enum) or scripted reconnaissance patterns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious AI-generated code commits to CI/CD pipeline
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses AI agent (Claude Code) integrated in GitHub Actions making automated code changes—attack vector is malicious prompt injection causing code generation that bypasses human review. Detection should alert on commits with unusual patterns (volume, velocity, or LLM-characteristic phrasing) made by automated accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-frequency automated commits to protected branches within short time windows, or commits containing code patterns consistent with LLM generation (unusual variable naming, verbose comments, generic function implementations). Correlate with GitHub Action runner logs showing unexpected AI-model API calls.

suggestion.title: GitHub token exfiltration via AI agent context injection
suggestion.rationale: CI/CD context (GitHub tokens, secrets) is accessible to agents. Malicious prompt or poisoned training data could instruct agent to output or transmit tokens. Need to detect anomalous secret access or transmission.
log_sources: Network egress (outbound API calls from runner)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub runner processes attempting to read or transmit GITHUB_TOKEN or custom secrets to unexpected destinations. Monitor for atypical outbound connections from CI/CD runners to non-whitelisted domains during AI-model API calls.

suggestion.title: Malicious GitHub Action manifest injection
suggestion.rationale: Attack could modify workflow YAML to insert malicious steps. Pipeline should detect unauthorized edits to .github/workflows/ files, especially if committed by automated accounts or preceded by prompt-injection indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect additions of new steps to GitHub Actions workflows that instantiate runners with elevated privileges, pull secrets, or exfiltrate artifacts. Flag edits to workflows made by non-human accounts or outside normal change-control windows.

suggestion.title: Unexpected AI model API calls from CI/CD runner context
suggestion.rationale: Legitimate Claude Code calls are expected; malicious prompts or jailbreaks should trigger unusual API usage patterns (high token count, repeated queries, attempts to extract training data, model introspection).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-volume or repeated API calls to LLM services from CI/CD contexts, unusual prompt patterns (e.g., attempts to bypass safety guidelines, exfiltration payloads), or calls to non-standard model endpoints.

suggestion.title: HTTP 401 Authentication Prompt from External/Unexpected Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'polyfill[.]io domain became active again and started responding with HTTP 401 authentication requests. User browsers interpret that as a request for a username and password, so they serve a login prompt.' Browsers natively prompt users for credentials on 401 Unauthorized, bypassing typical credential monitors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP 401 Unauthorized responses from external domains not in approved authentication service whitelist. Correlate with affected sites (Toshiba, Muji, Samsung) and polyfill.io domain. Distinguish from legitimate proxies and CDNs by requiring domain to be on known-compromised list or anomalous geographically.

suggestion.title: Stale External Library Reference to Compromised CDN
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'some sites using the service failed to clean all their pages over the past two years, so remnants of Polyfill code remained' — websites migrated to polyfill.com/polyfill.top but missed script references, enabling injection when original domain re-registered.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all <script> includes and external resource references for polyfill.io. Flag any requests to polyfill[.]io from organizations known to have migrated to polyfill.com or polyfill.top. Inventory all JavaScript CDN dependencies and alert on loads from unapproved library domains.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Attack: Chinese Entity Takeover of OSS Library Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'in 2024 [polyfill.io] was purchased by a Chinese entity and added malicious scripts that impacted more than 100,000 websites' — attacker acquired legitimate JavaScript library domain after original creator lost registration, enabling injection at scale across supply chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor domain re-registrations of popular open-source library CDNs (polyfill, jQuery, bootstrap CDN mirrors, etc.). Alert on domain registrant changes to previously-trusted JS libraries. Correlate domain takeover with subsequent malicious script injection via CDN cache analysis or honeypot clients.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Fake Browser Login Prompt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'users who entered their account login data in the authentication screens to change their passwords' — confirms credential entry into HTTP 401 prompts. Both Toshiba and Muji confirmed users may have compromised credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate browser native authentication prompts (HTTP 401) with subsequent user password changes or forced resets. Alert if users from affected sites (Toshiba.com, Muji.jp, Samsung.com) change credentials within hours of unexpected 401 prompts. Cross-reference with credential stuffing detection.

suggestion.title: Cross-Organizational Supply Chain Impact Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article lists Toshiba, Muji, Zojirushi, FiNC, Ishiyaku, Hobonichi, Samsung all affected by same polyfill.io injection — indicates coordinated supply chain compromise affecting multiple industries/regions simultaneously.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create supply-chain incident correlation: when >3 unrelated Fortune 500/major retail brands report same malicious CDN injection within 48-hour window, escalate to supply-chain compromise alert. Track remediation timelines (Toshiba/Muji disabled service within days) to identify orgs slower to patch.

suggestion.title: Detect Exploitation Attempts Against Known FFmpeg CVEs
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'AI Agent Uncovers 21 Zero-Days in FFmpeg' — represents high-impact code execution vectors immediately weaponizable by threat actors. Pipeline generated no impact-phase detection despite clear vulnerability indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal child process spawning from ffmpeg.exe or libffmpeg.so, temp directory writes from media processing, and unexpected network callbacks from codec libraries. Establish baseline for legitimate media transcoding and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Track Vulnerable Software Inventory — FFmpeg Affected Versions
suggestion.rationale: 21 FFmpeg zero-days implies specific version ranges are vulnerable. Article phrase 'AI Agent Uncovers 21 Zero-Days in FFmpeg' directly indicates need for version-based inventory detection, which pipeline failed to generate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all endpoints for FFmpeg binary versions, registry keys, and installation paths. Cross-reference against disclosed affected versions. Alert on unpatched instances and flag environments where FFmpeg should not exist.

suggestion.title: Monitor Chrome Patch Deployment for 429 Bug Patches
suggestion.rationale: Article phrase 'Chrome Patches Record 429 Bugs' indicates high-volume patch cycle with security-critical fixes. Pipeline generated no detection for patch deployment lag or update verification despite explicit mention of record-breaking patch scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track Chrome version distribution across fleet. Alert on systems running versions older than patched releases for >7 days post-patch publication. Flag endpoints where auto-update is disabled while Chrome remains in use.

suggestion.title: Detect Media File Processing Anomalies (FFmpeg Attack Surface)
suggestion.rationale: FFmpeg zero-days typically trigger via malformed media files. Article phrase 'Zero-Days in FFmpeg' establishes media file handling as attack surface; pipeline provided no execution-phase detection for malformed media + process spawning patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious file extensions with FFmpeg spawning (e.g., .mp4 + unexpected children, abnormal CPU/memory during decode). Track email attachments with media extensions followed by ffmpeg execution within minutes of delivery.

suggestion.title: Identify Browser Exploitation via Chrome CVEs
suggestion.rationale: Chrome's 429 patched bugs span multiple attack vectors (renderer exploits, sandbox escapes, V8 engine flaws). Article phrase 'Chrome Patches Record 429 Bugs' establishes initial-access and privilege-escalation threat surface; pipeline missed corresponding detection hypotheses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unpatched Chrome versions with suspicious post-browsing activity: unexpected binary downloads, credential harvesting patterns, or lateral movement indicators. Monitor for watering hole delivery if article mentions supply-chain context.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Risk — Vulnerable FFmpeg/Chrome in Embedded Applications
suggestion.rationale: FFmpeg and Chromium are embedded in numerous third-party tools (Electron apps, streaming software, video editors). Article mentions specific product names but pipeline generated zero downstream-risk or supply-chain exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all installed software using embedded FFmpeg or Chromium libraries and track their version strings. Alert on vulnerable versions, especially for tools running with elevated privileges. Monitor for exploitation chains where attacker pivots from embedded lib compromise to system access.

suggestion.title: Serv-U Exploitation Attempt via CISA KEV Vector
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the vulnerability is 'actively exploited.' Pipeline failed to map initial-access detection for the known exploitation pattern. Must detect inbound attempts to trigger DoS condition on affected Serv-U versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound connections to Serv-U service ports (22, 5632) for exploit payload signatures or unusual request patterns followed by service disruption. Flag sources without legitimate business context.

suggestion.title: Serv-U Service Disruption and Restart Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: DoS flaw's impact is service unavailability; article describes denial-of-service as the attack result. Pipeline ignored the operational-impact detection tier required for availability threats.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Serv-U process crashes, unexpected restarts (>3 in 5 minutes), or service stop/start event clustering. Correlate timing with suspicious network traffic to Serv-U ports to confirm exploitation.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance Scanning for CISA KEV Serv-U Instances
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must identify Serv-U instances before exploitation. Article's mention of CISA KEV indicates automated scanning activity should be expected. Pipeline failed to surface discovery-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid connection attempts to port 5632 (primary Serv-U) or port 22 with Serv-U-specific banner probes. Flag bulk port scanning from external sources or scanning from internally-compromised hosts.

suggestion.title: Serv-U Configuration and Version Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Pre-exploitation phase requires version identification. Article's specific reference to 'Serv-U' product variant suggests attackers must enumerate versions before triggering DoS. Pipeline missed this reconnaissance step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS requests to Serv-U service endpoints (e.g., status pages, admin interfaces) seeking version strings. Flag connections combining reconnaissance patterns (multiple ports, banners, service identification requests).

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is 'actively exploited' with 'no patch available'. Pipeline must detect exploitation attempts against this public-facing management interface. Article title establishes urgent need for exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco SD-WAN Manager interfaces for CVE-2026-20245 exploitation signatures, including malformed requests to known vulnerable endpoints, unexpected POST operations to management APIs, or access patterns inconsistent with legitimate management traffic.

suggestion.title: Suspicious SD-WAN Manager Authentication or Session Activity
suggestion.rationale: Actively exploited vulnerabilities often result in unauthorized access or session hijacking. No patch availability means organizations must detect behavioral anomalies rather than patch signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag authentication events to SD-WAN Manager with unusual geographic origin, user-agent strings, or timing patterns. Alert on concurrent session creation from the same source targeting the vulnerability window.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20245 Reference Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names CVE-2026-20245 as the vulnerability. Pipeline should index this CVE identifier as a reference IOC for correlating threat intelligence feeds, vulnerability databases, and threat actor disclosures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate inbound network traffic and web access logs against known CVE-2026-20245 POC signatures. Cross-reference threat actor reports mentioning this CVE to identify infrastructure or timing alignment with observed exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: WordPress Admin Account Creation via Everest Forms PHP Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attackers leveraging eval() to execute wp_insert_user() and create admin account 'diksimarina'. Direct detection gap: 'Telemetry data from Wordfence firewall and malware scanner for WordPress shows that the vulnerability is being exploited in the wild to create rogue administrator accounts.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress user creation events (wp_insert_user or wp_create_user function calls, wp_users table INSERT) for accounts created via web requests without standard WP-Admin login prior. Flag accounts with names matching malicious indicators (e.g., 'diksimarina', 'admin_', numerically-suffixed admin variants) or created during POST requests to form endpoints.

suggestion.title: PHP eval() Execution with User-Controlled Complex Calculation Input
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability mechanism: 'accepts values submitted through form fields and inserts them into a PHP code string. Then, it executes the resulting code using PHP's eval() function.' Attack payload pattern: single quote to close string literal, followed by PHP statement. Direct article phrase: 'an attacker can close the intended string, inject arbitrary PHP code, and comment out the remaining generated code.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to Everest Forms Pro Complex Calculation fields for injection payloads: single quotes in form values, PHP comment syntax (//, #, /* */), function calls (wp_insert_user, system, exec, passthru). Flag requests where sanitize_text_field() output contains quote-preceded PHP code patterns.

suggestion.title: Everest Forms Pro Plugin Form Submission with Code Injection Syntax
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector explicitly described: 'The attacker submits a value for a text field that begins with a single quote to close the wrapping string literal, followed by a PHP statement.' Detection gap for pre-execution phase: requests to form endpoints contain injection attempts before eval() fires.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to Everest Forms endpoints (especially Complex Calculation fields) containing payloads with single quotes followed by PHP function calls, semicolons, comment markers. Baseline: legitimate form submissions should not include quote+semicolon patterns or wp_* function names.

suggestion.title: Successive Failed Everest Forms Submissions from High-Volume IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'exploitation attempts originate primarily from two IP addresses, 202.56.2[.]126 and 209.146.60.26, and recommends defenders block them.' 'Firewall blocking over 29,300 attempts.' Detection gap: high-volume form submission attempts before successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on IPs submitting >10 POST requests to Everest Forms plugin endpoints within a 1-hour window, or any single request from known attacker IPs (202.56.2[.]126, 209.146.60.26). Correlate with injection payload signatures to confirm exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: New WordPress Administrator Created from Unauthenticated Request Context
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated to execute arbitrary code.' Article notes: 'Administrator-level access gives attackers full power.' Detection gap: privilege escalation from no auth to admin via single form submission.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect WordPress user role changes or new admin account creations when the preceding event is NOT a logged-in admin action but instead a GET/POST to a plugin form endpoint. Correlate session logs to confirm no authenticated admin was responsible.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Smart TV Network Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes apps being 'turned into proxies for web-scraping' — implies sustained outbound HTTP traffic to diverse, non-entertainment destinations. Pipeline extracted zero UCs despite this being core attack signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor smart TV devices for sustained HTTP traffic to non-entertainment domains, high request-per-minute rates, or destination diversity anomalies. Establish baseline for streaming/firmware updates and alert on sustained deviations indicating proxy misuse.

suggestion.title: Trojanized App Installation on Smart TVs
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'free apps' as attack vector — software supply-chain compromise delivered via user installation. Pipeline missed initial access detection opportunity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag installations from untrusted app stores, unsigned packages, or apps requesting unusual network/storage permissions. Cross-reference app signatures and publisher certificates against known malware families; establish allowlist of legitimate TV apps.

suggestion.title: Smart TV Proxy Behavior Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'proxies' — requires detection of forwarding patterns (rapid sequential requests to diverse unrelated destinations). Pipeline failed to propose this obvious C2/exfil UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high fan-in network patterns: single smart TV source making requests to many unrelated destinations with uniform User-Agent/header signatures. Compare against expected TV traffic profiles (streaming, OTA, NTP).

suggestion.title: Bulk Data Aggregation from Smart TV Proxy Network
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'proxies for AI' — implies coordinated data harvesting. Pipeline missed detection of aggregation traffic or large batch exfiltration signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify encrypted POST/PUT traffic from smart TVs to central collection servers with timing consistency (batch shipment patterns). Alert on large payloads, compression artifacts, or traffic outside business hours.

suggestion.title: Child Process Spawning from Smart TV Applications
suggestion.rationale: Article implies apps execute scraping code — requires detection of unexpected process spawning or shell invocations from app contexts, which smart TV apps should not perform.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for shell processes (sh, bash, curl, wget) spawned from non-system app UIDs or scheduled task creation from installer contexts. Smart TV apps should have minimal process tree depth.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Smart TV Network Destination Profiling
suggestion.rationale: Article describes scraping 'for AI' — implies requests to content sites and model-training infrastructure. Pipeline should flag requests to known data aggregation or AI training service endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain list of known web-scraping-hostile domains and AI training data brokers. Alert when smart TV devices make DNS queries or connections to these targets from app-controlled contexts.

suggestion.title: Smart TV Connections to Known Proxy Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists C2 domains (proxyjs.bright-sdk.com, clientsdk.brdtnet.com, etc.) and IPs. This is foundational IOC-based hunt; pipeline generated zero use cases despite having high-confidence network indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound network connections from smart TV devices to any enumerated proxy infrastructure domains (bright-sdk.com, brdtnet.com, luminatinet.com, luminati.io) or IPs (3.33.193.183, 15.197.193.114). High fidelity; consumer devices have minimal legitimate reason to contact proxy infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Suspicious App Enrollment Handshake with Proxy Network
suggestion.rationale: Article states apps 'quietly enroll' devices into proxy network. Behavioral detection: apps making initial contact with proxy infrastructure shortly after installation or launch, suggesting device registration/enrollment in proxy service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for apps making network connections to known proxy infrastructure domains within minutes of app installation or first run. Look for enrollment/handshake traffic patterns (e.g., registration, device ID transmission) that indicate proxy network enrollment.

suggestion.title: Elevated Sustained Outbound Traffic Forwarding from Smart TV
suggestion.rationale: Article describes devices being 'turned into proxies' to 'scrape web data.' Detection: smart TV devices exhibiting unusual sustained traffic volume, forwarding traffic to diverse external destinations, or making requests inconsistent with normal user-initiated browsing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect smart TV devices with sustained high outbound connection volume, traffic to unusual/numerous unique destinations, or traffic patterns suggesting the device is forwarding requests on behalf of external entities rather than serving local user needs.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated or Buried Consent Dialogs in Smart TV Apps
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically identifies deception mechanism: 'consent dialog buried in a TV remote's arrow-key navigation.' This is social engineering (T1204). Detection: apps that hide permission prompts in complex UI navigation, making true informed consent difficult.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor smart TV app behavior for consent dialog anomalies: dialogs requiring excessive navigation steps, auto-dismissing dialogs, dialogs defaulting to 'accept,' or dialogs rendered off-screen or with reduced visibility relative to normal app UI.

suggestion.title: Installation of Known Malicious Smart TV Free Apps
suggestion.rationale: Article references specific malicious free apps on Samsung, LG, Roku app stores. Requires app name/hash IOCs (not provided in article summary but should be sourced from Include Security research). File-based detection of known malicious apps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain inventory of known malicious smart TV app names and hashes. Alert on installation or execution of known malicious apps on smart TV devices. Cross-reference with official app store inventory to distinguish legitimate apps from malicious lookalikes.

suggestion.title: Detect Suspicious Code Commits to GitHub Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack 'hit 73 Microsoft GitHub repositories' in a supply chain attack. Malicious code commits would be the primary infection vector for downstream consumers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub API for commits by non-standard service accounts, commits introducing binary files or suspicious scripts to source repos, or commits bypassing branch protections. Correlate with sudden spikes in commit velocity or repo owner alerts.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthorized Access to Microsoft GitHub Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain compromise of 73 repos implies attacker gained write access through credential abuse, SSO compromise, or PAT token theft. Initial access is critical detection layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub/Azure AD logins from anomalous IPs, impossible-travel patterns, new SSH keys or personal access tokens added to accounts, or API calls from unfamiliar user agents outside normal working hours.

suggestion.title: Detect Worm-Like Propagation in Code Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Threat explicitly named 'Miasma Worm'—indicating self-replicating malware. Worms propagate across network boundaries; should detect replication patterns across shared development infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid file creation across multiple repos or shares, unusual processes spawned from git operations, mass SMB connections from development infrastructure, or scheduled tasks created on developer workstations following GitHub access.

suggestion.title: Detect Execution of Code from Compromised Microsoft Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack impact depends on downstream execution by developers/CI/CD systems using affected repos. Article scope suggests tooling already deployed to consumers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes spawned from git clone/pull operations, scripts executed from repo working directories, PowerShell invocations from .git directories, or build commands executing code from recently updated repos.

suggestion.title: Detect Malicious Package/Artifact Distribution from Poisoned Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks on code repos manifest as poisoned packages or binaries distributed downstream. This is the critical impact vector for a 73-repo compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager logs for unusual packages from Microsoft orgs, unsigned packages, unexpected dependencies, or spikes in pull/download volume. Alert on mass consumption of packages versioned after compromise timestamp.

suggestion.title: Bulk Repository Administrative Actions from Single Account
suggestion.rationale: Article states '72 Other Repositories Disabled' — sudden mass disables of repos within a short window is a hallmark of supply chain cleanup or attacker lockout. No UC was generated despite this being the impact signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect single service principal or user disabling/deleting >10 repositories within 60 minutes. Monitor for Repository.Delete, Repository.Disable events in GitHub/Azure audit logs; correlate with out-of-band incident reports or unusual auth patterns (e.g. new session from anomalous location).

suggestion.title: Malicious Workflow Injection into GitHub Actions
suggestion.rationale: Article targets 'AI Coding Agents' via supply chain — GitHub Actions workflows are the primary vector for dependency injection and agent compromise. No detection rule for modified workflows, new steps, or exfiltration commands was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on workflow YAML additions that execute external scripts (curl/wget), access secrets env vars, or trigger unusual outbound connections. Flag newly-added workflow steps referencing unknown actions or inline script shells in >10 repos within 24 hours.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise via Malicious Dependency Injection
