suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Python processes (python.exe, pip, python3) that import or execute the durabletask module, particularly unusual child process spawning or unexpected network activity following import. Baseline legitimate durabletask usage and alert on deviations (unusual args, non-standard parent process, suspicious child processes).

suggestion.title: Outbound network connections from Python durabletask execution
suggestion.rationale: Compromised package likely establishes C2; article describes supply-chain backdoor which implies command-and-control communication from infected hosts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected outbound connections (HTTP/HTTPS/DNS) from Python processes running durabletask code, especially to non-Microsoft domains, IPs not in allow-list, or using unusual ports. Correlate with process execution timeline of durabletask import.

suggestion.title: Registry or configuration file modifications from Python execution context
suggestion.rationale: Persistence mechanism for supply-chain backdoor; compromised package may modify system configuration to maintain foothold.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected registry writes (HKLM/HKCU) or config file modifications (hosts, scheduled tasks, startup folders) initiated by Python or its child processes. Flag modifications to persistence mechanisms when correlated with durabletask package usage.

suggestion.title: Unexpected file exfiltration from Python-executed durabletask
suggestion.rationale: Backdoored package may steal credentials, source code, or sensitive data; supply-chain compromises often harvest secrets from infected development/CI environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file reads of sensitive paths (credentials, SSH keys, .env files, source repos) by Python processes with subsequent network exfiltration. Look for unusual compression or archiving activity (tar, zip) spawned from Python context.

suggestion.title: Unsigned or untrusted code execution via pip install from malicious durabletask
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes this is a PyPI package compromise; Python package installation bypasses code-signing validation, executing arbitrary Python bytecode.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor pip install commands and detect installation of durabletask from untrusted or non-canonical PyPI sources. Flag deviations: typosquats, unusual version numbers, or installs before official package existed.

suggestion.title: Dependency resolution abuse via compromised durabletask in CI/build pipelines
suggestion.rationale: Development teams and CI systems auto-update dependencies; compromised package runs in build environments with broad system access, enabling lateral movement and artifact poisoning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual activity in CI/build job logs following durabletask import: unexpected network calls, artifact modifications, credential usage, or lateral movement to other repos/systems. Baseline legitimate build behavior and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Suspicious WebSocket C2 Traffic to External IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article states Plenet uses 'WebSocket protocol for C2 communications' and was deployed to internal appliances; detection should monitor internal-to-external WebSocket connections from non-standard hosts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network logs for WebSocket protocol connections (identified by Upgrade: websocket headers or port 443/80 traffic with WebSocket handshakes) originating from NAS devices, Storage Sync systems, or pfSense firewalls to external IP addresses. Flag if destination ASN is non-US or changes frequently.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized SSL VPN Access Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attackers 'used stolen credentials to enable and configure SSL VPN access on the victim's firewall'; detection must catch VPN service enablement and new user provisioning outside normal change control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor firewall configuration logs and Windows registry for changes to VPN services (enable/start events), creation of new VPN user accounts, and modifications to remote access policies. Correlate with successful authentication events from non-standard geographies or times.

suggestion.title: Malware Deployment to NAS and Appliance Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article details deployment of 'custom malware to a Synology NAS device' and 'BSD variant of Brickstorm on a pfSense firewall'; detection should identify file creation/modification on appliances from unexpected sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file creation/modification events on Synology NAS, pfSense firewalls, and Storage Sync appliances for binary files (ELF, Mach-O, .NET PE) created outside normal deployment windows or by unusual processes. Flag cross-platform binary deployment (Golang/Rust variants).

suggestion.title: Egnyte Storage Sync Unusual Access Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'compromised an Egnyte Storage Sync system and accessed it periodically through the victim's web SSL VPN'; detection should surface anomalous access to this appliance outside business norms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Egnyte Storage Sync appliance access logs for connections from non-standard IP ranges, after-hours access, or access patterns inconsistent with normal user behavior. Correlate with firewall logs showing persistent SSL VPN sessions from the same sources.

suggestion.title: Python Reverse Shell Execution (AgentPSD Detection)
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'AgentPSD is a simple Python-based reverse shell utility'; detection must catch Python spawning reverse shell or socket-connection patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for python.exe or python processes spawning with command-line arguments containing socket, reverse_shell, or subprocess patterns. Flag execution from non-standard directories (temp, appliance system paths) or from processes without typical Python parent chains.

suggestion.title: MSP-to-Victim Lateral Movement via Trusted Relationships
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Volexity has medium confidence that the attacker pivoted from the MSP into the victim organization's environment' via a compromised pfSense firewall; detection must identify unusual cross-organizational access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for authentication events and data flows from MSP infrastructure IP ranges into victim networks outside normal service-account activity windows. Flag if MSP-originated sessions bypass conditional access policies or originate from IPs previously marked as compromised.

suggestion.title: Serv-U POST Request with Content-Encoding: deflate Header
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack vector: 'specially crafted POST requests that crash the Serv-U service without authentication using Content-Encoding: deflate' — this is the weaponized signature and should be detectable on network and application logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound POST requests to Serv-U listener ports (HTTP/HTTPS for MFT service) containing the Content-Encoding: deflate header. Vendor confirmed legitimate Serv-U does not require this encoding, making it a reliable exploit signature.

suggestion.title: Serv-U Service Crash or Unexpected Restart
suggestion.rationale: Article states impact is to 'crash the Serv-U service' — process termination and restart cycles are directly observable in Windows Event Logs and Sysmon data and constitute impact IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Serv-U.exe (or Linux equivalent) unexpected termination (Event ID 7000-7006 for service crash, or Sysmon process exit) followed by automatic restarts, especially when temporally correlated with inbound POST surges.

suggestion.title: Detection and Inventory of Unpatched Serv-U Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies patched version as 15.5.4 Hotfix 1 released on 'Thursday' (2026-06-05). All versions prior are vulnerable and exploitable. Asset queries should flag exposed Serv-U endpoints with version <15.5.4 HF1.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management systems and perform port 21/115/990/2121 banner enumeration to identify Serv-U version. Cross-correlate with Shodan/Censys scans (article notes 12,000+ exposed instances). Generate priority list for immediate patching.

suggestion.title: Anomalous POST Request Rate to Serv-U Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires sending POST requests; legitimate Serv-U traffic is predominantly FTP/SFTP. A surge in POST volume to Serv-U listener IPs is indicative of scanning or exploit attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline POST request count to identified Serv-U services (filtered by destination port and URI path). Alert when 1-hour POST volume deviates >5 standard deviations above mean, especially from untrusted ASNs or spoofed/rotating source IPs.

suggestion.title: Low-Complexity Remote Exploitation Attempt on Serv-U
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Remote attackers can exploit... without privileges in low-complexity attacks that don't require user interaction' — this is a high-confidence indicator that any network access to the vulnerable service is exploitation-grade.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Any unauthenticated inbound POST request to Serv-U listener is treat-as-exploit until proven benign. Recommend allowlisting legitimate internal MFT workflows and dropping/alerting all other external POST traffic to Serv-U.

suggestion.title: Serv-U Denial-of-Service Resource Exhaustion Pattern
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-28318 stems from 'uncontrolled resource consumption weakness' — monitor for CPU/memory spikes in Serv-U processes, file descriptor exhaustion, or thread pool saturation events temporally linked to inbound malicious POST requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Serv-U process resource utilization (CPU >90%, memory delta >500MB in <10s, thread count spike) with network-visible POST patterns and request byte counts. High-confidence DoS indicator when sustained for 5+ seconds.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies CVE-2026-28318 in CISA KEV, which implies active exploitation. Vulnerability scanner hits are canonical first-line detection for asset exposure. Pipeline failed to operationalize asset-exposure hunting despite template reference in article.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-28318 hits on SolarWinds Serv-U. Prioritize internet-facing assets. Cross-reference patch dates against federal remediation deadline 2026-06-19 for compliance tracking and escalation.

suggestion.title: Deflate-Encoded POST Requests to Serv-U
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly specifies attack vector: 'specially crafted POST requests using the Content-Encoding: deflate header'. This is a unique, detectable signature for exploitation attempts. Pipeline did not extract or operationalize this indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for POST requests with Content-Encoding: deflate header targeting Serv-U ports/hosts. Deflate is uncommon in legitimate traffic. Cluster by source IP to identify potential exploitation campaigns. Correlate POST timing with service crashes for confirmation.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U Service Crash or Unexpected Restart
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability causes direct service failure: 'allows specially crafted POST requests ... to crash the Serv-U service'. Unexpected service restarts are direct impact indicators. Pipeline missed DoS/impact detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Serv-U process termination (Windows Event 7034, *nix SIGTERM/SIGKILL) without administrative action. Flag any restart within < 5 minutes. Correlate crash timestamp with inbound POST requests and deflate header for exploitation confirmation.

suggestion.title: Anomalous POST Request Volume to Serv-U Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires POST requests; baseline POST volume to Serv-U should be low in most environments. Unusual volume or external sources suggest reconnaissance or active attack. Article establishes POST as the attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline POST request volume to known Serv-U ports/endpoints. Alert on 5–10x spike from external, previously unseen, or high-risk IP ranges. Combine with deflate-header detection for higher confidence and fidelity.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U Patch Compliance Report
suggestion.rationale: Federal agencies required to remediate by 2026-06-19 per CISA KEV. Patch compliance is non-negotiable regulatory requirement. Pipeline produced zero inventory or patch-tracking use cases despite federal deadline being central to threat profile.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset management system for all Serv-U instances, versions, and patch status relative to CVE-2026-28318. Stratify by department/owner. Flag any vulnerable to CVE-2026-28318 or missing patch post-deadline. Enforce ownership accountability.

suggestion.title: Suspicious CSV File Upload to Cisco SD-WAN vManage
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by uploading a crafted file to the affected system.' Example log shows /home/admin/malicious.csv as the attack artifact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vManage file upload endpoints for CSV uploads to unexpected paths (especially /home/admin/*). Correlate with subsequent execution of /usr/bin/vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh. Flag uploads containing shell metacharacters or encoded payloads.

suggestion.title: Malicious Script Execution via vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh
suggestion.rationale: Article provides exact log signature from /var/log/scripts.log: 'Tenant list upload per vsmart serial number: /usr/bin/vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh -cli path /home/admin/malicious.csv vpn 0'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse /var/log/scripts.log for vScript entries invoking vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh with CSV paths outside standard directories. Alert on args containing /home/admin/ or other user-writable paths. Cross-correlate with file upload events within 60 seconds.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation from Netadmin Context to Root
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'insufficient validation of user-supplied input' allowing 'local attackers with low privileges to execute arbitrary commands as root.' Prerequisites state attacker must have netadmin privileges, implying escalation from that context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for privilege escalation events originating from vManage process context running as netadmin user, escalating to root. Alert on command injection patterns in process command lines. Baseline normal root escalation paths and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Configuration Push to SD-WAN Edge Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Cisco has observed limited cases where the exploitation of this bug resulted in a configuration change pushed to edge devices.' This is lateral movement and impact phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vManage-to-vSmart configuration push operations. Baseline normal configuration change frequency and payloads. Alert on pushes originated from recently compromised vManage instances, especially those where netadmin-to-root escalation was detected within preceding timeframe.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of CVE-2026-20182 as Entry Vector for CVE-2026-20245
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'To exploit this vulnerability, the attacker must have netadmin privileges...This would require valid credentials or exploitation of CVE-2026-20182 or CVE-2026-20127.' These are prerequisite CVEs; detection chain should include them.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vManage authentication endpoints for exploitation patterns of CVE-2026-20182 (auth bypass). Track failed authentication attempts followed by successful netadmin session establishment within short time window. Correlate with subsequent file upload or script execution events.

suggestion.title: Discovery of Unpatched Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unpatched zero-day' and 'Cisco has not yet released patches for CVE-2026-20245.' Detection scope must include vulnerability inventory against multiple related CVEs: CVE-2026-20245, CVE-2026-20182, CVE-2026-20127.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline all Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager instances by version. Cross-reference against known vulnerable versions for CVE-2026-20245, CVE-2026-20182, CVE-2026-20127. Flag any instances without security patches released after June 2026. This enables proactive defense.

suggestion.title: Fake FIFA Ticketing / Merchandise Site Access Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Fake Sites' as primary attack vector and 'World Cup 2026 Scams Are Already Live' — phishing via lookalike FIFA domains is the confirmed initial access method. No detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for user clicks on domains matching FIFA typosquats (e.g., fifa2026-tickets.com, world-cup-2026.info) or SSL certificate issuance to suspicious FIFA-branded domains. Correlate with login failures or successful logins from anomalous geolocations within hours of click.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Phishing Form Submissions
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists 'Stolen Logins' as primary compromise outcome. Pipeline should detect form-based credential theft from fake ticketing sites but produced no use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious user-agent or browser automation in HTTP POST requests to phishing domains, followed by rapid failed login attempts (credential spraying) against legitimate banking or email services within 24-48 hours. Correlate source IP geolocation.

suggestion.title: Banking Malware Execution and C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically names 'Banking Malware' as attack payload but pipeline extracted zero IOCs (malware hashes, command domains) and no execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of binaries downloaded from phishing email or sites. Monitor for DNS queries to banking trojan C2 domains, HTTP User-Agent spoofing financial institution apps, and suspicious process injection targeting browser or banking software.

suggestion.title: Account Takeover via Stolen Credentials at Banks
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Stolen Logins' are weaponized; pipeline should detect abuse of compromised credentials against banking endpoints but did not.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful logins to banking portals from IPs previously attributed to phishing click activity or geographically impossible travel. Flag login anomalies: first-time 2FA device, unusual login time, rapid transaction initiation post-login.

suggestion.title: FIFA-Themed Phishing Domain Infrastructure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title emphasizes 'Fake Sites' as live attack infrastructure. Pipeline should have extracted or generated domain patterns (typosquats, lookalikes, newly registered) but returned empty IOC set.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new domain registrations with FIFA, World Cup 2026, or country-specific World Cup keywords. Flag SSL certificates issued to domains with high edit-distance from fifa.com or official regional football associations. Correlate with email sending infrastructure WHOIS details.

suggestion.title: Multi-Factor Authentication Bypass or Interception Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'Stolen Logins' and 'Banking Malware' — implies attacker must bypass MFA to drain accounts. Pipeline did not generate detection for MFA evasion techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect approval or bypass of MFA from unusual devices or geolocations within hours of phishing click. Monitor for repeated MFA denial attempts followed by successful login on same account. Alert if banking malware process is observed communicating with MFA token delivery services.

suggestion.title: DbGate JSON script functionName injection — POST /runners/start with code-execution payload
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'The functionName value is interpolated directly into dynamically generated JavaScript source code via string concatenation.' This is the actual attack vector—detecting POST bodies with function injection syntax is more direct than child-process inference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to /runners/start and /runners/load-reader endpoints for JSON payloads containing 'functionName' with JavaScript meta-characters (backticks, curly braces, require/eval keywords). Baseline against known-good DbGate deployment request bodies if available.

suggestion.title: DbGate child_process module import in forked Node subprocess
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RCE executing 'in a forked Node.js child process.' Detection should monitor the calling pattern of require('child_process') or .spawn()/.exec() from within DbGate's runner context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within a Node.js process tree initiated from DbGate (bundle.js or /.dbgate/run/ paths), detect the instantiation of child processes using module-loader hooks or syscall interposition (execve/execvp). Combine with parent command-line context to exclude build-tool child processes.

suggestion.title: DbGate exposed /runners endpoint reconnaissance and validation
suggestion.rationale: Attacker must first discover or confirm the vulnerable endpoint is available. Article describes 'POST /runners/start' as the public-facing attack surface. Detection should flag repeated 404s or 403s on /runners/* paths followed by a successful POST.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect single source IP making GET or OPTIONS requests to /runners/* endpoints (reconnaissance), followed within 5 minutes by a POST to /runners/start or /runners/load-reader. Filter out authenticated DbGate admin accounts based on session tokens.

suggestion.title: DbGate authenticated endpoint access with HTTP request body code patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unsanitized `functionName` parameter' accepting code injection via dynamic `import()`. Need detection in HTTP request bodies, not just URL fields. Article phrase: 'The `require = null` mitigation is trivially bypassed via dynamic `import()`.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to /runners/load-reader endpoint where the HTTP request body contains JavaScript import() syntax, require() patterns, or references to shell execution modules (child_process, execSync). Flag requests from authenticated users with recent account creation or unusual geo/time patterns.

suggestion.title: DbGate root-privileged command execution post-RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'as root' execution explicitly. Need detection for the IMPACT phase once code execution succeeds. Article phrase: 'execute arbitrary OS commands as root'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for shell commands (sh, bash, cmd.exe, powershell) spawned from node/DbGate processes where the spawned process runs with root or SYSTEM privileges. Correlate with recent /runners/load-reader access from the same user/host within 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: DbGate anomalous credential usage for endpoint access
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Authenticated Remote Code Execution' and 'Any user with valid DbGate credentials can execute arbitrary OS commands'. Detection gap: credentials may be compromised. Need to surface unusual authentication patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DbGate authentication from new users, off-hours access, unusual geolocation, or authentication followed immediately (within 30s) by POST to /runners/load-reader endpoint with code-injection patterns. This bridges the 'valid credentials' assumption with the actual exploitation.

suggestion.title: Dynamic JavaScript import() execution in Node runtime
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically calls out the bypass mechanism: '`require = null` mitigation is trivially bypassed via dynamic `import()`'. This is the precise injection technique and warrants its own hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for node.exe or dbgate processes with command-line or memory arguments containing `import(` patterns, especially when spawned from or handling requests to the vulnerable endpoint. This captures the specific evasion technique used.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized role creation by non-admin user
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Any authenticated user could load the page and use its public actions to create new roles.' Pipeline missed the specific harmful action—role creation without authorization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST/CREATE operations to role creation endpoints where the user lacks admin privilege or administrative_role attribute. Flag role creation by non-admin users, newly-created users, or users with only read_users permission.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized admin user deletion
suggestion.rationale: Article states users 'could delete other users, including administrators.' This is direct impact that should alert on deletion of privileged accounts by unprivileged users.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DELETE operations against user records where the requesting user is not admin and the target user has admin_flag=true or role=administrator. Alert on any admin user deletion by non-admin accounts.

suggestion.title: Permission bypass - write action via read-only permission grant
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'RolePermission gated its write actions on the read-only `view_users` permission.' This is direct authorization defect where read permissions incorrectly allow write operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PUT/PATCH/DELETE operations to role-permission or team-settings endpoints where the user's permission set contains only view_users or read_users grants. Flag any modification operations from accounts with read-only permissions.

suggestion.title: RBAC privilege elevation via team settings mutation
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector is RBAC privilege escalation through team settings. Should detect suspicious role/permission assignments that bypass normal authorization workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect assignment of admin role or privileged permissions to non-admin users via team settings. Establish baseline of normal privilege grant patterns; flag role elevation of recently-created accounts, rapid permission grants to single user, or privilege elevation by non-standard administrator accounts.

suggestion.title: Shopper Livewire component method invocation without authorization
suggestion.rationale: Article references vulnerable Livewire endpoints: '*/livewire/update*' and '*/livewire/message/settings.team*'. These Laravel components execute methods without proper authorization checks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to Livewire message/update handlers targeting settings.team component. Alert on method calls (deleteUser, createRole, modifyPermission) invoked by users whose session/permission context does not grant authorization for those actions.

suggestion.title: WordPress Plugin Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Hackers Exploit Critical Everest Forms Pro WordPress Plugin Flaw' — no detection logic exists for attempts to trigger known vulnerable endpoints in this plugin family.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Everest Forms Pro plugin endpoints (typically /wp-content/plugins/everest-forms/) for suspicious parameter injection, unauthenticated RCE payload patterns, or known CVE exploitation signatures. Baseline normal admin/form submission patterns first.

suggestion.title: Suspicious WordPress Admin Account Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'site takeover' via plugin exploitation; attackers typically escalate by creating rogue admin accounts. No detection use case for this follow-on activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag user_register or wp_insert_user events where new admin (meta_key=wp_capabilities, meta_value='administrator') is created outside normal workflow windows, or by non-human service accounts, or with anomalous email domains.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Deployment in WordPress Plugin Directories
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of plugins often results in webshell writes to /wp-content/plugins/ or /wp-content/uploads/. Title emphasizes 'take over' implying persistence; no detection for suspicious file artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .php, .phtml, .php5 file creation or modification in /wp-content/plugins/ or /wp-content/uploads/ by web process (www-data, www, IUSR) outside known deployment windows. Cross-correlate with HTTP requests to those paths in same hour.

suggestion.title: Everest Forms Pro Plugin Version Audit
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Critical Everest Forms Pro WordPress Plugin Flaw' — no IOC or inventory check for vulnerable plugin versions installed across infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all WordPress installations for Everest Forms Pro presence and version. Flag any version ≤ [expected patched version from CVE] and correlate with contemporaneous exploitation attempts in web logs within 24-48 hours.

suggestion.title: WordPress wp-config.php Database Credential Extraction
suggestion.rationale: Plugin RCE often leads to exfiltration of database credentials for lateral movement or data theft. No detection for suspicious file access patterns targeting configuration files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests attempting to read or download wp-config.php, .env, or database.yml files, or log entries showing web process accessing those files for read outside normal plugin initialization.

suggestion.title: File Hash Match: Known Malicious PyPI Package (SHA1)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly provides IOC: 'SHA1: a01c2a21f24db63cb01a67016519aebeca438089' and recommends 'File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match' hunt. Pipeline IOCs section is empty—hash extraction failed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match files downloaded or staged in Python package caches (site-packages, pip cache, .cache) against SHA1 a01c2a21f24db63cb01a67016519aebeca438089. Alert on hash presence during package installation or import.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted PyPI Package Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'The package, named "parsimonius," was crafted to look almost identical to the widely used "parsimonious" library. The single missing letter'. Masquerading (T1036) is the attack pattern—near-homograph package names deceiving developers into installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor pip install logs and ProcessCreate events for package names matching high-similarity typosquats of popular libraries (parsimonious vs parsimonius, requests vs reqeusts, etc.). Cross-reference project dependencies against known malicious package name lists.

suggestion.title: Python Package Installation via pip Execute Phase
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'A deceptive Python package quietly made its way into the PyPI repository, putting thousands of developers at risk'. Installation executes setup.py, enabling arbitrary code execution (T1059.004). No detection covers this execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect python.exe, python3, or pip spawning child processes (subprocess, PowerShell, cmd) during package install. Alert when setup.py execution creates unexpected network sockets, file writes to system directories, or spawns shells.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package Metadata Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Malicious PyPI packages evade initial detection 'before it was caught and removed'. Metadata anomalies (mismatched author, suspicious dependencies, obfuscated code in __init__.py) are early indicators the article does not explicitly detail but are implied by the evasion narrative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Analyze package metadata from PyPI mirrors: flag packages with author/maintainer mismatch vs legitimate upstream, unexpected or excessive dependencies, or base64/zlib-encoded code in setup.py and __init__.py. Cross-check package name Levenshtein distance against top 10k PyPI packages.

suggestion.title: Python Import of Known Malicious Package
suggestion.rationale: Once installed, 'thousands of developers' would import the package. The article implies post-install execution, but no detection monitors for Python import of parsimonius or signature behavioral patterns post-execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Python process execution for import statements or sys.modules entries for 'parsimonius' or other known-malicious packages. Alert if legitimate projects (identified by .git, project config) attempt to load unauthorized variants.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Installation with Suspicious Post-Install Hooks
suggestion.rationale: Article describes supply chain attack via npm packages; malware variants execute post-installation. Pipeline missed detection for postinstall scripts despite explicit attack vector: 'npm in Supply Chain Attacks.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/ci operations for immediate child process spawning (powershell, bash, curl, wget) from node_modules paths. IronWorm and Miasma variants use postinstall hooks for code execution. Flag packages with no public repository, zero-day additions, or name-squatting variants.

suggestion.title: Anomalous npm Package Maintainer Authentication and Version Bumps
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain compromise requires attacker write access to npm packages. Article implies maintainer account takeover or credential abuse, yet pipeline extracted zero IOCs or authentication anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm tokens used from new geographies, multiple tokens for same package, or package version bumps within hours of authentication anomalies. Cross-reference identity provider logs for MFA failures or passwordless sign-in events targeting npm account holders.

suggestion.title: Transitive Dependency Chain Mutation in package-lock.json
suggestion.rationale: Miasma and IronWorm variants propagate via supply chain; attack likely introduces new or modified dependencies. Pipeline should detect lockfile anomalies indicating malicious transitive dependencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package-lock.json diffs for new packages absent from git history, versions newer than npm publish date, or typosquatted dependencies (e.g., 'lodash' vs 'lodash-es'). Flag when introduced by non-human automation or unusual accounts.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Code Execution from node_modules Directory
suggestion.rationale: Worm variants typically embed encoded/obfuscated payloads in npm packages. Pipeline should detect base64, gzip, or minified JavaScript eval() from dependency paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process spawning from **/node_modules/** with command lines containing base64 deobfuscation, `eval()`, or `require()` of dynamically constructed paths. Monitor for Node.js child processes executing system binaries (powershell, curl, nc). Correlate with recent npm install or CI/CD events.

suggestion.title: Command-and-Control Beaconing from Compromised npm Environments
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack establishes C2 for reconnaissance post-installation. Article titles two malware variants; pipeline should detect outbound HTTPS to suspicious domains from dev machines post-npm install.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTPS from development machines to non-whitelisted domains originating from Node.js or npm child processes. Flag DNS queries to homoglyphs of npm.js / github.com, unregistered TLDs, or known malware infrastructure. Correlate timing with package installation events.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation and Persistence via npm Postinstall Context
suggestion.rationale: Worm malware (IronWorm, Miasma) seeks lateral movement and persistence. Pipeline missed detection for UAC bypass or registry modification attempts triggered by postinstall hooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process creation with parent=npm/node.js spawning elevated children or executing known UAC bypass techniques (fodhelper, token impersonation). Detect registry writes to HKLM or system directory modifications from npm postinstall context. Cross-reference CVE databases for relevant privilege escalation exploits.

suggestion.title: Credit card skimming malware injection into payment processing pages
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'hides inside...payment platforms', characteristic of Magecart's JavaScript injection technique. No detection hypothesis was generated despite this being the primary attack vector for card skimming.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected modifications to payment form HTML/JavaScript files, particularly on URLs containing /checkout, /payment, /cart, /billing. Alert on inline or external script injection that exfiltrates form field data (cc_number, cvv, expiry). Baseline legitimate JavaScript hashes and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Abuse of payment service account for command and control
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attack 'uses Stripe...as both its command center'. This requires detecting unusual API authentication or account behavior that deviates from legitimate merchant patterns: 'uses Stripe...as both its command center and its data dump'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate Stripe API usage by your organization (API key age, request patterns, data endpoints accessed). Alert on new API keys, API calls from unusual geolocations, high-volume data retrieval from customer endpoints, or webhook endpoint modifications without change tickets.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of credit card data via compromised payment infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'data dump' of 'stolen card data'. This is bulk exfiltration of PII. Pipeline failed to flag collection/exfiltration kill chain phase despite explicit mention of stolen payment data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for queries aggregating credit card columns (cc_number, pan, card_data) with unusual volumes or no corresponding legitimate business transaction. Flag database exports to unknown accounts, S3/Blob uploads of customer payment tables, or API calls that retrieve card data outside normal transaction context.

suggestion.title: Firebase abuse for malware C2 and exfiltration staging
suggestion.rationale: IOC domain braintree-payment-app.firebaseio.com indicates Firebase Realtime Database as C2 infrastructure. Firebase abuse for malware is low-friction and high-evasion; requires distinct detection patterns from typical legitimate use.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Catalog legitimate Firebase projects owned by your organization. Alert on DNS queries to unexpected *.firebaseio.com domains, especially from non-corporate networks or endpoints not known to use Firebase. Monitor Firebase Realtime Database for unusual access patterns: rapid read/write cycles, large payloads, or commands encoded in JSON. Flag projects created with names spoofing legitimate services (e.g., 'braintree-payment-app' if not verified as official).

suggestion.title: Compromised payment processor account with persistence mechanisms
suggestion.rationale: Using legitimate Stripe account as C2 implies account takeover. Article mentions 'command center' and 'data dump' via Stripe accounts, suggesting attacker persistence via credential abuse or API key compromise: 'uses Stripe...as both its command center'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Stripe/payment processor account activity for credential compromise signals: unexplained password resets, new API key creation without internal request, webhook destination changes, 2FA method additions, or login from high-risk geolocations. Correlate with suspicious API usage (spike in data retrieval, unusual merchant activity) to detect persistence post-compromise.

suggestion.title: IIS Worker Process Spawning System Command Shells
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Custom Web Shell Framework' targeting IIS servers. Web shells execute attacker commands through IIS worker processes (w3wp.exe, aspnet_wp.exe). This is the primary execution mechanism implied by the attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when w3wp.exe or aspnet_wp.exe spawns cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or utilities (whoami, ipconfig, net, certutil) with non-empty arguments. Correlate process creation timestamps with IIS HTTP request logs to link web requests to shell command execution.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized .aspx/.asp File Writes to Web Root
suggestion.rationale: Custom web shell requires file deployment to IIS directories. Article title states web shell 'framework' targeting IIS, indicating persistent file placement in %SystemRoot%\inetpub\wwwroot or application directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ASPX, ASP, and JSPX file creation in IIS web directories. Flag writes from non-standard processes (exclude devenv.exe, msbuild.exe during deployments) and off-hours modifications. Correlate with web server restart events or app pool recycling.

suggestion.title: Suspicious HTTP Requests with Command-Execution Parameters
suggestion.rationale: Web shells receive remote commands via HTTP parameters (cmd=, exec=, shell=). Article's 'custom framework' implies parameterized RCE over HTTP; this is command-and-control via the web application itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Analyze IIS logs for HTTP requests to deployed .aspx files with suspicious query strings matching web shell parameter patterns. Group by source IP and frequency to identify command execution sessions. Cross-reference with File Events to confirm shell writes preceded the requests.

suggestion.title: IIS Configuration and Web.config Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Web shell deployment against hardened IIS often requires config changes to enable handler registration, custom modules, or disable protections. Article implies deliberate framework setup.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor modifications to ApplicationHost.config, web.config files, and HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\InetStp registry hive. Alert on handler registration, custom HTTP module installation, or authentication bypass configurations added post-baseline.

suggestion.title: Inbound Exploitation Traffic Targeting IIS (CVE Scanning)
suggestion.rationale: Article title states OP-512 'targets' IIS servers, implying initial compromise via exploitation. IIS vulnerability scanning and RCE exploitation are the likely initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound HTTP requests with exploitation signatures: double-encoded payloads, path traversal sequences in URLs, script injection in parameters, or requests to known IIS RCE endpoints. Correlate with outbound HTTP activity from the server post-request.

suggestion.title: OP-512 Threat Actor Attribution and Known Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names OP-512 as the threat cluster. SOC teams require a baseline of known OP-512 infrastructure (C2 domains, IPs, certificates, file hashes) for attribution and related-incident detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate detected web shell C2 infrastructure (domains, IPs, certificate hashes) against published OP-512 IOCs from security vendors and threat feeds. Flag any domain/IP reuse across internal investigations to map the actor's campaign scope.

suggestion.title: Anomalous SMTP Relay Activity from Cloud Compute Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article states servers hijacked for 'covert SMTP relay network' — this is the stated impact and primary detection vector. Pipeline missed the core malicious activity entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baselines of SMTP egress per cloud instance type/role. Alert on: (a) cloud instances initiating bulk SMTP connections (>100 in 1hr) to non-organizational mail relays, (b) instances sending to IPs flagged on spam blacklists (Spamhaus, SURBL), (c) outbound port 25/587/465 traffic to external mail servers from compute instances not designated as mail infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Cloud Service Principal / API Key Compromise — Batch Unauthorized Instance Access
suggestion.rationale: Hijacking of 230 instances across AWS, GCP, Azure implies coordinated credential theft or broad IAM policy misconfiguration. Article mentions cross-provider scale, implying systemic credential compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cloud provider authentication logs for: (a) service principal / IAM user login anomalies (new geo/IP source, batch logins in short window), (b) creation or rotation of access keys/tokens from unexpected contexts, (c) API calls to compute.instances or EC2 describe operations from unfamiliar principals, (d) failed authentication attempts followed by successful access within minutes.

suggestion.title: Malware Deployment to Cloud Instances — PCPJack Artifact and Behavioral Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article names PCPJack as the attack tool deployed to 230 instances. Pipeline failed to surface execution-phase detection logic or malware signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On cloud instances, detect: (a) suspicious privilege escalation (sudo, runas, SetSecurityRolesMembership), (b) installation of mail services (postfix, sendmail, exim) or creation of /etc/postfix/main.cf with attacker-controlled relayhost, (c) creation of cron jobs or systemd services for persistence, (d) unexpected child processes spawned by system daemons (e.g., sendmail spawning /bin/bash).

suggestion.title: Multi-Cloud Infrastructure Enumeration and Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Successful compromise of 230 instances across three cloud providers suggests prior reconnaissance to identify vulnerable/misconfigured resources. Article headline implies coordinated targeting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect automated enumeration from single source IPs: (a) repeated DescribeInstances, ListInstances, ListVMs, GetInstances across regions/subscriptions, (b) cross-provider API reconnaissance (e.g., AWS API calls from service principal attempting GCP queries), (c) enumeration followed by targeted API calls to specific instance IDs within hours, (d) enumeration from IPs not correlated with authorized DevOps teams.

suggestion.title: Mass Cloud Instance Startup / Activation from Attacker-Controlled Credentials
suggestion.rationale: 230 instances hijacked implies either existing instances reconfigured or deployment of new instances. Either scenario should show in compute API logs as bulk instance management from compromised credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on: (a) batch StartInstances or InstanceStart calls from single API key/service principal within short window (e.g., >5 instances in 1hr), (b) bulk InstanceModifyInstanceAttribute or ModifyInstancePlacement to instances sharing suspicious network properties, (c) creation of security groups/firewall rules allowing inbound SSH/RDP immediately before instance startup.

suggestion.title: Outbound Mail Traffic to Malicious SMTP Relay Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Relay network infrastructure implies attacker-controlled mail servers. Pipeline should extract C2 domains/IPs for relay endpoints from article and build network-based detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If article provides C2 relay endpoints, create deny-list for outbound SMTP/TLS connections from cloud instances to those IPs. Alternatively, detect connections to IPs with mail service fingerprints (MTA banner grabbing) not owned by cloud provider or customer organization. Monitor DNS queries from instances for dynamic mail relay domains.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Code Execution via Agentic GitHub Actions
suggestion.rationale: Article addresses 'Claude Code Github action case'—an agentic AI integrated into CI/CD. The core risk is malicious or compromised prompts triggering unintended code commits, package builds, or deployments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions workflow runs for unexpected code generation, compilation, or deployment triggered by natural-language inputs. Flag process chains launched by agentic runtimes that diverge from approved templates or exceed expected resource/network footprint.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration via AI-Generated Deployment Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Article focuses on 'Securing CI/CD'—an implicit threat is AI agents generating code that embeds or exfiltrates secrets (API keys, tokens, database credentials) into artifacts, logs, or external endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect secrets (AWS keys, PATs, database passwords) appearing in GitHub Actions logs, build artifacts, or code commits post-AI-generation. Correlate credential leaks with agentic action invocations using natural language that doesn't explicitly mention secret handling.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Poisoning via Malicious Prompt Injection in Agentic Workflows
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'agentic world'—implicit risk is prompt injection attacks where untrusted inputs (PRs, issue comments, external webhooks) guide the AI agent to generate backdoors, malware, or logic bombs into commits.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag commits generated immediately after pull requests or webhook events containing suspicious natural-language instructions (e.g., 'add a hidden function', 'skip tests', 'send output to external URL'). Correlate code diff entropy and entropy of source prompts.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Misconfigured Agentic Action Permissions
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses 'Securing CI/CD'—agentic actions may inherit overly broad GitHub permissions (repo admin, secrets access, deployment rights) due to misconfiguration or social engineering of the setup.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for agentic actions granted permissions beyond their declared purpose (e.g., write-all-repos, admin-secrets). Alert on permission escalations triggered by natural-language requests or undocumented role changes.

suggestion.title: Repository Takeover via Compromised Agentic Agent Credentials
suggestion.rationale: An agentic GitHub Action uses credentials (PATs, deploy keys, OIDC tokens) to commit and push code. Compromise of the agent's identity or token leakage enables full repository control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect commits signed with agentic action credentials appearing from unexpected IP ranges, timezones, or high-frequency automation patterns inconsistent with normal CI. Flag branch protection rule deletions or forced pushes by agentic identities.

suggestion.title: Downstream Package Tampering via Agentic Build Artifact Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article addresses CI/CD security—agentic action may be manipulated to alter published packages (npm, PyPI, NuGet) by modifying build scripts, version numbers, or checksums before release.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor build artifacts generated by agentic actions for unexpected modifications (version inflation, binary hash changes, new dependencies). Correlate with prompts or environment variable changes that were not explicitly approved.

suggestion.title: HTTP 401 Response from Third-Party Script CDN Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'polyfill[.]io domain became active again and started responding with HTTP 401 authentication requests'—this is the exact mechanism triggering malicious browser login prompts, the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP traffic for 401 responses from third-party JavaScript CDN domains, especially polyfill[.]io. Alert when user endpoints receive HTTP 401 from external script-serving infrastructure, as this triggers browser credential prompts—the phishing vector. Flag any 401 responses from known-compromised CDN domains or dormant infrastructure newly reactivated.

suggestion.title: Script Load from Known-Compromised Supply Chain Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'some sites using the service failed to clean all their pages over the past two years, so remnants of Polyfill code remained'—ongoing script loads from polyfill[.]io indicate incomplete remediation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests loading scripts from polyfill[.]io and other known-compromised CDN domains. Alert when endpoints initiate script fetches from polyfill[.]io, indicating websites have not fully remediated post-compromise. Maintain and alert on a maintained list of supply chain infrastructure known to have been compromised.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Browser Credential Prompt from Non-Authentication Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the user-facing attack directly: 'User browsers interpret [HTTP 401] as a request for a username and password, so they serve a login prompt'—detecting this anomalous credential event is direct attack detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected credential prompts during web browsing by correlating HTTP 401 responses from third-party domains with browser authentication dialog events. Alert when JavaScript CDN, polyfill, or external resource domains trigger Windows credential prompts, as legitimate services should never require authentication through external script sources.

suggestion.title: FFmpeg Process Execution with Malformed Media Input
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 21 zero-days in FFmpeg. Exploitation typically requires triggering via crafted media files or command injection. Phrase: 'AI Agent Uncovers 21 Zero-Days in FFmpeg'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FFmpeg execution with suspicious file arguments (non-standard paths, temp directories, UNC paths, encoding anomalies). Correlate with unpatched FFmpeg binary versions via binary analysis or version string logging.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Chrome Renderer Child Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Chrome's 429 patched bugs likely include sandbox/RCE escapes. Post-exploitation typically manifests as unexpected child processes from renderer. Phrase: 'Chrome Patches Record 429 Bugs'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on chrome.exe or chrome processes spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or non-standard children; flag when parent process has unusual command-line args or network connections.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Software Inventory Drift Detection
suggestion.rationale: No detection use case exists for identifying unpatched FFmpeg/Chrome in fleet, creating blind spot for exploitation. Phrase: implicit gap in article (vulnerability disclosure without patch-compliance monitoring).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Daily inventory scan of FFmpeg and Chrome versions; alert on instances not updated to post-vulnerability-disclosure versions within SLA window.

suggestion.title: Media File Anomaly in Email or Web Downloads
suggestion.rationale: FFmpeg zero-days are weaponized via malicious media files. Article mentions zero-day discovery but no email/download detection. Phrase: 'AI Agent Uncovers 21 Zero-Days in FFmpeg'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag media files (mp4, mkv, avi, etc.) arriving via email/web with anomalous encoding, null bytes, or archive nesting; alert if downloaded by users who subsequently run FFmpeg.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Intelligence Feed Lag Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'record 429 bugs' patched in Chrome but provides no timelines or CVE numbers in extracted content. Gap exists between patch release and organizational patching. Phrase: 'Chrome Patches Record 429 Bugs'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Chrome/FFmpeg patch advisories against fleet asset inventory; flag devices where days-to-patch exceeds SLA; escalate if exploits appear in threat feeds.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Actively Exploited SolarWinds Serv-U DoS Flaw.' Pipeline generated zero use cases for detecting exploitation attempts despite explicit active-exploitation status. Should monitor for craft of DoS payloads and suspicious Serv-U service port activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on abnormal inbound traffic to Serv-U service ports (typically TCP 21, 990, 5382, 5383, or configuration-specific ports). Detect patterns consistent with DoS exploitation: rapid connection sequences, malformed commands, or resource-exhaustion payloads.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U Denial of Service Impact Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly identifies vulnerability as 'DoS Flaw' in impact phase. Pipeline generated no detection use case for service unavailability, crash loops, or resource exhaustion—the core attack outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Serv-U process for repeated crashes, restarts within short time windows, or sustained high CPU/memory consumption. Alert on service unavailability, connection reset errors to Serv-U ports, or downstream client timeouts.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable SolarWinds Serv-U Version Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV catalog entry implies specific affected versions. Article does not specify pipeline should inventory and flag vulnerable Serv-U instances for patch priority.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Software Inventory for SolarWinds Serv-U installations. Cross-reference version numbers against CISA KEV affected versions and flag non-compliant instances for patch urgency.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Attempt Against Cisco SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states CVE-2026-20245 is 'actively exploited'—the pipeline must detect inbound requests to vulnerable endpoints. Article phrase: 'CVE-2026-20245 Flaw Actively Exploited'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager admin endpoints (typically port 443, path patterns /api/*, /admin/*) from untrusted networks. Track POST/GET requests with payloads indicative of CVE-2026-20245 exploitation (injection patterns, memory corruption markers, or known PoC signatures). Correlate with 4xx/5xx error spikes indicating scanning or failed exploit attempts.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Process Execution from SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation implies successful code execution. Article states 'no patch available'—vulnerable systems are actively compromised. Need to detect execution phase behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected process spawning (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/bash, curl, wget) launched by the Cisco SD-WAN Manager service account or its child processes. Alert on system calls to execve() or ShellExecute() originating from SD-WAN Manager memory space. Focus on processes with low prevalence or executing from temporary directories (/tmp, %TEMP%).

suggestion.title: Outbound Command & Control Communication from Compromised SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Active exploitation scenario implies attacker maintains persistence. Article phrase 'actively exploited' suggests ongoing c2 activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from Cisco SD-WAN Manager hosts to non-standard ports (non-80/443, non-RFC1918 CIDR blocks). Flag DNS queries to newly registered domains, dynamic DNS providers, or IPs associated with known exploit infrastructure. Detect encrypted traffic with anomalous TLS certificate chains or self-signed certs from the vulnerable service.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: SD-WAN Manager is a network management appliance with likely access to internal routing and device configuration. Exploitation enables lateral movement to connected infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect RDP, SSH, or WinRM connections originating from the SD-WAN Manager host to internal subnets, particularly to network infrastructure (routers, switches, firewalls). Flag credential forwarding from the manager to domain controllers or other high-value targets. Alert on unexpected lateral scanning activity initiated by the compromised manager.

suggestion.title: Unusual Authentication Activity on SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation may create backdoor accounts, enable default credentials, or bypass authentication. Pipeline should detect persistence mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for failed authentication attempts against SD-WAN Manager webUI followed by successful logins from unusual geolocations or IPs. Detect creation of new administrative accounts or privilege escalation of service accounts. Alert on password changes to high-privileged SD-WAN accounts outside maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Version Fingerprinting for Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Vulnerability Assessment
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'no patch available'—defenders must identify all vulnerable instances. Pipeline should extract affected version ranges to enable proactive discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Collect HTTP response headers or API responses from Cisco SD-WAN Manager instances to extract version strings (e.g., Server: Cisco/20.x.y). Cross-reference against CVE-2026-20245 affected-version list. Correlate vulnerable versions in your environment with network exposure (internet-facing, VPN-accessible, etc.) to prioritize remediation.

suggestion.title: PHP Injection via Form Field Single-Quote Escape
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack as 'value for a text field that begins with a single quote to close the wrapping string literal, followed by a PHP statement' — no detection for quote-based PHP escape payloads in form submissions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor form submissions to Everest Forms endpoints (plugin versions ≤1.9.12) for payloads containing single quotes, PHP keywords (eval, exec, wp_insert_user), and comment markers (//). Correlate with IPs 202.56.2.126 or 209.146.60.26.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized WordPress Administrator Account Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker 'calls wp_insert_user() to create a new administrator account with the username diksimarina' — no detection rule for admin creation post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on wp_insert_user() calls with role=administrator executed in non-admin context, especially with username 'diksimarina' or single-word patterns. Cross-reference with form submission timestamps from source IPs.

suggestion.title: High-Volume Exploitation Attempts from Known Attacker IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article states Wordfence 'blocked over 29,300 attempts' originating from 202.56.2.126 and 209.146.60.26 — no detection for distributed exploit attempts or volumetric signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Threshold alert: >50 requests per hour to vulnerable plugin endpoints from single IP with injection syntax payloads. Immediate alert for any requests from hardcoded IPs 202.56.2.126, 209.146.60.26.

suggestion.title: Post-Admin-Creation Webshell or Backdoor Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article notes breach consequences include 'installing plugins and themes, planting backdoors and webshells' — no detection for malicious file writes or plugin installs following unauthorized admin creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor wp-content/plugins and wp-content/themes for suspicious file creation or modification within 10 minutes after unauthorized admin account creation (especially 'diksimarina'). Flag newly installed plugins from non-authenticated contexts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Administrator Account Query by Username Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends defenders 'review administrator accounts for any suspicious activity, especially containing the string diksimarina' — no automated detection for this reconnaissance post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any WordPress user table queries or admin list access immediately following form submission activity. Specifically detect admin accounts with username 'diksimarina' or similar single-word patterns created after vulnerability window (post-March 18 patch release).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-3300 Signature Detection in Web Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article describes specific technical vulnerability in Complex Calculation feature's eval() context — no signature-based detection for known payload patterns targeting this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deploy WAF rule matching HTTP requests to Everest Forms plugin endpoints containing CVE-2026-3300 payload indicators: quote-comment sequences ('.*//), wp_insert_user function calls in form field values, eval() syntax in form parameters.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Web Scraping Activity from Smart TV
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states devices are 'turning smart TVs into web-scraping proxies'—direct description of collection/exfiltration phase. Pipeline failed to suggest detection for systematic content harvesting, high-volume DOM requests, or parsing activity inconsistent with normal streaming usage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Smart TV originating high-volume HTTP requests to news/publishing domains with parsing patterns (sequential page scraping, sitemaps, archives) without user interaction; sustained outbound bandwidth 10x baseline; repeated requests with non-standard user-agents or no user-agent header.

suggestion.title: Malicious Free App Installation with Network Abuse Permissions
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is explicitly 'free apps' on smart TVs. Pipeline missed initial access detection: apps claiming innocuous function (games, weather) while requesting network, storage, or execution permissions required for scraping infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Installation of app from unofficial store, sideload, or suspicious publisher; app manifest requests network + file system access for stated function; permission grant precedes network abuse; app signature/hash unknown to OS app stores.

suggestion.title: Command-and-Control Beaconing from Smart TV to Scraping Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article implies persistent botnet-like repurposing ('quietly turning into proxies'). Pipeline failed to suggest C2 detection: periodic outbound connections to attacker domains, heartbeat patterns, or data exfiltration channels from TV IP addresses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: TV device establishing outbound TCP/UDP to non-ISP, non-CDN domain on non-standard port; periodic beacons at fixed intervals during off-peak hours; DNS queries for attacker domains followed by immediate connection; data exfiltration in POST payloads.

suggestion.title: Unusual Sustained Resource Consumption on Smart TV (CPU/Memory/Bandwidth)
suggestion.rationale: Web scraping is resource-intensive. Article describes 'quiet' repurposing implying background execution. Pipeline missed impact detection: CPU/memory spikes from background process, sustained high bandwidth consumption, battery drain inconsistent with idle state.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: CPU usage >50% from unknown process during 10+ consecutive hours off-peak; network egress 5+ standard deviations above baseline; memory growth >100MB for single background process; power consumption elevated during user-idle periods.

suggestion.title: Execution of Embedded Scripts or Payload from Malicious App
suggestion.rationale: Article describes apps as active proxies (not passive stubs)—suggests script injection, WebView exploitation, or downloaded payload execution. Pipeline omitted execution-phase detection despite obvious attack step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: App spawning unexpected child processes (curl, wget, python, node); execution of scripts from /tmp or app data directory post-installation; process command line containing URLs or scraping keywords; app launching headless browser or WebView with non-standard arguments.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Scraped Content via Atypical Channels
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline produced no exfiltration detection despite article describing scraping 'for AI' training—implies large-scale data exfiltration. Should detect compression, archiving, encoding, or tunneling of harvested web content.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: App creating .zip, .tar, .rar archives of scraped content; POST requests containing gzip/base64-encoded payloads; large files transferred to single external IP over period of hours; exfiltration to cloud storage (S3, Azure Blob) with no legitimate user context.

suggestion.title: Smart TV Outbound Connections to Known Proxy Service Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article names domains `proxyjs.bright-sdk.com`, `proxyjs.brdtnet.com`, `clientsdk.bright-sdk.com` and IPs `3.33.193.183`, `15.197.193.114`—core IOCs for C2/exfiltration. No network-IOC use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Residential smart TV device establishing persistent outbound connections to proxy service FQDNs or IPs associated with residential proxy networks. Alert on connection success rate >80% over 24h from devices with no prior proxy configuration.

suggestion.title: Excessive Outbound Data Volume from Smart TV Over Residential Link
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'scrape web data for AI training' and enrollment into proxy network—implies sustained data exfiltration. No behavioral/traffic anomaly use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Smart TV device generating >500 GB/month outbound traffic to non-CDN, non-streaming endpoints, or sudden 10x increase in unique destination IPs. Baseline residential TV usage is <50 GB/month.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Application Installation from Official Smart TV App Stores
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is 'free apps available on Samsung, LG, Roku platforms'—initial access via supply-chain compromise. No app installation/persistence use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: App installation from official Samsung/LG/Roku stores followed by network connections to proxy infrastructure within 24 hours. Correlate app metadata (permissions, network access) against proxy-known malicious app signatures.

suggestion.title: DNS Queries to Residential Proxy Service Domains from Smart TV
suggestion.rationale: Article names Luminati/Bright Data domain ecosystem—DNS activity is early-stage indicator before C2 connection. No DNS-based detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Smart TV device querying `*.luminati.io`, `*.bright-sdk.com`, `*.brdtnet.com`, `*.luminatinet.com` domains. Single query = low fidelity; multiple queries to 3+ subdomains within 1h = medium fidelity.

suggestion.title: Smart TV Deceptive Consent Dialog Interaction Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article states consent 'buried in TV remote's arrow-key navigation'—indicates obfuscation/dark pattern. No defense-evasion/deception detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect app requesting elevated permissions (network, storage, device identifiers) via multi-step/nested dialogs, or permission requests routed through unrelated UI flows (e.g., consent buried in settings menu navigation).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Mass Commits to High-Value GitHub Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 73 Microsoft repos 'hit'—signals mass commit injection. Pipeline failed to generate detection for unusual commit activity from compromised/new accounts, commits merged without review, or commits to repos with high downstream impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect commits to high-trust repos (>10K stars, >100 forks, critical Microsoft projects) from newly-provisioned accounts, previously-inactive accounts, or accounts with atypical API token usage. Flag commits merged without review or branch protection bypasses in repos with enforced policies.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Malware Distribution via Package Registry
suggestion.rationale: Worm designation implies self-propagating malicious payload distributed downstream. Pipeline did not surface detection for unusual package publishes, new versions of established packages from compromised accounts, or backdoored dependencies.
log_sources: Package registry logs (NuGet, npm, GitHub Packages)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new package versions published from high-trust accounts outside business hours, multiple rapid publishes within minutes, unusual file sizes, suspicious new dependencies, or code changes inconsistent with release notes. Cross-reference with Miasma malware signatures.

suggestion.title: GitHub Account Compromise Detection - Atypical Access Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack implies GitHub account(s) compromised. Article title establishes compromise of accounts with write access to 73 repos. Pipeline missed detection for account anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sudden increases in API calls from compromised accounts, new personal access tokens created outside normal workflows, sign-ins from new geographies, PAT usage from non-standard IP ranges, or rapid authentication failures followed by success patterns.

suggestion.title: Malware Family Tracking - Miasma Worm Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Miasma Worm' as threat. Pipeline extracted zero malware-family-specific indicators: hashes, signatures, behavioral patterns, C&C infrastructure, persistence mechanisms required for family correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish Miasma Worm baseline: file hashes from known samples, registry persistence locations, named pipes, mutex objects, process execution patterns, and network indicators (C&C domains/IPs). Monitor for processes matching malware behavior in environments consuming affected repos.

suggestion.title: Downstream Consumer Malware Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: 73 repos indicates large downstream exposure surface. Pipeline did not generate detection for malware execution in environments consuming compromised dependencies from these repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In environments that consume the 73 affected repos, monitor for suspicious process spawning matching Miasma execution patterns (unexpected PowerShell/cmd invocation, repo enumeration tools, credential utilities). Correlate execution timeline with package update timestamps to establish causal link.

suggestion.title: GitHub Secrets and Credentials Exfiltration via API Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Worm designation suggests lateral movement and credential harvesting. Pipeline missed detection for abuse of GitHub API to exfiltrate secrets, environment variables, CI/CD tokens stored in repos, or Azure credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag bulk queries to GitHub API secret endpoints, mass repo cloning via raw API, repeated requests to environment variable endpoints, or API token usage from unexpected IP ranges. Monitor for exfiltration of Azure AD secrets, CI/CD pipeline tokens, or database credentials stored in repo files.

suggestion.title: GitHub Repository Disablement After Suspicious Commits
suggestion.rationale: Article states '72 Other Repositories Disabled' following supply-chain compromise. Detection should flag repositories disabled shortly after unusual push activity or permission changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repository disablement or forced deletion events preceded within 1-2 hours by commits from non-standard CI/CD actors, permission elevation in GitHub Actions secrets, or environment variable exfiltration patterns. Correlate with build log anomalies.

suggestion.title: Malicious GitHub Action Execution in Build Pipeline
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'Azure Functions Action' compromise and 'AI Coding Agents' as targets—indicating Actions framework abuse. Detection should catch execution of actions with suspicious permissions or network I/O.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub Actions executing new or recently-modified actions with secrets access, spawning shell commands to non-Microsoft endpoints, or invoking container images from untrusted registries. Cross-reference action version against GitHub Marketplace published versions.

suggestion.title: Credential Access via AI Agent Compromised Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Article frames attack as targeting 'AI Coding Agents'—implying poisoned dependencies or prompts. Should detect when AI agent contexts access credential stores, GitHub tokens, or cloud provider SDKs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for AI coding agent processes (e.g., Node.js, Python interpreters in GitHub Actions runners) accessing ~/.ssh, ~/.netrc, $GITHUB_TOKEN env vars, or cloud credential files. Flag unusual subprocess calls to `git config`, `gh auth`, or cloud CLI tools invoked by agent processes.

suggestion.title: Rapid Repository Forking or Cloning Before Disablement
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attackers typically exfiltrate repository code before disabling targets to preserve malicious changes. Should detect bulk clone/fork activity correlated with later disablement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple git clone or repository fork operations from a single GitHub user/token in 5-minute window, especially from CI/CD or programmatic contexts (GitHub Actions, API calls). Escalate if correlated with repository settings changes or disablement within 1 hour.

suggestion.title: Azure Functions Manifest or Configuration Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'Azure Functions Action' compromise. Should detect when function configurations, bindings, or connection strings are modified via GitHub Actions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Azure Functions logs and audit trails for function app settings changes originating from GitHub Actions deployments. Flag modifications to environment variables, managed identities, or storage bindings that lack corresponding pull-request approvals or code review.

suggestion.title: Suspicious durabletask PyPI Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'durabletask PyPI Package Compromised'—pipeline must detect installation of the named malicious package and flag it by version range.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor pip install activity and imports of package 'durabletask'. Correlate with package metadata queries to identify malicious version installation window. Alert on any installation in affected version range.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Process Spawn from Python Import
suggestion.rationale: Article describes supply-chain code compromise—malicious packages execute on import. Pipeline missed execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor child process creation, network outbound, and file writes spawned from python.exe or python3 process immediately after durabletask import. Flag unexpected shells, network beacons, or binary drops.

suggestion.title: PyPI Maintainer Account Compromise Pattern
