suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks often require attacker control of package maintainer credentials. Article references package compromise but pipeline surfaced no account-takeover detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unusual maintainer activity on PyPI: logins from new IPs, unusual upload patterns, rapid version bumps, metadata changes, or revoked API tokens. Correlate with GitHub push activity and CI/CD job logs.

suggestion.title: Mass Downstream Installation of Compromised Package
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise affects all downstream consumers. Article emphasizes broad impact but pipeline provided no aggregation-layer detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In environment, detect spike in pip install for 'durabletask' or auto-updates pulling the malicious version. Correlate installations across multiple hosts and apps to identify scope. Cross-reference with package metadata to confirm malicious version window.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Network Exfiltration Post-Package Load
suggestion.rationale: Compromised packages typically phone home or exfiltrate data. Article states attack but pipeline did not suggest command-and-control detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network connections from Python processes that imported durabletask. Flag outbound DNS queries to suspicious domains, HTTPS connections to unknown hosts, or traffic patterns consistent with data exfiltration or C2 beaconing.

suggestion.title: Package Integrity Failure — Hash or Signature Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Article implies code modification in published package. Pipeline should flag detection of integrity control bypass or checksum anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for disabled pip verification, missing or invalid signatures, hash mismatches during package verification, or forced installs despite verification failure. Correlate with package downloads to identify affected machines.

suggestion.title: Brickstorm Backdoor Execution on Storage Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names Brickstorm (Golang/Rust variants) deployed to Egnyte, pfSense, Synology NAS, and Linux servers; describes it as primary persistence mechanism 'undetected in the environments of various targets...for more than a year.' No UC generated despite identifiable process and network signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected binary execution on storage appliances (Egnyte, Synology NAS, Linux archive servers) and firewall devices (pfSense). Brickstorm variants may exhibit golang/rust binary signatures, socket creation patterns, or spawning from admin/system processes. Cross-reference with known C2 communication patterns and multiplexing behavior.

suggestion.title: M365 Access Evasion via SSL VPN Proxy + Stolen Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes attackers used 'Brickstorm proxying features and stolen credentials, the threat actor accessed the organization's Microsoft 365 environment' specifically to 'blend in with legitimate network traffic and evade Conditional Access policies that would have otherwise prevented access.' Critical bypass technique with no detection UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on M365 sign-ins sourced from SSL VPN gateway IPs (anomalous for normal users) using credentials that have not previously accessed from that source. Flag when Conditional Access policy indicators are suppressed or when a single VPN-source credential accesses multiple M365 services (Teams, SharePoint, Exchange) within short windows. Detect failed Conditional Access policy triggers followed by policy modification.

suggestion.title: Plenet (.NET Backdoor) Deployment to NAS Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article introduces 'previously undocumented' Plenet/Grimbolt: '.NET-based backdoor that offers interactive shell access, remote command execution, file manipulation' deployed to Synology NAS for persistence post-re-compromise. No UC for .NET reverse-shell detection on appliances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect .NET CLR spawning on Synology NAS or similar storage appliances (atypical for firmware). Monitor for WebSocket library imports or socket-creation syscalls from .NET processes. Alert on new scheduled tasks or service installations on NAS devices, which deviate sharply from normal appliance administration. Cross-reference with C2 domains extracted from infrastructure metadata.

suggestion.title: AgentPSD Python Reverse Shell Fallback Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article describes AgentPSD as 'simple Python-based reverse shell utility...fallback persistence mechanism...configured to connect to a different domain than the one Brickstorm used.' Deployed to same infrastructure but never executed (Brickstorm remained active), yet represents clear secondary access channel not detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python interpreter (python.exe, python3) spawning on servers and NAS devices with arguments matching reverse-shell patterns (socket import, subprocess pipes, `os.dup2` redirection). Monitor outbound network connections from Python processes to non-standard ports/domains, especially secondary C2 infrastructure distinct from primary backdoor. Flag Python scripts written to disk in atypical locations (appliance startup dirs, archive servers).

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from MSP-Managed Firewall to Customer Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article states VerdantBamboo placed 'BSD variant of Brickstorm on a pfSense firewall' at MSP, 'compromised at least 18 months earlier,' with 'medium confidence that the attacker pivoted from the MSP into the victim organization's environment.' Classic MSP-compromise-to-customer-lateral-move pattern with no pivot detection UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor MSP-managed firewalls for outbound connections to customer internal IP ranges from firewall administrative processes. Alert on configuration changes enabling new VPN routes, port forwards, or tunnel rules pointing to customer internal segments. Correlate with Brickstorm process execution or WebSocket C2 signatures originating from firewall egress. Cross-check MSP firewall admin logs for unusual config changes during 18-month dwell window.

suggestion.title: WebSocket Protocol C2 Communication Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article notes both Brickstorm and Plenet use 'WebSocket protocol for C2 communications' with 'multiplexing library for simultaneous data streams to the server.' Distinct, detectable network signature; no UC for WebSocket C2 fingerprinting or anomaly detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for WebSocket traffic (wss://, ws:// schemes) in proxy logs to rare or first-seen domains from non-browser processes (servers, appliances, NAS devices). Examine WebSocket payload patterns for multiplexing signatures (frame delimiters, simultaneous streams from single source to same destination). Alert on WebSocket connections from storage appliances or firewall devices—legitimate WebSocket is extremely uncommon on infrastructure endpoints.

suggestion.title: Serv-U POST request with Content-Encoding deflate header
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'SolarWinds Serv-U is susceptible to specially crafted POST requests that crash the Serv-U service without authentication using Content-Encoding: deflate'—this is the precise attack signature that must be the centerpiece of detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to Serv-U endpoints (ports 21, 22, 443) containing 'Content-Encoding: deflate' header. Article confirms this header is not legitimate for Serv-U functionality. Alert on any occurrence, especially from external sources or if temporally correlated with service unavailability.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U service crash or unexpected restart pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the vulnerability as causing the service to 'crash'—repeated unexpected restarts/crashes on vulnerable versions are the visible impact indicator of active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected Serv-U process termination or service restart. Flag rapid restart cycles (3+ restarts in 10 minutes) on unpatched Serv-U versions. Correlate with network traffic patterns to confirm DoS exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated network exploitation attempts on Serv-U
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes vulnerability is 'Remote attackers can exploit...without privileges' and 'without authentication'—any inbound connection to Serv-U from untrusted sources is an exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound connections to Serv-U service ports from external networks. Given the low-complexity, no-auth requirement, detect sudden spikes in connection attempts or port scans targeting FTP (21), SFTP (22), HTTP (443) ports associated with Serv-U.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Serv-U version detection and patching inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article notes patched version (15.5.4 Hotfix 1) and 'there is no information on how many have already been patched'—inventory of pre-patch versions is essential for vulnerability management.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory Serv-U installations and flag versions prior to 15.5.4 Hotfix 1 as vulnerable. Track patching closure rate. Priority: Shodan reports 12,000+ exposed instances; flag publicly-routable Serv-U on vulnerable versions immediately.

suggestion.title: Serv-U Internet Exposure Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [...template]' and directs substitution of CVE-2026-28318. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this being the primary recommended hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate assets running SolarWinds Serv-U exposed to internet via vulnerability scanner, network scan, or firewall inbound rules. Cross-reference with patch inventory to identify unpatched instances. Prioritize by internet-facing exposure.

suggestion.title: POST Requests with Content-Encoding: deflate to Serv-U
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exact exploitation technique: 'specially crafted POST requests using the Content-Encoding: deflate header'. Pipeline missed behavioral IOC that directly indicates exploitation attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP POST requests with Content-Encoding: deflate header targeting Serv-U endpoints. Track source IP and timestamp. Correlate temporal proximity with Serv-U service crashes or resource spikes for exploitation confirmation.

suggestion.title: Serv-U Service Crashes and Availability Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability mechanism: 'crash the Serv-U service without authentication'. Pipeline failed to translate impact into detection. Sudden service termination is direct evidence of exploitation or attack attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected Serv-U process termination or service stop events. Baseline normal restart patterns. Alert on unscheduled crashes, especially following inbound network traffic anomalies. Correlate with resource consumption spikes.

suggestion.title: Resource Exhaustion in Serv-U Process
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly described as 'uncontrolled resource consumption'. Pipeline generated no detection for anomalous CPU/memory by Serv-U, which precedes and confirms the crash mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline Serv-U CPU and memory utilization. Alert on sudden spike (>3σ deviation) sustained for >30 seconds without legitimate workload explanation. Combine with temporal correlation to POST requests for attack confirmation.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access Attempts to Serv-U
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes vulnerability can be exploited 'without authentication', signaling attackers bypass login controls. Pipeline should flag unauthenticated POST requests as higher-risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Serv-U access logs for POST requests originating outside authenticated sessions. Cross-reference with asset scope (should only be internal for sensitive instances). Combine with Content-Encoding: deflate header for exploitation likelihood assessment.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U Patch Compliance (CVE-2026-28318)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch due date (2026-06-19) and emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer'. Pipeline should create a use case for tracking patch status against known exploited vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for Serv-U installations flagged with CVE-2026-28318. Verify patched versions are deployed. Cross-reference with internet-exposure scans. Report exceptions with remediation timeline tracking.

suggestion.title: SD-WAN Manager Malicious CSV Upload to vSmart
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'uploading a crafted file' triggering command injection and provides exact log pattern: 'vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh -cli path /home/admin/malicious.csv vpn 0'. This is the core exploit vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager /var/log/scripts.log for execution of vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh with suspicious file paths, especially /home/admin/*.csv or non-standard paths. Correlate with netadmin user sessions. Flag executions with special characters or unusual argument patterns.

suggestion.title: Root Privilege Escalation via vconfd Command Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'execute arbitrary commands as root' and 'elevate their privileges as the root user' via 'command injection attacks', a direct privilege escalation from netadmin context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track root-context process spawning triggered by vconfd_script_upload_tenant_list.sh or related vconfd binaries. Flag embedded shell metacharacters (backticks, $(), |, &&) in file arguments or paths. Monitor for privilege escalation audit events from netadmin UID to UID 0.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Configuration Push to vSmart Controllers
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'configuration change pushed to edge devices' and 'uploading tenant configuration data to vSmart controllers to escalate privileges through legitimate commands' as the impact of successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline vSmart controller configuration push patterns by source account and time-of-day. Alert on config pushes from vManage outside maintenance windows, especially from netadmin-context accounts. Correlate with suspicious script execution timing on vManage.

suggestion.title: Chained Exploitation CVE-2026-20182 Enabling CVE-2026-20245
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'exploit this vulnerability, the attacker must have netadmin privileges' achievable via 'exploitation of CVE-2026-20182 or CVE-2026-20127', indicating attacker chain-escalates through prior auth-bypass CVEs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baselines for CVE-2026-20182 and CVE-2026-20127 exploitation indicators. Flag sequences: authentication anomalies → unexpected netadmin login success → file upload + vconfd script execution within short timeframe.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Creation in /home/admin Path
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploit via 'uploading a crafted file' with specific evidence of writes to /home/admin/ (example: malicious.csv). File creation in admin home by non-admin processes is anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any file write to /home/admin/* not originating from legitimate admin processes. Flag CSV, script, and configuration files. Correlate with HTTP POST/PUT requests to vManage file-upload endpoints during netadmin sessions.

suggestion.title: Anomalous vManage-vSmart Management Plane Communication
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation results in 'uploading tenant configuration data to vSmart controllers', indicating attacker-directed mgmt-plane communication. Abnormal inter-controller sync patterns indicate compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal vManage↔vSmart communication (volume, frequency, timing, payload size). Alert on large or frequent config syncs outside change windows, especially from netadmin-context accounts. Flag asymmetric traffic inconsistent with normal push patterns.

suggestion.title: FIFA-themed Phishing Infrastructure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Fake Sites' as live threat vector for World Cup 2026 scams. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs despite title clearly indicating domain-based initial access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect recently-registered or suspicious domains mimicking FIFA/World Cup infrastructure (fifa2026-, worldcup-, tournament-, ticketing-, registration- patterns). Flag domains with typosquatting, lookalike TLDs, or bulk WHOIS registrations. Correlate with phishing email campaigns and web proxy access logs.

suggestion.title: Banking Malware Distribution via Event-themed Lures
suggestion.rationale: Title cites 'Banking Malware' as active threat; pipeline extracted zero malware indicators. Should detect delivery and execution patterns specific to financial trojans leveraging World Cup interest.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for malware execution following World Cup-themed document/link clicks. Look for process trees spawned by Office macros or script interpreters (cmd, powershell, cscript) triggered by FIFA/tournament-themed files. Flag banking Trojans (Ursnif, Emotet variants if active, Zeus, etc.) by behavioral indicators: API hooks, credential stealing, network beaconing to C2.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting and Stolen Login Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title lists 'Stolen Logins' as attack output; no detection logic provided. Pipeline should surface credential dumping techniques and login spray attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous signin patterns post-phishing: bulk failed logins from new IPs, successful logins from impossible travel distances, or credential reuse across services. Flag password spray campaigns targeting FIFA-related account directories. Correlate with known credential dump sales and dark-web forum mentions.

suggestion.title: Evasion-Based Banking Malware Analysis
suggestion.rationale: Banking malware often employs anti-analysis; title indicates active live malware, but no evasion or sandbox-bypass techniques were mapped.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect obfuscation and sandbox evasion markers in banking malware samples: process hollowing, API hooking, virtual machine detection checks, debugger checks, and encrypted C2 communications. Flag samples that evade common sandboxes (Cuckoo, Any.run signatures).

suggestion.title: Macro-enabled Document Delivery for World Cup Scams
suggestion.rationale: Article context implies malware distribution; common vector is Office macros in World Cup-themed documents. Pipeline missed document-based execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Office documents (Word, Excel) with enabled macros, especially World Cup-related filenames or from external/suspicious sources. Detect spawning of shell processes (powershell, cmd, cscript) from Office parent processes, followed by network connections or file system modifications.

suggestion.title: World Cup Scam Campaign Attribution and Clustering
suggestion.rationale: Article references campaign-level threat ('FIFA World Cup 2026 Scams ARE live'—plural). Pipeline should cluster IOCs, identify threat actor or campaign ID for correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Group phishing domains, malware samples, and C2 infrastructure by shared registration details, SSL certificates, or network ASNs. Correlate with known threat-actor TTP databases (OSINT feeds, dark-web chatter) to attribute campaign to named actor or criminal group. Track campaign evolution over time.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated DbGate JWT issuance via /auth/login
suggestion.rationale: Article states: "'none' auth provider issues JWT tokens without credentials via `POST /auth/login`" — this is the authentication bypass enabling the entire attack chain. Pipeline missed the credential_access / initial_access boundary.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track POST requests to /auth/login endpoints returning JWT tokens (Authorization header or response body) without prior credential validation. Baseline: legitimate DbGate should require username/password or API key; unexpected success logins from external IPs indicate auth bypass exploitation.

suggestion.title: Node process spawning shells post-ZIP extraction
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RCE outcome. If zip slip writes to cron.d/systemd/init.d, execution follows. Pipeline missed T1059.001 execution indicator: Node spawning bash/sh.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parent process = node with command line containing 'dbgate' or '/api'; child process = bash/sh/dash. Anomalous if spawn timestamp correlates with prior archive extraction. Filter out npm/build-time shell spawns.

suggestion.title: SSH authorized_keys or sudoers file modification by non-root
suggestion.rationale: Article targets: "/root/.ssh/*" and "/etc/sudoers.d/*" — persistence/privilege-escalation writes. Pipeline missed T1098.004 (Account Manipulation) and T1548.004 (Sudoers abuse).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Modifications to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, ~/.ssh/config, or /etc/sudoers.d/* initiated by node process or unprivileged UID attempting privilege escalation. Success indicator: new line added to authorized_keys or sudoers with malicious COMMAND or key.

suggestion.title: Cron job creation in /etc/cron.d/ post-extraction (T1053.003)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly targets "/etc/cron.d/*", "/etc/cron.daily/*", "/etc/cron.weekly/*" — standard persistence. T1053.003 was listed but no detection generated. Should correlate with prior archive/unzip.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: New cron job file created in /etc/cron.d/ or /var/spool/cron/ with suspicious content (reverse shell patterns, base64, wget/curl exfil commands). Correlation: file creation timestamp within 60s of POST to /api/archive/unzip.

suggestion.title: ZIP archive with path-traversal sequences uploaded to DbGate
suggestion.rationale: Article vulnerability root: malicious ZIP with '../' entries. Detection at upload point prevents exploitation. Pipeline missed the initial_access indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: ZIP files containing directory-traversal sequences ('../', '..\\') in entry names detected in uploads to /api/archive/upload or /api/uploads/upload endpoints. Baseline: legitimate DbGate archives should not traverse parent directories.

suggestion.title: Web shell written to /etc/systemd/system/ or /etc/init.d/ (T1505.003)
suggestion.rationale: Article targets service/init directories (T1505.003 — Server Software Component: Web Shell was listed but not detected). Zip slip writes executable to init system.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Executable or script file (*.sh, *.service unit file) created in /etc/systemd/system/, /etc/init.d/, or /etc/rc.d/ by node process or from /tmp extraction directory. Correlate with ZIP extraction and socket/network activity from that systemd unit.

suggestion.title: HTTP POST to AIT-BSC /start endpoint with traversal payload
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes unauthenticated POST requests to dynamic packet-capture handlers with path-traversal form fields ('blind trust of path-related form fields'). This is the core exploitation vector and needs direct detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST requests to URI paths matching /*/start (case-insensitive) where query parameters or POST body contains traversal sequences (../, %2e%2e, %252e, =/etc/, =/home/, =/root/, =/var/, =/tmp/) combined with parameter names suggesting path control (log_dir_path, file_name_pattern, capture_path). Correlate unauthenticated access (no auth token in request header).

suggestion.title: Filesystem write to /var/opt/ait-bsc/logs with non-baseline filenames via path traversal
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'arbitrary file append' and 'bypass configured log root'—this is the impact phase. UC_21_1 names specific write targets (/var/opt/ait-bsc/logs and /home/elias/ait-venv/...) but does so with placeholder paths. Need to detect actual file-write patterns consistent with traversal exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation or modification in /var/opt/ait-bsc/logs (or parent directories accessed via AIT-BSC process) where filename contains or is prefixed by path components (../, %2e%2e URL-decoded equivalents). Correlate with HTTP POST to /*/start endpoint on the same host within 1-5 seconds. Flag if file extension suggests code (*.py, *.sh, *.cfg) or sensitive paths (*/etc/*, */root/*, */home/*/....*) are written.

suggestion.title: Python code execution from AIT-BSC-written file location
suggestion.rationale: Article names UC_21_1 which explicitly targets /home/elias/ait-venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/ait/core/ (Python package directory). If traversal allows write to site-packages, arbitrary code can execute on import. This is T1059.001 which article omits.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Python process (python, python3, ait-bsc process spawning python) that loads modules from /home/elias/ait-venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/ait/core/ (or similar site-packages variant) where those .py files were recently created/modified (within 10 minutes) and file creation origin correlates with HTTP POST to ait-bsc /start endpoint on same host.

suggestion.title: AIT-BSC process outbound C2 after exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes potential for 'dynamic creating packet capture handlers' and appending arbitrary files—if attacker writes Python C2 agent to site-packages, ait-bsc or Python child process initiates outbound connection. UC_21_3 exists but targets only public IPs; need variant for both public AND baseline-abnormal destinations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound TCP/UDP connections initiated by ait-bsc process (or child Python process spawned by ait-bsc) to non-RFC1918, non-loopback, non-link-local IPs on ports not in baseline for the host. Prioritize destination ports >10000 or non-standard (not 80, 443, 53, 25). Correlate with HTTP POST to /*/start within prior 30 minutes.

suggestion.title: Proof-of-concept or attacker tooling (python_poc.py, attacker_tcp.py) execution
suggestion.rationale: UC_21_1 in article explicitly names IOC process filenames: python_poc.py, attacker_tcp.py, dmc.py. These are mentioned as indicators of active exploitation. However, these appear to be generic PoC/pentesting names that will generate FP on legitimate pentesting. Include but with low confidence and require correlation with other signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution of python_poc.py, attacker_tcp.py, or dmc.py with HIGH false-positive rate—these are generic names used in penetration testing. Require correlation with: (a) HTTP POST to ait-bsc /start endpoint on same host, OR (b) process parent = ait-bsc or Python, OR (c) process spawning child process that makes outbound connection to non-baseline IP. Do not alert on isolated execution.

suggestion.title: Role creation by non-admin authenticated users
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Any authenticated user could...create new roles.' The Settings/Team/Index authorization bypass is the core attack vector; no detection exists for role-creation mutations by low-privilege accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST/PUT to role-creation endpoints (e.g., /settings/team/roles, /livewire/message/settings.team with role payloads). Baseline: only users with 'admin' or 'create_role' permission should succeed. Alert when users lacking these permissions attempt role creation, especially if HTTP 200/201 is returned (indicating success).

suggestion.title: User deletion by unauthorized accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Any authenticated user could...delete other users, including administrators.' This is explicit privilege escalation (deleting admins to remove barriers); absence from detection suite is critical gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DELETE or POST requests to user-removal endpoints from non-admin users. Cross-check user's RBAC entry at time of request: baseline is admin role only. Flag all deletions of admin-role users, regardless of requester role. Alert immediately on successful deletion (HTTP 200) by non-admin.

suggestion.title: RolePermission write operations with insufficient privilege
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Settings/Team/RolePermission gated its write actions on the read-only view_users perm...' indicating permission misconfiguration. Detect when write-operations succeed despite inadequate authorization tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PUT/PATCH to role-permission endpoints. Before the request, verify user's permission set includes 'write_permissions' or 'manage_permissions'. Flag write-attempts from users with only 'read_users', 'view_users', or other read-only permissions. Alert especially if the mutation grants the requester's own role elevated permissions.

suggestion.title: Rapid succession RBAC mutations within single session
suggestion.rationale: Attack describes two distinct authorization defects exploitable in rapid succession. Detect behavioral pattern: single authenticated user making multiple role/permission mutations (create, delete, modify) within short window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For each authenticated session, track all RBAC mutation requests (role creation, user deletion, permission write). Alert if session includes ≥2 distinct mutation types within 5-minute window, or ≥3 total mutations regardless of type. Baseline: legitimate admins should have lower mutation velocity; this pattern suggests escalation or takeover.

suggestion.title: Authentication followed by unauthorized team-settings access
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires valid account; baseline is that only some authenticated users should access team-settings at all. Detect auth event followed immediately by team-settings endpoint access by accounts not previously seen in that context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For each successful authentication event, check if the user subsequently accesses team-settings endpoints within 10 seconds. Baseline: extract list of users who have historically accessed team-settings (limit to <10% of user base). Alert on auth-to-team-settings sequence for users not in this baseline. High confidence if user immediately attempts role/permission mutations post-auth.

suggestion.title: Everest Forms Pro Exploitation via POST to Plugin Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'hackers exploit critical...flaw' with outcome 'take over sites'—this implies unauthenticated or pre-auth RCE or authentication bypass. Must detect POST/GET to /everest-forms/* endpoints with suspicious payloads or unusual response codes (200 on previously-404 paths).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP access logs for POST requests to /wp-content/plugins/everest-forms/* or /wp-json/everest* endpoints with payloads containing function calls, shell metacharacters, or base64-encoded PHP. Flag 403→200 transitions on plugin endpoints or successful requests followed by file write operations in /wp-content/uploads or /wp-content/plugins.

suggestion.title: Suspicious WordPress Admin Account Creation Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'take over sites'—attackers establishing persistence typically create admin accounts or backdoor users. The full article likely describes post-exploitation persistence patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress user table write operations (wp_users inserts) and wp-admin/user-new.php requests for non-admin source IPs or requests originating from the compromised plugin execution context. Correlate with suspicious wp_usermeta records indicating privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: Everest Forms Plugin Update or Configuration Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Attackers often disable auto-updates or modify plugin configs post-exploitation to prevent patch application. Article implies patching/update is the mitigation path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor wp-admin/options.php modifications, plugin.php update setting changes, and FTP/SFTP write operations to /everest-forms/* directories after exploitation detection. Flag modifications to auto_update_plugins or disable_plugin_* settings within minutes of exploitation.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Detection in Uploads Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Plugin RCE typically leads to web shell placement for persistence. 'Take over sites' implies attackers retain access—web shells are the standard mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /wp-content/uploads/ for newly-created .php, .phtml, .phar files with executable permissions, especially if filenames contain obfuscation patterns (hex, base64-like strings, or single letters). Correlate file creation with preceding HTTP 200 responses to the vulnerable plugin endpoint.

suggestion.title: Unexpected PHP Execution in WordPress Plugin Directory
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation path involves plugin directory code execution. Direct process execution (not HTTP-triggered) via wp-cron, system calls, or eval suggests successful code injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor spawning of child processes (php.exe, /usr/bin/php) from the web server process with working directories set to /wp-content/plugins/everest-forms or parent. Watch for system() / exec() calls within plugin context reading/writing to sensitive files (wp-config.php, .htaccess, wp_users table).

suggestion.title: Database Credential Exfiltration via Plugin RCE
suggestion.rationale: Site takeover requires database access. RCE via the plugin likely reads wp-config.php or directly accesses database credentials for persistence or data theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor MySQL/MariaDB authentication failures from localhost using credentials that differ from the primary application pool credentials. Correlate with wp-config.php file read operations triggered by PHP interpreter child processes originating from the web server. Flag unusual database client connections (direct mysql CLI, direct JDBC) post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted Python Package Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes package 'parsimonius' crafted to mimic 'parsimonious' — typosquatting is the entire attack mechanism, yet no detection maps to catching single-letter package name substitutions or package confusion attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Python package manager operations for installations matching known-legitimate library names with single-character substitutions or homoglyph variants. Flag 'parsimonius' installs when 'parsimonious' is organizational baseline; correlate with mismatched author metadata or suspicious publish timestamps.

suggestion.title: Malicious Python Package Code Execution
suggestion.rationale: Compromised package imported by developers; malware executes at import time or installation. Article confirms supply-chain delivery but payload details not visible in truncated body; Python code execution is implicit in this attack class.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Python interpreter spawning anomalous child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, curl, wget, nc) shortly after importing or installing flagged package names. Alert on execution context mismatch: python.exe spawning system tools from user/temp directories.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise via Package Repository Injection
suggestion.rationale: Malicious package injected directly into PyPI public repository. Organizations require supply-chain monitoring beyond post-compromise hashing: detection of confusingly-named packages, publisher account anomalies, rapid version iteration patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest PyPI package metadata feeds; flag packages with names containing common typos against established organizational dependencies. Alert on author account anomalies (new publishers, name changes) or suspicious version churn. Cross-reference installed/pinned versions against threat-intel package blocklists.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation with Postinstall Execution
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks targeting npm typically inject code in postinstall scripts. Article title explicitly names npm as attack vector with 'Worm Variant' behavior indicating self-propagating code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm/node processes spawning child processes with suspicious command lines (especially powershell, cmd, bash, curl, wget). Correlate with recent npm install/update activity and postinstall script execution timing. Alert on unsigned or obfuscated child processes from node_modules directories.

suggestion.title: Worm-like Package Dependency Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Worm Variant' which implies self-propagating characteristics. Supply chain worms typically modify dependent packages to spread transitively across the dependency tree.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect recursive package.json modifications or unexpected version pinning changes in node_modules. Look for npm registry write operations from compromised package namespaces. Flag packages with abnormally high dependency fan-out or circular dependency injection.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Distribution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Hit npm'—the attack surface is package distribution. Pipeline should have extracted affected package names, versions, and registry metadata.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference npm package download metadata against threat intel feeds for IronWorm and Miasma variants. Block installations of flagged package names/versions. Monitor for package registry API calls (registry.npmjs.org) requesting suspicious or recently-created packages with typosquatting patterns.

suggestion.title: Process Spawning from node_modules with Network Egress
suggestion.rationale: Worm activity requires command-and-control or lateral movement; articles on npm worms typically describe C2 callbacks or data exfiltration after code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected outbound network connections (HTTP/HTTPS/DNS) originating from node_modules-hosted code or npm processes. Flag domains not in allowlist for legitimate npm CDNs. Correlate connection timing with postinstall script execution.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Child Process Launch from npm Global Packages
suggestion.rationale: npm global package execution (npm install -g) runs in privileged context and can persist across projects. Supply chain worms exploit this for lateral code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation from ~/.npm or npm global package directories with high privilege levels or unusual parent processes (system, svchost). Detect unexpected persistence mechanisms (scheduled tasks, startup folders, registry modifications) linked to npm package names.

suggestion.title: Stripe API Abuse for Command & Control
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states the attack 'uses Stripe, the widely used online payment service, as both its command center and its data dump.' Pipeline generated no C2 detection for this abuse pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Stripe API calls from non-payment systems or unusual source IPs. Monitor for anomalous request patterns to Stripe endpoints: unexpected cadence, non-transactional data retrieval, or API activity from customer-facing servers. Alert on Stripe API key exfiltration or use outside normal payment contexts.

suggestion.title: Credit Card Data Exfiltration via Payment Gateway
suggestion.rationale: Core attack objective: 'stolen card data' exfiltrated through Stripe infrastructure. No detection for PAN/card data being staged or transmitted outside normal transaction flows via payment APIs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate local access to payment forms or keylogged card data with outbound Stripe API calls. Detect bulk or batch card-data transmission patterns inconsistent with legitimate transaction processing. Alert on card data appearing in Stripe API payloads outside normal e-commerce workflows.

suggestion.title: Malicious JavaScript Injection into Payment Checkout Pages
suggestion.rationale: Magecart attacks fundamentally rely on JavaScript injection into payment pages. Article: 'malware hiding inside one of the most trusted payment platforms.' No detection for the injection delivery vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned or unexpected JavaScript loaded into payment checkout contexts from non-standard sources. Monitor for dynamic code execution (eval, Function()) or script injection during payment flows. Flag script tags referencing Firebase domains in checkout pages.

suggestion.title: Firebase Instance Abuse as Malware C2 & Data Sink
suggestion.rationale: IOC `braintree-payment-app.firebaseio.com` indicates repurposed Firebase as attacker infrastructure for C2 and exfiltration. No detection for this abuse pattern despite explicit mention.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for connections to non-whitelisted Firebase instances (*.firebaseio.com) from production systems. Alert on sustained connections, unusual data volumes, or Firebase access from servers not requiring it. Correlate with process execution or malware indicators.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Compromise in Payment Processing SDKs
suggestion.rationale: Magecart is fundamentally a supply-chain attack. Article: 'hiding inside one of the most trusted payment platforms.' No detection for unauthorized payment library modifications or unexpected integrations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor payment SDKs and vendor integrations for unauthorized modifications, additions, or changes outside change-management workflows. Alert when payment libraries are loaded from unusual paths or with unexpected file hashes. Detect new payment-provider integrations added post-deployment.

suggestion.title: IIS Web Shell File Creation in Web Root
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifies 'custom web shell framework' deployed to IIS; no UC exists to detect .aspx/.asp file writes to sensitive IIS directories (wwwroot, bin, App_Code). Missing core persistence detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation or modification of .aspx, .asp, or .ashx files in IIS web directories (C:\inetpub\, C:\Program Files\IIS). Flag rapid multi-file creation. Correlate with recent IIS access logs containing suspicious HTTP patterns.

suggestion.title: IIS Worker Process Spawning Command Interpreter
suggestion.rationale: Custom web shell execution requires child process launch. Article describes IIS-targeting attack but no UC for w3wp.exe or ApplicationPoolIdentity spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or csc.exe—critical execution detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect w3wp.exe, iisexpress.exe spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or csc.exe with low or no parent command line. Alert on ApplicationPoolIdentity or DefaultAppPool executing interactive shells outside scheduled tasks.

suggestion.title: IIS Log Injection / Encoded Web Shell Request Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article implies custom framework with unknown signature. No UC for IIS HTTP request pattern detection (e.g., base64-encoded payloads, suspicious query strings, or shell command keywords in logs).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search IIS logs for requests to uncommon .aspx paths, base64/URL-encoded User-Agent or Referer headers, or querystring parameters containing shell keywords (cmd=, exec=, shell=). Look for 200/201 responses followed by unusual request patterns.

suggestion.title: Exploit Detection: IIS Public-Facing Application Attack
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'targets Microsoft IIS servers'—suggests exploitation of known or zero-day IIS vulnerability. No UC for malformed HTTP requests, path traversal attempts, or remote code execution probes against IIS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on IIS logs containing HTTP 400/500 errors preceded by malformed requests, null-byte injection, Unicode encoding, or attempts to access restricted paths (e.g., /web.config, /.aspx in unusual locations). Correlate with subsequent file writes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious IIS Log Clearing / Truncation
suggestion.rationale: Custom APT cluster would cover tracks. Article describes sophisticated framework but no UC for IIS log file deletion or event log tampering post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect truncation of inetpub\logs\LogFiles or deletion of IIS ETL files. Alert on processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, certutil.exe) with file handles to IIS log directories. Monitor Windows Event Log for abnormal deletion patterns within seconds after suspicious process execution.

suggestion.title: Detect Suspicious SMTP Relay Configuration on Cloud Instances
suggestion.rationale: Core attack claim: 'Covert SMTP Relay Network' across 230 compromised servers. Pipeline generated zero detection logic for outbound relay abuse despite being the stated operational objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on high-volume outbound SMTP connections (port 25, 465, 587) from cloud instances to external IP ranges, especially with >100 SMTP transactions/hour to distinct recipients. Correlate with process creation for mail daemons (postfix, sendmail, exim) on non-mail-appliance hosts. Monitor for persistent relay activity over days.

suggestion.title: Detect Cloud Instance Compromise via Initial Access Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Hijacks [servers]' across major cloud providers, implying successful exploitation or credential abuse. Pipeline generated zero initial-access detection despite 'hijack' indicating prior compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for RDP/SSH login anomalies (failed brute-force attempts, unusual geographies) followed by service installation within 5 minutes. Alert on public-facing cloud instance exploitation patterns: web shell uploads, application error logs, or privilege escalation API calls post-access.

suggestion.title: Detect Persistence Mechanisms Post-Cloud Compromise
suggestion.rationale: 'Covert [sustained] SMTP Relay Network' implies persistent backdoor/scheduled execution, but pipeline generated zero persistence-phase detections (cron jobs, systemd services, scheduled tasks).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cron job creation or systemd timer installation launching mail relay daemons post-compromise. Alert on new user account creation with sudo privileges. Track modifications to cloud IAM roles or service account credentials enabling persistence.

suggestion.title: Detect Malware Staging: PCPJack Download and Execution Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Threat actor/malware 'PCPJack' named in title but zero process execution or malware-specific IOCs extracted by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for process chains: curl/wget → chmod +x → bash/sh execution on cloud VMs. Monitor for downloads of shell scripts followed immediately by execution. Alert on suspicious interpreter invocations (python, perl, bash) with network connections.

suggestion.title: Detect Cloud IAM or Credential Compromise Enabling Multi-Provider Access
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies synchronized compromise across AWS, GCP, Azure—suggests shared credential abuse or coordinated campaign vector. Pipeline generated zero cross-cloud correlation logic or credential-compromise detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed/successful API authentications across AWS, GCP, Azure within 1-hour windows from identical source IPs or user agents. Alert on enumeration patterns (DescribeInstances, list-vms, Get-AzureVM) followed by lateral movement. Monitor for stolen API keys or service account credentials used across cloud platforms.

suggestion.title: Detect Abuse of Cloud Infrastructure for Spam/Phishing Distribution
suggestion.rationale: 'SMTP Relay Network' explicitly for covert email abuse (phishing/spam). Zero impact-phase detection for email reputation abuse or outbound spam patterns from cloud sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cloud instance IPs appearing on spam blacklists (Spamhaus, Barracuda) in real-time. Alert on cloud VMs generating >50 external email recipients/hour with identical or near-identical message bodies (bulk phishing indicator). Cross-reference cloud source IPs against mail server reputation databases hourly.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Secret Exposure via Agent Environment Variable Access
suggestion.rationale: Article premise 'securing CI/CD in agentic world' establishes that AI agents in GitHub Actions have access to secrets and environment variables. No detection logic exists for unauthorized enumeration or exfiltration of $GITHUB_TOKEN or other secrets by runner processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions runner processes for enumeration commands (env, printenv, set, Get-ChildItem env:) or direct access to GitHub secret environment variables. Flag runs with outbound connections to non-GitHub/non-standard CI infrastructure immediately after secret access.

suggestion.title: Malicious Code Generation and Commit by Agentic Automation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Claude Code Github action'—indicates direct agent-to-repository code generation. No use case detects for AI-generated code containing command injection, encoded payloads, or credential-exfiltration logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect commits authored by GitHub Actions service account with suspicious content: command-injection syntax (backticks, $(...) subshells in shell contexts), base64/hex-encoded strings, credentials in logs/artifacts, or outbound connections to attacker infrastructure from post-execution hooks.

suggestion.title: Workflow YAML Injection to Extract Organization Secrets
suggestion.rationale: Agentic systems modifying .github/workflows files can add malicious steps. No detection for workflow manifest tampering that exfiltrates secrets to pull-request comments, external webhooks, or attacker-controlled artifact storage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor .github/workflows/*.yml modifications for addition of steps that export secrets via outputs, curl secrets to external URLs, or create runners with elevated permissions. Correlate with new external repository collaborators or untrusted runner IP ranges.

suggestion.title: HTTP 401 Authentication Challenges from External CDN Domains
suggestion.rationale: polyfill[.]io domain 'became active again and started responding with HTTP 401 authentication requests'—the core attack mechanism triggering unexpected browser login prompts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor proxy and network logs for HTTP 401 status codes from external third-party domains where authentication should not be required. Correlate with known compromised CDN infrastructure. Alert on sudden 401 response spikes from single external domain to multiple internal clients within short time window.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Native Browser Auth Prompts on Legitimate Sites
suggestion.rationale: User browsers visiting Toshiba and Muji 'interpret that as a request for a username and password, so they serve a login prompt'—native browser UI driven by malicious HTTP 401.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In session context, correlate successful HTTP 200/302 to known legitimate e-commerce/retail domains (Toshiba, Muji, Samsung) followed within seconds by HTTP 401 from external third-party domain in same client session. Flag as anomalous authentication pattern; likely supply-chain trojan.

suggestion.title: Reactivated Dormant Malicious Domain—Post-Compromise Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: polyfill[.]io was compromised in 2024, 'lay dormant', then 'starting in late May 2026, the polyfill[.]io domain became active again'—indicator of malicious actor regaining control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference DNS queries and network flows against threat intel feeds tracking known-compromised supply-chain infrastructure. Flag any client attempting to contact polyfill[.]io or previously dormant malicious domains post-reactivation. Pivot on historical whois/DNS changes to correlate ownership transfer events.

suggestion.title: Upcleaned Legacy Third-Party Script Inclusions from Malicious CDN
suggestion.rationale: 'Some sites using the service failed to clean all their pages over the past two years, so remnants of Polyfill code remained'—detection must identify persistent vulnerable script references.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan web application source code and proxied requests for script src= or link href= patterns pointing to polyfill[.]io, polyfill.io, or similar CDN variants. Generate inventory of applications with stale malicious dependencies still embedded. Priority: identify sites where javascript remains unpatched despite 2+ years of known compromise.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise via Expired Domain Hostile Repurchase
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'when the domain expired, it could be claimed by anyone' followed by purchase 'by a Chinese entity' that 'added malicious scripts that impacted more than 100,000 websites'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for domain expirations and re-registrations in critical supply-chain infrastructure (CDNs, JavaScript libraries, package managers). Alert on repurchase by previously unseen registrants or entities in high-risk jurisdictions. Cross-reference repurchased domains against historical compromise records and passive DNS data to identify dormant malware hosting.

suggestion.title: Coordinated Multi-Vendor Web Property Compromise via Shared Malicious Dependency
suggestion.rationale: Seven distinct organizations identified (Toshiba, Muji, Zojirushi, FiNC, Ishiyaku, Hobonichi, Samsung) all compromised through shared polyfill[.]io dependency—indicates ecosystem-wide supply-chain blast radius.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate known-compromised organization domains and pivot on shared third-party dependencies. Build dependency graph of internal vs. external web properties using same malicious library versions or CDN. Expand from 7 public victims to full exposure inventory; prioritize organizations in e-commerce, retail, manufacturing verticals where credentials have high value.

suggestion.title: Cgroups v1 Release-Agent Privilege Escalation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states the flaw 'may allow attackers' to exploit cgroups v1 release_agent feature; pipeline missed detection of writes to cgroup.release_agent or manipulation of handler scripts that signal privilege-escalation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious writes to `/proc/*/cgroup*` paths or `/sys/fs/cgroup*`, particularly modifications to release_agent handlers. Flag processes writing to cgroup.release_agent with shell metacharacters or executable paths. Correlate with subsequent process execution at elevated privilege scope.

suggestion.title: Elevated-Privilege Code Execution Post-Cgroups Escape
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the vulnerability allows exploitation for code execution; pipeline omitted detection for sudden privilege escalation or unexpected high-integrity process spawning as second stage of the attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process spawning with privilege-level jump (unprivileged parent → root/system child) originating from cgroups manipulation context. Flag /bin/sh, /bin/bash, or other shell execution from cgroup-related contexts without standard escalation paths (sudo, doas, etc.).

suggestion.title: Kernel cgroups Feature Abuse — Anomalous Handler Invocation
suggestion.rationale: Article notes the release_agent feature is exploited; pipeline did not flag detection for unexpected invocation or registration of system handlers tied to cgroup events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for writes to `/sys/fs/cgroup/*/release_agent` or registration of cgroup event_control handlers without administrative context. Alert on shell or binary paths written to release_agent that are not in expected system directories.

suggestion.title: Detect FFmpeg Process Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article announces '21 Zero-Days in FFmpeg' but pipeline extracted zero detection use cases. Should detect memory-corruption exploits targeting FFmpeg transcoding/media processing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal child processes spawned from ffmpeg.exe or libavcodec, unusual memory allocations in media codec threads, or ffmpeg crashes followed by process injection. Baseline: ffmpeg should only spawn expected filter chains or encoder subprocesses.

suggestion.title: Chrome Renderer Process RCE via Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'Chrome Patches Record 429 Bugs'; 429 CVEs suggest widespread attack surface. Pipeline should detect privilege escalation from Chrome renderer sandbox to system.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on chrome.exe or chromium spawning elevated system processes (SYSTEM, NT AUTHORITY) without user interaction, or on unexpected DLL injection into Chrome sandbox processes. Expected behavior: Chrome runs as user; any privilege boundary crossing is anomalous.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Software Inventory Deviation
suggestion.rationale: 21 FFmpeg + 429 Chrome vulns = massive affected surface. Article should trigger baseline asset updates. Pipeline missed IOC enrichment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any ffmpeg version <latest-post-June-2026 or Chrome version <latest-post-June-2026 in asset inventory. Correlate with internet-facing systems (web servers, media servers). Absence of patching 30+ days post-disclosure is high-risk.

suggestion.title: Exploit Kit Payload Delivery for Codec Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article title suggests AI agent discovered vulns; implies sophisticated attack chains. Pipeline should detect delivery mechanisms (watering-hole, ad networks, drive-by downloads) that weaponize codec exploits.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect delivery of crafted media files (.mp4, .mkv, .webm, .aac) from untrusted sources followed within seconds by ffmpeg or Chrome process crash or abnormal memory activity. Baseline: media files should come from known CDNs or internal repositories only.

suggestion.title: SolarWinds Serv-U Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'actively exploited' SolarWinds Serv-U flaw with no detection logic generated. Serv-U is a file transfer service exposed on predictable ports; exploitation attempts should be detectable via malformed protocol requests or known payload signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound connections to Serv-U ports (22, 23, 990, 992, 8080) for exploit-pattern payloads or protocol violations. Track failed authentication bursts followed by successful access. Alert on Serv-U process execution with suspicious command-line arguments indicating payload delivery.

suggestion.title: Serv-U Process Crash and Restart Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: DoS vulnerability typically manifests as service instability or crash. Article describes 'DoS flaw' but pipeline did not generate detection for availability impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected Serv-U process termination followed by rapid restart within 5-minute windows. Track unusual system resource consumption (CPU/memory spikes) preceding crash events. Correlate with inbound traffic anomalies to the same endpoint.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Traffic Volume to Serv-U Default Ports
suggestion.rationale: DoS attacks generate identifiable traffic patterns; article emphasizes 'actively exploited' but no network-based DoS detection use case provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline traffic volume to Serv-U ports per source. Alert when single source exceeds 2x baseline in 5-minute window, or aggregate traffic from multiple sources to Serv-U port exceeds 10x baseline. Flag incomplete/truncated protocol handshakes.

suggestion.title: Serv-U Service Availability Monitoring via Event Logs
suggestion.rationale: Impact-phase DoS attacks should trigger service monitoring alerts; pipeline did not map to availability-monitoring use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Windows Event Log (ID 7000–7009, 7031–7034) and syslog for service start/stop/failure events on Serv-U. Alert on unplanned service shutdown or repeated restart cycles. Correlate with authentication failures (Event ID 4625) or network errors.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Serv-U Credential Access
suggestion.rationale: Serv-U is used for file transfer and remote access; exploits may enable credential theft or session hijacking. Article does not detail attack chain beyond DoS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for successful Serv-U authentication followed by rapid file enumeration or system file access (e.g., SAM, NTDS). Alert on Serv-U spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or copying sensitive files. Track lateral movement from Serv-U host to other internal systems.

suggestion.title: CISA KEV Catalog Vulnerability Tracking Integration
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'CISA adds to KEV Catalog'—pipeline should ingest CISA KEV as an IOC/vulnerability feed but did not surface this source.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference CISA KEV feed daily. Identify all Serv-U instances in internal asset inventory. Flag any Serv-U instances running vulnerable versions and prioritize for patching. Monitor for scanning/enumeration activity targeting these known-vulnerable assets.

suggestion.title: Cisco SD-WAN Manager CVE-2026-20245 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly states 'CVE-2026-20245 Flaw Actively Exploited' — pipeline failed to surface the primary attack vector (vulnerability exploitation itself) despite this being the core attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound requests to Cisco SD-WAN Manager (vManage) administration interfaces for malformed HTTP requests, oversized payloads, unusual parameter encoding, and exploitation signatures matching CVE-2026-20245 exploitation tools. Alert on POST requests to API endpoints combined with HTTP 200/500 error patterns consistent with successful exploitation.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution from SD-WAN Manager Service Context
suggestion.rationale: CVE in network control plane appliance with active exploitation ('actively exploited') logically progresses to remote code execution. Pipeline did not surface execution-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor child processes spawned by SD-WAN Manager service accounts (vmanage, system, root). Flag unexpected shell spawning (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/bash), script interpreter invocation, or network utilities (curl, wget) executed from management service context.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised SD-WAN Manager
suggestion.rationale: SD-WAN Manager sits on the network control plane with privileged access to routing and policy infrastructure. Article signals 'no patch available,' indicating dwell time for lateral movement. Pipeline missed this high-value pivot point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on network connections originating from SD-WAN Manager infrastructure to unexpected internal destinations (domain controllers, asset management systems, data repositories). Monitor for reconnaissance patterns (DNS lookups for sensitive hosts, port scanning behavior) and lateral movement protocols (RDP, WinRM, SSH) from the compromised appliance.

suggestion.title: Persistent Backdoor Installation in SD-WAN Manager Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Zero-day with no patch ('no patch available') implies attackers can maintain dwell time. Compromise of network control plane would be leveraged for persistence. Pipeline did not generate persistence detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SD-WAN Manager audit logs and configuration change tracking for unauthorized account creation, new administrative credentials, addition of startup scripts/scheduled tasks, or modification of device templates. Flag changes that persist across reboots or create hidden management interfaces.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Exploitation of SD-WAN Manager Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-20245 exploitation could bypass authentication (leading to unauthorized admin access) or escalate unprivileged context to system level. Pipeline did not surface privilege-escalation detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for successful authentication to SD-WAN Manager following exploitation attempts. Flag creation of new administrative accounts, elevation of existing accounts to privileged groups, or assumption of roles with system-level permissions outside normal maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via SD-WAN Manager Network Access
suggestion.rationale: SD-WAN Manager has privileged vantage on enterprise network traffic and routing control. Compromised instance can stage and exfiltrate sensitive data. Despite zero-day nature suggesting ongoing attacks, pipeline did not anticipate exfiltration-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline outbound traffic from SD-WAN Manager. Alert on large data transfers to non-approved external IP addresses, unknown C2 domains, or encrypted tunnels (SSH, HTTPS tunnel) to suspicious destinations. Correlate timing with exploitation attempt windows to identify data staging and exfiltration activity.

suggestion.title: Everest Forms Pro Complex Calculation PHP Injection Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attacker submits a value for a text field that begins with a single quote to close the wrapping string literal, followed by a PHP statement' — injection signature (quote + PHP function + comment marker) must be detected at form submission or WAF layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on POST/GET requests to Everest Forms Pro plugin form endpoints containing payloads with quote-escaping patterns (single quote followed by PHP functions like wp_insert_user, wp_create_user, or other executable functions with trailing comment markers //). Monitor form data fields for PHP syntax elements.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Administrator Account Creation from Web Handler
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attacker can close the intended string, inject arbitrary PHP code, and comment out the remaining generated code' leading to 'wp_insert_user() to create a new administrator account' — admin creation triggered from form processing (not admin UI) is anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect wp_insert_user() or wp_create_user() API calls executed in web request context (form handlers, plugin callbacks) rather than admin page or CLI. Correlate admin-level account creation with form submission events or plugin-processing stack traces. Alert on account creation with admin role/capabilities outside standard admin workflows.

suggestion.title: New Administrator Account Named 'diksimarina' or Variants
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'review log files and administrator accounts for any suspicious activity, especially containing the string diksimarina' — this is a direct IOC for post-exploitation detection and account hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query WordPress user/admin tables for accounts matching 'diksimarina' or phonetic/typo variants. For all WordPress sites, establish baseline of admin account creation rate and alert on new admin accounts created outside business hours or normal workflows. Cross-reference account creation timestamps with form submission/plugin logs.

suggestion.title: Sustained Exploitation Attempt Rate from Primary Attacker IPs
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exploitation attempts originate primarily from two IP addresses, 202.56.2[.]126 and 209.146.60.26' and 'firewall blocking over 29,300 attempts' — high-volume attack signature from specific sources is detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Block or alert on all inbound traffic from 202.56.2[.]126 and 209.146.60.26. For broader detection, establish threshold for per-source form submission failure rate (e.g., >50 failed attempts in 1 hour from single IP to Everest Forms Pro endpoints). Correlate with Wordfence/WAF block telemetry.

suggestion.title: eval() Function Execution with Unsanitized User Input (PHP Code Injection)
suggestion.rationale: Article core vulnerability: 'executes the resulting code using PHP's eval() function' and 'sanitize_text_field() function, which does not escape single quotes' — server-side code execution from form data is the root cause and detectable via AST/runtime instrumentation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Log/alert all eval() calls in production code, especially in plugin handlers. Verify eval() arguments do not originate from HTTP request parameters, POST data, or database values populated from user input. Flag eval() on concatenated strings containing user-supplied data. Most production WordPress deployments should not eval() user-controlled input; blanket alerting is justified.

suggestion.title: Malicious App Installation from Third-Party TV App Stores
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Free Apps Are Quietly Turning Smart TVs Into...'. Attackers distribute deceptive apps via app stores. Pipeline missed initial-access phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor smart TV app installation events for apps requesting network permissions but claiming utility-only functionality. Alert on install-then-connect patterns where app establishes C2 connection within 5 minutes of installation. Correlate app metadata (name, publisher, permissions) against known malicious signatures.

suggestion.title: High-Volume Outbound HTTPS from Smart TV to Unusual Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'turning Smart TVs Into Web-Scraping Proxies'. TV devices should not initiate high-volume HTTP/HTTPS to arbitrary external domains. Pipeline missed collection/exfiltration detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when smart TV devices generate >1GB outbound HTTPS traffic per day to domain whitelist outside entertainment/streaming providers. Flag repeated connections to newly-registered or low-reputation domains. Correlate with DNS queries for reconnaissance patterns (iterative domain enumeration, common scraping targets).

suggestion.title: Abnormal App Permission Escalation on Smart TV
suggestion.rationale: Article implies apps request broad network access disguised as legitimate utility. Pipeline missed permission-anomaly detection during initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag smart TV apps requesting network access (TCP/UDP, DNS, proxy settings) when app category is listed as 'game' or 'utility'. Alert on apps modifying system proxy settings or installing root certificates post-installation. Correlate permission requests with missing documentation in app store listing.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance of Web Content via Smart TV User-Agent
suggestion.rationale: Article: apps scrape web content 'for AI'. Pipeline missed detection of systematic reconnaissance/web-harvesting behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTP requests from smart TV devices with systematic URL patterns (e.g., /page/1, /page/2, ...) or User-Agent strings spoofing web crawlers. Alert on extraction of specific content types (e.g., repeated text extraction from news/social media domains). Correlate with known AI training data harvesters' behavioral signatures.

suggestion.title: Persistent Callback Patterns from Compromised Smart TV
suggestion.rationale: Article describes apps as 'proxies' implying persistent C2 relationship. Pipeline missed command-and-control detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect smart TVs establishing persistent TCP/443 connections to non-streaming infrastructure domains. Alert on beaconing patterns (e.g., heartbeat intervals every 5–30 min). Flag domains with low reputation scores, recently registered (< 30 days), or sharing IP space with known C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Compromise: Trojanized Apps in TV App Stores
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Free Apps' as distribution vector. Pipeline missed supply-chain threat assessment and app-integrity monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate app versions/hashes across TVs. Alert when app binary differs from store-listed hash or contains unexpected network code. Monitor for app publishers suddenly publishing multiple utilities with overlapping network permissions. Implement app-store crawling to identify publishers with rapid release cadence and minimal user reviews.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Free App Installation from Official Smart TV App Stores
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Free apps available on Samsung, LG, Roku, and other major smart TV platforms have been quietly enrolling millions of living room devices'—apps masquerade as legitimate utilities but distribute proxy malware through official channels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious app installations on Smart TV platforms; identify apps with rapid adoption post-release, deceptive descriptions (free utility + vague permissions), or permission requests exceeding legitimate use case (network + device ID + location for 'media player').

suggestion.title: Smart TV Device Registration with Commercial Proxy Network C2
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'secretly enrolling millions of living room devices into a commercial residential proxy network'—devices establish C2 connections to Bright Data/Luminati infrastructure domains for proxy command and control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on network connections from consumer IoT devices (Smart TVs, set-top boxes) to known proxy infrastructure domains (luminati.io, bright-sdk.com, brdtnet.com, proxyjs.* subdomains). Cross-reference with legitimate Smart TV traffic baselines; whitelist official firmware/app update servers.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Persistent Proxy Execution on Smart TV After App Installation
suggestion.rationale: Apps silently execute proxy functionality on device boot—'consent dialog buried in a TV remote's arrow-key navigation' enables imperceptible persistence. Proxy process runs continuously to serve C2 requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Smart TV app startup behavior post-installation; identify apps that establish outbound network connections immediately on boot or device wake, particularly to proxy infrastructure. Baseline legitimate app behavior and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via Unauthorized Smart TV Proxy Network Enrollment
suggestion.rationale: Devices are 'used to scrape web data for AI training' and proxy external requests—device bandwidth is hijacked to exfiltrate data for third parties. User's residential network is abused without knowledge or consent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sustained, high-volume outbound traffic from Smart TV devices to commercial proxy domains without corresponding user-initiated requests. Spike detection on bytes transferred from residential IPs to proxy infrastructure. Correlate with app activity logs.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion via Deceptive UI Consent Burial in TV Navigation
suggestion.rationale: Attack deliberately obscures enrollment consent in complex TV remote navigation: 'consent dialog buried in a TV remote's arrow-key navigation'—users click through without understanding implications, evading informed security decisions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor app permission grant logs for suspicious permission request sequencing—network + device ID + location requested in buried menus. Identify apps requesting sensitive permissions without clear user-facing justification in UI or changelog.

suggestion.title: Compromised App Store Supply Chain—Malicious Free App Proliferation
suggestion.rationale: Attack compromises legitimate app distribution channels (Samsung, LG, Roku stores)—threat actor or insiders inject proxy code into 'free' app builds, affecting supply chain integrity at scale.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor app store distribution for code-signing anomalies, unexpected version updates, or apps with sudden metadata changes (description, permissions) post-submission. Correlate app update timestamps with proxy infrastructure registration. Flag apps by new/unvetted publishers.

suggestion.title: GitHub Repository Compromise — Unusual Commit Activity
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack via 73 Microsoft GitHub repositories indicates attackers achieved write access to commit or merge malicious code; pipeline must detect anomalous git history patterns. Article title explicitly names 'GitHub Repositories' as attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub audit logs for unusual push/merge events to Microsoft-owned repositories outside normal CI/CD windows, commits from newly-added collaborators with no prior history, or mass repository modifications within short timeframe. Alert on commit authors not in whitelist or commits bypassing required code review.

suggestion.title: Miasma Worm — Artifact Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Miasma Worm' as payload; must detect execution of worm binaries or suspicious scripts injected into supply chain packages. This is the post-compromise execution phase where worm propagates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of files named or signed with 'Miasma' variant, processes spawning from package installations or repository-cloned code directories, suspicious PowerShell/bash execution from git working directories, or child processes from package managers (npm, pip, nuget) executing unsigned code.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package Repository Poisoning — Mass Modification
suggestion.rationale: Attack affecting 73 repositories suggests either mass repo compromise or coordinated injection into published packages; pipeline must detect anomalous bulk modifications to package manifests or source trees.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on simultaneous or near-simultaneous commits to multiple Microsoft-controlled repositories from same actor/service account, modifications to package.json/requirements.txt/csproj across multiple repos in same org, or unusual package version bumps/re-publishing from compromised credentials.

suggestion.title: GitHub Credentials Compromise — Unauthorized Access Pattern
suggestion.rationale: 73 simultaneous repos accessed suggests compromised GitHub personal access tokens, deploy keys, or service account credentials used for write access. Article phrase 'worm hits 73 repositories' implies persistent access capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GitHub PAT/SSH key usage from unusual geolocations, times of day, or IP ranges compared to baseline; multiple failed authentication attempts followed by success; service accounts accessing repositories outside their normal scope; API token usage from non-whitelisted applications.
